# Release/publish workflows hand signing and registry secrets to third-party actions pinned by mutable tags

## Details
Every credentialed workflow in the release and publishing pipeline executes third-party GitHub Actions referenced by mutable git refs (`@v7`, `@v4`, `@v2`, `@stable`, `@v8.1.0`) rather than by commit SHA, and several jobs additionally install unpinned code (pip without versions or hashes, apt --allow-unauthenticated, curl|sh rustup) before a later step in the same job uses a secret. GitHub Actions resolves `uses: owner/repo@ref` by fetching that ref when the job runs; a tag is a mutable git ref that the action owner (or whoever compromises that account or its release automation) can retarget, so the code that receives the project's secrets is chosen upstream at run time rather than fixed by this repository (as in the March 2025 tj-actions/changed-files incident, where every version tag was moved to a credential-exfiltrating commit).

The most severe sink is release-publish.yml:41-47: `crazy-max/ghaction-import-gpg@v7` receives GPG_PRIVATE_KEY and GPG_PASSPHRASE as inputs and imports the key with trust_level 5; the following steps sign SHA256SUMS-<version>(-arm64/-armv7) with it (tools/build-release.sh sign, tools/sign-release-arm.sh). release-checklist.md:36 documents that this is the `cln@blockstream.com` key, SECURITY.md lists that key as valid for validating release signatures, and repro.md:235 tells users that a good signature plus a matching checksum means the binaries are safe to install. docker-build.yml and docker-publish.yml give DOCKER_USERNAME/DOCKER_PASSWORD to docker/login-action@v4 and push `<owner>/lightningd` (`latest` included) via build-push-action@v7 / buildx. crate-io.yml gives CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN to katyo/publish-crates@v2 on every push to master after installing the toolchain via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable. pypi-publish.yml installs `uv` via astral-sh/setup-uv@v8.1.0 (no `version:` input, so the uv binary itself is fetched unpinned) and runs that binary with UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN (PyPI/TestPyPI) in its environment; pypi-build.yml builds the published sdists/wheels with the same binary. readme-rpc-sync.yml does an unpinned `pip install requests mako grpcio-tools`, runs .github/scripts/setup.sh (`apt-get --allow-unauthenticated`, `curl https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`) and a full `make`, then exposes README_API_KEY to a Python script that imports those packages; rdme-docs-sync.yml passes the same key on the command line of readmeio/rdme@v10. repro.yml and coverage-nightly.yaml hand e-mail and Codecov credentials to dawidd6/action-send-mail@v17 and codecov/codecov-action@v6. release.yml forwards every repository secret to each called workflow with `secrets: inherit`.

A step receives only the secrets it is passed, but the steps of one job share the runner: an earlier malicious action can replace binaries on PATH (setup-uv's `uv` is exactly what later runs with UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN) or leave a background process reading later steps' environments, so the exposure is the union of secrets used anywhere in the job. No workflow in the release path declares a GitHub `environment:` (only publish-site.yaml does), so these are plain repository secrets with no deployment-protection gate. Repository-level settings (allowed-actions list, SHA-pin enforcement) are not visible in the checkout, but an allowlist by action name does not stop a retargeted tag, and the release checklist documents these workflows running as written, so SHA-pin enforcement cannot be active.

1. [.github/workflows/release-publish.yml:41–47](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/.github/workflows/release-publish.yml#L41-L47)
   crazy-max/ghaction-import-gpg@v7 (mutable tag, resolved at run time) receives GPG_PRIVATE_KEY and GPG_PASSPHRASE directly as inputs and imports the key with trust_level 5; whatever code that tag resolves to holds the release-signing key. release-checklist.md:36 documents this as the cln@blockstream.com key, which SECURITY.md lists as valid for release signatures; lines 54-63 then sign SHA256SUMS-<version>(-arm64/-armv7) with it.

   All sub-workflows are called with `secrets: inherit`, so every repository secret is available to each of these jobs.

   codecov/codecov-action@v6 receives CODECOV_TOKEN (the same component class as the 2021 Codecov uploader compromise).

## Impact
Disclosure of the GPG release-signing private key and passphrase (the cln@blockstream.com key, release-checklist.md:36), the Docker Hub password, crates.io and PyPI tokens, and README/e-mail/Codecov credentials (C:H); the same code can alter the artifacts being signed or built in that job and publish arbitrary artifacts under the project's identity (I:H). Availability of the pipeline itself is not materially affected. Subsequent-system impact: The stolen credentials let the attacker publish trojaned elementsproject/lightningd images, cln-rpc/cln-plugin/cln-grpc crates and pyln packages, and sign a forged SHA256SUMS with a key SECURITY.md lists as valid for releases; repro.md:235 tells users that a good signature plus matching checksum means the binaries are safe to install. Operators who install such a build hand the attacker their hsm_secret and funds and lose control of the node (C:H/I:H/A:H).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker position: control of any referenced third-party action repository or tag (maintainer-account or release-automation compromise), of the astral.sh/rustup download endpoints, or of an unpinned PyPI package used by readme-rpc-sync. Delivery: retarget the tag or publish a malicious version; the next release tag push, master push (crate-io.yml), docs push or nightly run executes it on the runner with the secrets shown. No privileges on ElementsProject/lightning and no user interaction are needed; the single requirement is the upstream compromise. Assumes GitHub Actions resolves `uses:` refs at run time (platform behaviour, not verifiable in the checkout).

## Recommended fix
1. Third-party actions that receive or run alongside publishing secrets are referenced by mutable tags, so their code is chosen by the action owner at run time. Fix criteria: Pin every non-GitHub-owned action (and preferably GitHub-owned ones) to a full commit SHA with a version comment, enable the repository/organisation 'allowed actions' policy, and move publishing secrets into protected GitHub Environments scoped to the release workflows. Verify: no `uses:` line in .github/workflows resolves to a branch or tag.
2. Jobs that hold a secret first install unpinned code (pip install without versions/hashes, apt --allow-unauthenticated, curl|sh rustup) that runs in the same process environment as the secret. Fix criteria: Install Python dependencies from a hash-pinned lock (uv sync / pip --require-hashes), drop --allow-unauthenticated, and separate secret-bearing steps into a minimal job that does not build or install anything. Verify: the readme-rpc-sync and rdme-docs-sync jobs that see README_API_KEY run only pinned, verified code.
3. The release-signing private key lives in CI and is imported with trust level 5 by a third-party action. Fix criteria: Keep the long-lived release key offline (release captains sign manually, as the checklist already supports) or use a dedicated CI subkey with limited validity and detached verification; if a CI key is retained, import it with native gpg commands rather than a third-party action. Verify: no third-party action input receives the private key material.

# Zero-conf fundee channel re-records channel open at confirmation; balance below push_msat makes lightningd fatal() in a block-processing crash loop

## Details
channel_record_open() (lightningd/channel_control.c:1085) emits the bookkeeping 'channel_open' coin movement and derives the opening balance from the channel's *current* balance: for a channel the peer opened it computes start_balance = our_msat - push and calls fatal() if that subtraction underflows. That is only correct while our_msat >= push, i.e. before the fundee has sent anything on the channel (opening_control.c:147 sets a fundee's our_msat to the opener's push_msat). For a zero-conf channel the function is run twice: first from peer_got_channel_ready() -> lockin_complete() when channel_ready is exchanged at depth 0 (channel becomes CHANNELD_NORMAL and usable, blockheight 0 'channel_proposed'), and again from channel_apply_scid() (channel_control.c:873, lockin_has_completed(channel, false)) when the funding tx first confirms, from channel_funding_found() during block processing. Between the two the channel is in normal use, so once the fundee has forwarded or paid anything out over it, our_msat < push and the second call hits fatal("Unable to sub our_msat ... - push ..."), aborting lightningd.

Because the block is processed inside the DB transaction around the bcli response (plugin.c:737/785) and fatal() aborts before commit, wallet_block_add and the scid assignment roll back: on restart the channel is still NORMAL without an scid, the same block is fetched again and the same fatal() recurs on every restart until the operator intervenes (manual DB edit or closing the channel another way).

Attack (requires the victim to accept a zero-conf channel from the attacker's node): the attacker A opens a channel to victim V with push_msat P and V's openchannel hook returns mindepth 0 (default minimum_depth is funding_confirms, opening_common.c:58; the shipped cln-lsps-client grants mindepth 0 to its configured LSP without checking push_msat, client.rs:661-721, so an LSPS2 client is a zero-conf fundee of whatever its LSP opens). After channel_ready, A routes one payment to itself through V with the zero-conf channel as V's outgoing hop (V forwards over zero-conf channels by default, tests/test_opening.py::test_zeroconf_forward), so V's our_msat drops below P. A then lets the funding confirm (A is the opener and controls broadcast timing). V's lightningd fatal()s while connecting that block and keeps doing so on every restart. The same happens without attacker intent for any honest zero-conf fundee that spends pushed funds before confirmation. The onchain_control.c:1819 funding-spent path uses the same stale computation.

Not a splice issue: on splice lock update_channel_from_inflight() (peer_control.c:2497) sets channel->push = inflight->lease_fee, which handle_add_inflight() creates as AMOUNT_MSAT(0) (channel_control.c:963), before lockin_complete() re-records the open, so that call cannot underflow.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1085–1108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1085-L1108)
   channel_record_open() derives start_balance from the *live* channel->our_msat: for a channel the peer opened (opener == REMOTE) it computes our_msat - channel->push and calls fatal() when amount_msat_sub() underflows. That identity (our_msat >= push) only holds until the fundee has sent anything on the channel; the function is nevertheless re-run on an already-operating zero-conf channel.
2. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:860–877](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L860-L877)
   channel_apply_scid(): when the funding of a zero-conf channel (minimum_depth == 0, scid still NULL) first confirms, it calls lockin_has_completed(channel, false) -> channel_record_open() a second time, after the channel has been CHANNELD_NORMAL and forwarding since channel_ready. Nothing records that the open was already emitted or that our_msat has moved.
3. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1286–1309](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1286-L1309)
   peer_got_channel_ready(): with minimum_depth 0, depth 0 >= 0 so lockin_complete(CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN) moves the channel to CHANNELD_NORMAL before any confirmation. The first channel_record_open (blockheight 0, 'channel_proposed') passes because at that moment our_msat == push.
4. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:146–148](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L146-L148)
   For a v1 fundee channel our_msat starts exactly equal to the opener's push_msat and channel->push is persisted (push_msatoshi, wallet.c:2758/2222) and never changed for a v1 channel.
5. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2093–2108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2093-L2108)
   A fulfilled outgoing HTLC deducts hout->msat from channel->our_msat, so one payment forwarded out over the zero-conf channel (attacker routes to itself: in over another channel, out over this one) leaves our_msat < push.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2664–2675](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2664-L2675)
   channel_funding_found() (scriptpubkey watch registered by channel_watch_funding, fired synchronously from chaintopology.c filter_block_txs -> watch_check_tx_outputs while the block is connected) -> depthcb_update_scid() -> channel_apply_scid(): the trigger runs inside block processing, under the attacker's timing (the opener chooses when to broadcast the funding tx).
7. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:839–845](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L839-L845)
   The openchannel hook's `mindepth` field is what sets uc->minimum_depth = 0 for a fundee (default is funding_confirms, opening_common.c:58): the path exists only when the operator's plugin accepts a zero-conf channel from the attacker's node.
8. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:661–720](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs#L661-L720)
   Shipped cln-lsps-client returns {"mindepth": 0} for an open_channel from the LSP it requested a JIT channel from, without checking push_msat or any other parameter ("Fixme: Check that channel parameters are as negotiated"), so a CLN node acting as LSPS2 client is a zero-conf fundee of whatever its LSP opens.
9. [lightningd/plugin.c:736–785](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L736-L785)
   Block processing runs inside the DB transaction wrapped around the bcli plugin's JSON response (want_db_transaction); fatal() aborts before db_commit_transaction, so wallet_block_add (chaintopology.c:1017) and the channel_set_scid done in channel_apply_scid roll back. After restart the channel is still NORMAL with no scid, channel_watch_funding is re-registered (peer_control.c:3156-3166), the same block is fetched again and the same fatal() recurs: a crash loop until the operator intervenes.
10. [lightningd/log.c:1131–1143](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L1131-L1143)
   fatal_vfmt() logs and abort()s lightningd.
11. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:1812–1820](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L1812-L1820)
   The funding-spent path calls channel_record_open(channel, blkh, true) for a channel without scid or remote_channel_ready using the same live our_msat - push computation; a fix must cover this caller too.

## Impact
lightningd aborts while connecting the block and, because the block and scid writes are rolled back, aborts again on every restart: the whole node is persistently down (all channels, all HTLC timeouts unattended) until the operator repairs the database. No confidentiality or integrity impact beyond the DoS.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer whose zero-conf channel open the victim accepts (openchannel hook mindepth 0, e.g. the victim's configured LSP via the shipped cln-lsps-client, or any operator zero-conf policy plugin) — a deployment/trust condition on the victim, hence AT:PRESENT; no credentials on the victim are needed (PR:NONE) and no victim action (UI:NONE): the attacker opens with push_msat, routes one payment through the victim out over the channel from a second channel it controls, then lets the funding confirm. lightningd fatal()s during block processing and again on every restart. The project concedes only double-spend risk on that channel to a mindepth-0 peer (doc/schemas/hook/openchannel.json:189-192), not node availability.

## Recommended fix
channel_record_open() derives the opening balance from the live our_msat and treats an underflow against the persisted push as an invariant violation (fatal), but it is re-invoked on already-operating channels: zero-conf scid assignment in channel_apply_scid() and the funding-spent path in onchain_control.c, where our_msat has legitimately moved. Fix criteria: Re-recording the open at late scid assignment or funding spend must never abort lightningd: compute the opening balance from persisted opening data (our_funds and push at open, or the start balance stored with the proposed-open event) instead of current our_msat, and downgrade any residual underflow to a logged error. Verify: zero-conf fundee channel with push_msat, fundee forwards or pays out part of the pushed funds before confirmation, funding confirms; lightningd stays up, the channel gets its scid, and bookkeeper events remain consistent; same for the funding-spent path with an unconfirmed channel.

# Bookkeeper refresh snapshots chain and channel moves separately; peer-timed pushed open kills lightningd

## Details
Bookkeeper rebuilds its view of accounts from two independent lightningd RPCs issued back to back: refresh_moves_ (plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:286-320) calls listchainmoves, and only when that reply has been processed does listchainmoves_done (260-284) call listchannelmoves. Each reply is a snapshot of lightningd's table at the time lightningd handles that request (lightningd/coin_mvts.c:296-400), and lightningd does not read the next request on a connection until the previous reply is consumed (lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1199-1201), so other events — including channeld messages — are serviced between the two snapshots.

parse_and_log_channel_move (1643-1649) requires the channel move's account to already exist and plugin_err()s otherwise ("Received channel event, but no account exists"). Accounts are created solely from chain moves (parse_and_log_chain_move:1529-1532). lightningd's channel_record_open (lightningd/channel_control.c:1085-1139) writes the channel_open chain move and then, in the same synchronous call and DB transaction, a `pushed` (or `lease_fee`) channel move for the same channel whenever push_msat is non-zero. If that call executes between bookkeeper's two snapshots, listchannelmoves returns the pushed move for an account whose channel_open bookkeeper has not ingested: find_account returns NULL, plugin_err exits bookkeeper, and because bookkeeper is an important builtin plugin, lightningd exits (lightningd/plugin.c:297-303).

Who controls the timing: a remote peer opening an inbound channel to us with push_msat >= 1 msat (openingd accepts any push_msat <= funding, openingd.c:944-950; inbound opens are accepted by default). channel_record_open(…, record_push=true) runs from lockin_complete, which peer_got_channel_ready (channel_control.c:1287-1309) invokes the instant the peer's channel_ready arrives once our funding depth is met; after we send our channel_ready the peer picks that instant (dual_open_control.c:2148 and onchain_control.c:1813-1820 are equivalent callers). The peer cannot observe bookkeeper's window directly, so each attempt is a timing race; attempts are repeatable with several pre-opened pushed channels (funds recoverable by cooperative close).

When the refresh happens: with the non-default dynamic option bkpr-currency set (bookkeeper.c:2083, doc/lightningd-config.5.md:581), the wait loop at 1875-1911 re-runs a full refresh on every chain or channel move, which the same peer generates at will (keysend payment over an existing channel, or lock-in of a first pushed channel), so the peer can both open the window and aim at it. Without bkpr-currency the window opens only on operator-initiated bkpr-* RPCs (dashboards polling bkpr-listbalances, sql-plugin bkpr tables) and the peer must coincide with it blind; the utxo_deposit/utxo_spend notification handlers are not fed by lightningd itself.

The earlier dismissal of this sink (dismissed-bookkeeper-1646-a095) reasoned that lightningd always records the chain open before any channel move and that bookkeeper pages chain moves before channel moves; both are true but do not help, because the two pages are not one snapshot.

Effect: a one-shot lightningd shutdown per success (channels, HTLC handling and chain monitoring stop until restart; contrib/init/lightningd.service has Restart=on-failure, so the outage is a restart cycle where systemd is used). It is not a crash loop: the chainmoves_index datastore write is queued before listchannelmoves and processed first, so after restart the refresh fetches the channel_open before the pushed move.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1643–1649](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1643-L1649)
   parse_and_log_channel_move looks the channel move's account_id up with find_account (account.c:253, a plain htable lookup) and plugin_err()s when it is absent. Accounts are only ever created from chain moves (find_or_create_account at bookkeeper.c:1529-1532), so a channel move whose channel_open chain move this refresh has not ingested is fatal to the plugin.
2. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:260–319](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L260-L319)
   refresh_moves_ sends listchainmoves (start=chainmoves_index+1); only in its reply callback listchainmoves_done does limited_listchannelmoves send listchannelmoves. The two replies are separate lightningd snapshots taken in different io_loop iterations; nothing bounds the channel-move page to the chain-move snapshot.
3. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1085–1138](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1085-L1138)
   channel_record_open saves the channel_open chain move (wallet_save_chain_mvt) and, when channel->push is non-zero and record_push is true, immediately saves a pushed/lease_fee channel move for the same account in the same call. Both rows are committed in the same per-event DB transaction, so a refresh whose listchainmoves predates and listchannelmoves postdates this call sees only the channel move.
4. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1287–1309](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1287-L1309)
   peer_got_channel_ready handles the peer's channel_ready forwarded by channeld (channeld.c:601-642) and, if our depth already meets minimum_depth, calls lockin_complete -> lockin_has_completed(channel, true) -> channel_record_open immediately. After we have sent our channel_ready the remote peer alone chooses the instant this write happens.
5. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1199–1201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L1199-L1201)
   read_json refuses to read the next request from a connection while a reply is still unconsumed, so between answering listchainmoves and reading bookkeeper's listchannelmoves lightningd necessarily runs further io_loop iterations in which channeld pipes (and hence channel_ready -> channel_record_open) are serviced; the window is real, not theoretical.
6. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1875–1910](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1875-L1910)
   When the non-default dynamic option bkpr-currency (bookkeeper.c:2083; doc/lightningd-config.5.md:581) is set, bookkeeper runs a permanent wait(chainmoves/channelmoves created) loop that calls refresh_moves on every new movement, so a remote peer reopens the inter-snapshot window at will by paying the node (keysend) or by locking in another channel. Without that option, refreshes happen only on operator-initiated bkpr-* RPCs (and sql-plugin bkpr tables, sql.c:1851-1852); the utxo_deposit/utxo_spend handlers (1792-1799) are not emitted by lightningd itself.
7. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L302)
   bookkeeper is a builtin important plugin (plugins_set_builtin_plugins_dir: everything but cln-renepay); its plugin_err exit makes lightningd_exit(ld, 1).
8. [lightningd/coin\_mvts.c:296–399](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/coin_mvts.c#L296-L399)
   listchainmoves and listchannelmoves are independent RPCs, each reading the current table state; both emit account_id via json_add_mvt_account_id (178-186) as the channel id, so the pushed move's account name equals the not-yet-seen channel_open's account name. There is no combined or consistent-snapshot query bookkeeper could use.

## Impact
lightningd exits when the important bookkeeper plugin dies: channel operation, HTLC handling and on-chain monitoring stop until the operator (or systemd Restart=on-failure) restarts the node; the peer must win the race again to repeat. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Unauthenticated remote peer opens an inbound channel with push_msat >= 1 msat and delays its channel_ready until it estimates bookkeeper is between its listchainmoves and listchannelmoves snapshots. A race must be won (AC:H per CVSS 4.0's race-condition guidance); the attacker can force and roughly time the window only where the operator has set the non-default bkpr-currency option (refresh on every movement the peer triggers), otherwise it must coincide blind with operator-initiated bkpr-* refreshes (AT:P). Attempts are repeatable at the cost of an on-chain channel open each; a win terminates lightningd.

## Recommended fix
1. Bookkeeper assumes two separately-snapshotted RPC pages (listchainmoves then listchannelmoves) form one consistent view, and treats a channel move for a not-yet-seen account as a fatal invariant violation. Fix criteria: A channel move whose account is unknown must not terminate the plugin: either defer/re-fetch chain moves before processing channel moves (e.g. bound listchannelmoves to the chainmoves snapshot or loop until a consistent pair is obtained), or create/queue the account and resolve it when the chain open arrives. Verify: inserting a channel_open plus pushed move between the two RPC replies (e.g. with a test hook) leaves bookkeeper and lightningd running and the balances correct.
2. Invariant violations on data received from lightningd are handled with plugin_err in an important plugin, converting any ordering surprise into a node-wide outage. Fix criteria: Non-corruption inconsistencies in ingested movement data should be logged (LOG_BROKEN) and skipped or retried rather than killing the plugin. Verify that bookkeeper survives an unknown-account channel move and reconciles it on the next refresh.

# Bookkeeper uses raw account names as datastore key elements; empty name kills lightningd

## Details
Bookkeeper persists per-account state in lightningd's datastore under keys whose last element is the account name exactly as it arrived in a coin movement: ["bookkeeper","account",<name>] (account.c:144-159) and ["bookkeeper","onchain_fee",<name>] (onchain_fee.c:173-188). Account names are not validated anywhere: parse_and_log_chain_move (bookkeeper.c:1529) calls find_or_create_account on whatever account_id listchainmoves returns, and lightningd's injectutxodeposit/injectutxospend (lightningd/coin_mvts.c:421-495) accept `account` as an arbitrary param_string, including the empty string, and store it verbatim.

A datastore key whose trailing element is "" hits the already-verified lightningd defect datastore-trailing-empty-key-part-duplicate-insert-fatal: the row is created once, but every later existence check misses it, so any further create-capable write (must-create, create-or-append) re-INSERTs the same primary key and db_fatal()s lightningd. Bookkeeper performs exactly such a second write deterministically: insert_chain_fees_diff (onchain_fee.c:296-311) appends a new record to ["bookkeeper","onchain_fee",<acct>] with create-or-append every time the computed on-chain fee attributed to (acct, txid) changes, and maybe_update_onchain_fees recomputes that fee for every chain move on the txid (bookkeeper.c:1544).

Attack (position: a commando/clnrest rune bearer whose rune permits injectutxodeposit -- the same position accepted for bkpr-csv-export-gmtime-null-deref-injected-timestamp; the utxo_deposit notification path at bookkeeper.c:1692-1743 reaches the same sink but is only driven by installed plugins):
1. injectutxodeposit account="" outpoint=<F>:98 amount_msat=1000 ..., where F is the funding txid of any of the node's public channels (known from gossip). F already has wallet withdrawal debits and channel_open/change credits in chain_moves, so withdraw >= deposit and a non-zero fee is split between the channel account and ""; the first create-or-append of ["bookkeeper","onchain_fee",""] succeeds.
2. injectutxodeposit account="" outpoint=<F>:99 amount_msat=2000. The fee changes, insert_chain_fees_diff issues a second create-or-append for the same key, json_datastore misses the existing row, wallet_datastore_create's INSERT violates PRIMARY KEY(key), db_exec_prepared_v2 -> db_fatal -> lightningd exits. (With injectutxospend also permitted, the self-contained deposit/spend/deposit sequence of test_bookkeeper_custom_notifs works without needing F.)
Both moves are processed in the next bookkeeper refresh (any bkpr-* RPC such as a dashboard's bkpr-listbalances, or immediately and continuously when bkpr-currency is set).

Persistence: the injected chain moves cannot be deleted, and lightningd dies before bookkeeper's queued chainmoves_index write is processed (requests are handled in order), so on every restart the next refresh re-processes both moves and re-triggers the fatal INSERT; deldatastore of the exact key only buys one more cycle. Recovery requires manual datastore surgery or disabling the plugin.

Secondary sinks from the same unvalidated name: account must-replace writes for "" (maybe_update_account/account_update_closeheight) fail with DOES_NOT_EXIST and, through the NULL errcb -> plugin_broken_cb path, plugin_err the important plugin.

This differs from the datastore finding in entry point (coin-movement account names rather than the datastore RPC), privilege (an injectutxodeposit rune rather than a datastore rune) and fix location (bookkeeper/lightningd must reject or encode account names), so it is filed separately and names that record.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/onchain\_fee.c:173–187](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/onchain_fee.c#L173-L187)
   ds_ofee_path builds the datastore key ["bookkeeper","onchain_fee",acctname] from the account name verbatim and onchain_fee_datastore_add writes it with mode create-or-append and the default errcb. With acctname == "" the key has an empty trailing element; the first write creates the row, every later write for the same account is a second create of an identical primary-key blob.
2. [plugins/bkpr/onchain\_fee.c:280–310](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/onchain_fee.c#L280-L310)
   insert_chain_fees_diff writes a new fee record (and a new datastore append) every time the computed fee attributed to (account, txid) differs from the sum already recorded, so a second deposit on the same txid deterministically produces the second write.
3. [lightningd/coin\_mvts.c:421–459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/coin_mvts.c#L421-L459)
   injectutxodeposit binds `account` with param_string (common/json_param.c:456-463 copies the token verbatim, so "" is accepted), builds a foreign deposit with alt_account "" (set_mvt_account_id) and persists it via wallet_save_chain_mvt; is_duplicate keys on account/outpoint/spending_txid/tags, so distinct outpoints are distinct rows. The command is not dev_only, so runes are the only bound. listchainmoves returns the name verbatim as account_id (json_add_mvt_account_id, lines 178-185, 197).
4. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1529–1551](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1529-L1551)
   parse_and_log_chain_move accepts any account_id string from listchainmoves, calls find_or_create_account with it, then maybe_update_onchain_fees for the move's txid, which reaches insert_chain_fees_diff for every non-external account in the tx. No validation of the account name anywhere in bookkeeper.
5. [common/coin\_mvt.h:322–330](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/coin_mvt.h#L322-L330)
   is_wallet_account/is_external_account are exact string comparisons against the wallet and external names, so "" is neither: maybe_update_onchain_fees (onchain_fee.c:573-668) counts it in no_accts and attributes a fee share to it, which is what triggers the onchain_fee datastore write for the empty name.
6. [lightningd/datastore.c:139–199](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/datastore.c#L139-L199)
   json_datastore's existence check (wallet_datastore_first + datastore_key_eq) cannot see a row whose key ends in an empty element because the NUL-joined blob splits back to a shorter key (wallet/datastore.c:83-125; verified as datastore-trailing-empty-key-part-duplicate-insert-fatal); the exact-match parent checks also miss it, so in create-or-append / must-create mode it re-runs wallet_datastore_create, whose INSERT violates PRIMARY KEY(key) and db_fatal()s lightningd.
7. [plugins/bkpr/account.c:144–158](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/account.c#L144-L158)
   ds_path/account_datastore_set likewise build ["bookkeeper","account",acctname] from the raw name (must-create / must-replace). For "" the row is created once and then becomes invisible to must-replace (DATASTORE_UPDATE_DOES_NOT_EXIST -> plugin_broken_cb -> plugin_err via the NULL errcb at libplugin.c:937-938), a secondary fatal path for the important plugin.
8. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:260–283](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L260-L283)
   listchainmoves_done processes every move (issuing the per-account datastore writes) before queuing the create-or-replace of bookkeeper/chainmoves_index; lightningd handles the plugin's requests in order and dies at the fee write, so the index never advances and the next refresh after restart re-processes the same moves and re-triggers the fatal INSERT.
9. [tests/test\_bookkeeper.py:1104–1121](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tests/test_bookkeeper.py#L1104-L1121)
   test_bookkeeper_custom_notifs shows the maintainers' expected flow: a second deposit on the same spending txid of a custom account recomputes the fee and yields a second onchain_fee record (len == 2). With the account name "" that second record is the fatal duplicate INSERT.

## Impact
lightningd exits via db_fatal; all channel, HTLC and on-chain monitoring stops. The poisoned chain moves persist and bookkeeper's index does not advance, so the node re-crashes at every subsequent refresh until the operator performs manual datastore surgery or disables bookkeeper. Integrity impact limited to mis-keyed bookkeeper datastore rows and falsified accounting the rune already permits.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a rune bearer permitted injectutxodeposit (commando over the peer connection, or clnrest). Two RPC calls with account="" on distinct outpoints of a txid the node already has a withdrawal for (any public funding txid) deterministically produce two create-or-append writes to a datastore key with an empty trailing element; the second write db_fatal()s lightningd at the next bookkeeper refresh. No race, no special configuration, repeatable on every restart.

## Recommended fix
1. Bookkeeper embeds unvalidated, externally supplied account names directly as datastore key elements (account.c:146, onchain_fee.c:175), so a name the datastore cannot round-trip (empty, or other pathological values) turns routine state writes into a fatal duplicate insert. Fix criteria: Account names used in datastore keys must be guaranteed round-trippable: reject empty (and otherwise unencodable) names when ingesting chain moves, or encode names (e.g. hex) before using them as key elements. Verify: injectutxodeposit with account="" followed by a second deposit on the same txid leaves lightningd running and bookkeeper either rejects the account or records fees for it correctly across a restart.
2. lightningd's injectutxodeposit/injectutxospend accept any string as an account name, including the empty string, which is also the reserved onchaind meaning for 'this channel'. Fix criteria: The inject RPCs must reject empty account names (and names colliding with reserved/channel identifiers) with an invalid-params error. Verify: injectutxodeposit account="" returns an error and no chain move is stored.
3. Bookkeeper treats any datastore error reply as fatal (NULL errcb -> plugin_broken_cb), so a recoverable bookkeeping write failure terminates an important plugin. Fix criteria: Datastore write failures for per-account state should be logged and degrade gracefully rather than calling plugin_err. Verify: forcing a must-replace on a missing key logs an error while bookkeeper and lightningd keep running.

# Unsolicited channeld send_error_reply deletes a live funded channel or fatal()s lightningd

## Details
lightningd's forget_channel() (channel_control.c:1511-1522) is used only by cancel_channel_before_broadcast()/process_check_funding_broadcast() for an opener-side CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN channel whose funding tx has verifiably not been broadcast; it asks channeld (via subd_send_msg, not subd_req) to send an error to the peer and waits for WIRE_CHANNELD_SEND_ERROR_REPLY, on which handle_error_channel() -> forget() -> delete_channel() removes the channel.

handle_error_channel() does not verify that the reply was solicited (channel->error set) or that the channel is a forgettable unfunded stub, and subd.c:499-509 only matches replies for outstanding subd_req() requests, so channel_msg() routes an unsolicited WIRE_CHANNELD_SEND_ERROR_REPLY to handle_error_channel for every channeld-owned channel in any state. A compromised channeld (threat-model adversary 6 — channeld after a peer-side exploit, running with the peer's connection) therefore writes one 2-byte message on its master pipe and lightningd:

- if the channel has any HTLC in flight (trivially arranged by the peer): fatal()s in destroy_channel() ('Freeing channel ... has hout/hin', channel.c:66-77), taking down the whole node and every other channel. The DB writes of wallet_channel_close() are in the transaction subd.c:493 opened and are rolled back by the abort, so the HTLC persists and the crash repeats on each restart once the peer reconnects and re-exploits channeld;
- otherwise: permanently forgets a live, funded channel. delete_channel() stops watching the funding outpoint, sets the DB row to CLOSED and deletes htlc_sigs/anchors (wallet.c:3091-3160), tells hsmd to forget the channel, and emits channel_state_changed CLOSED, on which chanbackup regenerates the SCB without this channel (chanbackup.c:698-707). The node has abandoned a funded channel with no close transaction, no onchaind, no penalty path and no backup, recorded on disk as a normal closed channel.

What the project already concedes to a compromised channeld: lightningd grants it HSM_PERM_SIGN_REMOTE_TX (channel_control.c:1819-1826) and hsmd's handle_sign_remote_commitment_tx (libhsmd.c:1643-1688) signs any one-input remote commitment without amount validation, so the peer can already drain this channel's balance; channeld can also force-close via status_peer_error -> channel_errmsg. The loss of the channel balance is therefore not the gain of this path. What this path hands the position beyond that is (1) a repeatable crash of lightningd itself — the project's own handlers route bad channeld input to channel_internal_error (channel_control.c:1502) and guard channeld-driven state transitions (channel_control.c:1456), so lightningd is designed not to die on a subdaemon's message — and (2) falsification of lightningd's persistent state for a live channel (CLOSED row, funding unwatched, hsmd forgotten, SCB dropped), which abandons the funds even against an honest peer's later unilateral close and conceals any theft as a normal close.

Fix direction: forget() must only be reachable for a channel lightningd itself decided to forget (channel->error set by forget_channel, state CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN with opener == LOCAL and unbroadcast funding, no HTLCs); any other send_error_reply should be treated as a channeld protocol violation (channel_internal_error) rather than a forget.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1499–1509](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1499-L1509)
   handle_error_channel(): any WIRE_CHANNELD_SEND_ERROR_REPLY from channeld calls forget(channel) with no check that lightningd requested it (channel->error set by forget_channel) or that the channel is an unfunded opener-side CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN stub. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1477–1496](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1477-L1496)
   forget(): delete_channel(channel, false) unconditionally, then answers any pending fundchannel_cancel commands.
3. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1695–1696](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1695-L1696)
   channel_msg() dispatches WIRE_CHANNELD_SEND_ERROR_REPLY to handle_error_channel for every channeld-owned channel in any state (CHANNELD_NORMAL, AWAITING_SPLICE, SHUTTING_DOWN...). Contrast peer_start_closingd_after_shutdown at 1456, which guards its channeld-driven channel_set_state with a state check.
4. [lightningd/subd.c:493–508](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L493-L508)
   sd_msg_read(): each subdaemon message is wrapped in a DB transaction and only replies to outstanding subd_req() requests are matched by type; forget_channel sends channeld_send_error via subd_send_msg, so send_error_reply is never a tracked reply and always falls through to channel_msg, solicited or not.
5. [lightningd/channel.c:89–130](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L89-L130)
   delete_channel(): channel_unwatch_funding() (funding outpoint no longer watched), wallet_channel_close() (DB row set to CLOSED, htlc_sigs/inflights/anchors deleted), hsmd_forget_channel, state_changed notification (chanbackup refreshes the SCB, dropping the channel), then tal_free(channel). Persisted state is changed before any invariant check.
6. [lightningd/channel.c:63–86](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L63-L86)
   destroy_channel(): fatal() if any htlc_in/htlc_out is still attached — for a live channel with an HTLC in flight the forget becomes a lightningd abort(). fatal_vfmt (log.c:1130-1146) aborts before subd.c commits the transaction, so the DB is rolled back and the crash is repeatable on every restart/reconnect.
7. [wallet/wallet.c:3091–3159](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L3091-L3159)
   wallet_channel_close() deletes htlc_sigs, channeltxs, inflights, annotations, feerates and local_anchors and sets channels.state=CLOSED: after restart the channel is a closed channel with no onchaind watching, although the funding output is unspent and the peer holds signed (and revoked) commitments.
8. [channeld/channeld.c:6853–6866](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6853-L6866)
   The only honest emitter: handle_send_error() replies send_error_reply solely in response to lightningd's own channeld_send_error and then exit(0). Any send_error_reply for a channel lightningd did not ask to forget comes from a compromised channeld.

## Impact
Availability HIGH: a single unsolicited message makes lightningd fatal() whenever the channel has an HTLC in flight, taking down every channel on the node, repeatably. Integrity HIGH: lightningd's persistent record of a live funded channel is falsified (channels.state=CLOSED, htlc_sigs/anchors deleted, funding unwatched, hsmd forget, SCB regenerated without it); the node abandons the channel's funds even against an honest peer's later close and any theft is recorded as a normal close. Draining the channel balance itself is already conceded to a compromised channeld via HSM_PERM_SIGN_REMOTE_TX and is not counted here. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a compromised channeld process (threat-model adversary 6) for an established channel, i.e. local code on the host confined to one channel's pipe and hsmd capabilities. It writes WIRE_CHANNELD_SEND_ERROR_REPLY on its master pipe; subd.c matches only subd_req replies so the message reaches channel_msg -> handle_error_channel -> forget() in any channel state. With an HTLC attached (the peer can add one) the node aborts, and since the abort precedes the transaction commit the condition persists across restarts; without, the funded channel is marked CLOSED, unwatched and dropped from hsmd and the SCB. Deterministic, no race, no deployment condition.

## Recommended fix
handle_error_channel trusts channeld's send_error_reply as authority to delete the channel, with no check that lightningd requested the forget or that the channel is a forgettable (unfunded, opener-side, pre-broadcast) stub, and subd's reply matching does not cover it because forget_channel uses subd_send_msg rather than subd_req. Fix criteria: A send_error_reply must only delete the channel when lightningd itself initiated forget_channel() for it (channel->error set, state CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, opener LOCAL, funding unbroadcast, no HTLCs); otherwise it is a channeld protocol violation handled by channel_internal_error. Verify that an unsolicited send_error_reply on a CHANNELD_NORMAL channel (with and without HTLCs) leaves the channel row, funding watch, SCB and hsmd state intact and does not abort lightningd.

# lightningd never recovers owner-less channel on live connection; peer_spoke ignored, orphan queue grows

## Details
lightningd/peer_control.c handle_peer_spoke() receives connectd's one-time notice that a peer sent a message for a channel_id with no attached subdaemon. For a channel lightningd knows, in a channel_state_wants_peercomms state, with channel->owner == NULL (the maintainers' own comment lists this as case '2. subd exited'), it logs 'channel already active' and returns (lines 2208-2239) unless the state is DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN. It neither re-spawns channeld/closingd, nor replies, nor asks connectd to disconnect, so connectd's freshly minted conn-less subd for that channel_id lives on and every later peer message with that id is appended to its unbounded msg_queue (connectd/multiplex.c:1592-1619; the sink verified as connectd-orphan-subd-unbounded-queue) with no further notice to lightningd.

The owner-less-but-connected state is reachable by a remote peer without any crash: channeld's peer_reconnect() answers a channel_reestablish whose next_revocation_number is below our next_index[LOCAL]-1 (and not next_index[LOCAL]-2) with peer_failed_warn_nodisconnect() (channeld.c:6251-6263, comment: 'We don't disconnect: they might send an error'); only the channel_id match, absent next_funding TLVs and next_commitment_number != 0 are checked before it. common/peer_failed.c:67-78 sends STATUS_PEER_ERROR with disconnect=false, warning=true, hands the peer fd back and exits. lightningd's handle_peer_error() -> channel_errmsg() takes the warning branch and calls channel_fail_transient(channel, disconnect=false) (peer_control.c:665-670); channel_err() only clears channel->owner (channel.c:1326-1348). The returned peer_fd is dropped with tmpctx, so connectd's subd socket closes; destroy_connected_subd() (multiplex.c:1447-1469) removes the subd and keeps the TCP connection because nothing requested draining. The same state follows any channeld crash: destroy_subd() invokes errcb with peer_fd=NULL and disconnect=false (subd.c:655-658) -> channel_fail_transient(disconnect=false).

Nothing restarts the subdaemon afterwards: connect_activate_subd() (peer_control.c:1437) runs only from peer_connected_hook_final() on a fresh connection, and connectd's ping timer is satisfied by the peer's pongs. The channel therefore stays unserviced while the peer is reported connected, and connectd accumulates the peer's messages for that channel_id without bound; connectd is must_not_exit (subd.c:663-668) so its OOM-kill terminates lightningd.

Distinct from connectd-orphan-subd-unbounded-queue (connectd's unbounded orphan queue reached via an unknown-channel channel_reestablish; its lightningd-side fix at peer_control.c:2355-2373 does not touch this branch) and from the 'We raced' branch at 2208 (owner set; recovered via tx_abort -> handle_splice_abort restart).

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2204–2239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2204-L2239)
   handle_peer_spoke for a known channel in a channel_state_wants_peercomms state: when channel->owner is NULL (the maintainers' own comment names this case '2. subd exited') it logs 'channel already active' and returns. Only DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN restarts a subdaemon; for CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN/NORMAL/AWAITING_SPLICE/SHUTTING_DOWN and CLOSINGD_SIGEXCHANGE nothing is re-spawned, connectd is not told to attach a subd, and the peer is not disconnected. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:6251–6263](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6251-L6263)
   peer_reconnect(): a channel_reestablish whose next_revocation_number is below next_index[LOCAL]-1 (and not next_index[LOCAL]-2) is answered with peer_failed_warn_nodisconnect ('We don't disconnect: they might send an error'). This runs before check_current_dataloss_fields (6328), so a peer with a channel on which it has sent two commitment_signed can enter the owner-less-but-connected state on demand, with no crash required.
3. [common/peer\_failed.c:67–78](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/peer_failed.c#L67-L78)
   peer_failed_warn_nodisconnect sends STATUS_PEER_ERROR with disconnect=false and warning=true, passes the peer fd back to lightningd and exits channeld.
4. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:642–670](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L642-L670)
   channel_errmsg: both the peer_fd==NULL branch (subdaemon crash, 642-648) and the warning branch (665-670) call channel_fail_transient with the caller's disconnect flag, which is false on these paths; the returned peer_fd is simply dropped with tmpctx, closing connectd's subd socket.
5. [lightningd/channel.c:1326–1348](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1326-L1348)
   channel_err only clears channel->owner; force_peer_disconnect runs solely when disconnect is true. No timer or other mechanism later restarts the subdaemon: connect_activate_subd (peer_control.c:1437, sole caller 1616) runs only from peer_connected_hook_final on a fresh connection.
6. [lightningd/subd.c:636–659](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L636-L659)
   Second route into the same state: when a channel subdaemon crashes or exits, destroy_subd invokes errcb(channel, NULL, 'Owning subdaemon ... died', err_for_them=NULL, disconnect=false, warning=false), so the peer connection is deliberately left up (peer-triggerable via verified channeld assert findings).
7. [connectd/multiplex.c:1447–1469](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1447-L1469)
   destroy_connected_subd: when the subd socket closes connectd removes the subd from peer->subds and wakes the read loop; the peer TCP connection is kept unless draining was already requested.
8. [connectd/multiplex.c:1592–1621](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1592-L1621)
   The peer's next message for the channel_id finds no subd, so connectd mints a conn-less subd, sends connectd_peer_spoke once and enqueues the message; every later message for that id is matched by find_subd (63-87) and appended to the same unbounded msg_queue with no further notice to lightningd (sink shared with verified connectd-orphan-subd-unbounded-queue).

## Impact
Unbounded heap growth in lightning_connectd (bounded only by the 1 MB/s per-peer intake limit), never released while the connection lives; connectd is must_not_exit so its OOM-kill ends lightningd: full node outage, HTLC timeouts and forced closes. Independently the affected channel is unserviced while reported connected until the peer chooses to reconnect, so in-flight HTLCs on it time out. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote peer with one channel to the victim on which it has sent two commitment_signed (victim next_index[LOCAL] >= 3; e.g. add then fail one HTLC). It reconnects and sends channel_reestablish with next_revocation_number=0, a nonzero next_commitment_number and no TLVs: channeld warns and exits with disconnect=false; lightningd clears channel->owner and keeps the connection. It then streams 65 KB messages tagged with the channel's id, interleaved with pings; lightningd answers the single peer_spoke by returning and connectd appends everything to the orphan queue. Any peer-triggered channeld crash enters the same state. No defence to defeat; deterministic.

## Recommended fix
1. handle_peer_spoke returns for a known channel in a peercomms state whose owner is NULL (other than DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN), neither re-spawning the subdaemon nor telling connectd to disconnect or discard the subd, so the orphan subd and its queue persist and the channel is never serviced. Fix criteria: On peer_spoke for a known channel with no owner, lightningd must either restart the appropriate subdaemon and attach it via connectd_peer_connect_subd (which drains the orphan) or disconnect the peer. Verify: after a 'peer in the past' channel_reestablish warning (or a killed channeld) with the connection kept, stream channel messages for that id; connectd RSS must stay bounded and the channel must be re-serviced or the peer disconnected.
2. A channel subdaemon can end with disconnect=false (destroy_subd on crash, peer_failed_warn_nodisconnect on a stale reestablish), leaving a connected peer with an owner-less channel and no recovery until the peer reconnects. Fix criteria: When a channel subdaemon ends while the peer stays connected, service must be restored within bounded time (re-spawn or forced reconnect), or the no-disconnect warning path must be followed by a disconnect as soon as the peer sends any non-error channel message. Verify: an HTLC sent by the peer after such an exit is processed without the peer reconnecting, or the peer is disconnected.

# openchannel hook reply after peer reconnect: NULL openingd deref and write to freed uncommitted channel

## Details
When a remote peer sends open_channel (v1), openingd forwards openingd_got_offer and blocks in wire_sync_read on lightningd (openingd/openingd.c:1036-1037) while lightningd runs the asynchronous `openchannel` plugin hook (opening_control.c:889-907). The hook payload keeps raw pointers to the openingd subd and the uncommitted channel `uc`; plugin_hook_call_() steals the payload onto ph_req (plugin_hook.c:388), so it outlives both.

While the hook is pending the attacker drops the TCP connection and immediately reconnects. connectd removes the previous connection at once ('on the assumption it's dead', connectd/connectd.c:319-325) and sends connectd_peer_reconnected; lightningd's peer_connected() then runs peer_channels_cleanup(peer) (peer_control.c:1919-1925) -> kill_uncommitted_channel() -> tal_free(uc) (opening_common.c:120-127). destroy_uncommitted_channel() calls subd_release_channel(), which tal_free()s openingd (subd.c:928-936); openingd's destructor openchannel_payload_remove_openingd() sets payload->openingd = NULL (opening_control.c:713-719), and uc is gone, leaving payload->uc dangling. (A bare disconnect is not enough: peer_disconnected() deliberately leaves subds running, peer_control.c:2398-2416, and openingd cannot see the EOF while blocked on lightningd; the operator's `connect`/`disconnect` RPCs reach the same cleanup, but the reconnect is the attacker-driven route.)

When the plugin then replies, openchannel_hook_deserialize() (opening_control.c:768-860) runs with openingd == NULL and payload->uc freed, and unlike openchannel_hook_final() (721-733, `if (!openingd) return;`) it never checks:
- `{"result":"reject"}`: log_debug(openingd->ld->log, ...) at 796 dereferences NULL -> lightningd SIGSEGV;
- `continue` with `mindepth`: json_to_u32 writes payload->uc->minimum_depth into freed memory (839), then openingd->ld->log at 840 -> SIGSEGV;
- `continue` with `reserve`: tal(payload->uc, ...) and json_to_sat write into/under the freed uc (848-849), then openingd->ld->log at 850.
A plain `continue` (or `continue` with only `close_to` from the first plugin) reaches only the guarded final callback and is safe. `reject`, `mindepth` and `reserve` are documented replies (doc/schemas/hook/openchannel.json). The dual-funding deserializers openchannel2_hook_deserialize() and rbf_channel_hook_deserialize() (dual_open_control.c:721-733, 560) have the missing guard.

Precondition: a loaded plugin on the v1 `openchannel` hook whose reply is `reject` or carries `mindepth`/`reserve`. No shipped plugin takes this path by default: cln-lsps-client registers the hook (client.rs:117) but disables itself unless `experimental-lsps-client` is set (client.rs:121-124), and replies `mindepth: 0` only for a peer id recorded in the datastore as an LSP the operator requested a JIT channel from (client.rs:681-708), so with it enabled the LSP itself is the attacker position. Third-party channel-acceptor plugins that reject unsolicited opens (the common reason to use this hook) make any remote peer the attacker. Any plugin that performs an RPC round trip before answering leaves a window of several lightningd event-loop turns, and the attacker can retry at will; no funds or channel are needed.

Result: lightningd crashes (all channels, forwarding and RPC offline until restart); on the mindepth/reserve paths a u32 write and a tal allocation land in freed heap memory first.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:768–860](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L768-L860)
   openchannel_hook_deserialize() loads openingd = payload->openingd and never checks it for NULL; on `reject` it logs via openingd->ld->log (796): NULL dereference when openingd has been freed. This is where the fix belongs (the guard openchannel_hook_final() already has).
2. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:838–855](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L838-L855)
   On `continue` with `mindepth` or `reserve` it writes payload->uc->minimum_depth, allocates on payload->uc and writes payload->uc->reserve, then logs via openingd->ld->log. uc was freed with the uncommitted channel: write-after-free, then NULL dereference.
3. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:713–718](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L713-L718)
   openchannel_payload_remove_openingd(): destructor on the openingd subd that sets payload->openingd = NULL, documenting that openingd can die while the hook is pending.
4. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:721–732](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L721-L732)
   openchannel_hook_final() does check `if (!openingd) return;` — the intended handling of a dead daemon, applied only to the final callback and not to the deserializer.
5. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:889–907](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L889-L907)
   opening_got_offer(): payload holds raw openingd and uc pointers, the destructor is installed on openingd only (none on uc), and plugin_hook_call_openchannel() is asynchronous.
6. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:370–396](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L370-L396)
   plugin_hook_call_() steals the payload onto ph_req (child of hook->hooks), so the payload outlives openingd and uc; the plugin's later reply drives deserialize_cb with the stale pointers (plugin_hook_callback, 272-284).
7. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1919–1925](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1919-L1925)
   peer_connected() on a reconnect for a peer we already track calls peer_channels_cleanup(peer) to force subds out — the attacker-driven teardown of uc while the openchannel hook is still pending.
8. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:163–175](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L163-L175)
   peer_channels_cleanup() calls kill_uncommitted_channel(peer->uncommitted_channel, "Disconnected").
9. [lightningd/opening\_common.c:120–126](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_common.c#L120-L126)
   kill_uncommitted_channel() tal_free()s uc.
10. [lightningd/opening\_common.c:11–24](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_common.c#L11-L24)
   destroy_uncommitted_channel(): releases the openingd subd (payload->openingd becomes NULL via its destructor) while uc itself is being freed, leaving payload->uc dangling.
11. [lightningd/subd.c:928–935](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L928-L935)
   subd_release_channel() tal_free()s the openingd subd, running openchannel_payload_remove_openingd().
12. [connectd/connectd.c:319–325](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L319-L325)
   connectd peer_connected(): a new connection for a node id already present destroys the previous peer immediately ('on the assumption it's dead') and reports connectd_peer_reconnected (423-429); the remote peer controls this by dropping and re-establishing TCP.
13. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2398–2417](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2398-L2417)
   peer_disconnected() only marks PEER_DISCONNECTED and leaves subds running; a bare disconnect does not free uc, which is why the exploit uses the reconnect path.
14. [openingd/openingd.c:1036–1037](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L1036-L1037)
   openingd blocks in wire_sync_read on lightningd for the got_offer reply, so it does not observe the peer EOF during the hook; the hook stays pending until the plugin replies.
15. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:662–717](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs#L662-L717)
   Shipped cln-lsps-client registers the openchannel hook (117), performs RPC round trips before replying and returns `mindepth: 0` for a recorded LSP peer id — the uc write path. It is active only with `experimental-lsps-client` (121-124), so by default the precondition is a third-party acceptor plugin replying `reject`.
16. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:721–732](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L721-L732)
   openchannel2_hook_deserialize() begins with `if (!dualopend) { openchannel2_hook_cb(payload); return false; }`; rbf_channel_hook_deserialize() (560) has the same guard. The v1 deserializer is the only one in the opening path without it.

## Impact
Deterministic SIGSEGV of lightningd on the reject path (all channels, forwarding and RPC offline until restart): availability HIGH. On the mindepth/reserve paths a u32 and a tal child allocation are written into freed memory before the NULL dereference: heap corruption of the node process, bounded by the immediate crash (integrity LOW). No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote unauthenticated peer (Noise handshake only) sends open_channel, drops TCP and reconnects. connectd destroys the old connection immediately and lightningd's peer_connected() kills the uncommitted channel and openingd while the asynchronous openchannel hook is pending; the plugin's reject/mindepth/reserve reply then dereferences NULL openingd or writes to the freed uc. Window spans the plugin's deliberation (several event-loop turns for any plugin doing an RPC call); retries are free. AT:PRESENT because a loaded plugin on the v1 openchannel hook replying reject or setting mindepth/reserve is required and no shipped plugin does so by default (cln-lsps-client only with experimental-lsps-client, and only for the recorded LSP peer), and because the trigger is a timing race.

## Recommended fix
openchannel_hook_deserialize dereferences payload->openingd and payload->uc although the openingd destructor documents that the daemon (and with it uc) can be freed before the plugin replies; only the final callback checks. Fix criteria: After the uncommitted channel is torn down, no openchannel hook callback may touch openingd or uc: deserialize must return early (finishing the chain) when payload->openingd is NULL, and payload->uc must be invalidated when uc is freed (e.g. a destructor on uc, or deriving uc from the live openingd). Verify by sending open_channel, disconnecting and reconnecting before a slow openchannel-hook plugin replies with reject/mindepth/reserve: lightningd must stay up and drop the reply.

# Gossip-supplied DNS addresses are resolved synchronously in connectd: a channel peer stalls all peer I/O for hours

## Details
connectd resolves BOLT7 type-5 DNS address descriptors with a blocking getaddrinfo() inside its single-threaded event loop (connectd/connectd.c:1144; io_loop at 2605-2609), once per descriptor, while walking the address list of an outbound connection attempt (try_connect_one_addr, `goto next` at 1233-1235 advances to the next entry). The list is built by append_gossmap_addresses (186-264) from the target node's own node_announcement in gossip_store with no cap on the number of entries, and is walked on every reconnect of an 'important' peer (reconnect(), 836-848; backoff 1s..300s) and on every connect request lightningd sends (connect_to_peer, 2002), including startup reconnects (peer_control.c:3199) and the `connect` RPC.

A node_announcement is peer-authored. gossipd stores it after signature verification with any number of addresses (gossmap_manage.c:1190-1251); fromwire_wireaddr checks only hostname syntax (wireaddr.c:49-84, is_dnsaddr 401-444) and nothing bounds the descriptor count. A 65535-byte announcement carries ~2,700 descriptors of the form `<unique-label>.attacker.example` (or ~13,000 five-byte ones).

A peer that has a channel with the victim is 'important' once the channel is committed (channel.c:1004-1021: any post-lockin channel qualifies, remote-opened included, since reconnect and reconnect_private default true at lightningd.c:261-262), so connectd reconnects to it with gossip addresses after it disconnects (connect_control.c:530-548). Each getaddrinfo then blocks until the host resolver gives up (glibc stub defaults timeout 5s x attempts 2 per nameserver, or the recursive resolver's SERVFAIL after its own upstream timeout); distinct labels defeat negative caching. Thousands of names x several seconds is hours during which connectd services nothing: no BOLT8 reads/writes for any peer, no pings/pongs (remote peers drop us), channeld/lightningd writes to their connectd socketpairs back up undelivered, gossip and onion messages stop. HTLCs in flight cannot be forwarded, fulfilled or failed, so they time out and peers force-close. The stall repeats on every reconnect cycle the attacker provokes and at every restart.

Only --disable-dns (options.c:1628, turns the branch into the cheap 'dns disabled' skip at 1129-1134) or --always-use-proxy (hands DNS names to the Tor proxy at 1127) avoid the blocking call; both are off by default and the documentation describes disable-dns only as turning off DNS bootstrapping, not as a hardening requirement.

If the operator has set --autoconnect-seeker-peers (default 0), gossipd also asks lightningd to connect to random announced nodes (seeker.c:855-877, gossip_control.c:169-188), so any node with a public channel anywhere in the network can be the target without a channel to the victim.

Secondary amplification: every A/AAAA record returned is appended to connect->addrs (1156-1175) and each is later tried with a timed connect, so a cooperating resolver can also inflate the list and keep the connecting slot busy.

## Evidence
1. [connectd/connectd.c:1126–1177](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L1126-L1177)
   The DNS branch of try_connect_one_addr calls getaddrinfo() synchronously for each ADDR_TYPE_DNS entry in connect->addrs, then 'goto next' moves to the following entry. connectd is single-threaded (io_loop at 2605-2609): while getaddrinfo blocks, no peer socket, lightningd or gossipd message is serviced. There is no cap on how many DNS entries are walked and no timeout other than the system resolver's.
2. [connectd/connectd.c:186–263](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L186-L263)
   append_gossmap_addresses copies every IPv6/DNS, IPv4 and Tor-v3 descriptor from the target node's own node_announcement (read from gossip_store) into the connect list, with no limit on count. The peer authors this message.
3. [connectd/connectd.c:836–847](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L836-L847)
   reconnect(): for an important peer the backoff timer re-runs the connect with imp->addrs plus the gossmap addresses, so the attacker's descriptors are walked again on every reconnect cycle (1s..300s backoff, 850-882).
4. [connectd/connectd.c:1999–2004](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L1999-L2004)
   connect_to_peer appends the gossmap addresses to *every* connect request from lightningd (transient or not), so startup reconnects (peer_control.c:3199), `connect` RPC and gossipd seeker requests all walk the list.
5. [lightningd/connect\_control.c:530–547](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/connect_control.c#L530-L547)
   tell_connectd_peer_importance: as soon as a peer establishes a channel with us it becomes 'important' and connectd is told to (re)connect to it. Opening a channel to a node is permissionless for a remote peer, so this is the attacker's way into the reconnect path.
6. [common/wireaddr.c:49–83](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/wireaddr.c#L49-L83)
   fromwire_wireaddr accepts DNS descriptors with a 1..255 byte hostname validated only syntactically by is_dnsaddr (401-444: letters/digits/hyphen/dot/underscore, single-label names allowed). Nothing bounds the number of descriptors; a node_announcement (<=65535 bytes, 142 fixed bytes) holds ~13,000 five-byte DNS descriptors or ~2,700 with a 20-byte attacker-domain hostname.
7. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1190–1250](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1190-L1250)
   gossipd stores a node_announcement after fromwire_wireaddr_array parses and the signature verifies; it imposes no limit on the number or type of addresses, so the hostile announcement lands in gossip_store for connectd to read.
8. [lightningd/options.c:1014](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1014)
   use_dns defaults to true; only --disable-dns (1628) turns the branch into the cheap 'dns disabled' skip.
9. [gossipd/seeker.c:855–876](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/seeker.c#L855-L876)
   Secondary path: with --autoconnect-seeker-peers set (default 0, options.c:475) gossipd asks lightningd (gossip_control.c:169-188) to connect to a random announced node, so any node in the gossip graph, not only a channel peer, can be the target.

## Impact
connectd's event loop is blocked for hours: all peers' traffic stops, pings go unanswered so peers disconnect, channeld writes to connectd stall, HTLCs cannot be settled or failed and time out with on-chain force-close consequences. lightningd stays up but is cut off from the network. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a remote Lightning node with a committed channel to the victim (permissionless; lightningd then marks it important, connectd reconnects on disconnect). It signs and gossips a node_announcement with thousands of distinct DNS descriptors under a zone whose authoritative server never answers, then disconnects. On the victim, connectd.c:2002/843 pull those addresses from gossip_store and connectd.c:1144 calls getaddrinfo synchronously for each, blocking connectd's only thread for the resolver timeout per name. Default configuration (use_dns=true, reconnect=true) suffices; repeatable each reconnect cycle. Assumes the host libc resolver blocks several seconds per unanswered name (glibc resolv defaults timeout 5s, attempts 2).

## Recommended fix
try_connect_one_addr performs a blocking, untimed DNS resolution in connectd's single event loop for each gossip-supplied DNS descriptor, with no bound on how many such descriptors a peer's node_announcement may contribute. Fix criteria: Hostile node_announcement addresses must not be able to block connectd: cap the number of DNS (and total) descriptors taken from gossip per connect attempt to a small constant, and/or resolve asynchronously (helper process or non-blocking resolver) with a connectd-controlled timeout. Verify that a node_announcement with thousands of unresolvable hostnames leaves connectd responsive to other peers and lightningd throughout a reconnect attempt.
