# sendpay/sendonion: unbounded first-hop delay wraps cltv_expiry into the past; lightningd force-closes its own channel at the next block

## Details
send_onion() (lightningd/pay.c:786-796) sets the outgoing HTLC's absolute expiry to `get_network_blockheight()+1 + first_hop->delay` and passes it to send_htlc_out(). `delay` is supplied by the RPC caller: param_route_hop (sendonion first_hop, pay.c:1322, json_to_number, only `>= 1` enforced although the schema documents u16) and param_route_hops (sendpay route, pay.c:1465, json_to_u32, no bound). The addition is unsigned 32-bit and nothing checks the result, so delay = 2^32 - (height+1) + k wraps the sum to the small absolute height k, i.e. an HTLC that is already expired. Neither send_htlc_out()/new_htlc_out() (peer_htlcs.c:746-815; no cltv checks for am_origin HTLCs) nor channeld's add_htlc (full_channel.c:670, rejects only >= 500000000) notices: channeld commits the HTLC, sends update_add_htlc to the peer, and rcvd_htlc_reply() (peer_htlcs.c:720) puts the hout into ld->htlcs_out, where it stays until RCVD_REMOVE_ACK_REVOCATION (peer_htlcs.c:2187).

BOLT #2 requires an offering node to 'MUST NOT offer an HTLC with a timeout deadline before its cltv_expiry', and CLN enforces exactly that in its two sibling offering paths — injectpaymentonion (pay.c:2087-2106, 'never offer an expired HTLC; that's dumb') and forward_htlc (peer_htlcs.c:950-974) — but not in sendpay/sendonion.

The consequence is self-inflicted: htlcs_notify_new_block() (peer_htlcs.c:3026-3062), run on every new block, iterates all of ld->htlcs_out with no hstate filter and, for any hout with height >= cltv_expiry+1 whose channel is not already on-chain or errored, calls channel_fail_permanent(REASON_PROTOCOL, 'Offered HTLC ... hit deadline') -> drop_to_chain() (channel.c:1164). lightningd thus unilaterally closes its own channel at the first block after the wrapped HTLC is accepted by channeld, unless the peer has already failed the HTLC and the removal has been fully revoked.

Attacker: a rune bearer permitted `sendpay` or `sendonion` (commando, always on, or clnrest). Rune `pname`/`parr` restrictions are evaluated on top-level params only (lightningd/runes.c:862-895), so an operator cannot bound the nested route/first_hop `delay`; the only control the project offers for this caller is the method grant itself. The caller also picks the first-hop peer/channel (pay.c:1116 find_channel_for_htlc_add), so any channel of the node can be targeted. Two realisations: (1) first_hop is a peer the attacker controls, whose channeld accepts the expired HTLC (only the 500000000 check) and never fails it: the victim's next block force-closes that channel deterministically. (2) first_hop is an honest peer, which fails the HTLC (incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details / expiry_too_soon / malformed onion) after the commitment round trips; the attacker keeps fresh expired HTLCs (distinct payment hashes, up to max_accepted_htlcs) continuously in flight on that channel, so whenever the next block arrives an expired hout is present and the channel is closed. The victim pays the commitment/anchor fees if opener, has its balance locked for to_self_delay, and loses the channel; funds are not stolen since onchaind simply times the HTLC out.

What the bug adds beyond what a sendpay rune concedes: a bearer could already induce a BOLT-mandated force-close by routing an HTLC to a node it controls that stalls until the real deadline, but that needs the attacker's own channel/route, takes the full cltv delta (hours), and is the protocol's intended response to a stalled HTLC. The wrap gives an immediate, infrastructure-free unilateral close of any chosen channel for an HTLC the honest peer would have failed within seconds.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/pay.c:786–795](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L786-L795)
   send_onion() computes the outgoing HTLC's absolute expiry as `base_expiry + first_hop->delay` (unsigned int + u32, wraps mod 2^32) with no overflow, 'already expired' or max_htlc_cltv check and hands it to send_htlc_out(). This is the single offering path for sendpay (send_payment -> send_payment_core -> send_onion) and sendonion; the fix belongs here (or in send_htlc_out for am_origin HTLCs).
2. [lightningd/pay.c:1322–1324](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1322-L1324)
   param_route_hop (sendonion first_hop) parses delay with json_to_number into the u32 route_hop.delay and enforces only `>= 1`; doc/schemas/sendonion.json documents delay as u16 but nothing enforces an upper bound, so delay = 2^32 - base_expiry + k wraps the sum to k.
3. [lightningd/pay.c:1462–1468](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1462-L1468)
   param_route_hops (sendpay route) reads cltv_out/delay with json_to_u32 and applies no bound; a one-hop route to a direct peer with a wrapping delay reaches send_onion unchanged.
4. [lightningd/pay.c:2085–2106](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L2085-L2106)
   The sibling origin path injectpaymentonion refuses an HTLC whose cltv is <= current height ('never offer an expired HTLC; that's dumb') or > height + max_htlc_cltv, citing BOLT #2 'MUST NOT offer an HTLC with a timeout deadline before its cltv_expiry'. sendpay/sendonion are the only HTLC-offering entry points without this control.
5. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:950–974](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L950-L974)
   forward_htlc applies the same two checks (expiry_too_soon / expiry_too_far) before send_htlc_out for forwarded HTLCs, confirming the project treats offering an expired HTLC as a defect to be prevented.
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:746–814](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L746-L814)
   send_htlc_out() -> new_htlc_out() performs no cltv validation for an am_origin HTLC, sends channeld_offer_htlc to channeld, and rcvd_htlc_reply() (line 720) connect_htlc_out()s the hout into ld->htlcs_out as soon as channeld accepts it locally, before any commitment round trip.
7. [channeld/full\_channel.c:661–672](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L661-L672)
   channeld's add_htlc only rejects cltv_expiry >= 500000000 (blocks_to_abs_locktime); a cltv of 0 or any past height is accepted, committed and sent to the peer in update_add_htlc (channeld.c handle_offer_htlc).
8. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2184–2188](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2184-L2188)
   update_out_htlc keeps the hout in ld->htlcs_out until RCVD_REMOVE_ACK_REVOCATION (remove_htlc_out). Against an honest peer that fails the HTLC, the hout therefore remains for the full add/commit/revoke plus fail/commit/revoke exchange (several RTTs plus the peer's processing) — the window a new block must land in.
9. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:3026–3061](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L3026-L3061)
   htlcs_notify_new_block(), run on every block, iterates every hout in ld->htlcs_out with no hstate filter and calls channel_fail_permanent(REASON_PROTOCOL, 'Offered HTLC ... hit deadline') for any hout with height >= cltv_expiry + 1 (htlc_out_deadline, line 2952) whose channel is not already on-chain or errored; an HTLC offered with a past cltv trips this at the very next block.
10. [lightningd/channel.c:1160–1165](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1160-L1165)
   channel_fail_perm sets AWAITING_UNILATERAL and calls drop_to_chain(): lightningd broadcasts its own commitment transaction, unilaterally closing the channel over which it offered the expired HTLC.

## Impact
Each targeted channel is unilaterally closed by the victim itself (drop_to_chain): commitment and anchor fees if it is the opener, balance locked for to_self_delay, and the channel is gone until the operator funds and confirms a new one. Because the caller selects the first-hop peer/channel (pay.c:1116) and htlcs_notify_new_block fails every channel holding an expired hout, every channel of the node can be closed within one block interval, denying the node its Lightning function in a sustained way. No funds are stolen (the expired HTLC is timed out on-chain) and nothing is disclosed.

## Reproduction steps
1. A rune bearer with sendpay or sendonion rights submits the RPC over commando (default-on, any connected peer with a rune) or clnrest with route[0].delay / first_hop.delay chosen so base_expiry + delay wraps to a past height, and amount within what the rune and channel allow; the first-hop peer/scid is caller-chosen. channeld accepts (only the >= 500000000 check) and the hout enters ld->htlcs_out. With an attacker-controlled peer the next block force-closes deterministically; with an honest peer the attacker keeps expired HTLCs continuously in flight (distinct payment hashes) so an expired hout is present whenever the next block arrives — no race must be won and no non-default deployment setting is needed. Network vector (Lightning transport or HTTP), low complexity, no user interaction; privileges are the rune (PR:L), which is the project's intended bound on such callers.

## Recommended fix
send_onion() (used by both sendpay and sendonion) derives the outgoing cltv_expiry as base_expiry + caller-supplied u32 delay with wrapping arithmetic and offers the HTLC without the 'not already expired' and 'not beyond height + max_htlc_cltv' checks that injectpaymentonion and forward_htlc apply. Fix criteria: Before send_htlc_out() is called for a sendpay or sendonion origin HTLC (or centrally in send_htlc_out for am_origin HTLCs), reject with a JSON-RPC invalid-params error any first-hop delay for which base_expiry + delay overflows u32, yields a cltv <= the current block height, or exceeds height + max_htlc_cltv; verify that such a request returns an error, no channeld_offer_htlc/update_add_htlc is emitted, and no channel_fail_permanent follows at the next block.

# Dual-funding candidate spent in COMMIT_READY: NULL last_tx deref then use of deleted channel

## Details
A remote peer that opens a dual-funded channel to us (--experimental-dual-fund) can crash lightningd by getting its funding candidate mined and spent while we are still in DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY.

Flow: during interactive-tx completion dualopend sends dualopend_commit_ready; lightningd's wallet_commit_channel() persists the channel in DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY, creates the inflight with last_tx == NULL (new_inflight, channel.c:211) and, via channel_watch_inflight_outs(), installs a funding_spent() txowatch on the candidate outpoint (dual_open_control.c:1563-1668). dualopend then writes our commitment_signed to the peer and waits for theirs (dualopend.c:2374-2378). If the peer never sends commitment_signed but keeps the connection alive, lightningd stays in COMMIT_READY indefinitely (it is not channel_state_uncommitted, so it is not forgotten until the 2016-block fundee timeout), while the peer holds our signature on its commitment transaction.

If the peer funded every input of the candidate (the default when we are accepter with no funder contribution), it needs no tx_signatures from us: it broadcasts the funding tx, waits for confirmation, then broadcasts its commitment tx. When that confirms, filter_block_txs fires our txowatch: funding_spent() (peer_control.c:2738) finds the spent outpoint among channel->inflights and calls adopt_opening_candidate() -> update_channel_from_inflight(), which dereferences inflight->last_tx->psbt (2512-2515) with last_tx == NULL: lightningd SIGSEGVs.

Had that not crashed, the continuation is also unsound: onchaind_funding_spent() (onchain_control.c:1809) calls channel_fail_saw_onchain(); for a COMMIT_READY channel with no tx_signatures sent, channel_fail_perm() takes the open_uncommitted branch and delete_channel()s (channel.c:1146-1156), and onchaind_funding_spent() then reads/writes the freed channel (1812-1830: channel->scid, channel_record_open, channel_set_state). The sibling v1 path is safe because opening_fundee_finished commits straight to CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, which channel_fail_perm never deletes.

Attacker position: an ordinary remote peer following the protocol until it withholds one message; no subdaemon compromise. Cost: fees for two on-chain transactions; its own funds return via to_local. Precondition: our node runs with --experimental-dual-fund and accepts the open (default behaviour with that option). Impact: lightningd process dies (all channels, HTLC forwarding, RPC offline until the operator restarts it); repeatable with a fresh open each time. On restart the watch is not re-installed for COMMIT_READY channels (peer_control.c:3150-3153), so it is not a restart loop, but the channel row stays in COMMIT_READY and the spent candidate is never handled on-chain (no onchaind is ever started for it).

RBF variant: the same sink is reachable for an RBF candidate negotiated while the channel is DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN. wallet_update_channel() (dual_open_control.c:1284-1362) creates the RBF inflight with last_tx == NULL and installs channel_watch_inflight_outs() on it before the RBF commitment exchange completes; a peer that funds the RBF alone, receives our commitment_signed for it and withholds its own can mine and spend that candidate, and funding_spent() -> adopt_opening_candidate() dereferences the NULL last_tx exactly as above.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2738–2793](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2738-L2793)
   funding_spent() is the txowatch callback for every inflight outpoint. With no state check it calls adopt_opening_candidate() for a dual-funding candidate whose outpoint was spent (2757-2769), then wallet_insert_funding_spend() and onchaind_funding_spent() (2790-2793). Nothing excludes a channel still in DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY.
2. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2509–2512](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2509-L2512)
   update_channel_from_inflight() (called by adopt_opening_candidate) passes inflight->last_tx->psbt to bitcoin_tx_with_psbt() at 2511 with no NULL check. In COMMIT_READY the inflight was created by wallet_commit_channel and has never been given a commitment (last_tx == NULL, set only by inflight_set_last_tx from wallet_update_channel_commit on DUALOPEND_COMMIT_RCVD): NULL pointer dereference, lightningd SIGSEGV.
3. [lightningd/channel.c:177–211](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L177-L211)
   new_inflight() initialises inflight->last_tx = NULL (211); it is only set by inflight_set_last_tx(), reached from wallet_update_channel_commit() on DUALOPEND_COMMIT_RCVD, i.e. after the peer's commitment_signed has arrived.
4. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1560–1667](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1560-L1667)
   wallet_commit_channel(): on dualopend_commit_ready the channel is moved to DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY (1563), the inflight is created with no last_tx (1644), and channel_watch_inflight_outs() installs a funding_spent txowatch on the candidate outpoint 'from the moment the peer could broadcast it' (1666-1668). The watch is therefore live while the inflight has no commitment.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:2329–2394](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2329-L2394)
   Ordering: dualopend sends commit_ready and blocks for COMMIT_SEND_ACK (2329-2363), then peer_write()s OUR commitment_signed to the peer (2374-2375) and only then waits for the peer's commitment_signed (2378). A peer that withholds its commitment_signed leaves lightningd in COMMIT_READY while holding our signature on its commitment transaction.
6. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:1809–1831](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L1809-L1831)
   Second sink on the same trigger: onchaind_funding_spent() calls channel_fail_saw_onchain() and continues (channel->scid, channel->peer->ld, channel_record_open, channel_set_state at 1812-1830). For a COMMIT_READY channel channel_fail_perm() deletes the channel, so these are use-after-free accesses.
7. [lightningd/channel.c:1106–1165](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1106-L1165)
   channel_fail_perm(): for channel_state_open_uncommitted() (OPEN_INIT, OPEN_COMMIT_READY) with no tx_signatures sent, it delete_channel()s and returns (1146-1156) — the channel pointer held by onchaind_funding_spent is freed.
8. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:3150–3152](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L3150-L3152)
   On restart the inflight spend watch is not re-installed for COMMIT_READY channels ('Nothing to watch'), so the crash is one-shot per attempt rather than a restart loop; it bounds, not removes, the impact.
9. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1358–1361](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1358-L1361)
   RBF variant: wallet_update_channel() (channel in DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN) also creates the new RBF inflight with last_tx == NULL and immediately installs the funding_spent watch on its outpoint. The RBF commit_ready/commit_send_ack ordering is the same (dualopend.c:2990-3048), so a peer that withholds its RBF commitment_signed and mines+spends the RBF candidate reaches the same NULL dereference in adopt_opening_candidate; here channel_fail_perm would not delete the channel, but the crash happens first.

## Impact
Deterministic SIGSEGV of lightningd (or, on the alternate path, use-after-free of the deleted channel) terminates the node: every channel's HTLC handling, gossip and RPC stop until an operator restarts it; repeatable per attempt. No confidentiality impact. Integrity: the channel row is left in COMMIT_READY with its candidate spent on-chain and never reconciled by onchaind.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote peer opens a dual-funded channel funding all inputs, receives our commitment_signed, withholds its own while keeping the connection up, mines the funding tx, then mines its commitment tx spending the funding output. Our txowatch fires funding_spent() -> adopt_opening_candidate() -> update_channel_from_inflight() NULL deref. Requires only that we run --experimental-dual-fund (non-default) and accept the open; no compromise, no race.

## Recommended fix
funding_spent()/adopt_opening_candidate() assume every inflight has a commitment (last_tx) and that the channel survives channel_fail_saw_onchain(); neither holds for DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY, yet the candidate outpoint is watched in that state. Fix criteria: A spend of a candidate outpoint while the channel has no commitment for it must not dereference last_tx nor proceed into onchaind_funding_spent on a channel that channel_fail_perm will delete: either defer the spend watch until the inflight has a last_tx (COMMITTED), or in funding_spent()/onchaind_funding_spent() detect the uncommitted/no-last_tx case, fail-and-forget the channel and return DELETE_WATCH without touching it afterwards. Verify by replaying the described sequence on a dual-fund-enabled node: lightningd must stay up and log the forgotten channel.

# channeld splice_abort blocks forever on the peer's tx_abort echo (reachable from splice checks and from any channel_reestablish next_funding), bypassing the stfu timeout and starving lightningd

## Details
channeld's splice_abort() (channeld.c:2009-2058) is the NORETURN path used whenever channeld must abort a splice: it writes tx_abort and then loops on peer_read() until the peer echoes tx_abort, discarding everything else. The read has no timeout and runs inside a peer_in/req_in handler, so channeld's main loop - the only place timers expire and lightningd's pipe is read - is suspended for as long as the peer withholds the echo. The peer keeps the TCP/Noise link alive by sending pings, which connectd answers locally and counts as traffic (multiplex.c:803-824, 1537), so nothing on the victim side ever ends the wait.

Two peer-driven routes reach it:
1. Reestablish (no quiescence needed): on every reconnect, channel_reestablish's next_funding TLV is taken from the peer (6078); if we have no inflight and the txid is not our funding txid, channeld calls splice_abort("next_funding_txid not recognized.") (6147). Any peer with a channel can thus park channeld at reestablish, before the channel is operational, with a single TLV.
2. Splice checks (under quiescence): in a peer-initiated splice the peer's splice_init relative amount (4360-4367) and the inputs/outputs it adds feed check_balances(); 'splicing out more than its balance', 'did not provide enough', and the fee bounds (3565-3799) all call splice_abort, as does check_duplicate_inflight (2071). The same checks run on the initiator side (4767) against the peer's contributions. check_balances runs before channeld_add_inflight (4515), so nothing is persisted before the wait.

The operator's own `abort_channels` command (handle_abort_req, 5275) also ends in this wait, so the peer can veto the operator's splice-recovery path; only `disconnect` recovers.

What the park defeats: the 10-minute stfu_timer (296-298) that is CLN's designed bound on peer-held quiescence never fires; lightningd's channeld_fulfill_htlc/fail_htlc, channeld_send_shutdown (`close`, resolving only via its 48 h unilateral timeout), feerate and blockheight updates are never read while lightningd still reports the channel as connected and CHANNELD_NORMAL; committed HTLCs resolve only via lightningd's deadline force-close (peer_htlcs.c:3013-3110). lightningd's single watchdog - the 30 s htlc_offer_timeout that disconnects the peer (peer_htlcs.c:725-742, 796) - arms only when lightningd attempts a new outgoing HTLC on this channel, which a peer that holds all the liquidity (or a channel still in reestablish) never provokes. If the peer answers the tx_abort with a `warning`, splice_abort exit(0)s with no status message and lightningd sees only 'Owning subdaemon channeld died (0)' (subd.c:656).

The maintainers recognised the hazard at 4411-4418 and switched the feerate bound to a disconnect, but every other splice_abort caller still blocks. dualopend's open_abort (dualopend.c:351-380, 1717-1721) shows the non-blocking pattern: send tx_abort, return to the loop in an aborted mode, drop non-tx_abort messages. This is distinct from the verified record at channeld.c:4479 (synchronous interactive-tx / commitment_signed / tx_signatures waits during a splice): that record's waits and fix criteria do not include the tx_abort acknowledgement loop, and the reestablish route here needs no splice at all.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/channeld.c:2009–2057](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L2009-L2057)
   splice_abort(): writes tx_abort, then `do { msg = peer_read(); ... } while (fromwire_peektype(msg) != WIRE_TX_ABORT)` - a blocking wire_sync_read (common/peer_io.c:18-27) with no timeout, discarding every other message; the only other exit is a peer error/warning, on which it exit(0)s without any status to lightningd. The main loop (timers, MASTER_FD) is suspended for the duration.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:6133–6149](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6133-L6149)
   peer_reconnect(): remote_next_funding is taken straight from the peer's channel_reestablish TLV (line 6078, no feature gate); with no local inflight and a txid that is not the current funding txid, channeld calls splice_abort(peer, NULL, "next_funding_txid not recognized."). Any peer with a channel can trigger this at every reconnect - no quiescence, no splice negotiation, no option_splice usage - and the channel never finishes reestablish.
3. [channeld/channeld.c:3563–3579](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3563-L3579)
   check_balances(): a splice-out larger than the side's balance calls splice_abort; opener_relative is the peer's splice_init relative_satoshis, unchecked before this point.
4. [channeld/channeld.c:3743–3799](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3743-L3799)
   Fee-too-low / fee-too-high checks also route to splice_abort; the fee is computed from the inputs/outputs the peer added in the interactive-tx negotiation.
5. [channeld/channeld.c:4360–4367](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4360-L4367)
   splice_accepter(): fromwire_splice_init writes the peer's relative amount directly into peer->splicing->opener_relative; there is no magnitude check before check_balances.
6. [channeld/channeld.c:4479–4505](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4479-L4505)
   Accepter flow: interactive negotiation, then check_balances (4501) - before channeld_add_inflight (4515) - so nothing is persisted or signed before the blocking wait; the harm is the park, not state corruption.
7. [channeld/channeld.c:5271–5275](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L5271-L5275)
   handle_abort_req(): the operator's `abort_channels` RPC also lands in splice_abort, so the operator's own splice-recovery command is subject to the peer withholding its tx_abort echo; only `disconnect` recovers.
8. [channeld/channeld.c:4411–4418](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4411-L4418)
   Maintainers' own comment: 'splice_abort() blocks reading until it is [acked]: a peer that proposes a nonsense feerate and then goes silent would leave us parked in that read with the channel quiesced in STFU' - the hazard is acknowledged and avoided for the feerate bound only.
9. [channeld/channeld.c:259–299](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L259-L299)
   stfu_did_timeout()/the 10-minute stfu_timer (296-298) is CLN's designed bound on a peer holding the channel quiescent; it fires only via timers_expire() in the main loop.
10. [channeld/channeld.c:7271–7319](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L7271-L7319)
   Main loop: timers_expire() and MASTER_FD reads happen only here; a synchronous peer_read inside a handler suspends both, so the stfu timer never fires and lightningd's fulfill/fail/offer/shutdown/fee/blockheight requests sit unread.
11. [connectd/multiplex.c:803–823](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L803-L823)
   connectd hangs up only when the peer has been silent for 60 s and a probe ping went unanswered; last_recv_time is refreshed by any received message (line 1537), and the peer's own pings are handled locally (1046-1066) and never reach channeld, so the link stays up indefinitely.
12. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:725–741](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L725-L741)
   lightningd's only watchdog on channeld: a 30 s timer (armed at 796-798) on a newly offered HTLC that disconnects the peer if channeld does not reply. It arms only when lightningd tries to add an outgoing HTLC on this channel - which a peer holding all liquidity, or a channel still in reestablish, never provokes. Fulfill, fail, shutdown, fee and blockheight requests have no timer.
13. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:3013–3109](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L3013-L3109)
   With channeld parked, committed HTLCs are resolved only by lightningd's deadline force-close.

## Impact
The channel daemon for that channel is parked for as long as the peer chooses, invisibly (lightningd reports it connected and normal): the designed 10-minute quiescence bound is bypassed, no HTLC fulfil/fail, shutdown, fee or blockheight requests are processed, the operator's abort_channels is itself vetoed, committed HTLCs end in a deadline force-close, and in the reestablish route the channel never becomes operational. Scope is each channel the attacker holds with the victim; recovery needs the operator to notice and run `disconnect`. Nothing is persisted or signed before the wait, so no integrity or confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote peer with a channel (splicing default-on, options.c:1270). Route 1: on reconnect send channel_reestablish with a next_funding TLV carrying an arbitrary txid; channeld writes tx_abort and blocks (6147). Route 2: send stfu, then splice_init with relative_satoshis below minus its balance (or an underpaid interactive-tx), complete the negotiation; check_balances calls splice_abort and channeld blocks. In both, the peer never echoes tx_abort and keeps sending pings so connectd keeps the link. Default configuration, no shipped control to defeat, no victim interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. splice_abort() waits synchronously and without bound for the peer's tx_abort acknowledgement inside a message handler, suspending channeld's timers (including the stfu timeout) and its reading of lightningd's requests. Fix criteria: After sending tx_abort, channeld must return to its main loop (in an aborted mode that drops non-tx_abort peer messages, as dualopend's open_abort does) or bound the wait and warn/disconnect on expiry, and must report the abort outcome to lightningd on every exit including the peer-warning branch. Verify that a peer that triggers our tx_abort and then only pings results in channeld disconnecting within the stfu timeout, with lightningd's fulfill/fail/send_shutdown/abort requests still acted on.
2. peer_reconnect() handles an unrecognised next_funding txid with no local inflight by entering the blocking splice_abort path, so a single channel_reestablish TLV from any peer parks channeld before the channel is operational. Fix criteria: An unrecognised next_funding at reestablish must be answered without an unbounded wait (non-blocking abort or warn/disconnect), and reestablish must complete or fail within a bounded time regardless of what the peer sends afterwards.

# Peer-initiated splice runs entire negotiation in synchronous peer reads, defeating the stfu timeout

## Details
When a peer sends splice_init (or tx_init_rbf) to a quiescent channel, channeld handles the whole splice inside the peer_in call: splice_accepter() runs process_interactivetx_updates() (common/interactivetx.c read_next_msg loop), then resume_splice_negotiation() which waits for the peer's commitment_signed via peer_expect_msg_four() and for the peer's tx_signatures via peer_read() at line 4080. Each wait is a synchronous read with no timeout; the main loop, which is the only place timers expire and lightningd's pipe is read, is suspended throughout.

The peer controls when, and whether, each awaited message arrives. Quiescence is a protocol requirement for splicing, and CLN's defence against a peer holding the channel quiescent is the 10-minute stfu_timer (stfu_did_timeout -> warn+disconnect). Because the timer is never serviced while blocked, a peer that sends splice_init and then withholds the next tx_add_*/tx_complete, commitment_signed or tx_signatures (while answering connectd's pings) holds the channel quiescent and channeld parked indefinitely, something the design explicitly tries to prevent.

State around the waits: by the time the commitment and signature waits run, channeld_add_inflight has been persisted and hsmd told about the splice (4660-4713). In the sign-first case our tx_signatures are handed to lightningd (channel moves to CHANNELD_AWAITING_SPLICE) and to the peer before we block for theirs (4050-4080); the peer then holds a fully-signed splice it can broadcast at any time while our daemon cannot process `abort_channels`, `close`, HTLC fulfills/fails or fee updates. Reconnection does recover (peer_reconnect resumes via next_funding), so the persisted state is not itself dangerous; the defect is that a connected peer can choose to never let the wait end and CLN's timeout for that situation is inert.

Consequences while parked: lightningd requests are unread; pending HTLCs can only be resolved by lightningd's deadline force-close; `close` resolves after its 48 h unilateral timeout; the operator must notice and `disconnect`. The initiator-side waits (splice_initiator_user_finalized 4865, splice_initiator_user_signed 5085 -> same functions) have the same structure but require the operator to have started a splice.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/channeld.c:4479–4485](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4479-L4485)
   splice_accepter(): after replying splice_ack/tx_ack_rbf, process_interactivetx_updates() is called synchronously inside the peer_in handler for the peer's splice_init/tx_init_rbf; nothing else in channeld runs until the peer chooses to let it return.
2. [common/interactivetx.c:89–107](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/interactivetx.c#L89-L107)
   read_next_msg() loops on peer_read() (wire_sync_read, no timeout; common/peer_io.c:18-27), discarding unknown odd messages, and process_interactivetx_updates() (lines 509-520) keeps calling it until both sides have sent tx_complete.
3. [channeld/channeld.c:3159–3185](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3159-L3185)
   peer_expect_msg_four(): a bare peer_read() (line 3169) awaiting commitment_signed/tx_signatures/tx_abort, used by interactive_send_commitments() (3247-3262) called from resume_splice_negotiation().
4. [channeld/channeld.c:4050–4081](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4050-L4081)
   resume_splice_negotiation(): when we sign first, channeld_update_inflight and channeld_splice_sending_sigs are written to lightningd and our tx_signatures to the peer, then channeld blocks in peer_read() (line 4080) for the peer's tx_signatures.
5. [channeld/channeld.c:4515–4553](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4515-L4553)
   Accepter path: channeld_add_inflight is persisted via master_wait_sync_reply (4527) and hsmd updated (4547) before resume_splice_negotiation(peer, true, true, true, true, 0) (4553) enters the commitment and signature waits.
6. [channeld/channeld.c:307–309](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L307-L309)
   maybe_send_stfu(): the 10-minute stfu_timer (stfu_did_timeout -> peer_failed_warn, line 260-263) is CLN's bound on a peer holding the channel quiescent; it expires only via timers_expire() in the main loop (7284), which does not run while a handler is blocked in peer_read().
7. [channeld/channeld.c:4411–4421](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4411-L4421)
   The project's own comment: a peer that 'goes silent would leave us parked in that read with the channel quiesced in STFU' — the parked state is recognised as an outcome to avoid, so the surrounding synchronous reads are not intended design.
8. [connectd/multiplex.c:803–823](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L803-L823)
   send_ping(): connectd hangs up only when a ping goes unanswered; a peer that answers pings (or sends any traffic) keeps the connection, so channeld's wait is unbounded.
9. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:3539–3550](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L3539-L3550)
   Recovery requires the operator to notice and run `disconnect` with force=true (refused otherwise while the channel is in a peercomms state); lightningd has no timer on an in-progress splice.

## Impact
The channel daemon is parked for as long as the peer chooses: the channel is quiescent (no HTLC updates), lightningd's pipe is unread so `close`, HTLC fulfil/fail, fee and blockheight updates are not processed, and pending HTLCs resolve only via lightningd's deadline force-close (on-chain cost). Unlike a crash, nothing recovers automatically: the peer stays connected, so no reconnect occurs until the operator runs `disconnect force=true`. The persisted inflight and (sign-first case) released tx_signatures are recovered on reconnect via next_funding, so no integrity or confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A connected peer with a splice-capable channel (splicing default-on, options.c:1270) sends stfu; channeld replies stfu and arms the 10-minute stfu_timer; the peer sends splice_init and then withholds the next tx_add_*/tx_complete, commitment_signed or tx_signatures while answering connectd's pings. channeld is blocked in a synchronous peer_read() inside the peer_in handler so the timer is never serviced. Default configuration, no control to defeat, no victim interaction.

## Recommended fix
Splice negotiation steps (interactive-tx loop, commitment exchange, tx_signatures exchange) are implemented as unbounded synchronous peer reads inside a peer_in handler, so channeld's timers (notably the stfu timeout) and lightningd requests are not serviced. Fix criteria: A peer that stalls at any step of a splice must be bounded by the quiescence timeout: either drive the negotiation from the main loop so stfu_timer fires, or give the synchronous reads a deadline tied to the remaining stfu time and warn/disconnect on expiry. Verify that a peer withholding tx_complete, commitment_signed or tx_signatures (while pinging) results in a disconnect within the stfu timeout and that lightningd's channeld_abort/send_shutdown are acted on.

# Release builder images execute unpinned, unverified remote installers before producing signed release tarballs

## Details
The release tarballs that the project signs (SHA256SUMS-v<version>.asc from the cln@blockstream.com CI key in release-publish.yml, then co-signed by release captains after local reproduction) are produced inside builder images defined by contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.{jammy,noble,resolute} and contrib/docker/Dockerfile.builder.fedora. The documented security model (doc/getting-started/advanced-setup/repro.md:19,37-40,94-95) is a minimal trusted base built from the distribution's own installation media, explicitly rejecting Docker Hub images as 'yet another trusted third party', with the claim that verifying the Dockerfile is sufficient to trust the resulting builder image; release-checklist.md calls the Fedora output a 'reproducible Fedora image'.

The builder Dockerfiles nevertheless download and execute code whose content is chosen by the remote at build time, with no pinned revision and no checksum or signature:

- Ubuntu builders: `git clone https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv.git` at HEAD (noble:40, resolute:40, jammy:49) and then run its `pyenv install 3.10.0`, so whatever pyenv commit exists that day installs the Python that runs every code generator; `wget -qO- https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` (noble:50, resolute:50, jammy:60) installs the newest uv unchecked; `wget https://sh.rustup.rs -O rustup-install.sh && bash rustup-install.sh` (noble:52-55, resolute:52-55, jammy:62-65) runs an unpinned installer script (only the Rust toolchain version is pinned afterwards); jammy builds lowdown from a GitHub tag tarball with no hash (jammy:33-41).
- Fedora builder: `curl https://sh.rustup.rs | sh` (37), lowdown tarball without hash (41-49), `wget -qO- https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` (63), and a Bitcoin Core tarball placed in /usr/local with no SHA256SUMS/GPG verification (52-59) although the main Dockerfile (35-42) verifies the same artefact.

Everything else in the build is pinned: apt packages are checksummed in tools/repro-build*.sh, Python dependencies by uv.lock hashes, crates by Cargo.lock checksums, the Rust toolchain by version. The installers and pyenv are the unverified gap, and they run as root in the image that then compiles lightningd, the subdaemons and the Rust plugins.

These fetches happen at exactly the moment the signed artefacts are produced: release-build.yml:56-61 builds the cl-repro images on a fresh runner for every tag push, tools/build-release.sh:210 builds the Fedora image with --no-cache, and contrib/cl-repro.sh:30 builds the release captain's and co-signers' images with --no-cache. A compromise of astral.sh, static.rust-lang.org/sh.rustup.rs, the pyenv or lowdown GitHub repositories (or the GitHub archive endpoint), or bitcoincore.org during a release window therefore lands in the signed tarballs. Reproducibility is the intended detector, but because every reproducer follows the same Dockerfile and fetches current content, a poisoned upstream served during the window reproduces 'successfully' and attracts additional signatures; the repro.md statement that verifying the Dockerfile suffices does not hold while its effect depends on remote state.

(The Fedora builder's `dnf update -y` fetches GPG-signed packages and is a reproducibility, not an integrity, issue; it is not part of this finding.)

## Evidence
1. [contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.noble:40–55](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.noble#L40-L55)
   Builder image clones pyenv at HEAD (no commit pin) and runs its `pyenv install`, then `wget -qO- https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` (whatever installer astral.sh serves that day, no checksum) and `wget https://sh.rustup.rs -O rustup-install.sh && bash rustup-install.sh` (unpinned installer script; only the toolchain version 1.85 is pinned afterwards). All run as root in the image that compiles the release. Dockerfile.resolute lines 40-55 are identical.
2. [contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.resolute:40–55](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.resolute#L40-L55)
   Identical unpinned pyenv HEAD clone, uv installer and rustup-init script for the Ubuntu 26.04 release tarball.

   lowdown is fetched as a GitHub-generated tag tarball with no hash or signature check and then `./configure && make && make install` executes its build scripts as root.

   `curl https://sh.rustup.rs | sh` runs the unpinned rustup installer script as root (toolchain 1.92.0 is pinned, the installer is not).

   lowdown tag tarball fetched without any hash and built/installed as root.

   `wget -qO- https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` installs the current uv with no checksum; uv then drives `uv venv`/`uv pip install`/`uv run make` for the whole Fedora build (tools/build-release.sh:19-24).
8. [contrib/docker/Dockerfile.builder.fedora:51–59](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/docker/Dockerfile.builder.fedora#L51-L59)
   Bitcoin Core binaries are installed into /usr/local/bin and /usr/local/lib with no SHA256SUMS or GPG check, unlike the main Dockerfile (lines 35-42) which verifies the same artefact against contrib/keys/bitcoin. Lower significance: the release build does not execute bitcoind, so this is an unverified binary in the builder rather than a direct path into the tarball.
9. [contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.noble:64–76](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.noble#L64-L76)
   The image CMD runs `uv sync` and tools/repro-build*.sh on the toolchain installed above and copies the resulting clightning-*.tar.xz into /repo/release*, the directory the project signs.
10. [.github/workflows/release-build.yml:50–73](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/.github/workflows/release-build.yml#L50-L73)
   On every release tag push the workflow debootstraps a base and runs `docker build ... < contrib/reprobuild/Dockerfile.<dist>` on a fresh runner, so every remote fetch above happens at release time, then runs tools/build-release.sh; release-publish.yml:41-63 then signs the resulting SHA256SUMS with the project key and uploads them to the GitHub release draft.
11. [tools/build-release.sh:204–213](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/build-release.sh#L204-L213)
   bin-Fedora builds Dockerfile.builder.fedora with --no-cache at release time (CI and release captain alike), so its fetches are repeated for every release, and runs the build inside it.
12. [contrib/cl-repro.sh:30](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/cl-repro.sh#L30)
   Release captains and co-signers create their cl-repro-<dist> images with --no-cache from the same Dockerfiles (release-checklist.md:34,52,70,122), so independent reproducers fetch the same current remote content rather than a pinned one; a poisoned upstream served during the release window reproduces identically and attracts co-signatures.
13. [doc/getting-started/advanced-setup/repro.md:37–40](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/getting-started/advanced-setup/repro.md#L37-L40)
   The documented model: base built from OS installation media because Docker Hub would be 'yet another trusted third party'. Lines 94-95 state 'Verifying the Dockerfile therefore is sufficient to ensure that the resulting cl-repro-<codename> image is reproducible', which does not hold while the Dockerfile's effect depends on unpinned remote state.

## Impact
Arbitrary root code in the builder can alter lightningd, subdaemons and all plugins placed in the release tarballs that the project then signs with its CI key; co-signers rebuilding from the same Dockerfiles in the same window confirm the poisoned result. No pipeline secrets are present inside the builder containers (GPG keys live in the separate release-publish job), so confidentiality and availability of the pipeline are not affected beyond a failed build. Subsequent-system impact: Users who download the signed tarballs from the GitHub release and install them per installation.md run the trojaned node with full access to hsm_secret, wallet and channel funds.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker position: control over content served by any unpinned upstream (astral.sh install.sh, sh.rustup.rs/static.rust-lang.org rustup-init, pyenv GitHub HEAD, lowdown tag tarball, bitcoincore.org tarball) during a release window; HTTPS is used, so a network MITM would additionally need a CA-level position. Delivery: serve modified content when release-build.yml, tools/build-release.sh bin-Fedora or contrib/cl-repro.sh rebuilds the builder image (all do so fresh/--no-cache). The code executes as root in the build container and shapes every emitted binary, which release-publish.yml then signs and uploads. No privileges on the CLN project are required.

## Recommended fix
1. Builder images fetch and execute installers, a git clone and source tarballs whose content is chosen by the remote at image-build time, with no pinned revision or checksum, violating the documented 'verifying the Dockerfile is sufficient' integrity model. Fix criteria: Every remote artefact the builder executes (pyenv, uv, rustup-init, lowdown, Bitcoin Core) is fetched at an explicit version and verified against a checksum or signature committed in this repository (or replaced by a distribution package from the frozen release pocket, as the Ubuntu images already do for lowdown). Verify: a change in any remote artefact makes the builder image build fail rather than silently differ.
2. The Fedora builder, whose output is signed and described as reproducible, installs its toolchain from unpinned installers and an unverified Bitcoin Core tarball, unlike the main Dockerfile which GPG-verifies the same tarball. Fix criteria: The Fedora builder verifies every download it installs (Bitcoin Core via SHA256SUMS + GPG against contrib/keys/bitcoin, installers by pinned version and checksum). Verify: two Fedora builder images built from the same commit on different days install byte-identical toolchains, and a tampered download aborts the build.

# Official Docker image build clones the VLS signer by mutable git tag and runs unpinned uv/rustup installers as root

## Details
The multi-stage Dockerfile that produces the official `elementsproject/lightningd:<version>`, `:<version>-vls` and `:latest[-vls]` images (release.yml on every release tag or dispatch → docker-build.yml pushes by digest with Docker Hub credentials → docker-publish.yml tags; also `tools/build-release.sh docker`, release-checklist.md step 13/14) pulls executable code from remote sources with no integrity binding in this repository:

1. Dockerfile:206 clones the Validating Lightning Signer with `--branch ${VLS_VERSION}` (`ARG VLS_VERSION=v0.14.0`, line 184) from gitlab.com. A tag is a mutable label: no commit hash, tag signature or tarball checksum is checked, so whoever can change what GitLab serves for that tag (the VLS project owners, a compromised maintainer account, or GitLab itself) chooses the source that becomes `remote_hsmd_socket`. Line 220 compiles it with `cargo build --release` without `--locked` (CLN's own builds use `--locked`, Makefile:388), so an absent or inconsistent Cargo.lock in the fetched tree is silently re-resolved. Line 272 ships the result in the `-vls` image, and docker-images.md:165-193 tells operators to run it as the hsmd replacement — a root process inside the node container that fronts every signing request. This is the only shipped third-party source the project does not bind: submodules are fetched at gitlink commit hashes (line 154) and bitcoin-cli is GPG-verified against committed keys (lines 35-42).

2. Dockerfile:64-65 `ADD https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh` / `ADD https://sh.rustup.rs` fetch installer scripts without `--checksum=` (available in the declared `dockerfile:1.7-labs` syntax) or a version, and lines 143-144 / 203-204 execute them as root in the stages that build every binary of both images; no Rust toolchain version is requested (the Fedora builder pins 1.92.0 at contrib/docker/Dockerfile.builder.fedora:37). Docker ADD and git over HTTPS authenticate the host, not the content: a modified script served by the script host (the Codecov-uploader pattern) runs with full control of the build. A committed checksum would close that script-host vector and make any upstream change fail loudly; it would not, by itself, remove the project's reliance on static.rust-lang.org / astral's GitHub releases for the binaries the scripts download, which is why this part is secondary to the VLS clone.

In either case the attacker's code lands in the official image's binaries with no reproducible-build cross-check (repro builds cover tarballs, not Docker images) and nothing a reviewer of this Dockerfile could compare against. Operators who follow installation.md (`docker pull elementsproject/lightningd:latest` / `:v26.06.6`) then run it with their node database, RPC authority and, for `-vls`, the signer proxy.

## Evidence
1. [Dockerfile:206](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L206)
   `git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLS_VERSION} https://gitlab.com/lightning-signer/validating-lightning-signer.git` fetches the Validating Lightning Signer source by tag name. A git tag is mutable; no commit hash, tag signature or tarball checksum is checked, so nothing in this repository binds what is compiled. TLS authenticates gitlab.com, not the content.
2. [Dockerfile:184](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L184)
   `ARG VLS_VERSION=v0.14.0` is the only pin: a tag label. docker-build.yml passes no VLS_VERSION build-arg, so every release build resolves this label against whatever GitLab serves at build time.
3. [Dockerfile:220–226](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L220-L226)
   VLS is built with plain `cargo build --release` (no `--locked`, unlike CLN's own CARGO_OPTS at Makefile:388), so if the fetched tree's Cargo.lock is absent or inconsistent cargo silently re-resolves dependencies; the output tree is stripped into /tmp/vls_install.
4. [Dockerfile:272](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L272)
   The resulting `remote_hsmd_socket` is copied into the published lightningd-vls-signer image at /var/lib/vls/bin/, where the docs tell operators to run it as the hsmd replacement (`--subdaemon=hsmd:/var/lib/vls/bin/remote_hsmd_socket`), i.e. inside the node container as root, in the path of every signing request.
5. [Dockerfile:64–65](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L64-L65)
   `ADD --chmod=750 https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh` and `ADD --chmod=750 https://sh.rustup.rs` fetch installer scripts with no `--checksum=` (supported by the declared `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7-labs` frontend) and no version in the URL; whatever the script hosts serve at build time is what runs.
6. [Dockerfile:143–144](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L143-L144)
   The fetched scripts execute as root in the `builder` stage that produces every binary of both published images (`uv run make install-program`, and the Rust toolchain that compiles cln-grpc, clnrest, lsps, wss-proxy, bip353, currencyrate). No toolchain version is requested either (contrast contrib/docker/Dockerfile.builder.fedora:37, which pins `--default-toolchain 1.92.0`).
7. [Dockerfile:203–204](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L203-L204)
   The same unpinned scripts are executed again as root in the `vls-builder` stage before VLS is compiled.
8. [Dockerfile:35–42](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L35-L42)
   Contrast: bitcoin-cli, the other third-party binary shipped in the image, is verified via SHA256SUMS + GPG against keys committed in contrib/keys/bitcoin, showing build-time downloads are treated as a threat and that a repository-bound trust anchor is the project's standard.
9. [Dockerfile:153–154](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/Dockerfile#L153-L154)
   Contrast: the project's other third-party source (submodules) is fetched at gitlink commit hashes bound to this repository's history; VLS is the one shipped third-party source with no such binding.
10. [.github/workflows/docker-build.yml:63–75](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/.github/workflows/docker-build.yml#L63-L75)
   On every release (release.yml: tag push or workflow_dispatch, `secrets: inherit`) this Dockerfile is built for targets `lightningd` and `lightningd-vls-signer` on three platforms and pushed by digest to the dh-repository-owner/lightningd repository with DOCKER_USERNAME/DOCKER_PASSWORD.
11. [.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:66–76](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml#L66-L76)
   The pushed digests are then tagged `elementsproject/lightningd:<version>` / `:<version>-vls` and, for non-rc tags, `:latest` / `:latest-vls` — the tags installation.md tells users to pull.
12. [doc/contribute-to-core-lightning/docker-images.md:165–193](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/contribute-to-core-lightning/docker-images.md#L165-L193)
   The project's own documentation directs operators to the `-vls` image flavour "which comes with pre-built remote_hsmd_socket binaries" and to start lightningd with `--subdaemon=hsmd:/var/lib/vls/bin/remote_hsmd_socket`, establishing that the unpinned VLS build is the shipped signer proxy, not an unused artefact.

## Impact
The vulnerable system is the CLN Docker release pipeline. Attacker code runs as root inside the image build and can alter every binary copied into the published images (lightningd, all plugins, remote_hsmd_socket): integrity HIGH. Under the docker-container buildx driver the RUN steps do not see the runner's Docker Hub login, so pipeline secrets are not read: confidentiality NONE. Breaking the build is possible but incidental: availability NONE. Subsequent-system impact: Operators who pull the published tags (installation.md:30-37; docker-images.md:165-193 for -vls) run the trojaned lightningd / plugins / signer proxy as root in the node container with the node database, RPC socket and, for -vls, the hsmd signing path: full compromise of node confidentiality, integrity (funds) and availability.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker position: a party able to change what gitlab.com serves for the VLS tag v0.14.0 (VLS maintainers, a compromised maintainer account or GitLab), or what astral.sh / sh.rustup.rs serve as installer scripts. Delivery: move the tag or alter the script, then wait for the next release build (release.yml fires on every version tag push and on workflow_dispatch, `secrets: inherit`), which fetches the content over TLS — authenticating the host but checking nothing against this repository — executes/compiles it as root in the builder, and pushes the image to Docker Hub. No privileges on the CLN repository and no action by the eventual victim are needed; the one precondition outside the attacker's control is the upstream compromise, rated as AT:P. The threat model names curl|sh installers in build images and the Docker release pipeline as in-scope supply-chain surface.

## Recommended fix
1. The VLS signer source is fetched by a mutable git tag and built without a locked dependency set, so nothing in this repository binds the code shipped as remote_hsmd_socket. Fix criteria: Fetch VLS at an explicit commit hash (or verify the tag's signature against a VLS release key committed under contrib/keys, or verify a release tarball against a committed SHA256), and build it with `cargo build --locked`. Verify: moving the upstream tag does not change the built remote_hsmd_socket, and a missing or mismatched Cargo.lock aborts the build.
2. The uv and rustup installer scripts are downloaded and executed as root without a pinned version or checksum, and no toolchain version is requested. Fix criteria: Pin the uv and rustup-init versions and verify them with `ADD --checksum=sha256:...` (or sha256sum against values committed in the repo), or install rustup-init / uv binaries whose SHA256 is recorded in the repository, and request an explicit Rust toolchain version as the Fedora builder already does. Verify: any change in the remote script or binary content causes the build to fail.

# pyln plugin loop exits on rune-bearer params lightningd forwards but Python json.loads rejects

## Details
pyln-client's Plugin.run() loop (contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:937-951) splits stdin on '\n\n' and hands each frame to _multi_dispatch(), which calls json.loads(payload.decode('utf8')) at line 829 with no exception handling; run() has none either, so any exception from the decoder unwinds past plugin.run() and the plugin process exits with a traceback. lightningd is the trusted writer of that channel, but the params object of a JSON-RPC request is relayed byte-for-byte from the remote caller: after checkrune succeeds, commando's execute_command() (plugins/commando.c:286-289) re-emits each member of the peer's params with json_add_jsonstr(json_tok_full(...)); lightningd's parser (common/json_parse_simple.c) validates only UTF-8 in strings, token structure and nesting depth <= 256, never primitive length; checkrune (lightningd/runes.c:861-893) caches params by name without inspecting values; and for a plugin-owned method plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch() (lightningd/plugin.c:1346) forwards the whole request via json_stream_forward_change_id() (plugin.c:1187-1212), which copies everything except the id. Independently, parse_request() builds the rpc_command hook payload from the raw request (jsonrpc.c:1108-1125, serialised by json_add_tok memcpy at 799-816) and delivers it to every plugin hooking rpc_command before the target command parses any parameter.

CPython's json module converts integer literals with int()/PyLong_FromString, which since 3.10.7/3.11.0 raises ValueError ('Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion') for base-10 literals longer than sys.get_int_max_str_digits() (default 4300). pyproject requires Python >= 3.10. A single commando custom message (<= 65535 bytes; multi-part up to 1 MB, commando.c:458) such as {"method":"summary","params":{"x":111...(4301+ digits)},"id":1,"rune":...} therefore passes checkrune (unless a pname rule names that key), is forwarded unchanged by commando and lightningd, and makes json.loads() raise in the plugin before dispatch. The plugin exits and lightningd does not restart it: its RPC methods, hooks (htlc_accepted, invoice_payment, ...) and subscriptions are lost until the operator intervenes. If the operator started it with important-plugin, lightningd itself exits (lightningd/plugin.c:297-302, lightningd_exit).

Two routes exist for a rune bearer: (a) the rune permits a method implemented by a pyln-client plugin (the documented readonly rune, doc/schemas/createrune.json:208, includes method=summary); or (b) the rune permits any method at all and some pyln plugin registers the rpc_command hook. clnrest and cln-grpc are not vectors (serde_json / protobuf typing reject the literal); commando is. No builtin plugin is written in Python, so the vulnerable system is any third-party plugin built on the published pyln-client package.

Dependency assumptions: (1) CPython >= 3.10.7 / 3.11 with the default int_max_str_digits of 4300 (not disabled via PYTHONINTMAXSTRDIGITS/sys.set_int_max_str_digits); interpreters 3.10.0-3.10.6 lack the limit and are not affected. (2) jsmn (external/jsmn, submodule absent from this checkout) tokenizes a primitive up to the next delimiter with no length bound, as lightningd's own use of multi-megabyte requests relies on. This is distinct from the verified record checkrune-pname-raw-key-first-duplicate-vs-plugin-decoding (authorisation divergence on duplicate keys at runes.c:861) and from pyln-plugin-traceback-in-error-reply-to-rune-bearers (information disclosure in error replies at plugin.py:146).

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:829](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L829)
   _multi_dispatch() decodes every frame from lightningd with json.loads(payload.decode('utf8')) outside any try/except; the stdlib decoder converts integer literals with int(), which raises ValueError for literals longer than sys.get_int_max_str_digits() (default 4300) on CPython >= 3.10.7/3.11. The exception propagates to the caller. This is the primary fix location.
2. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:937–951](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L937-L951)
   run() is the only read loop; it has no exception handling, so the ValueError from _multi_dispatch terminates run() and the plugin process exits with a traceback. lightningd does not restart a dead plugin.
3. [plugins/commando.c:272–317](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L272-L317)
   After checkrune succeeds, execute_command() re-emits each member of the peer's params object or array verbatim with json_add_jsonstr(json_tok_full(...), json_tok_full_len(...)), so a 4301+-digit number literal supplied by the rune bearer is forwarded unchanged into the request sent to lightningd. try_command() (lines 371-429) only requires params to be an object or array and passes them to checkrune with json_add_tok.
4. [lightningd/plugin.c:1316–1351](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1316-L1351)
   For a plugin-owned method, plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch() performs no param() parsing and forwards the whole request with json_stream_forward_change_id(), so the literal reaches the Python plugin's stdin exactly as the peer wrote it.
5. [lightningd/plugin.c:1187–1212](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1187-L1212)
   json_stream_forward_change_id() copies the request buffer from toks->start to toks->end with json_stream_append, replacing only the id token; no member is re-encoded or bounded.
6. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1108–1125](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L1108-L1125)
   parse_request() duplicates the raw request into the rpc_command hook payload and calls plugin_hook_call_rpc_command() after only method lookup, filter parsing and deprecation checks, before the target command parses any parameter; a pyln plugin hooking rpc_command therefore receives the literal for ANY method the rune permits, not only its own.
7. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:799–815](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L799-L815)
   rpc_command_hook_serialize() copies every member of the raw request into the hook payload with json_add_tok(), which memcpy's the token's full bytes (common/json_stream.c:393-404), preserving the oversized literal.
8. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L302)
   When the dead plugin was started with important-plugin, plugin_conn_finish's death handler logs 'Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(), so the rune bearer's request takes the whole node down in that configuration; otherwise only the plugin's methods, hooks and subscriptions are lost.

## Impact
The vulnerable system is the pyln-client-based plugin process, which terminates and is not restarted by lightningd: total loss of its RPC methods, hooks (e.g. htlc_accepted, invoice_payment) and subscriptions until the operator intervenes, repeatable at will. If the operator registered it with important-plugin, lightningd exits as well (plugin.c:297-302), with on-chain consequences for a Lightning node. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer holding an operator-issued rune (PR:L) that permits either a method served by a pyln-client plugin (the documented readonly rune includes method=summary) or, when a pyln plugin hooks rpc_command, any method at all. Over the always-on commando channel (AV:N) they send one custom message whose params object carries an integer literal of 4301+ digits (fits in a single 65535-byte message). checkrune passes, commando and lightningd forward the raw bytes, and json.loads() in the plugin raises a ValueError nothing catches; the plugin exits. Deterministic, no race or environmental precondition beyond the vulnerable component being present (AT:N, AC:L), no user interaction. The rune's method scope is the attacker's privilege, not an attack requirement.

## Recommended fix
1. The stdin frame parser treats every byte lightningd relays as well-formed for Python's decoder and lets a decode failure escape the dispatch loop, although request params originate from remote RPC callers. Fix criteria: A frame that json.loads() cannot decode must not terminate the plugin: the loop must catch decode errors (ValueError/RecursionError/UnicodeDecodeError), log them and, when an id can be recovered, answer with a JSON-RPC parse error. Verify by sending a plugin method call whose params contain a 5000-digit integer literal via commando and confirming the plugin stays alive and returns an error.
2. lightningd forwards remote-caller params to plugins without bounding number literal length, so a value lightningd itself never interprets can be weaponised against the plugin's decoder. Fix criteria: Requests relayed to plugins (plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch and the rpc_command hook) should reject or bound primitive token lengths beyond what any consumer can decode, or commando should refuse such params before checkrune. Verify that the request above is refused with an error before reaching the plugin.

# Crash log fallback writes predictable /tmp path without O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW

## Details
On any lightningd crash (fatal() -> abort(), failed assert, SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL/SIGFPE) the crashdump signal handler (common/daemon.c:78-90) calls bt_exit = log_backtrace_exit(), which dumps the whole in-memory log book to a file. It first opens `crash.log.<YYYYmmddHHMMSS>` relative to the cwd, which lightningd set to the 0700 config netdir at options.c:1875. If that open fails, it falls back to `/tmp/lightning-crash.log.<YYYYmmddHHMMSS>` opened with `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0600` and no O_EXCL, no O_NOFOLLOW and no mkstemp (lightningd/log.c:1117-1119), although the project already uses mkstemp (common/utils.c:227 tmpdir_mkstemp, lightningd/configs.c:450) and O_CREAT|O_EXCL (options.c:1370 hsm_secret, plugin.c:2665) for every other file it creates where another party might pre-create the name.

The name is predictable to the second and the directory is world-writable, so an unprivileged local user on the same host can blanket upcoming seconds (one directory entry per second is cheap) with:
- regular files they own with mode 0666: open() on an existing file ignores the 0600 creation mode, O_TRUNC empties it, and the whole log book is written into an attacker-readable file;
- symlinks: lightningd follows them and truncates/overwrites any file the lightningd uid can write (e.g. lightningd.sqlite3 in the lightning-dir; when run as root, anything), filling it with log text.

What is dumped: log_dump_to_file writes every ring-buffer entry. The 16 MiB ring (RING_BITS 24) stores every entry regardless of the configured --log-level: logv() and log_io() call add_entry() unconditionally (log.c:690-692, 728-729), and the IO callers at jsonrpc.c:1150/1197 and plugin.c:711 are ungated, so the dump contains raw JSON-RPC requests/responses and plugin traffic at any log level. The maintainers' own comment at log.c:1235-1238 says that IO traffic contains secrets such as runes and refuses to serve it through getlog; RPC responses also carry payment preimages, invoice data and any recent exposesecret output.

Preconditions: (1) the primary open in the config netdir must fail — realistic organic causes are EROFS after an ext4 errors=remount-ro event or inode/space exhaustion on the lightning-dir filesystem (both of which also make sqlite writes fail and so themselves fatal() lightningd), and a co-tenant sharing that filesystem without quotas can induce inode exhaustion; (2) a crash, which the attacker can wait for, induce via (1), or trigger through peer-reachable fatal() paths recorded in this scan. Deployment conditions, stated as assumptions: the shipped systemd unit (contrib/init/lightningd.service) sets PrivateTmp=true, which isolates /tmp under that unit only; tarball, nix, manual and macOS runs have no such isolation. On Linux the regular-file variant is blocked where fs.protected_regular>=1 and the symlink variant where fs.protected_symlinks=1 (kernel defaults are 0; systemd-based distributions usually enable both); macOS has no equivalent. The finding holds wherever lightningd runs on a multi-user host without those isolations.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/log.c:1112–1126](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L1112-L1126)
   When the primary open of crash.log.<timestamp> in the cwd (the 0700 config netdir) fails, log_backtrace_exit falls back to /tmp/lightning-crash.log.<YYYYmmddHHMMSS> opened with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC and no O_EXCL or O_NOFOLLOW, then dumps the entire log book into whatever that path resolves to. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [lightningd/log.c:1082–1097](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L1082-L1097)
   log_dump_to_file writes every ring-buffer entry to the opened fd. The ring stores all entries regardless of the configured print level (add_entry is unconditional in logv at log.c:690-692 and in log_io at log.c:728-729), so the dump includes DEBUG lines and raw RPC/plugin IO traffic at any --log-level.
3. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1193–1197](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L1193-L1197)
   Every byte read from an RPC connection is passed to log_io unconditionally (likewise responses at jsonrpc.c:1150 and plugin traffic at plugin.c:711), so raw JSON-RPC traffic — which log.c:1235-1238 says may contain runes and which getlog refuses to serve — is in the ring buffer that the crash dump writes.
4. [common/daemon.c:78–106](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/daemon.c#L78-L106)
   crashdump is installed for SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/SIGBUS/SIGILL/SIGFPE and calls bt_exit (= log_backtrace_exit in lightningd via daemon_setup at daemon.c:177), so every fatal()/assert()/abort() path in lightningd reaches the dump code, including peer-triggerable fatal() paths recorded in this scan.
5. [lightningd/options.c:1875–1889](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1875-L1889)
   lightningd chdirs into the 0700 config netdir, so the primary crash.log open normally lands inside the protected directory; the /tmp fallback is reached only when that open fails (EROFS, ENOSPC/inode exhaustion, EDQUOT, permission change). This bounds the precondition and shows the project's intended control for the crash log is the 0700 directory, which the fallback bypasses.

## Impact
Confidentiality: the whole 16 MiB log book is written into an attacker-readable file; because add_entry is unconditional the dump includes raw JSON-RPC and plugin IO traffic at any configured log level — rune strings (which log.c:1235-1238 names as secrets and getlog refuses to serve), payment preimages and invoice data in RPC responses, peer ids and channel/payment activity — material a local user can turn into RPC authority via a leaked rune on clnrest when enabled. Integrity: via a symlink the dump truncates and overwrites any file writable by the lightningd uid, including lightningd.sqlite3 (channel state) and, when run as root, hsm_secret. Availability: a node whose database was overwritten with log text cannot restart until the operator restores a backup, an interruption beyond the crash that already occurred.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is an unprivileged local user on the lightningd host who is not the operator and has no RPC-socket or lightning-dir access. They pre-create /tmp/lightning-crash.log.<ts> entries (0666 files or symlinks) for a range of upcoming seconds, then wait for or provoke a lightningd crash at a time when the config-dir open fails (EROFS after a remount-ro, inode/space exhaustion on the lightning-dir filesystem — inducible by a co-tenant sharing that filesystem — or an operator permission change). Attack complexity is high because a non-default host condition must hold and, on Linux, fs.protected_symlinks/protected_regular must be unset (kernel defaults, but systemd distributions enable them); the shipped systemd unit's PrivateTmp=true also removes the shared /tmp under that unit. macOS and tarball/nix/manual Linux runs on multi-user hosts are exposed. Timing is not a barrier since the attacker can blanket many seconds with entries.

## Recommended fix
log_backtrace_exit creates a file at a predictable, attacker-influenceable path in a world-writable directory without O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW, so an existing file or symlink planted by another local user is silently opened, followed and truncated. Fix criteria: The crash dump must never follow a pre-existing path in a shared directory: create it atomically with an unpredictable name (mkstemp/tmpdir_mkstemp, or O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW with a failure path that gives up rather than retries into an existing entry), or drop the /tmp fallback and write only inside the 0700 lightning-dir. Verify that pre-creating /tmp/lightning-crash.log.<ts> as a 0666 file or as a symlink before a crash neither receives the dump nor causes the symlink target to be truncated.
