# Per-logger log_prefix reference never released: unbounded leak driven by peer reconnects and RPC connections

## Details
lightningd/log.c keeps one `struct log_prefix` per logger so ring-buffer entries can keep pointing at the prefix string after the logger that produced them is gone. The design is reference counting: `log_prefix_new()` starts the count at 1 (the logger's own reference) and parents the object to `log->log_book`, `init_log_hdr()` takes one reference per entry via `log_prefix_get()`, and `del_front_log()` drops one as entries are evicted from the 16 MiB ring. However `destroy_logger()` only removes the logger from `log_book->loggers` and never drops the logger's own reference, so the count can never return to zero and every prefix ever created (struct plus formatted name string, two tal allocations of roughly 100-150 bytes together) stays allocated under the process-lifetime `log_book`.

Loggers are created on peer-driven events, not only at startup:
- `handle_peer_spoke()` (peer_control.c:2258-2272) creates `new_uncommitted_channel()` (one logger, opening_common.c:42) and `peer_start_openingd()` → `new_channel_subd()` → `new_subd()` (a second logger, subd.c:742) for every open_channel a connected peer sends for an unknown channel_id. Only concurrent opens are bounded ("Multiple simultaneous opens not supported"); sequential open-then-abort attempts are not.
- Every reconnect to a peer with an existing channel spawns a fresh channeld through `new_subd()` (peer_control.c:1489), leaking one prefix per reconnect.
- `jcon_connected()` (jsonrpc.c:1272) creates one per JSON-RPC connection, freed in `destroy_jcon` with its prefix leaked (trusted local callers; clnrest opens a connection per HTTP request).

An unauthenticated peer running an open-attempt or reconnect loop therefore grows lightningd's heap monotonically for the life of the process, a few hundred bytes per iteration, with no reclamation path short of restart. Growth is slow relative to the fork/exec cost each iteration also imposes, but it is unbounded by any attacker-independent constant, which is the property the project's own comment at peer_control.c:2282-2288 (MAX_INFLIGHT_OPENS, "keeping per-peer resource use bounded") says it intends to hold. The leak is not visible to the developer tooling: dev-memdump skips the log_book subtree (memdump.c:49-51) and dev-memleak still finds the prefix pointer inside ring-buffer entries until they are evicted.

This is distinct from the ring buffer itself, which is bounded and evicts; the leak is in the side-table of prefix objects referenced by that ring.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/log.c:555–557](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L555-L557)
   destroy_logger() only unlinks the logger from log_book->loggers; it never calls log_prefix_drop(log->prefix), so the reference log_prefix_new() gave the creating logger is never released. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [lightningd/log.c:100–106](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L100-L106)
   log_prefix_new() allocates the prefix under ctx with refcnt = 1 (the logger's own reference) plus a tal_strdup of the formatted name.
3. [lightningd/log.c:571–573](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L571-L573)
   new_logger() parents the prefix to log->log_book (process lifetime), not to the logger, so freeing the logger does not free it; only the refcount can.
4. [lightningd/log.c:171–175](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L171-L175)
   log_prefix_drop() frees only when refcnt reaches 0; with the creator's reference never dropped this is unreachable.
5. [lightningd/log.c:249–263](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L249-L263)
   del_front_log() is the only call site of log_prefix_drop(); it releases exactly the reference init_log_hdr() took via log_prefix_get() (line 649) for each evicted ring entry, so entry references balance and the logger's initial reference is the one that leaks.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2258–2271](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2258-L2271)
   Remote entry point: handle_peer_spoke() receives an open_channel for an unknown channel_id from any connected peer and calls new_uncommitted_channel() (one logger) and peer_start_openingd() (a second logger via new_channel_subd/new_subd). Only concurrent opens are limited; a peer may repeat open-then-disconnect indefinitely.
7. [lightningd/subd.c:741–745](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L741-L745)
   new_subd() calls new_logger() for every subdaemon spawn (openingd per open attempt, channeld per reconnect, dualopend, closingd, onchaind); the subd is freed when the process exits but its prefix stays under log_book.
8. [lightningd/opening\_common.c:42–43](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_common.c#L42-L43)
   new_uncommitted_channel() creates a 'chan#N' logger per inbound open_channel attempt; uc is tal_freed on disconnect/error (opening_common.c:96, 126), leaking the prefix each time.
9. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1481–1491](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1481-L1491)
   On every reconnect to a peer with a live channel, peer_start_channeld() spawns a new channeld via new_channel_subd(), creating and later leaking a 'channeld-chan#N' prefix per reconnect.
10. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1272–1273](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L1272-L1273)
   A per-connection 'jsonrpc#<fd>' logger is created for each JSON-RPC socket connection and freed in destroy_jcon (line 146); its prefix leaks per connection. Callers here are trusted local clients (or clnrest, which opens a ClnRpc per request, plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs:80), so this is a secondary, lower-trust-gain path.
11. [lightningd/memdump.c:49–50](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/memdump.c#L49-L50)
   dev-memdump skips the whole 'struct log_book' subtree ("we know they grow"). The dev-memleak conservative scan (common/memleak.c:348-360 enters all tal objects; prefixes are removed only when a pointer to them is found) still sees leaked prefixes via the ring buffer's log_hdr entries until those entries are evicted from the 16 MiB ring, which test runs never reach; hence neither developer tool exposes the leak.

## Impact
Impact is confined to lightningd's resident memory: a monotonically growing heap never reclaimed until restart. Each iteration leaks only a few hundred bytes and costs the node a fork/exec, so meaningful exhaustion requires sustained abuse over a long period; rated LOW availability. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any node that completes the BOLT8 handshake with a lightningd listening on the default port 9735 sends init then open_channel with a random temporary channel_id; lightningd spawns openingd and creates two loggers, the peer disconnects (or sends an error), openingd exits, the uncommitted channel is freed and both prefixes leak. Alternatively a peer with an existing channel reconnects in a loop, leaking one channeld prefix per reconnect. No credentials, user interaction, special configuration or race are needed.

## Recommended fix
destroy_logger() releases the logger's list membership but not the reference it holds on log->prefix, violating the refcount invariant that log_prefix objects are freed when no logger or ring entry refers to them. Fix criteria: After a logger is freed, its log_prefix must be freed as soon as no ring-buffer entry references it; repeatedly creating and destroying loggers (e.g. peer reconnect loop, channel-open attempts, RPC connections) must leave the number of live log_prefix allocations bounded by the number of live loggers plus ring entries. Verify by counting tal children of the log_book across a reconnect loop, and by removing (or narrowing) the memdump.c exclusion so the memleak scan can observe prefix objects.

# Tiny advertised htlc_max on a channel with learned liquidity aborts renepay in get_flow_paths

## Details
renepay's MCF solver (plugins/renepay/mcf.c) linearises each channel direction into four arcs. Arc 0 has capacity a = known_min - htlc_total (in sats) and is not clipped by the channel's advertised htlc_max (`cap_on_capacity` only limits arcs 1..3, lines 517-521), and channel_is_available imposes no htlc_max gate. When get_flow_paths decomposes the solution into routes it computes the route's smallest htlc_max and largest htlc_min in sats and, if the flow `delta` exceeds htlc_max, re-draws `delta = pseudorand_interval(MAX(htlc_min, htlc_max/2), htlc_max)` (lines 1402-1411). pseudorand_interval returns a value in the half-open range [a,b) (b only when a==b). Hence htlc_max == 0 sats (gossip htlc_maximum_msat < 1000) yields pseudorand_interval(0,0)=0, and htlc_max == 1 sat with htlc_min 0 yields pseudorand(1)=0. `assert(delta>0)` at line 1440 then aborts cln-renepay (mcf.c does not define NDEBUG; asserts are compiled in).

Reaching it needs a channel direction with learned known_min >= 1 sat whose advertised htlc_max is below 2 sat. Channels start at known_min = 0 (uncertainty.c:102), but known_min is written by chan_extra_can_send (known_min = htlc_total) for every hop upstream of the erring node on any failed attempt (routetracker.c:144-148), and by chan_extra_sent_success for the reverse direction of a successful hop; it persists in the global uncertainty network and decays only over TIMER_FORGET_SEC = 600000 s (~7 days).

Attack (two colluding routing nodes B and C with a public channel B-C, zero fees to attract flow): the victim pays anyone via ...->B->C->D. C returns TEMPORARY_CHANNEL_FAILURE and embeds a valid channel_update for B->C signed by B with htlc_maximum_msat=999 (routefail.c update_gossip forwards whatever update is embedded to addgossip, lines 153-173; gossipd checks only signature and timestamp). route_failure_register records known_min(B->C)=amount while the HTLC is still counted (routefail.c:51), payment_collect_results frees the route (htlc_total back to 0), refreshgossmap in the retry loop (mods.c program step 20) picks up the new htlc_max, and on the retry linearize_channel gives B->C arc 0 a capacity of `amount` sats at zero probability cost while cap_on_capacity is 0. The MCF routes through it, get_flow_paths computes htlc_max=0 -> delta=0 -> abort. The channelfilter that drops tiny-htlc_max directions (mods.c:1213-1260) runs only before the retry loop and, for payments <= 99 sat, would not exclude 999 msat anyway, so B simply broadcasting the update via normal gossip after any prior success or failure through B-C within ~7 days also works for small payments. htlc_max in [1000,1999] msat with htlc_min 0 reaches the same delta=0.

cln-renepay is the only builtin plugin not marked important, so lightningd survives, but the plugin process dies and is not restarted: all in-flight renepay payments lose tracking and every renepay/renepaystatus RPC fails until the operator restarts it.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/mcf.c:1388–1440](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mcf.c#L1388-L1440)
   get_flow_paths converts the route's infimum htlc_max and supremum htlc_min to sats by integer division. If htlc_min > htlc_max, htlc_min is zeroed (1391-1398). If delta > htlc_max, delta = pseudorand_interval(MAX(htlc_min, htlc_max*50/100), htlc_max) (1402-1411). With htlc_max == 0 sats (gossip htlc_maximum_msat < 1000) this is pseudorand_interval(0,0) == 0; with htlc_max == 1 sat and htlc_min == 0 it is 0 + pseudorand(1) == 0. assert(delta>0) at 1440 then aborts cln-renepay. mcf.c does not define NDEBUG (only dijkstra.c does), so the assert is live in release builds.
2. [plugins/renepay/mcf.c:1257–1263](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mcf.c#L1257-L1263)
   pseudorand_interval(a,b) returns b only when a==b, otherwise a + pseudorand(b-a), which lies in the half-open range [a,b). pseudorand(1) is isaac64_next_uint(ctx,1) (common/pseudorand.c:42) and is always 0.
3. [plugins/renepay/mcf.c:486–526](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mcf.c#L486-L526)
   linearize_channel: capacity[0] = a = known_min - htlc_total (sats) is not bounded by cap_on_capacity (the channel's htlc_max in sats); only arcs 1..3 are (517-521). channel_is_available (446-457) admits any enabled, non-disabled direction with no htlc_max gate. A direction with learned known_min therefore carries up to known_min sats of zero-probability-cost flow through the MCF even when its advertised htlc_max is 0 or 1 sat, so the decomposed route has delta > htlc_max.
4. [plugins/renepay/chan\_extra.c:258–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/chan_extra.c#L258-L302)
   chan_extra_can_send_ sets known_min = max(known_min, x) with x = the direction's current htlc_total: any failure downstream teaches renepay that this hop can carry the attempted amount. chan_extra_sent_success (402-442) likewise leaves the reverse direction with known_min >= the amount via chan_extra_adjust_half. new_chan_extra (uncertainty.c:88-104) starts channels at known_min = 0, so prior interaction with the channel is what the attacker needs.
5. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:142–148](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L142-L148)
   route_failure_register: on any failure, every hop before the erring node receives uncertainty_channel_can_send; the hop before the failing node learns known_min = amount. It is called from routefail_start (routefail.c:51) while the route is still pending (HTLC counted); the route is freed in payment_collect_results (routetracker.c:276-277, destructor remove_route -> uncertainty_remove_htlcs) so htlc_total is back to 0 before the retry's compute_routes.
6. [plugins/renepay/routefail.c:153–173](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routefail.c#L153-L173)
   update_gossip hands whatever channel_update is embedded in the onion error to addgossip without checking which channel it describes, so the erring node C can deliver a valid update signed by its colluding upstream node B setting htlc_maximum_msat=999 for B->C in the same failure that teaches known_min(B->C). gossipd (gossmap_manage.c:1024-1130, process_channel_update) verifies signature and timestamp only; neither it nor common/gossmap.c imposes a floor on htlc_maximum_msat (999 is exact in fp16, common/fp16.c:6-40). B may equally broadcast the update through normal gossip.
7. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:1213–1259](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L1213-L1259)
   channelfilter disables directions whose htlc_max is below 1% of the payment amount, but it is program step 14, before the do/while retry loop (steps 16-33); refreshgossmap (step 20) inside the loop picks up the new htlc_max without re-filtering, and uncertainty_update (uncertainty.c:74-96) does not clamp known_min. For payments <= 99 sat the filter never excludes a 999 msat htlc_max, so the across-payment variant works for small payments too.

## Impact
The vulnerable component is the cln-renepay plugin process: assert() aborts it (asserts are compiled in; mcf.c has no NDEBUG). The loss is total and persistent for that component: lightningd does not restart a non-important plugin, so every renepay payment in flight loses its tracker and the renepay/renepaystatus RPCs fail until the operator intervenes. lightningd itself keeps running because renepay is not marked important, and HTLCs already handed to sendpay are settled by lightningd, so there is no confidentiality or integrity impact and no on-chain consequence.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker runs two routing nodes B, C with a public channel between them and low fees so the victim's MCF routes a payment through B->C->D. C fails the HTLC with TEMPORARY_CHANNEL_FAILURE carrying B's channel_update (htlc_maximum_msat=999 for B->C), or B broadcasts it via normal gossip; renepay learns known_min(B->C)=amount from the failure, retries, routes through arc 0 of B->C (zero probability cost, capacity = known_min, unbounded by htlc_max), and aborts in get_flow_paths. No credentials; network only; the victim merely performs a routine renepay payment through the public graph. Attack requirements are present: the victim must use renepay and the solver must select the attacker's channel, which depends on graph position and fees (runtime state the attacker influences but does not fully control).

## Recommended fix
1. get_flow_paths draws a replacement delta from pseudorand_interval whose half-open range collapses to 0 when the route's htlc_max rounds to 0 or 1 sat (or htlc_min > htlc_max), then asserts delta > 0. Fix criteria: A route whose minimum htlc_max (in the solver's sat units) cannot carry at least one unit, or whose htlc_min exceeds its htlc_max, must be handled gracefully (flow dropped and the offending direction disabled, or an error returned to the caller) rather than asserted on; delta must be provably >= 1 for any surviving route, e.g. by drawing from a closed interval with a floor of 1. Verify by feeding a solution route with htlc_max 999 msat and 1000 msat and htlc_min 0 / 2000 msat: minflow must return a result or an error, never abort.
2. linearize_channel caps only arcs 1..3 by the advertised htlc_max; arc 0 (known liquidity) is unbounded, so the MCF assigns a direction more flow than its htlc_max allows and the decomposition must shrink it. Fix criteria: The total capacity assigned to a channel direction in the linear network must never exceed its advertised htlc_max (apply cap_on_capacity to arc 0 as well, or exclude directions whose htlc_max is below one solver unit from the network). Verify that a direction with known_min 100000 sat and htlc_max 999 msat receives zero flow in the solution and one with htlc_max 5 sat receives at most 5 sat.

# pyln-proto BOLT8 handshake ignores Act 1/Act 2 MAC failures (ValueError never raised)

## Details
pyln-proto's Noise_XK implementation (contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py, shipped in the PyPI wheel; `packages = ["pyln"]`) verifies the Poly1305 tag of Act 1 on the responder side and of Act 2 on the initiator side inside `try/except InvalidTag`, but both except branches only construct `ValueError(...)` and never `raise` it (wire.py:147-149 and 183-184). Execution falls through to `h.update(c)` and the handshake continues as if the tag had verified. `cryptography.exceptions.InvalidTag` is the documented exception `ChaCha20Poly1305.decrypt` raises on tag mismatch (pinned `cryptography>=46`), so the branch is taken and silently discarded.

BOLT8 requires the responder to 'terminate the connection without any further messages' when the Act 1 MAC fails (the initiator does not know the responder's static key) and the initiator to do the same when the Act 2 MAC fails; connectd/handshake.c returns `handshake_failed` at both points (handshake.c:594-596, 948-950).

Responder side (`LightningServerSocket.accept` -> `shake`, wire.py:294-303): any TCP client that sends version 0x00, any valid compressed secp256k1 point E_i and 16 arbitrary bytes receives Act 2 `0x00 || E_r || c2`. Because `init_handshake` seeds `h` with the responder's static public key S_r (wire.py:109) and `temp_k2` derives from `ck1 = HKDF(ck0, ECDH(s_r, E_i))`, c2 is a function of S_r plus values the attacker already holds (its own e_i, the received E_r, its own c1). The attacker can therefore recompute c2 for every candidate node ID offline and confirm which one the listener holds, where a conformant responder yields at most one online candidate test per connection. The Act 1 MAC exists precisely to prevent this (Noise XK responder identity hiding). Act 3 (wire.py:214, 222) still raises on a bad tag, so an initiator without `es` cannot complete the handshake; there is no key-agreement or authentication bypass.

Initiator side (`connect` -> `shake`): a responder not holding the expected static key is not rejected and the initiator still emits Act 3. The Act 3 ciphertext is keyed by `temp_k2` (requires `es`), so the initiator's static key is not disclosed and the first `read_message` fails; this half is a protocol deviation without a demonstrated leak.

The finding holds for any consumer that exposes the responder side (`is_initiator=False`) to untrusted peers; the repository ships `examples/listen.py` binding 0.0.0.0:9735 as the intended usage. pyln-proto's own description warns it is 'not deemed secure enough to handle any amount of real funds', a disclaimer about funds rather than an operator obligation to fence the listening socket.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py:145–151](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py#L145-L151)
   Responder Act 1: decryptWithAD raises InvalidTag when the initiator's tag does not verify; the except branch constructs ValueError(...) without `raise`, so control falls through to h.update(c) and the responder proceeds to Act 2 with an initiator that proved nothing. This is the primary fix location.
2. [contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py:181–186](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py#L181-L186)
   Initiator Act 2: same unraised ValueError; a responder that cannot produce a valid tag (does not hold the expected static key) is not rejected and the initiator proceeds to send Act 3. Protocol deviation; no key disclosure because Act 3 is keyed by temp_k2.
3. [contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py:294–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py#L294-L302)
   LightningServerSocket.accept -> shake responder branch: after handshake_act_one_responder returns (MAC failure ignored) the responder computes and sends Act 2 unconditionally to the unauthenticated initiator.
4. [contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py:101–114](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py#L101-L114)
   init_handshake seeds the handshake hash h with the responder's static public key and the chaining key with the protocol name; together with ck1 = HKDF(ck0, ECDH(s_r, E_i)) this makes the Act 2 tag c2 a deterministic function of S_r and values the attacker holds, i.e. an offline oracle on the listener's node ID once Act 2 is emitted without the Act 1 check.
5. [contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py:214–222](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-proto/pyln/proto/wire.py#L214-L222)
   Act 3 responder does not catch InvalidTag, so decryptWithAD raises and the handshake aborts for an initiator lacking es; this bounds the impact to the Act 2 identity oracle and rules out an authentication bypass.
6. [connectd/handshake.c:944–950](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/handshake.c#L944-L950)
   C reference responder: on Act 1 MAC failure returns handshake_failed, as BOLT8 requires; shows the expected behaviour the Python implementation deviates from.
7. [contrib/pyln-proto/examples/listen.py:20–27](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-proto/examples/listen.py#L20-L27)
   Context only (not shipped in the wheel): the project's documented usage of LightningServerSocket as a listening BOLT8 endpoint bound to 0.0.0.0, reachable by arbitrary TCP peers.

## Impact
Confidentiality: the static node identity behind the listening socket becomes confirmable offline against any candidate list from a single connection, defeating the Noise XK responder identity-hiding property BOLT8's Act 1 termination rule exists to provide (threat-model privacy asset). Limited disclosure, hence LOW. Integrity/availability: none; Act 3 still verifies, so no session is established without es and no state is modified.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote TCP client reaching a pyln-proto LightningServerSocket (the responder side of the shipped library). It opens one connection, sends 50 bytes (0x00, any valid secp256k1 point, 16 arbitrary bytes) and receives Act 2 because the MAC failure at wire.py:147 is swallowed. Offline it recomputes the Act 2 tag for each candidate node ID from public gossip and confirms the listener's identity. No credentials, no user interaction, no defence to defeat; a conformant responder would close the connection and allow only one online guess per connection.

## Recommended fix
1. handshake_act_one_responder catches InvalidTag from decryptWithAD and constructs a ValueError without raising it, so an initiator that does not know the responder's static key is not rejected and the responder emits Act 2, violating BOLT8's 'MUST terminate without any further messages' and leaking an offline oracle on the responder's node ID. Fix criteria: An Act 1 message whose tag does not verify must abort the handshake with an exception before any Act 2 bytes are written to the socket; a test sending a valid ephemeral point with a random 16-byte tag must observe the connection closed with no Act 2 reply.
2. handshake_act_two_initiator has the same unraised ValueError, so the initiator proceeds to compute and send Act 3 against a responder that failed to prove possession of the expected static key. Fix criteria: An Act 2 message whose tag does not verify must abort the handshake before Act 3 is computed or sent; a test with a responder using a different static key must observe the initiator raising and sending nothing further.

# pyln Gossmap crashes on peer-authored node_announcement alias that is not valid UTF-8

## Details
pyln.client.Gossmap (published on PyPI as pyln-client) parses the node's gossip_store directly. In _add_node_announcement() the 32-byte alias field of every live node_announcement is decoded with bytes(...).decode('utf-8') (strict). The alias is authored by the remote node that signed the announcement; BOLT #7 says the sender MUST use valid UTF-8 but imposes no receiver-side rejection, and gossipd's handle_node_announcement (gossipd/gossmap_manage.c:1176-1215) stores the raw bytes without utf8_check. Therefore any node on the Lightning network with an announced channel can broadcast a node_announcement whose alias contains, e.g., 0xFF or a truncated multibyte sequence. Gossip propagation delivers it to every node's gossip_store, where it stays until that node's announcement is superseded or pruned.

On such a node, Gossmap.__init__ -> refresh() -> _add_node_announcement() raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is not caught anywhere in the loop: the Gossmap object cannot be constructed, and an already-constructed one fails on every refresh() once the record arrives. All consumers of the class (GossmapStats, third-party Python plugins and tools that build routing/analytics views from the store) fail deterministically, network-wide, from one 32-byte field. A plugin that constructs Gossmap in its init handler never starts (if configured important-plugin, lightningd does not start); one that refreshes on a timer or in a hook dies with an uncaught exception.

The same loop has related robustness gaps that are not peer-triggerable (WIRE_GOSSIP_STORE_ENDED after gossipd compaction hits reopen_store()'s `assert False` at line 585; _set_channel_amount would KeyError on a store whose first record is a channel_amount) but those stem from gossipd housekeeping or corruption, not from a remote peer's data, and are noted only as context.

No shipped CLN tool imports Gossmap outside the test suite; the vulnerable system is any installation of the published pyln-client package that uses the class against a live gossip_store.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/gossmap.py:579](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/gossmap.py#L579)
   _add_node_announcement() does bytes(fields['alias']).decode('utf-8') with the default strict error handler; any byte sequence in the 32-byte alias that is not well-formed UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError.
2. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/gossmap.py:614–645](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/gossmap.py#L614-L645)
   refresh() iterates every live record and dispatches WIRE_NODE_ANNOUNCEMENT to _add_node_announcement() with no try/except, so UnicodeDecodeError propagates out of refresh() and, via __init__ (line 404), out of the constructor; the same record re-raises on every later refresh() while it is live in the store.
3. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/gossmap.py:392–404](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/gossmap.py#L392-L404)
   Gossmap.__init__ calls refresh() unconditionally, so a single such record makes the Gossmap object unconstructible for every consumer of the library on that node; the exception is also raised on every later refresh().
4. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1147–1214](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1147-L1214)
   gossipd accepts a node_announcement after only fromwire parsing (alias read into raw u8[32], line 1176), wireaddr-descriptor parsing and signature verification; process_node_announcement() then calls gossip_store_add() (line 1147) to append the message verbatim. No utf8_check exists anywhere in gossipd/, so any node with an announced channel can persist a non-UTF-8 alias into every node's gossip_store.
5. [plugins/topology.c:378–382](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/topology.c#L378-L382)
   Contrast: the C consumer (listnodes) escapes the alias with json_escape/json_add_escaped_string rather than requiring it to be valid UTF-8, confirming the project already treats the alias as untrusted bytes elsewhere.

## Impact
The Python consumer crashes deterministically and stays unusable while the record is live in the store, so availability of every pyln Gossmap-based tool or plugin is lost; if that plugin is marked important, lightningd itself stops or fails to start. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any Lightning node with a public channel (needed for gossipd to accept its node_announcement). It signs and broadcasts a node_announcement whose alias bytes are not valid UTF-8; gossip propagation (AV:N) carries it to every node, whose gossipd appends it unvalidated to gossip_store. Any pyln Gossmap user on any of those nodes then raises UnicodeDecodeError on construction or refresh. No privileges on the victim, no user interaction, deterministic, no defences to evade; it works against any installation that uses the class.

## Recommended fix
1. The alias, a remote-peer-authored byte string that gossipd stores unvalidated, is strictly decoded as UTF-8 and the resulting exception escapes refresh(). Fix criteria: A node_announcement whose alias is not valid UTF-8 must not prevent Gossmap construction or refresh: the alias should be decoded leniently (replacement/backslash escapes) or kept as bytes, and the record should still be loaded. Verify by loading a store containing a node_announcement with alias bytes 0xFF... and confirming Gossmap() succeeds and the node is present.
2. refresh() has no per-record error isolation, so any single malformed-but-stored record aborts the whole parse. Fix criteria: A parse failure in one record must be recorded (e.g. counted/logged) and skipped rather than propagated, so the remaining records are still loaded. Verify with a store containing one undecodable record followed by valid ones.

# pyln-testing PostgresDbProvider starts a trust-auth superuser Postgres any local user can reach

## Details
pyln-testing is a published PyPI package (pypi-publish.yml; contrib/pyln-testing/pyproject.toml ships the whole `pyln` package including db.py) that the README says is used by the community plugin directory and third-party plugin CI. When run with TEST_DB_PROVIDER=postgres (non-default, documented at doc/contribute-to-core-lightning/testing.md:70 and used by the project's own CI matrix), PostgresDbProvider.start() (db.py:180-227) creates a cluster with `initdb --pwfile=... --auth=trust --username=postgres` and launches it with `postgres -k /tmp/ -D <pgdir> -p <port> -F -i`.

Per PostgreSQL's documented contract (assumption: the system PostgreSQL CI installs via apt, unpinned): `--auth=trust` sets both `--auth-local` and `--auth-host`, so the generated pg_hba.conf has `local all all trust`, `host all all 127.0.0.1/32 trust` and `host all all ::1/128 trust`; `-k /tmp/` places the Unix socket at `/tmp/.s.PGSQL.<port>` with the default `unix_socket_permissions=0777`; `-i` sets `listen_addresses='*'`. The harness appends only `max_connections`/`shared_buffers` to postgresql.conf and never tightens pg_hba.conf. The `--pwfile` password (`cltest`) is never consulted: the DSN handed to lightningd (db.py:88) carries a different literal (`password`) and the harness's own psycopg2 connections pass no password at all, so every connection succeeds only because authentication is `trust`.

Consequence: for the lifetime of the test session, any other account on the same host can connect over `/tmp/.s.PGSQL.<port>` or `127.0.0.1:<port>` as the PostgreSQL superuser `postgres` with no credential. A PostgreSQL superuser can read and rewrite the lightningd databases of the harness nodes and, more importantly, run arbitrary commands and read/write arbitrary files as the OS user running the harness (`COPY ... TO/FROM PROGRAM`, `pg_read_server_files`/`pg_write_server_files`, `lo_import`/`lo_export`, server-side extensions). This is a local privilege escalation from any unprivileged account to the test-runner account and whatever credentials that account or its CI job holds. The port is trivially discoverable: the socket is visible in /tmp and reserve_unused_port() publishes it as `/tmp/pyln-testing-ports/<port>.lock`.

The harness otherwise excludes other local accounts from its state: test_base_dir is created with tempfile.mkdtemp (0700, fixtures.py:41) and lightningd's RPC sockets are 0600, so node DBs and RPC are private to the runner; the trust-auth cluster bypasses that boundary. The project documents no single-user-host requirement for the postgres provider (README.md, testing.md).

Secondary consequences of the same configuration: a co-tenant can pre-create `/tmp/.s.PGSQL.<port>.lock` so the harness's postgres fails to start, and because the harness and lightningd connect by TCP to `localhost:<port>` without server authentication, a co-tenant who binds the reserved loopback port before postgres does can impersonate the database to the test nodes.

Because pg_hba lists only loopback addresses, remote hosts are refused despite `-i`; the attack is rated local. The project's GitHub-hosted CI runners are single-tenant and the postgres jobs carry no secrets, so the exposure matters for the package's third-party users and for developers on shared machines.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/db.py:197–216](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/db.py#L197-L216)
   initdb is run with --auth=trust --username=postgres, so both the `local` and `host` lines of the generated pg_hba.conf accept the superuser `postgres` with no credential. The cluster is then started with `-k /tmp/` (Unix socket in the world-shared /tmp with default 0777 socket permissions), `-i` (listen_addresses='*') and a port drawn from reserve_unused_port(). Nothing afterwards tightens pg_hba.conf; only max_connections/shared_buffers are appended to postgresql.conf.
2. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/db.py:87–90](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/db.py#L87-L90)
   The DSN handed to lightningd (`postgres://postgres:password@localhost:<port>/<db>`) uses the literal `password`, while initdb's --pwfile (db.py:181-185) set the superuser password to `cltest` and the harness's own psycopg2 connections pass no password. All of these succeed, which is only possible because authentication is `trust`: no credential protects the cluster.
3. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/fixtures.py:829–834](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/fixtures.py#L829-L834)
   The provider is selected and started for the whole session whenever TEST_DB_PROVIDER=postgres; the project's documentation (doc/contribute-to-core-lightning/testing.md:70) and CI matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yaml:404, 576) run the harness this way.
4. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/fixtures.py:38–41](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/fixtures.py#L38-L41)
   test_base_dir is created with tempfile.mkdtemp (mode 0700), so the harness deliberately keeps node directories, hsm_secrets and RPC sockets private to the runner's account; the trust-auth cluster in /tmp and on loopback is the one path that hands other local accounts the runner's authority.
5. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py:255–279](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py#L255-L279)
   The chosen port is written as a world-readable lock file `/tmp/pyln-testing-ports/<port>.lock` (directory created with default mode at utils.py:177-178), so a co-tenant does not even need to port-scan to find the listener.

## Impact
PostgreSQL superuser implies arbitrary command execution and file read/write as the OS user running the test session, giving full compromise of that account (its files, SSH/CI credentials, the regtest nodes' hsm_secrets and databases) and the ability to kill or corrupt the test run.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any unprivileged account on a host where someone runs pyln-testing with TEST_DB_PROVIDER=postgres (non-default option, documented and used in CI). The attacker watches /tmp/pyln-testing-ports/ or /tmp/.s.PGSQL.* to learn the port, connects with `psql -h /tmp -p <port> -U postgres` (trust, no password) and runs `COPY x FROM PROGRAM '<cmd>'` to execute code as the harness user. No defence is in the way; the only requirements are the non-default DB provider and a shared host.

## Recommended fix
The test cluster is initialised with trust authentication for the superuser and started listening on all interfaces with its Unix socket in the world-shared /tmp, so no credential or filesystem permission separates the harness from other local accounts. Fix criteria: Only the harness process (and the lightningd processes it spawns) can authenticate to the test cluster: e.g. password/scram or peer auth with a secret generated per session and passed in the DSN, the Unix socket placed in the session's 0700 temp directory, and listen_addresses restricted to loopback (drop -i). Verify that `psql -U postgres` from another local account over both the socket and 127.0.0.1:<port> is refused, and that remote hosts cannot complete a TCP connection to the port.

# Blinded-path failures beyond the introduction node index past route hops and abort renepay

## Details
renepay models a BOLT12 blinded path as one fake channel from the path's first_node_id to a fake routing destination (mods.c blindedhints_cb, 619-645). flow_to_route() (route.c:74-77) removes that fake last hop, so route->hops holds only the k real channels ending at the introduction node (path_len = k). The onion built by create_onion()/sphinx_append_blinded_path() (routetracker.c:343-372, 280-307) however contains k-1 non-final hops plus one sphinx hop per blinded-path hop (N hops), and lightningd keeps all (k-1)+N shared secrets from the sendonion call (lightningd/pay.c:1353, 1385-1389, route_nodes = NULL).

When the HTLC fails inside the blinded path, lightningd unwraps the error with all secrets (pay.c:610-614) and, because sendonion payments have no route_nodes, reports erring_index = origin_index + 1 with erring_channel/erring_node = NULL (pay.c:466-479, 527); the sendpay_failure notification carries it (json_sendpay_fail_fields). For the j-th blinded node (j >= 1) this is k + j, strictly greater than path_len. A CLN node inside a blinded path whose incoming update_add_htlc carries path_key — every hop after the introduction node, including the recipient — answers any failure with an onion-wrapped invalid_onion_blinding generated with its own shared secret (peer_htlcs.c:153-164, 209-215, 1647-1656), so for a 2-hop path (introduction node + recipient) any recipient-side rejection yields erring_index = k + 1.

renepay's handle_failure() (routefail.c:272-280) only distinguishes erring_index == path_len (FINAL) from 0 (ORIGIN) and treats all other values as INTERMEDIATE. For WIRE_INVALID_ONION_BLINDING it executes assert(*result->erring_index < path_len) (line 319), which fails -> abort(). For any other failcode a non-CLN or deliberately misbehaving blinded node might send (incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details, mpp_timeout, temporary_channel_failure, ...), the INTERMEDIATE branches read route->hops[erring_index-1] or route->hops[erring_index] past the end of the tal array (lines 350, 398, 440, 468, 516), feed garbage node ids / scids into the disabledmap, and then route_failure_register() (routetracker.c:134-140) calls plugin_err() because last_good_channel = erring_index - 1 >= path_len. Either way the plugin dies.

The trigger condition is a blinded path of N >= 2 hops failing at a hop after the introduction node. CLN's own offers plugin emits exactly such a 2-hop path (direct peer + us) for unannounced payees (offers_invreq_hook.c:340-343); public CLN payees get a 1-hop stub path (N = 1, erring_index = path_len, FINAL, no bug), but a payee authoring its own invoice chooses the path length freely. The renepay tests (tests/test_renepay.py test_offers, test_offer_selfpay, test_unannounced) only exercise successful BOLT12 payments, so the mismatch is never hit in CI.

Consequence: when the operator pays a BOLT12 invoice with `renepay` and the recipient (or any blinded hop after the introduction node) rejects the HTLC — wrong amount, already-paid invoice, MPP timeout, or a deliberately failing payee — the cln-renepay plugin aborts or plugin_err()s. renepay is the one builtin plugin not marked important (lightningd/plugin.c:2585), so lightningd survives, but the renepay payment engine and all its in-flight payment tracking are lost until the operator restarts the plugin. This is the renepay sibling of xpay-blinded-path-erring-index-oob-abort with a lower threshold (any 2-hop path, which is what CLN itself produces).

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/routefail.c:272–327](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routefail.c#L272-L327)
   handle_failure() classifies erring_index == path_len (tal_count(route->hops)) as FINAL_NODE, 0 as ORIGIN_NODE and every other value as INTERMEDIATE_NODE, with no check that erring_index <= path_len. For WIRE_INVALID_ONION_BLINDING from an INTERMEDIATE_NODE it executes assert(*result->erring_index < path_len) (line 319), which fails and abort()s whenever the erring sphinx hop lies inside the blinded path beyond the introduction node (erring_index = path_len + j, j >= 1).
2. [plugins/renepay/routefail.c:345–352](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routefail.c#L345-L352)
   For every other failcode a blinded node might return, the INTERMEDIATE_NODE branches read route->hops[*erring_index - 1] (lines 350, 398, 468) or route->hops[*erring_index] (lines 440, 516) with erring_index > path_len: out-of-bounds heap reads past the tal array whose garbage node_id/scid is fed into the payment's disabledmap.
3. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:129–160](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L129-L160)
   route_failure_register() (called from routefail_end after handle_failure) computes last_good_channel = erring_index - 1 and calls plugin_err() when it is >= path_len (lines 134-140), so every route whose erring_index > path_len kills the plugin even when handle_failure did not assert.
4. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:280–306](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L280-L306)
   sphinx_append_blinded_path() adds one sphinx hop per hop of the payee-authored blinded path (N hops: first_node_id then each blinded_node_id), so the onion and the shared_secrets array passed to sendonion have (k-1)+N entries while route->hops has only the k real channels.
5. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:343–371](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L343-L371)
   create_onion() adds one non-final sphinx hop for route[first_index..pathlen) (k-1 hops for hops[0..k-2].node_id when first_index = 1) and then either the blinded path or a single final hop; shared_secrets is sized by create_onionpacket from the total sphinx hop count.
6. [plugins/renepay/route.c:74–77](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/route.c#L74-L77)
   flow_to_route() strips the fake last hop (introduction node -> fake routing destination) when blinded_destination is set, so route->hops ends at the introduction node and path_len counts only the k real channels.
7. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:619–644](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L619-L644)
   blindedhints_cb() models each payee-supplied blinded path as a single fake channel (scid = path index) from path->first_node_id to payment->routing_destination, regardless of how many hops the blinded path contains.
8. [lightningd/pay.c:466–527](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L466-L527)
   remote_routing_failure(): for sendonion payments (route_nodes == NULL) erring_channel/erring_node are NULL and erring_index = origin_index + 1, where origin_index is the 0-based sphinx index from unwrap_onionreply() over all path_secrets including the blinded hops (payment_failed, lines 610-614). For blinded hop j >= 1 this is k + j > path_len.
9. [lightningd/pay.c:1353–1389](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1353-L1389)
   json_sendonion() accepts the plugin's shared_secrets as path_secrets and calls send_payment_core() with NULL route_nodes/route_channels, which is the branch remote_routing_failure() takes.
10. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:153–223](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L153-L223)
   blind_error_return() is true for every node whose incoming update_add_htlc carries path_key — every blinded hop after the introduction node, including the recipient (the introduction node forwards request->next_path_key at line 1349; the receiver stores added->path_key in new_htlc_in at 2406-2412). mk_failed_htlc() (209-215) then returns invalid_onion_blinding created with that node's own shared secret, so the origin index the payer recovers is the blinded node's own sphinx position; lines 1647-1656 do the same for parse-time failures.
11. [plugins/renepay/json.c:126–135](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/json.c#L126-L135)
   get_data_details() copies lightningd's erring_index from the sendpay_failure notification verbatim into result->erring_index without comparing it to the route length.
12. [plugins/offers\_invreq\_hook.c:340–343](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_invreq_hook.c#L340-L343)
   CLN's own offers plugin builds a 2-hop blinded path (best direct peer + us) for unannounced nodes, so an honest unannounced CLN payee that merely rejects the HTLC (already paid, wrong amount) produces erring_index = k + 1 and triggers the abort; a malicious payee chooses the path length freely (invoice_decode only rejects zero-hop paths).

## Impact
assert()/plugin_err() terminate cln-renepay, the impacted component; it is not an important plugin (plugin.c:2585) so lightningd stays up and pay/xpay keep working, but renepay and all its in-flight payment state are unavailable until the operator manually restarts it (`plugin start`), a total loss of that component's availability. The out-of-bounds reads are one-past-the-end heap reads of struct route_hop that only poison the per-payment disabledmap before the plugin dies; nothing is written and nothing leaves the host.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker is the payee (threat-model adversary 3: payment counterparty), or any node inside the blinded path after the introduction node. They publish an offer whose invoice carries a blinded path of 2+ hops (what CLN's offers plugin itself emits for unannounced nodes); the victim operator pays it with `renepay`; the attacker fails the HTLC with any error (a stock CLN recipient converts every rejection to invalid_onion_blinding automatically). lightningd reports erring_index = path_len + 1, renepay asserts (routefail.c:319) or plugin_err()s (routetracker.c:137). No configuration, race or privilege is required; the only interaction is the operator choosing to pay the attacker's invoice via renepay, which is also triggered by honest unannounced CLN payees that merely reject a payment.

## Recommended fix
handle_failure() and route_failure_register() index route->hops with lightningd's erring_index, which counts sphinx hops (including every blinded-path hop after the introduction node) while route->hops only counts real channels up to the introduction node. Fix criteria: Any erring_index >= tal_count(route->hops) is treated as a failure at or beyond the final real hop (the blinded destination) without indexing route->hops and without plugin_err(); a node inside a 2+-hop blinded path failing with invalid_onion_blinding or any other code results in a normal route failure (payment fails or retries) and the plugin keeps running.

# funder RBF builds PSBT with unreserved inputs; signpsbt refusal becomes hook error and lightningd fatal

## Details
The funder plugin (shipped, `important`) answers the `rbf_channel` hook by re-funding our side from the UTXOs it saved in the datastore for the original open. In listfunds_success() it computes committed_funds from those outpoints and, if the policy now asks for more (MATCH scales the peer's new funding_satoshis; AVAILABLE/fuzz can also grow it, and a higher RBF feerate shrinks each input's net value), build_utxopsbt_request() appends further confirmed, unreserved wallet UTXOs. The request is sent with `reservedok: true` and `reserve: 0` (funder.c:732-734) - the comment says "We don't re-reserve any UTXOS", but reserve=0 means utxopsbt does not reserve the *new* inputs either (reservation.c:419). A previously used input whose 72-block reservation has lapsed while the funding tx stayed unconfirmed is likewise accepted (funder.c:644) and not re-reserved. lightningd's rbf_channel_hook_cb forwards the PSBT to dualopend without reserving anything.

When the peer completes the RBF negotiation and sends commitment_signed, lightningd invokes the openchannel2_sign hook. The funder calls `signpsbt` with signonly over all inputs it marked as ours (funder.c:328-351). walletrpc.c:705-711 refuses: "Aborting PSBT signing. UTXO ... is not reserved". The funder's error callback is forward_error, which turns the signpsbt error into the hook reply's `error` member (libplugin.c:621-630, 563-572). plugin_hook.c:278-283 treats a hook reply without `result` as fatal(): lightningd shuts down. The channel stays in DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN with the inflight, so after restart the peer can repeat the RBF and crash the node again.

Who triggers it: the remote peer that opened (or leased) a v2 channel to which our funder contributed. It controls the timing of tx_init_rbf (e.g. waits >72 blocks for the reservation to lapse - exactly the low-feerate situation RBF exists for) and the new funding amount (which with the MATCH policy, or any lease where the old inputs no longer cover our_funding at the higher feerate, forces fresh unreserved inputs). No defence stands in the way: the funder never checks reservation state and lightningd never reserves hook-supplied inputs. None of tests/test_opening.py's RBF tests exercises a funder that needs new inputs or an expired reservation (test_v2_rbf_liquidity_ad / test_v2_rbf_abort_retry re-use a single large UTXO immediately).

Secondary effect: even where signing would succeed (new inputs reserved by some other path), inputs committed to a funding transaction without reservation can be double-spent by a concurrent withdraw/fundpsbt, invalidating the negotiated funding transaction.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/funder.c:724–734](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L724-L734)
   RBF path: listfunds_success() hands the previously used outpoints plus freshly selected wallet UTXOs to utxopsbt with `reservedok: true` and `reserve: 0`. Nothing else ever reserves these inputs.
2. [plugins/funder.c:556–571](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L556-L571)
   build_utxopsbt_request() appends additional confirmed, unreserved wallet UTXOs (avail_utxos) until committed_funds >= our_funding, so whenever the policy result exceeds what the old inputs cover net of the new feerate, brand-new unreserved inputs enter the PSBT.
3. [plugins/funder.c:639–682](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L639-L682)
   A previously used outpoint is accepted even when listfunds reports it reserved=false (reservation lapsed after the default 72 blocks while the funding tx sat unconfirmed); unreserved non-previous UTXOs are collected into avail_utxos.
4. [plugins/funder.c:328–350](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L328-L350)
   openchannel2_sign hook handler calls signpsbt with signonly = all inputs carrying our marker and uses forward_error as the error callback, so any signpsbt refusal is returned as the hook's reply.
5. [plugins/funder.c:446–459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L446-L459)
   psbt_funded() marks every input of the utxopsbt result as ours and returns the PSBT to lightningd, committing the unreserved inputs to the negotiation.
6. [wallet/reservation.c:415–420](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/reservation.c#L415-L420)
   finish_psbt(): `if (reserve) reserve_and_report(...)` - with reserve=0 the selected UTXOs are not reserved at all (utxopsbt passes *reserve through at 1097-1099). RESERVATION_DEFAULT is 72 blocks (line 16).
7. [wallet/walletrpc.c:705–710](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/walletrpc.c#L705-L710)
   signpsbt: match_psbt_inputs_to_utxos() fails the whole command with 'Aborting PSBT signing. UTXO %s is not reserved' for any wallet input that is not currently reserved.
8. [plugins/libplugin.c:621–629](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin.c#L621-L629)
   forward_error() replies to the (hook) command with a raw `error` member via command_done_raw (563-572); jsonrpc_stream_start (421-430) adds only jsonrpc/id, so the reply has no `result`.
9. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:273–282](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L273-L282)
   plugin_hook_callback(): a hook reply without a `result` member (error code != PLUGIN_TERMINATED) is fatal("Plugin %s for %s returned non-result response") - lightningd exits.
10. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:512–555](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L512-L555)
   rbf_channel_hook_cb() forwards the plugin's PSBT to dualopend unchanged; lightningd performs no reservation of hook-supplied inputs anywhere in this file (handle_commit_received at 3966-3991 then invokes openchannel2_sign for the REMOTE-opened channel).
11. [openingd/dualopend.c:3786–3803](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3786-L3803)
   rbf_remote_start(): only the opener (the remote peer, since funder contributes as accepter) may initiate RBF, and the peer's tx_init_rbf sets the new opener funding (funding_output_contribution TLV) and feerate - the inputs that drive our_funding and per-input fee in listfunds_success.
12. [plugins/funder\_policy.c:184–216](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder_policy.c#L184-L216)
   MATCH policy scales the peer-chosen their_funding (or requested lease) by policy_mod, so the peer raising its contribution in tx_init_rbf raises our_funding above what the previous inputs cover.

## Impact
lightningd exits via fatal() during channel funding, taking all channels, HTLC handling and on-chain watching offline until restarted; the peer can re-trigger on every reconnect, so availability impact is HIGH. No confidentiality impact. Funds are not directly lost (nothing is signed), so integrity NONE.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: remote peer that opened a dual-funded channel to a node whose funder policy contributed (lease or match/available/fixed). It sends tx_init_rbf either after the 72-block reservation on our original inputs lapsed (funding tx unconfirmed) or with a larger funding amount so the policy needs more inputs; both are ordinary RBF behaviour. The funder re-funds with unreserved inputs, the peer finishes negotiation, signpsbt refuses, the hook returns an error and lightningd fatals. Requires the victim to run --experimental-dual-fund with a contributing funder policy (non-default), hence AT:PRESENT. Repeatable after restart.

## Recommended fix
1. listfunds_success() requests utxopsbt with reserve=0 for the RBF PSBT, so newly selected inputs (and previously used inputs whose reservation lapsed) are committed to the funding negotiation without being reserved, which signpsbt later refuses. Fix criteria: Every input the funder contributes to an RBF PSBT must be reserved before the PSBT is returned from the rbf_channel hook (e.g. non-zero reserve with reservedok for the re-used inputs, or an explicit reserveinputs call), and the funder must verify reservation state before returning. Verify: an RBF where the funder needs an additional UTXO, or occurs after the original reservation expired, reaches tx_signatures with signpsbt succeeding.
2. json_openchannel2_sign_call() uses forward_error for signpsbt failures, so a recoverable wallet refusal becomes a JSON-RPC error reply to a hook, which lightningd treats as fatal. Fix criteria: A signpsbt failure inside the openchannel2_sign hook must never produce an error-shaped hook reply: the funder should log and return a `continue`/`reject` result so lightningd fails only this channel open. Verify: with a deliberately unreserved input, lightningd stays up and the open fails cleanly.

# bkpr-report format parser recurses without depth limit on caller-controlled nesting

## Details
`bkpr-report`'s format mini-language supports nested conditionals (`{tag[?if-set][:if-not-set]}`, each part may itself contain tags; documented in doc/schemas/bkpr-report.json). parse_report_format (plugins/bkpr/report.c:243-351) implements this by direct recursion: for each `{tag?` or `{tag:` it calls itself to parse the inner part (lines 310, 318, 329) with no depth limit. The input is the caller's `format` string taken verbatim by param_escaped_string (no length cap). The recursion depth is set entirely by the attacker: a format of N repetitions of `{tag?` (5 bytes per level, `tag` being a valid report tag) pushes N frames before the innermost call hits the end of string and returns 'Unterminated tag' at line 264 -- the error is produced only after the stack has already been consumed. Commando forwards requests up to 1 MiB (plugins/commando.c:458) and clnrest up to 2 MiB (handlers.rs:28), so roughly 200,000 levels fit in one request; each frame holds six pointer locals plus the return address and callee-saved registers (well over 40 bytes), so the default 8 MiB stack is exhausted deterministically and the bookkeeper process dies with SIGSEGV. No depth counter, length limit or stack rlimit exists on the path (lightningd sets only RLIMIT_NOFILE). A balanced input (`{tag?`*N followed by `}`*N) parses successfully and then recurses to the same depth again in format_event (lines 457, 467) for every event and in tal's del_tree when the command is freed.

bookkeeper is a builtin plugin loaded as important (plugins/bkpr/Makefile:42; lightningd/plugin.c:2578-2585), so its death makes lightningd shut down (lightningd/plugin.c:297-302) with the on-chain consequences the threat model attaches to node downtime.

The attacker is a rune bearer permitted `bkpr-report` -- over commando from any connected peer, or over clnrest HTTPS. The shipped `readonly` rune (method^list|method^get|method=summary) does not cover bkpr-report, so the operator must have issued a rune naming it; but a rune meant to let a bookkeeping client read income reports must not let that client stop the node, and that is exactly the bound runes are meant to enforce. gRPC certificate holders can also reach BkprReport, but they already hold full node authority. The same recursion exists in format_event and in freeing the parsed tree, so the fix must bound the depth at parse time.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/report.c:243–351](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/report.c#L243-L351)
   parse_report_format recurses into itself for every '{tag?' (line 310) and '{tag:' (lines 318, 329) with no depth counter; the only exits are the terminator or the '\0' check at line 264, which is reached only after the innermost call, i.e. after the full depth has been pushed. Depth equals the number of nested tag openers in the caller's string.
2. [plugins/bkpr/report.c:353–371](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/report.c#L353-L371)
   param_report_format hands the raw RPC 'format' string (param_escaped_string → json_escape_unescape_len, no length cap) straight to parse_report_format with term '\0'.
3. [plugins/bkpr/report.c:432–472](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/report.c#L432-L472)
   format_event recurses into fmt->ifset[i]/fmt->ifnotset[i] (lines 457, 467) to the same depth for each event, and because each nested report_format is tal-allocated as a child of its parent, tal_free of the tree recurses through ccan tal del_tree to the same depth when cmd is freed.
4. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:513–529](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L513-L529)
   json_bkpr_report binds the required 'format' parameter via param_report_format; bkpr-report is registered in the bookkeeper command table (line 1828) and the plugin is a builtin loaded as important (plugins/bkpr/Makefile:42 → list_of_builtin_plugins).
5. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L302)
   When an important plugin dies lightningd logs 'Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!' and exits, so a SIGSEGV in bookkeeper takes the whole node down.
6. [plugins/commando.c:458–459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L458-L459)
   commando accepts requests up to 1 MiB from a peer presenting a rune (clnrest accepts 2 MiB, plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:28); at 5 bytes per '{tag?' level that permits ~200k nested levels, far beyond what an 8 MiB stack can hold.

## Impact
Stack exhaustion kills the bookkeeper plugin with SIGSEGV. bookkeeper is an important builtin plugin, so lightningd exits (plugin.c:297-302) and channels go unmonitored until the operator restarts; the same caller can repeat it after every restart. No data disclosure or modification.

## Reproduction steps
1. A rune bearer allowed bkpr-report (commando over the peer connection, or clnrest over HTTPS) sends one request whose format is a few hundred KB to 1 MiB of repeated '{tag?'. parse_report_format recurses once per level with no bound; the depth is chosen by the attacker and the request-size limits of the exposed interfaces (1 MiB commando, 2 MiB clnrest) allow ~200k levels against an 8 MiB stack. The crash is deterministic, needs no timing or victim interaction, and the only privilege required is a rune covering a read-only reporting method.

## Recommended fix
parse_report_format, format_event and the tal tree they build recurse once per nesting level of a caller-controlled format string with no depth or length bound, so an RPC caller limited to a read-only method controls the stack depth of an important plugin. Fix criteria: The nesting depth of the format language must be bounded to a small constant at parse time (and/or the format length capped), returning a clean JSON-RPC badparam error for deeper input before any recursion proceeds past the limit. Verify by sending a bkpr-report whose format nests tens of thousands of levels (both unterminated and balanced) and confirming the plugin returns an error and keeps running.

# Roll-up PSBT mutated after a destination committed; late peer sigs make wally_psbt_combine fatal

## Details
multifundchannel drives several dual-funded (v2) opens from one roll-up PSBT (mfc->psbt), re-deriving every destination's node PSBT from it each openchannel_update round (perform_openchannel_update, plugins/spender/openchannel.c:798-877). Each dualopend commits to whatever transaction it holds when run_tx_interactive returns: as soon as a round's PSBT_UPDATED yields an empty changeset, send_next sends tx_complete and, if the peer's last message was also tx_complete, opener_commits runs (openingd/dualopend.c:1532-1577, 2190-2196, 3436-3450).

Destinations therefore commit in different rounds whenever one destination's peer contributed in the previous round: in round N the contributing destination P sees no new changes and commits on T_N, while every other destination Q must first relay P's peer's tx_add_input to its own peer, and that peer may lawfully answer with a further tx_add_input instead of tx_complete (they_complete is reset every iteration). Q's round-N reply then carries a changed PSBT; round N+1 folds it into the roll-up (T_{N+1} != T_N), re-sends openchannel_update(T_{N+1}) to the already-SECURED P (rejected with 'Channel open not in progress', dual_open_control.c:3202-3211, because open_attempt was freed on commit) and leaves P registered against a roll-up it no longer matches.

Once committed, P's peer sends tx_signatures; dualopend forwards them (handle_tx_sigs), lightningd combines them into the inflight and emits openchannel_peer_sigs carrying the inflight PSBT (T_N) (dual_open_control.c:2319-2431). json_peer_sigs (openchannel.c:563-574) calls wally_psbt_combine(mfc->psbt, psbt) and on failure plugin_err - process exit. libwally refuses to combine PSBTs whose unique transaction ids differ (BIP-174/370 combiner rule; lightningd relies on the same behaviour at dual_open_control.c:2346 but handles it non-fatally). spenderp is an important plugin, so lightningd exits with it (lightningd/plugin.c:297-303) mid-funding, with inputs reserved and peer P holding a committed, unbroadcast channel. The window stays open until post_cleanup_redo_multifundchannel replaces mfc->destinations and mfc->psbt after the cleanup round trips.

Ordering: the plugin receives RPC replies on its RPC connection and notifications on stdin (plugins/libplugin.c), so P's secured reply and P's sigs notification are not strictly FIFO; the crash needs the notification processed after round N+1's fold, which happens once Q's reply is already in (Q needs one RTT, P's commitment exchange two). A peer under the attacker's control - P itself delaying tx_signatures, or Q answering promptly - makes that ordering certain. Honest CLN accepters send all their changes before their first tx_complete and never add afterwards, so the late addition is adversarial (or non-CLN) behaviour; the candidate's original ordering (a non-contributing destination committing while a contributing one's reply changes) is impossible, since the non-contributing destination has to relay the contribution first.

Assumption: libwally-core's wally_psbt_combine (external/libwally-core submodule; gitlink absent from this checkout, version unverified) returns WALLY_EINVAL for differing PSBT ids.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/spender/openchannel.c:563–573](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/openchannel.c#L563-L573)
   json_peer_sigs combines the peer's signed PSBT (the inflight transaction that peer committed to) into the roll-up mfc->psbt and calls plugin_err (process exit of an important plugin) when wally_psbt_combine fails, which it does whenever the two PSBTs describe different transactions.
2. [plugins/spender/openchannel.c:798–876](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/openchannel.c#L798-L876)
   perform_openchannel_update short-circuits only when every v2 destination is SECURED/SIGNED. Otherwise it folds every destination's reply into the parent (changing the roll-up transaction when any peer added an input), rewrites every node PSBT from the parent, and sends openchannel_update to all v2 destinations, including ones already SECURED whose peer has committed to the previous transaction.
3. [openingd/dualopend.c:1532–1576](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1532-L1576)
   send_next: when the PSBT_UPDATED from lightningd yields an empty changeset it sends tx_complete and reports finished; a destination whose own peer was the only contributor in the previous round sees no changes and completes, while the others still have that contribution to relay.
4. [openingd/dualopend.c:2190–2195](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2190-L2195)
   run_tx_interactive resets they_complete every iteration and loops until both sides' consecutive tx_complete: a peer may answer a relayed tx_add_input with a further tx_add_input after having sent tx_complete, and the next send_next then fetches changes (reply with a changed PSBT, commitments_secured false).
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:3436–3449](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3436-L3449)
   opener_start runs opener_commits as soon as run_tx_interactive returns, so destinations commit in whichever round their own interactive exchange finishes, not in a common round.
6. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:2319–2431](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L2319-L2431)
   handle_peer_tx_sigs_msg combines the peer's tx_signatures into the inflight funding PSBT (the committed transaction) and emits openchannel_peer_sigs with that PSBT; combine failure here is handled non-fatally, unlike in the plugin.
7. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3202–3210](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3202-L3210)
   After commit channel->open_attempt is freed (3931/3965); a further openchannel_update whose PSBT txid differs from the inflight returns 'Channel open not in progress', so the secured destination fails and the mfc enters redo while its peer's sigs are still arriving and the roll-up already differs.
8. [openingd/dualopend.c:2860–2868](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2860-L2868)
   An honest CLN accepter sends tx_signatures as soon as accepter_commits returns (after lightningd's SEND_TX_SIGS), i.e. right behind its commitment_signed, so the secured peer's openchannel_peer_sigs notification closely trails its 'commitments_secured' reply; an attacker-run peer chooses the timing freely.

## Impact
plugin_err exits spenderp, an important plugin, so lightningd shuts down mid-funding with inputs reserved and a peer holding a committed-but-unbroadcast channel. Even in the non-crash ordering the secured destination's open is destroyed ('Must spend input to reset'). No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker runs a remote node the victim chose as one v2 destination of a multifundchannel (dual-fund enabled) alongside at least one other v2 destination whose peer contributes an input (liquidity seller, funder policy, or a second attacker node). When the plugin relays that contribution, the attacker's peer answers with its own tx_add_input, so the roll-up changes after the other destination has committed; that destination's tx_signatures notification then fails wally_psbt_combine and spenderp exits, taking lightningd down. Controlling both destinations removes all timing uncertainty. No privileges; requires the victim to be running that command.

## Recommended fix
1. perform_openchannel_update keeps mutating the roll-up PSBT and re-driving openchannel_update for destinations that have already exchanged commitments, so the roll-up no longer matches the transaction a committed peer will sign. Fix criteria: Once any v2 destination reports commitments_secured, the roll-up transaction must be frozen: further peer changes from other destinations must fail that other destination (or be rejected) rather than alter the funding transaction, and SECURED destinations must not be sent further openchannel_update calls. Verify with two v2 peers where exactly one contributes an input: the open completes (or fails cleanly for the contributing peer) and the roll-up txid never changes after the first commitment.
2. json_peer_sigs turns a combine failure - reachable from peer timing/behaviour - into process termination via plugin_err. Fix criteria: A PSBT that cannot be combined with the roll-up must fail/clean up that destination (openchannel_abort, unreserve) and return an error to the caller; spenderp must not exit. Verify by delivering an openchannel_peer_sigs with a different-txid PSBT for a registered destination: the command fails gracefully and lightningd stays up.
