# listnodes re-emits gossip node alias bytes unvalidated; invalid UTF-8 kills topology plugin, lightningd exits

## Details
The topology plugin (shipped, `important`, sole provider of `listnodes`) renders each node's alias straight from the gossip_store record: fromwire_node_announcement() yields the raw 32 alias bytes, json_add_node() (plugins/topology.c:378-382) wraps them with json_escape() and json_add_escaped_string(). ccan's json_escape only escapes control characters, quotes and backslashes; bytes >= 0x80 pass through untouched. BOLT 7 says the alias MUST be valid UTF-8, but nothing in CLN enforces it: the wire field is `byte,32` (peer_wire.csv:364), so fromwire does not utf8_check it, and gossipd's gossmap_manage_node_announcement() (gossmap_manage.c:1190-1226) checks only parseability, wireaddrs and the signature before persisting the message.

lightningd reads plugin replies through jsonrpc_io_parse() -> json_parse_input(), whose validate_jsmn_datum() rejects any string token failing utf8_check() (json_parse_simple.c:353-356). plugin_read_json() turns that into plugin_kill() (plugin.c:719-725); destroy_plugin() sees the plugin is important and calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1) (plugin.c:297-303). So a single node_announcement whose alias contains e.g. 0xFF or a truncated multibyte sequence makes every `listnodes` reply that includes that node unparsable and shuts the node down.

Who triggers it: any gossip participant with one public channel can broadcast such an announcement; every CLN node that stores it is affected, and the bad record persists in gossip_store so the failure recurs after restart. The crash fires whenever anything asks topology for that node or for all nodes: an operator or UI (`lightning-cli listnodes`, RTL/Thunderhub polling), a rune bearer via clnrest/commando, and automatic paths: `checkmessage` without pubkey calls listnodes id=<recovered key> (signmessage.c:215-227) - so a victim verifying a message signed by the attacker's node key crashes - and the default `sql` plugin's nodes refresh calls listnodes per new node_announcement (sql.c:1266-1272). The sql plugin already hex-encodes non-UTF-8 column text (sql.c:483-486), showing the maintainers know plugin output must be valid UTF-8; topology has no equivalent guard. DNS hostnames in the same announcement are validated (wireaddr.c:76-86), making the alias the single unvalidated gossip string on this path.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/topology.c:378–382](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/topology.c#L378-L382)
   json_add_node(): the raw 32 alias bytes parsed from the stored node_announcement at 360-368 are tal_strndup'd (NUL padding ends the string) and passed through json_escape() into json_add_escaped_string() with no utf8_check(), so whatever bytes the announcing node signed land verbatim between quotes in the plugin's listnodes reply on stdout. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [ccan/ccan/json\_escape/json\_escape.c:113–123](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/json_escape/json_escape.c#L113-L123)
   escape() only rewrites bytes < 0x20, 0x7f, '"' and '\\'; every byte >= 0x80 is copied unchanged (the 'taken' fast path at 44-60 steals the raw string outright), so invalid UTF-8 sequences survive escaping.
3. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:353–356](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L353-L356)
   validate_jsmn_datum(): every JSMN_STRING must pass utf8_check(); otherwise the whole parse fails. This validator runs on everything lightningd reads from a plugin's stdout (jsonrpc_io.c:79-86).
4. [lightningd/plugin.c:719–724](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L719-L724)
   plugin_read_json(): a jsonrpc_io_parse() error on plugin output is answered with plugin_kill() (SIGKILL + tal_free).
5. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L302)
   destroy_plugin(): topology is a builtin `important` plugin, so its death logs 'shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1).
6. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1190–1225](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1190-L1225)
   gossipd accepts a node_announcement after only fromwire parsing, wireaddr parsing and signature verification; the alias is never validated before the message is persisted to gossip_store for every reader.
7. [wire/peer\_wire.csv:364](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/peer_wire.csv#L364)
   node_announcement.alias is declared `byte,32`, not a `utf8` field, so the generated fromwire_node_announcement does not apply fromwire_utf8_array's utf8_check.
8. [lightningd/signmessage.c:215–226](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/signmessage.c#L215-L226)
   checkmessage without `pubkey` automatically calls listnodes id=<recovered key> on the topology plugin; a message signed by the attacker's node key reaches the vulnerable path with no explicit listnodes call.
9. [plugins/sql.c:1266–1271](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/sql.c#L1266-L1271)
   The default `sql` plugin's nodes refresh issues listnodes id=<node> for each new node_announcement in gossip_store when a query touches the nodes table - another automatic caller.
10. [common/wireaddr.c:76–85](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/wireaddr.c#L76-L85)
   Contrast: DNS hostnames in the same announcement are rejected by is_dnsaddr() at parse time, so the alias is the one gossip-authored string that reaches JSON output unvalidated.

## Impact
lightningd exits (lightningd_exit after the important plugin is killed), taking channels, HTLC processing and chain watching offline; the record persists in gossip_store so the crash recurs on every listnodes until the attacker's alias changes - availability HIGH. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any Lightning node with one public channel (or anyone who can relay gossip). It signs and broadcasts a node_announcement whose alias holds invalid UTF-8; gossipd stores it unconditionally. Thereafter any listnodes covering that node - a routine operator/UI/rune-bearer call, or the automatic checkmessage/sql paths - makes topology emit an unparsable reply and lightningd exits. No non-default configuration is needed (topology and gossip are always on) and no defence must be bypassed; a human or tool merely has to perform the routine listnodes/checkmessage action (UI:PASSIVE).

## Recommended fix
1. json_add_node() in plugins/topology.c emits gossip-authored alias bytes without verifying they are valid UTF-8, violating the invariant that plugin stdout is strictly valid JSON (which lightningd enforces by killing the plugin). Fix criteria: The alias emitted by listnodes must always be valid UTF-8 (e.g. utf8_check() and fall back to a sanitised/hex form, as sql.c does for column text). Verify: a stored node_announcement with alias bytes 0xFF... yields a successful listnodes reply and lightningd keeps running.
2. gossipd persists node_announcements whose alias violates BOLT 7's UTF-8 requirement, exposing every gossip_store reader to the invalid bytes. Fix criteria: Optionally, gossipd rejects (or sanitises before storing) node_announcements whose alias is not valid UTF-8, consistent with how malformed wireaddrs are already rejected. Verify: such an announcement is not written to gossip_store.

# multifundchannel retry re-registers mfc in notification list: self-loop and use-after-free

## Details
multifundchannel supports best-effort retries (`minchannels`): when a destination fails after the parallel channel starts, redo_multifundchannel runs mfc_cleanup (unreserveinputs, openchannel_abort/fundchannel_cancel for the survivors), then post_cleanup_redo_multifundchannel (multifundchannel.c:1681-1793) drops failed destinations, resets the survivors to START_NOT_YET and re-runs the whole flow on the same `struct multifundchannel_command` via command_timer. The mfc is allocated under `cmd` (multifundchannel.c:1990) and lives until the command finishes.

For v2 (dual-funded) destinations the mfc must be found from `openchannel_peer_sigs` notifications, so perform_funding_tx_finalize (multifundchannel.c:921) calls register_mfc(mfc) = `list_add_tail(&mfc_commands, &mfc->list)` + `tal_add_destructor(mfc, destroy_mfc)` (openchannel.c:21-27). Nothing records that the mfc is already linked, no code unlinks it between attempts (the only list_del is destroy_mfc), and the retry runs perform_funding_tx_finalize again, so the same list node is inserted twice and the destructor is added twice. With ccan list_add_before_ (ccan/ccan/list/list.h:228-236) and a single live mfc this yields head.next == mfc, mfc.next == mfc, mfc.prev == mfc: a self-loop (with other registered mfcs the list is corrupted in similar ways: the earlier node drops out of the forward chain and the head keeps a stale pointer after free).

Why a v2 destination survives the redo: post_cleanup only drops v2 destinations that are FAILED or has_commitments_secured() (multifundchannel.c:1712). In the opener's interactive-tx loop (openingd/dualopend.c send_next:1532-1575) dualopend sends the changes delivered by an `openchannel_update`, then, when its cached changeset is exhausted, calls fetch_psbt_changes -> WIRE_DUALOPEND_PSBT_CHANGED -> lightningd answers the pending `openchannel_update` with `commitments_secured:false` (dual_open_control.c:3699) before tx_complete is ever sent. perform_funding_tx_finalize always adds the funding outputs after openchannel_init, so round 1 of openchannel_update always delivers changes and therefore always returns commitments_secured=false for every v2 destination; only a later round with no changes reaches tx_complete/commitment_signed and SECURED. Hence when the attacker destination B fails in round 1, every other v2 destination A is in MULTIFUNDCHANNEL_UPDATED, passes the has_commitments_secured filter, gets openchannel_abort'ed and retried, and the retry re-registers the mfc.

Making B fail at the update stage is peer-controlled: after accept_channel2 B waits for the tx_add_output carrying the funding output (added only in the update phase) and sends tx_abort, an error, or disconnects. dualopend handles this via open_abort/negotiation_aborted -> process exit -> dualopen_errmsg (dual_open_control.c:4320) -> channel_cleanup_commands (lightningd/channel.c:1250-1268) -> command_fail of the pending openchannel_update -> openchannel_update_err -> fail_destination_tok -> FAILED; perform_openchannel_update's first loop (openchannel.c:802-806) then calls redo_multifundchannel. A serial_id collision in B's contribution that makes update_parent_psbt fail (openchannel.c:832-841) reaches the same redo with A still UPDATED. An honestly flaky peer in the same position triggers the same corruption.

Consequences:
1) While the retried command runs, any openchannel_peer_sigs for a channel_id that is not one of this mfc's destinations makes find_dest_by_channel_id (openchannel.c:29-44; list_for_each_safe on the self-looped list) spin forever: lightningd emits that notification for every dual-funded channel whose peer sends tx_signatures (dual_open_control.c:2429), including a channel the attacker opens to the victim, so spenderp stops servicing fundchannel/multifundchannel/multiwithdraw/splice and never answers again.
2) When the command completes and `cmd`/mfc are freed, destroy_mfc runs twice; list_del on the self-looped node only rewrites the node's own pointers (list.h:324-333; CCAN_LIST_DEBUG is not defined in release builds), so mfc_commands.n.next/prev keep pointing at freed memory. The next openchannel_peer_sigs notification (attacker-triggered as above, or the operator's next v2 fundchannel) dereferences the freed mfc (`tal_count(mfc->destinations)`, dest->channel_id), and the next register_mfc writes `freed->next = new` into freed memory: use-after-free read/write in the `important` spender plugin, whose crash makes lightningd exit, or peer-signature notifications matched against garbage.

tests/test_opening.py::test_multifunding_v2_best_effort only retries before register_mfc (connect/fundchannel_start failures) or after the v2 destination is already SECURED (so it is dropped) and never exercises this path.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/spender/multifundchannel.c:914–925](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/multifundchannel.c#L914-L925)
   perform_funding_tx_finalize calls register_mfc(mfc) whenever there are v2 destinations. It runs once per attempt, so a retry re-registers the same mfc; this is where the fix belongs (register once per command lifetime).
2. [plugins/spender/openchannel.c:15–26](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/openchannel.c#L15-L26)
   register_mfc does list_add_tail(&mfc_commands, &mfc->list) and tal_add_destructor(destroy_mfc) with no check that the node is already linked; a second add of the sole element makes mfc->list.next/prev point to itself while the head still points at it, and the doubled destructor leaves the head dangling after free. destroy_mfc is the only list_del in the plugin.
3. [plugins/spender/multifundchannel.c:1700–1791](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/multifundchannel.c#L1700-L1791)
   post_cleanup_redo_multifundchannel drops only FAILED or commitment-secured v2 destinations (1712-1722), resets the rest to START_NOT_YET and re-runs perform_multifundchannel via command_timer on the same mfc; the mfc and its list node are reused, never freed or unlinked between attempts.
4. [plugins/spender/openchannel.c:790–841](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/openchannel.c#L790-L841)
   perform_openchannel_update runs after every v2 destination's openchannel_update has returned; a FAILED destination (peer tx_abort/error/disconnect -> openchannel_update_err -> fail_destination_tok) or an update_parent_psbt failure triggers redo_multifundchannel while the other v2 destinations are still UPDATED (commitments_secured=false), i.e. survivors that will be retried.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:1532–1574](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1532-L1574)
   send_next: after the changes delivered by an openchannel_update are sent, dualopend calls fetch_psbt_changes (PSBT_CHANGED -> openchannel_update returns commitments_secured=false, dual_open_control.c:3699) before it will send tx_complete. Since the funding outputs are added only in the update phase, round 1 always leaves every v2 destination UPDATED, not SECURED, so a surviving v2 destination at redo time is the normal case, not a race.
6. [plugins/spender/openchannel.c:29–43](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/openchannel.c#L29-L43)
   find_dest_by_channel_id walks mfc_commands with list_for_each_safe on every openchannel_peer_sigs notification (emitted by lightningd for every dual-funded channel whose peer sends tx_signatures, dual_open_control.c:2429); on the self-looped list it never terminates unless a destination matches, and after the mfc is freed it dereferences the dangling head pointer.
7. [ccan/ccan/list/list.h:227–236](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/list/list.h#L227-L236)
   list_add_before_ with n already the tail sets n->prev = n and n->next (via p->prev->next) = n: the self-loop. list_del_ (324-333) then only rewires n's own pointers, leaving h->n.next/prev pointing to the freed node; CCAN_LIST_DEBUG is not defined in release builds.

## Impact
Infinite loop in the important spender plugin disables all on-chain spend RPCs (fundchannel, multifundchannel, multiwithdraw, splice) until lightningd is restarted; the use-after-free (read of freed mfc/destinations in find_dest_by_channel_id, write of freed->next in the next register_mfc) crashes spenderp and, because it is an important plugin, lightningd exits. The dangling-node write and garbage channel_id matching give limited integrity impact (peer signatures could be combined into the wrong in-flight funding PSBT). No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote peer that the victim lists as one destination of a multifundchannel with at least one other dual-fund destination and minchannels below the destination count (e.g. an operator buying liquidity from several advertised nodes). The victim must run with experimental-dual-fund, which v2 destinations already require. After accept_channel2 the attacker waits for the tx_add_output carrying the funding output (sent only in the openchannel_update phase) and sends tx_abort or disconnects; lightningd fails the pending openchannel_update (dualopen_errmsg -> channel_cleanup_commands), spender redoes with the other v2 destination still UPDATED (round 1 of openchannel_update always returns commitments_secured=false, dualopend send_next/fetch_psbt_changes), and the retry re-registers the mfc, corrupting mfc_commands. The attacker then opens a dual-funded channel to the victim and sends tx_signatures to raise a stray openchannel_peer_sigs: during the retry this hangs spenderp; after the command finishes it dereferences the freed mfc. No shipped defence intervenes (no registered-flag, ccan list debug off). Deterministic once the victim issues such a command; the same corruption also arises from an honestly flaky peer.

## Recommended fix
1. register_mfc is invoked on every funding attempt of the same multifundchannel_command without tracking that the list node is already linked, so the best-effort retry path double-inserts it into mfc_commands and double-adds the destructor. Fix criteria: An mfc is present in mfc_commands at most once for its lifetime: register it once per command (or unlink before re-registering) and add the destructor once. Verify by forcing a retry with a surviving v2 destination (another v2 peer sends tx_abort during the openchannel_update round) and then delivering openchannel_peer_sigs for an unrelated channel both during and after the command: find_dest_by_channel_id terminates, and no freed memory is reachable from the list.
2. find_dest_by_channel_id trusts the intrusive list to be well-formed and is reached from every openchannel_peer_sigs notification, so any list corruption becomes a hang or a dangling dereference in an important plugin. Fix criteria: Notification handling cannot loop or dereference freed memory on a malformed mfc_commands list (e.g. CCAN_LIST_DEBUG-style checks or list_del_init plus a linked-state flag), so a future double registration fails loudly instead of corrupting memory.

# splicein/spliceout interpolate caller strings into splice script, allowing segment injection

## Details
`splicein` and `spliceout` (plugins/spender/splice.c, registered unconditionally in splice_commands) are thin wrappers that build a splice-script program by string interpolation and hand it to the full splice-script compiler/executor used by `dev-splice`:

    splicein:  tal_fmt("wallet -> %s + fee; %s -> %s", amount, amount, channel)
    spliceout: tal_fmt("%s -> %s + fee; 100%% -> %s", channel, amount, destination)

All three parameters are read with `param_string`, which copies the raw JSON token bytes (common/json_param.c:456-463) with no validation and no escape decoding. The DSL treats `;` (and a raw newline) as a statement delimiter (common/splice_script.c is_delimiter, line 2450) and `->` as its operator, so any parameter containing `;` terminates the intended segment and appends arbitrary further segments. (Because `param_string` does not decode JSON escapes, a `\n` escape does not become a delimiter over JSON-RPC; `;` needs no decoding and suffices.) parse_splice_script compiles the whole string into a list of actions, listpeerchannels_get_result runs validate_splice_cmd (which only checks fee-payer count and bitcoin-address destinations) and handle_splice_cmd then stfu's and splices every channel named by any action.

Examples that compile to multiple independent actions:

- spliceout channel=<C> amount=100000 destination="wallet; <D> -> 100%"  → script `<C> -> 100000 + fee; 100% -> wallet; <D> -> 100%`: additionally drains 100% of channel D to the on-chain wallet.
- spliceout channel=<C> amount="1M; <D> -> 100%; wallet -> 1M"  → also empties D even when `destination` is not supplied and the rune pins `channel` exactly.
- splicein channel="<C>; <D> -> 100%" amount=1000  → splices 1000 sat into C and empties D.

Why this matters under the recorded threat model: runes are the intended bound on lesser callers (commando peers, clnrest clients), and `pname<param>` conditions let an operator grant e.g. `method=spliceout&pnamechannel=<C>`. lightningd/runes.c check_condition evaluates such a condition against the raw token of the named parameter only, so `amount`/`destination` remain free-form; because the wrappers splice those strings into a program rather than treating them as data, the bearer can act on every channel of the node (splice liquidity out of any channel to the wallet, move funds between arbitrary channels, choose a feerate via `+fee@N`) — operations the rune never granted. Funds stay in node custody (bitcoin-address payouts are rejected by validate_splice_cmd), but all channel balances can be rearranged, routing liquidity destroyed and on-chain fees incurred at the bearer's discretion. The documented interface (doc/schemas/splicein.json, spliceout.json) describes `channel`, `amount` and `destination` as single values, i.e. one splice action on one channel; the sanctioned path for a channel-pinned rune reaches only that channel.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/spender/splice.c:2226–2234](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/splice.c#L2226-L2234)
   json_splicein reads `channel` and `amount` via param_string and interpolates them verbatim with tal_fmt("wallet -> %s + fee; %s -> %s"); no escaping or rejection of ';', newline or '->'.
2. [plugins/spender/splice.c:2271–2284](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/splice.c#L2271-L2284)
   json_spliceout does the same with `channel`, `amount` and the optional `destination` string via tal_fmt("%s -> %s + fee; 100%% -> %s").
3. [common/json\_param.c:456–463](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_param.c#L456-L463)
   param_string is a raw tal_strndup of the JSON token bytes: no validation, so ';' and '->' arrive unchanged (JSON escapes are not decoded, so a literal ';' is the usable delimiter).
4. [common/splice\_script.c:2450–2465](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/splice_script.c#L2450-L2465)
   is_delimiter treats '\n' and ';' as segment separators and parse_splice_script tokenises the whole interpolated string, so a parameter containing ';' starts a new, fully independent splice action.
5. [plugins/spender/splice.c:2105–2144](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/splice.c#L2105-L2144)
   listpeerchannels_get_result compiles the composed script, applies only validate_splice_cmd (fee-payer count, bitcoin-address rejection) and calls handle_splice_cmd; nothing re-checks that the actions are confined to the channel/amount the caller named.
6. [plugins/spender/splice.c:2019–2040](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/splice.c#L2019-L2040)
   handle_splice_cmd stfu's every channel_id present in any compiled action and proceeds to execute them all (splice_init/update/signed, fundpsbt, signpsbt, broadcast).
7. [lightningd/runes.c:897–911](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L897-L911)
   check_condition evaluates a pname<param> rune restriction against the raw token of that one named parameter; a rune pinning `channel` leaves `amount` and `destination` unconstrained, which is why the injection escalates past the rune's bound.
8. [doc/schemas/spliceout.json](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/schemas/spliceout.json) (whole file)
   The schema presents `channel`, `amount` and `destination` as single values (a channel identifier/query, an amount, a destination), i.e. the interface promises one splice action on one channel — the scope a rune author relies on.

## Impact
The bearer gains control over splice actions on every channel of the node: arbitrary rebalancing between channels and wallet, draining channel liquidity, choosing on-chain feerates. Funds stay in node custody so this is not theft, but channel balances (the asset a channel-pinned rune was meant to scope) are fully under attacker control: integrity HIGH. Draining channels halts routing and incurs on-chain fees: availability LOW. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A rune bearer permitted `splicein` or `spliceout` (via commando from a peer connection, or clnrest) supplies a channel/amount/destination string containing ';' followed by extra `<chan> -> <amount>` segments. The wrapper interpolates it verbatim, parse_splice_script accepts the extra segments, validate_splice_cmd does not inspect channel scope, and the executor performs every action. The attacker needs only a rune for these methods (PR:L); the attack is a single RPC call with no timing or environmental precondition.

## Recommended fix
json_splicein/json_spliceout treat caller-supplied channel, amount and destination strings as splice-script source text, so DSL metacharacters (';', newline, '->') in a parameter change the program structure instead of being data. Fix criteria: The wrappers must produce exactly one splice action for the named channel/amount/destination regardless of parameter contents: either construct the splice_script_result structs directly from typed parameters, or reject any parameter containing delimiter/arrow/whitespace characters before composing the script. Verify that spliceout with destination "wallet; <D> -> 100%" (and the amount/channel variants) is rejected and no action on D is attempted.

# Splice script autocomplete_chan_id writes 33 bytes into 32-byte stack channel_id

## Details
The splice-script compiler (common/splice_script.c, linked into the shipped `spenderp` plugin, which lightningd loads as `important`) autocompletes partial channel ids in autocomplete_chan_id(). It derives `len = strlen(token->str) / 2`, bounds it only against PUBKEY_CMPR_LEN (33, the node-id size) instead of sizeof(candidate.id), and calls `hex_decode(token->str, len * 2, candidate.id, len)` where `candidate` is a stack `struct channel_id` whose `id` array is 32 bytes. For any token of 66 or 67 hex characters, len is 33 and hex_decode writes 33 bytes, overflowing the stack object by one byte whose value the caller chooses (the 33rd decoded byte).

Reachability: type_data() tries, in order, percent/?/*, NODEID_REGEX (which only matches 64 chars: `^0[23][0-9A-Fa-f]{62}$`), bitcoin address, CHANID_REGEX (64 chars), `wallet`, `fee`, autocomplete_node_id, then autocomplete_chan_id. A 66-char hex string that is not the node id of one of our channel peers (a typo, any node we have no channel with, or a deliberately chosen value) fails autocomplete_node_id (match == NULL) and falls through to autocomplete_chan_id with len 33, triggering the write. The unit test corpus (common/test/run-splice_script.c) only uses 66-char ids that match a configured channel peer, so the branch is never exercised.

Attacker: any RPC caller allowed to invoke `splicein`, `spliceout` or `dev-splice` — the operator, or a rune bearer via commando (over the peer connection), clnrest or grpc. splicein/spliceout interpolate the `channel`, `amount` and `destination` strings directly into the script (`wallet -> %s + fee; %s -> %s`), so e.g. `splicein channel=<any> amount=aa<64 hex>` or `spliceout channel=aa<64 hex> amount=1000` suffices; because `amount` is also interpolated, a rune that pins `channel` to a specific id does not prevent the trigger. The compile runs in listpeerchannels_get_result before any dryrun or stfu step.

Impact: with the default `-fstack-protector-strong` (configure CDEBUGFLAGS), GCC/Clang place array-containing locals adjacent to the guard, so the overflowing byte most likely lands on the canary's low byte and any non-zero value aborts spenderp with 'stack smashing detected'; because spenderp is an important plugin, lightningd shuts down. Where the protector is absent or the frame layout differs, it is a one-byte stack write of attacker-chosen content into adjacent frame data (`match`, `len`, saved registers). Either way an RPC call a rune bounds to 'splice on channel X' becomes a node-wide crash primitive.

## Evidence
1. [common/splice\_script.c:1023–1041](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/splice_script.c#L1023-L1041)
   autocomplete_chan_id computes len = strlen(str)/2, rejects only len > PUBKEY_CMPR_LEN (33), then hex_decode(token->str, len*2, candidate.id, len). candidate is a struct channel_id (u8 id[32]); for a 66- or 67-character token len==33 so hex_decode writes 33 bytes into the 32-byte stack buffer.
2. [common/splice\_script.c:1169–1198](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/splice_script.c#L1169-L1198)
   type_data reaches autocomplete_chan_id for any TOK_STR not matched earlier. A 66-hex-char string does not match NODEID_REGEX (64 chars), CHANID_REGEX (64), wallet/fee/address; autocomplete_node_id returns false when no peer has that node id, so control falls to autocomplete_chan_id with len 33.
3. [common/splice\_script.c:29–30](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/splice_script.c#L29-L30)
   CHANID_REGEX and NODEID_REGEX both match exactly 64 characters (NODEID_REGEX is ^0[23][0-9A-Fa-f]{62}$), so a real 66-character node id never takes the regex path and always falls to the autocomplete functions with len == 33.
4. [ccan/ccan/str/hex/hex.c:24–39](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/str/hex/hex.c#L24-L39)
   hex_decode writes exactly bufsize bytes to buf when slen == 2*bufsize; the caller passes bufsize=33 for a 32-byte destination.
5. [plugins/spender/splice.c:2227–2235](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/splice.c#L2227-L2235)
   splicein interpolates the caller's raw 'channel' and 'amount' strings into the script compiled by parse_splice_script in listpeerchannels_get_result (2105-2107), before any dryrun/stfu step; spliceout (channel/amount/destination) and dev-splice (free-form script) likewise. Because 'amount' is interpolated too, a rune that pins the channel parameter does not block the trigger.

## Impact
Deterministic abort of spenderp (important plugin) terminates lightningd: availability HIGH. The write is one attacker-controlled byte beyond a stack object; in builds without the stack protector, or where the byte misses the canary, it corrupts adjacent frame data, so a low integrity impact is recorded; no confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A rune bearer (commando over the peer connection, clnrest, grpc) or operator calls splicein/spliceout/dev-splice with a 66- or 67-character hex token that is not a current peer's node id; the 'amount' parameter is interpolated into the script as well, so a rune restricting the channel parameter does not block it. The script compiler runs unconditionally before dryrun or stfu; hex_decode writes the 33rd byte past the stack struct. No defence stands in the way other than the stack canary, which converts the write into an abort of the important plugin.

## Recommended fix
autocomplete_chan_id bounds the decoded length against PUBKEY_CMPR_LEN (33) instead of sizeof(struct channel_id) (32), so hex_decode can be asked to fill 33 bytes of a 32-byte stack buffer. Fix criteria: The decoded prefix length passed to hex_decode must never exceed sizeof(candidate.id) (and sizeof(candidate.k) in the node-id sibling); tokens longer than 64 hex characters must be rejected or truncated before decoding. Verify by compiling a script containing a 66- and 67-character hex token that matches no peer and confirming the compiler returns an error rather than writing past the buffer (ASan build).

# Duplicate peer tx_signatures regresses destination state, aborting spenderp (lightningd exits)

## Details
The spender plugin (spenderp, an `important` builtin loaded by plugins_set_builtin_plugins_dir, plugin.c:2576-2583; its death makes lightningd exit, plugin.c:297-303) collects peers' funding signatures for v2 (dual-funded) opens via the `openchannel_peer_sigs` notification. In json_peer_sigs (plugins/spender/openchannel.c:581-585) the destination state is rewritten on every notification:

    if (dest->state != MULTIFUNDCHANNEL_SECURED)
        dest->state = MULTIFUNDCHANNEL_SIGNED_NOT_SECURED;
    else
        dest->state = MULTIFUNDCHANNEL_SIGNED;

The code assumes exactly one notification per channel. But a remote peer can send `tx_signatures` as many times as it likes once commitments are exchanged: dualopend's main loop dispatches every WIRE_TX_SIGNATURES to handle_tx_sigs (openingd/dualopend.c:4330), which has no duplicate guard (its only early-outs are our own channel_ready already sent, peer channel_ready seen, missing psbt, txid mismatch, no commitments) and forwards WIRE_DUALOPEND_FUNDING_SIGS each time (dualopend.c:1449-1453); lightningd's handle_peer_tx_sigs_msg (dual_open_control.c:2319-2431) combines the PSBT and unconditionally ends with notify_openchannel_peer_sigs. Nothing in the path suppresses a repeat.

Single destination (plain `fundchannel` is a thin wrapper around a one-destination multifundchannel, plugins/spender/fundchannel.c:35-79; the destination is v2 whenever the peer negotiated option_dual_fund, multifundchannel.c:1572-1575): notification #1 moves the dest SECURED->SIGNED, check_sigs_ready -> collect_sigs -> perform_signpsbt sends `signpsbt` to lightningd and sets sigs_collected. Notification #2, processed while signpsbt is in flight (one RPC round trip including synchronous hsmd signing), moves SIGNED->SIGNED_NOT_SECURED; check_sigs_ready finds it not ready and returns. When the signpsbt reply arrives, after_signpsbt (multifundchannel.c:640) does `assert(dest->state == expected_state)` with expected_state == MULTIFUNDCHANNEL_SIGNED and aborts. Asserts are compiled in (no NDEBUG). lightningd sees the important plugin die and exits.

Multiple destinations: if the duplicate arrives after the attacker's destination has reached SIGNED but before all other destinations are SIGNED, the regressed destination can never become SIGNED again (the only SIGNED_NOT_SECURED->SIGNED transition is in openchannel_update_ok, openchannel.c:744-745, and no further openchannel_update round runs once every destination is SECURED/SIGNED), check_sigs_ready never fires, the multifundchannel command never completes, its UTXOs stay reserved and every peer's channel stays stuck at DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED.

Timing: libplugin processes stdin notifications one at a time and synchronously (ld_read_json, libplugin.c:2270-2294), so notification #1 fully runs (including sending signpsbt) before #2 is read; RPC replies arrive on the plugin's separate RPC connection, so per-message ordering between #2 and the signpsbt reply is not guaranteed, but the acceptor (with no inputs it sends tx_signatures right after its commitment_signed) simply sends several copies spaced across the round-trip; any copy landing in the SIGNED window triggers the abort, copies landing earlier (dest still UPDATED) are absorbed by openchannel_update_ok, and copies landing after after_signpsbt (state DONE) are harmless because mfc_cleanup treats SIGNED_NOT_SECURED as nothing-to-do.

Preconditions: the victim runs with --experimental-dual-fund and issues fundchannel/multifundchannel towards the attacker's node (e.g. to buy advertised liquidity); the attacker is an unauthenticated remote peer and needs no privileges on the victim.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/spender/openchannel.c:576–589](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/openchannel.c#L576-L589)
   json_peer_sigs unconditionally rewrites dest->state on every openchannel_peer_sigs notification: any state other than SECURED (including SIGNED and DONE) becomes SIGNED_NOT_SECURED. A second notification for the same channel therefore moves a destination from SIGNED back to SIGNED_NOT_SECURED.
2. [plugins/spender/multifundchannel.c:631–642](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/multifundchannel.c#L631-L642)
   after_signpsbt (the signpsbt reply callback) asserts every v2 destination is still MULTIFUNDCHANNEL_SIGNED. If the second notification was processed while signpsbt was in flight, the state is SIGNED_NOT_SECURED and assert() aborts the plugin.
3. [plugins/spender/openchannel.c:468–523](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/openchannel.c#L468-L523)
   check_sigs_ready requires every v2 destination to be exactly SIGNED; a destination regressed to SIGNED_NOT_SECURED can never return to SIGNED (the only transition is in openchannel_update_ok, which is not called again), so in the multi-destination case the command hangs forever with UTXOs reserved.
4. [openingd/dualopend.c:1364–1453](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1364-L1453)
   handle_tx_sigs has no guard against a second tx_signatures after commitments: it re-finalizes the peer's inputs and sends WIRE_DUALOPEND_FUNDING_SIGS to lightningd each time (the only early-outs are channel_ready already seen, missing psbt, txid mismatch, no commitments).
5. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:2319–2430](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L2319-L2430)
   handle_peer_tx_sigs_msg combines the PSBT and always ends with notify_openchannel_peer_sigs; nothing suppresses repeated notifications for the same inflight.

## Impact
spenderp is an important plugin: its abort makes lightningd exit (plugin.c:297-303), taking the whole node down while channel-funding transactions and reservations are in flight. In the multi-destination variant the command hangs forever with wallet UTXOs reserved and all peers' opens stuck. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer that the victim opens a dual-funded channel to (fundchannel or multifundchannel, --experimental-dual-fund enabled). After the commitment_signed exchange the attacker sends tx_signatures twice (or several times, spaced over the signpsbt round-trip). dualopend and lightningd forward each as a fresh openchannel_peer_sigs notification; spenderp regresses the destination state and the pending after_signpsbt assert aborts the plugin, which lightningd treats as fatal. No defenses stand in the way; the only requirements are the non-default dual-fund option and the victim initiating the open.

## Recommended fix
1. json_peer_sigs treats every openchannel_peer_sigs notification as the first one and overwrites dest->state, so a repeated notification moves a SIGNED (or DONE) destination back to SIGNED_NOT_SECURED, violating the state machine's monotonicity that after_signpsbt and check_sigs_ready rely on. Fix criteria: A repeated notification for a channel whose destination is already SIGNED, DONE or FAILED must leave the state unchanged (and not re-run combine/check_sigs_ready). Verify by delivering two openchannel_peer_sigs for the same channel_id around a signpsbt round-trip: the command must complete normally, no assert fires, and the multi-destination command does not hang.
2. after_signpsbt turns a peer-reachable state deviation into a process abort via assert(). Fix criteria: A destination in an unexpected state at signpsbt completion must result in a failed/cleaned-up command (unreserve, abort peers) rather than plugin termination. Verify that no peer-driven sequence of notifications can reach an assert()/plugin_err in the spender signing path.

# Legacy encrypted hsm_secret derives its key with a fixed Argon2id salt, allowing precomputed and multi-target passphrase cracking

## Details
The legacy 73-byte encrypted hsm_secret format protects the node's 32-byte master seed at rest with libsodium secretstream (XChaCha20-Poly1305) under a key derived by Argon2id (OPSLIMIT/MEMLIMIT_MODERATE) from the operator's passphrase. get_encryption_key() (common/hsm_secret.c:53-79) passes a hard-coded 16-byte salt, "c-lightning\0\0\0\0\0", for every installation, so the passphrase-to-key mapping is identical across all Core Lightning nodes. The whole point of a KDF salt is defeated: an attacker who obtains encrypted hsm_secret files (leaked backups, stolen disks, exposed lightning-dir volumes) can (a) precompute a dictionary of (passphrase -> key) pairs once, before any theft, and test any later-obtained file instantly, and (b) crack a corpus of N stolen files for the Argon2id cost of one, since one derivation per guess serves every target. With a per-file random salt each guess would cost the full MODERATE Argon2id work (256 MiB, roughly a second) per target. Whether a given file falls still depends on the passphrase being within the attacker's dictionary; the fixed salt removes the per-target cost that salting is meant to impose and makes bulk/precomputed attacks economical. The format is structural: 73 bytes = secretstream header + 32-byte seed + Poly1305 tag (HS_HEADER_LEN + HS_CIPHERTEXT_LEN), identified purely by length in detect_hsm_secret_type(), with no room for a salt.

lightningd itself no longer writes this format (hsmd/hsmd.c:323, 387-388: new secrets are always BIP39 mnemonics, and --encrypted-hsm is deprecated at lightningd/options.c:608-611), but the weakness is not confined to pre-existing files: the installed tools/lightning-hsmtool (Makefile:464 BIN_PROGRAMS) `encrypt` command (tools/lightning-hsmtool.c:169-249) still produces new fixed-salt files from a legacy 32-byte plain seed, the installed manpage doc/lightning-hsmtool.8.md documents it without caveat, and lightningd-config.5.md's hsm-passphrase section directs legacy users to it. Because a pre-v25.12 raw seed cannot be converted into a BIP39 mnemonic that derives the same keys, this is the only at-rest protection the project offers legacy nodes, and lightningd/hsmd will continue to decrypt such files indefinitely (extract_encrypted_secret, common/hsm_secret.c:226-262). get_encryption_key also accepts any passphrase of length >= crypto_pwhash_argon2id_PASSWD_MIN (0), so an empty passphrase yields a file whose key is a public constant.

The threat model lists hsm_secret as a key asset with the filesystem as its boundary but does not enumerate the holder of a disclosed at-rest file; the encrypted-hsm_secret feature exists specifically to defend against that holder, so this is a weakness of that shipped control rather than a trusted-principal or host-compromise case. The read path for existing files is legitimately kept for compatibility; the remediable defect is that new encryptions are still produced without a per-file salt and no salted migration format exists.

## Evidence
1. [common/hsm\_secret.c:53–78](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/hsm_secret.c#L53-L78)
   get_encryption_key derives the secretstream key with crypto_pwhash (Argon2id13, MODERATE limits) using the constant salt "c-lightning\0\0\0\0\0" (line 56); the key is a deterministic function of the passphrase alone, identical across every installation. The only passphrase bound is libsodium's PASSWD_MIN (0), so an empty passphrase is accepted.
2. [tools/lightning-hsmtool.c:169–248](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/lightning-hsmtool.c#L169-L248)
   encrypt_hsm, the installed hsmtool `encrypt` command, still converts a legacy 32-byte plain seed into a new 73-byte file via get_encryption_key + encrypt_legacy_hsm_secret (lines 214-220) and writes it in place of hsm_secret; new fixed-salt files are still produced, and this is the only at-rest protection available for pre-v25.12 raw seeds.
3. [common/hsm\_secret.c:362–379](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/hsm_secret.c#L362-L379)
   encrypt_legacy_hsm_secret writes only the secretstream header plus ciphertext (ENCRYPTED_HSM_SECRET_LEN = 73 bytes); the format has no field for a per-file salt, so the fixed salt is structural to the format rather than an oversight in one caller.
4. [common/hsm\_secret.c:226–261](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/hsm_secret.c#L226-L261)
   extract_encrypted_secret is the production read path (hsmd load_hsm, hsmtool): it re-derives the key with get_encryption_key and decrypts, so lightningd/hsmd accept and depend on the fixed-salt format for existing nodes indefinitely.
5. [doc/lightning-hsmtool.8.md:23–28](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/lightning-hsmtool.8.md#L23-L28)
   The installed manpage documents `encrypt` as the way to make hsm_secret decryptable only at lightningd startup, with no warning that the format uses a shared salt; lightningd-config.5.md's hsm-passphrase section points legacy users here. This is the project's promised protection against a holder of the file.

## Impact
A successful passphrase recovery yields the 32-byte master seed, from which all on-chain wallet keys, node identity and channel keys derive (hsmd_init is handed secret_data directly). The attacker can read every secret (VC:H) and sign transactions spending the node's on-chain and channel funds (VI:H). The running node's availability is not affected (VA:N).

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker must hold a copy of a 73-byte encrypted hsm_secret (leaked backup, stolen disk, exposed volume), an offline position with no privileges on the running node (AV:L, AT:P, PR:N, UI:N). The gain the fixed salt provides over a correctly salted KDF materialises only through up-front investment or scale: a precomputed Argon2id(passphrase, "c-lightning") dictionary built before any theft, or a corpus of many victims' files cracked for the cost of one; and success still requires the passphrase to fall within the attacker's dictionary, with each distinct guess costing the full Argon2id MODERATE work once (AC:H). The code (common/hsm_secret.c:56) makes the amortisation unconditional for every legacy-encrypted node.

## Recommended fix
1. Password-based key derivation for the legacy encrypted hsm_secret uses a constant Argon2id salt shared by every installation, so the derived key depends on the passphrase alone and cracking work can be precomputed and amortised across all nodes; the fixed-length 73-byte format leaves no room to store a salt. Fix criteria: Newly created encrypted secrets (hsmtool `encrypt`) must use a per-file random salt stored alongside the ciphertext in a new, length-distinguishable format; the fixed-salt derivation is retained only for reading and migrating existing 73-byte files, and a migration path (e.g. hsmtool re-encrypting an existing legacy file into the salted format) is offered. Two files encrypted with the same passphrase must have different KDF salts and keys.
2. get_encryption_key and hsmtool `encrypt` accept any passphrase length down to libsodium's PASSWD_MIN of zero, so an empty or trivial passphrase produces an 'encrypted' file whose key is a public constant. Fix criteria: hsmtool `encrypt` refuses an empty passphrase and warns on trivially short ones; documentation for the legacy encrypt command states that the at-rest protection is only as strong as the passphrase.

# maxparts=1 getroutes builds O(n²) localmods in the parent, stalling the routing engine

## Details
When a getroutes request has maxparts == 1 (explicit parameter, or forced by the deprecated auto.no_mpp_support layer at askrene.c:595-598), do_getroutes (askrene.c:607-612) builds the temporary layer remove_small_channel_layer (267-297): it iterates every channel in the gossmap and, for each channel whose capacity is below the payment amount, records a disable update for both directions. add_layer then calls layer_add_localmods (layer.c:1363-1375), which forwards each update to gossmap_local_updatechan. That function locates the channel's localmod with find_localmod (gossmap.c:1038-1045), a linear scan over the growing mods array (sizeof(struct localmod) = 160 bytes), which the gossmap author explicitly sized for 'a few' entries (gossmap.c:983-985). With n small channels the construction performs on the order of n² short_channel_id comparisons across a multi-megabyte array, then gossmap_apply_localmods (askrene.c:616) serialises 2n fake channel_updates. All of this runs in the single-threaded parent before fork() (askrene.c:~687), so the askrene-timeout deadline (route_seconds, handed only to the child at 673-675) does not bound it and askrene-max-threads does not apply; no other askrene RPC — reaping finished children, askrene-reserve/unreserve, inform-channel, layer management, or other callers' getroutes — is serviced until it completes.

On a mainnet gossmap (assumption: ~40-50k public channels, so a ~6-8 MB mods array not resident in cache), a large amount makes most channels 'small' and gives on the order of 1e9+ comparisons per request, i.e. seconds of parent CPU per call on server hardware and far more on the low-power hosts CLN nodes commonly run on.

Who triggers it: any getroutes caller — a rune bearer over commando (always on) or clnrest whose rune permits getroutes — by sending maxparts=1 with a large amount_msat, any two valid pubkeys (gossmap lookup happens after the cost) and layers=[], repeatedly; each request is tiny but blocks the askrene parent for seconds, so a trickle keeps cln-askrene saturated and every xpay/pay/renepay-fallback payment on the node stalls while it continues. Independently, a payee (untrusted payment counterparty) selects the path for the operator's own payments by issuing a bolt11 invoice without OPT_BASIC_MPP (xpay.c:2873, 2934-2935) — keysend payments take it unconditionally (xpay.c:3212) — incurring the stall on every getroutes attempt and, by failing HTLCs, on every retry within retry_for.

This is algorithmic complexity rather than volume: the per-request cost is quadratic in a count the request's amount selects (bounded only by gossmap size), it runs outside the shipped per-request deadline, and a linear or hash-indexed construction would cost milliseconds.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:267–297](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L267-L297)
   remove_small_channel_layer walks every gossmap channel and, for each whose capacity is below the requested amount, records a disable update for both directions in a temporary layer (layer_add_update_channel, hash insert). For a large amount on a mainnet gossmap this is tens of thousands of updates.
2. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:594–612](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L594-L612)
   do_getroutes forces maxparts=1 for the deprecated auto.no_mpp_support layer (595-598) and, whenever maxparts == 1 (caller parameter, default 100), calls add_layer(remove_small_channel_layer(...)) at 607-612. add_layer (364-377) calls layer_add_localmods. All of this executes in the parent process before the fork() at ~687; source/destination validity is only checked afterwards (~627-645), so the cost is paid even for unknown node ids.
3. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:1363–1375](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L1363-L1375)
   layer_add_localmods iterates the layer's local_updates hash and calls gossmap_local_updatechan once per stored update — 2 per small channel.
4. [common/gossmap.c:1038–1045](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/gossmap.c#L1038-L1045)
   find_localmod is a linear scan over localmods->mods (comment at 983-985: 'We only expect a few, so we use a simple array'); gossmap_local_updatechan calls it at 1160 for every update and appends a 160-byte struct localmod on a miss (1163-1170), so n small channels cost ~n² short_channel_id comparisons over a multi-megabyte, cache-unfriendly array.
5. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:673–675](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L673-L675)
   The shipped bound on per-request routing cost, askrene-timeout (route_seconds, default 10 s at 1564/1571-1575), is a deadline handed to the forked child only; the parent-side layer construction above is not covered by it, nor by askrene-max-threads (max_children=4), since it runs before a child slot is consumed.
6. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:2873](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L2873)
   xpay derives disable_mpp from the payee's invoice feature bits (no OPT_BASIC_MPP) and sets payment->maxparts = 1 at 2934-2935; keysend sets maxparts = 1 unconditionally at 3212. getroutes_for passes maxparts to getroutes (1963-1967) on every routing attempt and retry, so a payee selects this code path for the operator's own payments to them.

## Impact
While the trickle of requests continues, the single-threaded cln-askrene parent is blocked, so no getroutes, reserve/unreserve or inform-channel from xpay/pay/renepay fallbacks is serviced and the node cannot send payments; the stall is sustained for as long as the attacker keeps sending. lightningd, channels, forwarding and receiving stay up; the plugin does not crash. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. A caller holding a rune that permits getroutes (commando is always on; clnrest when enabled) sends getroutes with maxparts=1, a large amount_msat, two valid pubkeys and layers=[]; the parent spends seconds building quadratic localmods before forking, and repeating the request every few seconds keeps askrene saturated. No defenses apply: askrene-timeout bounds only the child, max_children only counts forked children, and parameter validation of source/destination happens after the cost. The alternative payee vector (non-MPP invoice or keysend, PR:N but requiring the operator to initiate a payment) is weaker and bounded to that payment's retry window. Rated on the rune-bearer route; the cost estimate assumes a mainnet-sized gossmap.

## Recommended fix
1. remove_small_channel_layer encodes a per-channel decision as tens of thousands of localmod updates, and gossmap_local_updatechan resolves each by linear search over an array designed for a handful of entries, giving quadratic parent-side work. Fix criteria: A maxparts=1 getroutes with a large amount on a mainnet-sized gossmap must complete its parent-side preparation in time linear (or n log n) in channel count — e.g. by filtering small channels in the child via the capacities array/disabled bitmap instead of localmods, or by giving gossmap_localmods a hash index — and must not block other askrene RPCs for more than a bounded, small time.
2. Expensive per-request preparation proportional to gossmap size runs in the single-threaded parent, where neither askrene-timeout nor askrene-max-threads applies. Fix criteria: Work proportional to gossmap size should run in the forked child under the route deadline (or be otherwise bounded), so that one caller's request cannot stall reaping, reservations or other callers' getroutes.

# Postgres connection failure logs the full --wallet DSN including the database password

## Details
The documented PostgreSQL configuration is --wallet=postgres://${USER}:${PASSWORD}@${HOST}:${PORT}/${DB} (doc/beginners-guide/backup-and-recovery/advanced-db-backup.md:241), and lightningd marks --wallet OPT_CONCEAL because "DSN can contain a database password" (options.c:1487-1488), rendering it as "..." even to listconfigs callers on the RPC socket (configs.c:68-69). db_postgres_setup() nevertheless builds its failure message from the raw DSN — "Could not connect to %s: %s" with db->filename (db/db_postgres.c:39) — whenever PQconnectdb() does not reach CONNECTION_OK. db_open_() with create=true escalates that to db_fatal (db/utils.c:372-374); lightningd's errorfn db_error() logs it at LOG_BROKEN to stdout or every --log-file (wallet/db.c:96; log.c:468-471, 999) and then fatal_vfmt() prints it to stderr and exits (log.c:1136-1140). Because wallet_new() runs at lightningd.c:1322, before complete_daemonize() (1505) and before crashlog is set (1515), the line reaches the launching stderr even with --daemon. db/utils.c:351-356 echoes the DSN the same way on a mistyped scheme.

Any ordinary failure to reach the database server — PostgreSQL restart, boot ordering (the shipped unit orders only After=bitcoind.service), network blip, pg_hba or DNS misconfiguration — therefore writes the wallet database credential in clear text into the lightningd log file, stderr and, under the shipped systemd unit or Docker image (both built with libpq: Dockerfile:114,236), into the journal or container log; with Restart=on-failure it is re-logged on every restart attempt while the server is down. Readers of those sinks (adm/systemd-journal group members, docker-group users, log shippers and aggregation systems, anyone who receives a pasted log) are principals the project otherwise keeps away from node state via the 0700 lightning-dir, the 0600 RPC socket and the OPT_CONCEAL redaction. The credential, together with the host:port in the same string, gives whoever reads it full read/write access to the wallet database: channel state, HTLC preimages, secrets and runes can be read, and rows that lightningd trusts on reload can be rewritten or dropped.

Filed because the maintainers' explicit redaction of this value is defeated by the driver's own error path; the mechanism is information exposure through log files (CWE-532).

## Evidence
1. [db/db\_postgres.c:38–41](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_postgres.c#L38-L41)
   db_postgres_setup(): when PQstatus(db->conn) != CONNECTION_OK it formats db->error as "Could not connect to %s: %s" with db->filename — the raw --wallet DSN, which in the documented form is postgres://user:password@host:port/db — followed by libpq's error text. This is the message the fix must redact.
2. [db/utils.c:372–376](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/utils.c#L372-L376)
   db_open_(): when setup_fn fails and create is true (lightningd's wallet path, wallet/db.c:106 passes true) it calls db_fatal(db, "Error calling DB setup: %s", db->error), carrying the DSN into the errorfn.
3. [wallet/db.c:91–101](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/db.c#L91-L101)
   lightningd's errorfn db_error(): logv(ld->log, LOG_BROKEN, ...) writes the message to every configured log sink (stdout by default, log.c:468-471; or each --log-file, opened with fopen("a") at log.c:999 with no restrictive mode), then fatal_vfmt() repeats it.
4. [lightningd/log.c:1130–1145](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L1130-L1145)
   fatal_vfmt(): vfprintf(stderr, fmt, ap) prints the message to stderr; crashlog is still NULL at this point (set only at lightningd.c:1515), so it exit(1)s. Under the shipped systemd unit (Type=simple) and the Docker entrypoint stderr is the journal / container log.
5. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1322](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1322)
   wallet_new() → db_setup() → db_open() runs here, before complete_daemonize() (line 1505) redirects stderr to /dev/null and before crashlog is set (1515): even with --daemon the failure line reaches the launching stderr, and the LOG_BROKEN line reaches stdout/--log-file.
6. [lightningd/configs.c:68–69](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L68-L69)
   The shipped control for this secret: get_opt_val() renders any OPT_CONCEAL option as "..." in listconfigs, so even an RPC-socket caller is denied the DSN. The driver error path prints the value this redaction exists to hide.
7. [lightningd/options.c:1487–1490](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1487-L1490)
   --wallet is registered OPT_EARLY|OPT_CONCEAL with the comment "DSN can contain a database password": the maintainers' explicit intent that the DSN is a secret.
8. [db/utils.c:351–356](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/utils.c#L351-L356)
   The generic open path also echoes db->filename in two db_fatal messages ("Could not extract driver name from", "Unable to find DB driver for"), reachable with a mistyped scheme (e.g. postgre://user:pw@host) in a DSN that still carries credentials.
9. [contrib/init/lightningd.service:31–33](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/init/lightningd.service#L31-L33)
   Shipped unit: Type=simple (stdout/stderr → systemd journal, readable by adm/systemd-journal group members and log shippers) and Restart=on-failure, so while the database is unreachable the credential is re-logged on every restart. The unit orders only After=bitcoind.service, not after PostgreSQL, so a boot-time ordering failure is routine.
10. [doc/beginners-guide/backup-and-recovery/advanced-db-backup.md:241](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/beginners-guide/backup-and-recovery/advanced-db-backup.md#L241)
   The documented way to configure the backend is --wallet=postgres://${USER}:${PASSWORD}@${HOST}:${PORT}/${DB}: the password is in the DSN by the project's own instructions, with no guidance to use .pgpass/PGPASSWORD or to protect logs.

## Impact
The exposed credential (with host:port in the same string) is the key to lightningd's own persistent state, the wallet database — part of the vulnerable system per the recorded threat model ("State in sqlite3/PostgreSQL"). A reader on the lightningd host can reach whatever pg_hba allows that host to reach, then read every channel state, HTLC preimage, secret and rune (confidentiality HIGH), rewrite rows lightningd trusts on reload — channel state, commitment data, runes — which can lead to broadcast of revoked state or RPC authority (integrity HIGH), and drop or corrupt the database, bricking the node (availability HIGH).

## Reproduction steps
1. Needs the PostgreSQL backend configured in the documented password-in-DSN form and a connection failure at open — a routine operational event (database restart ordering at boot, network outage), repeated on every supervisor restart while the server is down — after which the DSN sits in the lightningd log, stderr/journal or container log. The attacker is a local principal with read access to those sinks (journal group, log file, docker logs) or a downstream log consumer; no interaction with lightningd or the operator is needed. AV:L because reading the sink requires local or log-pipeline access; AT:P for the connection-failure condition; PR:L for the lesser local account.

## Recommended fix
The postgres driver and the generic db_open_ path interpolate the raw DSN (db->filename) into error strings that lightningd logs and prints, although the option layer deliberately conceals that value because it can carry a database password. Fix criteria: No log, stderr or fatal message produced from db_postgres_setup(), db_open_() or any other consumer of db->filename may contain the DSN's credential component: print only a redacted form (scheme, host, port, dbname with user/password stripped, or a fixed placeholder) in the "Could not connect to", "Could not extract driver name from" and "Unable to find DB driver for" messages, and audit every other use of db->filename in db/ for the same leak. Verify by forcing a connection failure with --wallet=postgres://u:secret@... and confirming 'secret' appears in neither the log file, stdout nor stderr.

# checkmessage passes unvalidated recovery id to libsecp256k1, aborting lightningd

## Details
The `checkmessage` JSON-RPC method (lightningd/signmessage.c) decodes the caller-supplied `zbase` string into 65 bytes and immediately calls `secp256k1_ecdsa_recoverable_signature_parse_compact(secp256k1_ctx, &rsig, u8sig + 1, u8sig[0] - 31)`. The recovery id argument is computed from the first decoded byte with no range check. The lnd-compatible encoding puts 31+recid (31..34) in that byte, but `from_zbase32` accepts any first byte, so a caller can make recid any value in -31..224.

libsecp256k1 (bundled with the pinned libwally-core submodule) guards that parameter with `ARG_CHECK(recid >= 0 && recid <= 3)`. ARG_CHECK does not simply return failure: it first calls the context's illegal-argument callback, and the default callback prints `[libsecp256k1] illegal argument` and calls abort(). lightningd uses libwally's global context (common/setup.c:58) and never installs a non-aborting callback (no `secp256k1_context_set_illegal_callback` anywhere in the repository), so a `checkmessage` call whose zbase decodes to a first byte outside 31..34 terminates lightningd with SIGABRT. The crash happens before `command_check_only`, so even `check checkmessage ...` triggers it.

The maintainers clearly know this libsecp256k1 behaviour: the bolt11 decoder validates the recovery id with `valid_recovery_id()` (common/bolt11.c:985, 1026) before making the identical call. `checkmessage` is the one caller without that guard.

Who can trigger it: any JSON-RPC caller permitted to invoke `checkmessage` — including partially trusted rune bearers over commando (peer custom messages) or clnrest, provided their rune allows the method (e.g. a `method=checkmessage` rune, or any rune whose restrictions do not exclude it). The threat model treats rune bearers as bounded principals; crashing the node (with all channels' subdaemons dying with it) exceeds anything a `checkmessage` grant is meant to permit. A 104-character zbase32 string whose first two characters encode a first byte of 0x00 (e.g. 'yy' followed by 102 valid zbase32 chars) is sufficient.

Assumption: libsecp256k1's `secp256k1_ecdsa_recoverable_signature_parse_compact` ARG_CHECKs recid and the default illegal callback aborts (true for every upstream release including the one bundled in the pinned libwally-core), and libwally does not install a custom illegal callback on its global context.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/signmessage.c:178–183](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/signmessage.c#L178-L183)
   json_checkmessage calls secp256k1_ecdsa_recoverable_signature_parse_compact with recid = u8sig[0] - 31, where u8sig[0] is the first byte decoded from the caller's zbase string (any value 0..255, so recid ranges -31..224). Only 31..34 yield a legal recid 0..3; libsecp256k1 treats any other value as an illegal argument and invokes the context's illegal_callback, which by default aborts the process.
2. [lightningd/signmessage.c:36–55](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/signmessage.c#L36-L55)
   from_zbase32 only verifies that each character is in the zbase32 alphabet and that the string decodes to a whole number of bytes (65 for a 104-char input); it imposes no constraint on the first byte, so the caller fully controls recid.
3. [common/bolt11.c:985](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L985)
   The sibling decoder for bolt11 invoices explicitly range-checks the recovery id with valid_recovery_id() before calling parse_compact (line 1026-1031), showing the maintainers know the libsecp256k1 call must not receive an out-of-range recid; checkmessage lacks the same guard.
4. [common/setup.c:58](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/setup.c#L58)
   lightningd's secp256k1_ctx is libwally's global context (wally_get_secp_context); nowhere in the tree is secp256k1_context_set_illegal_callback called, so the libsecp256k1 default (print + abort()) is in force.

## Impact
lightningd aborts; all per-channel subdaemons and important plugins go down with it. Node is offline until restarted, with the usual on-chain risks of an unavailable Lightning node (HTLC timeouts, inability to respond to peer force-closes). No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any RPC caller allowed to invoke checkmessage who is not otherwise fully trusted — a rune bearer whose rune permits the method (e.g. method=checkmessage), reaching lightningd over commando (always on; plugins/commando.c:319-346 forwards any rune-valid request via execute_command) or clnrest. Delivery: one request {"message":"x","zbase":"yy"+102 zbase32 chars}. from_zbase32 (signmessage.c:36-56) checks only the alphabet and byte count, so the 65-byte output's first byte is attacker-chosen; signmessage.c:178-181 passes u8sig[0]-31 (range -31..224) as recid before command_check_only, so even `check checkmessage` triggers it. Explicit dependency assumption (external/libwally-core submodule pins are stripped from this checkout, so unverifiable here): libsecp256k1's secp256k1_ecdsa_recoverable_signature_parse_compact guards recid with ARG_CHECK(recid >= 0 && recid <= 3), whose default illegal_callback prints and abort()s, and libwally's wally_get_secp_context() context (common/setup.c:58) carries no custom callback — no secp256k1_context_set_illegal_callback call exists anywhere in this tree. common/daemon.c:77-104 installs a SIGABRT handler with SA_RESETHAND that logs a backtrace and re-raises, so lightningd dies. The project's tests (tests/test_misc.py:2669) only exercise an invalid-alphabet zbase and valid signatures, never a decodable zbase with first byte outside 31..34. No race, no special configuration; a rune permitting the method is the only privilege needed, and such a grant concedes signature verification, not node termination.

## Recommended fix
json_checkmessage derives the recovery id from attacker-controlled data and hands it to a libsecp256k1 API whose argument check aborts the process on out-of-range values, instead of validating it first as bolt11.c does. Fix criteria: checkmessage must reject (with a JSON-RPC invalid-params error) any decoded signature whose first byte is outside 31..34 before calling secp256k1_ecdsa_recoverable_signature_parse_compact; a zbase string decoding to a first byte of 0x00 or 0xff must produce an RPC error and leave lightningd running. Optionally also install a non-aborting secp256k1 illegal-argument callback as defence in depth.
