# Elements: lightningd asserts on non-L-BTC/blinded output in any tx spending a watched channel output

## Details
When Core Lightning runs on an Elements chain (`--network=liquid` or `liquid-regtest`, bitcoin/chainparams.c:165-214; a supported chain exercised in CI's liquid-regtest matrix), lightningd converts every transaction that spends an output it watches for onchaind into a `struct tx_parts` with tx_parts_from_wally_tx(tmpctx, tx->wtx, -1, -1) (lightningd/onchain_control.c:289). For each output of that transaction the Elements branch (bitcoin/tx_parts.c:49-57) does `asset = wally_tx_output_get_amount(...)` followed by `assert(amount_asset_is_main(&asset))`.

The watched outputs are all outputs of the unilateral-close commitment transaction (watch_tx_and_outputs, onchain_control.c:321-339): the peer's to_remote output, the peer's to_local output after its CSV, and HTLC outputs. The transaction that spends them is authored entirely by the remote peer. On Liquid, a normal wallet sweep produces blinded outputs (asset commitment prefix 0x0a/0x0b) and may carry other assets (e.g. USDt) in the same transaction. amount_asset_is_main() (common/amount.c:719-728) compares the 33-byte asset field byte-for-byte to chainparams->fee_asset_tag (0x01 + L-BTC tag), so any blinded or non-L-BTC output makes the assert fail and lightningd abort(). Asserts are compiled in release builds (no NDEBUG).

The spend is seen in chaintopology.c:52-67 while processing the block, inside the per-callback DB transaction, so the block is not committed; on restart lightningd refetches it and, independently, onchaind replay (replay_block, onchain_control.c:444-461) re-drives onchain_txo_spent for the same spend. Either way the same assert fires again, so the node stays down (and onchaind cannot time out HTLCs or claim penalties) until the operator deploys changed code. Every other lightningd block path treats a non-main asset as something to skip (watch.c:461, wallet.c:3361, chaintopology.c:997, closing_control.c:186, bitcoind.c:753); only tx_parts.c (and the consumer side in onchaind) treats it as an invariant.

The attacker needs a channel with the victim (permissionless) and a force close by either side; it then spends its own commitment output with a blinded output, the default behaviour of an Elements wallet, so this is also an accidental availability bug for any Liquid node whose peer sweeps with a confidential address. Anchors are disabled on Elements (options.c:1854-1859), so there is no anyone-can-spend anchor vector; the attacker position is the channel peer. The project's own test harness deliberately uses unconfidential addresses on elementsd (pyln-testing utils.py:843-848), which is why CI's liquid-regtest closing tests never produce such a spend. Non-Elements deployments are unaffected (amount_asset_is_main() returns true when !is_elements).

Assumption about libwally (external/ submodule absent; pinned libwally-core submodule): wally_tx_from_bytes with WALLY_TX_FLAG_USE_ELEMENTS stores each output's asset as the raw 33-byte commitment (asset_len == 33, prefix byte preserved) and wally_tx_output_clone_alloc copies it, which is what wally_tx_output_get_amount() (bitcoin/tx.c:827-838) already requires via its asset_len assert.

## Evidence
1. [bitcoin/tx\_parts.c:49–56](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/tx_parts.c#L49-L56)
   tx_parts_from_wally_tx() iterates every output of the spending transaction and, when chainparams->is_elements, calls wally_tx_output_get_amount() then assert(amount_asset_is_main(&asset)) (marked 'FIXME: non l-btc assets'). A confidential (blinded) asset commitment or an explicit asset other than the chain's fee asset makes amount_asset_is_main() false and aborts lightningd. The outputs belong to whoever spent the watched outpoint, not to this node.
2. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:283–299](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L283-L299)
   onchain_txo_spent() runs in lightningd and calls tx_parts_from_wally_tx(tmpctx, tx->wtx, -1, -1) (all inputs, all outputs) on the transaction that spent one of the commitment outputs onchaind is watching, before anything else inspects or validates that transaction.
3. [lightningd/chaintopology.c:52–66](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/chaintopology.c#L52-L66)
   filter_block_txs(): for every transaction of every block from elementsd, every input is matched against the txowatch table and txowatch_fire() is called with the full parsed transaction (parsed with WALLY_TX_FLAG_USE_ELEMENTS, bitcoin/tx.c:612-613, so each output carries its raw 33-byte asset commitment). This is how the peer's spend of a watched output reaches onchain_txo_spent. It runs inside the per-callback DB transaction, so the abort leaves the block uncommitted and it is refetched on restart.
4. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:321–338](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L321-L338)
   watch_tx_and_outputs() registers a txowatch on every output of the commitment transaction (to_local, to_remote and HTLC outputs), with onchain_txo_watched -> onchain_txo_spent as the callback.
5. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:444–460](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L444-L460)
   replay_block(): on restart, onchaind replay re-fetches blocks from the close height and calls onchain_txo_spent() for every transaction spending a replayed-watched txid, so the same spend hits the same assert again regardless of what the block DB recorded. The outage persists across restarts until the code is changed.
6. [common/amount.c:719–727](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/amount.c#L719-L727)
   amount_asset_is_main() compares the 33-byte asset field byte-for-byte to chainparams->fee_asset_tag (explicit prefix 0x01 + L-BTC tag, chainparams.c:16-25); blinded assets (prefix 0x0a/0x0b) and any other explicit asset compare unequal.
7. [bitcoin/tx.c:821–845](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/tx.c#L821-L845)
   wally_tx_output_get_amount() copies the raw asset bytes of the output into amount.asset without any normalisation (value set to 0 for non-explicit assets), so the assert in tx_parts.c sees the spender's asset commitment as-is.
8. [lightningd/watch.c:461–463](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/watch.c#L461-L463)
   Contrast: lightningd's other block-processing paths (watch_check_tx_outputs here, wallet.c:3361, chaintopology.c:997, closing_control.c:186, bitcoind.c:753) treat a non-main asset as 'skip'; tx_parts.c is the one place where the spender's asset choice is treated as an invariant.
9. [lightningd/options.c:1854–1858](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1854-L1858)
   Anchor outputs are disabled on Elements (OPT_ANCHORS_ZERO_FEE_HTLC_TX removed from our features), so there are no anyone-can-spend anchor outputs on Liquid commitments; the triggering transaction is authored by the channel peer spending its own to_remote/to_local/HTLC outputs.

## Impact
lightningd (the whole node) aborts deterministically and re-aborts on every restart while the offending spend is replayed: a persistent outage requiring a code change to recover. While down, onchaind cannot time out HTLCs or sweep/penalise, so the peer gains a window to settle on-chain contracts in its favour (integrity LOW). No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote channel peer on a Liquid/Elements deployment (a supported chain, not an opt-in hardening setting). It opens or holds a channel, lets it force-close (it can broadcast its own commitment at any time), then spends its to_remote/to_local/HTLC output with a transaction that has a blinded or non-L-BTC output (default Elements wallet behaviour). When the block containing that spend is processed, chaintopology.c fires the txowatch, onchain_txo_spent calls tx_parts_from_wally_tx, and the assert aborts lightningd; on restart both the block refetch and onchaind replay re-trigger it. No authentication beyond having had a channel; the attack requirement is a channel with the victim plus a force close.

## Recommended fix
1. tx_parts_from_wally_tx() treats 'every output of a third-party transaction is an explicit fee-asset output' as an invariant (assert) on Elements, although the outputs are authored by whoever spent the watched outpoint. Fix criteria: Converting a spending transaction into tx_parts must succeed for any consensus-valid Elements transaction: non-main or blinded outputs must be represented (e.g. satoshi left 0 / flagged as non-main) or skipped without aborting, and a block containing a blinded sweep of a watched commitment output must be processed by lightningd without crashing, both on the live path and on onchaind replay.
2. onchaind's consumer side assumes every tx_parts output it receives is an explicit L-BTC output. Fix criteria: onchaind must tolerate tx_parts outputs that are blinded or non-L-BTC (treat them as unknown-amount outputs that cannot match any of our expected scripts/amounts) without asserting or misclassifying the spend.

# data_version is u32 but bound and read as 32-bit signed: node bricks after 2^31 commits

## Details
Every dirty database transaction ends with db_data_version_incr() (db/exec.c:138-153), the optimistic lock that protects against concurrent writers: UPDATE vars SET intval = intval + 1 WHERE name = 'data_version' AND intval = ?. The in-memory counter is u32 (db/common.h:60) but it is bound with db_bind_int(), a C int, and restored at startup by db_data_version_get() (db/exec.c:41-58) through db_col_int(), also int.

When the stored counter reaches 2^31 the conversions break the lock on sqlite3: db->data_version is 2147483648 in the u32, db_bind_int() converts it to -2147483648, sqlite3_bind_int binds that against the stored 64-bit 2147483648, the UPDATE matches no row, db_count_changes() returns 0 and db_fatal("Optimistic lock on the database failed ... Aborting") kills lightningd. On restart db_data_version_get() reads the stored 2147483648 via sqlite3_column_int (truncated to INT_MIN, stored into the u32 as 2147483648 again). The db_setup() transaction is always dirty because db_migrate() executes UPDATE version SET version=? unconditionally (wallet/db.c:72-76) and db_exec_prepared_v2 marks any non-readonly statement dirty (db/utils.c:190), so lightningd dies inside db_setup() on every subsequent start. On PostgreSQL vars.intval is declared INTEGER (wallet/migrations.c:553) and the postgres rewriter does not widen it, so it is int4: intval + 1 raises 'integer out of range' at 2147483647 and db_exec_prepared_v2 calls db_fatal(); the stored value then stays at 2147483647 and every later dirty commit, including db_setup's, fails the same way. In both backends the node cannot start until the operator hand-edits vars.intval, and the error message blames concurrent access.

Who advances the counter: each lightningd event-loop callback runs in its own transaction (lightningd/io_loop_with_timers.c:28-33). handle_peer_connected() and peer_disconnected() call wallet_save_network_event() unconditionally for every peer (lightningd/peer_control.c:1901, 2407; wallet/wallet.c:7615-7647 is a plain INSERT), so an unauthenticated peer with no channel produces two dirty transactions per connect/disconnect cycle. A peer with a channel produces several per HTLC add/fail and commitment cycle (wallet_channel_save, HTLC state writes). The threshold is fixed by the code at 2^31 increments; at the node's maximum commit rate (bounded by fsync, hundreds to low thousands per second) that is on the order of one to several months of sustained traffic from a single peer. The outcome is not load that stops with the traffic but a deterministic, persistent startup failure: once the stored value crosses the boundary the node stays down after the traffic ends. A long-lived very busy routing node also drifts toward the same hard lifetime cap on its own.

This is a sibling of the db_set_intvar/db_get_intvar truncation at db/exec.c:60-91 (same vars.intval 32-bit round trip) but a distinct code path: db_data_version_incr/db_data_version_get bind and read directly, so fixing the intvar helpers does not fix this counter.

## Evidence
1. [db/exec.c:138–153](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/exec.c#L138-L153)
   db_data_version_incr() binds db->data_version (u32) with db_bind_int(), whose parameter is a C int. Once the counter is 2^31 the bound value is INT_MIN (or INT_MAX under any saturating conversion), the WHERE intval = ? clause matches no row, db_count_changes() != 1 and db_fatal() aborts lightningd. It runs from db_commit_transaction() (line 207) for every dirty transaction.
2. [db/exec.c:41–58](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/exec.c#L41-L58)
   db_data_version_get() reads intval with db_col_int() (int) into a u32: a stored 2147483648 comes back as INT_MIN, is stored as 2147483648 in the u32, and fails the bind above on the first dirty commit of every startup.
3. [db/common.h:58–60](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/common.h#L58-L60)
   data_version is declared u32: the design intends an unsigned 32-bit counter, but both halves of the round trip are signed 32-bit.
4. [wallet/db.c:72–76](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/db.c#L72-L76)
   db_migrate() executes UPDATE version SET version=? unconditionally on every startup; db_exec_prepared_v2 marks the transaction dirty for any non-readonly statement (db/utils.c:190), so the db_setup() transaction (wallet/db.c:112-117) always ends in db_data_version_incr(): once the stored counter is past the boundary lightningd dies during db_setup on every start.
5. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1901–1905](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1901-L1905)
   handle_peer_connected() calls wallet_save_network_event(NETWORK_EVENT_CONNECT) for every peer connectd reports, before any channel lookup: an unauthenticated peer with no channel produces one dirty transaction per connection.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2407–2409](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2407-L2409)
   peer_disconnected() records NETWORK_EVENT_DISCONNECT unconditionally, so each connect/disconnect cycle by any peer costs two data_version increments; channel traffic (commitment_signed/revoke_and_ack handling via wallet_channel_save and HTLC updates) adds several more per HTLC cycle.
7. [wallet/wallet.c:7615–7647](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L7615-L7647)
   wallet_save_network_event() is an unconditional INSERT INTO network_events executed with db_exec_prepared_v2, i.e. a write that dirties the enclosing transaction.
8. [lightningd/io\_loop\_with\_timers.c:28–33](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/io_loop_with_timers.c#L28-L33)
   Each event-loop callback and timer runs inside its own db_begin_transaction/db_commit_transaction pair, so every peer-driven message that writes commits separately and advances the counter by one.
9. [db/db\_sqlite3.c:258–260](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_sqlite3.c#L258-L260)
   sqlite driver binds DB_BINDING_INT via sqlite3_bind_int; the stored INTEGER (64-bit in sqlite) 2147483648 never equals the bound -2147483648. db_sqlite3_column_int (363-366) reads with sqlite3_column_int, truncating on reload.
10. [db/db\_postgres.c:105–111](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_postgres.c#L105-L111)
   postgres binds DB_BINDING_INT as a 4-byte INT4; db_postgres_column_int (183-195) requires exactly 4 bytes. With vars.intval an int4 column, UPDATE ... SET intval = intval + 1 raises 'integer out of range' at 2147483647, which db_exec_prepared_v2 turns into db_fatal(); same persistent end state one increment earlier.
11. [wallet/migrations.c:553](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/migrations.c#L553)
   vars.intval is declared INTEGER. The PostgresRewriter in devtools/sql-rewrite.py (lines 60-84) maps only BLOB, _ROWID_ and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, so on PostgreSQL the column is a 4-byte int4 and must be widened as part of the fix.

## Impact
Availability: lightningd aborts in db_setup() on every start until manual database surgery, leaving channels unmonitored (missed penalties/timeouts). No confidentiality impact; no integrity impact beyond the stuck counter.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote peer that completes the Noise handshake drives write transactions: handle_peer_connected/peer_disconnected insert a network_events row for every peer (no channel or identity check), and a peer with a channel adds several writes per HTLC/commitment cycle. Each dirty commit increments data_version by exactly one, so the attacker needs about 2^31 commits, i.e. roughly 10^9 connect/disconnect cycles or fewer HTLC cycles, sustained at the victim's fsync-bound commit rate for weeks to months; that volume is the only barrier (AT:P), there is no privilege, rune or operator action involved. Once reached, lightningd db_fatal()s on the next commit and on every restart until the operator edits vars.intval; the effect persists after the traffic stops.

## Recommended fix
1. data_version (u32) is bound in db_data_version_incr() and read in db_data_version_get() through the 32-bit signed db_bind_int/db_col_int path, and vars.intval is int4 on PostgreSQL, so the optimistic-lock comparison stops matching (sqlite) or the increment overflows (postgres) at 2^31 and the failure recurs on every startup. Fix criteria: The data_version round trip must be lossless for the full counter range on both backends: bind and read it as a 64-bit value and widen vars.intval to a 64-bit column on PostgreSQL via migration (or wrap the counter safely). Verify by setting vars.intval to 2^31 - 1, 2^31 and 2^32 + 5 in a test database and confirming lightningd starts and commits normally; a database already stuck at 2^31 (sqlite) or 2^31 - 1 (postgres) must start after upgrade.
2. The optimistic-lock failure message attributes any mismatch to concurrent access, hiding a counter-range fault from the operator. Fix criteria: When the lock UPDATE matches no row, the error must report the expected and stored data_version values so an out-of-range or wrapped counter is diagnosable.

# Wallet sqlite DB and replica created at sqlite default mode 0644, exposing stored runes and preimages

## Details
db_sqlite3_setup() (db/db_sqlite3.c:129 and :149) creates lightningd.sqlite3 and the optional replica with sqlite3_open_v2(..., SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE, NULL). No mode is passed (no file: URI with modeof=, no fchmod after open), the umask is not tightened and the resulting mode is never checked, so the file takes sqlite's compiled default SQLITE_DEFAULT_FILE_PERMISSIONS (0644 in stock builds, including Debian's libsqlite3-0 installed by the Dockerfile) masked by the process umask; -journal/-wal files inherit that mode. wallet_new() runs at lightningd.c:1322, before complete_daemonize() at :1505 sets umask(0), so the inherited operator umask applies: 0022 (the shipped contrib/init/lightningd.service sets no UMask=) yields 0644.

The only protection is the containing directory. options.c:1876-1888 creates <lightning-dir>/<network> with 0700 only when chdir() into it fails; a directory that already exists is accepted with whatever mode it has and is never re-checked. The documented workflows make that the normal case: users are told to create ~/.lightning/bitcoin/config before first start (configuration.md:13) and to copy hsm_secret / emergency.recover / the backed-up DB into $LIGHTNINGDIR before starting (recovery.md:16,45), so the network directory is operator-made under umask 022 (0755). The replica (the ':' suffix of --wallet) never gets a lightningd-created directory at all; advanced-db-backup.md recommends an NFS-mounted NAS or USB disk and warns only about cloud storage.

The file is not just metadata. The runes table holds every issued rune in full (wallet.c:6840-6851). A rune is the bearer credential commando checks on every custom message from any connected peer and that clnrest accepts in the Rune header, so a local reader obtains exactly the RPC authority the operator delegated (full node control, including withdraw, for a common unrestricted rune) without touching the 0600 RPC socket. The file also holds invoice/HTLC preimages, HTLC shared secrets, payment path_secrets, all channel and peer state and the plugin datastore.

The project's own standard for files in lightning-dir is explicit owner-only modes independent of umask and directory: hsm_secret 0400 (hsmd.c:393), gossip_store 0600, emergency.recover 0400, log file 0600, RPC socket 0600 (documented as 'only the user that launched lightningd can command it'), and in this release clnrest/wss-proxy TLS private keys 0600 'regardless of umask' (certs.rs:7-17, CHANGELOG.md:27 under Fixed). The wallet database is the one credential-bearing file left at the library default (CWE-276).

Dependency assumption: libsqlite3 is distro-provided and unpinned; the stock unix VFS creates the main database with SQLITE_DEFAULT_FILE_PERMISSIONS = 0644 via open(2) under the process umask and gives journal/WAL files the main file's mode. A distribution that overrides that compile-time default would change the resulting mode.

Conditions: the network directory pre-exists with group/other traversal (operator-created per the documented workflows), or the main/replica DSN points into any directory lightningd did not create 0700. Attacker: an unprivileged local account on the host, or any account on a host sharing the NFS/USB replica location.

## Evidence
1. [db/db\_sqlite3.c:112–137](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_sqlite3.c#L112-L137)
   db_sqlite3_setup() creates the main wallet with sqlite3_open_v2(filename, &sql, SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE, NULL): default VFS, no file: URI modeof=, no fchmod after open, no umask tightening and no check of the resulting mode. The file is created with sqlite's compiled default (SQLITE_DEFAULT_FILE_PERMISSIONS, 0644 in stock builds) masked only by the process umask; -journal/-wal files copy the main file's mode. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [db/db\_sqlite3.c:146–155](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_sqlite3.c#L146-L155)
   The replica named after ':' in --wallet is opened the same way, so the full wallet copy is created 0644 in an operator-supplied directory that lightningd never creates or checks; the documentation recommends a NAS/NFS or USB location for it.
3. [lightningd/options.c:1876–1887](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1876-L1887)
   The network directory is created 0700 only when chdir() into it fails. A pre-existing <lightning-dir>/<network> (operator mkdir under umask 022 gives 0755, as the documented 'create ~/.lightning/bitcoin/config before start' and 'copy hsm_secret into $LIGHTNINGDIR before start' workflows require) is accepted with whatever mode it has and never re-checked or chmod'ed, so the only protection the DB has is absent.
4. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1322](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1322)
   wallet_new() -> db_setup() runs here, before complete_daemonize() at line 1505 sets umask(0); the DB is therefore created under the operator's inherited umask (0022 in the shipped systemd unit, which sets no UMask=), giving 0644 rather than world-writable; a 0077 umask is the only thing that would make it 0600 and is nowhere documented as required.
5. [wallet/wallet.c:6840–6850](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L6840-L6850)
   db_rune_insert stores every issued rune in full (rune_to_base64) as TEXT in the runes table. A rune is the bearer credential for commando (checkrune on every custom message from any connected peer) and clnrest; reading the file yields usable RPC credentials with whatever scope the operator issued, bypassing the 0600 RPC socket. The master rune secret itself comes from hsmd (runes.c:170) and is not in the file.
6. [wallet/migrations.c:206–224](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/migrations.c#L206-L224)
   channel_htlcs stores payment_key (preimage) and shared_secret; invoices stores payment_key; payments stores preimages and path_secrets; datastore holds plugin state. All of this sits in the 0644 file along with every channel, peer and payment record (privacy).
7. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/certs.rs:7–16](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/certs.rs#L7-L16)
   The project's own standard for credential files in lightning-dir: write_private_key() sets 0600 explicitly, and doc/CHANGELOG.md:27 records this release's fix 'create TLS private keys with restrictive (0600) permissions regardless of umask' under Fixed. The wallet DB holding runes is the one credential-bearing file still left at the library default.
8. [hsmd/hsmd.c:393](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/hsmd.c#L393)
   hsm_secret is created O_EXCL 0400; likewise gossip_store 0600 (gossipd/gossip_store.c:202), emergency.recover 0400 (plugins/chanbackup.c:195), log file 0600 (lightningd/log.c:1115), RPC socket 0600 (rpc-file-mode, documented as 'only the user that launched lightningd can command it'). The project treats other local accounts as untrusted for exactly the assets the DB contains.
9. [doc/getting-started/getting-started/configuration.md:13](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/getting-started/getting-started/configuration.md#L13)
   Documented workflow: users create ~/.lightning/bitcoin/config before first start, i.e. they mkdir the network directory themselves under their own umask; nothing tells them it must be 0700 and lightningd does not enforce it.
10. [doc/beginners-guide/backup-and-recovery/advanced-db-backup.md:54–60](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/beginners-guide/backup-and-recovery/advanced-db-backup.md#L54-L60)
   The replica is recommended to live on a network-mounted (NFS v4) NAS or a USB disk in an operator-created directory; the only confidentiality warning is against rented cloud storage. The replica file is created 0644 there, readable by any user of any client of the share.

## Impact
Confidentiality HIGH: the entire wallet database (every issued rune, invoice and HTLC preimages, shared secrets, payment path secrets, channel/peer state, datastore) is readable. Integrity HIGH: a stolen rune grants the RPC authority it encodes and bypasses the 0600 socket that is the project's local-user control; operators commonly issue unrestricted or broad runes for commando/clnrest clients, in which case the reader can withdraw funds, open/close channels and change configuration; with only restricted runes the integrity gain is correspondingly smaller. Availability LOW: a sufficiently scoped rune can stop the node or close channels, but that follows from rune scope rather than the file read. The master rune secret is derived in hsmd and is not in the file, so the reader cannot mint new runes.

## Reproduction steps
1. A local unprivileged account on a host whose lightning network directory (or --wallet / replica directory) is traversable simply opens lightningd.sqlite3, which is 0644, with any sqlite client or by copying the file. From the runes table it takes a stored rune and uses it over commando from its own Lightning node connected to the victim (commando runs checkrune on every custom message from any peer) or via clnrest if enabled, obtaining that rune's RPC authority; it also reads preimages, HTLC shared secrets, path secrets and all channel/payment history. No race or control bypass is needed. The deployment precondition (network directory or replica directory not 0700) is a normal outcome of the documented setup and backup workflows, hence AT:P; privileges are those of any local login (PR:L).

## Recommended fix
1. The sqlite driver relies on the library default file mode and on the surrounding directory for the confidentiality of a file containing bearer credentials (runes) and payment secrets. Fix criteria: The wallet database, its journal/WAL files and any replica are created owner-only (0600) regardless of umask and directory mode (e.g. temporarily set umask 077 around sqlite3_open_v2, or open with a file: URI and modeof=/fchmod after creation), and an existing database with wider permissions is tightened or loudly warned about at startup. Verify by starting lightningd in a pre-existing 0755 network directory with umask 022 and checking that lightningd.sqlite3, its -journal/-wal and the replica are 0600.
2. lightningd accepts a pre-existing lightning-dir/network directory with any permissions and never re-checks it, so the implicit 0700 guarantee the rest of the design relies on does not hold for operator-created directories. Fix criteria: At startup lightningd verifies the network directory is not group/other accessible (or chmods it to 0700) and logs a clear warning or refuses to start when it is, and the documentation states the permission requirement for operator-created lightning directories and replica locations.

# Zero-length update_fail_htlc reason persists outgoing HTLC without resolution; fatal() after restart

## Details
BOLT2 `update_fail_htlc` carries `[u16 len][reason]`; CLN accepts len == 0. The generated decoder returns reason == NULL (tools/gen/impl_template:368), channeld wraps it as an onionreply with NULL contents (channeld.c:2824; tal_dup_ returns NULL for a NULL source), towire writes a 0-length blob, and lightningd's fromwire_onionreply() (common/onionreply.c:12-21, via fromwire_tal_arrn() returning NULL for 0 bytes) yields a *non-NULL* `struct onionreply` whose `contents` is NULL. peer_failed_our_htlc() (peer_htlcs.c:1791-1854) stores it as hout->failonion; in memory this passes htlc_out_check() because only the pointer is tested.

The wallet layer serialises the failure with db_bind_onionreply() -> db_bind_talarr(contents) (wallet.c:3553-3561, db/bindings.c:253-265), which binds SQL NULL for a NULL array. Every subsequent state write for this HTLC — SENT_REMOVE_REVOCATION from peer_sending_revocation() -> update_out_htlc() -> htlc_out_update_state(), then SENT_REMOVE_ACK_COMMIT — therefore records `failuremsg = NULL`, which the loader treats as 'no resolution' (wallet.c:3689-3698). In-memory and persisted representations disagree.

Without a restart the path is benign: remove_htlc_out() -> fail_out_htlc() -> payment_failed() -> unwrap_onionreply() returns NULL for empty contents and the payment ends as PAY_UNPARSEABLE_ONION. The defect bites across a restart.

An attacker who is our direct channel peer (or a downstream node whose empty reason CLN intermediaries relay unchanged, since wrap_onionreply() preserves length) fails an HTLC we *originated* (am_origin: we paid their invoice, or they are the first hop of our payment) with an empty reason, then withholds the final revoke_and_ack. The HTLC sits in SENT_REMOVE_ACK_COMMIT with a NULL-persisted resolution for as long as the attacker likes, bounded only by the HTLC's cltv (which, as invoice issuer, they set up to pay's ~2016-block cap) before htlcs_notify_new_block() force-closes.

If lightningd restarts in that window (routine upgrade/reboot), the HTLC is reloaded with failonion == NULL and failmsg == NULL. The COMPAT_V061 repair fixup_htlcs_out() skips am_origin HTLCs (peer_htlcs.c:3161-3174), so nothing restores a resolution; no load-time check aborts, and channeld's channel_force_htlcs() accepts the removing-state HTLC with failed == NULL, so the channel re-establishes. When the attacker sends revoke_and_ack, peer_got_revoke() -> changed_htlc() -> update_out_htlc() -> remove_htlc_out() -> htlc_out_check(hout, __func__) hits "Removing, no resolution" and corrupt() calls fatal() (peer_htlcs.c:2076-2082, htlc_end.c:78-90, 232-238). The abort discards the uncommitted DB transaction (io_loop_with_timers.c:29-32), so after every restart the peer can re-send the revoke and lightningd dies again: a remotely sustained crash loop until the operator blocks the peer and force-closes, or edits the DB.

For forwarded HTLCs the same NULL persistence occurs (hout and, after fail_in_htlc(), hin), but on default builds (COMPAT=1, Makefile:84-86) fixup_hout()/fixup_hin() substitute temporary_node_failure at load (with log_broken), so only the am_origin case crashes on default builds; with --disable-compat the incoming side also fatal()s at startup via wallet_htlcs_load_in_for_channel (wallet.c:3828-3832).

Root cause: zero-length onion replies are represented as 'onionreply present, contents NULL' in memory but as 'no failure' in the database; neither the wire layer nor wallet_htlc_update() normalises or rejects the empty reply.

## Evidence
1. [wallet/wallet.c:3553–3560](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L3553-L3560)
   wallet_htlc_update() stores the failure via db_bind_onionreply(failonion). For an onionreply whose contents pointer is NULL this binds SQL NULL, so the row records 'no resolution' although in memory hout->failonion is non-NULL and the HTLC is in a removing state.
2. [db/bindings.c:253–264](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/bindings.c#L253-L264)
   db_bind_onionreply() -> db_bind_talarr(r->contents): a NULL contents array becomes db_bind_null(), indistinguishable from 'never failed'.
3. [wallet/wallet.c:3689–3697](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L3689-L3697)
   On reload wallet_stmt2htlc_out() maps a NULL failuremsg column to out->failonion = NULL (and localfailmsg NULL), so the HTLC comes back with hstate in a removing state and no preimage/failonion/failmsg.
4. [wire/fromwire.c:239–253](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/fromwire.c#L239-L253)
   fromwire_tal_arrn() returns NULL for a zero-length array without failing the cursor.
5. [common/onionreply.c:12–40](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/onionreply.c#L12-L40)
   fromwire_onionreply() therefore returns a non-NULL onionreply with contents == NULL for a 0-length reply; new_onionreply()/dup_onionreply() preserve a NULL contents via tal_dup_talarr(NULL) == NULL.
6. [tools/gen/impl\_template:368](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/gen/impl_template#L368)
   Generated fromwire_update_fail_htlc() yields reason == NULL when the peer sends len == 0; the message is otherwise accepted.
7. [channeld/channeld.c:2802–2826](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L2802-L2826)
   handle_peer_fail_htlc() accepts a zero-length reason and forwards it to lightningd as an onionreply with NULL contents (towire writes u16 0).
8. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1791–1853](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1791-L1853)
   peer_failed_our_htlc() sets hout->failonion = dup_onionreply(failed->onion) (NULL contents); htlc_out_check() passes in memory because the pointer is non-NULL, and every subsequent wallet_htlc_update() for this HTLC persists NULL.
9. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:3161–3173](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L3161-L3173)
   fixup_htlcs_out() (COMPAT_V061 repair at load) deliberately skips am_origin HTLCs, so our own payments' outgoing HTLCs are not repaired on reload.
10. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2076–2081](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2076-L2081)
   After restart, when the peer's revoke_and_ack arrives, update_out_htlc() -> remove_htlc_out() calls htlc_out_check(hout, __func__) with a non-NULL abortstr.
11. [lightningd/htlc\_end.c:232–237](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/htlc_end.c#L232-L237)
   htlc_out_check() returns corrupt("Removing, no resolution") for a removing-state HTLC with no preimage/failonion/failmsg; with abortstr set, corrupt() calls fatal().

## Impact
lightningd aborts on every reconnect of the attacker after a restart, keeping the whole node (all channels, all HTLCs) down until the operator blocks the peer and force-closes or edits the database. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: remote peer we have a channel with and to whom we send an HTLC we originated (they issue an invoice we pay, or are the first hop of our payment); or a downstream node whose empty reason is relayed unchanged by CLN intermediaries, though then the honest direct peer's prompt revoke_and_ack shrinks the window to a round-trip. The attacker sends update_fail_htlc with len 0 plus commitment_signed, then withholds revoke_and_ack, leaving the HTLC persisted with failuremsg NULL for up to the HTLC's cltv window (~2016 blocks). Exploitation additionally requires that lightningd restart inside that window (AT:PRESENT: an execution condition the attacker cannot force; routine upgrades/reboots satisfy it). No credentials, no interaction with attacker content by the operator. After the restart the attacker reconnects and sends revoke_and_ack; lightningd fatal()s in remove_htlc_out and, because the transaction is rolled back, again on every subsequent restart.

## Recommended fix
1. wallet_htlc_update()/db_bind_onionreply() collapse an onionreply with empty contents into SQL NULL, which the loader interprets as 'no resolution', so persisted and in-memory HTLC state diverge. Fix criteria: A failed HTLC must round-trip through the database with a non-NULL resolution regardless of reply length (e.g. store a zero-length blob, or normalise empty replies to a concrete failure such as temporary_node_failure before persisting). Verify: fail an originated HTLC with a 0-length reason, restart before the peer's revoke_and_ack, deliver it, and confirm lightningd stays up and the payment is reported failed.
2. The wire layer accepts a zero-length update_fail_htlc reason and represents it with a NULL contents pointer that downstream code does not expect. Fix criteria: Either reject (warn/fail channel) a zero-length reason in channeld, or ensure onionreply decoding never produces a NULL contents array for a present reply, so all consumers see a consistent representation. Verify with the same scenario and with a forwarded HTLC under --disable-compat.

# addpsbtinput/addpsbtoutput abort lightningd on a caller-supplied PSBTv2 that forbids adding inputs/outputs

## Details
json_addpsbtoutput (wallet/reservation.c:645-744) and json_addpsbtinput (753-922) accept an optional caller-supplied `initialpsbt` (param_psbt -> wally_psbt_from_base64_n, common/json_param.c:940-952, bitcoin/psbt.c:868-882) and append to it in place. Every other lightningd RPC that extends a caller PSBT first normalises it with psbt_set_version(psbt, 2) and returns a JSON-RPC error on failure (reserveinputs reservation.c:95-100, unreserveinputs 156-161, signpsbt walletrpc.c:823, openchannel_init dual_open_control.c:3449, fundchannel_complete opening_control.c:1083, splice_init/update channel_control.c:2449/2500/2535). psbt_set_version also sets WALLY_PSBT_TXMOD_INPUTS|OUTPUTS on the PSBT (bitcoin/psbt.c:1109-1120), as create_psbt does for internally created PSBTs ('By default we are modifying them internally; allow it', psbt.c:29-30). The addpsbt* handlers instead run only validate_psbt(), which checks nothing but that wally can compute a serialized length (psbt.c:921-925), then hand the PSBT as-is to psbt_using_utxos -> psbt_append_input (reservation.c:891-893, 302-304) or psbt_append_output -> psbt_add_output (727-728).

Both helpers treat a libwally refusal as an invariant violation: psbt_append_input does `wally_err = wally_psbt_add_tx_input_at(...); assert(wally_err == WALLY_OK);` (psbt.c:233-234) and psbt_add_output does the same for wally_psbt_add_tx_output_at (262-272). Asserts are compiled into release builds (no NDEBUG anywhere).

Dependency assumption (libwally-core, the external/libwally-core submodule; its source is absent from this checkout and the tree records no commit pin): for a version-2 PSBT, wally_psbt_add_tx_input_at / wally_psbt_add_tx_output_at check the PSBT_GLOBAL_TX_MODIFIABLE flags (psbt_can_modify) and return WALLY_EINVAL when the inputs (resp. outputs) bit is unset; a v2 PSBT parsed from bytes without that optional field has flags 0 (BIP-370: absent means not modifiable). CLN's own code corroborates this: create_psbt and psbt_set_version explicitly set the flags so that internal appends succeed, and walletrpc.c:1013 notes that 'later calls may fail' when the version is not normalised.

A caller therefore base64-encodes a minimal PSBTv2 (magic, PSBT_GLOBAL_TX_VERSION, PSBT_GLOBAL_INPUT_COUNT=0, PSBT_GLOBAL_OUTPUT_COUNT=0, PSBT_GLOBAL_VERSION=2, no TX_MODIFIABLE field) and passes it as initialpsbt: addpsbtoutput with any satoshi >= dust reaches psbt_add_output and aborts; addpsbtinput with any non-zero satoshi reaches psbt_append_input as soon as the wallet holds one spendable UTXO and aborts. lightningd dies, taking every important plugin with it. A legitimately produced external PSBTv2 whose creator cleared the modifiable flags would crash the node the same way instead of yielding an error.

Attacker position: the operator, local-socket users and plugins are trusted, so the relevant attacker is a rune bearer — commando (always on, rune-checked per request over a Lightning peer connection) or clnrest — whose rune permits method addpsbtoutput or addpsbtinput. Such a rune bounds the bearer to adding an output/inputs to a PSBT (and, for addpsbtinput, reserving wallet UTXOs); killing the node is outside that bound. The shipped spender plugin's splice flow also calls these RPCs, but with a PSBT it created itself via create_psbt (plugins/spender/splice.c:2174), so that route is not attacker-controlled.

## Evidence
1. [wallet/reservation.c:783–798](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/reservation.c#L783-L798)
   addpsbtinput takes the caller's initialpsbt and runs only validate_psbt(); no psbt_set_version(2) and no check of the PSBT's TX_MODIFIABLE flags before inputs are appended.
2. [wallet/reservation.c:891–893](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/reservation.c#L891-L893)
   The unmodified caller PSBT is passed as `base` to psbt_using_utxos, which appends every selected UTXO via psbt_append_input (reservation.c:302-304).
3. [wallet/reservation.c:673–687](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/reservation.c#L673-L687)
   addpsbtoutput likewise accepts initialpsbt with only validate_psbt(); this route needs no wallet UTXO.
4. [wallet/reservation.c:727–728](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/reservation.c#L727-L728)
   psbt_append_output on the caller's PSBT.
5. [bitcoin/psbt.c:198–234](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/psbt.c#L198-L234)
   psbt_append_input asserts wally_psbt_add_tx_input_at returned WALLY_OK; a v2 PSBT without the inputs-modifiable flag makes libwally return WALLY_EINVAL (dependency assumption), so the assert aborts lightningd.
6. [bitcoin/psbt.c:262–298](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/psbt.c#L262-L298)
   psbt_add_output / psbt_insert_output / psbt_append_output assert wally_psbt_add_tx_output_at returned WALLY_OK.
7. [bitcoin/psbt.c:921–924](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/psbt.c#L921-L924)
   validate_psbt only checks that wally can compute the PSBT's serialized length; it does not normalise version or modifiable flags.
8. [bitcoin/psbt.c:1109–1119](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/psbt.c#L1109-L1119)
   psbt_set_version(..., 2) is what sets WALLY_PSBT_TXMOD_INPUTS|OUTPUTS; the other wallet/channel RPCs call it on caller PSBTs, addpsbtinput/addpsbtoutput do not.
9. [bitcoin/psbt.c:19–34](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/psbt.c#L19-L34)
   create_psbt sets the modifiable flags on every internally created PSBT ('By default we are modifying them internally; allow it') — in-repo acknowledgement that libwally refuses appends without them.
10. [wallet/reservation.c:95–99](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/reservation.c#L95-L99)
   Contrast: reserveinputs converts the caller PSBT to v2 (setting modifiable flags) and returns a clean error if that fails.
11. [common/json\_param.c:940–951](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_param.c#L940-L951)
   param_psbt accepts any base64 PSBT libwally can parse, including a PSBTv2 lacking PSBT_GLOBAL_TX_MODIFIABLE.

## Impact
assert() aborts lightningd; all channel, HTLC and on-chain monitoring stops and every important plugin dies with it until the operator restarts, with peers able to force-close on HTLC timeouts meanwhile. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. The triggering input is the base64 `initialpsbt` parameter of addpsbtoutput or addpsbtinput. The operator, plugins and local-socket users are trusted, so the attacker is a rune bearer — commando over a Lightning peer connection (always on, checkrune per request) or clnrest — whose rune permits one of these two methods (PR:L, AV:N). A single request carrying a minimal crafted PSBTv2 with no TX_MODIFIABLE field deterministically reaches the assert; no race and no configuration beyond holding such a rune (addpsbtinput additionally needs one spendable wallet UTXO). Exploitability rests on the stated libwally-core assumption that v2 wally_psbt_add_tx_input_at/_output_at return WALLY_EINVAL when the corresponding modifiable bit is unset; the submodule source is absent from the checkout, though CLN's own create_psbt/psbt_set_version flag-setting corroborates it.

## Recommended fix
addpsbtinput/addpsbtoutput operate on a caller-controlled PSBT without normalising it (version/modifiable flags), while the append helpers treat any libwally refusal as an internal invariant violation (assert). Fix criteria: A caller-supplied initialpsbt that libwally refuses to extend must produce a JSON-RPC error (e.g. FUNDING_PSBT_INVALID) and leave the daemon running; verify by calling addpsbtoutput/addpsbtinput with a PSBTv2 lacking the TX_MODIFIABLE inputs/outputs bits and observing an error response. Either normalise the PSBT (psbt_set_version(psbt, 2) with failure handled) before appending, or make psbt_append_input/psbt_append_output report failure to these RPC callers instead of asserting.

# getroutes aborts askrene when a named layer is removed before the request is dispatched

## Details
getroutes validates its `layers` argument by name in param_layer_names (askrene.c:95-132) and then keeps only the strings in getroutes_info. The actual lookup happens later in apply_layers (askrene.c:389-412), which is reached either (a) from listpeerchannels_done after an asynchronous `listpeerchannels` round trip whenever `auto.localchans` is listed, or (b) from destroy_live_command when the request had been parked in the FIFO `waiters` list because max_children (default 4) routing children were already running. In both cases other JSON-RPC commands are processed by the plugin in between. If `askrene-remove-layer` deletes one of the named layers in that window, find_layer() returns NULL for a name that is not `auto.localchans`/`auto.no_mpp_support`/`auto.include_fees`, and the code falls into `assert(streq(layernames[i], "auto.sourcefree"))`, which fails and calls abort(). Asserts are compiled into release builds, and cln-askrene is an `important` plugin, so lightningd shuts down.

Attack path (deterministic): a caller permitted getroutes, askrene-create-layer and askrene-remove-layer (e.g. a commando/clnrest rune bearer) creates layer L; issues getroutes with layers [L, "auto.localchans"] (or fills the four child slots with slow getroutes and then queues one naming L); then issues askrene-remove-layer L before the queued/async request is dispatched. When it is dispatched the assert fires. A caller with only askrene-remove-layer can achieve the same by removing a layer that a concurrent xpay/renepay payment names (xpay always passes the persistent `xpay` layer plus its per-payment private layer, and waits on listpeerchannels every time), racing the operator's own payments.

The rune authorises layer management and route queries, not termination of the node; the crash is therefore an impact beyond the granted authority. Root cause: a check-then-use gap on a name-keyed resource across asynchronous boundaries, with the unknown-name case handled by an assert rather than an error.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:389–411](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L389-L411)
   apply_layers re-resolves every caller-supplied layer name with find_layer(); a NULL result that is not one of the three auto.* names hits assert(streq(layernames[i], "auto.sourcefree")) and aborts the plugin.
2. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:95–131](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L95-L131)
   param_layer_names validates that each name exists only at parameter-parse time; it stores the names as strings, not layer pointers, so later removal is not detected.
3. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:965–972](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L965-L972)
   When num_live_requests >= max_children (default 4) the parsed request is parked in askrene->waiters and begins only when another request finishes, giving an arbitrarily long window in which other RPCs run.
4. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:876–886](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L876-L886)
   With auto.localchans (always used by xpay) begin_request issues an asynchronous listpeerchannels; do_getroutes/apply_layers only run from listpeerchannels_done, so other RPC commands are processed in between even without the queue.
5. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:852–865](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L852-L865)
   destroy_live_command dequeues a waiter and calls begin_request -> do_getroutes -> apply_layers without re-validating the layer names.
6. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:1399–1416](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L1399-L1416)
   askrene-remove-layer is synchronous and unconditional: remove_layer() frees the layer and deletes it from the hash table, so a subsequent find_layer() returns NULL.
7. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:976–979](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L976-L979)
   remove_layer frees the layer; destroy_layer removes it from askrene->layers.

## Impact
abort() in an important plugin terminates lightningd (plugin.c builtin plugins are important), halting all payment, channel and HTLC handling until the operator restarts. No data is read or modified.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any RPC caller admitted to askrene methods, including a network rune bearer via commando or clnrest. Steps: create a layer, call getroutes naming it together with auto.localchans (or queue it behind four busy children), immediately call askrene-remove-layer on it. The request is dispatched later, find_layer returns NULL, the assert aborts the plugin and lightningd stops. No special deployment state is needed; the waiter queue makes ordering deterministic.

## Recommended fix
1. apply_layers treats a layer name that no longer resolves as an impossible condition (assert) although layers can be removed between parameter validation and dispatch. Fix criteria: A getroutes request whose named layer has disappeared by dispatch time must complete with a JSON-RPC error (or re-resolve/skip the layer) and never abort; the create/getroutes/remove sequence described above must leave the plugin running.
2. Layer identity is carried across asynchronous boundaries by name only, so removal is undetected. Fix criteria: Either resolve layers to pointers at parse time and keep them alive (or invalidate pending requests) until dispatch, or re-validate names at dispatch and fail gracefully; concurrent askrene-remove-layer must not be able to crash in-flight getroutes requests.

# check_invoice_request_usage reads one unordered payments row, so a payee can collect a single-use invoice_request more than once

## Details
check_invoice_request_usage() (lightningd/pay.c:798-849) is the control that makes a single-use invoice_request we published payable at most once: its comment says "we must not attempt more than one payment at once for single_use invoice_request we publish", doc/schemas/invoicerequest.json promises "only one person can take the money", and tests/test_pay.py:5219-5225 expects a second sendinvoice while the first is pending to fail with "pay attempt failed". The guard queries every payments row carrying that local_invreq_id (wallet/wallet.c:4708-4741, no ORDER BY, no LIMIT, no index on local_invreq_id) but examines only the first row returned and frees the statement: COMPLETE/PENDING reject, FAILED admits. The decision is thus a property of whichever row the engine returns first, not of the set. On SQLite the unindexed scan returns the lowest rowid, i.e. the oldest payment for that request (id is BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY rewritten to INTEGER, aliasing rowid; UPDATEs keep the rowid). Assumption: SQLite returns rows of an unordered, unindexed SELECT in rowid order (standard behaviour, not an SQL guarantee); on PostgreSQL heap order is unpredictable and the guard is unreliable in both directions.

Attack (payee as adversary): the operator issues a single-use invoice_request to the payee (invoicerequest, e.g. a refund). (1) The payee answers with invoice #1 by onion message; offers_inv_hook.c:185-201 verifies it and calls xpay with localinvreqid; injectpaymentonion admits it (no rows yet) and the HTLC goes out, inserting the first payments row. As final node the payee fails that HTLC with any error (a stock CLN payee can simply delinvoice before the HTLC arrives); payment_failed() (pay.c:640) marks the oldest row FAILED. The request remains active because mark_used only runs on success (pay.c:374). (2) The payee sends invoice #2 (a fresh payment_hash): the hook sees the request active and starts xpay; check_progress passes (new hash) and check_invoice_request_usage reads the FAILED row first and admits the HTLC. The payee holds it. (3) The payee sends invoice #3, #4, ...: each is admitted the same way because the first row is still the FAILED one, regardless of the PENDING rows behind it. (4) The payee fulfils all held HTLCs and receives N times the invreq amount. The variant in which the payee fails part 1 of a single payment and holds its retried part 2 pending before sending invoice #2 works identically. The amount per invoice is bounded by invreq_amount (hook line 187), so the loss is a multiple of the amount the operator authorised once.

Secondary effect: a second concurrent MPP part of the same payment_hash sees a PENDING first row and is refused as "already in progress", so multi-part payment of a single-use invoice_request is stranded unless a FAILED row happens to sort first; this is the open lead at pay.c:798-849.

Fix: the check must consider every row (any COMPLETE row, or any PENDING row for a different payment_hash, rejects) independently of row order, and should permit further parts of the same payment_hash.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/pay.c:822–846](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L822-L846)
   After confirming the invoice_request is active and single-use, the guard calls payments_by_invoice_request(), reads only the first stepped row with payment_get_details(), frees the statement and decides on that row alone: COMPLETE/PENDING reject, FAILED falls through and admits the new HTLC. Any PENDING or COMPLETE rows after the first are never examined, so once a FAILED row is the first row returned the guard admits every later payment for the same single-use request.
2. [wallet/wallet.c:4708–4740](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L4708-L4740)
   payments_by_invoice_request() is `SELECT ... FROM payments WHERE local_invreq_id = ?` with no ORDER BY and no LIMIT; payments_next() steps once. Which row comes first is an engine detail: on SQLite the unindexed scan returns the lowest rowid (the oldest payment), on PostgreSQL heap order.
3. [wallet/migrations.c:986](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/migrations.c#L986)
   local_invreq_id is added to payments without any index (the only payments indexes are payments_idx on payment_hash, line 939, and payments_update_idx on updated_index, line 1030); id is BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, rewritten to INTEGER for SQLite (devtools/sql-rewrite.py:47) so it aliases rowid and the unordered scan yields the oldest row first.
4. [plugins/offers\_inv\_hook.c:185–200](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_inv_hook.c#L185-L200)
   When the payee delivers a signed BOLT12 invoice for one of our stored invoice_requests over an onion message (offers.c:325-329 -> handle_invoice), the offers plugin only checks the request is still `active` and the amount does not exceed invreq_amount, then calls xpay with localinvreqid. The payee can deliver any number of invoices (distinct payment_hashes) while earlier ones are in flight; there is no per-invreq in-flight tracking in the plugin.
5. [lightningd/pay.c:1926–1930](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1926-L1930)
   json_injectpaymentonion calls check_invoice_request_usage() for every part before offering the HTLC; this is the guard the xpay/offers flow relies on. sendpay (1112-1114) uses the same guard.
6. [lightningd/pay.c:359–377](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L359-L377)
   payment_succeeded() marks the invoice_request used only when a part completes; while payments are merely pending or have failed the request stays active, so the hook keeps accepting invoices and the single-row check is the only thing preventing concurrent payments.
7. [lightningd/pay.c:640–642](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L640-L642)
   payment_failed() sets the payments row to PAYMENT_FAILED on any onion error returned for the HTLC; as final node the payee chooses that error (e.g. incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details, which a stock CLN payee produces by deleting the invoice before the HTLC arrives), so the payee decides that the oldest row for the invreq is FAILED.
8. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1539–1540](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L1539-L1540)
   xpay forwards localinvreqid on every injectpaymentonion part, so every part consults check_invoice_request_usage and every HTLC inserts a payments row carrying local_invreq_id (register_payment_and_waiter, pay.c:2138-2144).
9. [lightningd/offer.c:391](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L391)
   createinvoicerequest defaults single_use to true, so the single-use branch of check_invoice_request_usage is the normal case for every invoicerequest the operator issues.

## Impact
The node pays the invoice_request amount two or more times: a direct, attacker-chosen loss of channel funds, a multiple of the amount the operator authorised exactly once, which is the integrity property the guard exists to protect. No confidentiality impact. Availability LOW: legitimate concurrent MPP parts of a single-use request are refused by the same first-row semantics, stranding our own payments.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the payment counterparty (threat-model adversary 3) who legitimately received one of our single-use invoice_requests, a normal business flow (refund). They need no privileges on our node and no operator action at attack time: they deliver invoices by onion message, fail their own first HTLC as final node, then deliver further invoices whose HTLCs are all admitted because the oldest payments row is FAILED, and fulfil them. Deterministic on SQLite (default backend) given the rowid-order assumption; attack_requirements PRESENT because an outstanding single-use invoice_request to the attacker must exist.

## Recommended fix
check_invoice_request_usage() bases its single-use decision on the first row of an unordered multi-row result instead of on the whole set of payments recorded for the invoice_request, and the offers hook has no in-flight tracking per invoice_request. Fix criteria: The check iterates every payments row for the local_invreq_id and rejects when any row is COMPLETE, or PENDING for a different payment_hash, regardless of row order; a second payment attempt for the same invoice_request while another attempt is pending, with an earlier FAILED row present, is refused on both SQLite and PostgreSQL; further MPP parts of the same payment_hash are still accepted.

# db_set_intvar/db_get_intvar truncate s64 to 32 bits; wrapped deleted_forward_fees makes getinfo db_fatal() and crash-loops startup

## Details
The vars-table integer API in db/exec.c advertises 64-bit storage (void db_set_intvar(struct db *, const char *, s64) / s64 db_get_intvar(...)) but implements it with db_bind_int()/db_col_int(), both C int (db/bindings.c:43-59). Every 64-bit quantity stored through it keeps only its low 32 bits and reads back sign-extended: sqlite binds with sqlite3_bind_int and reads with sqlite3_column_int (db/db_sqlite3.c:259, 366); postgres sends a 4-byte INT4 and reads exactly 4 bytes (db/db_postgres.c:105-110, 183-195), and vars.intval is declared INTEGER (wallet/migrations.c:553), i.e. int4 on postgres.

One caller stores a monetary sum through it. wallet_forward_delete() (wallet/wallet.c:5957-5963), reached from the delforward RPC (lightningd/forwards.c:264-292) and therefore from the autoclean plugin whenever autoclean-succeededforwards-age is set (default 0 = never; plugins/autoclean.c:102-108), adds the msat fees (in_msatoshi − out_msatoshi) of each deleted settled forward to the intvar deleted_forward_fees. Let D be the true cumulative deleted fees; the row holds D mod 2^32, and whenever bit 31 of that is set db_get_intvar returns the negative value (D mod 2^32) − 2^32.

wallet_total_forward_fees() (wallet/wallet.c:5680-5683) converts that to amount_msat, a u64 equal to 2^64 − K with K = 2^32 − (D mod 2^32) in (0, 2^31], then calls amount_msat_accumulate(&total, deleted) where total is the fee sum of settled forwards still in the forwards table. add_overflows_u64 fires exactly when total ≥ K, and the code then calls db_fatal() → db_error → fatal_vfmt (wallet/db.c:91-101), aborting lightningd. When total < K the call does not abort but reports a value near 2^64; when bit 31 is clear it reports D mod 2^32, silently wrong for every D ≥ 2^31 msat. The fatal window therefore recurs every 2^32 msat (~4.29M sat, ~0.043 BTC) of deleted fees: as D mod 2^32 climbs through [2^31, 2^32), K shrinks toward 0 and any routing node whose not-yet-cleaned settled forwards hold ≥ K msat of fees trips it. With autoclean age ≥ autoclean cycle, the per-cycle increment of D is at most the remaining total, so the window cannot be skipped.

wallet_total_forward_fees() is called unconditionally by getinfo (lightningd/peer_control.c:3673-3675) for fees_collected_msat, so once in the window any getinfo — from the operator, any rune holder (getinfo is in practically every read-only rune), clnrest/grpc clients or a plugin — kills the node. The important builtin plugins pay (plugins/pay.c:239), keysend, askrene, offers, topology, chanbackup and recover call getinfo in init, which lightningd serves during plugins_config() after jsonrpc_listen() (lightningd/lightningd.c:1419-1423), so lightningd dies on every subsequent startup. While down, autoclean cannot advance D out of the window, so the crash loop persists until the operator hand-edits vars.intval (or starts with every getinfo-at-init plugin disabled and manually deletes enough forwards).

Who drives the counter: routing peers and payment counterparties forwarding through the node. check_fwd_amount (lightningd/peer_htlcs.c:378-404) only requires in − fee ≥ out, so a payer may overpay fees arbitrarily (bounded by channel/HTLC limits): a hostile party with channels on both sides can push D to just below a 2^32 boundary with forwards that autoclean later deletes, then route one fresh settled forward whose fee ≥ K, at a worst-case cost of about 2^32 msat paid to the victim, and after waiting out the configured autoclean age. A busy node reaches the window by itself once lifetime deleted fees pass ~0.02 BTC.

The same truncation affects the u64 wait indexes written by wait_index_bump() (lightningd/wait.c:150-156) and restored by load_indexes() (wallet/db.c:464-473), which wrap after 2^31 events and break wait/list pagination, and bip32_max_index/next_pay_index; these share the root cause and fix.

This holds only on nodes where forward deletion is enabled (autoclean-succeededforwards-age configured, or delforward used by the operator or a plugin); the option is documented and opt-in, not a shipped control.

## Evidence
1. [db/exec.c:60–77](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/exec.c#L60-L77)
   db_set_intvar() takes an s64 but stores it with db_bind_int(stmt, val), whose parameter is a C int: the value is silently truncated to its low 32 bits in both the UPDATE and INSERT branches.
2. [db/exec.c:79–90](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/exec.c#L79-L90)
   db_get_intvar() returns s64 but reads the column with db_col_int(), which returns int: the stored 32-bit value is sign-extended, so anything with bit 31 set comes back negative.
3. [wallet/wallet.c:5957–5963](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L5957-L5963)
   wallet_forward_delete() (delforward RPC, driven by autoclean) adds each deleted settled forward's msat fee to the running total and persists it with db_set_intvar("deleted_forward_fees", deleted.millisatoshis): a u64 msat sum stored through the 32-bit path, so the row holds D mod 2^32.
4. [wallet/wallet.c:5680–5683](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L5680-L5683)
   wallet_total_forward_fees() reads the variable back as amount_msat(db_get_intvar(...)); when bit 31 of the stored value is set the negative s64 becomes a u64 of 2^64 − K (K = 2^32 − (D mod 2^32)), amount_msat_accumulate() overflows whenever the remaining settled-forward fee total is ≥ K, and the code calls db_fatal(), killing lightningd; otherwise the reported total is wrong.
5. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:3673–3675](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L3673-L3675)
   json_getinfo() unconditionally calls wallet_total_forward_fees() for fees_collected_msat, so every getinfo call reaches the fatal path while the counter is in the window.
6. [plugins/pay.c:239–240](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L239-L240)
   The important builtin pay plugin issues getinfo during init (as do keysend, askrene, offers, topology, chanbackup, recover), served by lightningd during plugins_config() after jsonrpc_listen(); once in the window lightningd dies on every startup and autoclean cannot advance the counter out of it.
7. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:378–404](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L378-L404)
   check_fwd_amount() only requires amt_in − fee ≥ amt_to_forward, so the payer chooses how much fee (in_msatoshi − out_msatoshi) a forward carries: remote parties control the size of each increment to deleted_forward_fees and to the remaining settled total.
8. [db/bindings.c:43–58](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/bindings.c#L43-L58)
   db_bind_int(struct db_stmt *, int) and int db_col_int() are the 32-bit chokepoints the s64 intvar API is built on; the 64-bit db_bind_s64/db_col_s64 exist (bindings.c:70-80, 291-294) but are not used by exec.c.
9. [db/db\_sqlite3.c:258–260](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_sqlite3.c#L258-L260)
   sqlite driver binds DB_BINDING_INT with sqlite3_bind_int (32-bit); db_sqlite3_column_int (363-367) reads with sqlite3_column_int, so the round trip is 32-bit on sqlite.
10. [db/db\_postgres.c:105–110](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_postgres.c#L105-L110)
   postgres driver sends DB_BINDING_INT as a 4-byte INT4 and db_postgres_column_int (183-195) requires exactly 4 bytes, so the vars.intval round trip is 32-bit on postgres as well.
11. [wallet/migrations.c:553](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/migrations.c#L553)
   vars.intval is declared INTEGER, which is int4 on PostgreSQL: fixing the bindings alone would not widen the column there, so a schema migration is part of the fix.
12. [wallet/db.c:91–101](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/db.c#L91-L101)
   lightningd's db errorfn: db_fatal() logs LOG_BROKEN and calls fatal_vfmt(), aborting the whole daemon.
13. [lightningd/wait.c:150–155](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/wait.c#L150-L155)
   wait_index_bump() persists the u64 wait indexes (last_<subsystem>_<index>_index) through the same db_set_intvar path; they are restored by load_indexes() (wallet/db.c:464-473) via db_get_intvar, so they wrap at 2^31 events (secondary consequence of the same root cause).

## Impact
Availability: lightningd aborts on getinfo and crash-loops at startup until the operator hand-edits vars.intval; channels are unmonitored meanwhile. Integrity: fees_collected_msat is wrong for all lifetime deleted fees ≥ 2^31 msat (and near 2^64 in the non-fatal part of the window); wait indexes wrap at 2^31 events. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Precondition on the deployment: forward deletion enabled (autoclean-succeededforwards-age set, default never, or delforward used). Routing peers and payers forward HTLCs through the node and choose the fee each carries (check_fwd_amount only bounds it from below); autoclean later moves each settled forward's fee into the 32-bit deleted_forward_fees counter. Once D mod 2^32 ≥ 2^31 and the fees of not-yet-cleaned settled forwards reach 2^32 − (D mod 2^32), the next getinfo — issued by any rune holder, RPC client or the pay plugin's init — makes lightningd db_fatal(), and it fails at every startup thereafter. No privileges are needed; a hostile party can force it at a worst-case cost of ~2^32 msat (~0.043 BTC) paid to the victim plus waiting out the autoclean age, and a busy node reaches the window on its own.

## Recommended fix
1. db_set_intvar/db_get_intvar promise s64 but bind and read through 32-bit db_bind_int/db_col_int, silently truncating and sign-extending. Fix criteria: An intvar written with any s64 value must read back equal to that value on both sqlite3 and postgres, including a migration that widens vars.intval to a 64-bit column on postgres. Verify by storing 2^31, 2^32+1 and a negative value and reading them back; audit every db_set_intvar/db_get_intvar caller for 64-bit quantities (deleted_forward_fees, wait indexes, bip32/bip86_max_index, next_pay_index).
2. wallet_total_forward_fees treats an impossible negative stored total as fatal rather than as corrupt data, turning the truncation into a node-wide crash loop reachable from getinfo and plugin init. Fix criteria: A corrupt/negative deleted_forward_fees value must not abort lightningd: getinfo should log and report a clamped or absent value. Existing databases holding a wrapped value must be repaired or tolerated on upgrade so a node already in the fatal window starts again.
