# xpay out-of-bounds hop access and assert abort on errors from blinded paths with 3+ hops

## Details
xpay models a BOLT12 blinded path as a single fake route hop (add_blindedpath: scid = path index, destination = fakenode), so attempt->hops has one entry per real channel plus one fake entry. The onion, however, carries one sphinx hop per blinded-path hop (append_blinded_payloads). With k real hops and a blinded path of N hops, attempt->hops has k+1 entries while attempt->shared_secrets (sized by create_onionpacket from the sphinx hop count) has k+N entries.

When a part fails, update_knowledge_from_error() (xpay.c:959) calls unwrap_onionreply() with all k+N secrets and receives the erring sphinx index, which for an error generated by the final blinded node is k+N-1. The code assumes index <= tal_count(hops): it treats index == tal_count(hops) as 'final' (correct only for N==2) and otherwise uses `index` directly to address attempt->hops with no bounds check. For N >= 3, index >= k+2 > tal_count(hops):

- xpay.c:977-991 reads hops[i] for i up to index-1 (out of bounds) and sends askrene-inform-channel 'unconstrained' for the garbage scidd/amount, to the persistent 'xpay' layer if the garbage fake_channel byte is 0;
- xpay.c:996 reads hops[index-1].next_node (out of bounds) to decide from_final, which therefore is almost always false;
- the non-final branch reads hops[index] in process_channel_update_from_onion_error (765), in the switch (1130, 1157) and in the disable_channel/channel_capacity labels (1176, 1185-1191);
- describe_scidd() (561-567) reads hops[index].scidd out of bounds and then hits assert(index < tal_count(attempt->hops)) -> abort(). It is reached for WIRE_TEMPORARY_CHANNEL_FAILURE, the whole 'weird error' group, and via the strange_error label for every failcode not listed in the switch (there is no default), e.g. incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details or mpp_timeout sent by a recipient that does not convert to invalid_onion_blinding;
- outgoing_notify_failure() (675-683) emits the out-of-bounds heap bytes in the pay_part_end notification.

xpay is a builtin important plugin (plugin.c:2578-2586); an abort() takes lightningd down (plugin.c:297-302). The ordinary `pay` command is redirected to xpay by default (take_over_pay = true, xpay.c:3570), so every BOLT12 payment goes through this code.

Attack: the payee publishes an offer; its invoice (fetched by the victim via fetchinvoice/xpay/pay) contains a blinded path with N >= 3 hops (the recipient may pad with dummy hops to itself per BOLT 4, or use three real nodes; invoice_decode only requires N != 0). When the HTLC reaches the last blinded hop, the payee returns any failure other than invalid_onion_blinding (e.g. temporary_channel_failure or incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details): xpay aborts and lightningd exits. With invalid_onion_blinding (what a CLN recipient would send) the process does not abort but reads roughly 112-byte struct hop entries beyond the hops array and feeds the garbage to askrene. Honest 3+-hop blinded paths from other implementations that fail for ordinary reasons are also affected; CLN's own offers plugin emits 2-hop paths, which is why tests (tests/test_xpay.py:824) never exercise the case.

Root cause: update_knowledge_from_error() conflates sphinx hop indices with route hop indices; any index >= tal_count(hops) (anything inside the blinded path beyond its second hop) must be clamped to the fake hop / final node before attempt->hops is indexed.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:959–1000](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L959-L1000)
   update_knowledge_from_error() unwraps the failure onion with tal_count(attempt->shared_secrets) secrets (one per sphinx hop, including every blinded-path hop) and receives `index` in [0, sphinx_hops-1]. It then uses that index against attempt->hops (one entry per askrene route hop, the whole blinded path being one fake hop): the loop at 977 reads hops[i] for i < index, line 994 only special-cases index == tal_count(hops), and line 996 reads hops[index-1]. No check that index <= tal_count(hops) exists; with a blinded path of N >= 3 hops the final blinded node's index is tal_count(hops)+N-2.
2. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:561–566](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L561-L566)
   describe_scidd() reads attempt->hops[index].scidd before its assert(index < tal_count(attempt->hops)), which fires and abort()s. Reached from the non-final branch for temporary_channel_failure (1129), the 'weird error' group (1148), the strange_error label (1168) that every failcode absent from the switch falls into (e.g. incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details, mpp_timeout) and the channel_update path (1108).
3. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1370–1407](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L1370-L1407)
   append_blinded_payloads() adds one sphinx hop per hop of the recipient-authored blinded path (tal_count(path->path)); create_onion() (1451-1469) adds one sphinx hop per real route hop and breaks at the fake hop, so create_onionpacket() (common/sphinx.c:541) allocates (route_hops-1)+N shared secrets while attempt->hops has route_hops entries.
4. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1101–1193](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L1101-L1193)
   Non-final branch: process_channel_update_from_onion_error(index) reads hops[index].scidd (765), the switch reads hops[index] for temporary_channel_failure (1130) and invalid_onion_blinding (1157), and the disable_channel/channel_capacity labels (1176, 1185-1191) read hops[index].fake_channel/scidd/amount_out; all out of bounds for index >= tal_count(hops), and the garbage is sent as askrene-inform-channel/askrene-update-channel (to the persistent 'xpay' layer when the garbage fake_channel byte is zero).
5. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:675–682](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L675-L682)
   outgoing_notify_failure() is called at 1015 with the same index and reads hops[failindex-1].next_node and hops[failindex] out of bounds, emitting those heap bytes in the pay_part_end notification.
6. [common/sphinx.c:855–896](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L855-L896)
   unwrap_onionreply() sets *origin_index = i for any i < numhops whose HMAC verifies; numhops is the sphinx hop count including every blinded hop, so the erring blinded node's sphinx position is reported directly.
7. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:2080–2136](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L2080-L2136)
   add_blindedpath() models the entire blinded path as one fake channel (scid = path index, destination = xpay->fakenode), so askrene's route, and hence attempt->hops, has exactly one entry for the whole path regardless of its hop count.
8. [common/bolt12.c:598–617](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L598-L617)
   invoice_decode() rejects only zero-hop blinded paths and requires one payinfo per path; it places no upper bound on hops in a recipient-supplied blinded path, and xpay_core (2769-2788) adds none (only the onion's 1300-byte limit applies).
9. [lightningd/pay.c:1727–1756](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1727-L1756)
   injectonion_fail() returns the raw failure onion (wrapped once with the local hop secret) as error data 'onionreply' for xpay to unwrap, so the recipient's failure message reaches update_knowledge_from_error() unaltered.
10. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:208–214](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L208-L214)
   A compliant CLN recipient inside a blinded path converts every failure to invalid_onion_blinding (the non-aborting but still out-of-bounds-reading case); a recipient running other software or deliberately returning any other failcode reaches the assert.
11. [lightningd/plugin.c:2578–2585](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2578-L2585)
   cln-xpay is registered as an important plugin; its abort() makes lightningd shut down (plugin.c:297-302).

## Impact
Abort of the important cln-xpay plugin shuts lightningd down, leaving in-flight HTLCs/channels unattended until restart (availability HIGH). The OOB reads also leak a few heap bytes into pay_part_end notifications and push garbage constraints into askrene layers (including the persistent 'xpay' layer), a minor confidentiality/integrity effect on routing knowledge.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a payment counterparty (payee). They hand the victim a BOLT12 offer/invoice whose blinded path has 3 or more hops (dummy hops are spec-legal and need no cooperation from anyone else), the victim runs `pay`/`xpay` on it, and the attacker's node — the final blinded hop — fails the HTLC with any failcode other than invalid_onion_blinding. xpay unwraps the error at sphinx index k+N-1 >= tal_count(hops)+1, reads outside attempt->hops and reaches describe_scidd()'s assert → abort → lightningd exits. Default configuration; the only requirement is that the victim chooses to pay the invoice.

## Recommended fix
1. update_knowledge_from_error() uses the sphinx erring-hop index returned by unwrap_onionreply() directly as an index into attempt->hops, although blinded paths add more sphinx hops than route hops; no bounds check exists and describe_scidd() asserts instead of handling it. Fix criteria: Any erring index at or beyond the last real route hop (i.e. inside the blinded path) must be mapped to the fake blinded-path hop / 'final node' handling before attempt->hops is indexed, and every access to attempt->hops[index] / hops[index-1] must be provably in-bounds. A BOLT12 payment through a 3+-hop blinded path that fails from the last hop with any failcode must produce a clean payment failure with lightningd still running and no garbage askrene-inform/update calls.
2. describe_scidd() reads attempt->hops[index] before its assert, and the assert turns a recipient-triggerable condition into a process abort of an important plugin. Fix criteria: describe_scidd() (and outgoing_notify_failure) must validate index before dereferencing and must not abort on out-of-range input from onion errors; an out-of-range index should be logged and treated as 'destination'.

# Fundee funding-timeout deletes live zero-conf channel; pending HTLC makes lightningd fatal() repeatedly

## Details
channel_notify_new_block() implements the BOLT #2 fundee rule 'forget the channel if it does not see the funding transaction after 2016 blocks' via is_fundee_should_forget() (lightningd/channel_control.c:2093-2129). The predicate checks only opener==REMOTE, scid==NULL, age >= dev_max_funding_unconfirmed (2016), our_funds==0 and msat_to_us_max==0; it never looks at channel->state. A zero-conf channel opened to us (openchannel hook returned mindepth 0, applied at opening_control.c:839-846) reaches CHANNELD_NORMAL on channel_ready without an scid: peer_got_channel_ready (channel_control.c:1287-1310) calls lockin_complete because depth 0 >= minimum_depth 0, and lockin_complete (1159-1186) accepts the two aliases in lieu of an scid; scid is only set when the funding confirms (channel_apply_scid 854-879). Such a channel carries HTLCs (channel_state_can_add_htlc, channel.h:522-545). Our balance only rises in remove_htlc_in() when an incoming HTLC is fully removed with a preimage (peer_htlcs.c:2024-2057), and an incoming HTLC is only removed from ld->htlcs_in at SENT_REMOVE_ACK_REVOCATION (peer_htlcs.c:2146), i.e. after the peer's own revoke_and_ack; lightningd never fails unfulfilled incoming HTLCs at their deadline (peer_htlcs.c:3080-3094). So the remote peer decides both that the channel keeps msat_to_us_max==0 (no push, never let a fulfil complete) and that an htlc_in stays attached (add an HTLC and withhold the final revoke_and_ack, or never ack our fail).

When the node holds >= 101 'forgettable' channels (forgettable_channels_to_keep = 100, channel_control.c:2158-2192) the oldest are passed to delete_channel(channel, true) (2206). delete_channel() (channel.c:89-131) unwatches, deletes the DB row, tells hsmd to forget the channel and tal_free()s it; the destructor destroy_channel() (channel.c:63-87) calls fatal() if any htlc_in/htlc_out is still attached. fatal() aborts (log.c:1130-1144) inside the per-plugin-reply DB transaction that wraps bcli's block response (plugin.c:706-737; want_db_transaction is true after startup, plugin.c:2556), so nothing is committed; on restart the same block is fetched and the same channel with the same hin is loaded, and lightningd dies again. Even if the block had been committed, the predicate is height-based and fires on every subsequent block. The node stays in a crash loop until the funding confirms or the operator edits the database (cancel_channel_before_broadcast refuses channels with HTLCs, channel_control.c:2300-2310, and dev-forget-channel goes through the same delete path).

Even without a pending HTLC, the path silently deletes an operational CHANNELD_NORMAL channel out from under its channeld and peer; our funds are zero by construction so no money is lost.

The supporting 100 forgettable channels are ordinary unfunded v1 fundee opens: peer_control.c:2254-2268 accepts a new open_channel whenever the previous one has been committed (funding_signed sent), with no cap, from any node id; honest abandoned opens also count (the Boltz comment at 2155-2157). The attacker opens the zero-conf channel first and the stubs afterwards so that cmp_channel_start (2131-2138) makes the live channel the oldest.

Reachability condition: we become a zero-conf fundee only when a plugin returns mindepth 0 from the documented openchannel hook field (doc/schemas/hook/openchannel.json:185-189). In the shipped tree that is the LSPS client (plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:662-722), active when the operator sets experimental-lsps-client (doc/lightningd-config.5.md:895) and has run lsps-lsps2-invoice (which calls lsps-lsps2-approve, client.rs:492, writing the one-shot lsps/client/<lsp_id> record). The attacker is therefore the LSP peer the user chose for a JIT channel; the LSPS2 zero-conf design concedes that peer the funds in the unconfirmed channel, not the availability of the whole node. The same exposure applies to any operator plugin that grants mindepth 0 to a peer.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2093–2128](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2093-L2128)
   is_fundee_should_forget() decides on opener==REMOTE, scid==NULL, age >= 2016, our_funds==0 and msat_to_us_max==0 only; it never checks channel->state or attached HTLCs, so a zero-conf channel in CHANNELD_NORMAL with an unconfirmed funding qualifies like an unfunded CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN stub. This is the predicate the fix must change.
2. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2140–2207](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2140-L2207)
   channel_notify_new_block() collects every qualifying committed channel, keeps the 100 newest by first_blocknum, and calls delete_channel(channel, true) on the rest, on every block.
3. [lightningd/channel.c:63–86](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L63-L86)
   destroy_channel() (tal destructor) calls fatal() if any htlc_in or htlc_out is still attached to the channel; for a live zero-conf channel the remote peer decides whether an incoming HTLC is attached.
4. [lightningd/channel.c:89–130](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L89-L130)
   delete_channel() deletes the DB row, tells hsmd to forget the channel and tal_free()s the channel object with no HTLC check, reaching the destructor's fatal().
5. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1287–1310](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1287-L1310)
   peer_got_channel_ready(): for a zero-conf channel depth (0) >= minimum_depth (0), so lockin_complete() runs on channel_ready and the channel becomes CHANNELD_NORMAL while channel->scid stays NULL (lockin_complete 1159-1186 accepts aliases in lieu of scid).
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2024–2056](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2024-L2056)
   remove_htlc_in() is the only place our_msat and msat_to_us_max increase, and only when an incoming HTLC is fully removed with a preimage; a peer that never lets a fulfil complete keeps msat_to_us_max at zero.
7. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2137–2147](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2137-L2147)
   update_in_htlc() removes an incoming HTLC from ld->htlcs_in only on SENT_REMOVE_ACK_REVOCATION, which requires the peer's own revoke_and_ack; until then channel_has_htlc_in() finds it.
8. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:3080–3093](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L3080-L3093)
   htlcs_notify_new_block() ignores unfulfilled incoming HTLCs ('that's their problem'), so a withheld HTLC stays attached indefinitely.
9. [lightningd/plugin.c:706–736](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L706-L736)
   bcli's block reply is handled inside a DB transaction; fatal() aborts (log.c:1130-1144) before commit, so the block and the deletion roll back and the identical state is reloaded on restart, reproducing the fatal().
10. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:839–845](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L839-L845)
   The openchannel hook's documented mindepth field is written straight into uc->minimum_depth; mindepth 0 makes us a zero-conf fundee for that open.
11. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:662–721](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs#L662-L721)
   Shipped producer of mindepth 0: with experimental-lsps-client set, the openchannel hook returns mindepth 0 for the LSP the user approved via lsps-lsps2-invoice/approve (one-shot datastore record written at 266-298, invoked from lsps-lsps2-invoice at 492). The LSP is a remote peer that forwards HTLCs over the unconfirmed channel.
12. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2300–2309](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2300-L2309)
   The RPC cancel path refuses to forget a channel that has HTLCs attached ('not safe to cancel'), showing the invariant the block-driven forget violates.
13. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2254–2267](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2254-L2267)
   A new open_channel is accepted whenever no uncommitted channel is pending, with no cap on committed unfunded fundee channels; any peer can supply the 100 newer 'forgettable' channels that push the live zero-conf channel into the deleted set.

## Impact
lightningd fatal()s while processing a block; the transaction rolls back and the identical state is reloaded, so it fatal()s again at the same block on every restart (and would on every later block regardless). The whole node, all channels and all in-flight HTLCs are down until manual DB surgery or until the attacker lets the funding confirm. No confidentiality impact; integrity impact limited to the (rolled-back) deletion of an operational channel, or the silent deletion when no HTLC is attached.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote peer that opened a zero-conf channel to the victim: in the shipped tree, the LSP the victim approved a JIT channel from while running with experimental-lsps-client (or any peer an operator plugin grants mindepth 0 to via the documented openchannel hook). It never lets the funding confirm, adds one HTLC and withholds the final revoke_and_ack (or never acks our fail), and ensures the victim holds >= 101 fundee channels with unseen funding older than 2016 blocks, which free unfunded v1 opens from any node ids supply. No credentials or interaction on the victim are needed beyond the pre-existing JIT request; the conditions are the LSPS client being enabled for that LSP and a two-week wait, hence attack_requirements PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
1. is_fundee_should_forget() treats 'no scid after 2016 blocks' as 'never became operational', which is false for zero-conf channels that reached CHANNELD_NORMAL and may carry HTLCs. Fix criteria: A channel is only forgotten by the funding timeout if it is still in a pre-open state (CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN / DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN) with no HTLCs ever attached; zero-conf channels in CHANNELD_NORMAL are excluded (or handled by a fail/close path that resolves HTLCs first). Verify: a fundee zero-conf channel with an unconfirmed funding and a pending incoming HTLC survives 2016+ blocks with >100 forgettable channels present and lightningd keeps running.
2. delete_channel() can be reached for a channel with attached HTLCs, and destroy_channel() turns that into a process-wide fatal() inside a rolled-back transaction, producing a restart loop. Fix criteria: Deleting a channel that still has HTLCs must be refused (logged, channel skipped) rather than aborting the daemon, so that a single peer-controlled channel state cannot stop block processing; verify by forcing the forget path on a channel with an hin and observing the channel is skipped and the block is committed.

# Peer tx_abort frees channel while openchannel2_sign hook holds its pointer (UAF)

## Details
lightningd's handler for the first commitment_signed of a remotely-opened v2 channel (handle_commit_received, opener == REMOTE) puts a raw `struct channel *` into an openchannel2_sign hook payload and calls the plugin hook asynchronously (default: the `funder` plugin, which may call `signpsbt`). The payload is stolen onto the hook request (plugin_hook.c:388) so it outlives both dualopend and the channel; only `payload->dualopend` is NULLed by a destructor. When the hook returns, openchannel2_sign_hook_cb dereferences `payload->channel` unconditionally (log, inflight list, tal_free/tal_steal of inflight->funding_psbt, wallet_inflight_save, watch_opening_inflight, and channel_saved_err_broken_reconn when dualopend is gone).

A remote peer can free that channel inside the window:
1. Peer opens a v2 channel to us; we accept (funder default policy continues even with 0 contribution). After the interactive tx, lightningd runs wallet_commit_channel (channel saved, state DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY, inflight without last_tx); dualopend sends our commitment_signed and waits for theirs.
2. Peer disconnects without sending commitment_signed. destroy_subd -> dualopen_errmsg(peer_fd=NULL, disconnect=false) only channel_fail_transient()s: the channel survives.
3. Peer reconnects; peer_connected -> connect_activate_subd -> peer_restart_dualopend (reinit, has_commitments=false); do_reconnect_dance completes (peer may omit next_funding), state->reconnected = true.
4. Peer sends a valid commitment_signed immediately followed by tx_abort. dualopend handle_commit_signed (openingd/dualopend.c:1334-1362) writes COMMIT_RCVD and returns to the loop; it then handles tx_abort and writes STATUS_PEER_ERROR (disconnect=false, warning=false) and exits.
5. lightningd handle_commit_received: wallet_update_channel_commit moves the channel to DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED, sets inflight->last_tx, and (updated==true, opener REMOTE) calls plugin_hook_call_openchannel2_sign with payload->channel = channel.
6. lightningd reads the queued STATUS_PEER_ERROR: dualopen_errmsg -> `!warning && state == DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED && !channel_funding_sigs_sent` -> forget_channel_open -> delete_channel -> tal_free(channel) (inflights freed with it). Ordering is deterministic: both messages are already queued on the dualopend pipe, while the plugin reply needs a separate process round-trip.
7. The funder replies; openchannel2_sign_hook_cb runs on the freed channel: channel_current_inflight() walks a freed list head, inflight->funding is read, `tal_free(inflight->funding_psbt)` frees already-freed memory (tal header corruption / tal error -> abort) or, if the chunk was reused, corrupts live heap; wallet_inflight_save writes garbage to the DB; finally channel_saved_err_broken_reconn asserts on freed state.

Result: deterministic lightningd crash (all channels go offline; HTLCs/forwards stall; on-chain timeouts can follow) and heap corruption from attacker-timed input. Precondition: the node advertises dual-funding (`--experimental-dual-fund`, non-default). The same dangling-pointer defect is reachable by the operator's own openchannel_abort during the hook window.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1128–1198](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1128-L1198)
   openchannel2_sign_hook_cb dereferences payload->channel (channel->log, channel_current_inflight(channel), inflight->funding_psbt tal_free/tal_steal, wallet_inflight_save, watch_opening_inflight, channel_saved_err_broken_reconn) after the asynchronous hook returns. Only payload->dualopend is protected by a destructor; payload->channel is a raw pointer with no lifetime tie, and the callback is explicitly written to run even when dualopend is gone ('Peer's gone away, let's try reconnecting').
2. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3968–3991](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3968-L3991)
   handle_commit_received (opener == REMOTE, first commitment) stores the raw channel pointer in the hook payload and calls plugin_hook_call_openchannel2_sign; the channel is in DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED with i_sent_sigs == false while the plugin (funder, signpsbt) works.
3. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:4358–4398](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L4358-L4398)
   dualopen_errmsg for a peer tx_abort (peer_fd set, disconnect=false, warning=false) reaches the branch '!warning && state == DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED && !channel_funding_sigs_sent' and calls forget_channel_open, which delete_channel()s (tal_free) the channel the in-flight hook payload still points at.
4. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:4303–4310](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L4303-L4310)
   forget_channel_open deletes (frees) the channel unless we already sent tx_signatures; during the sign hook we have not.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:1334–1362](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1334-L1362)
   On a reconnected channel, handle_commit_signed verifies the peer's commitment_signed, writes WIRE_DUALOPEND_COMMIT_RCVD to lightningd and returns to the poll loop WITHOUT waiting for SEND_TX_SIGS (unlike accepter_commits at 2402-2406), so the very next peer message (tx_abort) is processed and forwarded immediately.
6. [openingd/dualopend.c:1586–1631](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1586-L1631)
   handle_tx_abort -> open_abort -> negotiation_aborted(aborted=true) -> peer_failed_received_errmsg(disconnect=false) sends STATUS_PEER_ERROR to lightningd on the same pipe right behind COMMIT_RCVD, so lightningd processes the delete before any plugin can answer the hook.
7. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:386–388](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L386-L388)
   The hook payload is tal_steal()ed onto the plugin_hook_request, so it survives the channel/dualopend being freed and the callback runs later with the stale channel pointer.

## Impact
Use-after-free with frees and writes through dangling pointers in lightningd: reliable crash of the main daemon (availability HIGH, with on-chain consequences for every channel) and possible heap corruption / DB rows written from freed memory (integrity LOW). No confidentiality impact identified.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any Lightning peer able to connect (no auth beyond BOLT8). They open a v2 channel, disconnect before commitment_signed, reconnect, then send commitment_signed+tx_abort back-to-back. lightningd processes the queued tx_abort status (deleting the channel) before the plugin can answer the openchannel2_sign hook, so no race needs to be won. Requires only that we run with dual-funding enabled (--experimental-dual-fund, non-default) and the default funder plugin.

## Recommended fix
openchannel2_psbt_payload holds a raw struct channel pointer across an asynchronous plugin hook, and the channel can be deleted (forget_channel_open on tx_abort / abort) while the hook is outstanding; the callback then uses the freed channel. Fix criteria: The hook callback must never dereference a channel that has been freed: either tie the payload's channel reference to the channel's lifetime (destructor clearing it, or look the channel up by id/dbid on return and bail if absent/closed), or refuse to delete a channel that has an outstanding openchannel2_sign request. Verify by running the reconnect + commitment_signed + tx_abort sequence against a node with the funder plugin: lightningd must log the abort and return cleanly from the hook without touching the deleted channel (no crash, valgrind/ASan clean).

# featurebits_unset clears whole byte so channel_type_accept admits unknown channel_type bits 40-55

## Details
BOLT 2 requires a node receiving open_channel/open_channel2 to fail the channel if `channel_type` is not one of the defined types (option_static_remotekey, or option_anchors+option_static_remotekey, each optionally with the option_scid_alias (46) and option_zeroconf (50) variants). Core Lightning enforces this in common/channel_type.c:channel_type_accept by blanking the two variant bits in a copy of the peer's proposal and comparing the result for exact equality with the two known base types.

The blanking helper is wrong. common/features.c:548 `featurebits_unset` computes `(*ptr)[len - 1 - bit / 8] &= (0 << (bit % 8))`; `0 << n` is 0, so the statement is `&= 0` and zeroes the entire byte containing the bit instead of the single bit. Clearing bit 46 erases bits 40-47 and clearing bit 50 erases bits 48-55 of the copy (bits are packed big-endian, byte index len-1-bit/8). Any channel_type the peer proposes that is a known base type plus any combination of bits 40-45, 47-49, 51-55 (e.g. {12,22,44}: bit 44 lives in the same byte as bit 46, is wiped by featurebits_unset(46), trim_features drops the now-zero byte, and channel_type_eq matches channel_type_anchors_zero_fee_htlc) passes the equality test. channel_type_accept then returns a channel_type built from the peer's ORIGINAL bytes `t` (line 163), so the undefined bits are adopted as the negotiated type, echoed back in accept_channel/accept_channel2, delivered to lightningd in openingd_got_offer (and from there into the `openchannel`/`openchannel2` hook payload every plugin sees, opening_control.c:708), handed to channeld, persisted in the channels table (wallet.c:2781) and reloaded on restart. The only other check, the feats[] loop at lines 134-148, inspects bits 12/22/46/50 only (via feature_offered, so it also cannot distinguish odd from even). Bits >= 56 and bits outside 40-55 still fail the equality test, so the reach is exactly bits 40-45, 47-49, 51-55.

Attacker: any remote peer that connects and sends open_channel/open_channel2 (inbound opens are accepted by default). The adopted type is persisted once funding_created/funding_signed are exchanged, which costs the attacker nothing on-chain because the funding transaction need never be broadcast; the fundee keeps the unconfirmed channel until it is forgotten.

Consequences in this release: (1) CLN violates the BOLT 2 MUST-fail requirement and records channel state containing peer-chosen undefined bits. (2) Those bits surface in RPC output: json_add_channel_type (common/json_channel_type.c:44) emits channel_type_name strings such as "channel_type/even", "payment_metadata/even", "keysend/even" or "unknown_40/even", which lie outside the enum the project documents for `channel_type.names` (doc/schemas/listpeerchannels.json:141-150). The generated Rust model (cln-rpc/src/primitives.rs:66 `ChannelTypeName`, a serde-derived closed enum with no fallback variant; used by cln-rpc model.rs:7929 ListpeerchannelsChannelsChannelType) cannot deserialize such a value, so under the assumption that serde 1.x rejects unknown unit variants, cln-grpc (enabled by default on 127.0.0.1:9736) fails every ListPeerChannels response, and ListClosedChannels once the channel closes, for as long as a channel with such a type exists in the database. (3) The commitment-transaction logic itself consults only bits 12/20/22/46/50 through channel_type_has, so no funds-affecting behaviour changes today; odd bits 47/51 are treated as their even counterparts, which is the same thing the peer could legitimately request with 46/50 and is gated identically (zeroconf still requires the plugin to return minimum_depth 0, openingd.c:1061). (4) Forward compatibility: if a future channel-type bit in 40-55 changes commitment semantics, this release would silently agree to it without implementing it.

featurebits_unset has exactly this one caller; common/test/run-channel_type.c never exercises channel_type_accept or featurebits_unset.

## Evidence
1. [common/features.c:548](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/features.c#L548)
   featurebits_unset is meant to clear one bit but executes `(*ptr)[len - 1 - bit / 8] &= (0 << (bit % 8))`; `0 << n` is 0, so the whole byte holding `bit` is zeroed. For bit 46 this wipes bits 40-47, for bit 50 bits 48-55.
2. [common/channel\_type.c:150–164](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/channel_type.c#L150-L164)
   channel_type_accept copies the peer's proposed channel_type, calls featurebits_unset for the variants OPT_SCID_ALIAS (46) and OPT_ZEROCONF (50) (line 152), then tests the blanked copy for equality with the two known base types (155-158). Because whole bytes were zeroed, any proposal whose extra bits lie in 40-55 compares equal. On success it returns the peer's ORIGINAL bytes `t` (line 163), so the unknown bits survive into the negotiated channel_type.
3. [common/channel\_type.c:134–147](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/channel_type.c#L134-L147)
   The preceding feats[] loop only vets bits 22, 12, 46 and 50 (via feature_offered, which also accepts the odd bit). No other bit is examined, so the equality test is the only guard against unknown bits, and it is the one defeated by the byte-wide clear.
4. [openingd/openingd.c:900–901](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L900-L901)
   The fundee path feeds the peer's open_channel channel_type TLV (open_tlvs->channel_type, raw bytes authored by the remote peer) straight into channel_type_accept and adopts the returned type as state->channel_type for the channel.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:2554–2555](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2554-L2555)
   Same acceptance of the peer's open_channel2 channel_type in the dual-funding accepter path.

## Impact
Integrity LOW: the node accepts, echoes, persists and reports a channel_type the specification requires it to reject, with peer-chosen undefined bits in persisted channel state and in the openchannel hook payload shown to plugins; commitment construction is unaffected because only bits 12/20/22/46/50 are consulted, so there is no control over funds. Availability LOW: the out-of-schema `channel_type.names` strings break strict consumers of the documented schema; the default-on cln-grpc plugin's ListPeerChannels (and ListClosedChannels) fails to deserialize while such a channel exists (assumption: serde 1.x derive on the closed enum cln-rpc/src/primitives.rs:66 rejects unknown variants). lightningd itself does not crash (feature_name handles unknown bits). Confidentiality none.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote peer connects (or we connect to it), completes the Noise handshake and sends open_channel/open_channel2 whose channel_type TLV is a known base type plus any bit in 40-45, 47-49, 51-55. openingd.c:900 / dualopend.c:2554 pass the raw bytes to channel_type_accept, which returns them as accepted; to persist the type the peer completes funding_created/funding_signed without ever broadcasting the funding transaction. No credentials, no user action, no non-default configuration: inbound channel opens are enabled by default and the type is adopted before any funding is committed. Deterministic.

## Recommended fix
1. featurebits_unset uses `&= (0 << (bit % 8))`, which clears the whole byte rather than the single feature bit, so the blanking step in channel_type_accept destroys information about neighbouring bits 40-55. Fix criteria: featurebits_unset must clear exactly the requested bit and leave all other bits unchanged (unit test: set bits 40..55, unset 46 and 50, verify only those two are cleared). channel_type_accept must then reject proposals such as {12,22,44} or {12,47} and accept only the defined types with even variant bits 46/50; a peer sending open_channel/open_channel2 with such a type must receive a negotiation failure instead of an accept_channel echoing it.
2. channel_type_accept relies solely on an equality test after blanking and has no explicit allow-list check that every set bit in the proposal is one of the defined even channel-type bits (12, 22, 46, 50). Fix criteria: Independently of the operator fix, validate that every set bit of the proposed channel_type is one of the defined even channel-type bits and that no odd bit is set; any other bit must cause rejection. Add a regression test in common/test/run-channel_type.c covering channel_type_accept with unknown and odd bits, so that persisted channel_type.names always stay within the enum documented in doc/schemas/listpeerchannels.json.

# createinvoice/signinvoice crash lightningd on oversized bolt11 whose re-encoding exceeds 65535 u5

## Details
`signinvoice` and `createinvoice` accept an arbitrary bolt11 string from the RPC caller, decode it with `bolt11_decode_nosig()` and re-encode it with `bolt11_encode()` to attach our node's signature. `bolt11_encode_()` returns NULL when the data part exceeds 65535 five-bit groups (common/bolt11.c:1398), and neither caller checks for that:

- `json_signinvoice` (lightningd/invoice.c:1997-2013) passes `b11enc` to `json_add_invstring()`, which does `strstarts(NULL, "lni")` (common/json_stream.c:414) → SIGSEGV of lightningd.
- `json_createinvoice` (invoice.c:1710-1739) passes `b11enc` to `invoices_create()` → `invoice_index_created()` → `assert(invstring)` (wallet/invoices.c:803) → abort; without the assert `db_bind_text(NULL)` would `strlen(NULL)`.

The decoder places no upper bound on the input: `bech32_decode_alloc()` decodes with `max_input_len = (size_t)-1` (bolt11.c:716), the tagged-field loop (bolt11.c:887-936) accepts any number of fields, and unknown tags or repeated non-repeatable tags are retained in `extra_fields` (up to 1023 u5 each) and re-emitted verbatim by `encode_extra()`. A string with valid `p`, `s`, `d` fields plus ~64 unknown-tag fields of 1023 u5 (about 66 KB, with a valid bech32 checksum and any 65 filler bytes as the 'signature', since nosig decode ignores it) decodes successfully and re-encodes to more than 65535 u5.

The maintainers already recognised that createinvoice must bound crafted-bolt11 input (the `expiry >= 2^32` gate at invoice.c:1704, tested in tests/test_invoices.py::test_createinvoice_expiry_too_large), but the size dimension is unguarded.

Attacker: a rune bearer whose rune permits `signinvoice` or `createinvoice`, over commando (requests up to 1 MB, plugins/commando.c:459) or clnrest. Those methods are documented as 'minimal sanity checks are done' and intended for delegating invoice minting (e.g. to an LSP/front-end); crashing the whole node is beyond what such a rune grants. Local socket users are trusted and out of scope.

This is the same root cause as the separately recorded `invoice`-RPC finding (invoice-rpc-oversized-fallbacks-null-bolt11enc-assert) but with a different entry point and input (the full bolt11 string rather than the fallbacks array) and an additional sink (json_add_invstring NULL deref).

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/invoice.c:1997–2013](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L1997-L2013)
   json_signinvoice re-encodes the caller's decoded bolt11 and passes b11enc straight to json_add_invstring() with no NULL check.
2. [common/json\_stream.c:412–417](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_stream.c#L412-L417)
   json_add_invstring() calls strstarts(invstring, "lni") on the NULL pointer: SIGSEGV.
3. [lightningd/invoice.c:1709–1738](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L1709-L1738)
   json_createinvoice's bolt11 branch likewise ignores a NULL b11enc and passes it to invoices_create(), which asserts (wallet/invoices.c:803) and then would strlen(NULL) in db_bind_text().
4. [common/bolt11.c:1393–1399](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L1393-L1399)
   bolt11_encode_() re-emits every retained unknown field verbatim and returns NULL once the data exceeds 65535 u5; the function's NULL return is never handled by lightningd callers.
5. [common/bolt11.c:707–726](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L707-L726)
   bech32_decode_alloc() decodes with max_input_len = (size_t)-1, so there is no length bound on the input string; the hoisted 90-char checks in the vendored bech32.c do not apply.
6. [common/bolt11.c:887–935](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L887-L935)
   The tagged-field loop accepts any number of fields; unknown tags (or duplicates of non-repeatable tags) are stored in extra_fields via unknown_field() up to 1023 u5 each, with no cap on the total, so a string with ~64 such fields decodes fine and re-encodes to >65535 u5.
7. [wallet/invoices.c:797–806](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/invoices.c#L797-L806)
   invoice_index_created asserts invstring non-NULL (release builds keep asserts), so createinvoice aborts lightningd.

## Impact
Deterministic crash/abort of lightningd: channels offline, HTLC timeouts possible, repeatable on every restart while the rune is valid. No disclosure or data modification.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a rune permitting signinvoice (or createinvoice). They construct a bech32 'lnbc...' string: 35-bit timestamp, valid p (52 u5), s (52 u5), d fields, then ~64 unknown-tag fields each with data_length 1023, 65 arbitrary trailing bytes, valid bech32 checksum. Send `signinvoice invstring=<that>`; decode succeeds, bolt11_encode returns NULL, json_add_invstring segfaults lightningd. For createinvoice, add a preimage whose SHA256 equals the p field; the assert in invoice_index_created aborts. Single request, deterministic.

## Recommended fix
json_signinvoice and json_createinvoice treat bolt11_encode()'s NULL return as a valid string; the decoder accepts unbounded input length and unbounded retained unknown fields. Fix criteria: A NULL from bolt11_encode() must yield a JSON-RPC error in both handlers before json_add_invstring()/invoices_create() are reached; and/or bolt11_decode_nosig() must reject invoices whose total data part exceeds what can be re-encoded (65535 u5). Verified by submitting an oversized bolt11 to signinvoice and createinvoice and observing an error with lightningd still running.

**Severity:** HIGH

# invoice RPC with many fallbacks makes bolt11_encode return NULL, aborting lightningd on assert

## Details
`bolt11_encode_()` (common/bolt11.c:1398) returns NULL when the invoice's data part exceeds 65535 five-bit groups. The `invoice` RPC never checks this return value: `invoice_complete()` (lightningd/invoice.c:853-878) hands `b11enc` to `invoices_create()`, which calls `invoice_index_created(ld, UNPAID, label, b11enc)` (wallet/invoices.c:289), which `assert(invstring)`s (wallet/invoices.c:803). Asserts are compiled into release binaries, so lightningd aborts. Were the assert absent, `db_bind_text(stmt, NULL)` at line 314 would call `strlen(NULL)` and crash anyway.

The only unbounded input to the encoder on the `invoice` path is the optional `fallbacks` array (invoice.c:1185-1202): the label is capped at 128 bytes and the description at BOLT11_FIELD_BYTE_LIMIT, but any number of valid on-chain addresses (duplicates allowed) are accepted and each becomes an `f` tagged field of 36 (P2PKH) to 56 (P2TR/P2WSH) u5. Roughly 1,200-1,800 fallbacks (a 50-75 KB JSON request) are enough; lightningd's JSON-RPC reader has no request-size cap (common/jsonrpc_io.c grows a membuf), commando accepts requests up to 1 MB (plugins/commando.c:459), and clnrest forwards bodies unchanged.

Attacker: a rune bearer whose rune permits the `invoice` method — the most commonly delegated method (web shops, point-of-sale, LNURL servers) — over commando or clnrest. The rune grants 'create invoices'; it does not grant 'crash the node', so this is privilege escalation from a partially trusted caller to full denial of service of lightningd (channels offline, HTLC timeouts, repeatable after each restart). A local socket user is trusted and out of scope.

Sibling of the same root cause on `createinvoice`/`signinvoice` is recorded separately (createinvoice-signinvoice-oversized-bolt11-null-encode-crash), where the caller controls the whole bolt11 string.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/invoice.c:853–877](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L853-L877)
   invoice_complete() calls bolt11_encode() and passes the result b11enc to invoices_create() without checking for NULL.
2. [common/bolt11.c:1397–1399](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L1397-L1399)
   bolt11_encode_() returns NULL when the encoded data part exceeds 65535 5-bit groups; this happens before hsm signing, and every caller in lightningd ignores the NULL return.
3. [wallet/invoices.c:286–289](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/invoices.c#L286-L289)
   invoices_create() passes b11enc to invoice_index_created() before any DB write.
4. [wallet/invoices.c:797–806](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/invoices.c#L797-L806)
   invoice_index_created() asserts invstring != NULL; asserts are compiled into release builds (no NDEBUG), so lightningd aborts. Even without the assert, db_bind_text(stmt, NULL) at line 314 does strlen(NULL).
5. [lightningd/invoice.c:1185–1201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L1185-L1201)
   The `fallbacks` array parameter is unbounded: every element is parsed into a scriptpubkey and appended to b11->fallbacks; only the label (128 bytes) and description (639 bytes) have size limits.
6. [common/bolt11.c:1182–1213](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L1182-L1213)
   Each fallback is encoded as an `f` field of 36-56 u5 (P2PKH 36, P2TR/P2WSH 56), so ~1200-1800 entries push the data part past 65535 u5.

## Impact
lightningd aborts: all channels and subdaemons go down until the operator restarts; in-flight HTLCs can time out on-chain. No data disclosure or modification.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a rune permitting `invoice`. They send one `invoice` request with amount_msat, label, description and a `fallbacks` array of ~1,800 valid P2PKH addresses for the node's network (the same address repeated works). Every address parses, bolt11_encode returns NULL because the data part exceeds 65535 u5, invoices_create asserts and lightningd aborts. Deterministic, single request, no race; commando always on, so the only requirement is the rune the attacker already has.

## Recommended fix
invoice_complete() (and the other bolt11_encode callers) treat bolt11_encode()'s NULL return as a valid string, and nothing bounds the number/size of fallbacks accepted by the invoice RPC. Fix criteria: A NULL from bolt11_encode() must produce a JSON-RPC error rather than reaching invoices_create()/db_bind_text(); and/or the invoice RPC must reject fallback arrays whose encoded size cannot fit a BOLT11 invoice before encoding. Verified by issuing `invoice` with ~2000 fallback addresses and observing an error with lightningd still running.

# createinvoice dereferences NULL invoice_payment_hash when adding stub blinded path to bolt12 invoice

## Details
The `createinvoice` RPC accepts a caller-supplied BOLT12 invoice string (documented as 'minimal sanity checks are done') and, for invoices that carry no `invoice_paths`, synthesises a one-hop stub blinded path so that payments can later be recognised (lightningd/invoice.c:1768-1769). `add_stub_blindedpath()` derives the path_id from `inv->invoice_payment_hash` via `bolt12_path_id()` (invoice.c:1638-1640), which hashes `sizeof(struct sha256)` bytes at that pointer (common/bolt12_id.c:25). 

The decoder used on this path is `invoice_decode_minimal()` (common/bolt12.c:396), which only runs `fromwire_tlv_invoice` plus the feature/chain check; every TLV field is optional, so an invoice without `invoice_payment_hash` (for example the bech32 encoding of an empty TLV stream under the `lni` HRP) decodes successfully. The sanity check `if (!inv->invoice_payment_hash) return command_fail(...)` exists, but at line 1808 — after the stub path has been built. The result is a NULL-pointer read inside `sha256_update()` and a SIGSEGV of the lightningd main process.

Who can trigger it: anyone able to issue `createinvoice` — a local RPC user (trusted) but also any rune bearer whose rune permits the `createinvoice` method, reachable over commando (peer custom messages) or clnrest HTTP. A rune that permits `createinvoice` grants the ability to mint invoices, not to kill the node; killing lightningd takes every channel offline (HTLC timeouts, forwarding, on-chain monitoring) until the operator restarts it, and a bearer can repeat it on every restart. The in-tree caller (plugins/offers_invreq_hook.c:1166) always sets the payment hash, so the plugin path is not affected; only direct RPC callers are.

A secondary consequence of the same ordering: `hsm_sign_b12_invoice()` (line 1774) signs the caller's invoice with the node key before any of the content checks and even in `check`-only mode, so an invoice that is later rejected has already received a valid node signature in memory (not returned to the caller on failure, so impact is limited to the crash above).

There are no records in the findings store at this location.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/invoice.c:1751–1769](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L1751-L1769)
   json_createinvoice decodes the caller-supplied bolt12 string with invoice_decode_minimal() (line 1751) and, when inv->invoice_paths is NULL, calls add_stub_blindedpath() at lines 1768-1769 — before the invoice_payment_hash NULL check at line 1808. This ordering is the root cause; the fix must validate mandatory fields before building the stub path.
2. [lightningd/invoice.c:1637–1640](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L1637-L1640)
   add_stub_blindedpath() passes inv->invoice_payment_hash (possibly NULL) straight into bolt12_path_id() with no check.
3. [common/bolt12\_id.c:20–37](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12_id.c#L20-L37)
   bolt12_path_id() -> bolt12_path_secret() -> hash_from_base() calls sha256_update(&ctx, payment_hash, sizeof(*payment_hash)) i.e. reads 32 bytes from the NULL pointer: SIGSEGV in lightningd.
4. [common/bolt12.c:396–436](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L396-L436)
   invoice_decode_minimal() only parses the TLV and checks features/chain; unlike invoice_decode() (lines 572-587) it does not require invoice_payment_hash, invoice_amount, invoice_paths or any other field, so an 'lni1...' string with an empty or minimal TLV stream is accepted.
5. [lightningd/invoice.c:1808–1813](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L1808-L1813)
   The intended guard ('Missing payment_hash in invoice') is placed after add_stub_blindedpath() and hsm_sign_b12_invoice(), so it can never protect the stub-path code.

## Impact
Deterministic crash of the lightningd main daemon: all channels go offline, pending HTLCs may time out on-chain, subdaemons are killed. No confidentiality or integrity effect on its own.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a rune permitting `createinvoice` (commando is always on; clnrest if enabled) or is any lesser RPC caller bounded by a rune. They send `createinvoice invstring=lni1 label=x preimage=<any 32 bytes>`: bolt12 bech32 carries no checksum (common/bech32_util.c from_bech32_charset), so `lni1` with no data yields an empty TLV stream; fromwire_tlv_invoice returns a talz'd struct with every field NULL (tools/gen/impl_template:211); check_features_and_chain passes on mainnet with no invreq_chain (or the attacker adds the chain TLV). invoice_paths is NULL so add_stub_blindedpath runs, bolt12_path_id hashes 32 bytes at NULL via ccan sha256_update/add() memcpy (ccan/ccan/crypto/sha256/sha256.c:179-186; the OpenSSL backend reads the same pointer), and lightningd segfaults. Deterministic, no race, no non-default configuration beyond the rune; also reachable through the `check` command since command_check_only() is evaluated after the crash point. In-tree callers (plugins/offers_invreq_hook.c:1166, plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1559) always set invoice_payment_hash, so only direct RPC callers trigger it.

## Recommended fix
json_createinvoice uses inv->invoice_payment_hash (and signs the invoice) before validating that the mandatory fields are present; invoice_decode_minimal does not enforce them. Fix criteria: A bolt12 invoice supplied to createinvoice that lacks invoice_payment_hash (or invoice_amount) must be rejected with a JSON-RPC error before add_stub_blindedpath() or hsm_sign_b12_invoice() run, and before command_check_only() returns. Verified by submitting an 'lni' string encoding an empty TLV stream and observing an error response with lightningd still running.

# Payee-supplied oversized BOLT12 blinded-path encrypted_recipient_data aborts xpay via make_tlv_hop, shutting down lightningd

## Details
common/onion_encode.c:make_tlv_hop() builds a hop payload by serialising a tlv_payload and prefixing its length with bigsize_put(). It handles only the 1-byte and 3-byte bigsize cases; if the TLV stream is 65536 bytes or more, bigsize_put() returns 5 and the function calls abort(). Nothing upstream bounds the one attacker-authored field that can push the stream past that size.

BOLT12 blinded paths: blinded_path_hop.enclen is a u16 (wire/onion_wire.csv:25-26), so each recipient-authored encrypted_recipient_data may be up to 65535 bytes. common/bolt12.c invoice_decode() (595-606) checks only the signature, required fields and num_hops != 0. plugins/xpay/xpay.c decodes the RPC-supplied invoice string (2706-2713; from_bech32_charset has no length cap), steals invoice_paths into payment->paths (2770), builds a fake channel from the payee-chosen first_node_id to xpay->fakenode (2115-2141) and routes to it (1881-1883). Once askrene returns a route and the reservation succeeds (reserve_done -> do_inject -> create_onion, 1546-1555), create_onion() (1454-1458) calls append_blinded_payloads() (1397-1402), which passes encrypted_recipient_data to onion_blinded_hop() (onion_encode.c:101-122) -> make_tlv_hop(). With ~65532+ bytes in the hop, the TLV stream (type 10 + 3-byte bigsize length + data, plus current_path_key) exceeds 65535 bytes and the plugin aborts before anything is sent to the network.

xpay is a builtin `important` plugin (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2585), and since take_over_pay defaults to true (xpay.c:3570) the ordinary `pay` command is also routed through xpay. When the plugin aborts, lightningd/plugin.c:297-302 shuts lightningd down (lightningd_exit).

Attack: the payee (or anyone who can get the victim operator to pay an invoice, e.g. a merchant/LNURL flow) crafts a BOLT12 invoice signed with their own key whose single blinded path has one hop carrying 65535 bytes of encrypted_recipient_data and a first_node_id the victim can route to (a direct peer, a well-connected public node). The invoice is ~105k bech32 characters, within a single lightning-cli argument (< 128 KiB); the JSON-RPC reader (common/jsonrpc_io.c, 1 MiB chunks, unbounded membuf) accepts it. The victim runs `pay`/`xpay` on it and the node process exits.

The BOLT11 `payment_metadata` route is NOT exploitable: BOLT11 tagged fields have a 10-bit data_length (common/bolt11.c:905), capping `m` at 1023 u5 = 639 bytes. The same sink is reachable in lightningd itself through sendpay's RPC-supplied payment_metadata (lightningd/pay.c:1247), but that caller is trusted RPC. The root cause is that make_tlv_hop() aborts on an input-size condition instead of failing, and that neither bolt12 decoding nor xpay bounds the per-hop payload (which can never legitimately exceed the 1300-byte onion anyway).

## Evidence
1. [common/onion\_encode.c:15–33](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/onion_encode.c#L15-L33)
   make_tlv_hop() serialises the hop TLV stream and calls bigsize_put() on its length, handling only the 1- and 3-byte encodings. When the TLV stream is >= 65536 bytes bigsize_put() returns 5 and the function falls through to abort(). The comment 'We can't have over 64k anyway' is the only guard; the function cannot report failure.
2. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1397–1405](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L1397-L1405)
   append_blinded_payloads() passes each blinded hop's recipient-authored path->path[i]->encrypted_recipient_data straight to onion_blinded_hop() with no length check; a hop with ~65532+ bytes makes the TLV stream exceed 65535 bytes and make_tlv_hop() aborts the plugin.
3. [common/onion\_encode.c:101–122](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/onion_encode.c#L101-L122)
   onion_blinded_hop() copies the caller-supplied enctlv into tlv->encrypted_recipient_data (TLV type 10, 'byte,...' in onion_wire.csv:11-12, length written as a bigsize) and returns make_tlv_hop(); it neither validates the size nor can return failure.
4. [wire/onion\_wire.csv:24–27](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/onion_wire.csv#L24-L27)
   blinded_path_hop.enclen is a u16, so the generated fromwire accepts up to 65535 bytes of encrypted_recipient_data per hop in any blinded_path, including invoice.invoice_paths (bolt12_wire.csv:158-159).
5. [common/bolt12.c:595–606](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L595-L606)
   invoice_decode() validates the payee's signature and required fields and rejects only paths with num_hops == 0; it imposes no bound on any hop's encrypted_recipient_data size. The attacker is the payee and signs the invoice with their own key.
6. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:2706–2770](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L2706-L2770)
   xpay (and `pay`, redirected to xpay by default) decodes the RPC-supplied invstring with invoice_decode() and steals b12inv->invoice_paths into payment->paths unchecked; from_bech32_charset() (common/bech32_util.c:74) places no limit on the invoice string length, so a ~105k-character invoice carrying a 64 KiB hop decodes.
7. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:2115–2141](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L2115-L2141)
   For each blinded path xpay adds a fake channel from the payee-chosen first_node_id to xpay->fakenode in its private askrene layer; getroutes_for() (1881-1883) then routes to fakenode, so the payee controls the introduction node and can pick one the victim can trivially reach (a direct peer or a well-connected public node).
8. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1454–1458](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L1454-L1458)
   create_onion() calls append_blinded_payloads() as soon as a route hop reaches fakenode. It is reached from getroutes_done() -> askrene-reserve -> reserve_done() -> do_inject() (1546-1555, 1497-1500) before anything is sent to the network, so the abort needs no cooperation from any peer.
9. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L302)
   cln-xpay is registered as an important builtin plugin (plugin.c:2576-2585, only cln-renepay is excluded); when it dies lightningd logs 'Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(), so the abort() takes the whole node down.
10. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3570](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L3570)
   take_over_pay defaults to true (xpay-handle-pay, doc/lightningd-config.5.md:561), so the ordinary `pay` command is redirected to xpay via the rpc_command hook; the default configuration is the vulnerable one.

## Impact
cln-xpay is an important plugin; its abort makes lightningd call lightningd_exit(), taking the whole node offline until the operator restarts it (in-flight HTLCs cannot be resolved while down, with potential on-chain consequences). No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a payment counterparty: they hand the victim a validly signed BOLT12 invoice whose blinded path has a hop with 65535 bytes of encrypted_recipient_data (enclen is u16, invoice_decode never bounds it). The victim operator (or an automated paying plugin) runs `pay`/`xpay` on it. Decoding succeeds, routing to the attacker-chosen introduction node proceeds via xpay's fake-channel layer, and the first create_onion() call hits make_tlv_hop()'s abort() before any network traffic. No special configuration is needed (xpay-handle-pay defaults on); the only requirement is that the victim chooses to pay the invoice, which is a deliberate user action.

## Recommended fix
1. make_tlv_hop() in common/onion_encode.c treats an oversized TLV stream (bigsize_put returning 5) as impossible and calls abort(), so the payload-size invariant is enforced by crashing rather than by returning an error. Fix criteria: A hop payload whose TLV stream does not fit the supported length encoding (or exceeds ROUTING_INFO_SIZE) must cause onion_blinded_hop()/onion_final_hop()/onion_nonfinal_hop() to return NULL (or otherwise report failure) and every caller (xpay create_onion/append_blinded_payloads, lightningd sendpay, renepay) must handle that by failing the payment attempt; feeding a 64 KiB encrypted_recipient_data or payment_metadata through these functions must not terminate the process.
2. xpay accepts recipient-authored BOLT12 blinded paths whose per-hop encrypted_recipient_data (u16 enclen, up to 65535 bytes) is never bounded before building the onion, although no legitimate hop payload can exceed the 1300-byte onion. Fix criteria: Before attempting to build an onion, xpay (or bolt12 invoice_decode / new_payment) must reject invoices in which any blinded hop's encrypted_recipient_data cannot fit within a single onion hop payload, returning a JSON-RPC error; `pay`/`xpay` on such an invoice must fail cleanly with lightningd still running.

# payersign/createinvoicerequest empty or invalid tweak makes hsmd and lightningd disagree, lightningd fatal()s

## Details
lightningd/offer.c signs BOLT12 payer material through hsmd with an optional alias tweak, and the two sides disagree on what an empty tweak means. lightningd's payer_key() (offer.c:341-355) ALWAYS adds SHA256(nodealias_base || tweak) to our node pubkey, for any tweak length including 0 or NULL. hsmd's handle_sign_bolt12_2 (hsmd/libhsmd.c:893-935) tweaks only when the decoded `tweakmessage` is non-NULL, and the generated decoder (tools/gen/impl_template:368, `*field = len ? tal_arr(...) : NULL`) turns publictweaklen == 0 into NULL. So whenever lightningd sends a zero-length publictweak, hsmd signs with the raw node key while lightningd expects the tweaked key; hsm_sign_b12's sanity check (offer.c:88-92) fails and calls fatal("HSM gave bad signature ..."), which logs a crashlog and abort()s lightningd (lightningd/log.c:1138-1149).

Reachable triggers:
1. `payersign` with `tweak: ""` (valid empty hex): json_tok_bin_from_hex (common/json_parse.c:139-151) returns a non-NULL zero-length tal_arr; payer_key tweaks; towire emits publictweaklen 0; hsmd decodes NULL and signs untweaked -> fatal.
2. `payersign` with any non-hex `tweak` (e.g. "zz"): param_bin_from_hex (common/json_param.c:701-711) tests the out-pointer `bin` instead of `*bin`, so it returns success with *bin == NULL; payer_key(NULL, 0) still tweaks; tal_count(NULL) == 0 so hsmd again gets no tweak -> fatal.
3. `createinvoicerequest` with an lnr1 whose invreq_metadata TLV (type 0) is present with length 0. TLV blobs decode to a non-NULL empty array (tools/gen/impl_template:89), so param_b12_invreq's `must have invreq_metadata` passes. The payer_id check at offer.c:402-415 requires invreq_payer_id == payer_key(""), and its error text prints that expected pubkey, so one failing call reveals it and a second call with that payer_id reaches hsm_sign_b12 with the empty tweak -> fatal.
4. `createproof` (plugins/offers_proof.c:338-348) forwards the paid invoice's invreq_metadata as the payersign tweak; invoice_decode (common/bolt12.c:545-620) does not require invreq_metadata, and json_add_hex(NULL, 0) yields "". Invoices obtained via fetchinvoice always carry invreq_metadata (invoice_matches_request, plugins/fetchinvoice.c:138-158, compares TLV range 0-159 with our invreq), so this needs an out-of-band bolt12 invoice lacking the field that the operator paid with pay/xpay and then ran createproof on: payee-authored input with operator interaction.

Attacker position: a commando (plugins/commando.c:420-425 forwards any method after checkrune) or clnrest rune bearer whose rune permits `payersign` or `createinvoicerequest`. A rune with no method restriction already permits `stop`, but method-restricted runes that still match these methods are realistic: `method^pay` (a natural restriction for a payment app) prefix-matches `payersign`, and a BOLT12 wallet rune may allow `createinvoicerequest`; neither concedes shutting the node down. One request aborts lightningd (all channel monitoring, HTLC handling and subdaemons stop until restart) and can be repeated on every restart. No confidentiality or integrity impact: the untweaked signature is never returned because the process aborts first.

Fix: make lightningd and hsmd agree on empty-tweak semantics (treat empty as 'no tweak' on both sides, or reject empty/NULL tweaks at the RPC boundary before calling hsmd) and make param_bin_from_hex actually fail on invalid hex.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/offer.c:459–485](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L459-L485)
   json_payersign takes `tweak` via param_bin_from_hex, unconditionally derives a tweaked key with payer_key() (even for NULL / zero-length tweak) and then calls hsm_sign_b12 with that tweak and key. No check that the tweak is non-empty.
2. [lightningd/offer.c:65–92](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L65-L92)
   hsm_sign_b12 sends towire_hsmd_sign_bolt12_2(..., publictweak) and then sanity-checks the returned signature against `key`; on mismatch it calls fatal(), which aborts lightningd (lightningd/log.c:1130-1155).
3. [lightningd/offer.c:341–354](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L341-L354)
   payer_key always adds SHA256(nodealias_base || tweak) to our node pubkey, including when public_tweak_len == 0 (or public_tweak is NULL). The expected key is therefore always a tweaked key.
4. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:893–934](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L893-L934)
   hsmd only tweaks when `tweakmessage` is non-NULL; otherwise it signs with the untweaked node key. The generated fromwire (tools/gen/impl_template:368, `*field = len ? tal_arr(...) : NULL`) yields NULL for a zero-length publictweak, so a zero-length tweak sent by lightningd is signed with the raw node key, contradicting lightningd's payer_key().
5. [common/json\_param.c:701–710](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_param.c#L701-L710)
   param_bin_from_hex tests `bin != NULL` (the out-pointer) instead of `*bin`, so a non-hex `tweak` string is accepted and the caller receives *bin == NULL. In payersign this becomes publictweak == NULL -> hsmd signs untweaked, while payer_key(NULL,0) returns a tweaked key.
6. [lightningd/offer.c:400–433](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L400-L433)
   Second trigger: createinvoicerequest with an lnr1 whose invreq_metadata TLV has length 0 (TLV byte arrays decode to a non-NULL empty tal_arr, so the `must have invreq_metadata` check passes). If invreq_payer_id equals payer_key("") (which the error message at 411-415 discloses), tweak is the empty array and hsm_sign_b12 hits the same mismatch -> fatal.
7. [plugins/offers\_proof.c:338–347](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_proof.c#L338-L347)
   Third trigger: createproof passes the paid invoice's invreq_metadata as the payersign tweak; invoice_decode (common/bolt12.c:545-620) does not require invreq_metadata, so a paid bolt12 invoice lacking it yields tweak "" and the same fatal().

## Impact
fatal() in hsm_sign_b12 writes a crashlog and abort()s lightningd itself (lightningd/log.c:1138-1149), not a plugin, stopping HTLC handling, on-chain monitoring and every subdaemon until an operator restarts; the request can be repeated after each restart. No confidentiality or integrity impact: the mismatched (untweaked) signature is never returned because the process aborts first.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker holds a rune usable over commando (any connected peer, rune-authenticated) or clnrest that permits `payersign` or `createinvoicerequest` — e.g. a method-restricted rune such as `method^pay`, which prefix-matches `payersign`. One request `payersign messagename=x fieldname=y merkle=<32B hex> tweak=""` (or tweak="zz") makes lightningd fatal() deterministically. For createinvoicerequest two requests suffice: the first error discloses payer_key(""), the second with that payer_id and a zero-length invreq_metadata reaches the same fatal. No race and no non-default configuration; the rune is the privilege, so PR:L. The createproof trigger is a secondary, operator-interaction path and does not set the metrics.

## Recommended fix
1. lightningd's payer_key() tweaks for any tweak length, while hsmd's handle_sign_bolt12_2 treats a zero-length (NULL after decode) publictweak as 'no tweak'; the mismatch is turned into fatal() by hsm_sign_b12's sanity check. Fix criteria: lightningd and hsmd must apply identical tweak semantics: either both treat an empty tweak as 'sign with node key' or lightningd rejects empty/NULL tweaks in payersign and createinvoicerequest with a JSON-RPC error. After the fix, `payersign ... tweak=""` and `tweak="zz"` return an RPC error (or a signature that verifies), and lightningd never reaches fatal() from RPC-controlled tweak input.
2. param_bin_from_hex tests the out-pointer rather than the decoded result, so invalid hex is accepted and callers receive NULL. Fix criteria: param_bin_from_hex must fail with 'should be a hex value' whenever json_tok_bin_from_hex returns NULL; all callers (payersign included) then never see a NULL binary parameter.
3. createinvoicerequest accepts a zero-length invreq_metadata and createproof forwards a missing invreq_metadata as an empty tweak. Fix criteria: Reject invreqs whose invreq_metadata is empty in createinvoicerequest, and have createproof skip or error on invoices without invreq_metadata, so no path produces an empty tweak for hsm_sign_b12.
