# Peer-chosen channel_announcement for a pre-history block makes lightningd fetch the whole block and gettxout every P2WSH output (pruned backend: 60 s bcli stall or fatal)

## Details
gossipd verifies each incoming channel_announcement's funding output by asking lightningd (gossipd_get_txout). lightningd's get_txout (gossip_control.c:78-115) tries the wallet's utxoset and blocks table; for any block older than the node's own chain history (everything before its first blockscan_start, tip-15 on first run) it calls bitcoind_getfilteredblock() for the whole block. bitcoind.c then (1) has bcli download the full raw block and (2) walks every P2WSH output in that block, issuing one bcli `getutxout` (one synchronous bitcoin-cli gettxout subprocess) per output, sequentially, before answering. Blocks are processed one at a time; process_getfiltered_block_final coalesces only identical heights and then picks the pending request with the highest height.

An unauthenticated remote peer controls the trigger: a channel_announcement needs only four signatures made with the attacker's own node/bitcoin keys and an scid naming any block in [504500, blockheight-6]. gossipd checks the signatures and, if the scid is not already known or pending, forwards a get_txout immediately (gossmap_manage.c:743-756); up to PENDING_LIMIT (10000) can be outstanding, and connectd applies no per-peer gossip limit. By choosing a distinct never-fetched old block per announcement the attacker converts ~430 bytes of gossip into a multi-MB block transfer plus O(P2WSH outputs in that block) subprocess spawns, repeatable over the hundreds of thousands of pre-history blocks the node has never cached. Because the scheduler serves the highest pending height first, choosing heights just below the node's root preempts every legitimate historical lookup (notably a node's initial gossip sync, where essentially all channels are in pre-history blocks) for as long as the queue is kept non-empty; while 10000 attacker scids are pending, map_add drops legitimate announcements outright.

bcli executes each bitcoin-cli synchronously, so every block transfer and gettxout also delays all other backend calls (block polling, fee estimation, sendrawtransaction) queued behind it. If the operator's bitcoind is pruned (documented as partially supported, doc/getting-started/advanced-setup/bitcoin-core.md), the impact is larger: bcli's getrawblockbyheight loops on getblock/getblockfrompeer for up to bitcoin-retry-timeout (60 s) per attacker block, blocking bcli entirely, and if the block cannot be obtained from a peer in that time it returns a JSON-RPC error which get_bitcoin_result turns into fatal() (bitcoind.c:115-140, 451) - lightningd exits.

This exceeds what the BOLT requires: a UTXO check needs one block lookup to map txindex->txid and one gettxout for the single named outpoint, not one gettxout per P2WSH output in the block. No per-peer limit, no cap on distinct in-flight heights and no prioritisation of lightningd's own needs exist along this path.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/gossip\_control.c:78–114](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/gossip_control.c#L78-L114)
   get_txout serves gossipd's UTXO query for a peer-supplied channel_announcement. If the scid's block is absent from the wallet's blocks table (every block older than the node's first blockscan_start, i.e. tip-15 on first run) it calls bitcoind_getfilteredblock() for the entire block. No cap, per-peer attribution or cost bound exists at this layer; got_filteredblock (lines 38-77) caches the block, so each distinct pre-history block is fetched exactly once, and the attacker has hundreds of thousands never fetched.
2. [lightningd/bitcoind.c:712–780](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/bitcoind.c#L712-L780)
   process_getfilteredblock_step1 receives the full raw block from bcli, collects every P2WSH output in it, and starts a strictly sequential chain of bitcoind_getutxout() calls (step2, lines 690-710): one bcli `getutxout` (one bitcoin-cli gettxout subprocess) per P2WSH output in the block, not just the single outpoint the scid names.
3. [lightningd/bitcoind.c:784–857](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/bitcoind.c#L784-L857)
   Calls queue in bitcoind->pending_getfilteredblock and are processed one block at a time; process_getfiltered_block_final coalesces only identical heights and then starts the pending call with the HIGHEST height (most_recent_filteredblock_call). An attacker who picks heights just below the node's root therefore preempts every legitimate historical lookup (which have lower, random heights) for as long as it keeps the queue non-empty.
4. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:672–755](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L672-L755)
   A channel_announcement needs only the sender's own four signatures and an scid with blocknum in [when_lightning_became_cool=504500, blockheight-6]; if not already known/pending it is added to pending_ann_map (cap PENDING_LIMIT=10000, map_add lines 212-233) and a gossipd_get_txout is sent to lightningd immediately. There is no per-source accounting; once 10000 attacker entries are pending, map_add drops legitimate announcements too.
5. [plugins/bcli.c:344–436](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L344-L436)
   bcli's getrawblockbyheight runs bitcoin-cli synchronously (run_bitcoin_cli -> execute_bitcoin_cli -> waitpid, lines 150-205), so every block transfer and every gettxout blocks the single-threaded bcli plugin and delays all other backend calls behind it. When bitcoind is pruned, `getblock` fails and the loop retries `getblockfrompeer` with sleep(1) for up to bitcoind->retry_timeout (default 60 s, line 862) before returning command_done_err(BCLI_ERROR).
6. [lightningd/bitcoind.c:439–451](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/bitcoind.c#L439-L451)
   getrawblockbyheight_callback passes the bcli reply through get_bitcoin_result (lines 115-140), which calls bitcoin_plugin_error -> fatal() on any JSON-RPC error. So on a pruned backend, one attacker announcement whose block bitcoind cannot obtain from a peer within 60 s terminates lightningd.
7. [wallet/wallet.c:5087–5098](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L5087-L5098)
   wallet_have_block knows only blocks lightningd has processed since its first blockscan_start (chaintopology.c:1484-1576; blocks are rolled back only upward, wallet_blocks_rollback) plus filtered blocks previously cached. Every earlier block takes the expensive branch.
8. [connectd/multiplex.c:915–926](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L915-L926)
   handle_gossip_in forwards every inbound gossip message to gossipd; the only drop is a global 500000-message queue length, so a single peer can feed unlimited announcements.

## Impact
Availability: the single getfilteredblock worker, bcli and bitcoind are kept busy for as long as the attacker feeds distinct blocks; legitimate historical channel_announcement verification (including a fresh node's initial gossip sync) is preempted by height ordering and, once 10000 attacker scids are pending, further announcements are dropped, degrading routing knowledge. Other bcli calls see added latency from the synchronous bitcoin-cli runs. lightningd keeps running and block processing uses a separate path, so the general-case impact is partial (LOW). On a pruned bitcoind the same trigger can stall bcli for 60 s per block or terminate lightningd via fatal(); that outcome is conditional on the deployment and is described rather than rated. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any peer that can connect (connectd forwards all gossip to gossipd with no per-peer limit). They generate channel_announcements signed with their own two keypairs for scids in distinct blocks older than the victim's first block and send them as ordinary gossip; no on-chain cost. gossipd verifies signatures, finds the scid unknown, and asks lightningd; lightningd fetches the whole block and runs a getutxout per P2WSH output, one block at a time, highest height first. Works against every deployment because lightningd never stores pre-start blocks; the pruned-backend escalation (bcli stall / fatal) depends on the operator's bitcoind configuration and is not reflected in the metrics.

## Recommended fix
1. get_txout resolves a single outpoint by fetching an entire historical block and probing every P2WSH output in it, so one unverified peer message costs work proportional to block size rather than O(1). Fix criteria: Resolving the funding output of an unverified announcement must cost a bounded amount of bitcoind work independent of block contents (e.g. look up only the requested txindex/outnum), or the expensive filtered-block path must be bounded per peer and in total in-flight distinct heights, with lightningd's own needs prioritised. Verify by sending N announcements for N distinct old blocks and confirming bcli request count grows O(N), not O(sum of P2WSH outputs), and that other lookups are not starved.
2. gossipd forwards a get_txout for every signature-valid announcement with no per-source accounting, so a single peer can occupy the entire 10000-entry pending set and the downstream queue. Fix criteria: A single peer must not be able to fill the pending-announcement set or the txout queue; per-peer or cost-aware limits should drop or defer excess requests from one source. Verify by having one peer send >10000 unique announcements and confirming other peers' announcements are still verified promptly.
3. A historical-block fetch made on behalf of unverified gossip is treated like a chain-sync fetch: bcli blocks for up to retry_timeout trying peers, and lightningd turns the resulting backend error into fatal(). Fix criteria: A block that the backend cannot supply for a gossip UTXO lookup must be reported to gossipd as a failed lookup (and not retried synchronously for tens of seconds), never cause lightningd to exit. Verify on a pruned bitcoind by announcing an scid in a pruned block and confirming lightningd stays up and bcli remains responsive to other calls.

# Peer error delivered via peer_spoke force-closes an unconfirmed fundee channel instead of forgetting it

## Details
A fundee whose channel's funding was never broadcast may forget the channel on `error` (BOLT #2/#5), and lightningd does so when the error arrives through channeld: channel_errmsg (lightningd/peer_control.c:700-714) calls channel_fail_forget for opener==REMOTE && CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN. The same message delivered through connectd's peer_spoke path is handled differently: connectd starts reading peer messages immediately after init (connectd/multiplex.c:1756-1773) and, for the first message on a channel_id with no attached subd, sends connectd_peer_spoke with is_peer_error() set (multiplex.c:1591-1612). handle_peer_spoke then calls channel_fail_permanent(REASON_REMOTE) for every wants_peercomms channel (peer_control.c:2196-2201), with no opener/state check. channel_fail_perm (lightningd/channel.c:1106-1166) moves the never-funded channel to AWAITING_UNILATERAL and calls drop_to_chain, which has hsmd sign our commitment, persists it with wallet_transaction_add, adds a funding_spend_watch and hands it to broadcast_tx with commit_tx_send_finished (peer_control.c:295-316, 482-518), which returns false until the tx is mined. For a funding outpoint the opener never created it is never mined, so chaintopology keeps it in outgoing_txs and re-sends it to bitcoind every 30-60 s (chaintopology.c:157-241); resend_closing_transactions repeats the signing and rebroadcast at every restart (peer_control.c:560-575). The channel is released only by the 2016-block fundee timeout, which also keeps the newest 100 (channel_control.c:2092-2128, 2142-2190).

An unauthenticated remote peer triggers this deterministically and at no on-chain cost: open_channel -> accept_channel -> funding_created with an arbitrary txid -> funding_signed (lightningd commits the channel in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, opening_control.c:561-597), disconnect, reconnect, and send `error` for that channel_id immediately after `init`. Because lightningd attaches channeld only from peer_connected_hook_final after the asynchronous peer_connected hook (registered by the default chanbackup plugin) completes (peer_control.c:1543-1617), connectd has no subd when it reads the error and emits peer_spoke; lightningd force-closes instead of forgetting. Compared with the path the project already concedes (leaving the channel in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, which costs nothing while the peer is away), each such cycle leaves a persistent AWAITING_UNILATERAL channel with an hsmd signature, a wallet transaction row, a txo watch and a perpetual sendrawtransaction loop against bitcoind that continues after the attacker disconnects and survives restarts, repeatable without bound (the channeld-based open-count bound does not count CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN channels, peer_control.c:2044-2088).

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2196–2201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2196-L2201)
   handle_peer_spoke: for any channel in a wants_peercomms state (which includes CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, channel.h:733-744) a connectd-reported `error` goes straight to channel_fail_permanent(REASON_REMOTE), with no opener/awaiting-lockin check. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [connectd/multiplex.c:1591–1612](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1591-L1612)
   connectd reads peer messages as soon as init completes (multiplex_peer_setup, 1756-1773, is entered directly from peer_connected without waiting for lightningd). The first message for a channel_id with no subd is reported via connectd_peer_spoke carrying is_peer_error() (common/wire_error.c:173-179: the sanitized description of any WIRE_ERROR).
3. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:700–713](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L700-L713)
   channel_errmsg, the channeld-delivered path for the identical message, implements the BOLT #2 fundee rule: opener==REMOTE && CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN -> channel_fail_forget (channel.c:1204-1222 deletes the channel). The two delivery paths diverge.
4. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1543–1616](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1543-L1616)
   lightningd attaches channeld only from peer_connected_hook_final, after the asynchronous peer_connected plugin hook (registered by the default `important` chanbackup plugin, plugins/chanbackup.c:1187-1190) has completed. An error sent back-to-back with init therefore reaches connectd before any subd exists and is routed via peer_spoke rather than channeld.
5. [lightningd/channel.c:1106–1165](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1106-L1165)
   channel_fail_perm: CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN is wants_onchain_fail (-> AWAITING_UNILATERAL) and not open_uncommitted (channel.h:780-802), so the channel is kept and drop_to_chain is invoked for a funding outpoint that never existed.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:482–517](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L482-L517)
   drop_to_chain -> sign_and_send_last: hsmd signs our commitment, wallet_transaction_add persists it, broadcast_tx is armed with commit_tx_send_finished, which returns false (keep retrying) until wallet_transaction_height() is non-zero — never, for an unminable tx.
7. [lightningd/chaintopology.c:157–240](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/chaintopology.c#L157-L240)
   broadcast_done adds the otx to outgoing_txs when the finished callback returns false; rebroadcast_txs then re-sends every outgoing tx to bitcoind (bcli: one bitcoin-cli sendrawtransaction per tx) every 30-60 s for as long as the channel object lives.
8. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:560–574](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L560-L574)
   resend_closing_transactions (called at startup from lightningd.c:1485) re-runs drop_to_chain for every AWAITING_UNILATERAL channel, so each zombie costs another hsmd signature and rebroadcast entry on every restart.
9. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2092–2127](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2092-L2127)
   The only release path: is_fundee_should_forget requires 2016 blocks since first_blocknum (channel_notify_new_block also keeps the newest 100 forgettable channels), so each zombie persists ~2 weeks.

## Impact
Each zombie channel costs one hsmd signing request (repeated at every restart), persistent channel and transaction rows, a txo watch, and a bitcoind sendrawtransaction via bcli every 30-60 s for ~2016 blocks, persisting after the attacker disconnects; many of them load bcli/bitcoind and lightningd's rebroadcast timer, degrading block and fee processing. No funds are at risk (our commitment for a non-existent funding cannot be mined; fundee has zero balance) and nothing is disclosed.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote peer after the Noise handshake. Creating an unfunded fundee channel needs no transaction (the fundee cannot verify the funding txid). On reconnect the attacker sends `error` back-to-back with `init`; connectd reads it before lightningd's peer_connected hook round-trip (chanbackup) finishes and before connectd_peer_connect_subd arrives, so peer_spoke carries errmsg and the force-close branch runs. No race in any practical sense: a single TCP stream versus a multi-process IPC round trip. Repeatable per channel without limit.

## Recommended fix
1. handle_peer_spoke's error branch applies channel_fail_permanent to every wants_peercomms state, omitting the fundee-may-forget rule that channel_errmsg implements for opener==REMOTE && CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN (and the dual-funding DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN equivalent in dual_open_control.c). Fix criteria: A remote error for a channel in which we are fundee, have never seen the funding on-chain and have never had funds must produce the same outcome on both delivery paths: the channel is deleted, no commitment is signed or handed to broadcast_tx, and no transaction or watch is persisted. Verify: fundee channel in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN; peer reconnects and sends error as its first message; listpeerchannels no longer shows the channel and outgoing_txs gains no entry.
2. drop_to_chain/channel_fail_perm will sign and perpetually rebroadcast a commitment for a funding outpoint that has never been seen on-chain and in which we hold no funds, so any future path that permanently fails such a channel recreates the zombie. Fix criteria: channel_fail_perm (or drop_to_chain) treats a fundee channel with no funding seen on-chain, zero our_funds and zero msat_to_us_max as forgettable rather than droppable to chain, so the outcome does not depend on which caller failed the channel.

# Reestablish for a forgotten channel is answered to any peer, not only its counterparty

## Details
handle_peer_spoke (lightningd/peer_control.c) handles a channel_reestablish whose channel_id matches no live channel of the sending peer by consulting ld->closed_channels (peer_control.c:2317-2330). closed_channel_map is keyed and compared on channel_id only (closed_channel.h:37-53) and the code never compares closed_channel->peer_id with the sender. If a record with a stored remote shachain exists, lightningd replies with send_reestablish() -- a channel_reestablish carrying next_commitment_number, next_revocation_number and your_last_per_commitment_secret derived from the *original counterparty's* revealed secrets -- then the error 'Channel is closed and forgotten'. A channel_id that was never ours (or whose record predates shachain retention) gets 'Unknown channel for channel_reestablish' instead. The live-channel branch (find_channel_by_id(peer, ...) at 2162) is scoped to the asking peer; the forgotten-channel branch is not.

Reachability: connectd forwards any peer message with a channel_id for which no subd exists as CONNECTD_PEER_SPOKE regardless of channel relationship (connectd/multiplex.c:1595-1613), so any node that completes the Noise handshake can send channel_reestablish for arbitrary channel_ids. channel_ids are funding_txid XOR outnum, derivable from the chain for every spent 2-of-2 P2WSH funding output, so the prober can enumerate or target closed Lightning channels and learn (a) whether that on-chain output was a channel of this node -- deanonymising unannounced (never-gossiped) channels and linking the node to on-chain history -- (b) its commitment counters and (c) the counterparty's last per_commitment_secret. Every channel closed since v25.05 (CHANGELOG #8162 added this reply) keeps its remote shachain (wallet_channel_close does not delete it; only wallet_channel_delete does), so the oracle covers all recently closed channels. If the prober has no live channel it is disconnected after each answer and must reconnect; with one live channel peer_has_other_live_channel() (2370-2372) suppresses the disconnect and probing is unlimited on one connection.

The revealed secret is of little direct value (revocation keys also need our basepoint secret and the channel is already resolved on-chain), so the impact is a privacy/information-disclosure oracle, not fund loss. The fix is feasible: the peers row persists while any channels row -- including state=CLOSED -- references it (wallet.c:3246-3268), so closed_channel->peer_id is populated for channels closed on current versions and can be compared with the sender; only records from older DBs may have NULL peer_id.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2317–2330](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2317-L2330)
   For a channel_reestablish naming a channel_id that is not a live channel of this peer, the closed-channel map is searched by channel_id alone; if a record with a stored remote shachain exists lightningd calls send_reestablish() and sends the distinguishable error 'Channel is closed and forgotten' without checking that the requesting peer is closed_channel->peer_id. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [lightningd/closed\_channel.h:10–53](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/closed_channel.h#L10-L53)
   closed_channel records carry peer_id, but the htable is keyed (keyof_closed_channel) and compared (closed_channel_eq_cid) on cid only; peer_id is never consulted on the reestablish path.
3. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1987–2039](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1987-L2039)
   send_reestablish discloses next_commitment_number, next_revocation_number and the counterparty's last revealed per_commitment_secret from the stored shachain to whichever peer asked.
4. [connectd/multiplex.c:1595–1613](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1595-L1613)
   For any peer message carrying a channel_id with no matching subd, connectd creates a subd and sends CONNECTD_PEER_SPOKE to lightningd, regardless of whether the peer has any channel: this is how an arbitrary connected node reaches handle_peer_spoke.
5. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2162–2163](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2162-L2163)
   By contrast, live channels are looked up with find_channel_by_id(peer, ...) scoped to the requesting peer, so only the forgotten-channel branch lacks the ownership check.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2333–2340](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2333-L2340)
   channel_ids not in the closed map (or without a retained shachain) get a different error text ('Unknown channel for channel_reestablish') and no reestablish message, giving the prober a yes/no oracle.
7. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2370–2372](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2370-L2372)
   After a reestablish reply the peer is disconnected only if it has no other live channel; a prober holding one live channel with the victim is never disconnected and can probe without limit on a single connection.
8. [wallet/wallet.c:2238–2242](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L2238-L2242)
   The remote shachain is loaded into the closed_channel record whenever still present in the DB; wallet_channel_close does not delete it, so every channel closed on current versions is answerable (and thus enumerable) via this path.

## Impact
Discloses to unauthorised peers whether a given funding output was this node's channel (deanonymising unannounced closed channels and linking the node identity to on-chain history), the channel's commitment counters, and the counterparty's last per-commitment secret. The secret cannot be turned into a revocation key without this node's basepoint secret and the channel is already resolved on-chain, so no integrity or availability impact and no fund loss; confidentiality impact is limited to this privacy oracle.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote node able to complete the Noise handshake (no channel, funds or prior relationship required) sends channel_reestablish messages with candidate channel_ids derived from spent 2-of-2 funding outputs on-chain or from gossip; connectd forwards each as peer_spoke and lightningd answers from the closed_channels map keyed by channel_id alone. Each probe yields a distinguishable answer. Without a live channel the prober is disconnected after each reply and must reconnect (free); with a single live channel peer_has_other_live_channel() suppresses the disconnect and probes are unlimited on one connection.

## Recommended fix
The forgotten-channel lookup in handle_peer_spoke is keyed by channel_id only and does not verify that the requesting peer is the channel's recorded counterparty before replying with channel state. Fix criteria: A channel_reestablish for a closed/forgotten channel is answered with send_reestablish and the 'closed and forgotten' error only when closed_channel->peer_id is present and equals the sender's node_id; otherwise the sender receives exactly the same response as for a channel_id that was never ours. A regression test in which a third node sends channel_reestablish for another peer's closed channel_id must observe no channel_reestablish message and the generic 'Unknown channel' error.

# v1 fundee raises its reserve to the opener's dust_limit, leaving opener dust_limit unbounded

## Details
BOLT 2 requires the receiver of open_channel to fail the channel if dust_limit_satoshis is greater than channel_reserve_satoshis (and if it is below 354 sat). CLN's v1 accepter does neither. In fundee_channel() (openingd/openingd.c:984) the reserve we impose on the opener is computed by set_reserve(state, remoteconf.dust_limit), and set_reserve_absolute() (openingd.c:146-171) raises that reserve to the opener's dust_limit whenever the 1% default is smaller. The subsequent check `remoteconf.dust_limit > localconf.channel_reserve` (openingd.c:996-1005) is therefore unreachable, and check_config_bounds() (openingd/common.c:16-169) contains no dust_limit check at all. lightningd forwards dust_limit_satoshis to the openchannel hook but bounds nothing, and no shipped plugin registers that hook. The opener's dust_limit D is bounded only indirectly: funding - (their reserve + our reserve(=D)) - base fee must stay >= min_capacity_sat (10,000 sat default), so an opener can set D to just over half the channel capacity (with its own channel_reserve 0, also unchecked).

The opener's dust_limit is the trim threshold for the opener's commitment transaction (initial_channel_tx passes config[side].dust_limit; initial_commit_tx.c:227-264 drops to_remote below it, the value becoming miner fee; channeld/full_channel.c:397 does the same for every later remote commitment). openingd builds and signs that commitment (hsmd checks only 1 input / >0 outputs) and hands the signature over in funding_signed.

Attack: a remote peer opens a v1 channel of F sat to us (inbound v1 opens spawn openingd by default, lightningd/peer_control.c:2255-2271) with dust_limit D = F/2 + 1, channel_reserve = 0, push_msat = 0. We set our reserve to D; capacity = F - D - fee >= 10k sat passes; we accept and sign. Because the opener must keep >= D, our balance can never exceed F - D < D, so our to_remote output is trimmed on EVERY commitment the opener holds for the life of the channel. The peer then pays us (for goods/services) or routes its own payments through us to another node it controls, so we accrue balance up to ~F/2, then broadcasts its commitment: our entire balance goes to miners. In the routing case the attacker's cost is only the routing fee (the forwarded amount is already in its other channel) while we lose the amount we forwarded; with miner collusion the burned amount is recovered outright. Smaller D (e.g. D = 1% + epsilon) still burns our balance whenever it is below D at force-close time.

The same gap applies when the openchannel hook supplies a reserve (openingd.c:1075-1078) and under --dev-allowdustreserve. The funder path is protected because our reserve there is derived from our own dust_limit so the check at openingd.c:449 is live; the accepter path clearly intends the same bound (996-1005) but the bump defeats it, so this is CLN-specific, not inherent to the BOLTs. The missing lower bound (dust_limit < 354, even 0) is also unenforced; its consequence is noted but not traced here.

This is the v1 sibling of the verified dualopend finding dualopend-unbounded-remote-dust-limit-trims-our-commitment-output, whose evidence assumed the v1 accepter check at openingd.c:996 was effective; it is not. Unlike dual-funding, legacy inbound opens are accepted by default from any peer.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/openingd.c:146–177](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L146-L177)
   set_reserve_absolute(): when the opener's dust_limit exceeds the reserve we would impose (1% of funding, from set_reserve at 173-177), our channel_reserve is silently raised to equal the opener's dust_limit instead of refusing the open. After this call localconf.channel_reserve >= remoteconf.dust_limit always holds, which is what makes the later BOLT2 check unreachable. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [openingd/openingd.c:983–1005](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L983-L1005)
   fundee_channel(): set_reserve(state, remoteconf.dust_limit) at 984 runs first, so the check at 996-1005 'remoteconf.dust_limit > localconf.channel_reserve' can never be true (and is skipped entirely under --dev-allowdustreserve). It is the only place the v1 accepter compares the opener's dust_limit to anything.
3. [openingd/common.c:16–169](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/common.c#L16-L169)
   check_config_bounds(), the shared remote-config validator, never reads remoteconf->dust_limit. With our reserve now equal to the opener's dust_limit D and the opener free to set its own channel_reserve to 0, the only surviving constraint is funding - D - base_fee >= min_effective_htlc_capacity (10,000 sat by default), i.e. D can be just over half the channel.
4. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2255–2271](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2255-L2271)
   An inbound WIRE_OPEN_CHANNEL from any connected peer spawns openingd via peer_start_openingd() by default; no option gates acceptance of v1 opens, so fundee_channel() is reachable by any remote peer after the Noise handshake.
5. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:866–908](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L866-L908)
   opening_got_offer(): lightningd forwards dust_limit_satoshis to the openchannel hook payload but applies no bound itself; with no plugin registered the offer is accepted as-is. No shipped plugin registers the v1 openchannel hook (funder registers only openchannel2*).
6. [openingd/openingd.c:1075–1078](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L1075-L1078)
   A reserve supplied by the openchannel hook goes through the same set_reserve_absolute() bump, so a plugin-chosen reserve does not restore the bound either.
7. [openingd/openingd.c:1251–1282](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L1251-L1282)
   After funding_created we build the REMOTE commitment with initial_channel_tx(..., REMOTE, ...), have hsmd sign it and return funding_signed: the opener obtains a fully valid first commitment in which our to_remote is trimmed.
8. [common/initial\_channel.c:122–139](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/initial_channel.c#L122-L139)
   initial_channel_tx() passes channel->config[side].dust_limit, so for the opener's commitment the opener-chosen dust_limit is the trim threshold applied to our to_remote output.
9. [common/initial\_commit\_tx.c:227–263](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/initial_commit_tx.c#L227-L263)
   to_remote is omitted whenever other_pay < dust_limit; the trimmed amount becomes miner fee. The only guard (162-182) fails only when both outputs are <= the reserve, which the opener's large to_local always passes.
10. [channeld/full\_channel.c:397](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L397)
   channeld keeps building every later remote commitment with channel->config[side].dust_limit (the opener's unbounded value), so our balance stays trimmed from the opener's commitment for the life of the channel whenever it is below D (channeld/commit_tx.c:312 is the to_remote trim).
11. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1668–1675](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1668-L1675)
   handle_sign_remote_commitment_tx() checks only num_inputs == 1 and num_outputs > 0; a remote commitment consisting of the opener's to_local (+anchors) alone is signed.
12. [openingd/openingd.c:449–458](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L449-L458)
   Contrast: on the funder path our reserve was set from our own dust_limit (292-295), so this identical check is live and caps an accepter's dust_limit at max(1%, our dust). The accepter path intends the same bound but the bump at 146-171 defeats it.
13. [lightningd/options.c:1023](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1023)
   min_capacity_sat defaults to 10,000 sat: the only effective ceiling on the reserve sum, hence on the opener's dust_limit.

## Impact
Our full balance in the channel (everything we were paid or forwarded over it, up to ~half the capacity) is irrecoverable once the peer broadcasts its commitment: direct loss of funds, so integrity HIGH. No confidentiality impact; the node keeps operating, availability NONE.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any peer able to connect (inbound v1 opens are accepted from anyone by default) sends open_channel with dust_limit_satoshis up to ~funding/2 and channel_reserve 0. No defence stands in the way: the only check is dead code, check_config_bounds ignores dust_limit, the hook is not consulted about it by any shipped plugin, and hsmd signs the remote commitment. The attacker funds the channel itself, then pays or routes through the victim (a routing node forwards by default) so the victim accumulates balance, then force-closes with its own commitment. No victim interaction or special configuration is required; the attacker's capital is recovered via its own to_local, so cost is roughly the routing fee plus on-chain fees.

## Recommended fix
1. set_reserve_absolute() raises our reserve to the opener's dust_limit instead of treating an oversized dust_limit as a reason to refuse, which makes the BOLT2 dust_limit <= reserve check in fundee_channel() unreachable and leaves the opener's dust_limit unbounded. Fix criteria: The accepter must reject open_channel whose dust_limit_satoshis exceeds the reserve we would otherwise impose (or a sane absolute maximum, e.g. a few thousand sat) and whose dust_limit is below 354 sat, before accept_channel is sent, regardless of allowdustreserve or a hook-supplied reserve. Verify by offering open_channel with dust_limit = funding/2 (and dust_limit = 0) and confirming openingd replies with an error and no accept_channel/funding_signed is produced.
2. check_config_bounds() in openingd/common.c validates every remote config field except dust_limit, so neither v1 role nor dualopend gets a dust bound from the shared validator; the open_channel self-consistency rule dust_limit <= channel_reserve is also never enforced. Fix criteria: The shared remote-config validation must enforce 354 <= remote dust_limit <= remote channel_reserve and an absolute ceiling, so that a peer cannot choose a trim threshold above our possible balance on its commitment in any opening path.

# Unbounded unconfirmed fundee channels per peer, each spawning a channeld process

## Details
lightningd caps *concurrent* channel negotiations per peer (one uncommitted v1 open, peer_control.c:2261-2265; MAX_INFLIGHT_OPENS=3 pre-funding v2 opens, 2291-2300) but places no bound on the number of *committed, unconfirmed* fundee channels a peer may hold. The comment at peer_control.c:2042-2044 assumes that once a channel has a funding transaction the peer's effort is bounded by paying for it. That is false for the fundee side of a v1 open: funding_created (openingd.c:1118-1124) carries only a txid/outnum chosen by the opener plus a signature over our commitment tx, which the opener can produce for any outpoint without ever building or broadcasting a transaction.

Attack: a remote peer (any node_id, no channel, funds or on-chain activity) sends open_channel with any funding_satoshis above min-capacity-sat; openingd answers accept_channel; the peer sends funding_created with a fresh random txid and a valid signature. opening_fundee_finished (opening_control.c:543-600) checks only outpoint/channel_id uniqueness, inserts the channel into the DB in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, spawns a lightning_channeld (with a dedicated hsmd client socket) and frees peer->uncommitted_channel, so handle_peer_spoke admits the next open_channel at once. Each round trip therefore yields one more persistent channel row and one more live channeld process, with no limit; no option, hook or default plugin bounds it (only funder's openchannel2 hook is registered). If the peer disconnects and reconnects, peer_connected_hook_final (1603-1619) and connect_activate_subd (1479-1496) re-spawn a channeld for every one of these channels at once, and after a lightningd restart the rows reload and the flood recurs on reconnect. The channels are forgotten only 2016 blocks later (channel_control.c:2092-2128), keeping the 100 newest.

Impact: process, memory, pid and fd growth in lightningd, hsmd and connectd set purely by the attacker's message count. hsmd keeps one fd per live channeld but inherits the pre-raise soft RLIMIT_NOFILE because hsm_init (lightningd.c:1308) runs before setup_fd_limit (1409): once that limit is reached hsmd's socketpair() fails and it status_failed()s (hsmd.c:639-643), which is fatal for lightningd (subd.c:663-668). In lightningd itself, socketpair() failure on the open_channel path calls sockpair(tmpctx, NULL, ...) (peer_control.c:2268) whose error branch dereferences channel->log (61-77), a NULL-pointer crash. Short of a crash, fork/OOM failures for genuine channels and the per-block O(N) channel walk degrade the node for ~2 weeks. Other implementations bound pending fundee channels per peer; CLN's MAX_INFLIGHT_OPENS does not cover the committed-unconfirmed state.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2255–2272](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2255-L2272)
   WIRE_OPEN_CHANNEL from an unknown channel_id is admitted whenever peer->uncommitted_channel is NULL. The only bound is one *concurrent* v1 negotiation; nothing counts the peer's committed-but-unconfirmed (CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN) channels. sockpair() at 2268 is called with channel == NULL.
2. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2042–2085](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2042-L2085)
   channel_state_opening()/num_inflight_opens() (used only by the open_channel2 MAX_INFLIGHT_OPENS check at 2291-2300) deliberately exclude CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN/DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN on the assumption that a funding tx bounds the peer's effort; as fundee no funding tx is ever required to exist.
3. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:543–599](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L543-L599)
   opening_fundee_finished only checks funding-outpoint/channel_id uniqueness, then wallet_commit_channel() inserts the channel into the DB in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, peer_start_channeld() spawns a lightning_channeld (with its own hsmd client fd), and the uncommitted_channel is freed (opening_common.c:24 clears peer->uncommitted_channel), so the next open_channel from the same peer is admitted immediately.
4. [openingd/openingd.c:1118–1123](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L1118-L1123)
   As fundee, funding_created carries only a txid, output index and a signature over our commitment tx (verified by check_tx_sig at 1205 against the peer's funding pubkey). The opener can produce this for any random outpoint without constructing, funding or broadcasting a transaction.
5. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1603–1618](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1603-L1618)
   On every (re)connect, peer_connected_hook_final calls connect_activate_subd for every channel whose state wants peer comms, which includes CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN: N such channels mean N channeld processes per connection.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1479–1495](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1479-L1495)
   connect_activate_subd spawns a new lightning_channeld (socketpair + hsm client fd + fork/exec) for each CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN channel.
7. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2092–2127](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2092-L2127)
   is_fundee_should_forget forgets such channels only 2016 blocks (~2 weeks) after first_blocknum (dev-only option), and channel_notify_new_block (2156-2192) keeps the 100 most recent even then; within that window the number of persisted channels is unbounded and survives restarts.
8. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1409](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1409)
   setup_fd_limit raises lightningd's RLIMIT_NOFILE only here, after hsm_init (1308) and connectd_init (1338) have already forked hsmd and connectd, which therefore keep the operator's original soft fd limit; neither subdaemon raises its own.
9. [hsmd/hsmd.c:639–642](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/hsmd.c#L639-L642)
   hsmd holds one fd per live channeld client; when socketpair() fails (EMFILE at the inherited soft limit) hsmd status_failed()s, and hsmd is a must_not_exit global subd so lightningd exits via errx (subd.c:663-668).
10. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:61–77](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L61-L77)
   sockpair()'s failure branch dereferences channel->log and &channel->cid; on the WIRE_OPEN_CHANNEL path (2268) channel is NULL, so socketpair() failure from fd exhaustion in lightningd is a NULL-pointer crash.

## Impact
Unbounded process, memory, file-descriptor and DB growth driven by peer input, persisting ~2016 blocks and across restarts; exhaustion ends in a lightningd exit (hsmd status_failed at its inherited fd limit, or the NULL deref in sockpair's error path) or in fork/OOM failures that stop legitimate channels from getting a channeld. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote Lightning peer that completes the Noise handshake can run the open_channel / funding_created loop: no channel, funds or on-chain transaction is required, the signature is over a commitment tx the attacker can compute from accept_channel, and nothing in lightningd, openingd or the default plugins counts the resulting channels. The sequence is deterministic protocol traffic, a few round trips per channel, multiplied on every reconnect (one channeld per channel) and across node_ids.

## Recommended fix
1. Per-peer open admission in handle_peer_spoke counts only in-negotiation opens; committed fundee channels whose funding has never been seen on-chain (CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN / DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN with opener == REMOTE and no local funds) are not counted, so a peer can accumulate them without limit. Fix criteria: A peer must not be able to hold more than a small (configurable) number of fundee-side channels whose funding transaction has not been seen on-chain, and a global cap should bound the total across peers; open_channel/open_channel2 beyond that bound must be rejected (error + disconnect) before any channel, HSM client or subdaemon is created. Verify by driving the open_channel/funding_created loop from a test peer and checking that channel count and channeld process count stay bounded, including after reconnect and restart.
2. sockpair() is called with a NULL channel on the WIRE_OPEN_CHANNEL path, and its failure branch dereferences the channel. Fix criteria: sockpair() failure must not dereference a NULL channel: log against the peer and build the warning from the message's channel_id. Verify that forcing socketpair() to fail during an unsolicited open_channel does not crash lightningd.
3. hsmd and connectd are forked before lightningd raises its RLIMIT_NOFILE, so they keep the original soft limit and hsmd treats socketpair() failure as fatal. Fix criteria: Raise the fd limit before spawning global subdaemons (or have them raise it themselves) and make hsmd's per-client socketpair failure a per-request error rather than a daemon failure. Verify that exhausting hsmd's client fds does not terminate lightningd.

# sendinvoice crashes on invoice_request containing invreq_recurrence_cancel (NULL invoice_for_invreq result)

## Details
`sendinvoice` is the RPC an operator runs on an `lnr1...` invoice_request that a remote payer produced (doc/schemas/sendinvoice.json: 'creates and sends an invoice to the issuer of an invoice_request'); the string is counterparty-authored.

plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1524 builds the invoice with `sent->inv = invoice_for_invreq(sent, sent->invreq)` and at 1536/1539 writes `sent->inv->invoice_amount = ...` with no NULL check. `invoice_for_invreq()` (common/bolt12.c:818-844) serialises the invreq, keeps TLV ranges 0-159 and 1000000000-2999999999, and reparses them with `fromwire_tlv_invoice()`, returning its result unchecked. `invreq_recurrence_cancel` is TLV type 2000000094 in tlv_invoice_request (wire/bolt12_wire.csv:96), an even, empty record that tlv_invoice does not define (the invoice namespace has 2000000092/2000000093 only). The generated fromwire_tlv_invoice_request() allocates a non-NULL struct for the empty record, towire re-emits it, and the generated fromwire_tlv_invoice() (extra_types NULL, tools/gen/impl_template:288) rejects it as an unknown even type (wire/tlvstream.c:119-135, 213-214), so `invoice_for_invreq()` returns NULL and the next statement writes through it.

`param_invreq()` (fetchinvoice.c:1370-1491) is the only filter: it checks payer_id, metadata, the 0-159/1000000000-2999999999 range (2000000094 is inside), features, signature (the attacker signs with their own payer key, so this passes trivially), and absence of offer_issuer_id/offer_paths/offer_chains/offer_features/offer_quantity_max. It never rejects recurrence fields; the BOLT12 'MUST reject if invreq_recurrence_cancel is present' absent recurrence is not implemented here. The invoice_request hook sibling (offers_invreq_hook.c:1140-1146) strips the cancel field before invoice_for_invreq() precisely because the invoice parser cannot carry it.

Attack: a remote payer produces a valid self-signed invoice_request with invreq_amount plus an empty `invreq_recurrence_cancel` record and hands the lnr1 string to the operator (e.g. as a refund/withdrawal request). When the operator runs `sendinvoice invreq=<string> label=...`, the offers plugin segfaults. `offers` is in list_of_builtin_plugins and loaded `important` (lightningd/plugin.c:2579-2586), so lightningd exits. The crash precedes the `invoice_recurrence(sent->inv)` rejection at line 1585 and any RPC round-trip.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1524–1539](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L1524-L1539)
   json_sendinvoice() assigns sent->inv = invoice_for_invreq(sent, sent->invreq) at 1524 and, with no NULL check, writes sent->inv->invoice_amount at 1536/1539. The invoice_recurrence() rejection at 1585 comes after the dereference.
2. [common/bolt12.c:818–843](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L818-L843)
   invoice_for_invreq() serialises the invreq with towire_tlv_invoice_request(), keeps TLV ranges 0-159 and 1000000000-2999999999 via tlv_span(), and reparses them with fromwire_tlv_invoice(), returning that parser's result (NULL on failure) unchecked. Type 2000000094 is inside the kept range.
3. [wire/bolt12\_wire.csv:96](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/bolt12_wire.csv#L96)
   invreq_recurrence_cancel is tlvtype 2000000094 (even, empty record) of tlv_invoice_request; the tlv_invoice namespace (lines 104-178) defines 2000000092 and 2000000093 but not 2000000094, so the generated fromwire_tlv_invoice() (tools/gen/impl_template:288, extra_types NULL) cannot accept it.
4. [wire/tlvstream.c:119–134](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/tlvstream.c#L119-L134)
   tlv_type_is_allowed(): an even type not in the record's type table and with extra_types == NULL is rejected; fromwire_tlv() then fails (line 213-214 'unknown even') and the generated wrapper returns tal_free(record) == NULL.
5. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1370–1490](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L1370-L1490)
   param_invreq(), the only validation sendinvoice applies to the counterparty-authored invreq, checks range (2000000094 is in-range), features, payer_id/metadata, signature (attacker signs with their own payer key) and offer_* absence, but never rejects invreq_recurrence_cancel/counter/start.
6. [plugins/offers\_invreq\_hook.c:1140–1145](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_invreq_hook.c#L1140-L1145)
   The invoice_request hook sibling explicitly NULLs invreq_recurrence_cancel before invoice_for_invreq() ('doesn't exist in invoices, so temporarily remove') and restores it after; sendinvoice has no such guard.

## Impact
Write through a NULL struct pointer in the offers plugin (SIGSEGV). offers is an important builtin plugin, so its death stops lightningd: full node outage with on-chain exposure until restart. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote payment counterparty able to hand an lnr1 string to the operator — the documented sendinvoice workflow. The string must pass param_invreq, which only needs a self-consistent invreq signed by the attacker's own payer key with invreq_amount; an added empty TLV 2000000094 is in-range and is covered by the attacker's signature. The operator must then run sendinvoice on it (deliberate but routine step, hence UI:ACTIVE). Deterministic NULL write, no race, no privileges. A rune holder permitted to call sendinvoice (commando/clnrest) can trigger it directly as well.

## Recommended fix
1. json_sendinvoice() assumes invoice_for_invreq() cannot fail and dereferences its result unconditionally. Fix criteria: sendinvoice must return a JSON-RPC error when invoice_for_invreq() returns NULL; feeding an invreq containing invreq_recurrence_cancel (or any field the invoice TLV cannot carry) must yield an RPC error and leave the plugin running.
2. param_invreq() does not enforce the BOLT12 rule that invreq_recurrence_cancel/counter/start may only appear with a recurrence, and sendinvoice does not support recurrence at all. Fix criteria: param_invreq() must reject invreqs carrying invreq_recurrence_cancel (and, absent recurrence, invreq_recurrence_counter/start) before any invoice construction, matching the checks in the invoice_request hook.

# Upstream peer's malformed TLV 65537 makes cln-lsps-client hook error, lightningd fatal()

## Details
cln-lsps-client's `htlc_accepted` hook (client.rs:543-659) handles an incoming HTLC whose payment_hash matches a pending JIT invoice (datastore key lsps/invoice/<hash>, written by lsps-lsps2-approve / lsps-lsps2-invoice, deleted only when the invoice is paid). Once that gate passes it reads the opening fee the LSP is expected to attach as update_add_htlc TLV type 65537:

    let extra_fee_msat = req.htlc.extra_tlvs.as_ref().map(|tlvs| tlvs.get_u64(65537)).transpose()?.flatten().unwrap_or_default();

`TlvStream::get_u64` (tlv.rs:194-202) requires the value to be exactly 8 bytes and otherwise returns Err(BytesToU64). The `?` returns that error from the hook handler. Unlike every other failure in this handler (all wrapped in ok_or_continue!/some_or_continue!, client.rs:822-860), it is not converted to `{"result":"continue"}`. cln-plugin answers an Err from a hook callback with a JSON-RPC error object (plugins/src/lib.rs:982-1004, code -32700). lightningd's plugin_hook_callback (plugin_hook.c:273-283) treats any hook reply without a `result` member whose code is not PLUGIN_TERMINATED as a plugin bug and calls fatal(), aborting the whole node.

Who authors the input: the TLV extension of update_add_htlc is written by the direct channel peer that sends the HTLC. channeld keeps unknown odd types (channeld.c:682-722; wire/tlvstream.c:206-218) and lightningd hands them raw to the hook (peer_htlcs.c:1628-1634, 1298-1300) before any invoice or payment_secret check. In the LSPS2 flow that peer is the LSP, which is exactly the party expected to add TLV 65537 (the service side writes it as 8 bytes via set_u64, htlc.rs:226); a malicious or buggy LSP instead sends e.g. `fe 00 01 00 01 01 00` (type 65537, length 1) with a valid final-hop onion (TLV 2/4/8 present) for the JIT invoice's hash. The plugin's from_bytes_auto (tlv.rs:116-124) parses this as the single record {65537, 00}, get_u64 fails, the hook returns Err, lightningd dies. Any other peer with a channel to the client who knows the pending invoice's payment_hash (the payer, or anyone if the bolt11 is published) can do the same; the LSP alone suffices. Preconditions: the client enabled `experimental-lsps-client` (the plugin disables itself otherwise, client.rs:120-125) and has an outstanding JIT invoice, which is its normal operating state while waiting for a payment. The path does not depend on the build profile: release, Docker and documented source builds are all affected.

The recorded threat model lists a crash of lightningd on peer input as DoS with on-chain consequences. After restart lightningd replays the unresolved HTLC through the hook (htlcs_resubmit); extra_tlvs are not persisted (wallet/wallet.c:3611-3617) so the replay does not re-crash, but the attacker repeats with a fresh HTLC for as long as a JIT invoice is pending. This is distinct from the verified service-side finding at core/tlv.rs:116 (different plugin and sink: a length-prefix misparse re-encoded into the hook response, not a decode error propagated as a hook error).

## Evidence
1. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:587–594](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs#L587-L594)
   on_htlc_accepted reads the upstream peer's update_add_htlc TLV 65537 with tlvs.get_u64(65537) and propagates the decode error with `?` out of the hook handler. Every other failure in this handler (lines 547-585, 612-645) is wrapped in ok_or_continue!/some_or_continue! (client.rs:822-860) and answered with {"result":"continue"}; this one returns Err to cln-plugin.
2. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs:194–202](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs#L194-L202)
   get_u64 does `rec.value[..].try_into()` into [u8;8]; any TLV 65537 value whose length is not exactly 8 bytes yields Err(TlvError::BytesToU64). The peer chooses the length.
3. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:571–585](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs#L571-L585)
   The only gate before the sink: a datastore record lsps/invoice/<payment_hash> must exist, i.e. the HTLC's payment_hash is that of a pending JIT invoice (written by lsps-lsps2-approve at client.rs:289-296, deleted by on_invoice_payment at 530-538). The LSP forwarding the payment, and anyone holding the bolt11, knows this hash; no payment_secret check has happened yet because the hook fires before handle_localpay.
4. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs:213–228](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs#L213-L228)
   Htlc.extra_tlvs (cln_adapters/types.rs:38) is deserialised through from_bytes_auto. For the attacker's bytes `fe 00 01 00 01 01 00` the length-prefix guess fails (65537 != 2 remaining) and the raw parse yields exactly one record {type 65537, value 00}, so the plugin sees what lightningd sent.
5. [plugins/src/lib.rs:982–1003](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/src/lib.rs#L982-L1003)
   cln-plugin dispatches hook callbacks on the same CustomRequest path as RPC methods (hooks are merged into rpcmethods at lib.rs:432-434). An Err from the callback is sent back as {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":..,"error":parse_error(e)} with code -32700 (lib.rs:1142-1155): a reply with no `result` member.
6. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:273–282](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L273-L282)
   plugin_hook_callback: unless the error code is PLUGIN_TERMINATED (-4, the plugin died), a hook reply without a `result` member is fatal(): lightningd aborts.
7. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1628–1633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1628-L1633)
   hook_payload->extra_tlvs_raw = towire_tlvstream_raw(hin->extra_tlvs): the upstream peer's update_add_htlc TLV records, raw and unmodified, serialised to the hook as htlc.extra_tlvs at peer_htlcs.c:1298-1300 before any invoice/payment_secret validation.
8. [channeld/channeld.c:682–721](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L682-L721)
   handle_peer_add_htlc parses update_add_htlc; fromwire_tlv keeps unknown odd types such as 65537 in tlvs->fields (wire/tlvstream.c:206-218 only rejects unknown even types) and channel_add_htlc stores them as the HTLC's extra_tlvs, which reach lightningd via added_htlc (common/htlc_wire.c:197-215, FROMWIRE_TLV_ANY_TYPE).

## Impact
lightningd fatal() takes the entire node offline: all channels and pending HTLCs are unattended, risking on-chain timeouts, and the attack is repeatable after every restart while a JIT invoice is pending. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote peer with a channel to a node running cln-lsps-client. The LSP is always in that position during a JIT payment and is the party that normally sets TLV 65537; it learns the pending JIT invoice's payment_hash from the HTLC it forwards or from the bolt11. It sends update_add_htlc with a valid final-hop onion (TLV 8 present) and TLV 65537 of any length other than 8. The plugin returns an error for the hook and lightningd aborts. Deterministic; no defence to bypass; no authentication or privilege within the victim's system is involved. Requires the non-default `experimental-lsps-client` option and an outstanding JIT invoice (AT:P).

## Recommended fix
A decode failure of the peer-authored TLV 65537 in on_htlc_accepted is propagated with `?` as a hook error, which lightningd treats as a fatal plugin bug, instead of being handled like every other input failure in the handler. Fix criteria: No peer-controlled input to the htlc_accepted hook can make the handler return Err: a malformed, absent or oversized TLV 65537 results in `continue` (or an explicit `fail` of that HTLC) and lightningd keeps running. Verify by sending an HTLC for a pending JIT invoice with TLV 65537 of length 0, 1 and 9 and confirming lightningd stays up.

# sql plugin prints infinite REAL as bare 'inf'; lightningd kills the important sql plugin on parse failure and shuts down

## Details
The sql plugin's `sql` method runs a caller-supplied SELECT and streams rows back as JSON. In refresh_complete() (plugins/sql.c:476-478) a REAL column is written with

    json_add_primitive_fmt(ret, NULL, "%f", v);

with no check that v is finite. SQLite produces an infinite REAL from a plain SELECT -- `SELECT 1e999`, `SELECT 1e308*10`, `SELECT 1e308+1e308` -- none of which read a table or call a function, so sqlite_authorize() (which allows bare SQLITE_SELECT) and the sqlite3_limit() caps permit them. printf's %f renders +infinity as the bare token `inf`, which json_out_addv() copies verbatim, so the plugin writes

    {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"...","result":{"rows":[[inf]]}}

to its stdout. CLN compiles jsmn with JSMN_STRICT (common/json_parse_simple.h:9), under which a primitive may only begin with '-', a digit, 't', 'f' or 'n'; `inf` fails with JSMN_ERROR_INVAL and json_parse_input() returns false. lightningd's plugin reader (lightningd/plugin.c:719-724) treats any parse error on a plugin's stdout as fatal for that plugin: jsonrpc_io_parse() returns 'Failed to parse RPC JSON response ...' and plugin_read_json() calls plugin_kill(), which SIGKILLs the sql plugin and tal_free()s its struct. The sql plugin is a builtin loaded as `important` (plugin.c:2576-2590; plugins/Makefile:141-148), and plugin_kill() does not clear that flag (only the sanctioned `plugin stop` path does, plugin.c:1707), so the plugin's destructor destroy_plugin() (plugin.c:297-302) logs 'Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1): the entire node exits.

Who can trigger it: anyone permitted to call `sql` -- the operator (trusted) or, more importantly, a rune holder via commando (reachable over any Lightning peer connection) or clnrest whose rune permits method=sql. The sql plugin exists precisely to give such callers bounded read-only access: its documentation (doc/schemas/sql-template.json:86) promises 'Writing to the database is not permitted, and limits are placed on various other query parameters.' A single one-line query from such a caller instead takes the whole node offline (channels unmonitored, HTLCs unresolved) until the operator restarts lightningd -- an availability impact the rune did not grant.

Lesser variants: negative infinity prints as `-inf` and NaN as `nan`/`-nan`; these begin with permitted characters, so jsmn accepts them as primitives and lightningd forwards invalid JSON to the RPC client.

The fix belongs in the float emission path (reject or represent non-finite values, e.g. emit null or a string), since nothing else in the response pipeline guards against non-finite doubles. Dependency assumptions: system sqlite3 yields +Inf for `1e999` / `1e308*10` (sqlite3AtoF overflow and unchecked double arithmetic); glibc/libc printf formats INFINITY as `inf`; external/jsmn in strict mode rejects a primitive starting with 'i'.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/sql.c:476–478](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/sql.c#L476-L478)
   refresh_complete() emits every SQLITE_FLOAT column with json_add_primitive_fmt(ret, NULL, "%f", v) and no isfinite() check. C's %f renders +infinity as the bare token `inf` (and -inf / nan for the other non-finite values), which json_out_addv (ccan/ccan/json_out/json_out.c:218-250) copies verbatim into the JSON-RPC reply on the plugin's stdout.
2. [lightningd/plugin.c:719–724](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L719-L724)
   plugin_read_json(): any error from jsonrpc_io_parse() on the plugin's stdout is answered with plugin_kill(plugin, LOG_UNUSUAL, ...), which SIGKILLs the process and tal_free()s the plugin (plugin.c:440-460) without clearing plugin->important.
3. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L302)
   destroy_plugin() (registered as the plugin's tal destructor at plugin.c:379) runs on that tal_free: if p->important it logs 'Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1), so the whole node exits. Only the sanctioned `plugin stop` path clears `important` first (plugin.c:1707).
4. [lightningd/plugin.c:2576–2590](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2576-L2590)
   plugins_set_builtin_plugins_dir() registers every builtin plugin as important except cln-renepay. plugins/Makefile:141-148 adds plugins/sql to PLUGINS (hence list_of_builtin_plugins_gen.h) whenever HAVE_SQLITE3=1, so the shipped sql plugin is important by default.
5. [plugins/sql.c:1436–1453](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/sql.c#L1436-L1453)
   json_sql() prepares the caller's query under sqlite_authorize() (sql.c:331-442), which returns SQLITE_OK for SQLITE_SELECT; `SELECT 1e999` (or `SELECT 1e308*10`) reads no table and calls no function, so it passes the authorizer and sqlite3_limit caps and is stepped in refresh_complete().
6. [common/json\_parse\_simple.h:9](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.h#L9)
   JSMN_STRICT is defined for the whole tree. Under strict mode jsmn (external/jsmn submodule, absent from this checkout — assumed behaviour) accepts a primitive only if it begins with '-', a digit, 't', 'f' or 'n', and returns JSMN_ERROR_INVAL otherwise; `inf` therefore fails, and json_parse_input() (common/json_parse_simple.c:519-520) returns false.
7. [common/jsonrpc\_io.c:79–84](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/jsonrpc_io.c#L79-L84)
   jsonrpc_io_parse() turns the json_parse_input() failure into the error string 'Failed to parse RPC JSON response ...' that plugin_read_json() treats as fatal for the plugin.

## Impact
lightningd exits with code 1 ('Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!'), taking every subdaemon and plugin with it: the node stops monitoring channels, forwarding or resolving HTLCs, and serving RPC until the operator restarts it. No data is disclosed or modified.

## Reproduction steps
1. A caller permitted the `sql` RPC method -- typically a rune holder reaching the node over commando (any Lightning peer connection, rune-authenticated) or clnrest -- sends `sql query='SELECT 1e999'`. The authorizer allows it (bare SELECT, no table or function), sqlite3_step yields an SQLITE_FLOAT infinity, %f prints `inf`, lightningd's strict jsmn parse of the plugin's stdout fails, plugin_kill() frees the important sql plugin and destroy_plugin() calls lightningd_exit(). One request, deterministic, default configuration (sql is important by default; no option needed). Privileges: a rune granting method=sql (PR:L).

## Recommended fix
refresh_complete() formats REAL results with a bare %f, which emits non-JSON tokens (inf, -inf, nan) for non-finite doubles that a caller can produce with a plain SELECT; lightningd treats the resulting unparsable reply as a plugin fault, kills the plugin, and -- because the sql plugin is important -- shuts down the node. Fix criteria: Non-finite REAL results must never reach the JSON stream as bare inf/nan tokens: for !isfinite(v) emit JSON null (or a string, or fail the command with a proper error) so the reply always parses, including the -inf and nan variants. Verify that `sql query='SELECT 1e999'`, `SELECT -1e999`, `SELECT 1e308*10` and a NaN-producing expression each return a well-formed response, the sql plugin remains running, and lightningd stays up.

# Commando reply handler walks non-object result as object: out-of-bounds token read

## Details
When the local node issues `commando peer_id=<remote> method=...`, plugins/commando.c handle_reply() reassembles the remote's reply, parses it with json_parse_simple(), checks only that the root token is an object, and on the success path copies the members of `result` into the local JSON-RPC response:

    result = json_get_member(replystr, toks, "result");
    ...
    json_for_each_obj(i, t, result) {
        json_add_jsonstr(res, json_strdup(tmpctx, replystr, t),
                         json_tok_full(replystr, t+1), json_tok_full_len(t+1));
    }

`result` is never checked to be a JSMN_OBJECT. json_for_each_obj() assumes obj->size key tokens each followed by one value datum and advances with json_next(t+1). For `"result":[1,2,3]` placed as the last member (a JSMN_ARRAY, which validate_jsmn_parse_output accepts), the loop runs 3 times consuming 2 datums each: iteration 2 uses the zeroed sentinel as the value (emitting the malformed member `"3":` with no value), then json_next(sentinel+1) and iteration 3 dereference jsmntok_t slots beyond the tal array that json_parse_input() cut to exactly datumlen+1 (common/json_parse_simple.c:549-551). Garbage start/end/size from heap memory feed json_strdup() (tal_strndup from replystr+start), json_tok_full_len() and the unchecked memcpy in json_add_jsonstr(), and the recursive json_next(): out-of-bounds reads, wild-length copies into the response, or a segfault. The peer chooses the array length, so a long array of primitives walks tens of megabytes past the allocation and makes the crash reliable; even a short array yields malformed JSON that lightningd's jsonrpc_io_parse rejects, killing the plugin (lightningd/plugin.c:724). A result of type string/primitive is harmless (size 0); objects are structurally validated by validate_jsmn_keyvalue; only arrays are affected.

commando is a builtin plugin loaded as `important` (lightningd/plugin.c:2578-2586), so either the segfault or the plugin_kill on malformed output triggers lightningd_exit(1) (plugin.c:297-302): the whole node shuts down on one peer-authored reply.

Note on the key path: json_strdup() copies raw key bytes as the field name, but ccan json_out's check_fieldname() assert is compiled only with CCAN_JSON_OUT_DEBUG, which the Makefile sets only for DEBUGBUILD=1 (configure defaults DEBUGBUILD=0); in release builds the raw, still-escaped key bytes produce valid JSON, so that path is not a production defect.

The error branch is correctly defensive (checks code/message, uses json_add_string); only the success branch trusts the shape.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/commando.c:553–566](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L553-L566)
   handle_reply() takes the remote peer's `result` member and iterates it with json_for_each_obj() without checking it is a JSMN_OBJECT (only toks[0] was type-checked at line 496). Each iteration passes json_strdup(t) as a field name and json_tok_full(t+1)/json_tok_full_len(t+1) as the value to json_add_jsonstr(). For a JSMN_ARRAY result the walk leaves the parsed datum and the token array. This is the location the fix must change.
2. [common/json\_parse\_simple.h:140–142](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.h#L140-L142)
   json_for_each_obj advances with json_next(t+1), consuming two datums per iteration for obj->size iterations. Applied to a JSMN_ARRAY of N primitives it reads roughly N/2 datums past the array's last element; N is chosen by the peer.
3. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:546–551](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L546-L551)
   json_parse_input() resizes the token array to exactly datumlen+1 and writes a single zeroed sentinel (type -1, start=end=size=0); nothing is referenceable beyond it, so the walk reads past the tal allocation once it passes the sentinel.
4. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:173–181](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L173-L181)
   json_next() recurses tok->size times from tok+1. Called on the first out-of-bounds slot (sentinel+1) it reads a garbage size from heap memory beyond the allocation and walks arbitrarily far.
5. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:11–23](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L11-L23)
   json_tok_full()/json_tok_full_len() compute the value pointer and (int) length from the out-of-bounds token's start/end; garbage values yield a wild pointer or a negative length that becomes a huge size_t at the memcpy.
6. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:56–58](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L56-L58)
   json_strdup() is tal_strndup(buffer + tok->start, tok->end - tok->start); with an out-of-bounds token's garbage start it dereferences replystr plus an arbitrary offset.
7. [common/json\_stream.c:223–235](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_stream.c#L223-L235)
   json_add_jsonstr() memcpy()s jsonstrlen bytes into json_member_direct()'s return without a NULL check; a huge garbage length makes mkroom() fail and return NULL, or copies out-of-bounds bytes into the response. Even the benign sentinel iteration (length 0) emits `"key":` with no value, producing malformed JSON.
8. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–301](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L301)
   When a plugin dies (segfault) or emits unparsable JSON (plugin_kill at line 724 on jsonrpc_io_parse error), an important plugin's death calls lightningd_exit(1). commando is registered important at lines 2578-2586 (list_of_builtin_plugins, all but cln-renepay), so either outcome stops the whole node.
9. [plugins/commando.c:485–510](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L485-L510)
   Replies are accepted when peer id and 64-bit request id match an outstanding outgoing command (the id was sent to that peer in the request), so the author is exactly the remote node the local operator targeted with the `commando` RPC; up to 500MB of reply body is buffered, parsed, and its root checked only for being an object.

## Impact
commando is loaded as an important builtin plugin; its death (crash, or plugin_kill after it emits unparsable JSON) causes lightningd_exit(1), stopping the whole Lightning node — loss of channel monitoring and payment service until the operator restarts it. Out-of-bounds heap bytes may be copied into the RPC response, but that response goes only to the local caller, so no confidentiality impact accrues to the attacker.

## Reproduction steps
1. The local operator (or an application acting for them) runs the `commando` RPC against the attacker's node, which puts an outgoing command keyed by (peer, random id) in outgoing_commands and sends the id to that peer. The attacker, as the authenticated peer, replies over the Noise transport with COMMANDO_MSG_REPLY_TERM carrying {"id":<ours>,"result":[1,1,1,...]} (a long odd-length array). handle_reply matches peer+id and walks the array as an object, reading past the token array; the plugin segfaults or emits malformed JSON and is killed. The attacker needs no rune and need not run CLN; it only has to be the destination the operator consciously chose to query.

## Recommended fix
handle_reply() assumes the remote `result` is a JSON object and walks it with json_for_each_obj(), which for a JSMN_ARRAY reads token slots beyond the parsed datum and the token array, feeding garbage offsets and lengths into string copies and the response writer. Fix criteria: A reply whose `result` token is not JSMN_OBJECT must be rejected with COMMANDO_ERROR_LOCAL or copied verbatim as a single token (json_tok_full/json_tok_full_len of `result` itself) rather than iterated as an object; the iteration must never read tokens outside the `result` datum. Verify by replying to an outstanding commando request with result arrays of lengths 1, 2, 3 and 100001 and confirming the plugin survives, lightningd stays up, and the local caller receives an error or the verbatim array.
