# fetchinvoice dereferences NULL gmtime() on payee-chosen invoice_recurrence_basetime, killing lightningd

## Details
The payer side of BOLT12 (`fetchinvoice` in the `offers` plugin) trusts the `invoice_recurrence_basetime` field of the invoice returned by the remote payee. In `handle_invreq_response()` (plugins/fetchinvoice.c:313-348), when the offer carries `offer_recurrence_optional`/`offer_recurrence_compulsory`, the code calls `offer_period_start(*inv->invoice_recurrence_basetime, next_period_idx, recurrence)` and `offer_period_paywindow(...)` to report the next period to the RPC caller. For `time_unit` 1 (days) or 2 (months) — which the attacker chooses when publishing the offer — `offer_period_start()` calls `time_change()` (common/bolt12.c:449-473), which does `tm = *gmtime(&prev)` with `prev = (time_t)basetime` and no NULL check.

`invoice_recurrence_basetime` is a tu64 chosen by the payee. `invoice_matches_request()` only compares TLV ranges 0-159 and 1000000000-2999999999, so type 3000000177 is unconstrained, and the only check is presence (line 292). A value such as 0x8000000000000000 becomes a negative time_t whose year cannot be represented in `int`; glibc, musl and macOS libc all return NULL from gmtime() in that case. Dereferencing the NULL struct pointer segfaults the `offers` plugin. `offers` is a builtin plugin registered as `important` (lightningd/plugin.c:2578-2590), so lightningd shuts down.

Attack: the attacker publishes an offer with a day- or month-based recurrence (any amount, e.g. a cheap subscription). When the victim node runs `fetchinvoice offer=... recurrence_counter=0 recurrence_label=...`, the attacker's node answers the invoice_request over the reply path with an otherwise valid, correctly signed invoice whose `invoice_recurrence_basetime` is >= 2^63 (or anything above ~6.7e16). All earlier checks (field match, node_id, signature, presence) pass, and the victim's lightningd dies deterministically before the RPC response is finished.

The maintainers' own test (common/test/run-bolt12_period.c) only exercises sane basetimes, and the hook side (offers_invreq_hook.c) only ever uses basetimes we generated, which is why this NULL return was never considered. Assumption: gmtime() returns NULL rather than aborting for out-of-range time_t on the libc the release is built against (true for glibc >= 2.x, musl and Apple libc).

## Evidence
1. [common/bolt12.c:449–473](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L449-L473)
   time_change() does `tm = *gmtime(&prev)` with prev = (time_t)basetime and no NULL check. glibc (__offtime) and musl return NULL with EOVERFLOW when the computed year does not fit in int, i.e. for any |t| above ~6.7e16 seconds, including every u64 basetime >= 2^63 (negative as time_t). The struct copy through the NULL pointer is a SIGSEGV in the offers plugin.
2. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:313–347](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L313-L347)
   handle_invreq_response() passes *inv->invoice_recurrence_basetime, a field authored by the remote payee (TLV 3000000177 is invoice-only, so it is not covered by invoice_matches_request), straight into offer_period_start() and offer_period_paywindow(). For time_unit 1 (days) or 2 (months) these reach time_change().
3. [common/bolt12.c:475–491](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L475-L491)
   offer_period_start() dispatches to time_change() for time_unit 1 and 2; the recurrence itself is echoed from our own invoice_request, so the attacker only needs to publish a days- or months-based recurring offer.
4. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:286–295](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L286-L295)
   The only validation of invoice_recurrence_basetime is presence; no range check is applied before it is used as a time_t.

## Impact
SIGSEGV in the offers plugin, which is `important`: lightningd terminates, taking down all channels' off-chain operation until restarted (missed HTLC timeouts have on-chain consequences). No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning node that publishes a recurring BOLT12 offer with time_unit 1 (days) or 2 (months); the recurrence fields (TLV 1000000024/25) are echoed from the victim's own invoice_request and so pass invoice_matches_request. The victim operator (or wallet software) calls fetchinvoice on it with recurrence_counter/recurrence_label, which the RPC requires for recurring offers (fetchinvoice.c:984-1012). The attacker replies over the onion-message reply path with an otherwise valid, correctly signed invoice whose invoice_recurrence_basetime (TLV 3000000177, outside the compared ranges 0-159 and 1000000000-2999999999) is >= 2^63. All preceding checks (field match, node_id, signature, presence at line 292) pass and offer_period_start() -> time_change() dereferences the NULL gmtime() result deterministically. No credentials or race; the only requirement is the deliberate fetchinvoice call by the victim. Assumption: the release libc (glibc on debian:bookworm-slim Docker images, musl, Apple libc) returns NULL from gmtime() for a year that overflows int rather than aborting or clamping.

## Recommended fix
1. time_change() dereferences the result of gmtime() without checking for NULL, so any basetime whose year overflows int crashes the caller. Fix criteria: offer_period_start()/time_change() must return an error (e.g. 0 or a failure flag) instead of crashing when gmtime()/gmtime_r() fails; a unit test feeding basetime values such as 0x8000000000000000 and UINT64_MAX with time_unit 1 and 2 must not crash.
2. fetchinvoice accepts any payee-supplied invoice_recurrence_basetime and uses it as a time_t. Fix criteria: handle_invreq_response() must reject (badinv) an invoice whose invoice_recurrence_basetime is outside a sane range (e.g. not representable as a positive time_t / not within a few decades of invoice_created_at) before computing period boundaries; a malicious invoice with an absurd basetime must produce an RPC error, not a plugin exit.

# Malformed rune tokens logged at INFO by command_fail_badparam are readable by any rune permitting getlog (readonly shorthand)

## Details
Rune bearers are partially trusted: a rune bounds which methods a bearer may call, and the documented `readonly` shorthand (`method^list|method^get|method=summary` & `method/listdatastore`, lightningd/runes.c:439-473) is the sanctioned way to grant view-only access. `getlog` matches `method^get`, so every readonly bearer can dump the node's in-memory log book. The project's own position is that getlog must not serve runes: doc/schemas/getlog.json:26 and the comment at lightningd/log.c:1235-1238 withhold `level=io` precisely because io logs 'can contain secrets (such as runes)'. INFO and DEBUG are served.

However `command_fail_badparam()` (common/json_command.c:19-33) writes the *raw rejected token* into that same log book at LOG_INFORM: `Invalid parameter %s (%s): token '<full JSON token>'` via `command_log()` -> `log_(cmd->ld->log, ...)` (lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1401-1413), the lightningd logger over `ld->log_book` (lightningd.c:224-228). It deliberately removes the token from the RPC error ('see logs for details') because, as its comment records, an LNBITS deployment that wrapped a valid rune in an extra pair of quotes caused the error message to contain the rune itself; the fix moved the rune into the log on the assumption that the log is operator-only. `param_rune()` (runes.c:222-240) copies the token bytes raw (`json_strdup` does not unescape) and calls `command_fail_badparam` whenever `rune_from_base64()` fails, which it does on any non-urlsafe-base64 byte such as a quote. `logv()` (log.c:669-694) sanitizes only non-printable bytes (base64 survives) and `add_entry()`s the line into the 16 MiB ring buffer unconditionally, regardless of `--log-level`.

Deposit path: clnrest's `verify_rune` (plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs:30-31) inserts the HTTP `Rune` header verbatim as a JSON string into `checkrune`, so a client that sends `Rune: "<rune>"` (the LNBITS case) causes lightningd to log `token '"\"<rune>\""'` on every request until the client is fixed. Local RPC callers of checkrune/showrunes/createrune with a mangled rune do the same. Commando is *not* a deposit path: plugins/commando.c:407-412 pre-validates the peer's rune with `rune_from_base64n` and answers 'Invalid rune' itself, so a malformed peer rune never reaches `param_rune`.

Read path: any bearer of a rune allowing `getlog` -- commando (always on; any peer that can connect and holds the rune) or clnrest -- calls `getlog` (default level INFO; `param_getloglevel` blocks only io, log.c:1239-1262), receives the whole ring buffer (`json_getlog`, log.c:1264-1286), extracts the `Invalid parameter rune` lines, strips the stray characters, and holds the victim client's rune with whatever authority it carries (wallet integrations commonly use broad or unrestricted runes: pay, withdraw, close, stop). This is an escalation from the attacker's own rune scope to another principal's, around the rune bound the project ships.

Holds when some legitimate client has submitted a recoverable-but-malformed rune (via clnrest or the local socket) and the entry is still within the 16 MiB ring buffer.

## Evidence
1. [common/json\_command.c:19–32](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_command.c#L19-L32)
   command_fail_badparam(): outside --developer/check mode it hides the token from the RPC error ('see logs for details') but writes it verbatim at LOG_INFORM via command_log(): "Invalid parameter %s (%s): token '%.*s'" using json_tok_full (quotes included). The comment records the LNBITS incident in which the rejected 'rune' token contained a usable rune. This treats the log book as operator-only; it is not. Fix location.
2. [lightningd/runes.c:222–239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L222-L239)
   param_rune(): json_strdup copies the raw token bytes (no unescape) and rune_from_base64() (ccan/ccan/rune/coding.c:342-371, urlsafe base64, -1 on any invalid byte) fails on a stray quote or other non-base64 character; the full token is then passed to command_fail_badparam. Used by checkrune (p_req 'rune', line 1003), showrunes (405) and createrune (583).
3. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs:30–31](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs#L30-L31)
   verify_rune() inserts the HTTP 'Rune' header value verbatim as a JSON string into the checkrune request (rpc_params.insert("rune", json!(rune))). A client sending Rune: "<rune>" (quotes included, the LNBITS case) causes param_rune to fail and the quoted rune to be logged on every request. Deposit path.
4. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1401–1413](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L1401-L1413)
   command_log() formats the message and calls log_(cmd->ld->log, level, ...), the lightningd logger created over ld->log_book (lightningd/lightningd.c:224-228) -- the same log book json_getlog() dumps.
5. [lightningd/log.c:669–693](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L669-L693)
   logv() replaces only non-printable bytes with '?' (urlsafe base64 and quotes survive), then add_entry()s every message into the 16 MiB ring buffer (RING_BITS 24) regardless of the configured print level; maybe_print() only governs the file/stdout output.
6. [lightningd/runes.c:439–472](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L439-L472)
   readonly_restrictions(): method^list|method^get|method=summary AND method/listdatastore. 'getlog' matches method^get, so the documented readonly rune (doc/schemas/createrune.json:206-210: 'not listdatastore: that contains sensitive stuff!') grants getlog; only listdatastore was considered sensitive.
7. [lightningd/log.c:1235–1285](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L1235-L1285)
   param_getloglevel() refuses only level=io, its comment stating io 'can contain secrets (such as runes)' -- the project's own statement that getlog must not serve runes. json_getlog() defaults to LOG_INFORM and dumps every ring-buffer entry at or above that level via json_add_log()/log_to_json(), so the INFO badparam line (with the rune) is returned.
8. [plugins/commando.c:407–424](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L407-L424)
   Commando pre-validates the peer's rune with rune_from_base64n() and answers 'Invalid rune' itself, so commando is NOT a deposit path for malformed runes. It is the always-on read path: a peer holding a getlog-permitting rune has its request checked by checkrune (nodeid=peer, method=getlog) and executed via execute_command() with no method filtering.

## Impact
The harvested rune confers whatever authority the victim client's rune carries, around the rune bound the attacker was given. Wallet integrations of the LNBITS kind need pay/invoice at least and are commonly issued unrestricted runes; with such a rune the attacker reads all node state, moves funds (pay, withdraw, close) and can stop the node, so confidentiality, integrity and availability of the node are fully compromised relative to the read-only access the attacker started with. Impact is bounded by the victim rune's scope, which the attacker does not choose.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote bearer of a rune that permits getlog, e.g. the documented 'readonly' rune, reaching the node via commando (always on; any peer that can connect on 9735) or clnrest (if enabled). They call getlog (default INFO), receive the 16 MiB ring buffer, and extract 'JSON COMMAND checkrune: Invalid parameter rune ... token' lines, stripping the stray quote/characters to recover the victim's rune. Precondition outside attacker control (AT:P): some legitimate client must have submitted a recoverable-but-malformed rune through clnrest (header passed verbatim, shared.rs:30-31) or the local socket -- the scenario the code comment records happening with LNBITS -- and the entry must still be in the ring buffer (a misconfigured client re-deposits it on every request). Commando peers cannot deposit (commando.c:407-412 pre-validates). No user interaction; no defense to defeat beyond holding a low-privilege rune.

## Recommended fix
1. command_fail_badparam() writes the raw rejected token to the log book at INFO, and the log book is not operator-only: json_getlog() serves INFO/DEBUG entries to any rune bearer permitted getlog. For credential-bearing parameters (rune) the token is a secret. Fix criteria: Rejected parameter tokens must not be logged in recoverable form for secret-bearing parameters (at minimum 'rune'): omit or redact the token, log a hash, or log it only at a level getlog never serves (io). Verify: submit a quoted valid rune to checkrune via clnrest and via the socket, then call getlog at every served level with a readonly rune; no recoverable rune text appears in the result.
2. readonly_restrictions() and getlog treat the log book as non-sensitive although it accumulates data from every RPC caller and plugin; only listdatastore is excluded from the readonly shorthand, while the project's own getlog documentation acknowledges the log can hold runes. Fix criteria: Either exclude getlog from the readonly shorthand (method/getlog) and document it, or guarantee getlog never returns other principals' credentials (e.g. redact at log_to_json or at every secret-bearing log site). Verify: a readonly rune can no longer obtain, via getlog, any token logged from another caller's failed parameter validation.

# Peer-initiated RBF of a leased dual-funded channel silently drops lease fee and lease terms

## Details
Liquidity-ads lease terms are only negotiated in the initial open. As accepter/lessor, accepter_start() (openingd/dualopend.c:2698-2734) computes lease_fee via lease_rates_calc_fee(), adds it to accepter_funding so the opener must fund it (enforced in check_balances() by adding lease_fee to initiator_outs), sets lease_expiry = blockheight + 4032 and has hsmd sign the will_fund commitment. All of this lives in struct tx_state.

When the lessee later sends tx_init_rbf (any time before lock-in, at >= 25/24 of the previous funding feerate), rbf_remote_start() (dualopend.c:3751-3864) builds a fresh tx_state via new_tx_state() whose lease fields are all zero/NULL, copies only the channel configs, forwards state->requested_lease to lightningd and takes our contribution from got_rbf_offer_reply, then proceeds through rbf_wrap_up() ('/* FIXME: lease fee rate !? */') to accepter_commits(). It never recomputes the lease fee, never re-signs the will_fund commitment and never carries over lease_expiry or the fee caps. Consequences for the replacement funding transaction:
- check_balances() requires initiator_inputs >= opener_funding + 0: the opener no longer has to pay the lease fee it agreed to.
- The shipped funder's rbf_channel hook (plugins/funder.c:1055-1077) scans requested_lease_msat and, per CHANGELOG #5650 ('funder now honors lease requests across RBFs'), re-funds the leased amount; calculate_our_funding() (funder_policy.c:226-240) lets a non-zero requested_lease bypass the default leases_only=true skip that would otherwise give a non-lease open nothing. The hook response has no lease-rate field, so no plugin can re-price the fee.
- commit_ready carries lease_expiry 0 / lease_fee 0 / lease_commit_sig NULL; lightningd's wallet_update_channel() (dual_open_control.c:1319-1330) writes those onto the channel and the inflight without any lease check, and on confirmation peer_control.c:2495-2502 copies them from the inflight, so the live channel has no lease at all: no CSV lock, no lessor closing restriction, no lease_chan_max_* fee caps.

A lessee therefore obtains the lessor's leased liquidity without paying the negotiated lease fee simply by RBF-ing right after the first negotiation (an ordinary action the shipped funder auto-accepts on feerate alone). The project's own lessee-side code expects the lease contribution to persist across an RBF (rbf_local_start, dualopend.c:3706-3719 aborts if the lessor offers less than requested_lease), and doc/schemas/openchannel_bump.json only warns the bumper that it 'will lose the lease'; nothing in the code or docs sanctions the lessor giving the liquidity away for free. The victim is a node advertising liquidity ads via the funder plugin (--experimental-dual-fund with lease rates); the loss is the lease fee revenue it agreed to and the lease's contractual terms.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/dualopend.c:3751–3863](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3751-L3863)
   rbf_remote_start() (we are accepter/lessor): builds a fresh tx_state via new_tx_state(), takes opener_funding from the peer's tx_init_rbf TLV, forwards state->requested_lease to lightningd in dualopend_got_rbf_offer and takes accepter_funding from got_rbf_offer_reply, copying only localconf/remoteconf from the previous attempt. It never sets tx_state->rates, never calls lease_rates_calc_fee(), never adds a lease fee to accepter_funding and never carries over lease_expiry/lease_commit_sig/lease_chan_max_*. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [openingd/dualopend.c:126–146](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L126-L146)
   new_tx_state() initialises lease_expiry = 0, lease_fee = 0, lease_commit_sig = NULL, lease_chan_max_* = 0; the RBF tx_state keeps these blank values.
3. [openingd/dualopend.c:2698–2733](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2698-L2733)
   The control that exists only on the original open: accepter_start() computes lease_fee with lease_rates_calc_fee() for the requested lease at the funding feerate and adds it to accepter_funding, so the opener must pay it. No equivalent step exists on the RBF path.
4. [openingd/dualopend.c:896–911](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L896-L911)
   check_balances() adds tx_state->lease_fee to initiator_outs; with lease_fee = 0 in the RBF the opener's inputs only have to cover opener_funding, so the negotiated fee is no longer required of the lessee.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:3556–3565](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3556-L3565)
   rbf_wrap_up(): '/* FIXME: lease fee rate !? */' immediately before accepter_commits() is invoked with the lease-less tx_state, acknowledging the fee is not handled.
6. [openingd/dualopend.c:2340–2355](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2340-L2355)
   accepter_commits() reports lease_expiry = 0, lease_fee = 0, lease_commit_sig = NULL and chan_max = 0 to lightningd in dualopend_commit_ready for the RBF candidate, while still reporting requested_lease.
7. [plugins/funder.c:1055–1076](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L1055-L1076)
   Shipped funder's rbf_channel hook scans requested_lease_msat ('FIXME: blockheights??'), accepts on feerate alone and re-funds from the previous UTXOs; it treats the RBF as a lease request (CHANGELOG: 'funder now honors lease requests across RBFs', #5650) and never refuses or re-prices it. The rbf_channel hook response has no lease-rates field, so no plugin can re-price either.
8. [plugins/funder\_policy.c:226–239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder_policy.c#L226-L239)
   calculate_our_funding(): with the default leases_only = true a non-lease open gets zero contribution, but a non-zero requested_lease (as passed for the RBF) bypasses that skip and the fund_probability skip, so the lessor contributes the leased amount to the fee-less replacement.
9. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1319–1329](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1319-L1329)
   wallet_update_channel() (RBF commit_ready path): channel->push = 0, lease_expiry = 0, lease_commit_sig = NULL, lease_chan_max_* = 0 are written onto the channel and the new inflight; lightningd performs no lease check of its own.
10. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2495–2501](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2495-L2501)
   On promotion of the confirmed inflight the channel's lease fields are copied from it, so the live channel has lease_expiry 0: no lease CSV, no closing restriction (closing_control.c:759-766 only blocks the lessor while lease_expiry is in the future), no fee caps.

## Impact
Financial integrity of the lessor: the negotiated lease fee (default 2000 sat base + 0.65% of the leased amount + funding weight fee) is never collected and the lease terms (expiry, fee caps, will_fund signature) are lost, so the lessor's capital is committed under terms it did not agree to. Principal is not at risk (the lessor can close at any time since lease_expiry is 0), so integrity impact is LOW. No confidentiality or availability effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote peer who opens a leased dual-funded channel with a node advertising liquidity ads, completes the first negotiation (exchanging tx_sigs), then sends tx_init_rbf with feerate >= 25/24 of the last (within the lessor's feerate_min/max) re-adding at least one of its inputs. The shipped funder accepts on feerate alone and re-contributes the leased amount; dualopend charges no fee. No defence to bypass, no race, no user interaction; the only condition is that the victim offers leases, which is the feature under attack rather than a separate deployment requirement.

## Recommended fix
1. rbf_remote_start() constructs the replacement tx_state without the lease negotiated in the original open and without any way to re-derive it, while lightningd and the funder keep honouring the lease request. Fix criteria: An RBF of a leased channel as lessor must either (a) carry forward the lease (rates, lease_expiry, lease_chan_max_*, a will_fund signature for the new attempt) and recompute lease_fee with the same rates at the new funding feerate, adding it to accepter_funding so check_balances() requires the opener to fund it, or (b) refuse the RBF (or contribute nothing) whenever requested_lease is set. Verify: after a peer RBF of a leased open, the opener's inputs must still cover the lease fee and the confirmed channel retains a non-zero lease_expiry and lease_commit_sig.
2. The shipped funder plugin treats the rbf_channel hook's requested_lease_msat as a lease to honour without any means (in the hook response) to attach lease rates or confirm a fee will be charged. Fix criteria: Either the rbf_channel hook response carries lease rates that lightningd forwards to dualopend for fee calculation, or the funder rejects RBFs that carry requested_lease_msat until dualopend enforces the fee. Verify: with leases_only=true the lessor never contributes to a fee-less replacement.

# sql plugin runs caller's SELECT with no execution-time or result-size bound

## Details
plugins/sql.c is the project's read-only query surface for partially-trusted callers: the manpage (doc/schemas/sql-template.json) advertises it 'for remote access', an authorizer restricts statements to SELECT over the exported tables, and sqlite_setup() (sql.c:275-292) applies sqlite3_limit() caps explicitly citing SQLite's guidance for 'SQL from untrusted sources'. Those caps bound the compiled statement, not its execution. refresh_complete() (sql.c:460-513) then runs the statement synchronously on the plugin's single thread:

    while ((err = sqlite3_step(dbq->stmt)) == SQLITE_ROW) { ... json_add_...(ret, ...) ... }

There is no sqlite3_progress_handler(), no sqlite3_interrupt() path, no cap on rows or output bytes, and no yield back to the event loop. The whole result is accumulated in the `ret` json_stream in memory and only handed to the output queue after the loop finishes (libplugin.c:470-475).

A caller permitted to run `sql` can therefore submit one query whose cost is polynomial in table size and whose output is unbounded, e.g.

    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channels a, channels b, channels c;
    SELECT a.*, b.* FROM nodes a, nodes b, nodes c;

The channels/nodes tables are populated from public gossip (tens of thousands of rows on mainnet), so a three-way cartesian product is 10^12-10^15 rows. The authorizer approves it (SELECT + READ of known tables + count), SQLITE_LIMIT_VDBE_OP=1000 constrains only program length (such a join compiles to a few dozen ops), and SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH constrains only a single value. SQLITE_RECURSIVE is denied, but that is incidental; ordinary joins suffice.

Two outcomes:
- COUNT variant: the plugin spins indefinitely. lightningd has no runtime watchdog for plugins (only PLUGIN_STARTUP_TIMEOUT), so the sql plugin stays wedged: every `sql`/`listsqlschemas` request from any caller (including the operator) hangs forever and the plugin stops consuming the `wait` responses that keep its tables current.
- Projecting variant: `ret` grows without bound until the process is OOM-killed (or tal aborts on allocation failure). sql is a builtin plugin on every sqlite3 build (plugins/Makefile:141-142) and builtins are registered `important` (plugin.c:2578-2586); on an important plugin's death lightningd calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1) (plugin.c:297-303). A single permitted request thus shuts down the entire node.

Who is the attacker: a rune holder whose rune permits `method=sql` (via commando from a remote peer, or via clnrest). Such a rune is documented as granting bounded read-only query access; the project explicitly guards this surface against untrusted SQL, and nothing in the sql, createrune or commando documentation concedes the ability to wedge the plugin or stop the node. The operator is trusted and out of scope.

This is a single-request algorithmic-complexity / unbounded-allocation availability defect, not request flooding; a `rate=` rune restriction does not mitigate it because one request suffices.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/sql.c:460–512](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/sql.c#L460-L512)
   refresh_complete() loops sqlite3_step() until SQLITE_DONE on the plugin's single thread, appending every row to the in-memory `ret` json_stream; there is no row cap, byte cap, step budget, time check or yield to the event loop.
2. [plugins/sql.c:275–292](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/sql.c#L275-L292)
   sqlite_setup() quotes SQLite's guidance for 'SQL from untrusted sources' and installs sqlite3_limit() caps (SQL length, columns, expression depth, VDBE program size, ...). These bound the compiled statement only; no sqlite3_progress_handler() or sqlite3_interrupt() path bounds execution, so a small program (a multi-way cartesian join) runs unboundedly.
3. [plugins/sql.c:331–382](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/sql.c#L331-L382)
   sqlite_authorize() approves SQLITE_SELECT and SQLITE_READ on any exported table and the listed functions (including count); it has no notion of query cost. Only SQLITE_RECURSIVE is incidentally denied; ordinary joins such as `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channels a, channels b, channels c` or `SELECT a.*, b.* FROM nodes a, nodes b, nodes c` pass.
4. [plugins/sql.c:1436–1453](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/sql.c#L1436-L1453)
   json_sql() prepares the caller-supplied query under the authorizer, then refresh_tables() -> refresh_complete() executes it; the query string is the `query` parameter of the `sql` RPC, reachable by any rune holder permitted that method (commando from a remote peer, or clnrest).
5. [plugins/libplugin.c:470–475](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin.c#L470-L475)
   The result json_stream is handed to the output list (ld_send) only in command_complete_nojson(), i.e. after refresh_complete() returns; nothing is flushed while the loop runs, so the projected cartesian product accumulates entirely in process memory until the plugin is OOM-killed (or tal aborts on allocation failure).
6. [plugins/Makefile:141–142](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/Makefile#L141-L142)
   sql is a builtin plugin on every sqlite3 build, and plugins_set_builtin_plugins_dir() registers every builtin except cln-renepay as `important`.
7. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–303](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L303)
   When an important plugin dies, lightningd logs 'shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1). An OOM-killed sql plugin therefore takes the whole node down; a CPU-spinning one is never detected (the only plugin timeout is PLUGIN_STARTUP_TIMEOUT) and wedges the sql service indefinitely.

## Impact
The projecting variant grows the in-memory result until the sql plugin is OOM-killed; because sql is a builtin `important` plugin, lightningd then calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1) (plugin.c:297-303) and the whole node stops, with the on-chain consequences the threat model attaches to a node crash. The COUNT variant wedges the sql plugin permanently (no runtime plugin watchdog), denying the sql service to every caller including the operator. No data is read or changed beyond what the rune already permits.

## Reproduction steps
1. A caller permitted the `sql` method (rune holder over commando from any connected peer, or an HTTPS client of clnrest) submits one SELECT joining the large exported gossip tables with no WHERE clause. The authorizer approves it, the tables are refreshed, and refresh_complete() steps the cartesian product synchronously until the plugin either spins indefinitely (COUNT) or exhausts memory (projection). Deterministic, no race, default configuration (commando always on, sql builtin on sqlite3 builds).

## Recommended fix
1. The sql plugin bounds the compiled statement (sqlite3_limit) but not its execution or output: refresh_complete() steps an untrusted SELECT to completion synchronously on the single plugin thread and buffers every row in memory before sending anything. Fix criteria: A single `sql` request must not be able to monopolize the plugin or grow its memory without bound: install a sqlite3_progress_handler() (or equivalent step/time budget) that aborts long-running statements with an RPC error, and enforce a cap on rows or serialized bytes returned (failing the request when exceeded). Verify that a three-way cartesian join over the channels table returns an error within a bounded time while the plugin keeps serving other requests and its RSS stays bounded.
2. A resource-exhaustion failure of the sql plugin is escalated to a full node shutdown because the plugin is registered `important` while serving partially-trusted (rune-holder) input. Fix criteria: Either the sql plugin's execution is bounded as above so a caller cannot drive it to OOM, or the death of the sql plugin on caller input no longer terminates lightningd (e.g. restart or non-important registration); the project should confirm that a rune permitting `method=sql` cannot be used to stop the node.

# Splice-out skips reserve and opener fee-affordability check, letting remote opener brick channel

## Details
check_balances() (channeld/channeld.c) validates a peer-initiated splice by requiring only that the initiator's post-splice channel balance is not negative: `amount_msat_can_add_sat_s64(in[TX_INITIATOR], opener_relative)`. Neither side's channel_reserve nor the opener's commitment-fee obligation is applied to the post-splice balances; the splice spec's rule ('MUST fail the negotiation if the balance for that side is less than 1% of the total channel capacity') is quoted and left as a DTODO. splice_accepter() takes relative_satoshis straight from the peer's splice_init, sets accepter_relative = 0 with no plugin hook, and lightningd's handle_add_inflight stores the inflight without any amount check.

Every other path that could lower a balance (update_add_htlc, update_fee) is gated by full_channel.c's reserve and fee-affordability checks; the splice path goes around them. The consequence matters when the remote peer is the channel opener (channel->opener == REMOTE, i.e. every inbound channel): the opener pays the commitment fee and anchors. A remote opener can splice_init with relative_satoshis = -(its whole balance) (or anything leaving less than base_fee + 660 + reserve), contribute an input for the on-chain fee and an output to itself, and our node completes the splice.

Two defects follow. (1) The inflight commitments are built by commit_tx() with the opener at 0: the return value of try_subtract_fee() is ignored, so the fee is silently zeroed, and the anchor outputs are added regardless; for an anchor channel our to_local (Y) plus a 330-sat anchor exceeds the new funding (Y), i.e. both sides sign a commitment whose outputs exceed its input (bitcoin_tx_check is serialization-only); for a non-anchor channel the commitment carries zero fee. No valid unilateral close exists for the new funding, so our balance is held hostage to the peer's cooperation. (2) At mutual splice_locked, channel_update_funding() applies remote_splice_amnt and view[LOCAL].owed[REMOTE] becomes 0. The next commitment_signed from the peer (even an empty one) reaches `assert(can_opener_afford_feerate(...))` in handle_peer_commit_sig, which requires the opener's balance to be at least fee + 660 + reserve, so channeld aborts. lightningd treats the subdaemon death as transient (channel_fail_transient), reconnects, and the peer can repeat it at will, leaving the channel permanently unusable.

When we are the opener, the same gap only drops the peer to the zero-balance state a single-funded fundee already starts in, which the protocol sanctions; the penalty-deterrent argument carries no gain there because no revoked state with a higher peer balance exists on the new funding output and later HTLC sends remain reserve-bounded.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/channeld.c:3561–3578](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3561-L3578)
   The only bound on the initiator's splice-out is amount_msat_can_add_sat_s64(in[TX_INITIATOR], opener_relative): post-splice balance >= 0. Neither channel_reserve nor the opener's fee + anchor obligation is enforced. This is where the fix must go.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:3806–3833](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3806-L3833)
   The spec rule (fail if a side's post-splice balance is below 1% of capacity) is quoted and explicitly left as 'DTODO: Spec out reserve requirements for splices'; no floor is applied.
3. [channeld/channeld.c:4436–4437](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4436-L4437)
   splice_accepter() uses the peer's relative_satoshis as opener_relative, sets accepter_relative = 0 with no plugin hook or lightningd gate; the only validation of the amount is check_balances at line 4501.
4. [channeld/channeld.c:2199–2206](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L2199-L2206)
   handle_peer_commit_sig asserts can_opener_afford_feerate() unconditionally on every peer commitment_signed when channel->opener == REMOTE ('We were supposed to check this was affordable as we go'); after a splice-out to zero this assert fails and channeld aborts.
5. [channeld/full\_channel.c:1342–1411](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L1342-L1411)
   can_opener_afford_feerate() requires view[!opener].owed[opener] (after HTLC adjustments) to be >= commit fee + 660 (anchors) + channel_reserve; with the remote opener spliced out to 0 it returns false.
6. [channeld/channeld.c:513–515](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L513-L515)
   At mutual splice_locked, channel_update_funding() applies the inflight's remote_splice_amnt to view[*].owed[REMOTE], making the remote opener's balance 0 for all subsequent commitment handling.
7. [channeld/commit\_tx.c:195](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/commit_tx.c#L195)
   The return value of try_subtract_fee() is ignored: when the opener cannot pay base_fee (+660), its output is zeroed and the commitment fee silently collapses to whatever remained (zero).
8. [channeld/commit\_tx.c:376–389](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/commit_tx.c#L376-L389)
   Anchor outputs (330 sat each) are added whenever to_local/to_remote exists, without checking against funding_sats; with the opener at 0 the outputs exceed the funding input, so both sides sign an invalid commitment for the new funding (bitcoin_tx_check at line 458 only round-trips serialization).
9. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:641–645](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L641-L645)
   A channeld crash (no peer_fd) is handled as channel_fail_transient: lightningd reconnects and the peer can trip the assert again on every reconnect, so the channel is permanently unusable rather than force-closed.

## Impact
Availability HIGH: channeld hits assert(can_opener_afford_feerate) on every subsequent peer commitment_signed, lightningd only reconnects, so the channel is permanently unusable; and the post-splice commitment transactions have zero fee (non-anchor) or outputs exceeding the funding input (anchor), so the victim cannot unilaterally close and its balance stays locked until the peer cooperates. Integrity LOW: the node signs and persists commitment state it cannot enforce on-chain. No confidentiality impact. Assumptions: a zero-fee non-TRUC commitment is rejected by Bitcoin Core default relay policy; hsmd does not independently verify commitment output sums (not read here).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer that opened a channel to the victim (channel->opener == REMOTE; any inbound channel). Splicing is on by default (option_splice advertised). After stfu it sends splice_init with relative_satoshis = -(its balance), adds an input for the on-chain fee and an output to itself; check_balances accepts (post-splice balance 0 >= 0), commitments are exchanged, the splice tx confirms and splice_locked is exchanged. Then any commitment_signed it sends aborts channeld, and no valid unilateral-close transaction exists for the new funding. Requires the attacker-funded channel and a confirmed splice tx (AT:P); no victim action.

## Recommended fix
1. check_balances() bounds a side's splice-out only by a non-negative post-splice balance; the channel reserve (and the splice spec's 1%-of-capacity floor) is never applied, so a peer can leave itself with nothing in the channel. Fix criteria: A splice that would leave a side that is withdrawing funds below its channel_reserve (or the spec's 1%-of-new-capacity floor) is refused via tx_abort before any commitment is signed; a remote splice_init with relative_satoshis = -balance is rejected and the channel continues normally.
2. The opener's obligation to pay the commitment fee and anchors is enforced on update_add_htlc and update_fee but not on splices, so a remote opener can splice out below base_fee + 660 + reserve, producing unenforceable commitments and tripping the commitment_signed assert. Fix criteria: The post-splice balance of the channel opener must cover the commitment fee at the current feerate (plus anchors) in addition to its reserve, mirroring full_channel.c's affordability checks; verify can_opener_afford_feerate() holds immediately after splice_locked for any accepted splice, and that a remote-opener splice-out leaving less than fee + anchors + reserve is tx_abort'ed.
3. handle_peer_commit_sig treats an unaffordable opener as an internal invariant (assert) and commit_tx() silently ignores try_subtract_fee() failure, so a state the peer can reach aborts channeld or yields an invalid commitment instead of a protocol failure. Fix criteria: An opener balance below fee + anchors + reserve at commitment time is handled as a peer protocol error (channel failed with an error message), never an abort or a silently zero-fee/over-committed transaction; verify that commit_tx construction rejects a commitment whose outputs would exceed funding_sats.

# Peer-supplied tx_signatures txid overwrites splice inflight outpoint, corrupting stored commitment tx

## Details
resume_splice_negotiation() in channeld/channeld.c parses the peer's `tx_signatures` with `fromwire_tx_signatures(tmpctx, msg, &cid, &inflight->outpoint.txid, ...)` (4099-4106), so the peer-authored `txid` field is written directly into the in-memory inflight record that identifies the pending splice's funding outpoint. The locally computed txid (`final_txid`, `psbt_txid()` at 4043) is never compared with it; openingd/dualopend.c:1412 performs exactly this comparison for dual-funding and fails on mismatch, channeld does not. The in-tree hsmd does not check which outpoint a commitment spends (libhsmd.c handle_sign_remote_commitment_tx only requires one input), and nothing downstream re-derives the outpoint from the PSBT.

Everything in channeld that identifies the inflight by txid then follows the attacker's value: send_commit() signs our commitment_signed for the inflight on `inflights[i]->outpoint` (1577-1600); commit_index_from_msg() (2443) routes an incoming commitment_signed whose `funding_txid` TLV equals the bogus txid to that inflight; handle_peer_commit_sig() builds our local commitment from the same corrupted outpoint and only checks the TLV matches it (2215-2248), so the peer's signature over that garbage transaction verifies. The accepted commitsig is forwarded to lightningd in channeld_got_commitsig, where peer_got_commitsig() stores it as inflight->last_tx/last_sig purely by list position (peer_htlcs.c:2617-2623) and wallet_inflight_save() persists it. handle_funding_depth() (6450-6490) matches the real splice txid against the corrupted field, finds no inflight and ignores the confirmation, so the corrupted session never locks.

lightningd's own inflight record stays correct (handle_splice_confirmed_signed / handle_update_inflight key it by the PSBT txid), so after a reconnect the new channeld is initialised with the correct outpoint but the stored garbage last_tx (channel_control.c:1942-1965); last_tx is set and remote_tx_sigs is true, so no splice resume happens (channeld.c:5869). splice_depth_cb then delivers the real txid, splice_locked is exchanged, and update_channel_from_inflight() promotes inflight->last_tx to channel->last_tx (peer_control.c:2509). drop_to_chain() signs and broadcasts channel->last_tx / inflight->last_tx (peer_control.c:475-510): the only non-revoked commitment we hold for the new funding spends a non-existent outpoint and cannot be relayed, so the node cannot unilaterally close or enforce HTLC timeouts until the peer chooses to send another commitment_signed.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/channeld.c:4099–4106](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4099-L4106)
   fromwire_tx_signatures() is given &inflight->outpoint.txid as the destination for the peer's txid field, so the remote peer's value replaces the locally computed splice funding txid. The local value (final_txid, psbt_txid() at 4043) is never compared with it, unlike openingd/dualopend.c:1412.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:2215–2248](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L2215-L2248)
   handle_peer_commit_sig() for commit_index>0 builds our local commitment from inflights[commit_index-1]->outpoint (now attacker-chosen) and only checks the peer's funding_txid TLV equals that same corrupted value, so the attacker's signature over the garbage transaction verifies and is accepted.
3. [channeld/channeld.c:2443–2466](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L2443-L2466)
   commit_index_from_msg() routes an incoming commitment_signed to an inflight by comparing its funding_txid TLV with inflights[i]->outpoint.txid, so the attacker labels its batched commitment_signed with the bogus txid to reach the inflight path.
4. [channeld/channeld.c:1577–1600](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L1577-L1600)
   send_commit() signs and sends our commitment_signed for each inflight using inflights[i]->outpoint, so our hsmd signs commitments on the attacker-chosen outpoint for every subsequent state update in the session.
5. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1666–1674](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1666-L1674)
   The in-tree hsmd's handle_sign_remote_commitment_tx only checks the tx has one input and some outputs; it does not verify the input is the channel's funding outpoint, so it provides no protection against signing a commitment on a bogus outpoint.
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2609–2626](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2609-L2626)
   peer_got_commitsig() stores inflight_commit_sigs[i]->tx as inflight->last_tx purely by list position and persists it via wallet_inflight_save(), never checking that the tx spends inflight->funding->outpoint.
7. [channeld/channeld.c:6450–6489](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6450-L6489)
   handle_funding_depth() matches lightningd's splice confirmation (real txid) against inflight->outpoint.txid; with the corrupted value no inflight matches and the depth notification is ignored, so the corrupted session never sends splice_locked.
8. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1942–1964](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1942-L1964)
   On reconnect lightningd initialises the fresh channeld from its own inflight record: the correct outpoint (kept correct because lightningd keys inflights by PSBT txid) together with the stored garbage last_tx, and remote_tx_sigs=true, so no splice resume occurs and lock proceeds on the real txid.
9. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2509–2512](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2509-L2512)
   On splice lock, update_channel_from_inflight() promotes inflight->last_tx to channel->last_tx with no check that it spends the new funding outpoint.
10. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:475–509](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L475-L509)
   drop_to_chain() signs and broadcasts channel->last_tx and every inflight->last_tx for a unilateral close; after lock the only non-revoked commitment is the garbage one, which cannot be relayed.

## Impact
Integrity: persisted channel state (inflight last_tx, then channel->last_tx) is replaced by an attacker-shaped transaction spending a non-existent outpoint, and hsmd is driven to sign commitments on an attacker-chosen outpoint. Availability: after lock the node holds no broadcastable commitment for the live funding, so it cannot unilaterally close or enforce HTLC deadlines on that channel; the balance stays locked for as long as the peer withholds a further commitment_signed. In-session the splice lock is also silently ignored. Confidentiality unaffected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer sharing a channel with the victim (an existing channel is the only precondition; no credential or privilege is granted). Splicing is enabled by default (lightningd/options.c:1270), so the peer can stfu+splice_init itself. At the final step it sends tx_signatures with its valid shared_input_signature but an arbitrary txid X, then drives one more commitment round in the same session (e.g. one update_add_htlc) whose inflight commitment_signed carries funding_txid X; our revoke_and_ack revokes the last valid inflight commitment. The splice tx confirms, the peer reconnects, splice_locked is exchanged, then it stops updating. No shipped control is bypassed.

## Recommended fix
1. channeld writes the peer's tx_signatures.txid directly into inflight->outpoint.txid instead of parsing into a local variable and comparing it with the txid computed from the negotiated PSBT. Fix criteria: A tx_signatures whose txid differs from the locally computed splice txid must be rejected (warn/disconnect) and must not modify any inflight state; after the fix, sending a bogus txid leaves inflight->outpoint unchanged and no commitment is ever built or signed on an outpoint other than the one derived from the PSBT.
2. lightningd stores inflight commitment transactions by list position without checking the transaction's sole input is the inflight's funding outpoint, so a corrupted channeld state propagates into the DB and into channel->last_tx on lock. Fix criteria: peer_got_commitsig()/update_inflight paths must verify each stored inflight tx spends exactly inflight->funding->outpoint (and update_channel_from_inflight must refuse to promote a last_tx that does not spend the new funding), failing the channel loudly rather than persisting an unbroadcastable commitment.

# Dual-funding never bounds peer dust_limit, letting peer's commitment tx trim our whole balance

## Details
dualopend accepts whatever `dust_limit_satoshis` the remote peer puts in open_channel2 (accepter role, dualopend.c:2483) or accept_channel2 (opener role, dualopend.c:3176) without any upper bound. The only parameter validation, check_config_bounds() in openingd/common.c, never reads remoteconf->dust_limit; set_reserve() derives both reserves from max(1% of total, the *opener's* dust_limit), so as opener we never compare the accepter's dust_limit to anything, and as accepter the opener's dust_limit simply becomes the reserve (so the v1 rule 'dust_limit <= reserve' is vacuous). lightningd's dual_open_control.c only forwards dust_limit_msat in the openchannel2 hook payload and the shipped funder plugin does not even parse it. The v1 sibling openingd.c (448-457, 996-1005) rejects remoteconf.dust_limit > our channel_reserve; dualopend has no equivalent in either role or on RBF (remoteconf is copied forward).

The peer's dust_limit is the trim threshold of *their* commitment transaction: new_initial_channel() stores it as config[REMOTE], initial_channel_tx(..., REMOTE, ...) passes config[side].dust_limit, and initial_commit_tx() omits to_remote (our balance) whenever other_pay < dust_limit, the amount becoming miner fee. Its only guard fails only if *both* to_local and to_remote are <= reserve. msg_for_remote_commit() builds that transaction and has hsmd sign it (hsmd checks only 1 input and > 0 outputs), and the signature is sent in commitment_signed before tx_signatures, after which the funding tx is broadcastable.

Attack, we are opener funding F: attacker accepts contributing A and sets dust_limit D with F - commit_fee - 660 < D <= A (so the attacker must lock up at least roughly our contribution, which it recovers via its own to_local). Our to_remote on their commitment is trimmed; their to_local stays; the reserve guard passes because A > reserve. check_balances()'s is_dust() only requires every funding-tx output to be >= D, satisfied by the funding output (F+A) and by our change if it is >= D or absent.

Attack, we are accepter contributing Y (funder policy or liquidity lease): attacker opens with X and sets D with Y < D <= X - commit_fee - 660; set_reserve makes reserve = D and check_config_bounds passes while X + Y - 2D - 660 - fee >= min-capacity. Our Y is trimmed from their commitment.

Result: once the funding tx confirms the peer holds a valid, fully signed commitment transaction in which our entire contribution is miner fee and can broadcast it at any time (or hand it to a miner for the fee); because channeld keeps the same remoteconf, every later remote commitment also omits our balance until it exceeds D. Total loss of our funding contribution to a dual-funded channel with a malicious peer, in either role. Holds whenever the node runs with --experimental-dual-fund and contributes funds to a v2 channel.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/dualopend.c:675–699](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L675-L699)
   set_reserve() derives both sides' channel_reserve from max(1% of total, the *opener's* dust_limit) only. As opener the accepter's dust_limit (remoteconf) is never compared to the reserve or anything else; as accepter the opener's dust_limit simply becomes the reserve, so 'dust_limit <= reserve' can never fail. The missing bound belongs here / right after this call in both roles (as openingd.c:990-1005 does for v1).
2. [openingd/common.c:16–168](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/common.c#L16-L168)
   check_config_bounds(), the only parameter validation dualopend runs on remoteconf, never reads remoteconf->dust_limit (neither against the reserve nor against an absolute maximum).
3. [openingd/dualopend.c:3174–3199](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3174-L3199)
   opener_start(): the peer's accept_channel2 dust_limit_satoshis is parsed straight into tx_state->remoteconf.dust_limit and then only passed to set_reserve()/check_config_bounds().
4. [openingd/dualopend.c:2478–2499](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2478-L2499)
   accepter_start(): same for open_channel2; the value is forwarded to lightningd's openchannel2 hook payload (dual_open_control.c:293) but neither lightningd nor the funder plugin bounds it.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:1165–1224](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1165-L1224)
   msg_for_remote_commit() builds the REMOTE commitment with initial_channel_tx(..., REMOTE, ...) and has hsmd sign it; the signature is handed to the peer in commitment_signed (opener_commits 2979-3012, accepter_commits 2363-2368) before tx_signatures.
6. [common/initial\_channel.c:122–134](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/initial_channel.c#L122-L134)
   initial_channel_tx() passes channel->config[side].dust_limit, i.e. the peer's own unbounded dust_limit, when building the peer's commitment transaction.
7. [common/initial\_commit\_tx.c:227–263](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/initial_commit_tx.c#L227-L263)
   to_remote (our balance on their commitment) is omitted entirely when other_pay < dust_limit; the value becomes miner fee. The only guard (lines 160-182) fails only if *both* to_local and to_remote are <= reserve, so our side alone being trimmed passes.
8. [openingd/dualopend.c:639–644](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L639-L644)
   is_dust() in check_balances() (used at 845 and 933) is the only effective constraint on the peer's dust_limit: every funding-tx output must be >= it. This still admits dust_limit in (our_commitment_balance, their_commitment_balance], because our commitment balance is our contribution minus (as opener) commitment fee and 660 sat anchors.
9. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1668–1674](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1668-L1674)
   handle_sign_remote_commitment_tx() sanity checks only num_inputs == 1 and num_outputs > 0; a remote commitment with only their to_local + anchor passes and is signed.
10. [plugins/funder.c:784–859](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L784-L859)
   The shipped funder plugin's openchannel2 handler does not scan dust_limit_msat at all; it contributes per policy regardless of the peer's dust_limit.
11. [openingd/openingd.c:448–456](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/openingd.c#L448-L456)
   The v1 sibling rejects remoteconf.dust_limit > our channel_reserve (and again at 996-1005). dualopend has no equivalent check in either role.

## Impact
Our entire funding contribution becomes miner fee in a commitment transaction we have signed and the peer can broadcast once funding confirms: direct, irreversible loss of funds (integrity HIGH). No confidentiality impact; the channel otherwise operates, so availability NONE.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote peer (authenticated only by the Noise handshake) sets dust_limit_satoshis in open_channel2 or accept_channel2. The attack needs the victim to contribute funds to a v2 channel with the attacker (operator opens or requests a lease from the attacker, or the funder plugin auto-contributes as accepter) and the attacker to lock up at least about as much capital as the victim's contribution, which it recovers via its own to_local output; these conditions beyond the attacker's control give AT:PRESENT. No defence has to be defeated: the value flows straight to the commitment builder and our signature is produced automatically; the only constraint (is_dust on funding-tx outputs) is satisfied by choosing dust_limit just above our commitment balance. In the accepter role no operator action is required (UI:NONE).

## Recommended fix
1. dualopend (opener_start/accepter_start via set_reserve and check_config_bounds) never bounds the remote dust_limit, so the peer can choose a trim threshold above our balance on their commitment transaction and we sign it. Fix criteria: Both roles must reject open_channel2/accept_channel2 whose dust_limit_satoshis exceeds the computed channel_reserve (as v1 does) and/or a sane absolute maximum, before any commitment is signed; the bound must also hold for the remoteconf carried into RBF. Verify: a peer offering dust_limit above our commitment balance is refused in both opener and accepter roles and the negotiation ends with tx_abort/error rather than a signed commitment.
2. The remote commitment is signed without any check that our own balance appears as an output when it exceeds our reserve. Fix criteria: Before signing a remote commitment at open, dualopend (or initial_commit_tx's guard) refuses to sign a transaction that trims our to_remote while our balance exceeds the channel reserve.

# Opener HTLC affordability check ignores pending update_fee, letting peer trip channeld assert

## Details
channeld's admission check for an HTLC offered by the remote channel opener (full_channel.c add_htlc, lines 785-822) verifies that the opener can still pay the commitment fee, but prices it with fee_for_htlcs() -> channel_feerate(channel, recipient=LOCAL) -> get_feerate() (fee_states.c:56-73), which returns only a feerate whose state carries HTLC_LOCAL_F_COMMITTED. An update_fee the peer has already sent but that we have not yet received commitment_signed for sits at RCVD_ADD_HTLC (LOCAL_F_PENDING only, htlc_state.c), so it is invisible and the HTLC is priced at the old, lower rate. Conversely, handle_peer_feechange (channeld.c:815-831) -> channel_update_feerate() validated the new rate only against the HTLC set present when update_fee arrived (it does include pending HTLCs, so the reverse ordering is caught; only update_fee-before-update_add_htlc slips through).

Sequence by a malicious remote opener:
1. update_fee(F_new > F_old) inside our accepted range; can_opener_afford_feerate(F_new) passes for the current HTLC set.
2. update_add_htlc with amount A chosen so that opener_balance - A - reserve - 660 (anchors) >= fee(F_old, n+1) but < fee(F_new, n+1). add_htlc accepts (it prices at F_old). For a non-dust HTLC the window is (F_new - F_old) * commit_weight / 1000 sat, trivially large.
3. commitment_signed. handle_peer_commit_sig() calls channel_rcvd_commit() -> change_htlcs() -> fee_incstate(), which moves both the HTLC and the feerate from RCVD_ADD_HTLC to RCVD_ADD_COMMIT (LOCAL_F_COMMITTED). Immediately after, it executes assert(can_opener_afford_feerate(channel, channel_feerate(LOCAL))) (channeld.c:2199-2206) — the same quantity (view[LOCAL].owed[REMOTE] - adding + removing vs fee + 660 + config[LOCAL].channel_reserve) now evaluated at F_new with the extra output — which is false. Asserts are compiled in (no NDEBUG), so abort() kills channeld with SIGABRT.

lightningd handles the death in subd.c destroy_subd() -> channel_errmsg() with peer_fd == NULL -> channel_fail_transient(): the channel is not force-closed, it simply waits for a reconnect. Because we never sent revoke_and_ack nor persisted the commitment, the peer retransmits the same update_fee/update_add_htlc/commitment_signed after channel_reestablish and channeld aborts again on every reconnection, leaving the channel wedged (no forwards, no settlement of new HTLCs) until the operator force-closes it. The root defect is the admission check in full_channel.c pricing an opener HTLC at the committed rather than the pending feerate; the hard-crash sink is the assert in channeld.c, which should be a protocol error (peer_failed_warn/err) at most.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/full\_channel.c:785–822](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L785-L822)
   When the remote opener adds an HTLC (sender==REMOTE, recipient==LOCAL), the affordability check computes fee_for_htlcs(..., recipient) and compares the opener's remainder (after reserve and 660-sat anchors) against it. fee_for_htlcs() (line 492-511) uses channel_feerate(channel, recipient), i.e. the feerate already committed on the local commitment, so a received-but-not-yet-committed update_fee (sitting in RCVD_ADD_HTLC) is ignored and the HTLC is accepted at the old, lower fee.
2. [common/fee\_states.c:56–72](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/fee_states.c#L56-L72)
   get_feerate() returns the first feerate whose state carries HTLC_F_COMMITTED for the side; RCVD_ADD_HTLC only has LOCAL_F_PENDING (common/htlc_state.c), so a pending peer update_fee is invisible to channel_feerate(LOCAL) until commitment_signed is processed.
3. [channeld/channeld.c:2199–2206](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L2199-L2206)
   handle_peer_commit_sig() asserts can_opener_afford_feerate(channel, channel_feerate(LOCAL)) when opener==REMOTE, immediately after channel_rcvd_commit() has promoted both the pending HTLC and the pending feerate to RCVD_ADD_COMMIT. Asserts are compiled in (no NDEBUG anywhere in the build), so the peer-reachable false result aborts channeld.
4. [channeld/channeld.c:815–831](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L815-L831)
   handle_peer_feechange() validates the peer's update_fee via channel_update_feerate() only against the HTLC set present at that moment, then parks the new rate as pending; nothing re-validates later HTLC additions against it, and the project's own peer_failed_warn here shows the peer's fee updates are treated as untrusted input.
5. [common/fee\_states.c:89–100](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/fee_states.c#L89-L100)
   start_fee_update() parks the peer's new feerate at first_fee_state(opener)=RCVD_ADD_HTLC (pending) after channel_update_feerate() has validated it only against the HTLC set that existed at that moment.
6. [channeld/full\_channel.c:1515–1529](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L1515-L1529)
   channel_rcvd_commit() -> change_htlcs() -> fee_incstate() advances both the pending HTLCs and the pending feerate (RCVD_ADD_HTLC -> RCVD_ADD_COMMIT) so that, immediately after, channel_feerate(LOCAL) is the new higher rate and the newly added HTLC counts as committed.
7. [channeld/full\_channel.c:1342–1430](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L1342-L1430)
   can_opener_afford_feerate() recomputes the requirement at the given feerate over committed+adding-removing HTLCs with the same reserve (config[!opener]) and anchor deduction as add_htlc; with the new rate and the extra HTLC output it is now false even though every individual step passed.
8. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:641–646](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L641-L646)
   channel_errmsg() with peer_fd == NULL (subdaemon crash, from subd.c destroy_subd) calls channel_fail_transient(): the channel is left waiting for reconnect rather than force-closed, so the peer can retransmit the same updates after channel_reestablish and crash channeld again, wedging the channel indefinitely.

## Impact
channeld for that channel aborts (SIGABRT) and keeps aborting on every reconnect; lightningd maps the subdaemon death to channel_fail_transient so the channel is neither force-closed nor usable: it cannot forward, add or settle HTLCs until the operator force-closes it, with the usual on-chain cost and lock-up of any HTLCs committed through it. lightningd itself and other channels stay up. No data disclosure or balance change.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer that opened a channel to the victim (so it is the fee-paying opener) - the normal position of any peer who connects and opens. It sends three ordinary protocol messages in the order update_fee, update_add_htlc with a tuned amount, commitment_signed; all are peer-authored, F_new only needs to be inside the victim's accepted range (typically a 10x-wide band), and no defense stands in the way since the reverse ordering is the only one checked. The crash is deterministic and repeats on every reconnect while the peer keeps the updates outstanding.

## Recommended fix
1. add_htlc prices an HTLC offered by the opener at the committed feerate of the recipient's commitment, ignoring a received-but-uncommitted update_fee that will apply to the very commitment the HTLC lands in. Fix criteria: The affordability check for an incoming opener HTLC must use the feerate that the next commitment_signed will commit (the pending update_fee if one is outstanding), so that accepting an HTLC never leaves can_opener_afford_feerate() false after channel_rcvd_commit(). Verify with the three-message sequence above: the HTLC must be rejected with CHANNEL_ERR_CHANNEL_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED and channeld must not abort.
2. handle_peer_commit_sig() enforces an invariant that depends on peer-controlled ordering with assert(), turning any discrepancy into a process abort. Fix criteria: A failed opener-affordability check on a received commitment_signed must be handled as a protocol error (warning/error and channel failure), never an abort; a fuzzed/malicious peer must not be able to terminate channeld through this path.

# tx_add_input on Elements indexes PSBT inputs by peer's prevtx_vout: heap out-of-bounds write

## Details
In run_tx_interactive()'s WIRE_TX_ADD_INPUT handler (openingd/dualopend.c), the peer's input is appended with psbt_append_input(), which returns the new input `in` at index psbt->num_inputs-1. When chainparams is an Elements chain (liquid / liquid-regtest) the code then calls psbt_elements_input_set_asset(psbt, outpoint.n, &asset). The callee's second parameter is the PSBT input index (bitcoin/psbt.c:506-523 does &psbt->inputs[in]; the other production caller wallet/db.c:540 passes 0 for a one-input PSBT), but `outpoint.n` is the peer-supplied `prevtx_vout` bound directly by fromwire_tx_add_input (dualopend.c:1832-1837). It is validated only against tx->wtx->num_outputs of the peer's own prevtx (1904-1911) and against is_segwit_output of that one output, so a peer can choose any index up to the number of outputs it packs into prevtx (~1400 minimal Elements outputs fit in a 65535-byte message). psbt->num_inputs at that moment is small — on the accepter side it is 0 before the opener's first tx_add_input — so prevtx_vout >= num_inputs (vout 1 with a 2-output prevtx suffices) already indexes past the wally inputs array.

psbt_elements_input_set_asset() has no bounds check: if the prevtx output value is non-zero it calls wally_psbt_input_set_amount(&psbt->inputs[in], value) (writes the peer-chosen u64 and has_amount flag at offset in*sizeof(struct wally_psbt_input) from psbt->inputs), then wally_psbt_input_set_asset(&psbt->inputs[in], ...) which, per libwally's replace_bytes semantics, frees whatever pointer lies in the `asset` slot of that out-of-bounds memory and stores a newly allocated 32-byte buffer there. This is a heap out-of-bounds write with attacker-chosen stride and 8-byte value plus a free() of an attacker-influenced pointer inside dualopend, triggered by a plain tx_add_input before any balance or completion checks. Indices below num_inputs instead overwrite another (possibly our own) input's PSET amount/asset.

Reachable from any peer that negotiates option_dual_fund with a node running on an Elements network with --experimental-dual-fund (accepter_start reaches run_tx_interactive at dualopend.c:2849 without operator interaction; bitcoin chains skip the is_elements() branch). Assumptions (external/ submodule not present in checkout): libwally-core as pinned by the external/ submodule implements wally_psbt_input_set_asset via replace_bytes (clear-and-free of the previous buffer) and grows psbt->inputs by doubling, so inputs_allocation_len is at most 2*num_inputs.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/dualopend.c:1953–1965](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1953-L1965)
   After psbt_append_input() returns the new input `in`, the elements branch calls psbt_elements_input_set_asset(psbt, outpoint.n, &asset) with the peer's prevtx_vout instead of the just-appended input's index; the amount comes from the peer's prevtx output value. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [bitcoin/psbt.c:506–522](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/psbt.c#L506-L522)
   psbt_elements_input_set_asset() dereferences &psbt->inputs[in] without comparing `in` to psbt->num_inputs, then wally_psbt_input_set_amount (u64 + flag write) and wally_psbt_input_set_asset (frees the existing asset pointer found there and stores a new allocation) operate on that out-of-bounds struct.
3. [openingd/dualopend.c:1832–1837](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1832-L1837)
   fromwire_tx_add_input binds outpoint.n directly from the peer's u32 prevtx_vout field (wire/peer_wire.csv:54).
4. [openingd/dualopend.c:1904–1910](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1904-L1910)
   The only bound on outpoint.n is tx->wtx->num_outputs of the peer-supplied prevtx; the peer controls how many outputs that tx has, so the index is effectively attacker-chosen.
5. [wallet/db.c:540](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/db.c#L540)
   The other production caller passes PSBT input index 0 for a one-input PSBT, confirming the parameter's contract is the PSBT input index, not a prevout vout.
6. [openingd/dualopend.c:2849](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2849)
   accepter_start() enters run_tx_interactive as TX_ACCEPTER after replying accept_channel2, so an unsolicited open_channel2 from any dual-fund-capable peer reaches the handler with psbt->num_inputs == 0 before the peer's first tx_add_input.

## Impact
Heap out-of-bounds write in dualopend at an attacker-chosen stride (up to ~1400 x sizeof(struct wally_psbt_input)) with an attacker-chosen 8-byte value, followed by a free of a pointer read from that out-of-bounds memory. Deterministic crash of the dual-open subdaemon at minimum (repeatable against every open attempt), and a realistic memory-corruption primitive toward code execution in a process holding channel keys material and a privileged connection to lightningd/hsmd. Confidentiality impact is bounded to what dualopend itself holds.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any peer that negotiates option_dual_fund sends open_channel2 (or accepts ours) and then one tx_add_input whose prevtx has >= 2 outputs, output[prevtx_vout] segwit with a chosen explicit value, and prevtx_vout >= psbt->num_inputs. No check compares prevtx_vout to the PSBT input count, and the write happens before check_balances or tx_complete logic. Precondition on the victim's deployment, not on any shipped security control: the node must run on an Elements network (liquid/liquid-regtest) with --experimental-dual-fund, hence AT:PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
1. The elements branch of the tx_add_input handler passes the peer's prevtx output index (outpoint.n) where the PSBT input index of the just-appended input is required. Fix criteria: The PSET amount/asset must be set on the input that was just appended (the index of `in` within psbt->inputs, i.e. psbt->num_inputs - 1), never on an index derived from prevtx_vout.
2. psbt_elements_input_set_asset() indexes psbt->inputs without checking against psbt->num_inputs. Fix criteria: psbt_elements_input_set_asset (and sibling helpers taking a PSBT input index) must reject or abort on indices >= psbt->num_inputs so a wrong index can never become an out-of-bounds write.
