# Gossip holding queues are count-capped, not byte-capped, and store unverified ~64KB messages for hours

## Details
gossmap_manage keeps five holding areas for gossip it cannot yet act on: early_ann_map and pending_ann_map (channel_announcements awaiting depth / UTXO lookup), early_cupdates and pending_cupdates (channel_updates for those scids), and pending_nannounces (node_announcements for unknown nodes while any announcement is outstanding). Each is limited by PENDING_LIMIT = 10000 *entries* (enqueue_cupdate line 141, enqueue_nannounce line 182, map_add line 216), but every entry retains a full copy of the peer-supplied message, and message size is bounded only by the BOLT8 u16 length (65535 bytes, common/cryptomsg.c:150). The generated parsers accept trailing bytes (impl_template:410), channel_announcement/node_announcement carry unvalidated u16-length features blobs, so each queue can hold ~10001 x 65535 B ~= 655 MB, roughly 3.3 GB across the five areas, all attacker-authored.

The attacker is any remote peer: connectd forwards every channel_announcement/channel_update/node_announcement to gossipd verbatim with no per-peer rate limit or size cap (connectd/multiplex.c:915-927). Cheapest sequence: (1) one channel_announcement signed with the attacker's own four keys whose scid blocknum is current_height+12 — it passes sigcheck and is parked in early_ann_map (lines 724-737) until height >= blocknum+5, i.e. 17 blocks (~3 h), and one new announcement per block keeps the map non-empty indefinitely; (2) up to 10001 channel_updates for that scid, each padded to ~65 KB — enqueued at lines 1083-1101 before any signature check (sigcheck_channel_update needs the channel's node_id and runs only in process_channel_update, line 905), so gossipd does no crypto and the attacker signs nothing; (3) while either map is non-empty, up to 10001 ~65 KB node_announcements for fresh keys (one self-signature each), queued at lines 1226-1237; (4) optionally fill early_ann_map/pending_ann_map themselves with ~65 KB announcements. The queues drain only via reprocess_queued_msgs (line 1313), which runs solely on a *successful* txout reply (line 868) and only once the maps are empty; disconnecting or banning the peer frees nothing because the entries belong to the queues, not the peer.

There is no amplification — the attacker must send roughly the bytes retained — but the gain is persistence: gossip is normally processed and discarded immediately, whereas here a few GB of unverified bytes stay resident for hours after the traffic stops, at the attacker's discretion. PENDING_LIMIT was intended as a flood defence (the log says 'being flooded ... dropping some') but is in the wrong units: for the ~140-byte channel_updates it assumes it bounds ~1.4 MB per queue; with attacker-chosen padding the same cap admits ~655 MB. gossipd is a must_not_exit subdaemon (lightningd/subd.c:663-669, 811), so if the host OOM-kills it lightningd exits — a full node outage. On memory-constrained hosts (Raspberry Pi / small VPS, often co-located with bitcoind) ~3 GB of attacker-pinned RSS is enough; on larger hosts it pins memory for hours and legitimate deferred gossip is dropped once the count caps are hit. Distinct from the verified unbounded leak at line 728 (gossipd-cannounce-far-future-scid-pca-leak): here memory is eventually released, but the cap bounds count rather than bytes and is applied to unverified data.

## Evidence
1. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:125–170](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L125-L170)
   enqueue_cupdate() drops only when tal_count(*queue) > PENDING_LIMIT (10000) — a count check at line 141 — and otherwise stores a full copy of the peer-supplied channel_update (tal_dup_talarr, line 166). Nothing bounds the bytes retained; the per-entry cost is whatever the peer sent, up to the transport maximum.
2. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1063–1101](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1063-L1101)
   A channel_update whose scid is in pending_ann_map or early_ann_map is enqueued here after only parse/chain_hash/timestamp checks. sigcheck_channel_update() runs only later in process_channel_update() (line 905) once the channel's node_id is known, so the retained bytes are unverified and the attacker signs nothing.
3. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:172–201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L172-L201)
   enqueue_nannounce() has the same count-only cap and copies the full node_announcement; it is used for every node_announcement for an unknown node while either announcement map is non-empty (lines 1226-1237). The one required signature is over the attacker's own fresh node key.
4. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:212–233](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L212-L233)
   map_add() caps pending_ann_map and early_ann_map at PENDING_LIMIT entries each; each pending_cannounce carries a full copy of the announcement (line 704) whose u16-length features blob (peer_wire.csv:349-350) is not validated.
5. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:723–742](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L723-L742)
   The gate: a self-signed channel_announcement with blocknum in (height+?, height+12] is parked in early_ann_map until is_scid_depth_announceable (blocknum + ANNOUNCE_MIN_DEPTH-1 <= height, ANNOUNCE_MIN_DEPTH=6) — for blocknum = height+12 that is 17 blocks (~3 h). One such announcement per block keeps the map non-empty indefinitely.
6. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1313–1331](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1313-L1331)
   reprocess_queued_msgs() drains pending/early cupdates and pending nannounces only when the respective maps are empty, and it is called from exactly one place: the successful-txout path of gossmap_manage_handle_get_txout_reply (line 868). The failure path (bad:/out:) does not call it, so the queues persist until the attacker's gate closes and some later genuine announcement succeeds. Disconnecting the peer frees nothing: entries are tal children of the queue, not the peer.
7. [connectd/multiplex.c:915–927](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L915-L927)
   handle_gossip_in() forwards every is_msg_for_gossipd() message from any connected peer to gossipd verbatim; the only check is the connectd->gossipd pipe backlog (500000 messages). There is no per-peer inbound gossip rate limit and no size cap below the transport maximum.
8. [common/cryptomsg.c:150](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/cryptomsg.c#L150)
   BOLT8 message length is a u16, so a single peer message may be up to 65535 bytes — the only bound on each retained copy.
9. [tools/gen/impl\_template:410](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/gen/impl_template#L410)
   Generated fromwire_* parsers return `cursor != NULL` without requiring plen == 0, so a 138-byte channel_update (no TLV stream in peer_wire.csv:371-381) padded with ~65 KB of trailing bytes parses successfully and is retained whole.
10. [lightningd/subd.c:663–669](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L663-L669)
   gossipd is created via new_global_subd (must_not_exit = true, line 811); if the host OOM-kills it, lightningd calls errx(1) and the whole node exits.

## Impact
No confidentiality or integrity impact. Availability: up to ~3.3 GB of attacker-controlled bytes pinned in gossipd for hours, outliving the connection; on memory-constrained hosts gossipd is OOM-killed and lightningd exits (must_not_exit), a full node outage with on-chain consequences; on larger hosts the node degrades and legitimate deferred gossip is dropped once the count caps are reached.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker connects as an ordinary peer (no channel needed; connectd autolistens on 9735 and forwards all gossip). One self-signed channel_announcement at height+12 opens the early_ann_map gate for 17 blocks; thereafter ~10000 maximum-size channel_updates for that scid (no signatures) and ~10000 self-signed maximum-size node_announcements are retained by gossipd, renewable every block. No shipped control must be bypassed — there is no per-peer inbound gossip rate limit, no byte budget, and bad_gossip() only logs. Attack requirements are PRESENT because gossipd must know a blockheight (synced node), the attacker must push ~3 GB over the link and re-arm the gate per block, and whether retention becomes an outage depends on host memory headroom the attacker does not control.

## Recommended fix
1. PENDING_LIMIT bounds the number of queued/pending gossip messages but not their aggregate size, and the copy of each message is made before the bound is consulted and before any authenticity check, so a peer can make gossipd retain a large volume of unverified bytes. Fix criteria: The total bytes retained across early/pending announcement maps, deferred channel_updates and deferred node_announcements must be bounded by a fixed budget (and ideally per source peer), with excess dropped before copying. Verify by replaying the sequence above and confirming gossipd's resident memory stays within the budget regardless of message sizes.
2. Deferred channel_updates are stored without checking that they are plausibly genuine, so queueing costs the attacker nothing while costing gossipd memory. Fix criteria: Deferred channel_updates should be rejected or heavily limited unless some cheap authenticity signal exists (e.g. verify against the node_ids in the pending channel_announcement for that scid, which are already known in pending_cannounce->node_id), and messages with gratuitous trailing bytes beyond the known fields should not be retained at full size. Verify that unsigned/garbage-padded updates for a pending scid are not held in memory.

# Unbounded memory leak in gossipd for channel_announcements more than 12 blocks ahead

## Details
gossmap_manage_channel_announcement() allocates `struct pending_cannounce *pca` from `gm` (the permanent gossmap_manage object) and copies the entire channel_announcement into it before deciding what to do with it. When the announcement's short_channel_id is not yet deep enough (`!is_scid_depth_announceable`) and its block number is more than 12 blocks past gossipd's current height, the function returns a warning string at gossipd/gossmap_manage.c:728 ("Bad gossip order: ignoring channel_announcement ...") without freeing `pca`. Because `pca` was allocated off `gm` rather than `tmpctx`, and no map holds a reference, the allocation (struct + 34-byte scriptpubkey + full copy of the message + node_id) is unreachable and leaked until gossipd exits.

Attacker and input: any remote Lightning peer (unauthenticated beyond the Noise handshake) authors channel_announcement bytes. connectd forwards every gossip message to gossipd verbatim (connectd/multiplex.c:915-928, 1081-1082) with no per-peer rate limit — only a 500000-message backpressure drop — and gossipd dispatches it at gossipd.c:196-201. To reach line 728 the attacker needs node_id_1 < node_id_2 (own keys), the right chain_hash, blocknum >= when_lightning_became_cool, an scid not previously seen, and four valid ECDSA signatures over the message — all produced with keys the attacker controls. Choosing blocknum = current_height + 13 (or larger) and iterating txnum/outnum yields an unlimited supply of distinct scids; none is added to txout_failures or any map, so the duplicate suppression at lines 681-689 never triggers. The `features` field is a u16-length blob that is not validated, so each message can be padded to ~65 KB (BOLT8 be16 frame limit), all of which is copied into the leaked object. The rejection only queues a BOLT1 warning back to the peer (gossipd.c:276-284 -> connectd.c:2526-2532 inject_peer_msg); the peer is not disconnected.

There is no cap: unlike the pending/early maps (PENDING_LIMIT) this path has no counter because pca never enters a map. The per-message cost to gossipd is four signature verifications, so a single peer can grow gossipd's heap by tens of MB per second on a fast link, or steadily over hours, until the host OOM-kills lightning_gossipd. gossipd is a must_not_exit global subdaemon (lightningd/gossip_control.c:309, subd.c:811), so its death makes lightningd errx(1) (subd.c:663-668) — a full node outage with the usual on-chain consequences (missed HTLC deadlines, no channel monitoring) until the operator restarts, after which the attack can be repeated.

The sibling early_ann_map branch a few blocks closer does free or store `pca`, showing the intent; the far-future branch simply returns before the allocation is released. The leak is reachable once gossipd knows a blockheight (`blockheight != 0`, set from lightningd's gossipd_new_blockheight at gossipd.c:414), i.e. in normal synced operation.

## Evidence
1. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:699–732](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L699-L732)
   pca is allocated as a child of the long-lived gossmap_manage object (line 699) and filled with a full copy of the peer-supplied channel_announcement (line 704, up to 65535 bytes), the 34-byte P2WSH scriptpubkey and the source node_id. On the far-future branch (lines 726-731: blockheight != 0 && blocknum(scid) > blockheight + 12) the function returns a tal_fmt'd warning string allocated on ctx and never frees pca; no map holds a reference, so it is unreachable and leaked for gossipd's lifetime. Every other exit after line 699 (known_amount, map_add failure, successful map_add) frees pca or hands it to a map.
2. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:620–697](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L620-L697)
   Checks before the allocation: parse success, node_id_1 < node_id_2, chain_hash match, blocknum >= when_lightning_became_cool, scid not in txout_failures, scid not already known/pending/early, and four valid ECDSA signatures. An attacker with its own node and bitcoin keys satisfies all of these; because the far-future path never inserts the scid anywhere (not txout_failures, not any map), the duplicate suppression at lines 681-689 never fires, so iterating txnum/outnum yields an unbounded supply of distinct leaking messages.
3. [connectd/multiplex.c:915–927](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L915-L927)
   handle_gossip_in forwards every peer gossip message (is_msg_for_gossipd, line 1081) to gossipd verbatim. The only guard is backpressure: drop when gossipd's outbound queue exceeds 500000 messages. There is no per-peer rate limit, inbound dedup or size restriction beyond the BOLT8 be16 length (common/cryptomsg.c:128-150).
4. [gossipd/gossipd.c:196–200](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossipd.c#L196-L200)
   Entry point: connectd's gossipd_recv_gossip carrying a WIRE_CHANNEL_ANNOUNCEMENT is dispatched to gossmap_manage_channel_announcement with the peer as source_peer and known_amount NULL, so the peer path reaches the far-future branch.
5. [gossipd/gossipd.c:276–283](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossipd.c#L276-L283)
   The returned warning string only becomes a BOLT1 warning queued to the peer via queue_peer_msg -> connectd gossipd_send_gossip -> inject_peer_msg (connectd.c:2526-2532). The peer is not disconnected or penalised, so a single connection can stream leaking announcements indefinitely.
6. [lightningd/subd.c:663–668](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L663-L668)
   gossipd is created by new_global_subd (lightningd/gossip_control.c:309), which sets must_not_exit = true (subd.c:811). When gossipd is OOM-killed or exits, lightningd calls errx(1) here and the whole node terminates.

## Impact
No confidentiality or integrity effect. Availability: unbounded, permanent (until restart) memory growth in gossipd driven purely by attacker traffic, culminating in OOM-kill of gossipd; lightningd treats gossipd exit as fatal (errx), so the entire node goes down and must be restarted by the operator or a supervisor, after which the attack can be repeated.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker connects as a Lightning peer (no privileges; nodes autolisten on 9735 and accept gossip from anyone). They generate one node/bitcoin key pair set, then stream channel_announcements whose scid block number is current_height+13 with varying txnum/outnum, each with four valid signatures and a large features blob. connectd forwards each to gossipd without rate limiting; gossipd verifies the signatures, allocates pca with a copy of the message, and returns at gossmap_manage.c:728 leaking it while only queueing a warning (no disconnect). Repeating until gossipd's RSS exhausts memory kills gossipd and therefore lightningd. No special deployment state is needed beyond gossipd having received a blockheight, which is normal operation.

## Recommended fix
The pending_cannounce object is allocated from the long-lived gossmap_manage context before all rejection checks are complete, and the far-future-scid rejection path returns without freeing it, violating the invariant that every allocation made for a rejected message is released. Fix criteria: A channel_announcement rejected for being more than 12 blocks ahead must leave gossipd's heap unchanged: either perform that check (and any other rejections) before allocating pca, or free pca on that return path. Verify by sending many such announcements (distinct scids, valid signatures) and confirming gossipd's memory does not grow, and by running the dev memleak check after such traffic.

# LSPS2 service holds incoming HTLC indefinitely waiting for client channel_ready

## Details
In the JIT flow the LSPS2 service, after fundchannel to the client succeeds (the funding tx is already broadcast), waits for the channel to reach CHANNELD_NORMAL by polling listpeerchannels every 10 seconds in an unbounded loop (core/lsps2/htlc.rs:208-218). handle_htlc_inner (service.rs:188) awaits that loop before answering the htlc_accepted hook, and lightningd holds the incoming HTLC with status 'Waiting for the htlc_accepted hook' (peer_htlcs.c:1246-1249) with no hook timeout. Nothing consults the HTLC's cltv_expiry (present in the hook request, cln_adapters/types.rs:33), elapsed time, or whether the channel has entered a non-progressing state; is_channel_ready (cln_adapters/rpc.rs:79-101) returns false for everything but CHANNELD_NORMAL.

lockin_complete (lightningd/channel_control.c:1159-1186) only moves a channel to CHANNELD_NORMAL once remote_channel_ready is set, i.e. after the client has sent channel_ready. A malicious client therefore controls whether the loop ever terminates: it buys a JIT scid (lsps2.get_info/lsps2.buy are open to any peer, subject to the operator's policy plugin), has a payment routed to the scid (from any node, via a third-party routing peer of the LSP or directly), accepts the channel open so the LSP broadcasts the funding transaction, then never sends channel_ready (or disconnects). The channel stays CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN and the incoming HTLC stays held. The only shipped protection covers the pre-funding case (the client rejecting the open makes fundchannel fail and the HTLC is failed with unknown_next_peer, tests/test_cln_lsps.py::test_lsps2_non_approved_zero_conf); nothing bounds the post-funding wait.

Because lightningd does not fail unfulfilled incoming HTLCs at their deadline ('If overdue, that's their problem', peer_htlcs.c:3086-3087), the upstream peer must force-close its channel with the LSP once cltv_expiry passes to reclaim the HTLC on-chain. If the payment was routed through a third party, that third party's channel with the LSP is force-closed; the attacker's own exposure is a small payment locked until expiry. Each attack also leaves a tokio task polling the RPC forever and an HTLC slot consumed on the upstream channel.

The LSPS2 'LSP trusts client' model (client_trusts_lsp: false, core/lsps2/service.rs:135) concedes that the LSP may lose the on-chain funding fee and have capacity locked in an abandoned zero-conf channel; the implementation-specific defect is that the held HTLC is never failed back before its deadline, converting that conceded loss into a forced on-chain closure of an unrelated upstream channel. Reachable only when the operator has enabled `experimental-lsps2-service` with a promise secret and an LSP-Policy plugin (doc/lightningd-config.5.md:902-912).

## Evidence
1. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs:204–218](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs#L204-L218)
   After fund_jit_channel succeeds the handler loops until is_channel_ready returns true, sleeping 10s between polls, with no bound on iterations, wall-clock time, or the HTLC's cltv_expiry; the FIXME comments acknowledge the missing timeout and unhandled channel states. The exit condition depends solely on the remote client sending channel_ready.
2. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln\_adapters/rpc.rs:79–100](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln_adapters/rpc.rs#L79-L100)
   is_channel_ready returns true only for CHANNELD_NORMAL and false for every other state, including states the channel never leaves without the client's cooperation (CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN with channel_ready withheld, peer disconnected) or terminal closing/onchain states, so the loop never terminates in those cases.
3. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs:154–200](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs#L154-L200)
   handle_htlc_inner awaits handler.handle() before producing the hook response; while it is pending lightningd holds the incoming HTLC. The hook request carries htlc.cltv_expiry (cln_adapters/types.rs:33) but it is never consulted.
4. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1159–1185](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1159-L1185)
   lockin_complete asserts remote_channel_ready before setting CHANNELD_NORMAL: the channel only reaches the state the plugin polls for once the client has sent channel_ready, which the client alone decides.
5. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:3080–3092](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L3080-L3092)
   lightningd deliberately does not fail unfulfilled incoming HTLCs at their deadline ('If overdue, that's their problem'), so the only resolution of a held HTLC is the upstream peer force-closing its channel with the LSP once cltv_expiry passes.
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1238–1249](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1238-L1249)
   While the htlc_accepted hook is outstanding the HTLC is parked with status 'Waiting for the htlc_accepted hook of plugin ...'; plugin_hook.c applies no timeout, so the hold lasts as long as the plugin's loop.

## Impact
Per attack the LSP loses on-chain fees and locks channel_capacity in a dead channel, and the upstream channel carrying the HTLC is force-closed by its peer when cltv expires (loss of that channel's liquidity/service plus on-chain costs). Repeatable against each upstream channel; HTLC slots on the upstream channel are also consumed while held.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote peer obtains a promise via lsps2.get_info (subject only to the operator's policy) and a JIT scid via lsps2.buy, routes a payment to the scid from any node, lets the LSP fund the zero-conf channel, then withholds channel_ready. No special position beyond being a Lightning peer; requires the experimental service to be enabled.

## Recommended fix
The channel-ready wait has no deadline and ignores the HTLC's cltv_expiry, so the hook never returns and the HTLC is never failed back. Fix criteria: The wait is bounded by a deadline derived from htlc.cltv_expiry (with a safety margin below lightningd's own fulfilment deadline) and by a wall-clock cap; on expiry, peer disconnect, or the channel entering a non-NORMAL terminal state, the hook returns 'fail' so the upstream HTLC is failed back before the upstream can time it out on chain. A test that withholds channel_ready must observe the HTLC failed back and no upstream force-close.

# Peer can grow an unbounded per-channel message queue for an orphaned subd in connectd

## Details
connectd demultiplexes every channel-scoped peer message by channel_id (multiplex.c read_body_from_peer_done). When find_subd() finds no `struct subd` for the channel_id, connectd creates one with `conn == NULL` (new_subd), tells lightningd via connectd_peer_spoke, and enqueues the message on `subd->outq`. Every later message carrying the same channel_id is matched by find_subd() to that same subd and appended to its outq, with no further notice to lightningd. `msg_queue` (common/msg_queue.c do_enqueue) has no cap, only a one-time log at 250000 entries; the only places that remove a conn-less subd are disconnect_peer() and destroy_peer_conn(), i.e. when the whole connection goes away. Nothing ever drains or discards the queue until the peer disconnects.

lightningd normally makes this harmless by disconnecting the peer after replying to an unknown-channel message (handle_peer_spoke send_error -> connectd_disconnect_peer). But lightningd/peer_control.c:2363-2372 deliberately does NOT disconnect when the unknown-channel message is a `channel_reestablish` and `peer_has_other_live_channel()` is true (any other channel of that peer in a channel_state_wants_peercomms state, which includes CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, i.e. an unconfirmed channel whose funding tx the attacker never has to broadcast). The maintainers' own comment at peer_control.c:2285-2290 records that connectd has no way to drop a subd and that leaving the connection up lets a peer accumulate orphaned subds; the reestablish path re-opens exactly that hole.

Attack: a peer with one channel (confirmed or merely negotiated to funding_signed) sends channel_reestablish with an arbitrary channel_id X. lightningd replies with an error and keeps the connection. connectd now holds an orphan subd for X forever. The peer then streams maximum-size (65535-byte) channel messages with channel_id X (any type extract_channel_id() recognises, e.g. update_add_htlc or further channel_reestablish), interleaving a `ping` after each one: the pong is enqueued to peer_outq, write_to_peer() flushes it and, finding nothing else to send, calls io_wake(&peer->peer_in) (multiplex.c:1329/1337, 1382), so the read loop keeps consuming. Every junk message is tal_dup'd onto the orphan's outq and never freed. The only brake is the per-peer incoming_stream_limit (1,000,000 bytes/s), so memory grows at ~1 MB/s per attacking connection (3.6 GB/hour) with no upper bound. Sending tx_abort for X sets rcvd_tx_abort so the next message creates yet another orphan subd for X (find_subd skips aborted ones), so peer->subds also grows without bound. When connectd is OOM-killed, lightningd treats connectd as must_not_exit (lightningd/subd.c:663-668) and exits, taking the whole node down.

## Evidence
1. [connectd/multiplex.c:1592–1619](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1592-L1619)
   Per-message dispatch: find_subd() by attacker-supplied channel_id; if absent, new_subd() with conn==NULL and peer_spoke to lightningd; then unconditional msg_enqueue(subd->outq, ...) with no bound and no check that the subd will ever be attached.
2. [connectd/multiplex.c:63–86](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L63-L86)
   find_subd() matches conn-less (orphan) subds exactly like attached ones, so all later messages for that channel_id are silently appended to the orphan's queue and lightningd is never told again; it also skips rcvd_tx_abort subds, so tx_abort lets the peer mint additional orphans for the same id.
3. [connectd/multiplex.c:1318–1339](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1318-L1339)
   write_to_peer() wakes &peer->peer_in whenever it has nothing left to send, so any reply the peer can provoke (a pong to its ping) re-arms the read loop; the enqueue-then-io_wait(peer_in) backpressure in read_body_from_peer_done is therefore bypassable.
4. [common/msg\_queue.c:48–62](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/msg_queue.c#L48-L62)
   msg_queue has no capacity limit; it only logs a backtrace once when more than 250000 messages are queued.
5. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2355–2372](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2355-L2372)
   For an unknown-channel channel_reestablish, lightningd sends the error but returns without connectd_disconnect_peer when the peer has another live channel, leaving the orphan subd (and its unbounded queue) alive in connectd.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2282–2299](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2282-L2299)
   Maintainer comment acknowledging that connectd cannot drop a subd and that keeping the connection up lets a peer accumulate orphaned subds; the reestablish path contradicts this mitigation.
7. [lightningd/channel.h:733–745](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.h#L733-L745)
   channel_state_wants_peercomms() includes CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN and DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN, so an unconfirmed (never-broadcast) channel satisfies peer_has_other_live_channel().
8. [lightningd/subd.c:663–668](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L663-L668)
   connectd is a must_not_exit subdaemon: when it is OOM-killed lightningd exits, so connectd memory exhaustion is a whole-node outage.

## Impact
Unbounded heap growth in lightning_connectd (~1 MB/s per attacking connection, never released while the connection lives). Exhaustion leads to connectd being killed, which lightningd treats as fatal (errx), so the entire node stops: no payments, no HTLC resolution, forced closes on timeouts. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote Lightning peer over the network. Precondition: one channel with the victim in any peercomms state; as fundee the victim enters CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN after funding_signed without any on-chain spend by the attacker. The attacker then sends channel_reestablish for a bogus channel_id (connection survives), and streams 65 KB messages tagged with that id interleaved with pings. No defensive mechanism must be defeated; the flow is deterministic and bounded only by the 1 MB/s per-peer intake limit. Multiple node_ids/channels multiply the rate.

## Recommended fix
1. connectd keeps an unattached (conn==NULL) subd and its outq indefinitely and keeps appending peer messages to it; there is no bound on queue size or on the number of such subds per peer, and no way for lightningd to tell connectd to discard one. Fix criteria: A conn-less subd must not accumulate messages without bound: either stop reading from the peer until lightningd attaches or discards the subd (true backpressure that ping/pong traffic cannot bypass), or cap bytes/messages queued per unattached subd and per peer and disconnect (or drop the subd) when exceeded, or add a lightningd->connectd message to discard a subd that lightningd will not service. Verify: with a live channel, send channel_reestablish for an unknown id followed by a sustained stream of large messages for that id; connectd RSS must stay bounded.
2. lightningd's unknown-channel channel_reestablish handling keeps the connection open while leaving connectd's orphan subd in place. Fix criteria: When lightningd decides not to disconnect after an unknown-channel message, it must ensure connectd does not retain an orphan subd for that channel_id (e.g. instruct connectd to discard it), or the peer must be rate-limited/disconnected on repeated unknown-channel traffic. Verify the same test above no longer grows memory.

# clnrest-register-path lets a restricted rune bearer re-scope or remove rune checks for any RPC

## Details
clnrest (plugins/rest-plugin) exposes the RPC method `clnrest-register-path`, which maps an HTTP path to an arbitrary lightningd RPC method and lets the registrant choose (a) whether a rune is required at all (GET only), and (b) what `method`/`params` are presented to lightningd's `checkrune` instead of the real ones. The command is a normal plugin RPC method, so it is callable by every rune bearer whose rune permits the method name — through clnrest itself (`POST /v1/clnrest-register-path`), through commando, or through wss-proxy/commando. Nothing ties the registration to operator authority.

A bearer of a rune that permits `clnrest-register-path` but is otherwise restricted (deny-list runes such as `method/pay&method/withdraw&method/createrune`, prefix runes such as `method^cln`, or runes restricted only by `rate`/`pnum`/`time`) can escalate to full node control:

1. Register `{"path":"v1/pay","rpc_method":"pay","rune_restrictions":{"method":"getinfo","params":{}}}`. shared.rs consults the dynamic router first, so the built-in `/v1/pay` route is shadowed. On `POST /v1/pay`, handlers.rs asks checkrune about `getinfo` with empty params and, on success, executes `pay` with the attacker's body. Any `method=getinfo`-style rune now pays invoices.
2. Register `{"path":"x","rpc_method":"createrune","rune_restrictions":{"method":"getinfo"}}`. lightningd's `creates_new_rune` guard (runes.c) only triggers when checkrune's `method` is createrune, so it is bypassed and an unrestricted rune is minted — persistent control that survives clnrest restarts.
3. Register `{"path":"pub","rpc_method":"listfunds","http_method":"GET","rune_required":false}`: anyone who can reach the listener reads node data with no rune at all.

The registration lives in `PluginState.dyn_router` until clnrest restarts; there is no list/unregister RPC, so the operator cannot audit what has been registered. The project's own `canonical_method`/`creates_new_rune` logic shows that method aliasing is treated as a rune-boundary violation; this command creates un-canonicalised aliases for every method and additionally lets the alias drop the rune check entirely.

Precondition: the attacker holds a rune whose restrictions admit the method name `clnrest-register-path` (the built-in `readonly` rune does not, since the name does not start with `list`/`get`). The schema documents the command as 'low-level ... for plugin developers' but does not warn that any rune permitting it is equivalent to an unrestricted rune.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/main.rs:211–264](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/main.rs#L211-L264)
   register_path is an ordinary plugin RPC method. Beyond lightningd's rune check for the method name 'clnrest-register-path' it performs no authorization. It accepts any rpc_method, any path (including 'v1/<builtin>'), rune_required=false for GET, and an arbitrary rune_restrictions object whose method/params replace the real ones in the later checkrune call. Registrations are only kept in memory, and there is no RPC to list or remove them.
2. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs:88–128](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs#L88-L128)
   path_to_rest_map_and_params consults the dynamic router before the built-in 'v1/<method>' mapping, so a registered dynamic path shadows the built-in route for the same URL and substitutes the registrant's ClnrestMap (rpc_method, rune_required, rune_restrictions).
3. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:260–289](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs#L260-L289)
   call_rpc_method skips verify_rune entirely for GET when rune_required is false, and otherwise calls verify_rune with rest_map.rune_restrictions (registrant-chosen method/params), then executes rest_map.rpc_method with the request's params. checkrune therefore judges a different method than the one executed.
4. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:309–327](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs#L309-L327)
   fill_rune_restrictions only substitutes the real rpc_method/params when the registrant left them unset; when set they are used verbatim.
5. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/parse.rs:96–113](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/parse.rs#L96-L113)
   The only constraint on registrations is that rune_required must be true for non-GET methods; there is no constraint on rpc_method, path, or rune_restrictions.method.
6. [lightningd/runes.c:941–957](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L941-L957)
   lightningd's creates_new_rune guard refuses createrune for restricted runes only when checkrune's own 'method' is createrune/invokerune. A dynamic path mapped to rpc_method=createrune with rune_restrictions.method='getinfo' makes clnrest ask checkrune about 'getinfo', so this guard never fires and a restricted rune can mint an unrestricted one.
7. [lightningd/runes.c:980–987](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L980-L987)
   canonical_method exists precisely so that an alias cannot bypass a 'method/...' restriction; clnrest-register-path creates arbitrary, un-canonicalised aliases for every RPC.

## Impact
Successful exploitation yields execution of any lightningd RPC (pay/withdraw/fundchannel/createrune/stop) with the full authority of the node, including minting an unrestricted rune: total loss of confidentiality, integrity (funds) and availability of the node.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a network client of clnrest (or commando) holding a rune whose method restrictions do not exclude `clnrest-register-path` but do exclude the methods they want (pay, createrune, ...). One POST registers a dynamic path with chosen rune_restrictions or rune_required=false; a second request to that path executes the target RPC. No defenses stand in the way; the only requirement is the operator having issued such a rune, which is a deployment state outside the attacker's control.

## Recommended fix
1. clnrest-register-path lets a caller authorised only for that method name define, for any other RPC, which method/params checkrune is asked about (or that no rune is needed), so the rune boundary enforced per-method by lightningd is replaced by the registrant's choice. Fix criteria: A caller whose rune does not permit method X must not be able to cause clnrest to execute X, regardless of registrations. Acceptable outcomes: registrations are only accepted from the operator/plugins (e.g. lightningd treats clnrest-register-path like createrune — refused for restricted runes), or clnrest always runs checkrune against the real rpc_method/params in addition to any registrant-supplied restrictions. Verify: with a rune `method/pay`, registering a path to `pay` with rune_restrictions.method=getinfo and calling it must be refused.
2. Dynamic paths are matched before the built-in `v1/<method>` routes, so a registration can silently replace the authorisation semantics of existing documented endpoints. Fix criteria: Registrations whose path lies under the built-in `v1/` namespace (or that would capture it via parameters) are rejected, or built-in routes are matched first. Verify: registering `v1/getinfo` or `{a}/{b}` fails and `POST /v1/getinfo` behaviour is unchanged after any registration.
3. Registrations are invisible and irrevocable at runtime (no list/unregister RPC), so an operator cannot detect or undo abuse. Fix criteria: Operators can enumerate and remove dynamic registrations, and registrations are logged at a level operators see by default.

# Per-connection memory leak when peer's init networks TLV has no common chain

## Details
In connectd/peer_exchange_initmsg.c peer_init_received(), when a remote peer's `init` message carries a `networks` TLV that does not include our genesis hash, connectd builds a warning with towire_warningfmt(NULL, ...), encrypts it with cryptomsg_encrypt_msg(NULL, &peer->cs, take(msg)) — which frees the taken plaintext and returns a fresh tal allocation with a NULL parent (common/cryptomsg.c:164) — and hands it to plain io_write(conn, msg, tal_count(msg), io_close_cb, NULL). ccan's io_write_() only records the pointer and length (ccan/ccan/io/io.c:205-218); io_close_cb then frees conn and its child early_peer, but the encrypted warning is a child of neither conn nor tmpctx and is never freed. The sibling reject paths in connectd.c peer_connected() avoid this by passing take(msg) to io_write_wire(), whose tal_dup_talarr(conn, ...) steals the buffer onto conn and whose do_write_wire frees it (wire/wire_io.c:142-160).

Any remote party that completes the BOLT8 Noise handshake (requires only the victim's public node_id; connectd autolistens on 9735 by default) triggers this on every connection by sending init with networks=[a foreign chain hash]. Each attempt leaks the encrypted warning (about 87 bytes: 18-byte encrypted header plus 53-byte warning plus 16-byte MAC, plus the tal header and malloc overhead, roughly 130-150 bytes) in lightning_connectd. No test exercises this path, so the developer memleak checker never sees it. Repeated connections cause steady, unrecoverable heap growth: the attacker pays a Noise handshake per attempt, so this is a slow leak rather than an immediate outage, but it is deterministic, remotely triggerable without credentials, persists after the attacker stops, and connectd is must_not_exit, so an eventual OOM kill takes lightningd down.

## Evidence
1. [connectd/peer\_exchange\_initmsg.c:102–104](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/peer_exchange_initmsg.c#L102-L104)
   Warning built with towire_warningfmt(NULL, ...) and encrypted with cryptomsg_encrypt_msg(NULL, &peer->cs, take(msg)) — the result is a fresh tal allocation with NULL parent (common/cryptomsg.c:164 tal_arr(ctx=NULL, ...)) — then handed to plain io_write(conn, msg, tal_count(msg), io_close_cb, NULL) without take() or a parent. io_close_cb frees conn and its child early_peer, but nothing frees msg.
2. [ccan/ccan/io/io.c:205–217](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/io/io.c#L205-L217)
   io_write_() stores the data pointer and length in the plan arg only; it neither takes ownership nor frees the buffer, so a NULL-parented tal buffer passed here is never released.
3. [wire/wire\_io.c:142–159](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/wire_io.c#L142-L159)
   Contrast: io_write_wire_() calls tal_dup_talarr(conn, u8, data), which steals a take()n buffer onto conn (freed on close) and do_write_wire tal_free()s it after writing; this is the ownership discipline the networks-mismatch path lacks.
4. [connectd/connectd.c:343–345](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L343-L345)
   Sibling reject path in peer_connected() (unsupported feature) encrypts the same way but passes take(msg) to io_write_wire(), so its buffer is owned by conn and freed; only the no-common-chain path leaks.

## Impact
Slow, unrecoverable heap growth in lightning_connectd proportional to the number of attacker connections; degrades availability over time and could eventually exhaust memory, but each attempt leaks only tens of bytes and costs the attacker a handshake, so impact is limited.

## Reproduction steps
1. Unauthenticated remote attacker connects to the node's listening address, completes the Noise handshake (requires only the victim's public node_id), and sends init with a networks TLV naming a foreign chain. The leak happens deterministically per connection. Repeating this many times is needed for noticeable impact.

## Recommended fix
The encrypted 'No common network' warning buffer is allocated with a NULL tal parent and passed to io_write(), which neither owns nor frees it, so it outlives the connection. Fix criteria: The warning buffer must be released once the connection closes or the write completes: allocate it as a child of conn (or tmpctx) or pass it with take() to a writer that steals/frees taken buffers, matching the sibling reject paths in connectd.c. Verify by repeatedly connecting with a mismatched networks TLV under the dev memleak check and confirming no NULL-parented allocation remains.

# Tor control PROTOCOLINFO COOKIEFILE path trusted: connectd reads and transmits arbitrary file

## Details
lightning_connectd authenticates to the Tor control port with the legacy COOKIE method. negotiate_auth() (connectd/tor_autoservice.c:195-257) sends PROTOCOLINFO 1 and, for every reply line containing `AUTH METHODS=` with `COOKIEFILE="<path>"` (and no `NULL`/usable `HASHEDPASSWORD`), reads `<path>` with grab_file_raw() — any file, regular or /proc, any size — and sends the complete contents hex-encoded in `AUTHENTICATE <hex>` to the same socket (lines 222-245). If a read fails it `continue`s to the next line, so one reply may carry several candidate paths and the first readable one is transmitted.

Nothing authenticates the party that answered: tor_autoservice()/tor_fixed_service() open a plaintext TCP connection to the operator-configured `autotor:`/`statictor:` TORIPADDRESS (default port 9051; any IPv4/IPv6/DNS target is accepted by parse_wireaddr_internal, common/wireaddr.c:666-688) and tor_response_line() only requires lines to begin with `250`. This is the 'malicious Tor' attack that the Tor control-spec's SAFECOOKIE method exists to prevent (assumption: Tor control-spec §3.5/§3.24, which warns that a controller using COOKIE can be made to disclose any readable file).

Because lightningd chdir()s into `<lightning-dir>/<network>` (lightningd/options.c:1875) and subdaemons inherit that cwd (hsmd itself opens `hsm_secret` by relative path, hsmd/hsmd.c:393), the impersonator needs no path knowledge: `250-AUTH METHODS=COOKIE COOKIEFILE="hsm_secret"` followed by `250 OK` yields the node's master secret (32 bytes, the same size as a genuine Tor cookie) in the next AUTHENTICATE line. The attacker then answers `250 OK` plus a fabricated `ServiceID=` to ADD_ONION and the node runs on. The wallet DB, rune secret, gRPC TLS keys or any other file readable by the lightningd user can be taken the same way.

Who can hold that position: (a) a local unprivileged user on the same host who binds 127.0.0.1:9051 (unprivileged port) while Tor is down, restarting, or not yet started at lightningd start — the exchange runs unattended at every connectd start (connectd.c:1593-1605) and the project's 0700 lightning-dir and 0400 hsm_secret are exactly the controls meant to deny such a user this file; (b) a party occupying, or on-path to, the control address when the documented remote TORIPADDRESS form is used (Tor in another container/host). There is no 32-byte length check, no SAFECOOKIE (AUTHCHALLENGE) support, and no preference for HASHEDPASSWORD when both are advertised.

## Evidence
1. [connectd/tor\_autoservice.c:222–245](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/tor_autoservice.c#L222-L245)
   negotiate_auth() takes the COOKIEFILE="..." path verbatim from the PROTOCOLINFO reply of whatever answered on the configured control-port address, reads it with grab_file_raw() (any path, any size, no 32-byte check; a failed read just moves to the next advertised path) and sends the full contents hex-encoded back to the same party in AUTHENTICATE.
2. [connectd/tor\_autoservice.c:60–78](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/tor_autoservice.c#L60-L78)
   tor_response_line() only requires lines to start with '250'; a fake server that answers '250 OK' to every command is indistinguishable from Tor — there is no server authentication at any point.
3. [connectd/tor\_autoservice.c:270–284](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/tor_autoservice.c#L270-L284)
   tor_autoservice() (and tor_fixed_service() at 312-328) opens a plaintext TCP connection to the operator-configured TORIPADDRESS:port and calls negotiate_auth() with no authentication of the server.
4. [lightningd/options.c:1875](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1875)
   lightningd chdir()s into <lightning-dir>/<network> and subdaemons inherit that cwd, so a relative COOKIEFILE="hsm_secret" resolves to the node's master secret without the attacker knowing any absolute path (hsmd/hsmd.c:393 opens the same relative name).
5. [connectd/connectd.c:1593–1604](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L1593-L1604)
   setup_listeners() (called from connect_init at every connectd start) invokes tor_autoservice()/tor_fixed_service() for every autotor:/statictor: addr, so the exchange happens unattended at each node start/restart.
6. [common/wireaddr.c:666–687](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/wireaddr.c#L666-L687)
   The autotor:/statictor: argument is parsed with parse_wireaddr() (default port 9051) accepting any IPv4/IPv6 address or DNS name — no loopback restriction, so remote control-port deployments are accepted.
7. [doc/lightningd-config.5.md:627–639](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/lightningd-config.5.md#L627-L639)
   Documentation states the autotor:/statictor: argument is 'the IPv4 or IPv6 address of the Tor control port', i.e. a remote control port over the network is a supported deployment; doc/getting-started/advanced-setup/tor.md:118-123 documents the default local form addr=statictor:127.0.0.1:9051.

## Impact
Disclosure of any file readable by the lightningd user, notably the (by default unencrypted) hsm_secret: node identity and every channel/on-chain key, i.e. total loss of confidentiality (C:H). Holding the master secret lets the attacker sign as the node and sweep its on-chain and channel funds, so the system's integrity is fully compromised too (I:H). The node keeps running after the fake `250 OK`/ServiceID, so no direct availability impact (A:N).

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker must be able to answer connectd's TCP connect() to the configured Tor control address when lightningd starts: a local unprivileged user binding 127.0.0.1:9051 while Tor is not listening (unprivileged port; Tor down/restarting or boot ordering), or, with the documented remote TORIPADDRESS form, a party occupying or on-path to that address on the administrative network segment (Docker network/LAN). The attacker replies `250-AUTH METHODS=COOKIE COOKIEFILE="hsm_secret"` + `250 OK` and receives `AUTHENTICATE <hex of hsm_secret>`; several paths may be offered in one reply. No credentials, no user interaction; autotor/statictor configured and the attacker able to answer on the address are the preconditions (AT:P). Scored for the adjacent-network variant; the same-host variant is AV:L/PR:L, an on-path attacker across routed networks AV:N/AC:H.

## Recommended fix
negotiate_auth() trusts a filesystem path supplied by the unauthenticated party on the Tor control socket and transmits that file's contents to it, so an impersonated Tor control server reads arbitrary files (including the relative-path hsm_secret) as the lightningd user. Fix criteria: A path advertised in PROTOCOLINFO must never cause file contents to be sent to the peer: implement SAFECOOKIE (AUTHCHALLENGE with HMAC-SHA256 proof, which never reveals the cookie) and prefer it or HASHEDPASSWORD whenever advertised; if plain COOKIE is retained, only send a file that is exactly 32 bytes and lies under an operator-configured cookie path, never a relative or arbitrary path. Verify by pointing autotor/statictor at a fake control server advertising COOKIEFILE="hsm_secret" and confirming no hsm_secret bytes leave the process.

# websocketd blocks forever on incomplete frame after upgrade, leaking a process per connection

## Details
lightning_websocketd is forked by connectd for each inbound connection on a `bind-addr=ws:` listener (connectd/connectd.c:683-762). connectd bounds every pre-handshake connection with a timer of `connection_timeout_secs` (default 60s, options.c:1026) that calls conn_timeout() -> io_close(conn) (connectd.c:481-486, 557-560); for a raw TCP peer that stalls, this tears the connection down. For a websocket peer, connectd's conn is only its end of the socketpair to the child; closing it merely makes the child's stdout readable/EOF.

websocketd sets stdin (the client socket) blocking (websocketd.c:328) and protects only the HTTP upgrade with alarm(60) (193-203), cancelled before the frame loop. In the frame loop, as soon as the client fd is readable, websocket_to_lightningd() calls read_payload_header(), which blocks in read_all() for the 2-byte header and again for the extended length/mask bytes (245, 264), then blocks in read() until the announced payload length is consumed (299-308). None of these reads has a timeout, and while blocked the process is not in poll(), so the EOF connectd produces on stdout is never observed; it never writes to stdout either, so the default SIGPIPE/EPIPE path never fires.

An unauthenticated client therefore completes the upgrade, sends one byte (or a header announcing N payload bytes followed by fewer), and simply keeps the TCP connection idle (no SO_KEEPALIVE is set anywhere in connectd/websocketd, so the kernel never times it out), or drops its packets without FIN/RST so its own side costs nothing. connectd's timer fires and closes its socketpair end, but the child stays blocked forever holding its pid, the TCP socket and the socketpair fd. connectd does not record the child's pid and sets SIGCHLD to SIG_IGN (connectd.c:2590), so nothing supervises or kills stale helpers.

Each such connection deterministically leaves one permanent process; repeating it accumulates processes without bound in lightningd's uid, until the process/pid limit or memory is exhausted. The defect is a per-connection leak triggered by a specific malformed frame that circumvents the project's own handshake-timeout control, not a bandwidth-volume attack. Reachable only when the operator has configured a websocket listener (`bind-addr=ws:...`, documented in doc/lightningd-config.5.md as the way to accept browser/WebSocket peers).

## Evidence
1. [connectd/websocketd.c:237–284](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/websocketd.c#L237-L284)
   read_payload_header() uses blocking read_all() on the client socket (stdin) for the 2-byte header (245) and the extended length/mask bytes (264) with no timeout; a client that sends 1 byte, or an incomplete extended header, parks the process here indefinitely.
2. [connectd/websocketd.c:292–315](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/websocketd.c#L292-L315)
   websocket_to_lightningd() then loops with blocking read() (306) until the announced payload length is consumed; a header announcing N bytes followed by fewer than N blocks here. No timeout exists after the HTTP phase.
3. [connectd/websocketd.c:188–204](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/websocketd.c#L188-L204)
   alarm(60) (default SIGALRM action terminates the process) protects only the HTTP upgrade; it is cancelled with alarm(0) at 203 before the frame loop, so the frame phase has no watchdog.
4. [connectd/websocketd.c:328–343](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/websocketd.c#L328-L343)
   stdin is set blocking and the main loop only notices connectd closing its socketpair end via poll() on stdout; once blocked inside read_all/read on stdin, the EOF on stdout (connectd's handshake-timeout close) is never observed, and the process never writes so EPIPE/SIGPIPE never fires.
5. [connectd/connectd.c:551–571](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L551-L571)
   conn_in() arms the project's shipped control for stalled pre-handshake connections: a connection_timeout_secs (default 60s) timer calling conn_timeout() (481-486), which io_close()s connectd's conn. For a websocket connection that conn is only connectd's end of the socketpair (758), so the timeout cannot reach the blocked child.
6. [connectd/connectd.c:683–761](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L683-L761)
   connectd forks and execs one lightning_websocketd per inbound websocket connection, dup2()s the client socket onto the child's stdin, does not record childpid after a successful exec, and abandons its own copy of the client fd (761); nothing tracks or kills the child when the socketpair conn is later closed.
7. [connectd/connectd.c:2588–2590](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L2588-L2590)
   SIGCHLD is set to SIG_IGN so children are auto-reaped but never supervised; a child that never exits is never noticed.

## Impact
Each connection leaves one permanent lightning_websocketd process (pid, TCP socket, socketpair fd, stack and library memory) in lightningd's uid; nothing in connectd bounds the count or reaps stuck children, and the attacker's own cost per leaked process is transient. Accumulation proceeds at the attacker's pace until the user's process limit or memory is exhausted. At that point lightningd cannot fork subdaemons (channeld/onchaind) and bcli's bitcoin-cli exec fails, which is plugin_err()-fatal to an important plugin (plugins/bcli.c:167-169) and so stops lightningd: total loss of node availability with on-chain consequences. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker TCP-connects to the node's websocket listener, sends a valid HTTP upgrade request, then one frame-header byte (or a header announcing a payload it never sends) and goes idle or drops its packets. websocketd blocks in read()/read_all() forever and survives connectd's 60s timeout close. Repeat for N connections. Needs the non-default `bind-addr=ws:` listener (AT:PRESENT); no credentials, no user interaction, no defenses to defeat.

## Recommended fix
1. websocketd's frame-reading path performs synchronous reads on the remote client socket with no timeout and outside poll(), so a half-finished frame header or payload pins the process indefinitely and hides connectd's socketpair EOF. Fix criteria: A websocketd whose peer stops mid-frame must exit within a bounded time, and must notice connectd closing the socketpair while a frame is incomplete: e.g. an idle alarm/poll timeout during frame reading, or non-blocking stdin with frame parsing driven from poll() over both fds. Verify by sending an upgrade plus one header byte (and separately a header announcing 65535 bytes with no payload), then idling, and confirming the helper exits after the handshake timeout.
2. connectd does not retain the helper's pid and does not terminate it when the associated socketpair conn is freed (timeout or error), so a wedged helper is never reaped by the component that owns the connection lifetime. Fix criteria: When connectd frees the conn associated with a websocket helper (handshake timeout, error, shutdown), the helper process must be terminated or otherwise guaranteed to exit within bounded time. Verify that after conn_timeout fires for a stalled websocket connection, no lightning_websocketd process for that connection remains.

# Hooks dispatched to plugins that have not received init during concurrent dynamic plugin starts

## Details
lightningd registers a plugin's hooks when it parses the getmanifest reply (plugin.c plugin_parse_getmanifest_response -> plugin_hooks_add -> plugin_hook_register, which tal_arr_expand()s hook->hooks at plugin_hook.c:205) and only afterwards marks the plugin NEEDS_INIT. The dispatcher plugin_hook_call_next() (plugin_hook.c:333-368) sends the hook request to every non-NULL hook_instance whose filters match, without consulting plugin->plugin_state, whereas plugins_notify() explicitly skips plugins that are not INIT_COMPLETE (plugin.c:2472/2506/2519).

For a single `plugin start` this is masked: plugin_manifest_cb -> check_plugins_manifests -> plugins_config queues init on the same pipe before any hook can be sent. But check_plugins_manifests() returns early (plugin.c:134) while any plugin is still AWAITING_GETMANIFEST_RESPONSE, and `plugin startdir`, `plugin rescan` and two overlapping `plugin start` calls spawn several plugins at once (plugin_control.c:148-164, 243-257). The plugin that answers getmanifest first then sits in NEEDS_INIT, with its hooks live, until the slowest sibling answers (a Python plugin importing its dependencies can take seconds; the manifest timeout is 60 s). Any hook fired in that window - peer_connected on an inbound connection (peer_control.c:1984), custommsg on any odd-typed message from a connected peer (connectd/multiplex.c:1013-1027 -> connect_control.c:418), htlc_accepted, onion_message_recv, openchannel, invoice_payment, rpc_command - is delivered to the uninitialised plugin. Daemon startup is not affected: connectd_activate (lightningd.c:1444) follows plugins_config (1423).

What the three first-party plugin libraries do with a pre-init hook:
- libplugin (all shipped C plugins): plugin_err("Did not receive 'init' yet") and exit (libplugin.c:2117-2125).
- cln-plugin: Builder::configure() errors on any non-init message after getmanifest and the process exits (lib.rs:416-428).
- pyln-client: dispatches the handler with plugin.rpc == None (plugin.py:704-733). For hooks in hook_fallbacks a thrown exception becomes a safe fallback; for every other hook (onion_message_recv, commitment_revocation, openchannel2*, rbf_channel, recover) an exception - e.g. the handler touching plugin.rpc - becomes a JSON-RPC error reply, which lightningd turns into fatal() (plugin_hook.c:280).

In the first two cases lightningd sees EOF, plugin_kill()s the (non-important, dynamically started) plugin, fails the operator's start command via plugin_cmd_killed and synthesises PLUGIN_TERMINATED so the chain continues (plugin.c:225-269, 440-460): the direct result is that the dynamic start fails and the hook event is processed without that plugin. A peer that can keep firing cheap hooks (connect/disconnect loop for peer_connected; a stream of odd-typed custom messages for custommsg, which connectd forwards unconditionally) can make every startdir/rescan of a plugin set that includes a slow sibling fail for the plugins registering those hooks. In the pyln case, if the plugin's handler for a non-fallback hook raises pre-init, the same race takes lightningd down.

Root cause: hook instances become dispatchable at manifest time rather than at INIT_COMPLETE, and plugin_hook_call_next() has no state gate equivalent to plugins_notify()'s. The documented contract (a-day-in-the-life-of-a-plugin.md:26-28: init is the readiness signal and only 'once those two methods were called' does lightningd pass requests through; db_write.json rule 3 is the sole documented pre-init hook) is violated. This is a lightningd ordering defect; the reachable window is opened by a sanctioned operator command (AT:PRESENT) but the trigger is any remote peer.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:333–367](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L333-L367)
   plugin_hook_call_next() walks hook->hooks[] and sends the hook request to hook->hooks[i]->plugin via plugin_request_send() (line 366) without consulting plugin->plugin_state; hook_callable() (302-330) only applies NULL and string/int filters. A plugin in NEEDS_INIT therefore receives peer-triggered hook requests before init.
2. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:195–206](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L195-L206)
   plugin_hook_register() appends the new hook_instance to hook->hooks with tal_arr_expand() (line 205) immediately, regardless of hook_start/hook_done usage counting, so the instance is dispatchable from the moment the getmanifest reply is parsed.
3. [lightningd/plugin.c:128–159](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L128-L159)
   check_plugins_manifests() returns at line 134-135 while any plugin is AWAITING_GETMANIFEST_RESPONSE; plugins_config() (line 159, which sends init) runs only once every concurrently started plugin has answered. A plugin that answered first sits in NEEDS_INIT with live hook registrations and no init queued until the slowest sibling answers (60 s manifest timeout).
4. [lightningd/plugin.c:1813–1826](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1813-L1826)
   plugin_parse_getmanifest_response() registers hooks (plugin_hooks_add, line 1821) and then sets plugin_state = NEEDS_INIT (1826): hooks are registered before the plugin is initialised.
5. [lightningd/plugin\_control.c:147–163](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_control.c#L147-L163)
   plugin startdir (and rescan at 243-257, and two overlapping `plugin start` calls at 66-88) register several plugins and call plugins_send_getmanifest() for all of them at once (line 162), creating the window in which some plugins are NEEDS_INIT while others are still answering getmanifest. Dynamic plugins are registered with important=false (add_plugin_dir, plugin.c:1927).
6. [lightningd/connect\_control.c:417–418](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/connect_control.c#L417-L418)
   Peer trigger: every custom message a connected peer sends is forwarded by connectd (connectd/multiplex.c:1013-1027 forwards all odd types unconditionally) and fires plugin_hook_call_custommsg(); peer_connected fires on every inbound connection (peer_control.c:1984). A channel-less peer can therefore fire hooks at arbitrary rate to hit the window.
7. [lightningd/plugin.c:2467–2523](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2467-L2523)
   By contrast, plugin_single_notify()/plugins_notify() skip any plugin whose plugin_state != INIT_COMPLETE (2472, 2506, 2519): notifications honour the init contract, hooks do not.
8. [plugins/libplugin.c:2117–2124](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin.c#L2117-L2124)
   libplugin (all shipped C plugins) treats any request before init as fatal: plugin_err("Did not receive 'init' yet, but got '%s'") (NORETURN, exits the plugin). lightningd then sees EOF -> plugin_conn_finish -> plugin_kill (plugin.c:838-856), which fails the operator's start command (plugin_cmd_killed) and synthesises PLUGIN_TERMINATED so the hook chain continues without the plugin (destroy_plugin, plugin.c:225-269).
9. [plugins/src/lib.rs:416–427](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/src/lib.rs#L416-L427)
   cln-plugin's Builder::configure() requires the message after getmanifest to be init; any other message (a hook request) returns Err("Got unexpected message") and the plugin exits.
10. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:704–732](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L704-L732)
   pyln has no init gate: _dispatch_request() runs the hook handler with self.rpc still None (set only in _init at 1032). Hooks listed in hook_fallbacks (256-268) get a safe fallback result on exception; for any other hook (onion_message_recv, commitment_revocation, openchannel2*, rbf_channel, recover) an exception becomes set_exception() (146-172), a JSON-RPC error reply.
11. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:273–282](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L273-L282)
   A hook reply without `result` (the pyln error reply above) makes lightningd fatal() at line 280; only PLUGIN_TERMINATED is tolerated.
12. [doc/developers-guide/plugin-development/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-plugin.md:26–28](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/developers-guide/plugin-development/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-plugin.md#L26-L28)
   The documented plugin contract: init 'is also the signal that lightningd's JSON-RPC ... is now up and ready', and 'Once those two methods were called lightningd will start passing through incoming JSON-RPC commands'. Only db_write (doc/schemas/hook/db_write.json:14, rule 3) is documented as callable before init.

## Impact
Deterministic outcome for libplugin/cln-plugin plugins: the dynamically started (non-important) plugin exits, the operator's start command fails, and the hook event is processed without it; the node keeps running. Rated availability LOW for this outcome. If the plugin in the window is a pyln plugin whose handler for a hook outside hook_fallbacks raises pre-init (plugin.rpc is None), the error reply makes lightningd fatal() - a HIGH-availability variant that depends on third-party plugin code and is not rated here. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote peer (no channel needed for peer_connected/custommsg hooks; connectd forwards every odd-typed custom message to lightningd unconditionally). The operator runs the documented `plugin startdir`, `plugin rescan`, or two overlapping `plugin start` calls so that one plugin has answered getmanifest while another has not (tests/test_plugin.py:270,319,4814 exercise startdir with many plugins). The peer connects or sends a custom message in that window; lightningd dispatches the hook to the NEEDS_INIT plugin. Deterministic once the window exists, and the peer can fire the trigger continuously so timing is not a difficulty (AC:L); the window is a non-default runtime state created by an operator action outside the attacker's control, hence AT:PRESENT. No authentication or defence to bypass.

## Recommended fix
1. plugin_hook_call_next() dispatches to hook instances regardless of plugin->plugin_state, while hook instances are registered (and live in hook->hooks[]) at getmanifest-parse time, before init is sent. Fix criteria: No hook other than db_write may be sent to a plugin whose plugin_state is not INIT_COMPLETE: either hook_callable()/plugin_hook_call_next() must skip (treat as `continue`) plugins not yet initialised, or hook instances must only be made dispatchable when init completes. Verify by starting two plugins concurrently (one slow to manifest) while a peer connects: the fast plugin must receive init before any hook request, and the hook chain must still complete.
2. check_plugins_manifests() withholds init from already-manifested plugins until every concurrently started plugin has answered getmanifest, widening the pre-init window. Fix criteria: A plugin that has answered getmanifest should either receive init without waiting on unrelated plugins, or be excluded from dispatch until it does; verify that `plugin startdir` with a slow plugin never leaves another plugin in NEEDS_INIT while hooks fire.
