# Peer-replayed commitment_signed hijacks pending openchannel_bump, then lightningd asserts on psbt_changed

## Details
Dual-funding channels we opened (opener == LOCAL) that are still awaiting lock-in can be RBF'd with `openchannel_bump`. `openchannel_bump()` (dual_open_control.c:2685) parks the RPC command in `channel->open_attempt->cmd` (2720-2722) and sends `dualopend_rbf_init`.

Independently, after any reconnect dualopend runs with `state->reconnected = true` (dualopend.c:4626; lightningd restarts dualopend for DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN channels at peer_control.c:1465-1472) and `handle_commit_signed()` (dualopend.c:1334) accepts *every* `commitment_signed` the peer sends: its only gate is `!state->reconnected` (1341); there is no `has_commitments` or once-only check. Each is verified against the current commitment and forwarded to lightningd as `dualopend_commit_rcvd`. The peer holds a valid signature on our first commitment (it produced it during the open) and can replay the original message bytes as often as it likes. The two hsmd round-trips per replay are stateless (libhsmd.c:372 `handle_setup_channel` just records and replies; libhsmd.c:1900 `handle_validate_commitment_tx` derives and replies, no counter), so dualopend never dies on a repeat.

lightningd's `handle_commit_received()` (dual_open_control.c:3910) calls `wallet_update_channel_commit()`, which correctly detects the repeat (same txid as `inflight->last_tx`, 1479-1492) and returns `updated=false`, but the `LOCAL` branch (3955-3967) ignores that result: if `channel->open_attempt->cmd` is set it builds a response from `channel_current_inflight()` (the *old*, already-committed inflight), answers the parked command with it, and frees `channel->open_attempt`. (An open_attempt without a cmd is also freed, 3956-3960.) The REMOTE branch, by contrast, returns early on `!updated` (3969-3972).

lightningd processes one subdaemon message per event-loop iteration (subd.c:483-582, `io_read_wire` re-armed after each `msgcb`), each commit_rcvd costing a DB transaction with `wallet_channel_save`, so a peer streaming replays keeps a backlog of commit_rcvd queued ahead of lightningd's read of the dualopend pipe. When the operator's `openchannel_bump` runs, the next queued commit_rcvd lands after `open_attempt->cmd` is set and before dualopend has consumed `rbf_init` (dualopend prefers REQ_FD, 4637-4648, but a commit_rcvd already written is forwarded regardless). Consequences:
1. The operator's `openchannel_bump` returns success with the old inflight's PSBT and `commitments_secured: true` (build_commit_response, 3143), i.e. a lie about the RBF.
2. dualopend continues the RBF: `rbf_local_start` (3581) sends tx_init_rbf, the attacker answers tx_ack_rbf, `rbf_wrap_up` (3488) -> `send_next` (1532) -> once the cached changeset is exhausted `fetch_psbt_changes()` (1499) sends `dualopend_psbt_changed`; lightningd's `handle_psbt_changed()` starts with `assert(channel->open_attempt)` (3663) and aborts the whole node. Every peer, HTLC and plugin on the node is taken down; on restart the attempt is gone so there is no crash loop, but repeating the bump reproduces it.

The ledger item dismissed-dual-open-control-3943-e67c judged the repeat benign because 'LOCAL path has no cmd'; that is false while an RBF bump is pending. Each replayed commitment_signed also costs lightningd a `channel_set_last_tx` + `wallet_channel_save` DB write (not counted here).

Root cause: `handle_commit_received` does not verify that the commitment it was handed belongs to the open attempt it is about to complete (e.g. that `updated` is true / the inflight is the attempt's), and dualopend forwards repeated commitment_signed without a once-only check.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3954–3967](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3954-L3967)
   handle_commit_received(), LOCAL opener branch: whenever dualopend forwards a DUALOPEND_COMMIT_RCVD it takes whatever command is parked in channel->open_attempt->cmd, answers it with build_commit_response(cmd, channel, channel_current_inflight()) and frees channel->open_attempt. Nothing ties the received commitment to the attempt: the commitment can be a re-send for the already-committed (old) inflight while open_attempt belongs to a freshly started RBF.
2. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:2685–2731](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L2685-L2731)
   openchannel_bump(): sets channel->open_attempt = oa with oa->cmd = the user's openchannel_bump command and sends dualopend_rbf_init. From this moment until dualopend's own commit_rcvd for the RBF, the LOCAL branch above will hand the bump command to any stray commit_rcvd.
3. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3650–3664](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3650-L3664)
   handle_psbt_changed() begins with assert(channel->open_attempt). Once the stray commit_rcvd freed the open attempt, the very next dualopend_psbt_changed of the still-running RBF negotiation aborts lightningd.
4. [openingd/dualopend.c:1334–1361](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1334-L1361)
   handle_commit_signed(): after a reconnect (state->reconnected) every peer commitment_signed is verified against the current commitment and forwarded to lightningd as dualopend_commit_rcvd, with no once-only guard. The peer can simply replay the original commitment_signed bytes.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:1499–1526](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1499-L1526)
   fetch_psbt_changes(): during the RBF negotiation (send_next -> fetch_psbt_changes) dualopend sends dualopend_psbt_changed to lightningd, the message that trips the assert above.
6. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1430–1497](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1430-L1497)
   wallet_update_channel_commit(): for a repeated commitment it returns false (txid matches inflight->last_tx) but handle_commit_received's LOCAL branch ignores the return value, so idempotency is not achieved on the LOCAL path (the REMOTE path does check it).
7. [openingd/dualopend.c:4637–4647](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L4637-L4647)
   dualopend main loop: REQ_FD is preferred but a peer message already being processed, or a commit_rcvd already written to lightningd's pipe, is not undone when rbf_init arrives; this is the race window the peer floods.

## Impact
lightningd aborts (assert) taking down every channel, HTLC and plugin: availability HIGH. The bump RPC receives a false success with the old PSBT and open_attempt state is destroyed, misleading the operator/automation: integrity LOW. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: the remote peer of a dual-funded channel we opened (opener LOCAL), after a reconnect and before lock-in. It replays our first commitment_signed in a loop; dualopend forwards each as commit_rcvd. When the operator runs openchannel_bump (dual-funding is opt-in via --experimental-dual-fund, and the bump is a manual RPC), any commit_rcvd landing after open_attempt->cmd is set resolves the command with stale data and frees the attempt; dualopend's RBF negotiation then sends psbt_changed and lightningd aborts on assert(channel->open_attempt). Requires winning the timing window and the experimental option, hence AT:PRESENT and UI:ACTIVE (operator must issue the bump).

## Recommended fix
1. handle_commit_received's LOCAL branch completes whatever open attempt is pending using whatever inflight is current, without checking that the received commitment is new and belongs to that attempt (it ignores wallet_update_channel_commit's updated=false). Fix criteria: A commit_rcvd that does not introduce a new commitment (updated == false), or whose inflight is not the one the pending open attempt negotiated, must not resolve or free channel->open_attempt; the bump command must only be answered by the RBF's own commitment. Verify by replaying commitment_signed while a bump is pending: the command stays pending and the RBF completes normally.
2. dualopend forwards every post-reconnect commitment_signed to lightningd, giving the peer an unbounded trigger for commit_rcvd side effects (and DB writes). Fix criteria: dualopend accepts at most one commitment_signed per funding attempt after reconnect (e.g. once tx_state->has_commitments is set, a further commitment_signed is ignored or treated as a protocol error) so repeats never reach lightningd. Verify that a second commitment_signed produces no commit_rcvd.
3. handle_psbt_changed asserts on channel->open_attempt instead of failing the attempt gracefully when state has been torn down. Fix criteria: A psbt_changed arriving with no open attempt must fail the dualopend negotiation (dualopend_fail / channel error) rather than abort lightningd. Verify no assert path remains reachable from subdaemon messages.

# bkpr-listbalances kills bookkeeper when an injected movement makes an account's debits exceed credits

## Details
do_list_balances (bookkeeper.c:932-950) computes credit - debit for every account bookkeeper knows and treats an underflow as a fatal invariant violation (plugin_err). For node-generated ledgers the invariant holds: the external account never receives debits (common/coin_mvt.c constructors only credit it; new_coin_external_spend credits 0), channel_close debits equal lightningd's channel->our_msat (onchain_control.c:1890 -> onchaind.c:3494), which is updated in the same functions that save the HTLC channel moves (peer_htlcs.c:2042/2095) and never twice for an on-chain fulfil (remove_htlc_out is reachable only from the HTLC state machine at RCVD_REMOVE_ACK_REVOCATION), penalty_adj is recorded as an equal credit/debit pair, and a splice's close debit is the previous balance. The invariant is not enforced for injected movements, which lightningd stores without any consistency check and which can never be deleted:

(a) injectutxospend (lightningd/coin_mvts.c:462-495) records a debit for any account and amount with no requirement that the account has a deposit; one call with account="x" leaves x with debit > credit.

(b) injectutxodeposit alone suffices: amount_msat is accepted up to u64 max (param_msat_as_sat requires only whole satoshis), new_foreign_deposit stores it as a credit, db_bind_credit_debit (wallet.c:7006-7017) binds it as a raw u64 into a signed 64-bit column, and db_col_credit_or_debit (7293-7306) reads a negative value back as a debit. injectutxodeposit account="x" amount_msat=18446744073709551000 is therefore returned by listchainmoves as a 616 msat debit tagged deposit, and account x has debit 616 > credit 0. (The same wrap mis-reports the movement to every listchainmoves consumer, a lightningd data-integrity defect noted here as evidence.)

Either way, the next bkpr-listbalances (a routine call for dashboards such as RTL, or made by the bearer if the rune allows it) runs do_list_balances, amount_msat_sub fails for account x, plugin_err exits bookkeeper, and lightningd exits because bookkeeper is important (plugin.c:297-303). The poisoned chain move persists in lightningd's database (there is no delete RPC), so after every restart the first bkpr-listbalances crashes the node again until the operator discovers the row and injects a compensating deposit of the right size.

Attacker position: a commando/clnrest rune bearer whose rune permits injectutxodeposit (or injectutxospend) -- the same deliberately-granted, non-default position accepted for bkpr-csv-export-gmtime-null-deref-injected-timestamp and bkpr-empty-account-name-datastore-key-lightningd-fatal. Such a rune concedes falsified accounting rows, not a persistent node shutdown. The utxo_deposit/utxo_spend notification path (bookkeeper.c:1692-1789) reaches the same sink but is only driven by installed plugins, which the threat model trusts.

Related sinks on the same injected data (not separately filed): account_get_credit_debit ignores json_to_msat failures (recorder.c:428-429, 449-450), and two wrapped amounts on one account make sqlite's SUM() overflow, which the sql plugin returns as an error and bookkeeper's jsonrpc_request_sync turns into plugin_err (libplugin.c read_sync_rpc_reply).

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:932–949](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L932-L949)
   do_list_balances sums every account (including 'external', before the skip at 949) and calls plugin_err when credit - debit underflows; the important plugin's exit stops lightningd. Every bkpr-listbalances call re-runs this, and the underlying chain moves cannot be deleted, so the failure recurs on every call after every restart.
2. [plugins/bkpr/recorder.c:400–465](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/recorder.c#L400-L465)
   account_get_credit_debit sums credit_msat/debit_msat over chainmoves and channelmoves for the account; it also ignores json_to_msat's return (428-429, 449-450), so a negative SUM (possible once wrapped amounts are mirrored) leaves credit/debit uninitialised.
3. [lightningd/coin\_mvts.c:462–494](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/coin_mvts.c#L462-L494)
   injectutxospend records a debit (new_foreign_withdrawal) for any account string and any amount with no check that a matching deposit exists, so a single call leaves an account with debit > credit.
4. [lightningd/coin\_mvts.c:402–454](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/coin_mvts.c#L402-L454)
   injectutxodeposit accepts any amount_msat up to u64 max (param_msat_as_sat only requires whole satoshis); new_foreign_deposit stores it as a credit.
5. [wallet/wallet.c:7006–7016](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L7006-L7016)
   db_bind_credit_debit binds a credit via db_bind_amount_msat (raw u64 -> signed 64-bit column); a credit >= 2^63 msat is therefore stored negative.
6. [wallet/wallet.c:7293–7305](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L7293-L7305)
   db_col_credit_or_debit reads the column as s64 and treats any negative value as a debit, so an injected deposit of 2^64-616 msat is returned by listchainmoves as a 616 msat *debit* tagged 'deposit' -- a debit with no credit for a fresh account, using injectutxodeposit alone.
7. [db/bindings.c:235–238](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/bindings.c#L235-L238)
   db_bind_amount_msat is a raw u64 bind with no range check; sqlite/postgres store it as signed INT64.

## Impact
lightningd exits whenever bkpr-listbalances is called, and the triggering chain move cannot be removed, so the node is repeatedly taken down until the operator diagnoses the account and injects a compensating movement of the right size. No confidentiality impact. Integrity of accounting rows is already within what an injectutxodeposit/injectutxospend grant concedes (the bearer can write arbitrary foreign deposits and withdrawals directly), so the wrapped-amount mis-report adds no integrity gain beyond the grant.

## Reproduction steps
1. A rune bearer permitted injectutxospend (or injectutxodeposit) issues one RPC over commando (plugins/commando.c forwards any method the rune passes checkrune for) or clnrest (generic POST /v1/{method}, rune required) creating a chain move whose debit exceeds the account's credits: a plain foreign withdrawal on a fresh account name, or a deposit >= 2^63 msat that db_bind_u64/sqlite3_bind_int64 (or INT8OID on postgres) persists negative and db_col_credit_or_debit reads back as a debit. Bookkeeper's refresh ingests it without error (maybe_update_onchain_fees skips with fewer than two events for the txid; do_account_close_checks returns NULL for a non-channel account with no close). The next bkpr-listbalances -- by any dashboard, the operator, or the bearer -- runs do_list_balances, amount_msat_sub(credit=0, debit>0) fails and plugin_err exits bookkeeper; lightningd exits because the plugin is important. The row is permanent (no delete RPC), so the crash recurs after every restart. Attack requirements are present because the deployment must have issued a rune granting this undocumented internal method (no doc/schemas entry; commented 'Internal interfaces for bookkeeper.c'); privileges are low (a method-scoped rune, not operator access).

## Recommended fix
1. do_list_balances treats an account whose debits exceed credits as a fatal condition in an important plugin, although injected (foreign) movements give no such guarantee. Fix criteria: A negative balance must be reported (e.g. logged and shown as a negative or zero balance / flagged account) rather than terminating the plugin. Verify: after injectutxospend of an unmatched withdrawal, bkpr-listbalances returns a result and lightningd keeps running.
2. lightningd persists coin-movement amounts as raw u64 in a signed 64-bit column and interprets the sign on read, so an injected credit >= 2^63 msat is stored and reported as a debit. Fix criteria: injectutxodeposit/injectutxospend must reject amounts that cannot be represented (>= 2^63 msat, or above the chain's total supply), and/or the credit/debit encoding must round-trip for every accepted value. Verify: injecting such an amount returns an invalid-params error and listchainmoves never reports a deposit as a debit.
3. account_get_credit_debit ignores parse failures of the summed amounts and a sql error on SUM overflow is fatal, so malformed or extreme mirrored values become crashes. Fix criteria: Parse failures and sql errors in balance computation must surface as an RPC error for that command, not plugin_err. Verify with a mirrored negative/overflowing sum that bkpr-listbalances returns an error and the plugin survives.

# dualopend SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE handler: unguarded channel_set_state lets a compromised dualopend fatal() lightningd

## Details
handle_channel_closed() (lightningd/dual_open_control.c:1757-1781) handles WIRE_DUALOPEND_SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE from the dualopend subdaemon. After peer_start_closingd() it unconditionally calls channel_set_state(channel, CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN, CLOSINGD_SIGEXCHANGE, ...), and channel_set_state() fatal()s when channel->state is not the stated old state (channel.c:1051-1053). The dispatcher (4067-4071) accepts the message in any state while dualopend owns the channel, so a compromised dualopend (threat-model adversary 6, e.g. after a peer-side exploit) that writes a bare SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE plus one fd without a preceding GOT_SHUTDOWN aborts the whole lightningd process:

- Channel in DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED / DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN: channel->shutdown_scriptpubkey[REMOTE] is NULL, so peer_start_closingd() calls channel_internal_error() and returns (closing_control.c:468-471). channel_fail_perm() frees the dualopend subd and moves the channel to AWAITING_UNILATERAL (channel.c:1128-1134). The handler continues into channel_set_state(), the state mismatches, fatal().
- Channel in DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT (uncommitted): channel_internal_error() deletes the channel (channel.c:1296-1300) and channel_set_state() then runs on freed memory.

The channeld equivalent peer_start_closingd_after_shutdown() (channel_control.c:1457-1476) guards the same transition with `if (channel->state == CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN)`; the dualopend handler lacks it.

An honest dualopend cannot reach this: shutdown_complete is emitted only when both shutdown_sent flags are set (dualopend.c:333-337); the REMOTE flag is set only after dualopend_got_shutdown has been sent and lightningd's send_shutdown reply received (543-579), by which time lightningd has stored the remote script and set CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN (dual_open_control.c:1708-1752; the `close` RPC sets the state before sending dualopend_send_shutdown, closing_control.c:919-929); on restart the reinit flags are derived from exactly that stored state and script (dual_open_control.c:4661-4662). The attacker is therefore the compromised subdaemon that lightningd's per-message checks (log_broken + tal_free on unexpected types, channel_internal_error on malformed ones) are meant to bound to its own channel; this path escalates that to loss of the whole node. The DB transaction around the message is rolled back on abort, so it is a one-shot crash per compromised daemon.

Note: the handler's parse-failure branch (1764-1770, close(fds[0]); close(fds[1]) after channel_internal_error) is dead code — the generated fromwire for a fieldless message only re-checks the type the dispatcher already matched and returns cursor != NULL (tools/gen/impl_template:350-410) — so the freed-fd/out-of-bounds close is not reachable and is not part of this finding.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1773–1780](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1773-L1780)
   handle_channel_closed() success path: new_peer_fd_arr(), peer_start_closingd(), then channel_set_state(channel, CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN, CLOSINGD_SIGEXCHANGE, ...) with no check of the current state and no check that peer_start_closingd succeeded. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [lightningd/channel.c:1051–1053](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1051-L1053)
   channel_set_state() fatal()s (abort of lightningd) when channel->state != old_state.
3. [lightningd/closing\_control.c:468–471](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/closing_control.c#L468-L471)
   peer_start_closingd(): with no remote shutdown script it calls channel_internal_error() and returns; the caller in dual_open_control.c continues into channel_set_state.
4. [lightningd/channel.c:1128–1135](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1128-L1135)
   channel_fail_perm(): channel_set_owner(NULL) frees the dualopend subd and, for committed states (DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED, DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN), moves the channel to AWAITING_UNILATERAL, so the handler's subsequent channel_set_state(CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN -> ...) mismatches.
5. [lightningd/channel.c:1296–1299](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1296-L1299)
   channel_internal_error() on an uncommitted channel (DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT) deletes the channel; the handler then calls channel_set_state() on freed memory.
6. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:4067–4070](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L4067-L4070)
   Dispatcher: WIRE_DUALOPEND_SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE is accepted whenever dualopend owns the channel, requests one fd and calls handle_channel_closed with no state precondition. The surrounding switch shows lightningd's intended bound on a misbehaving subd: unexpected types get log_broken + tal_free(dualopend), not a crash.
7. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1457–1476](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1457-L1476)
   The channeld sibling peer_start_closingd_after_shutdown() guards the same transition with `if (channel->state == CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN)`; the dualopend handler lacks this guard.
8. [openingd/dualopend.c:543–579](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L543-L579)
   Honest dualopend sets shutdown_sent[REMOTE] only after writing dualopend_got_shutdown and synchronously receiving lightningd's send_shutdown reply, i.e. after lightningd has stored the remote script and set CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN; shutdown_complete (333-337) needs both flags. The crashing path is therefore reachable only from a compromised dualopend.
9. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:4661–4662](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L4661-L4662)
   peer_restart_dualopend() seeds a restarted dualopend's shutdown flags from channel->state == CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN and channel->shutdown_scriptpubkey[REMOTE] != NULL, so a restarted honest daemon cannot hold both flags unless lightningd is already in the state the handler expects.

## Impact
fatal() aborts lightningd: every channel, forwarding and RPC stop until the operator restarts (availability HIGH); the enclosing DB transaction is rolled back so it is a one-shot crash, not a restart loop. No data is disclosed or altered: the close()-of-freed-fds branch is dead code, so no integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a compromised dualopend process (threat-model adversary 6) writing one 2-byte WIRE_DUALOPEND_SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE plus any fd on its master pipe without first sending GOT_SHUTDOWN. lightningd runs handle_channel_closed; peer_start_closingd fails for lack of a remote script (or the channel is uncommitted and gets deleted), and the unguarded channel_set_state fatal()s or dereferences the freed channel. Local position inside the host with lightningd's uid, no further conditions, deterministic.

## Recommended fix
handle_channel_closed assumes the channel is in CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN and that peer_start_closingd cannot fail or change the state, so it performs an unguarded channel_set_state that fatal()s (or runs on a deleted channel) on mismatch. Fix criteria: An unexpected or failed SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE from dualopend must fail only that channel: reject the message unless the channel is in CHANNELD_SHUTTING_DOWN with the remote shutdown script stored (or guard the transition as peer_start_closingd_after_shutdown does), and return without touching the channel after peer_start_closingd reports or causes a failure. Verify that an out-of-state SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE leaves lightningd running with the channel failed.

# dualopend commit handlers write channel->open_attempt after channel_internal_error freed the channel

## Details
handle_commit_ready() and handle_commit_received() (dual_open_control.c) process dualopend_commit_ready and dualopend_commit_rcvd. Several of their error paths call channel_internal_error() and then continue with `channel->open_attempt = tal_free(channel->open_attempt)` and `notify_channel_open_failed(ld, &channel->cid)` (3764-3769, 3783-3796, 3838-3844, 3928-3932; also 3866-3872 and 3892-3898 in the RBF arms).

For a first open the channel is DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT when COMMIT_READY arrives and DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY (no tx_signatures sent) when COMMIT_RCVD arrives. In both states channel_internal_error() frees the channel: directly via delete_channel() for the uncommitted state (channel.c:1294-1298), and via channel_fail_permanent() -> channel_fail_perm()'s open_uncommitted branch for COMMIT_READY (channel.c:1146-1156). The subsequent `channel->open_attempt = ...` is a write into freed heap memory and `&channel->cid` a read of it; with the allocator reusing the block this is memory corruption of lightningd, not just a crash. (In the RBF arms the channel is DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN, which survives, so 3866/3892 are only state-inconsistent, not UAF.)

Reachability. An honest dualopend produces well-formed messages, and the outpoint-reuse/amount-overflow conditions need a txid collision or absurd amounts, which is why lead dismissed-dual-open-control-3783-98ec judged 3783-3843 unreachable *by a peer*. That judgement did not consider the fromwire-failure sites (3764, 3928) nor the compromised-subdaemon position: a dualopend compromised through a peer exploit (threat-model adversary 6) sends a truncated COMMIT_READY or COMMIT_RCVD, or a COMMIT_READY naming another channel's funding outpoint, and lightningd writes to the freed channel. lightningd's channel_internal_error() is exactly the containment meant to bound such a daemon to its own channel; these handlers defeat it. This is the dualopend counterpart of the recorded compromised-channeld-htlc-reply-double-free and splice-abort-null-inflight-continue-after-internal-error patterns.

Remote-peer-only reachability is not claimed; the honest-peer bound of the earlier dismissal stands for 3783/3838.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3764–3769](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3764-L3769)
   handle_commit_ready(): on fromwire failure it calls channel_internal_error(channel, ...) and then writes channel->open_attempt = tal_free(channel->open_attempt) and reads channel->peer->ld and &channel->cid for notify_channel_open_failed. The first COMMIT_READY arrives while the channel is DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT (new_unsaved_channel, channel.c:363), where channel_internal_error() delete_channel()s it (channel.c:1294-1298): write and reads of freed memory.
2. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3928–3932](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3928-L3932)
   handle_commit_received(): same pattern on fromwire failure. This message arrives while the channel is DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY (set by wallet_commit_channel, 1563) with no tx_signatures sent (inflight->i_sent_sigs is only set at 1947, after commit), where channel_internal_error -> channel_fail_permanent -> channel_fail_perm takes the open_uncommitted branch and delete_channel()s (channel.c:1146-1156); the handler then writes to the freed channel.
3. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3783–3796](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3783-L3796)
   Funding-outpoint-in-use path: channel_internal_error() then channel->open_attempt = tal_free(...) and &channel->cid, in DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT (freed) for a first open. Unreachable for an honest peer (txid collision against a per-channel funding pubkey); a compromised dualopend chooses the outpoint field freely.
4. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3838–3844](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3838-L3844)
   wallet_commit_channel() failure path in DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT: channel_internal_error() frees the channel, then channel->open_attempt is written. Reachable from a compromised dualopend via an amount that fails amount_sat_to_msat() (dual_open_control.c:1536-1543).
5. [lightningd/channel.c:1281–1308](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1281-L1308)
   channel_internal_error(): for channel_state_uncommitted (only DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT, channel.h:709-713) it channel_set_owner(NULL) (freeing the dualopend subd via subd_release_channel) and delete_channel()s the struct before returning; otherwise channel_fail_permanent, which for DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY without sigs also deletes (1146-1156). Callers must not touch channel afterwards.
6. [lightningd/channel.c:89–130](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L89-L130)
   delete_channel(): after DB close, hsmd forget and the state-change notification it tal_free(channel)s (line 127), which also frees every tal child (open_attempt, log, inflights); the handlers' subsequent channel->open_attempt / channel->peer / channel->cid accesses are into this freed block.
7. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1560–1571](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1560-L1571)
   wallet_commit_channel() asserts DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT on entry and sets DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY; DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED is only set by wallet_update_channel_commit (1457-1473) when COMMIT_RCVD is processed, so the states at the sites above are as stated.

## Impact
Write-after-free into lightningd's heap: the handler reads the pointer at the freed channel's open_attempt slot and tal_free()s it, then stores NULL there, and reads channel->peer through the freed block (glibc free clobbers the first 16 bytes; delete_channel's DB/notification work and maybe_delete_peer may reuse the chunk). Undefined behaviour in the parent process: at minimum a crash of lightningd taking every channel down (availability HIGH); if the chunk was reused, a live object's pointer field is freed/zeroed with no attacker steering (integrity LOW). The containment channel_internal_error is designed to provide against a rogue dualopend is lost. No confidentiality effect shown.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker runs code inside a lightning_dualopend process (post peer-side exploit; the threat model's adversary 6) and writes to its lightningd pipe, which subd.c reads length-prefixed and dispatches by type to dual_opend_msg (4019-4040) with channel = dualopend->channel. Deterministic path: during a first open send a truncated dualopend_commit_ready (channel in DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT) or, after COMMIT_READY was accepted, a truncated dualopend_commit_rcvd (channel in DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMIT_READY, no sigs sent); channel_internal_error frees the channel and the handler writes channel->open_attempt and reads channel->peer->ld and channel->cid from the freed block. subd.c's mark_freed guard protects only sd, not the handler's own channel pointer. No race, no user interaction; the position is same-uid local code execution in a subdaemon.

## Recommended fix
The commit handlers treat channel_internal_error() as non-destructive and keep dereferencing channel, but in the uncommitted/COMMIT_READY states it frees the channel. Fix criteria: After channel_internal_error() the handler must return without touching channel (open_attempt cleanup already happens inside channel_cleanup_commands; notify_channel_open_failed must use a copied channel_id or be called before the error). Verify that a truncated COMMIT_READY/COMMIT_RCVD from dualopend fails the channel without any access to the freed struct (e.g. under ASan).

# payment_succeeded asserts on deleted payments row when a preimage appears on-chain after an on-chain HTLC failure

## Details
payment_succeeded() (lightningd/pay.c:359-377) assumes the payments row for (payment_hash, partid, groupid) still exists: it runs wallet_payment_set_status() (a no-op UPDATE if the row is gone), then wallet_payment_by_hash() and assert(payment). Its counterpart payment_failed() tolerates a missing row under COMPAT_V052 (the default build). A FAILED row is legitimately deletable (delpay, documented to delete 'all payment parts with matching status'; or the autoclean plugin's failedpays sweep), and the corresponding hout can still be fulfilled later by an on-chain preimage.

Path: we pay an MPP invoice (pay/xpay) and two parts A and B (same payment_hash, different partid, different amounts) go out over the same channel to a peer that is, or colludes with, the payee. The channel is force-closed; onchaind tracks both offered HTLC outputs (distinguished by amount, onchaind.c:2026-2056). A expires first (B's cltv_expiry at our hop is larger because its downstream route is longer, which the payee shapes via route hints/blinded paths up to the payer's maxdelay of 2016 blocks; alternatively, with equal expiries, the peer pins our timeout spend of B with a conflicting unconfirmed preimage spend). Our timeout spend of A reaches reasonable_depth (3) -> onchaind htlc_timeout(A) (onchaind.c:1378-1388) -> onchain_failed_our_htlc() (peer_htlcs.c:1913-1993) -> payment_failed() marks row A FAILED; hout A stays in ld->htlcs_out with failmsg set. In the window before the peer resolves B (potentially hundreds to ~2000 blocks), the operator runs `delpay <hash> failed` (pay.c:2342-2401; deletes every FAILED row for the hash, wallet.c:4116-4147, with no check for still-pending parts) or autoclean with autoclean-failedpays-age deletes part A once created_at is old enough. The peer then confirms its preimage spend of B -> onchaind extracted_preimage (onchaind.c:1066-1073) -> onchain_fulfilled_htlc() (peer_htlcs.c:1727-1789) iterates every hout on the channel with that hash: for hout A (am_origin, hout->in == NULL so the guard at 1760 does not apply, preimage NULL) it clears failmsg, forces RCVD_REMOVE_HTLC and calls fulfill_our_htlc_out() -> payment_succeeded(A) -> wallet_payment_by_hash() returns NULL -> assert fires and lightningd aborts.

The abort happens inside the per-message DB transaction (subd.c:493/590), so the fulfilment write is rolled back while hout A's failed state and the delpay were committed earlier. On restart hout A is reloaded (peer_control.c:3231-3262 loads HTLCs for every channel, ONCHAIN included), onchaind_restart() (onchain_control.c:1938-1975) replays the chain from the funding-spend block, re-sends htlc_timeout(A) (harmless: already failed) and then extracted_preimage(B), and lightningd aborts again: a crash loop until the operator repairs the database by hand. The same assert is reachable without MPP if our confirmed timeout spend is reorged out in favour of a preimage spend, which is not attacker-feasible; the MPP variant is attacker-timed.

Root cause: fulfilment bookkeeping dereferences a payments row that the system's own documented RPC (and a shipped plugin) may delete once the row is FAILED, and onchain_fulfilled_htlc() re-opens failed am_origin HTLCs without checking that their payment record still exists.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/pay.c:359–377](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L359-L377)
   payment_succeeded() runs wallet_payment_set_status() (an UPDATE that silently matches zero rows when the row is gone, wallet.c:4298-4336), then wallet_payment_by_hash() (returns NULL when no row matches, wallet.c:4252-4296) and assert(payment). Its counterpart payment_failed() (pay.c:547-576) tolerates a missing row under COMPAT_V052 (the default build); nothing here does.
2. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1727–1789](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1727-L1789)
   onchain_fulfilled_htlc() iterates every hout on the channel whose payment_hash matches the extracted preimage. For an am_origin hout, hout->in is NULL so the failonion guard at 1760 does not apply; if hout->preimage is NULL it frees failmsg/failonion, forces RCVD_REMOVE_HTLC and calls fulfill_our_htlc_out() -> payment_succeeded() (1690) without checking that the payments row still exists.
3. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1913–1993](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1913-L1993)
   onchain_failed_our_htlc() (from onchaind htlc_timeout / missing_htlc_output) sets failmsg, forces RCVD_REMOVE_HTLC, persists the hout and calls payment_failed() so the row becomes FAILED (and deletable), but the hout stays in ld->htlcs_out: remove_htlc_out() (2076) only runs on the channeld revoke path and free_htlcs() (2913) only on irrevocably_resolved, which cannot happen while another HTLC output is unresolved.
4. [lightningd/pay.c:2342–2401](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L2342-L2401)
   json_delpay rejects only status=pending; with status=failed and no partid/groupid it deletes every FAILED row for the payment_hash (wallet_payment_delete, wallet.c:4116-4147) while other parts of the same hash are still PENDING. doc/schemas/delpay.json documents exactly this ('all payment parts with matching status are deleted'). plugins/autoclean.c:490-509,555-575 issues the same delpay per failed part once created_at is older than autoclean-failedpays-age.
5. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1378–1388](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1378-L1388)
   onchaind reports htlc_timeout for one HTLC output as soon as our timeout spend of that output reaches reasonable_depth (3, onchain_control.c:1908), independently of other outputs with the same payment hash that are still unresolved. match_htlc_output (2026-2056) distinguishes outputs by amount, so two MPP parts with the same hash and different amounts are tracked separately.
6. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1066–1073](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1066-L1073)
   handle_htlc_onchain_fulfill() sends extracted_preimage when the peer's preimage spend of any of our offered HTLC outputs is mined (output_spent, 1272-1282). The peer chooses when that happens: any time before the output's cltv_expiry, or later by pinning our timeout spend.
7. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:488–558](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L488-L558)
   handle_extracted_preimage() and handle_onchain_htlc_timeout() forward both onchaind reports to peer_htlcs.c unconditionally, inside the per-message DB transaction of subd.c:493/590, so the abort rolls back the fulfilment write while the earlier FAILED state and the delpay stay committed.
8. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:1938–1975](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L1938-L1975)
   onchaind_restart() sets onchaind_replay_height to the funding-spend block (not a persisted progress height) and replays the chain from there on every startup, so the peer's preimage spend is re-delivered as extracted_preimage and the assert recurs on each restart while the row is missing: a crash loop.

## Impact
lightningd aborts on assert(payment) and, because onchaind replays the chain from the funding-spend block on every restart while the row stays deleted, crash-loops until the operator edits the database (re-inserting the row or deleting the HTLC). Every channel and in-flight HTLC is unserviceable meanwhile, with on-chain timeout consequences. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer that is, or colludes with, the payee of an MPP payment whose parts share our channel to it: it force-closes (or lets us), lets one part be timed out by us on-chain, and settles another part of the same hash with the preimage on-chain later, either simply before that part's later cltv_expiry (payee-shaped route) or by pinning our timeout spend. The row deletion in between is the operator's documented routine delpay of failed parts (UI:ACTIVE), or unattended when autoclean-failedpays-age is configured (then UI:NONE). attack_requirements PRESENT: an MPP payment with two parts on one channel, a force close, and the deletion inside the attacker-held window. No privileges: the peer needs only a channel with us.

## Recommended fix
1. payment_succeeded() asserts that the payments row exists even though FAILED rows are deletable via delpay/autoclean and an on-chain preimage can later resurrect the corresponding am_origin hout through onchain_fulfilled_htlc(). Fix criteria: A late preimage for an HTLC whose payments row has been deleted must not terminate lightningd: payment_succeeded() (and fulfill_our_htlc_out()) must handle a missing row by logging and continuing, as payment_failed() already does under COMPAT_V052, and onchain_fulfilled_htlc() should not re-open an already-failed am_origin HTLC whose payment record is gone. Verify: fail part A on-chain, delpay the FAILED row, deliver a preimage spend for part B of the same hash, and confirm lightningd stays up, records the preimage for B, and survives a restart with onchaind replay.
2. delpay (and autoclean on top of it) deletes FAILED parts of a payment_hash while other parts of the same hash are still PENDING and their HTLCs are live on-chain, leaving in-memory houts that reference deleted payment records. Fix criteria: Deleting a FAILED part while a sibling part of the same payment_hash is still pending or has an unresolved on-chain HTLC must either be refused, or must leave the runtime able to fulfil that hash later without dereferencing the deleted row.

# createproof `include` of invoice TLV types absent from payer_proof aborts the offers plugin

## Details
The `createproof` RPC (plugins/offers_proof.c, exposed by the `offers` plugin, documented in doc/schemas/createproof.json) builds a BOLT12 payer_proof from a paid bolt12 invoice. Its optional `include` parameter lists TLV field types to copy into the proof, either by name (restricted to field_names[]) or by raw u64 number (param_include_types, lines 393-398: any value accepted; the schema explicitly advertises numbers for 'unknown fields').

common/bolt12_proof.c:make_unsigned_proof_() copies every invoice field whose type the caller listed (include_field_fn), linearises them with towire_tlvstream_raw, and re-decodes the stream with fromwire_tlv_payer_proof(). The payer_proof TLV (wire/bolt12_wire.csv:198-270) does not define several even types that invoices legitimately carry: 0 (invreq_metadata, present in every invoice obtained via fetchinvoice because invoice_matches_request forces the invoice's 0-159 range to equal our invreq), 1000000024, 1000000026 and 2000000092 (recurrence fields). The generic TLV parser fails on unknown even types (wire/tlvstream.c:205-217), fromwire_tlv_payer_proof returns NULL, and the result is checked only by `assert(pptlv)` (bolt12_proof.c:134). The assert aborts the offers plugin; offers is an `important` builtin plugin, so lightningd shuts down (lightningd/plugin.c:297-305).

Trigger: `createproof invstring=<any paid bolt12 invoice or its offer> include=[0]` (or include=[1000000024] against a paid recurring-offer invoice). The name table omits these types, so the maintainers evidently knew they cannot be in a proof, but the numeric path was not filtered and the decode failure is treated as impossible. The shipped test (tests/test_pay.py:7558-7595) only exercises a defined type (170) and an unknown name.

Attacker: a commando or clnrest rune bearer whose rune permits `createproof` (a natural grant for an application that pays through the node and wants proofs of payment, or a `method^create`-style restriction), who knows or can obtain one completed bolt12 payment's invoice or offer string (the same application that paid it, or listsendpays if permitted). One request aborts lightningd, which can be repeated on each restart; the rune does not grant `stop`. The fully trusted operator can also trip it by accident, which is not the vulnerability but shows the input validation gap.

Fix: reject include types that are not defined in the payer_proof TLV (or at least known-undefined even types) in param_include_types, and make make_unsigned_proof_ return NULL / have the caller fail the command instead of asserting on a decode failure.

## Evidence
1. [common/bolt12\_proof.c:128–134](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12_proof.c#L128-L134)
   make_unsigned_proof_ serialises the selected invoice fields with towire_tlvstream_raw and re-parses them with fromwire_tlv_payer_proof; the result is only checked with assert(pptlv). Any selected field whose type the payer_proof TLV does not define (and is even) makes the decoder return NULL and the assert abort() the process.
2. [plugins/offers\_proof.c:364–408](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_proof.c#L364-L408)
   param_include_types accepts any u64 from the RPC caller as a TLV type to include (JSMN_PRIMITIVE -> json_to_u64 -> tal_arr_expand). Names are restricted to field_names[] (which deliberately omits type 0 and the recurrence types), but numbers bypass that table entirely.
3. [plugins/offers\_proof.c:136–140](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_proof.c#L136-L140)
   include_field_fn selects every invoice field whose numtype is in the caller's list, so a listed type that the paid invoice actually carries (e.g. 0 = invreq_metadata, present in every invoice obtained through fetchinvoice) is copied into the proof TLV stream.
4. [plugins/offers\_proof.c:326–335](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_proof.c#L326-L335)
   listsendpays_done calls make_unsigned_proof for each completed payment matching the caller's invstring; the caller-chosen include list reaches the assert here.
5. [wire/bolt12\_wire.csv:198–269](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/bolt12_wire.csv#L198-L269)
   The payer_proof TLV defines types 2-22, 80-91, 160-176, 240, 241 and 1001-1005 only. Invoice types 0 (invreq_metadata), 1000000024/26 (offer_recurrence_compulsory/base), 2000000092 (invreq_recurrence_counter) are even and undefined here, so fromwire_tlv_payer_proof rejects a stream containing them.
6. [wire/tlvstream.c:205–217](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/tlvstream.c#L205-L217)
   The generic TLV parser fails on any unknown even type (BOLT #1), which is what turns the included type-0 field into a NULL return and the assert failure.
7. [doc/schemas/createproof.json](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/schemas/createproof.json) (whole file)
   The schema documents numeric `include` entries as a supported way to 'reference unknown fields', so numeric input is an intended, exposed parameter rather than a debugging path.
8. [lightningd/plugin.c:296–305](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L296-L305)
   offers is a builtin important plugin; when it dies lightningd logs 'Plugin marked as important' and shuts down, so the plugin abort takes down the node.

## Impact
The offers plugin is important: its abort stops lightningd, halting all channel operation, HTLC handling and chain monitoring until an operator restarts it, and the call can be repeated. No data is disclosed or altered.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a rune (commando over the peer connection, or clnrest HTTPS) that permits createproof, and knows a bolt12 invoice or offer the node has paid. One JSON-RPC call with include=[0] makes listsendpays_done -> make_unsigned_proof_ -> fromwire_tlv_payer_proof fail -> assert -> SIGABRT in the offers plugin -> lightningd shutdown. Deterministic, no race, no user interaction. Requires a non-default deployment (rune issued with that method) and a completed bolt12 payment to reference, hence AT:PRESENT and PR:LOW.

## Recommended fix
1. param_include_types accepts arbitrary numeric TLV types without checking that the payer_proof TLV can carry them, so a caller can select invoice fields (type 0, recurrence types) that cannot be re-decoded as a payer_proof. Fix criteria: Numeric and named include entries must be restricted to types defined in the payer_proof TLV (or at minimum any even type undefined there must be rejected with a parameter error). Verify: `createproof ... include=[0]` returns a JSON-RPC error and the offers plugin stays alive.
2. make_unsigned_proof_ treats failure of fromwire_tlv_payer_proof as impossible (assert) although its input is selected by the RPC caller from counterparty-authored invoice fields. Fix criteria: A decode failure must be reported to the caller (return NULL and command_fail in listsendpays_done) rather than aborting; verify that no combination of include list and paid invoice terminates the plugin.

# renepay flow decomposition (find_positive_balance) loops forever on a flow cycle the feasible-flow BFS creates from payee-controlled route hints

## Details
get_flow_paths (plugins/renepay/mcf.c) turns the MCF solution into routes by repeatedly calling find_positive_balance from the source: starting at a negative-balance node it walks `while(balance[final_idx]<=0)` following, at each node, the first channel in gossmap chan order whose outgoing chan_flow is positive (lines 1207-1247). The walk keeps no visited set, decrements nothing and has no step bound; it halts only if following first-positive-flow channels always reaches a positive-balance node. If the aggregated flow contains a directed cycle B->C (channel c2), C->B (channel c1) and, at the moment the walk enters it, c2 is the first positive-flow channel at B and c1 the first at C, the walk alternates B,C,B,C forever (the maintainers' TODO at 1199-1206 admits this).

Such cycles are produced by the feasible-flow phase itself. find_admissible_path (853-874) is a BFS that accepts the FIRST traversable arc reaching a node. Adjacency lists are prepend-built while iterating nodes by index (600-616, 725-796), so a node's forward arcs come in reverse chan order and the dual (flow-cancelling) arcs contributed by lower-index neighbours come after them. When an augmenting path reaches C whose exit is saturated and must leave towards B, the forward arc of c1 (C->B) and the dual of c2 (cancelling existing B->C flow) both lead to B; with idx(B) < idx(C) the forward arc wins and a B->C/C->B flow cycle is created instead of flow being cancelled. get_flow_paths is invoked on this raw feasible flow at 1727, before any optimisation.

The payee controls everything needed. Traced construction (verified against the code's ordering rules): victim s has public channels to peers P2 (older in its gossip store) and P1 (newer), so s's chan order is [s-P2, s-P1] and its BFS adjacency is [P1, P2]. Attacker-owned real nodes B, C, t with two real channels announced in this order: P1-B (funded by the attacker with capacity Y, so renepay knows [0,Y]) and C-t (C signs htlc_max X < 0.95Y) - hence idx(B) < idx(C). The BOLT11 invoice for amount A > 0.95Y carries route hints, each a path ending at t: [B,C] (adds fake one-directional B->C = c2; C->t is a known scid and is skipped), [C,B,D,G] (adds G->t, D->G, B->D, C->B = c1), [P2,Q,C] (adds Q->C, P2->Q), with D, G, Q fresh pubkeys. Resulting chan orders: B: [P1-B, c2, B-D, c1]; C: [C-t, c2, c1, Q-C]. BFS phase: path 1 = s->P1->B->c2->C->t (C reached from B because P1 precedes P2 in s's adjacency; C->t is 1 hop versus D->G->t 2 hops) saturating C->t at X; path 2 = s->P1->B->D->G->t until P1->B saturates; path 3 = s->P2->Q->C->c1->B->D->G->t for the remainder, c1 chosen over the c2 dual because idx(B) < idx(C). Aggregated flow: c2 = X, c1 = A-0.95Y: a B<->C cycle. Decomposition: walk 1 from s takes s-P2 (first in chan order) ->Q->C, where C-t is first and still positive, delivering min(A-0.95Y, X); the next walk (via P2 or P1 depending on which saturated) arrives at C with C-t at zero, follows c1 to B, at B finds P1-B at zero and c2 positive, returns to C, and cycles indefinitely. The same holds for any A > 0.95Y and any X; if the victim's chan order is the mirror image the walk terminates, so the attacker needs to guess which of the victim's two channels is older (visible from scids) or simply issue a second, mirrored invoice.

Impact: cln-renepay spins at 100% CPU inside minflow with no timeout; every renepay/renepaystatus RPC hangs and all payments the plugin is tracking stop being driven until the operator kills/restarts the plugin. lightningd survives because cln-renepay is the one builtin plugin not marked important (lightningd/plugin.c:2585). Cost to the attacker: three nodes and two small on-chain channels, plus an invoice the victim (or its automated payout logic) pays.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/mcf.c:1186–1248](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mcf.c#L1186-L1248)
   find_positive_balance walks `while(balance[final_idx]<=0)` and at each node follows the FIRST channel in gossmap chan order (gossmap_nth_chan) with positive chan_flow in the outgoing direction. Nothing is decremented during the walk and there is no visited set or step bound, so if the aggregated flow has a directed cycle B->C, C->B whose edges are the first positive-flow channels at B and at C, the walk alternates B,C,B,C forever. The TODO at 1199-1206 concedes that nothing guarantees the MCF solution is cycle-free.
2. [plugins/renepay/mcf.c:819–873](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mcf.c#L819-L873)
   find_admissible_path (BFS, no costs) records prev[next] for the first traversable arc that reaches `next` and skips later ones. When the path arrives at C with C's exit saturated, the forward arc of a channel C->B and the dual (flow-cancelling) arc of a channel already carrying B->C flow both head to B; adjacency order decides, and when idx(B) < idx(C) the forward arc comes first, so the BFS creates a B->C/C->B flow cycle instead of cancelling flow.
3. [plugins/renepay/mcf.c:600–615](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mcf.c#L600-L615)
   linear_network_add_adjacenct_arc prepends: a node's adjacency is the reverse of its chan order, and dual arcs contributed by lower-index nodes (init_linear_network iterates nodes by index, 725-796) end up after the node's own forward arcs. This is what makes the BFS prefer the cycle-creating forward arc over the cancelling dual at C when idx(B) < idx(C), and what makes the BFS and the decomposition walk prefer channels in opposite orders at every node.
4. [plugins/renepay/mcf.c:1717–1735](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mcf.c#L1717-L1735)
   minflow calls get_flow_paths (which calls find_positive_balance for the source until its balance is zero, 1337-1350) on the raw feasible flow immediately after find_feasible_flow, before any cost-based optimisation; so a cyclic flow from the BFS phase alone hangs the plugin inside the `renepay` RPC.
5. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:467–606](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L467-L606)
   routehints_done feeds every BOLT11 `r` hop (payee-supplied) to add_hintchan, which for an unknown scid adds a one-directional channel between arbitrary pubkeys to the payment's local_gossmods with MAX_CAPACITY, htlc_max MAX_CAPACITY (passes channelfilter) and payee-chosen fees; hops whose scid already exists are skipped. Hints are processed in invoice order, so the payee fixes the order in which these fake channels (and the fake nodes they introduce) are appended to the gossmap, i.e. the chan order the walk uses and the node indices the BFS tie-break uses.
6. [common/gossmap.c:340–346](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/gossmap.c#L340-L346)
   node_add_channel appends, so a node's chan order (gossmap_nth_chan index) is the order channel records entered the gossmap: gossip-store order for public channels (which the owner controls by announcing in sequence), then localmods order for hint channels. add_channel (451-520) creates nodes in first-appearance order, fixing idx(B) < idx(C) when B's first channel is announced before C's.
7. [common/gossmap.c:1229–1309](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/gossmap.c#L1229-L1309)
   gossmap_apply_localmods creates hint channels via add_channel in mods order and writes a fake channel_update only for the half with changes (`if (!any_set) continue;`), so a hint channel is usable in one direction only: B->C and C->B become two distinct channels c2, c1 and their forward arcs are independent of each other's duals.

## Impact
cln-renepay loops forever inside get_flow_paths at 100% CPU; the plugin stops answering lightningd, every renepay/renepaystatus call hangs and in-flight renepay payments are no longer driven or reported until the operator restarts the plugin. lightningd itself continues because cln-renepay is not an important plugin. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker is the payee of an invoice the victim pays with renepay: it supplies the BOLT11 route hints (fake one-directional MAX_CAPACITY channels between pubkeys of its choice, in an order it fixes), owns the two real bottleneck channels (funding size and its own channel_update htlc_max) and announces them in the order that fixes the node-index tie-break. No credentials or exploit mitigation is involved; success depends on which of the victim's two channels is older in its gossip store, which is inferable from public scids and otherwise costs one extra mirrored invoice (attack requirements present). The victim must pay the attacker's invoice, a routine action that in payout services is automated.

## Recommended fix
1. find_positive_balance follows positive-flow channels with no cycle detection, no progress guarantee and no step bound, relying on an unenforced assumption that the MCF solution is acyclic. Fix criteria: The flow decomposition must terminate for every valid flow: track visited nodes per walk and, on revisiting a node, cancel the detected cycle's flow (subtract its bottleneck from the cycle's channels) before continuing, or bound the walk by the node count and fail minflow with an error instead of spinning. Verify with a unit test that feeds a flow containing a B->C/C->B cycle over two one-directional channels and confirms minflow returns routes or an error without hanging.
2. The augmenting-path searches (find_admissible_path and find_optimal_path on cost ties) take the first arc that reaches a node, so a forward arc into a node that already sends flow back is preferred over the cancelling dual arc and the solver emits cyclic flows. Fix criteria: Prefer the dual arc of an already-flowing channel on ties, or post-process the solution to cancel flow cycles (e.g. remove circulations) before decomposition, so the flow handed to get_flow_paths is acyclic. Verify that for the route-hint construction in the description no channel pair carries simultaneous B->C and C->B flow after the feasible-flow phase.

# channeld drops lightningd HTLC fulfill/fail/offer requests queued during quiescence (update_queue never drained)

## Details
channeld must not start new update conversations once quiescence (stfu) is being negotiated. To honour that, req_in() passes WIRE_CHANNELD_OFFER_HTLC, FEERATES, BLOCKHEIGHT, FULFILL_HTLC and FAIL_HTLC through handle_master_request_later(), which, while is_entering_stfu() is true (we or the peer sent stfu, or we want to), moves the request onto peer->update_queue and returns.

Nothing ever reads update_queue. The daemon references it in exactly three places (declaration at 173, the enqueue at 398, creation at 7244); end_stfu_mode() (247-259) resets the stfu flags without replaying it, and the main loop (7271-7281) only drains peer->from_master. When a splice completes normally (resume_splice_negotiation calls end_stfu_mode at 4123/4247 and reports splice_confirmed_signed; lightningd's handle_splice_confirmed_signed merely broadcasts the tx), channeld keeps running and every lightningd request diverted during quiescence is silently discarded.

Who controls entry into this state: the remote peer, by sending `stfu` (handle_stfu accepts it whenever OPT_QUIESCE is negotiated, which is the default). channeld answers with its own stfu as soon as it has no pending local updates; the channel then stays quiescent until the peer's splice completes (the peer may wait up to the 10-minute stfu_timer before splice_init). The operator's own `splice_init`/`stfu_channels` commands enter the same state, with no timer at all while waiting for the peer's stfu reply.

What is lost:
- channeld_fulfill_htlc / channeld_fail_htlc: lightningd has already moved the incoming HTLC to SENT_REMOVE_HTLC and stored the preimage/failure (peer_htlcs.c:429-467). It never resends unless channeld restarts (on reestablish channeld re-sends SENT_REMOVE_HTLC HTLCs, channeld.c:6392-6400). If the splice completes normally and no reconnection happens, the fulfill is never sent to the peer; lightningd and channeld/peer now disagree about the HTLC, and when it reaches htlc_in_deadline (cltv_expiry - (cltv_expiry_delta+1)/2) htlcs_notify_new_block() calls channel_fail_permanent (peer_htlcs.c:3081-3109) and force-closes the channel to claim it on-chain. A dropped fail leaves the peer's HTLC unresolved until the peer times it out.
- channeld_offer_htlc: lightningd waits for channeld_offer_htlc_reply (peer_htlcs.c:811); it never comes. This case is bounded: the 30-second htlc_offer_timeout (peer_htlcs.c:725-743) calls channel_fail_transient, killing the connection; channeld restarts, the hout is failed back with temporary_channel_failure, and the reestablish path re-sends any SENT_REMOVE_HTLC HTLCs. So a dropped offer costs a forced disconnect of the channel but also heals a concurrently dropped fulfill/fail.
- feerate/blockheight updates are re-sent later by lightningd and are merely delayed.

Attack: a peer M with a channel to us routes a payment through us to a node it controls, sends `stfu` (channeld replies at once since the committed HTLC is not a pending update), and has the downstream node fulfill while we are quiescent. Our fulfill towards M is enqueued and dropped; M completes a (small) splice, the channel keeps running with an HTLC that lightningd believes it has resolved, and at the deadline our node force-closes its own channel (on-chain fees, our funds locked for to_self_delay, routing capacity lost) while M keeps the connection up so no reestablish repairs it. The same loss occurs without malice whenever a fulfill or fail arrives during any honest splice, so honest splicing peers' channels are degraded too.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/channeld.c:395–401](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L395-L401)
   handle_master_request_later(): while is_entering_stfu() the lightningd request is msg_enqueue()d onto peer->update_queue and req_in returns as if handled.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:247–258](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L247-L258)
   end_stfu_mode() resets the stfu flags and timer but does not replay update_queue, so requests received during quiescence are lost when the splice/stfu completes normally.
3. [channeld/channeld.c:7244](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L7244)
   update_queue is created here; together with line 173 (declaration) and 398 (enqueue) these are the only references in the daemon: no msg_dequeue() of update_queue exists anywhere.
4. [channeld/channeld.c:7271–7280](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L7271-L7280)
   The main loop only dequeues peer->from_master; update_queue is never consulted.
5. [channeld/channeld.c:6922–6944](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6922-L6944)
   req_in routes WIRE_CHANNELD_OFFER_HTLC, FEERATES, BLOCKHEIGHT, FULFILL_HTLC and FAIL_HTLC through handle_master_request_later, so all five request types are diverted during stfu.
6. [channeld/channeld.c:328–384](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L328-L384)
   handle_stfu(): any peer's stfu is accepted once OPT_QUIESCE is negotiated (default); it sets want_stfu/stfu_sent[REMOTE] and calls maybe_send_stfu, which replies immediately when no local updates are pending (a committed HTLC is not a pending update).
7. [channeld/channeld.c:241–245](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L241-L245)
   is_entering_stfu() is true from the moment a peer-sent (or operator-sent) stfu is seen until end_stfu_mode, i.e. for the whole splice; there is no timer bounding the 'entering' phase (stfu_timer is only armed once both sides sent stfu, lines 297-299).
8. [channeld/channeld.c:4243–4256](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4243-L4256)
   After tx_signatures, resume_splice_negotiation calls end_stfu_mode, frees peer->splicing and reports splice_confirmed_signed; channeld keeps running (no exit/restart), so nothing replays the queued requests.
9. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:429–466](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L429-L466)
   fulfill_htlc() moves the incoming HTLC to SENT_REMOVE_HTLC, persists the preimage and sends channeld_fulfill_htlc once; lightningd does not resend it unless channeld is restarted (channeld.c:6392-6400 re-sends SENT_REMOVE_HTLC on reestablish).
10. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:3081–3108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L3081-L3108)
   If the fulfill is never transmitted, htlcs_notify_new_block() force-closes the channel (channel_fail_permanent) when the fulfilled HTLC reaches htlc_in_deadline.
11. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:725–742](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L725-L742)
   htlc_offer_timeout(): a dropped channeld_offer_htlc is bounded to 30 s, after which channel_fail_transient kills the connection and restarts channeld (which also replays queued fulfills via reestablish); the offer case is a forced disconnect, not a permanent hang.

## Impact
Channel state diverges between lightningd and channeld (lightningd records the HTLC as resolved, channeld and the peer still carry it). The channel ends up force-closed by lightningd's deadline handler (or by the peer timing out an unfailed HTLC), costing on-chain fees and locking our funds for to_self_delay; forwards offered during quiescence cause a forced disconnect after 30 s. Funds are not stolen (we hold the preimage and claim on-chain). Impact is confined to the affected channel, so integrity and availability are rated LOW rather than total.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any connected channel peer can send `stfu` (OPT_QUIESCE advertised by default since v24.11; splicing default-on). channeld replies when it has no pending local updates and remains in is_entering_stfu for the rest of the quiescence/splice, during which its main loop still reads lightningd requests and diverts them to the never-drained queue. The attacker times a downstream fulfill (routing through us to its own node) into that window, then completes a small splice so channeld never restarts. No defence stands in the way in a default configuration; the only cost is one on-chain splice transaction.

## Recommended fix
1. Requests deferred during stfu entry are stored in update_queue, which no code path ever dequeues, so deferred HTLC resolutions and offers are lost rather than delayed. Fix criteria: Every request deferred while entering/holding quiescence must be processed once quiescence ends (or when channeld exits so lightningd can resend). Verify: a channeld_fulfill_htlc delivered during a peer-initiated splice results in update_fulfill_htlc being sent to the peer after the splice completes without any reconnection, and a deferred channeld_offer_htlc produces a channeld_offer_htlc_reply.
2. The 'entering stfu' phase (we or the peer sent stfu, awaiting the other side) has no timeout, so a peer that never answers our stfu holds the channel in a state where lightningd requests are deferred indefinitely. Fix criteria: Bound the time between sending stfu and receiving the peer's stfu (warn/disconnect on expiry, as the existing 10-minute timer does for completed quiescence); verify that a peer ignoring our stfu results in a disconnect and that deferred requests are then processed on restart.
