# Millisatoshi string parsing lets a caller-chosen Decimal exponent trigger an enormous integer conversion

## Details
Millisatoshi (pyln.client.lightning) is the published pyln-client SDK's amount type and the one the plugin framework applies automatically: Plugin._coerce_arguments() (plugin.py:617-631) converts every parameter annotated `Millisatoshi` with Millisatoshi(val) before the handler runs (plugin.py:826 notes that annotations drive this conversion; tests/plugins/millisatoshis.py shows the documented usage `def echo(plugin, msat: Millisatoshi, ...)`). For string input the constructor does parsed = Decimal(v[0:-4]) for the 'msat' suffix and then evaluates `parsed != int(parsed)` (lightning.py:59) and int(parsed) (line 61). Decimal construction from a string is exact (CPython builds it under the max context) and accepts scientific notation with exponents far beyond any monetary range, e.g. Decimal('1e1000000000'). The 'msat' branch performs no arithmetic, so no context Emax check applies before int() is called (the 'sat'/'btc' branches multiply under the default context and raise decimal.Overflow above Emax 999999, bounding them to ~1e6 digits). int(parsed) must materialise 10^1000000000: in CPython's C decimal (libmpdec) dec_as_long -> mpd_qexport_u32 first shifts the coefficient left by the exponent (about 420 MB for 10^9 decimal digits) and then runs the schoolbook base conversion to 2^30 digits, which is quadratic in the operand size, so the call does not complete in practical time; the pure-Python fallback (_pydecimal) computes int(coefficient) * 10**exp with the same order of cost. Larger exponents ('1e10000000000msat' and beyond) instead fail with MemoryError or get the process OOM-killed. Neither the exponent nor the string length is bounded before conversion, and CPython's int_max_str_digits limit does not cover Decimal-to-int conversion.

A rune bearer who may call a pyln plugin method with a Millisatoshi-annotated parameter (or any method whose implementation passes a caller string to Millisatoshi()) sends via commando or clnrest {"amount_msat":"1e1000000000msat"}. commando's execute_command (commando.c:272-318) and lightningd's plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch (plugin.c:1312-1350, json_stream_forward_change_id) forward the params raw; _coerce_arguments() invokes the constructor on the plugin's only dispatch path (run() at plugin.py:937-951 reads stdin and calls _multi_dispatch -> _dispatch_request -> _exec_func synchronously, with no worker threads), so the plugin pins a CPU core and hundreds of MB indefinitely. Every subsequent hook request from lightningd (htlc_accepted, invoice_payment, openchannel, custommsg...) and every RPC call to that plugin stalls behind it; lightningd has no timeout on hook replies (plugin_hook.c has no timer; plugin.c's only timer is the startup manifest timeout), so HTLC forwarding or invoice acceptance that depends on that plugin's hooks stops node-wide until the operator restarts the plugin. A memory-exhausting variant kills the plugin outright (lightningd shuts down if it is marked important).

Scope: the vulnerable artifact is the pyln-client package published to PyPI (pypi-publish.yml, v26.06.6); no plugin shipped in plugins/ of this tree is written in Python, so the condition under which this holds is that the operator runs a plugin built on pyln-client that exposes a Millisatoshi-typed parameter (or calls Millisatoshi() on caller strings) to a rune bearer. Dependency assumption (not verified by execution): in CPython >= 3.10 (pyproject requires-python) int(Decimal('1E+1000000000')) materialises the full integer rather than rejecting it; this holds for both the libmpdec-backed _decimal (mpd_qshiftl then _baseconv_to_smaller) and _pydecimal (10**exp). The monetary domain gives a simple bound: 21e6 BTC is < 2.2e18 msat, so any adjusted exponent above ~19 can be rejected before conversion.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/lightning.py:48–62](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/lightning.py#L48-L62)
   Millisatoshi.__init__ parses 'Nmsat' strings with Decimal(v[0:-4]) (exact, max-context construction accepting exponents up to ~1e18) and immediately evaluates int(parsed) at line 59 (`parsed != int(parsed)`) and again at line 61, materialising the full integer; for '1e1000000000msat' that is a 10^9-digit integer. No bound on the exponent, the adjusted exponent or the string length precedes the conversion. The 'msat' branch does no arithmetic so no decimal context Emax check intervenes (unlike the 'sat'/'btc' branches).
2. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:617–631](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L617-L631)
   _coerce_arguments() calls Millisatoshi(val) for every method parameter whose annotation is Millisatoshi, so the framework itself performs the conversion on caller-supplied strings before the plugin's handler runs; _bind_pos and _bind_kwargs both call it (positional and keyword params alike).
3. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:937–951](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L937-L951)
   run() iterates stdin and calls _multi_dispatch() synchronously for each batch; _multi_dispatch -> _dispatch_request -> _exec_func -> _bind_*/_coerce_arguments all run on this single thread (the module imports only RLock from threading), so while the conversion runs no further request, hook or notification from lightningd is read or answered.
4. [lightningd/plugin.c:1312–1350](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1312-L1350)
   plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch forwards the incoming JSON-RPC request to the plugin via json_stream_forward_change_id with the original buffer and tokens: parameter values are passed through verbatim, so lightningd applies no type or range check to the amount string before the plugin sees it.
5. [plugins/commando.c:272–317](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L272-L317)
   execute_command re-emits each of the rune bearer's params (object members or array elements) with json_add_jsonstr from the raw token text, so the exponent-form amount string is entirely attacker-chosen and reaches lightningd and the plugin unchanged once checkrune has authorised the method.

## Impact
The plugin becomes unresponsive (or dies on the memory-exhausting variant); hooks it serves are never answered, so dependent node functions (HTLC forwarding, invoice acceptance, channel-open policy) stall until operator intervention, and an important plugin's death stops lightningd. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote peer holding a rune (PR:L) for a pyln plugin method whose parameter is Millisatoshi-annotated or is passed to Millisatoshi() (deployment condition, AT:P) sends one commando request (AV:N) with amount '1e1000000000msat'. commando/lightningd forward it raw, the framework's coercion calls Millisatoshi() on the dispatch thread and the conversion consumes ~420 MB and effectively unbounded CPU time, stalling all hook and method handling in that plugin. No user interaction, no defences to bypass.

## Recommended fix
1. Millisatoshi.__init__ converts an unbounded Decimal to int, so the cost of parsing a string is controlled by the caller's exponent rather than by the monetary domain. Fix criteria: String amounts must be validated before any big-integer materialisation: reject exponent notation or any value whose adjusted exponent/digit count exceeds the msat range (max ~2.1e18 msat) with ValueError in constant time. Verify that Millisatoshi('1e1000000000msat') raises immediately and that Millisatoshi('123.456sat') still parses.
2. The plugin framework performs Millisatoshi coercion of caller-supplied arguments synchronously on its only dispatch thread, so a slow conversion blocks all hooks. Fix criteria: Coercion failures or pathological inputs must be bounded so a single request cannot stall hook processing; once the constructor rejects oversized values, confirm that a malformed amount in one method call does not delay a concurrent htlc_accepted hook reply.

# startup_regtest.sh uses predictable /tmp/lN lightning-dirs; local user gets code execution via plugins/

## Details
contrib/startup_regtest.sh is the documented way to spin up local regtest nodes (README.md:56-59, beginners-guide, developers-guide). Unless LIGHTNING_DIR is set it uses `/tmp` (lines 80-83) and creates `/tmp/l1`, `/tmp/l2`, ... with `mkdir -p` (line 190). `mkdir -p` succeeds when the directory already exists regardless of owner, and nothing checks ownership or mode afterwards. The script then writes `/tmp/lN/config` through whatever path exists (line 192, follows symlinks) and starts `lightningd --lightning-dir=/tmp/lN` (line 225).

lightningd itself only creates the base and network directories with 0700 when chdir(<dir>/regtest) fails (lightningd/options.c:1875-1888); a pre-existing, attacker-owned directory is used as-is. It reads `<lightning-dir>/config` and `<lightning-dir>/regtest/config` with no ownership check (common/configdir.c:384-399), where `plugin=`, `important-plugin=` and `bitcoin-cli=` lines are honoured. It then registers `<lightning-dir>/plugins` and each subdirectory as plugin directories (lightningd/plugin.c:2049-2050, 1949-1964), accepts any regular file executable by anyone (plugin.c:1885-1892, stat follows symlinks) and exec's each one in plugins_init (lightningd.c:1271) before hsm_init or the DB is touched.

Attack: any other unprivileged account on the same host (shared dev box, CI builder, university host, container sharing /tmp) pre-creates `/tmp/l1` (mode 0777 so the victim's own writes succeed) containing `plugins/x` (any 0755 executable) and/or `regtest/config` with `plugin=/home/attacker/evil`. When the victim later sources the script and runs `start_ln`, lightningd, running as the victim, executes the attacker's binary with the victim's privileges and full node authority. /tmp's sticky bit does not help: it only prevents the victim from removing the attacker's directory, and protected_symlinks/protected_regular apply only inside sticky world-writable directories, not inside the attacker-owned /tmp/l1. Secondary effects: `cat > /tmp/l1/config` can be redirected via a symlink to truncate any file the victim can write, and the regtest hsm_secret, log and RPC socket land in an attacker-readable directory.

Root cause: a documented user-run script places security-sensitive state (configs, hsm_secret, an auto-executed plugin directory) under fixed, guessable names in a world-writable shared directory instead of a per-user private directory (mktemp -d, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, ~/...), and neither the script nor lightningd verifies ownership/permissions of a pre-existing lightning-dir before trusting it.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/startup\_regtest.sh:80–83](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/startup_regtest.sh#L80-L83)
   LIGHTNING_DIR defaults to /tmp (world-writable, sticky) when the user has not set it; the script is sourced per README/beginners/developers guides.
2. [contrib/startup\_regtest.sh:188–225](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/startup_regtest.sh#L188-L225)
   start_nodes() runs `mkdir -p $LIGHTNING_DIR/l$i` (succeeds silently when the directory already exists and is owned by another uid), writes the node config with `cat > .../config` (follows symlinks), then starts `lightningd --lightning-dir=$LIGHTNING_DIR/l$i`. Paths /tmp/l1, /tmp/l2 ... are fixed and guessable; no ownership or mode check anywhere.
3. [lightningd/options.c:1875–1888](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1875-L1888)
   lightningd only mkdir()s the base and network dirs (0700) when chdir(config_netdir) fails; a pre-existing /tmp/l1/regtest owned by another user is chdir'd into and used as-is with no ownership or permission check.
4. [lightningd/plugin.c:2048–2050](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2048-L2050)
   plugins_init sets default_dir = <lightning-dir>/plugins and registers everything found there; plugins_send_getmanifest then exec's each registered plugin.
5. [lightningd/plugin.c:1949–1964](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1949-L1964)
   plugins_add_default_dir adds the plugins directory and every subdirectory as plugin dirs; add_plugin_dir registers every acceptable file via plugin_register. No owner check on the directory or files.
6. [lightningd/plugin.c:1885–1891](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1885-L1891)
   plugin_fullpath accepts any regular file executable by anyone (stat, not lstat, so a symlink to an attacker binary elsewhere also qualifies).
7. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1271](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1271)
   plugins_init (which spawns the plugin processes) runs before handle_opts, pidfile_create and hsm_init (line 1308), so the planted executable runs as the victim even if later startup steps would fail.
8. [common/configdir.c:384–398](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/configdir.c#L384-L398)
   initial_config_opts reads <lightning-dir>/config and <lightning-dir>/<network>/config via grab_file_str with no ownership/mode check; an attacker-authored regtest/config with `plugin=`, `important-plugin=` or `bitcoin-cli=` lines is honoured as a second execution route.
9. [README.md:56–59](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/README.md#L56-L59)
   README (and doc/beginners-guide/beginners-guide.md, doc/developers-guide/developers-guide.md) instruct users to `. contrib/startup_regtest.sh` and run start_ln, so the /tmp default is the documented, user-run path.

## Impact
Arbitrary code execution in the victim's user context (lightningd exec's the planted plugin as the victim before hsm/DB init): full read/write of the victim's files, SSH keys, any real ~/.lightning, plus arbitrary file truncation via a symlinked config write. The regtest node state itself is low value, but the plugin path yields complete compromise of the victim account.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any unprivileged local account on the same host (AV:L, PR:L). Delivery: create /tmp/l1 (and /tmp/l2...) ahead of the victim's next start_ln containing plugins/<exe> or regtest/config with a plugin= line; mkdir -p tolerates the existing directory so no tight race is needed, but the attacker must pre-position before the victim's first run or after a destroy_ln (once the victim owns /tmp/lN the sticky bit stops the attacker replacing it) — hence AT:P. Trigger: the victim follows the documented workflow (`. contrib/startup_regtest.sh; start_ln`), a passive, normal action (UI:P). Works with default settings (LIGHTNING_DIR unset); no lightningd option or ownership check interferes.

## Recommended fix
1. The script stores lightning-dirs under fixed names in the shared /tmp and tolerates pre-existing directories, so another local user can pre-seed the directory lightningd will trust and auto-load plugins from. Fix criteria: Default LIGHTNING_DIR to a private, per-user location (mktemp -d, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, or ~/.lightning-regtest) and refuse to proceed when $LIGHTNING_DIR/lN already exists but is not owned by the current user with mode 0700. Verify: with an attacker-owned /tmp/l1/plugins/x present, start_ln must not execute it.
2. lightningd accepts a pre-existing --lightning-dir without checking ownership or permissions, then executes everything in its plugins/ subdirectory. Fix criteria: On startup lightningd should check that an existing lightning-dir (and plugins dir) is owned by the running uid and not group/world-writable, refusing to start or to load plugins otherwise. Verify: a lightning-dir owned by another uid causes a startup error rather than plugin execution.

# Error reply containing a lone surrogate from caller params aborts the pyln plugin

## Details
pyln-client decodes requests with json.loads() (plugin.py:829), which accepts the JSON escape \uD800 (a lone UTF-16 surrogate, syntactically valid JSON) and yields a Python str containing U+D800. Its writer, Plugin._write_locked() (plugin.py:766-770), serialises replies with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), leaving the surrogate raw, then encodes with the strict 'utf-8' codec via bytes(s, encoding='utf-8'), which raises UnicodeEncodeError ('surrogates not allowed'). Inside a method handler this is harmless: set_result() or plugin.log() raising inside the try block of _dispatch_request() is caught, and UnicodeEncodeError's own text renders the bad character as an ASCII '\ud800' escape. But Request.set_exception() is called from the except block (plugin.py:732) and embeds str(exc) into 'message' and traceback.format_exc() into 'traceback' (plugin.py:156-170); when the handler's exception text contains the caller's string verbatim, _write_locked() raises from within the except handler, and self.log(traceback.format_exc()) on the next line would raise the same way. Nothing above catches it: _multi_dispatch() and run() (plugin.py:937-950) have no handler, so the plugin process exits. lightningd then kills the plugin, and if it is marked important, calls fatal() (lightningd/plugin.c:297-300).

The triggering condition is the ordinary idiom the framework sanctions: the README (contrib/pyln-client/README.md:81-83) states that a raised exception 'causes a JSON error return', and plugin authors routinely raise RpcException(f"unknown label {label}") or Exception("... {}".format(param)) (the project's own tests/plugins/currencyUSDAUD5000.py:16 does exactly this with a caller param). Framework-generated errors alone do not trigger it (inspect's bind errors and int()/Millisatoshi errors use repr or constant text), so a consumer plugin interpolating a caller-supplied string into an exception message is required.

Delivery: a rune bearer sends via commando a call to the pyln plugin method with a string parameter "\ud800". commando's try_command/execute_command copy the token raw (json_tok_full, plugins/commando.c:289-300; json_add_jsonstr memcpy, common/json_stream.c:234-235), lightningd's validator only checks raw-byte UTF-8 (common/json_parse_simple.c:352-355; the escape is ASCII) and plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch forwards the request byte-for-byte except the id (lightningd/plugin.c:1204-1211, 1343). Any pyln plugin whose method raises an exception mentioning the value then crashes instead of returning an error. clnrest is not a vector (serde_json rejects lone surrogates); lightning-cli users are trusted.

Root cause: the error-reply path writes caller-derived text through a strict encoder with no fallback, and a failure inside set_exception() in the except branch is treated as unreachable, so a single bad reply terminates the whole plugin rather than one request. Dependency assumptions (CPython 3.x as used by pyln-client): json.loads accepts lone surrogate escapes; json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) emits them raw; str→bytes with 'utf-8' rejects surrogates unless errors='surrogatepass'/'replace'.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:146–172](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L146-L172)
   Request.set_exception() builds the error message from str(exc) and attaches traceback.format_exc(), both of which contain the exception text verbatim, then calls _write_result() -> _write_locked().
2. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:766–775](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L766-L775)
   _write_locked() serialises with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), which leaves a lone surrogate (U+D800..U+DFFF) as a raw code point, and then bytes(s, encoding='utf-8') raises UnicodeEncodeError ('surrogates not allowed').
3. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:720–733](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L720-L733)
   _dispatch_request() calls request.set_exception(e) from inside its except block; an exception raised there is not caught and propagates through _multi_dispatch() and run(), terminating the plugin process.
4. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:829](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L829)
   json.loads() decodes the JSON escape \ud800 into a Python str containing a lone surrogate, so a caller-supplied string value can carry a code point that the UTF-8 writer later refuses.
5. [plugins/commando.c:272–317](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L272-L317)
   commando re-emits the peer's params raw (json_strdup does not unescape; json_add_jsonstr copies json_tok_full), so the escape sequence \ud800 survives to lightningd and, via plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch()'s byte-for-byte forward (lightningd/plugin.c:1316-1352), to the Python plugin; lightningd's utf8_check (common/json_parse_simple.c:352-355) only inspects raw bytes and accepts the ASCII escape.

## Impact
The plugin process exits with an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError, losing all of its RPC methods, hooks and subscriptions until an operator restarts it; a plugin marked important takes lightningd down with it (lightningd/plugin.c:297-300). A rune granting a method call concedes none of this. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote peer holding an operator-issued rune that permits a pyln plugin method (PR:L; runes are the intended bound on such callers) sends over commando (AV:N) a string parameter containing a lone surrogate escape. commando and lightningd forward it raw with no validation an attacker must defeat (AC:L). The crash requires that the targeted plugin method interpolates the caller's string into an exception message, a common but deployment-dependent property of the consumer plugin (AT:P). Deterministic once such a method exists; no user interaction (UI:N).

## Recommended fix
1. _write_locked() encodes reply JSON with the strict utf-8 codec although the reply can contain code points json.loads() accepted from the caller (lone surrogates). Fix criteria: Serialising a reply must never fail for any value json.loads() can produce: use ensure_ascii=True or an error handler (surrogatepass/replace) so lone surrogates are emitted as \uXXXX escapes. Verify by returning or raising with a string containing '\ud800' and confirming a valid reply is written.
2. A failure inside set_exception()/_write_result() in the except branch of _dispatch_request() is unhandled and tears down the whole plugin. Fix criteria: Failures while writing an error reply must be contained: fall back to a minimal ASCII error reply and log, never propagate out of the dispatch loop. Verify that an exception injected into set_exception() leaves the plugin running.

# funderupdate policy_mod error path reads freed error string (use-after-free); large value unmaps it and crashes the important funder plugin

## Details
funder's `funderupdate` RPC parses its `policy_mod` parameter with param_policy_mod() (plugins/funder.c:1256-1279). It first calls u64_option(), which for a non-numeric value returns tal_fmt(tmpctx, "'%s' is not a number", arg) (libplugin.c:1619) — a heap string whose length tracks the caller's value. param_policy_mod() then does `tal_free(err)` (funder.c:1270) and falls back to parse_amount_sat(); if that also fails (e.g. policy_mod="abc"), it calls command_fail_badparam(cmd, name, buffer, tok, err) (1272-1273) with the pointer it just freed. command_fail_badparam (common/json_command.c:11-33) reads that freed string in every mode: into a LOG_INFORM line via command_log and then into the JSON-RPC error reply (`"%s: %s: invalid token (see logs for details)"`), or directly into the reply in dev/check mode. The sibling option parser amount_sat_or_u64_option() (funder.c:1692-1698) frees err and composes a fresh message; the RPC path copied the free without the new message.

Consequences. (1) Small values: the freed chunk is a tcache chunk whose tal_hdr absorbs the allocator's next/key words, and each tal_vfmt in the sink allocates (ccan tal/str/str.c:53) before vsnprintf reads `msg` (str.c:59), so the chunk can be recycled for the plugin's own log/reply strings and the caller receives a garbled error message built from stale heap — a use-after-free read, but the recycled content is the plugin's own freshly written text rather than secrets or pointers. (2) Large values: do_vfmt grows the error buffer by realloc doubling; for a policy_mod string of >=128 KiB the final buffer exceeds glibc's default M_MMAP_THRESHOLD and is an mmap'd chunk, which free() returns with munmap (documented in mallopt(3)). The subsequent strlen/vsnprintf of `msg` in command_log then faults, funder dies with SIGSEGV, and because funder is an important plugin lightningd logs 'Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1) (lightningd/plugin.c:297-302): the whole node stops. Both commando (1 MiB request cap, commando.c:458-459) and clnrest (2 MiB body cap, rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:28) accept requests that large, and lightningd forwards plugin-method params raw (plugin.c:1346).

Who reaches it: any RPC caller whose rune permits `funderupdate` over commando or clnrest. The createrune documentation tells operators to 'restrict the methods too' (doc/schemas/createrune.json:112), so a method-restricted rune is the project's intended bound on such a bearer; funderupdate concedes them only tuning of the dual-funding contribution policy, not reading funder's heap or stopping the node (they cannot call `stop` or `plugin stop`). An unrestricted-rune holder or the operator gains nothing (they could call `stop` directly). Dependency assumption: glibc malloc (Docker base debian:bookworm-slim, glibc 2.36) — mmap-backed allocation at or above the dynamic mmap threshold and munmap on free, per mallopt(3); the crash requires that no earlier mmap'd free in funder's lifetime raised the threshold above the chosen size, which the attacker counters by choosing a size near the 1-2 MiB caps.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/funder.c:1268–1273](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L1268-L1273)
   param_policy_mod(): `err = u64_option(cmd, arg_str, false, *mod)`; on failure it does `tal_free(err)`, then if parse_amount_sat() also fails it passes the already-freed `err` to command_fail_badparam(cmd, name, buffer, tok, err). This is the code the fix must change.
2. [common/json\_command.c:11–32](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_command.c#L11-L32)
   command_fail_badparam reads `msg` (the freed pointer) in every mode: in dev/check mode it is formatted into the reply (line 12-16); otherwise it is formatted into a LOG_INFORM line via command_log (25-29) and then again into the JSON-RPC error reply `"%s: %s: invalid token (see logs for details)"` (30-32). Each read goes through tal_vfmt, which allocates before vsnprintf reads the argument.
3. [plugins/libplugin.c:1610–1623](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin.c#L1610-L1623)
   u64_option() returns tal_fmt(tmpctx, "'%s' is not a number", arg) — a heap string whose size is set by the caller-supplied arg — so tal_free(err) is a real free() (ccan tal freefn = free) of the buffer that is subsequently read.
4. [ccan/ccan/tal/str/str.c:43–69](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/tal/str/str.c#L43-L69)
   do_vfmt grows the format buffer by doubling via tal_resize (realloc) until vsnprintf fits, then tal_resize(buf, off+ret+1): for a policy_mod string of >=128 KiB the error string's final buffer is a glibc mmap'd chunk, which free() munmaps; and for small strings the allocation at line 53 happens before vsnprintf reads the freed `msg` at line 59, so the freed chunk can be recycled under the read.
5. [plugins/funder.c:1370–1374](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/funder.c#L1370-L1374)
   funderupdate binds policy_mod via p_opt_def("policy_mod", param_policy_mod, ...) and is a plain plugin RPC method (commands[] at 1457-1462), so any RPC caller permitted `funderupdate` by their rune reaches the parser with an arbitrary string; lightningd forwards the params raw (plugin.c:1346 json_stream_forward_change_id).
6. [lightningd/plugin.c:297–302](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L297-L302)
   funder is loaded as an important plugin; when it dies lightningd logs 'Plugin marked as important, shutting down lightningd!' and calls lightningd_exit(ld, 1), so a SIGSEGV in funder stops the whole node.
7. [plugins/commando.c:458–459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L458-L459)
   commando reassembles rune-authorised requests up to 1 MiB (append_contents(..., 1024*1024)); clnrest accepts bodies up to 2 MiB (rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:28). Both exceed glibc's default 128 KiB mmap threshold, so a remote rune bearer can make the freed error string an mmap'd (hence unmapped-on-free) chunk.

## Impact
Availability HIGH: a policy_mod string of >=128 KiB makes the freed error string an mmap'd chunk that free() unmaps; the read in command_fail_badparam faults, the important funder plugin dies, and lightningd_exit(ld, 1) stops the whole node (plugin.c:297-302) until the operator or systemd (contrib/init/lightningd.service Restart=on-failure) restarts it, repeatably. Confidentiality LOW: for small values stale/recycled heap content from the freed chunk is formatted into the error reply and the log; in the traced sequence the recycled bytes are the plugin's own log text (tal_hdr absorbs the tcache pointers), so the disclosure is minor. No integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a commando or clnrest client whose rune permits funderupdate but not stop/plugin (createrune.json:112 directs operators to restrict methods, so such runes are the intended bound). It sends funderupdate with a policy_mod string that is neither an integer nor a satoshi amount; no check in lightningd or funder rejects the value before the free-then-use. Network reachable (commando over the Lightning peer connection; clnrest HTTP). AT:P because the crash outcome depends on allocator state outside the attacker's control (glibc mmap threshold not already raised above the chosen size); the UAF read itself is unconditional. PR:H because the rune grants administrative control over funder policy.

## Recommended fix
param_policy_mod() frees the u64_option() error string and then passes the dangling pointer to command_fail_badparam(), which formats it into the log and the JSON-RPC reply. Fix criteria: When both u64_option() and parse_amount_sat() reject policy_mod, the error returned must be built from live memory (a fresh message, as amount_sat_or_u64_option() does, or the u64_option string kept alive until after command_fail_badparam returns); no freed pointer may be read. Verify under ASan that `funderupdate policy_mod=abc` and a >=1 MiB non-numeric policy_mod both return a clean invalid-parameter error with no use-after-free report and the funder plugin stays up.

# CSV exporters pass unchecked gmtime() result to strftime for injected timestamps

## Details
All four CSV row emitters in plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c convert the event timestamp with

    time_t tv = ev->timestamp;
    strftime(timebuf, sizeof(timebuf), FMT, gmtime(&tv));

without checking gmtime()'s return value (lines 496, 568, 687, 773). Event timestamps are arbitrary u64 values: `injectutxodeposit` (lightningd/coin_mvts.c:421-460) takes `timestamp` as param_u64 with no range check, stores it verbatim in lightningd's chain_moves table (db_bind_u64), and `listchainmoves` returns it to bookkeeper, which stores it in the chain_event (bookkeeper.c:1440). For a value such as 2^62 (year ~1.5e11) the broken-down year does not fit in `int`; glibc's gmtime (assumption: glibc 2.36 as in the debian:bookworm-slim Docker base and the release tarballs; musl behaves the same) returns NULL with EOVERFLOW, and strftime dereferences the NULL `struct tm` -- a segfault in the bookkeeper plugin. Because bookkeeper is `important`, lightningd shuts down.

The poisoned event is persistent: it lives in lightningd's database (there is no RPC to delete chain moves) and is re-ingested after restart, so every subsequent `bkpr-dumpincomecsv` whose time window includes it (the default window is unbounded) crashes the node again until the operator finds the row and works around it (e.g. by passing end_time). The injected deposit must land in an income event: a deposit to a non-external account (e.g. `wallet` or any custom name) whose txid has no matching internal spend (incomestmt.c:143-189), which is the normal case for an invented outpoint.

Who can do this: a rune bearer -- via commando (plugins/commando.c:386-429 forwards any method the rune passes checkrune for) or clnrest (POST /v1/injectutxodeposit with a Rune header) -- whose rune permits `injectutxodeposit`. The method is undocumented (no doc/schemas entry, so cln-grpc does not expose it) and commented as an internal interface for bookkeeper, so such a rune is a deliberate, non-default grant: an operator exposing third-party-wallet bookkeeping to an external accounting client. A rune scoped to injecting bookkeeping entries concedes falsified accounting rows, not the ability to make the node crash on every accounting export. The export is triggered by the same bearer if the rune also allows `bkpr-dumpincomecsv`, or otherwise by the operator's own routine export. The `utxo_deposit` notification path (bookkeeper.c:1692-1743) reaches the same sink but is driven only by installed plugins, which the threat model trusts.

The bkpr-report sibling (report.c:69-93) has the related defect of ignoring gmtime_r/localtime_r failure and formatting an uninitialised struct tm, which is undefined behaviour but not a NULL dereference.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:483–496](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L483-L496)
   cointrack_entry: time_t tv = ev->timestamp (u64 copied verbatim from the chain event) then strftime(..., gmtime(&tv)) at line 496 with no NULL check; glibc gmtime returns NULL (EOVERFLOW) when the year does not fit in int and strftime dereferences it.
2. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:554–568](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L554-L568)
   koinly_entry: same unchecked gmtime() passed to strftime (line 568).
3. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:681–687](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L681-L687)
   harmony_entry: same unchecked gmtime() passed to strftime (line 687).
4. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:764–773](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L764-L773)
   quickbooks_entry: same unchecked gmtime() passed to strftime (line 773).
5. [lightningd/coin\_mvts.c:421–460](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/coin_mvts.c#L421-L460)
   injectutxodeposit takes `timestamp` as param_u64 with no range check, new_foreign_deposit (common/coin_mvt.c:611) stores it verbatim, wallet_save_chain_mvt persists it with db_bind_u64 (wallet.c:7124); listchainmoves echoes it at line 200. No doc/schemas entry exists, so cln-grpc does not expose this method; commando and clnrest forward any rune-permitted method.
6. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1440](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1440)
   Bookkeeper ingests the chain move's timestamp with json_to_u64, creates the custom account (find_or_create_account) and runs maybe_update_account/do_account_close_checks, none of which reject or abort on a plain foreign deposit (tests/test_bookkeeper.py::test_bookkeeper_custom_notifs exercises this flow through to bkpr-listincome).
7. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:143–189](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L143-L189)
   maybe_chain_income: a 'deposit' to a non-external account whose txid has no matching spending_txid row becomes an income event via chain_to_income, which copies ev->timestamp (line 40) into the income event the CSV emitters format. The default export window (0, SQLITE_MAX_UINT = INT64_MAX] includes 2^62.

## Impact
Segfault of the important bookkeeper plugin stops lightningd (plugin.c: important plugin death is fatal). The poisoned event persists in lightningd's DB with no RPC to remove it, so the crash recurs on every CSV export covering it until the operator intervenes. No confidentiality impact; integrity of accounting data is already within what the injectutxodeposit grant concedes.

## Reproduction steps
1. A rune bearer (commando over a Lightning peer connection, or clnrest HTTP) whose rune permits injectutxodeposit calls it with timestamp=4611686018427387904, a non-external account and an invented outpoint. lightningd persists the row; bookkeeper ingests it on its next refresh. Any bkpr-dumpincomecsv call (by the same bearer if the rune allows it, otherwise the operator's routine export) formats the row: gmtime returns NULL and strftime dereferences it, deterministically, on every export covering the row. Attack requirements are present because the deployment must have issued a rune granting this undocumented internal method; privileges are low (a method-scoped rune, not operator access). User interaction is none in the case where the rune also covers the export; where it does not, the operator's own routine export is the passive trigger.

## Recommended fix
1. The CSV emitters assume gmtime() always succeeds; event timestamps are externally supplied u64 values that can exceed the representable year range, making gmtime return NULL which strftime dereferences. Fix criteria: Timestamp formatting must handle gmtime/gmtime_r/localtime_r failure (emit a placeholder or the raw integer) in all four incomestmt.c emitters and in the report.c formatters; an injected deposit with timestamp 2^62 must be exported by bkpr-dumpincomecsv in every format without crashing the plugin.
2. injectutxodeposit and injectutxospend accept any u64 timestamp without validation, persisting values no consumer can represent. Fix criteria: lightningd rejects timestamps outside a sane range (e.g. beyond a bounded number of years from now) with a JSON-RPC parameter error, so no out-of-range timestamp reaches the chain_moves table.

# bkpr-report '{{' literal allocated on tmpctx is used after free

## Details
`bkpr-report` accepts a caller-supplied `format` string (doc/schemas/bkpr-report.json:62: "To include a literal `{`, write `{{`"). param_report_format (plugins/bkpr/report.c:355-370) parses it onto `cmd`, so the resulting report_format lives until the command completes. In parse_report_format the `{{` escape is handled by

    lit = tal_strndup(f->str, *start, p - *start);
    lit = tal_strcat(tmpctx, take(lit), "{");
    ...
    tal_arr_expand(&f->str, lit);

ccan tal_strcat_ -> tal_dup_ on a take()n source resizes the buffer in place and tal_steal()s it to the requested context (ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c:903-910), so this literal is owned by tmpctx while its pointer is retained in `f->str`. Every other literal (add_literal, report.c:231-242) is correctly owned by `f->str`.

json_bkpr_report (bookkeeper.c:513-528) then calls refresh_moves(), which never completes synchronously: it either joins an in-flight refresh and returns command_still_pending (bookkeeper.c:304-307) or starts the `listchainmoves` -> `datastore` -> `listchannelmoves` request chain with send_outreq (313-319). libplugin's plugin_main calls daemon_setup (plugins/libplugin.c:2465), which installs daemon_poll as the poll function (common/daemon.c:190); daemon_poll calls clean_tmpctx() before every poll() (common/daemon.c:165), freeing the `{{` literal. When do_bkpr_report finally runs (report.c:474-496), format_event (report.c:443-446) does `tal_strcat(ctx, take(out), fmt->str[i])` on the freed string: a heap use-after-free read (strlen + memcpy) whose bytes are copied into the `report` array returned to the caller.

What is read depends on heap reuse. The tal header (struct tal_hdr, 40 bytes, tal.c:29-36) precedes the user pointer, so the dangling pointer addresses chunk+40, past glibc's tcache metadata; if the ~48-byte chunk has not been reused the stale "{" is still there and the output looks correct, but the refresh allocates many tal objects of this size class (JSON result parsing of listchainmoves/listchannelmoves, tal_strdup'd strings, small structs), so the chunk is routinely reoccupied and the caller receives that occupant's leading bytes up to the first NUL. A strlen that runs across the heap top can crash the bookkeeper plugin, which is `important`, taking lightningd down; with a small chunk inside the arena that is the less common outcome.

Any RPC caller permitted to invoke `bkpr-report` triggers it with a format containing `{{`, e.g. `format="{{{account}"`: rune bearers over commando or clnrest, cln-grpc certificate holders (cln-grpc/src/server.rs:3834 BkprReport), or socket users. bkpr-report is an otherwise read-only, low-risk method to grant. The `{{` feature is documented but exercised by no test in tests/test_bookkeeper.py, so valgrind/ASan runs never cover it.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/report.c:274–286](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/report.c#L274-L286)
   For an escaped '{{' the literal is built with tal_strndup(f->str, ...) and then tal_strcat(tmpctx, take(lit), "{") (line 279). Because s1 is take()n, ccan tal_dup_ resizes it in place and tal_steal()s it to the new ctx, i.e. tmpctx (ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c:903-910). The now tmpctx-owned pointer is stored in f->str (line 281), whereas every other literal (add_literal) is owned by f->str, and the report_format itself is allocated on cmd (param_report_format, line 367).
2. [plugins/bkpr/report.c:440–446](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/report.c#L440-L446)
   format_event later reads fmt->str[i] for NULL fmt entries via tal_strcat (strlen + memcpy) -- this is the use of the freed tmpctx string.
3. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:513–528](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L513-L528)
   json_bkpr_report parses the format during param() and then calls refresh_moves(), which issues asynchronous listchainmoves/datastore/listchannelmoves requests before do_bkpr_report runs. The handler returns to the event loop in between.
4. [common/daemon.c:154–166](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/daemon.c#L154-L166)
   daemon_poll (installed by daemon_setup via io_poll_override, line 190; plugin_main calls daemon_setup) calls clean_tmpctx() on every poll, so all tmpctx children -- including the '{{' literal -- are freed before the asynchronous callbacks fire.
5. [plugins/bkpr/report.c:474–495](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/report.c#L474-L495)
   do_bkpr_report is the deferred callback that calls format_event with the now-dangling format.

## Impact
Bytes from whatever allocation reoccupied the freed ~48-byte chunk during the refresh (the dangling pointer is 40 bytes into the chunk, past tcache metadata) are copied into the report output: a limited, heap-layout-dependent disclosure of bookkeeper-plugin heap contents to a caller whose rune grants only a bookkeeping read. A strlen over freed/reused memory can also run off the heap and crash the important bookkeeper plugin, which stops lightningd, though with a small in-arena chunk this is the less common outcome. No integrity impact on node state.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any RPC caller allowed bkpr-report: a rune bearer via commando (over the Lightning connection) or clnrest, a cln-grpc cert holder (server.rs:3834), or a socket user. They send bkpr-report with a format string containing '{{'. parse_report_format deterministically stores a tmpctx-owned pointer in the cmd-owned format; refresh_moves_ always returns pending (joins an in-flight refresh or sends listchainmoves), so at least one daemon_poll -> clean_tmpctx runs before do_bkpr_report. No check stands in the way; the read of freed memory is deterministic, only its content varies with heap reuse.

## Recommended fix
The '{{' literal is built with tal_strcat(tmpctx, take(lit), "{"), which steals the string to tmpctx, while the pointer is retained in the long-lived report_format (f->str); the format outlives tmpctx because the command completes asynchronously after refresh_moves. Fix criteria: Every string referenced from a report_format must be owned by that report_format (or by cmd). After the fix, a bkpr-report whose format contains '{{' must produce the literal '{' correctly after the asynchronous refresh, with no tmpctx-owned pointers stored in f->str (verifiable with valgrind/ASan on a test that uses '{{' in bkpr-report).

# spenderp splice dereferences missing optional 'splice' feerate, crashing lightningd when estimates unavailable

## Details
When a splice is run without a script-pinned feerate (always the case for `splicein` and `spliceout`, whose generated scripts carry none and which expose no feerate parameter; splice.c:2244, 2294), continue_splice() (splice.c:1647-1648) calls load_feerate(), which issues `feerates style=perkw` to lightningd and handles the reply in feerate_get_result() (splice.c:791-797):

    tok = json_get_member(buf, result, "perkw");
    tok = json_get_member(buf, tok, "splice");
    if (!json_to_u32(buf, tok, &splice_cmd->feerate_per_kw)) ...

lightningd adds `perkw.splice` only `if (rate)` (chaintopology.c:746-748). splice_feerate() returns 0 when opening_feerate() returns 0 (chaintopology.c:634-637), i.e. when no force-feerates are configured and feerate_for_deadline() returns its documented 'don't know' value 0 because topo->feerates[0] is empty (chaintopology.c:433-440, 407-409). update_feerates() deliberately ignores empty estimate arrays (chaintopology.c:551-554), so this state holds exactly while lightningd has not received a single non-empty estimate since its own start: setup_topology() takes one synchronous estimatefees reply before the RPC comes up (chaintopology.c:1516, 1567), and bcli answers with an empty `feerates` array whenever getmempoolinfo or any estimatesmartfee call fails or returns no `feerate` (plugins/bcli.c:278-287, 532, 563, 573-581 — bitcoind's 'Insufficient data or no feerate found', the case for a fresh or blocksonly bitcoind). The window closes at the first successful 30-second poll (poll_seconds, chaintopology.c:1312). json_feerates flags this state with warning_missing_feerates (chaintopology.c:721-723), the feerates schema lists perkw.splice as optional, and the project's own design for it elsewhere is a clean failure (opening_control.c:1374-1377 'Cannot estimate fees'). json_get_membern() returns NULL for the missing member (json_parse_simple.c:225-237); json_to_u32 -> json_to_u64 then reads tok->start through the NULL token (json_parse_simple.c:62-65, 113-117), so spenderp segfaults. spenderp is loaded as an important builtin plugin (plugins/Makefile:138; plugin.c:2578-2590), so its death terminates lightningd.

The path is reachable by any RPC caller allowed to run splicein or spliceout (the operator, or a rune bearer through commando/clnrest/grpc whose rune permits the method; dev-splice additionally needs --developer, libplugin.c:1282) and needs no peer cooperation. The attacker does not control the missing-estimate precondition but can simply try: the crash is deterministic while it holds. It also fires after stfu_channels has succeeded (splice.c:2027-2037 -> 1964-1998 -> execute_splice -> continue_splice), so the targeted channels are quiescent at the moment lightningd dies. The sibling check for a present-but-zero value (`command_fail` 'Failed to load a default feerate', splice.c:798-801) shows the author anticipated an unavailable feerate but only for that shape.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/spender/splice.c:791–796](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/splice.c#L791-L796)
   feerate_get_result takes tok = json_get_member(buf, perkw_tok, "splice") and passes it straight to json_to_u32 without a NULL check; the member is optional in lightningd's reply, so a missing member is a NULL pointer dereference.
2. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:62–64](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L62-L64)
   json_to_u64 (reached via json_to_u32 at 113-117) unconditionally reads tok->start/tok->end; json_get_membern (225-237) returns NULL when the label is absent.
3. [lightningd/chaintopology.c:746–748](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/chaintopology.c#L746-L748)
   json_feerates emits perkw.splice only `if (rate)`; splice_feerate (634-637) returns 0 when opening_feerate returns 0, which feerate_for_deadline (433-440) documents as 'don't know' whenever topo->feerates[0] is empty. The same function flags that state with warning_missing_feerates (721-723).
4. [lightningd/chaintopology.c:551–554](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/chaintopology.c#L551-L554)
   update_feerates ignores empty estimate arrays, so topo->feerates[0] stays NULL (memset at 1313) for as long as lightningd has never received a non-empty estimate since start; setup_topology's single synchronous estimatefees (1516, 1567) does not change that when bcli returns none.
5. [plugins/bcli.c:573–581](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L573-L581)
   On non-regtest, an estimatesmartfee reply without `feerate` (bitcoind 'Insufficient data or no feerate found') makes bcli return estimatefees_null_response (278-287): an empty `feerates` array. getmempoolinfo or estimatesmartfee exiting non-zero (532, 563) does the same.
6. [plugins/spender/splice.c:1635–1648](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/spender/splice.c#L1635-L1648)
   continue_splice calls load_feerate whenever feerate_per_kw is 0, which is always the case for splicein/spliceout (2244, 2294: no feerate parameter, feerate_per_kw = 0) and only after stfu_channels has quiesced the target channels (2027 -> 1964-1998 -> execute_splice -> 1923).
7. [doc/schemas/feerates.json](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/schemas/feerates.json) (whole file)
   The feerates response schema lists perkw.splice as optional (required: min_acceptable, max_acceptable, floor, estimates only), so the plugin dereferences a field the API contract allows to be absent.

## Impact
Segfault of spenderp, an important builtin plugin, makes lightningd exit: full node outage until restarted, with the targeted channels left in STFU at the moment of death. No confidentiality or integrity impact; funds are not at risk beyond the outage.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is an RPC caller authorized to run splicein or spliceout — in adversarial terms a commando or clnrest rune bearer whose rune permits those fund-moving methods, reached over the network (peer connection or HTTPS). They issue a normal splicein/spliceout while lightningd has never obtained a fee estimate since start (bitcoind without estimatesmartfee data, e.g. a fresh or blocksonly node); the attacker does not control that state but can detect it (feerates reports warning_missing_feerates) or simply retry. No defence intervenes: the NULL token is dereferenced deterministically. PR is HIGH because the rune must grant a fund-moving method, which the project's rune design treats as privileged (readonly is the standard restriction); AT is PRESENT for the missing-estimate state.

## Recommended fix
feerate_get_result assumes the optional perkw.splice member is always present and passes a possibly-NULL token to json_to_u32, which dereferences it unconditionally. Fix criteria: A feerates reply lacking perkw.splice (lightningd's documented 'cannot estimate' state) must produce a clean RPC error that also releases the already-quiesced channels (the do_fail path), never a dereference. Verify by driving splicein while lightningd reports warning_missing_feerates and confirming the command fails with an error, the channels leave STFU, and spenderp stays alive.

# JSON validator accepts raw control characters in strings; labels re-emitted unescaped break strict consumers

## Details
CLN's JSON-RPC parser validates string tokens only for UTF-8 (common/json_parse_simple.c:353-356). Unescaped control characters (0x01-0x1F), which JSON forbids inside strings, pass both jsmn and validate_jsmn_datum. `param_label` (common/json_param.c:513-524) then stores the raw token bytes as a `struct json_escape` -- a type whose contract is "already valid JSON string content" -- and `json_add_escaped_string` (common/json_stream.c:335-348) re-emits those bytes verbatim into listinvoices/listoffers results, the invoice_creation and invoice_payment notifications, and the invoice_payment hook payload. Every other output path escapes (json_add_string via json_out), so labels are the asymmetric case.

Who can inject: a commando rune bearer whose rune permits `invoice` or `createinvoice` (an invoice-only rune is the canonical point-of-sale grant). commando parses the peer's bytes with the same lenient validator (plugins/commando.c:376) and forwards params values byte-for-byte with json_add_jsonstr (commando.c:286-294). lightningd accepts the request and stores the label. (clnrest/cln-grpc paths are not vectors: serde re-serializes and escapes the byte.)

Consequences:
1. Default configuration: cln-grpc (on by default), clnrest and pyln-client use strict parsers (serde_json, json.JSONDecoder). `listinvoices` (and `listoffers` for a poisoned offer label) fail for all of them with a parse error for as long as the invoice exists (expired invoices are kept until deleted; lightning-cli escapes argv so `delinvoice label=<raw>` from the CLI does not match -- the operator must delete via raw JSON or a `"..."` literal argument). The invoice_creation/invoice_payment notifications for that invoice are undecodable by cln-plugin, which answers lightningd with an id-less error that lightningd drops (plugin.c:677-682), so gRPC/REST subscribers silently miss them. lightning-cli prints the raw bytes, allowing terminal escape injection (0x1B) into the operator's terminal; the same applies to any remote node's reply printed with `lightning-cli --commando`.
2. With `experimental-lsps-client` enabled (cln-lsps-client, a builtin `important` plugin, registers the `invoice_payment` hook, plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:115): the attacker creates a 1 msat invoice with such a label and pays it from any node. lightningd serialises the hook payload with the raw byte (invoice.c:198-212); cln-plugin cannot parse it, recovers the request id (codec.rs:145-200) and replies with a -32700 error (lib.rs:1055-1059); plugin_hook_callback sees no `result` and calls fatal() (plugin_hook.c:268-275). lightningd aborts -- a remote crash of the node by a holder of an invoice-only rune, for the price of one millisatoshi. Any third-party Rust (cln-plugin) or Python (pyln, json.loads strict) plugin hooking invoice_payment produces the same fatal; a Python plugin subscribed to invoice_creation dies on the notification, which is itself fatal if the plugin is `important`.

Root cause: two layers disagree about what a valid JSON string is. The fix belongs at the boundary (reject unescaped control characters in validate_jsmn_datum, as JSON requires) and/or at param_label/json_add_escaped_string (escape before storing or emitting). Assumption stated: the pinned external jsmn behaves as upstream zserge/jsmn, which performs no control-character check in jsmn_parse_string.

## Evidence
1. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:353–365](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L353-L365)
   validate_jsmn_datum is the only content check CLN adds on top of jsmn for JSMN_STRING tokens, and it runs utf8_check alone (common/utils.c:184-200, a loop over ccan utf8_decode, which accepts every single-byte ASCII value except 0x00). RFC 8259 s7 forbids unescaped U+0000..U+001F inside strings, but 0x01..0x1F pass. The pinned jsmn (external/jsmn submodule, built with JSMN_STRICT=1 by external/Makefile:87; source absent from this checkout) is assumed to behave as upstream zserge/jsmn, whose jsmn_parse_string checks only escape sequences and \u hex digits, never raw control bytes. So a JSON-RPC request containing a raw 0x01 inside a string value is accepted as valid by json_parse_input() (json_parse_simple.c:511-547), which is what lightningd's RPC reader (common/jsonrpc_io.c:70-80) and commando's json_parse_simple use.
2. [common/json\_param.c:513–523](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_param.c#L513-L523)
   param_label wraps the raw token bytes into struct json_escape with json_escape_string_(), which (ccan/json_escape/json_escape.c:6-16) is a plain memcpy: the type's contract is 'already valid JSON string content'. A raw 0x01 that jsmn let through therefore becomes the stored label verbatim; no escaping ever happens on this path (unlike param_escaped_string + json_add_string).
3. [common/json\_stream.c:335–347](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_stream.c#L335-L347)
   json_add_escaped_string copies esc->s raw between quotes, so the stored byte is emitted into every response/notification/hook payload that carries the label (lightningd/invoice.c:44 listinvoices, invoice.c:198-212 invoice_payment hook payload, notification.c:201-258 invoice_payment / invoice_creation notifications, offer.c:27/369 listoffers). The output is 'valid' only for jsmn-based readers.
4. [plugins/commando.c:286–293](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L286-L293)
   Delivery vector: commando parses the peer's bytes with json_parse_simple (commando.c:376, same validator) and re-forwards each params value with json_add_jsonstr(json_tok_full(...)), a byte copy. clnrest and cln-grpc re-serialize via serde and would escape the byte as \u0001, so a rune bearer over commando is the way a raw control byte reaches lightningd's `invoice`/`createinvoice` label.
5. [plugins/src/codec.rs:85–109](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/src/codec.rs#L85-L109)
   cln-plugin (used by cln-grpc, clnrest, cln-lsps-client...) parses each stdin message with serde_json Value::from_str, which rejects raw control characters inside strings. On failure it synthesizes a -32700 error reply whose id is recovered textually by recover_id() (codec.rs:145-200), and lib.rs:1055-1059 sends that error reply back to lightningd. For a notification (no id) lightningd ignores it (plugin.c:677-682) and the plugin simply never sees the event; for a hook request the id is recovered and the error is delivered as the hook's answer.
6. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:268–284](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L268-L284)
   plugin_hook_callback treats any hook reply without a `result` member as fatal(): 'Plugin %s for %s returned non-result response'. plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:115 registers the invoice_payment hook (active when experimental-lsps-client is set), so paying an invoice whose label holds a raw control byte makes lightningd abort.
7. [cln-rpc/src/codec.rs:91–101](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/cln-rpc/src/codec.rs#L91-L101)
   Default-configuration impact: the client codec used by cln-grpc (on by default, 127.0.0.1:9736) and clnrest fails with 'failed to parse JSON' on the listinvoices/listoffers response, surfaced as RpcError 'reading response from socket' (cln-rpc/src/lib.rs:234-245); contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/lightning.py:327 uses a strict json.JSONDecoder and raises likewise. These methods stay broken for every such consumer while the poisoned invoice/offer exists.

## Impact
Worst case (experimental-lsps-client enabled, or any third-party strict-JSON plugin -- cln-plugin or pyln -- hooking invoice_payment): lightningd aborts via fatal() -- full availability loss of the node with on-chain consequences, repeatable each restart as the HTLC is retried. Default configuration: cln-grpc (on by default, 127.0.0.1:9736) and clnrest fail every listinvoices (and listoffers for a poisoned offer label) with a codec error (cln-rpc/src/codec.rs:91-102, lib.rs:243-247) for as long as the invoice exists; pyln-client's strict json.JSONDecoder (lightning.py:327) raises likewise; the invoice_creation/invoice_payment notifications for that invoice are undecodable by cln-plugin, whose id-less error reply lightningd drops (plugin.c:669-679), so gRPC/REST subscribers silently miss them; lightning-cli prints the raw bytes (terminal escape injection via 0x1B). Integrity impact is the corrupted operator view of invoices (LOW). No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a Lightning peer holding a commando rune that permits `invoice` or `createinvoice` (an invoice-only rune is the canonical point-of-sale grant). Over commando they send {"method":"invoice","params":{"amount_msat":1,"label":"x<0x01>","description":"d"}}. commando hex-decodes the custommsg (commando.c:570-600), json_parse_simple accepts it, checkrune receives params by raw token copy (json_add_tok, commando.c:424-428; param_params only checks the type, runes.c:242-251), and execute_command forwards the value bytes with json_add_jsonstr memcpy (commando.c:286-294). lightningd's reader accepts it (jsonrpc_io.c:70-80 -> json_parse_input), param_label stores the raw bytes (json_param.c:513-523; invoice.c:1167 checks only length) and the label round-trips the DB (db_bind_json_escape/db_col_json_escape). That alone breaks listinvoices for cln-grpc/clnrest/pyln consumers. If the operator has enabled experimental-lsps-client (non-default: plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:121-124 disables the plugin otherwise, hence AT:PRESENT for the worst case), the attacker then pays the 1 msat invoice from any node; the invoice_payment hook payload (invoice.c:198-212) is undecodable by cln-plugin, whose -32700 error reply (plugins/src/codec.rs:91-110, lib.rs:1055-1059; request id recovered because lightningd emits "id" before "params", jsonrpc.c:1584-1587) reaches plugin_hook_callback, which sees code -32700 != PLUGIN_TERMINATED (-4) and no `result` and calls fatal() (plugin_hook.c:268-275). Assumption: serde_json 1.0.151 (Cargo.lock) rejects unescaped control characters inside strings, as its documented RFC 8259 conformance states. No race, no user interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. validate_jsmn_datum accepts JSMN_STRING tokens containing unescaped bytes 0x00-0x1F, which RFC 8259 forbids, so jsmn-valid input is not JSON-valid and downstream strict parsers (serde_json, Python json) reject what lightningd re-emits. Fix criteria: json_parse_input() must reject any string token (keys and values) that contains an unescaped byte below 0x20; a commando/RPC request carrying such a byte is answered with a parse error and never reaches param()/the DB. Verify with a request whose label contains a raw 0x01: it is rejected, and existing round-trip tests with \u0001-escaped labels still pass.
2. param_label stores raw token bytes as an already-escaped json_escape and json_add_escaped_string emits them verbatim, so any byte the parser lets through is reproduced unescaped in results, notifications and hook payloads. Fix criteria: Labels (and every json_escape built from caller input) must be emitted as valid JSON string content for strict parsers: either normalise control characters to \u00XX escapes when the label is accepted, or escape them in json_add_escaped_string. Verify that listinvoices/invoice_payment payloads for a label containing control characters parse with serde_json and Python json, and that plugin_hook.c no longer receives a -32700 reply for such an invoice.
3. plugin_hook_callback turns a plugin's parse-error reply (-32700) into fatal(), so a single undecodable hook payload kills lightningd rather than failing the one hook call. Fix criteria: A hook reply that is a JSON-RPC error produced by the plugin's decoder (or any error other than PLUGIN_TERMINATED) should be handled without aborting lightningd -- e.g. logged and treated as the hook's default/continue result or as the plugin having failed that call. Verify that an invoice_payment hook answered with a -32700 error leaves lightningd running.

# bkpr-inspect reads an uninitialised txo_set array when the account has no open event, crashing the important bookkeeper plugin

## Details
`bkpr-inspect` (plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c, json_inspect -> refresh_moves -> do_inspect) takes an `account` string from the RPC caller (p_req at line 701). do_inspect checks only that the name is not 'wallet'/'external' (is_channel_account) and that bookkeeper has an account of that name, then calls `find_txo_chain(cmd, bkpr, cmd, acct, &txos)` with `struct txo_set **txos` an uninitialised stack local and ignores the boolean result. find_txo_chain (plugins/bkpr/recorder.c:167-191) returns false before its only write to `*sets` when `acct->open_event_db_id == NULL`. do_inspect then evaluates `tal_count(txos)` and dereferences `txos[i]->txid` / `->pairs` on the indeterminate pointer.

Mechanism of the crash: tal_count() calls tal_bytelen() -> to_tal_hdr(), which reads the tal header 24 bytes below the pointer and runs check_bounds() on it and on the header's parent/list pointers. In ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c:135-170 that bounds check is compiled in whenever NDEBUG is unset, which is CLN's release configuration (asserts are compiled in); a stale stack value outside the tal arena therefore triggers call_error("Not a valid header") -> the default tal errorfn (abort), while a value inside the arena yields a garbage element count and wild pointer dereferences. Either way the bookkeeper process dies. bookkeeper is a builtin plugin (plugins/bkpr/Makefile:41) registered as `important` (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2590), so its death shuts down lightningd.

Precondition — an account with no open event — is a supported state, not corruption: open_event_db_id is set only by MVT_CHANNEL_OPEN / MVT_CHANNEL_PROPOSED (account.c:172-179) and is reloaded as NULL from the datastore (account.c:107-112), while parse_and_log_chain_move creates an account for every account_id / originating_account in listchainmoves (bookkeeper.c:1529-1532). Such accounts arise from (a) the documented custom-account feature in plugins/bkpr/README.md — third-party plugins emitting `utxo_deposit`/`utxo_spend` for their own account names, forwarded to lightningd's injectutxodeposit (bookkeeper.c:1692-1743, lightningd/coin_mvts.c:421-455); (b) any `transfer_from=<name>` on such a deposit; (c) a node whose DB was lost and recovered, the case the recorder.c comment anticipates. Their names are visible via bkpr-listbalances / bkpr-listaccountevents.

Attacker position: any RPC caller permitted to run bkpr-inspect — a rune bearer over commando (peer custom messages) or clnrest (HTTP), a cln-grpc certificate holder (cln-grpc/src/server.rs:3642 exposes BkprInspect), or a socket user. The built-in `readonly` rune shortcut (lightningd/runes.c:439-470: method^list|method^get|method=summary) does not cover bkpr-inspect, so the grant must be explicit (e.g. method=bkpr-inspect or method^bkpr) — a plausible grant for an accounting client since the command is read-only. Such a grant concedes inspection of accounts, not the ability to abort the node; the bug turns it into an at-will lightningd shutdown. The condition under which it holds: an account without an open event exists on the node (custom-account plugin in use, or post-recovery) and the caller knows or guesses its name.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:574–600](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L574-L600)
   do_inspect declares `struct txo_set **txos;` (line 579) without initialising it, calls find_txo_chain(cmd, bkpr, cmd, acct, &txos) at line 593 discarding its bool result, then at line 600 evaluates tal_count(txos) and dereferences txos[i]->txid / ->pairs. The only guards before that are is_channel_account() (name is not 'wallet'/'external', common/coin_mvt.h:332) and find_account(); neither checks acct->open_event_db_id. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [plugins/bkpr/recorder.c:176–190](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/recorder.c#L176-L190)
   find_txo_chain returns false at line 184 when acct->open_event_db_id is NULL (logging 'Cannot find the open_event for %s: did we lose our db?') before the only assignment to the out-parameter, `*sets = tal_arr(ctx, struct txo_set *, 0)` at line 190. On that path the caller's pointer is never written. The other caller, account_onchain_closeheight (recorder.c:298), tests the return value and is safe.
3. [plugins/bkpr/account.c:161–178](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/account.c#L161-L178)
   maybe_update_account sets open_event_db_id only when a chain event carries MVT_CHANNEL_PROPOSED or MVT_CHANNEL_OPEN. new_account (account.c:56) initialises it to NULL and fromwire_account (account.c:107-112) reloads a NULL from the datastore, so an account created by any other movement persists across restarts with no open event.
4. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1528–1532](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1528-L1532)
   parse_and_log_chain_move calls find_or_create_account for every account_id and originating_account returned by lightningd's listchainmoves, so any non-wallet/non-external name appearing in a chain move becomes a bookkeeper 'channel' account that passes is_channel_account() yet has no open event.
5. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1692–1742](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1692-L1742)
   json_utxo_deposit forwards third-party plugins' `utxo_deposit` notifications (account and transfer_from strings verbatim) to lightningd's injectutxodeposit. plugins/bkpr/README.md documents this custom-account feature with the example account "nifty's secret stash"; such accounts are the supported, persistent state that makes the crash reachable.
6. [lightningd/coin\_mvts.c:421–454](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/coin_mvts.c#L421-L454)
   injectutxodeposit stores the arbitrary `account` and `transfer_from` strings as chain-move account ids (alt_account), which bookkeeper then materialises as accounts via listchainmoves.

## Impact
The bookkeeper plugin dereferences an indeterminate pointer and aborts (tal 'Not a valid header') or segfaults. bookkeeper is registered as an `important` plugin, so lightningd shuts down: channels go offline and HTLCs cannot be resolved until the operator restarts the node; the attacker can repeat the call after every restart as long as the account persists. No confidentiality or integrity impact: the failing command returns no output and the read does not reach any persisted state.

## Reproduction steps
1. The caller needs an RPC path that allows bkpr-inspect: a rune bearer via commando (reached over the Lightning peer connection) or clnrest, a cln-grpc mTLS cert holder, or a Unix-socket user; the readonly rune does not include it, so an explicit bkpr-* grant is required (PR:L). A single call with the name of an account lacking an open event suffices (AC:L, UI:N). Attack requirement outside the attacker's control: such an account must exist on the node (custom-account plugin using the documented utxo_deposit feature, injectutxodeposit transfer_from, or DB recovery) and its name must be known (listable via bkpr-listbalances if the rune permits, else guessed) — AT:P. No defence intervenes: the uninitialised read is undefined behaviour whose outcome on CLN's release build (tal bounds check active, asserts on) is an abort or SIGSEGV of the bookkeeper plugin.

## Recommended fix
do_inspect uses the `txos` out-parameter of find_txo_chain without initialising it and without honouring find_txo_chain's failure return, so the early-return path (account has no open_event_db_id) leaves it indeterminate and it is then read and dereferenced. Fix criteria: bkpr-inspect on an account whose open_event_db_id is NULL must return a well-formed JSON-RPC error (or an empty `txs` array) and must never evaluate tal_count(txos) or dereference it; every caller of find_txo_chain must either check its return value or receive a defined `*sets` on all paths (e.g. find_txo_chain always assigns `*sets` before any return, or do_inspect initialises txos to NULL and fails the command when find_txo_chain returns false). Verify by creating a custom account (injectutxodeposit account=X, or a plugin utxo_deposit) and calling bkpr-inspect X: the bookkeeper plugin must stay alive and reply.
