# Unbounded recursion draining the getroutes waiter queue through command destructors

## Details
askrene limits concurrent routing children to max_children (default 4, askrene.c:1565). json_getroutes parks every further request in askrene->waiters (askrene.c:965-971) with no bound on queue length. When a live request's command is tal_free()d, its destructor destroy_live_command (852-866) pops the next waiter and calls begin_request (868-888), which — unless auto.localchans is requested — calls do_getroutes synchronously. If that request fails synchronously (unknown source or destination node at 630-648, or pipe()/fork() failure at 677-695, all reaching `fail:` at 745-748), command_fail -> command_done_err -> command_complete_nojson (libplugin.c:470-478) calls tal_free(cmd), whose destructor runs destroy_live_command again inside the still-open frame, pops the next waiter, and so on. Nothing returns to the event loop between levels: the recursion depth equals the number of consecutively queued requests that fail synchronously.

An RPC caller admitted to getroutes can drive this: a readonly rune suffices (lightningd/runes.c:439-452 allows method^get), commando only caps partially-assembled messages at 16 (commando.c:416-417 drops a terminal message from incoming_commands before executing it, so executing commands per peer are unbounded), and lightningd's RPC reader (jsonrpc.c:1199-1201) only pauses on pending output, not on pending forwarded commands, so one connection can pipeline arbitrarily many requests. The attacker issues four hard-but-valid queries (linear_routes in child/mcf.c:1379-1385 iterates until the route_seconds=10 deadline), then pipelines thousands of getroutes naming a well-formed pubkey absent from the gossmap and no auto.localchans layer. When the first child finishes, the whole queue drains in one nested chain (tal_free -> del_tree -> notify -> destroy_live_command -> begin_request -> do_getroutes -> command_fail -> command_done_err -> command_complete -> command_complete_nojson -> tal_free ...). Two resources grow linearly with queue depth: the stack, and the heap — ccan tal runs destructors before freeing children (ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c del_tree_inner), so each level's cmd subtree, including the per-request capacities copy (568) and biases array (624) each sized by gossmap_max_chan_idx (hundreds of KB on a mainnet gossmap), stays allocated until the chain unwinds. With enough queued requests the process exhausts its stack (default 8 MiB; per-level consumption not measured — several thousand to low tens of thousands of levels assumed) or memory, and askrene — an `important` plugin — dies, which stops lightningd. Below that threshold the drain is a long synchronous burst blocking all route computation. The root defect is draining the waiter queue recursively from a tal destructor instead of scheduling the next waiter on the event loop, combined with an uncapped queue.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:852–866](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L852-L866)
   destroy_live_command is the tal destructor of a finishing getroutes command; it pops the next waiter and calls begin_request synchronously from inside tal_free(cmd), before that cmd's children are freed.
2. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:868–888](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L868-L888)
   begin_request attaches the same destructor to the popped command and, when auto.localchans is absent, calls do_getroutes directly with no asynchronous hop.
3. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:630–648](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L630-L648)
   do_getroutes fails synchronously for a well-formed source or destination pubkey that is not in the gossmap (also for pipe/fork failure at 677-695), jumping to the fail label.
4. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:745–748](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L745-L748)
   The fail label returns command_fail(cmd, ...) synchronously, which completes and frees the command inside the caller's frame.
5. [plugins/libplugin.c:470–478](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin.c#L470-L478)
   command_complete_nojson (reached from command_fail -> command_done_err -> command_complete) calls tal_free(cmd), running destroy_live_command nested inside the previous level: each queued synchronously-failing request adds a full set of frames.
6. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:965–971](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L965-L971)
   Once num_live_requests >= max_children every further getroutes is appended to askrene->waiters; there is no cap on queue length.
7. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:624](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L624)
   Per-request biases array (and the capacities copy at 568), each sized by gossmap_max_chan_idx, are allocated under cmd; because tal runs destructors before freeing children, every level's arrays remain allocated for the whole recursive drain, so heap grows linearly with queue depth as well as stack.
8. [lightningd/runes.c:439–459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L439-L459)
   The readonly rune shortcut allows any method beginning with 'get', so a bearer of the least-privileged standard rune may call getroutes over commando or clnrest.
9. [plugins/commando.c:414–417](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L414-L417)
   A terminal commando message is removed from incoming_commands before execution; the 16-entry cap (453-455) applies only to partially-assembled messages, so a peer can have an unbounded number of getroutes executing/queued concurrently.

## Impact
Stack exhaustion (or OOM from the per-level capacities/biases arrays retained during the drain on a mainnet-sized gossmap) kills askrene, an `important` plugin, which stops lightningd. Short of the crash the recursive drain is a long synchronous burst blocking route computation for every payer. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a getroutes-capable RPC caller: a connected peer holding a readonly rune via commando, or a clnrest/wss client with such a rune (PR:L). They send four valid, hard routing queries that occupy the children up to the 10 s route_seconds deadline (mcf.c:1379-1385), then pipeline thousands of getroutes with a pubkey absent from the gossmap and no auto.localchans; neither commando (cap only on partial messages), lightningd's RPC reader (pauses only on pending output) nor askrene (uncapped waiters) limits the backlog. When the first child completes, the queue drains in one nested recursion. Needs the slots held while a large request volume is queued, so attack_requirements PRESENT; otherwise low complexity and no user interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. The waiter queue is drained recursively from inside a tal destructor; a request that fails synchronously re-enters the destructor before the previous frame returns, so N consecutive synchronous failures nest N frame sets and retain N command subtrees. Fix criteria: Dequeuing the next waiter must happen iteratively or via the event loop (e.g. a zero-delay timer or io_always), so that any number of queued synchronously-failing requests use O(1) stack and each completed command's allocations are released before the next begins; the plugin must survive an arbitrarily long queue of unknown-destination requests.
2. Waiter queue length is unbounded, so one caller can accumulate an arbitrary backlog while the children are busy. Fix criteria: Queue depth should be bounded (per caller or globally) with an immediate error beyond the bound, so no single rune bearer or RPC connection can accumulate thousands of pending getroutes.

# Elements: peer prevtx output with non-L-BTC or blinded asset asserts in dualopend tx_add_input

## Details
On an Elements chain (liquid / liquid-regtest) with `--experimental-dual-fund`, the WIRE_TX_ADD_INPUT handler in openingd/dualopend.c parses the peer's `prevtx` (pull_bitcoin_tx_only, dualopend.c:1884, parsed with WALLY_TX_FLAG_USE_ELEMENTS via pull_wtx) and selects output `prevtx_vout` (both peer-chosen). After checking only that the index is in range (1890) and that the scriptPubKey is a segwit program (is_segwit_output, dualopend.c:1061-1076, script bytes only), the Elements branch at dualopend.c:1953-1966 calls bitcoin_tx_output_get_amount_sat(tx, outpoint.n) at line 1956. That helper (bitcoin/tx.c:329-335) does `assert(amount_asset_is_main(&asset_amt))`. amount_asset_is_main() (common/amount.c:719-728) compares the output's 33-byte asset field to chainparams->fee_asset_tag, so a prevtx output whose asset is any explicit asset other than L-BTC (prefix 0x01 followed by a different 32-byte asset id - parsed as a plain 33-byte explicit tag, so this does not depend on how libwally handles blinding) or a blinded asset commitment (prefix 0x0a/0x0b, the normal case for Liquid wallet outputs) makes the assert fail and dualopend abort(). Asserts are compiled into release builds (no NDEBUG).

This is a different defect from the verified finding dualopend-elements-tx-add-input-oob-psbt-input-index (psbt_elements_input_set_asset indexed by prevtx_vout at dualopend.c:1960): the assert fires earlier at line 1956 from the asset bytes rather than from the index, and using the correct PSBT input index does not address it. A peer that negotiates option_dual_fund reaches this with a single unsolicited open_channel2 followed by one tx_add_input (accepter_start enters run_tx_interactive as TX_ACCEPTER, dualopend.c:2849); the same handler is also reached as opener and during RBF. The crash kills only that per-peer dualopend instance (lightningd logs the subdaemon failure and the open attempt fails), so the impact is a repeatable denial of dual-funded channel opening on Elements nodes rather than a node-wide outage. The equivalent bitcoin-chain path skips the is_elements() branch and is unaffected. The finding holds only on a node configured for an Elements chain with --experimental-dual-fund enabled; nothing in lightningd/options.c (1855 strips only anchors on Elements) or the documentation disables dual-funding on Elements.

Assumption about libwally (external/ submodule absent): wally_tx_from_bytes with WALLY_TX_FLAG_USE_ELEMENTS stores each output's asset as its raw 33-byte confidential-asset encoding, as wally_tx_output_get_amount() (bitcoin/tx.c:821-846) expects; explicit asset tags are 33 bytes in the Elements serialisation regardless of blinded-output handling.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/dualopend.c:1953–1966](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1953-L1966)
   In the WIRE_TX_ADD_INPUT handler, when is_elements(chainparams), dualopend calls bitcoin_tx_output_get_amount_sat(tx, outpoint.n) (line 1956) on the output of the peer-supplied prevtx selected by the peer's prevtx_vout, without first checking that output's asset tag. This is the code the fix must change: reject a non-fee-asset output with open_abort before reading its amount.
2. [bitcoin/tx.c:329–335](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/tx.c#L329-L335)
   bitcoin_tx_output_get_amount_sat() does assert(amount_asset_is_main(&asset_amt)) (line 333) on the raw asset bytes of the output; on Elements any asset other than the explicit fee asset (an explicit non-L-BTC asset id, or a blinded 0x0a/0x0b commitment) fails this and aborts the calling process.
3. [openingd/dualopend.c:1882–1911](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1882-L1911)
   The prevtx is parsed from the peer's bytes with pull_bitcoin_tx_only (1884, which sets WALLY_TX_FLAG_USE_ELEMENTS on Elements); the only validation of the chosen output before the amount read is outpoint.n < num_outputs (1890) and is_segwit_output() (1906), which inspects the scriptPubKey only (dualopend.c:1061-1076) and never the asset or value fields.
4. [bitcoin/tx.c:821–846](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/tx.c#L821-L846)
   wally_tx_output_get_amount() copies the output's 33 asset bytes verbatim into amount.asset and only reads an explicit value when asset[0] == 0x01; the asset tag itself is returned unvalidated to the asserting caller.
5. [common/amount.c:719–728](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/amount.c#L719-L728)
   amount_asset_is_main() is a byte comparison of the 33-byte asset field against chainparams->fee_asset_tag, so an explicit asset with a different id, or a blinded (0x0a/0x0b) commitment, is 'not main'.
6. [openingd/dualopend.c:2849](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2849)
   accepter_start() enters run_tx_interactive as TX_ACCEPTER after sending accept_channel2, so an unsolicited open_channel2 from any dual-fund-capable peer followed by one tx_add_input reaches the handler with no operator interaction.

## Impact
Deterministic abort of the per-peer dualopend subdaemon; lightningd survives and the in-progress open fails. Repeatable at will, so channel-opening with dual-fund can be denied, but no funds are committed at that point and no other process is affected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote peer negotiating option_dual_fund with a node on liquid/liquid-regtest running --experimental-dual-fund sends open_channel2 then tx_add_input whose prevtx has a segwit output with a blinded or non-L-BTC asset at prevtx_vout. No further state is required; the assert fires on the first such message. Deployment preconditions (Elements chain + experimental dual-fund) are outside the attacker's control, hence AT:PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
The Elements branch of the tx_add_input handler reads the peer-chosen prevtx output's amount with a helper that asserts the asset is the fee asset, without first validating the asset of that output. Fix criteria: A peer-supplied prevtx output whose asset is not an explicit fee-asset (blinded or other asset) must be rejected with a negotiation failure (open_abort) rather than reaching an assert; library accessors used on peer-supplied outputs must return failure instead of aborting. Verify by sending tx_add_input with a blinded prevtx output on liquid-regtest and observing a clean abort of the negotiation with dualopend still alive.

# watch_found dispatches tx-less notifications to wallet handlers that dereference tx

## Details
lightningd's `watch_found` RPC (lightningd/watchman.c:587-634) is the channel through which the cln-bwatch plugin reports chain events. The handler treats `tx` as optional because WATCH_SCID 'not found' notifications legitimately omit it and blockdepth notifications carry only `depth`. However the dispatcher does not tie the tx-less shapes to handlers that tolerate them: `depth_handlers` is empty in this release (watchman.c:471-478), so a `depth` notification falls into `watch_handlers`, and both registered handlers — `wallet_utxo_spent_watch_found` (owner prefix `wallet/utxo/`) and `wallet_watch_spk` (`wallet/spk/`) — dereference `tx` unconditionally (`bitcoin_txid(tx, ...)` at wallet.c:8563 -> `wally_txid(tx->wtx, ...)`; `tx->wtx->num_outputs` at wallet.c:8281). lightningd segfaults.

Reachable only when the node runs with `--experimental-bwatch` (off by default; without it `ld->watchman` is NULL and `watch_found` returns 'Watchman not initialized', and bwatch never polls blocks). With it enabled there are two routes for an RPC caller whose rune permits the relevant method (commando over the Lightning transport, or clnrest); none of these methods carries a dev_only flag or any check of the caller's origin:

1. Direct: a caller permitted `watch_found` sends `{"blockheight":1,"owners":["wallet/utxo/<64 hex>:0"]}` — no tx, no txindex, no depth — which passes both consistency checks (watchman.c:608-614) and crashes lightningd on the first owner.

2. Indirect, via bwatch's add-watch RPCs: a caller permitted `addblockdepthwatch` registers owner `wallet/utxo/<valid txid>:0` (or `wallet/spk/0/p2wpkh`) with `start_block` <= current height. On the next processed block bwatch_check_blockdepth_watches (bwatch_scanner.c:249-266, called from bwatch.c:230) calls bwatch_send_blockdepth_found (bwatch_interface.c:65-88), which emits watch_found with `depth` and no `tx`; lightningd dispatches to the wallet handler with tx == NULL. Likewise `addscidwatch` with an scid whose block is <= tip and whose txindex exceeds that block's tx count makes maybe_fire_scid_watch (bwatch_scanner.c:163-201) send a tx-less watch_found immediately during the add-time rescan. Because bwatch persists watches in the datastore and reloads them at init (bwatch_store.c:485-490), a blockdepth watch re-crashes lightningd on every new block after every restart until the operator deletes the datastore entry — a persistent DoS of the node (no channel monitoring while lightningd is down).

The wallet handlers' suffix parsers validate syntax only (the comment at wallet.c:8366-8370 says the strings 'round-trip through bwatch ... so don't trust them blindly'), but the dispatcher never verifies that a tx-based handler actually received a tx. The design intent (comment at watchman.c:582-586) is that only the gossip scid handler sees tx == NULL; nothing enforces it.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/watchman.c:587–633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/watchman.c#L587-L633)
   json_watch_found makes tx optional (p_opt at 602). Its only consistency checks (608-614) are '!depth && !tx && txindex' and '!depth && tx && !txindex'; a request with depth set (blockdepth shape) or with neither tx nor txindex (the WATCH_SCID 'not found' shape) passes with tx == NULL and is dispatched to every owner in the array (624-629). The command has no dev_only flag or caller-origin check (636-640).
2. [lightningd/watchman.c:497–523](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/watchman.c#L497-L523)
   dispatch_watch_found: depth_handlers is empty ({NULL}, 471-478), so a depth notification falls through to watch_handlers (480-489); any owner starting with 'wallet/utxo/' or 'wallet/spk/' reaches the wallet handler with tx == NULL. Nothing ties the tx-less shapes to handlers that tolerate them.
3. [wallet/wallet.c:8546–8563](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L8546-L8563)
   wallet_utxo_spent_watch_found parses the suffix (syntax only), then calls bitcoin_txid(tx, ...) at 8563, which is wally_txid(tx->wtx, ...) (bitcoin/tx.c:506-509): NULL dereference in lightningd's main process.
4. [wallet/wallet.c:8274–8281](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L8274-L8281)
   wallet_watch_get_output reads tx->wtx->num_outputs (8281) before anything else; wallet_watch_spk calls it at 8415 right after the suffix parse, so 'wallet/spk/<n>/<form>' owners hit the same NULL dereference.
5. [plugins/bwatch/bwatch\_interface.c:65–88](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bwatch/bwatch_interface.c#L65-L88)
   bwatch_send_blockdepth_found sends watch_found with blockheight + depth + owners and no tx, for every owner string of a blockdepth watch. bwatch_send_watch_found (28-63) omits both tx and txindex when tx == NULL (40-45), producing the second tx-less shape.
6. [plugins/bwatch/bwatch\_scanner.c:249–265](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bwatch/bwatch_scanner.c#L249-L265)
   bwatch_check_blockdepth_watches, called on every newly processed block (bwatch.c:230), fires bwatch_send_blockdepth_found for every blockdepth watch with start_block <= new height, so a wallet/-owned blockdepth watch re-triggers the crash on each block.
7. [plugins/bwatch/bwatch\_interface.c:489–509](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bwatch/bwatch_interface.c#L489-L509)
   addblockdepthwatch (json_bwatch_add_blockdepth) accepts an arbitrary 'owner' string from any RPC caller and stores it verbatim via bwatch_add_watch; addscidwatch (441-463) does the same. The plugin command table (bwatch.c:475-485) registers them as ordinary RPC methods.
8. [plugins/bwatch/bwatch\_scanner.c:163–201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bwatch/bwatch_scanner.c#L163-L201)
   maybe_fire_scid_watch: when the scid's txindex (188) or outnum (196) is out of range for the block, it calls bwatch_send_watch_found(cmd, NULL, ...) — a tx-less watch_found — and this runs during the add-time rescan of the scid's block (add_watch_and_maybe_rescan 330-341 -> rescan_block_done -> bwatch_process_block_txs -> bwatch_check_scid_watches), so the registrant chooses the shape and timing.
9. [plugins/bwatch/bwatch\_store.c:485–490](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bwatch/bwatch_store.c#L485-L490)
   bwatch_load_watches_from_datastore reloads every watch type, including WATCH_BLOCKDEPTH and WATCH_SCID, at plugin init (bwatch.c:466); bwatch_add_watch persisted them (bwatch_store.c:524). The crash therefore recurs after each lightningd restart until the operator deletes the datastore entry.

## Impact
lightningd (the main daemon) segfaults on a NULL dereference in the wallet handler; all channels lose monitoring until restart, and the datastore-persisted blockdepth watch makes it re-crash on each new block after each restart until the operator removes the entry. No confidentiality or integrity effect beyond the crash.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a rune bearer (commando over the Lightning transport, or clnrest/HTTP) whose rune permits `watch_found`, or more plausibly one of bwatch's `addblockdepthwatch`/`addscidwatch` methods; the rune's method restriction is the project's documented bound on such a bearer (createrune.json) and does not concede a node crash. A local RPC-socket user or the operator is trusted and out of scope. Attack requirements: the node must run with the non-default `--experimental-bwatch` flag and the bearer's rune must allow one of these methods. One request suffices; via add*watch the crash fires on the next block (or immediately for the scid shape) and persists across restarts because the watch is stored in the datastore.

## Recommended fix
1. json_watch_found/dispatch_watch_found pass tx == NULL to handlers in watch_handlers, which are tx-based and dereference tx; the depth and scid-not-found shapes are not bound to handlers that accept them. Fix criteria: A watch_found whose tx is absent must never reach a tx-based handler: depth notifications dispatch only to depth_handlers (and are rejected when none matches), and tx-less tx-based notifications are accepted only for owner prefixes whose handler is documented to tolerate NULL. Verify that `watch_found` with owners ['wallet/utxo/<txid>:0'] and no tx, and a blockdepth/scid watch registered with a wallet/ owner, yield an RPC error or a logged skip rather than a crash.
2. The internal watchman RPCs (watch_found, watch_revert, block_processed, revert_block_processed, chaininfo) are ordinary json_commands callable by any RPC principal, and bwatch's add*/del*watch accept arbitrary owner strings, so lightningd-internal owner prefixes can be forged by rune bearers. Fix criteria: Notifications claiming lightningd-owned prefixes (wallet/, channel/, ...) are only acted upon when they originate from the bwatch plugin (e.g. the request arrives on the plugin's own connection or carries a per-session token), or the add-watch RPCs refuse owners with reserved prefixes from non-plugin callers. Verify a rune-authenticated caller cannot create a watch whose owner begins with wallet/.

# Wallet trusts bwatch watch owner strings as UTXO ownership authority

## Details
Under `--experimental-bwatch` (off by default; doc/lightningd-config.5.md:589), lightningd stands up the watchman and the wallet's authoritative UTXO table `our_outputs` (the only table coin selection reads: wallet_get_unspent_utxos, wallet.c:526-541) is maintained from bwatch `watch_found`/`watch_revert` RPC notifications. The notification's `owners` strings double as the authority for what to do: `wallet/spk/<keyindex>/<form>` means 'this output belongs to HD key keyindex', `wallet/utxo/<txid>:<n>` means 'this tx spends our outpoint'. lightningd generates these strings itself (owner_wallet_spk/owner_wallet_utxo) but the handlers accept whatever comes back and validate only syntax (spk_watch_suffix_to_keyindex, utxo_watch_suffix_to_outpoint) — the comment at wallet.c:8366-8370 says the strings must not be trusted blindly, yet no handler cross-checks the claim against the transaction: `wallet_watch_spk` never verifies the matched script is derived from `keyindex` (only that it is p2wpkh/p2tr/p2sh-p2wpkh shaped), and `wallet_utxo_spent_watch_found` never verifies that `tx` spends the named outpoint (`innum` is UNUSED).

Nothing binds the strings to lightningd. `json_watch_found`/`json_watch_revert` are ordinary json_commands whose only gate is `cmd->ld->watchman != NULL` (watchman.c:616). bwatch's `addscriptpubkeywatch`/`addoutpointwatch`/`del*watch`/`listwatch` are ordinary plugin RPCs that accept any `owner` with no prefix check (bwatch_add_watch, bwatch_store.c:503-560), persist it in the datastore, rescan from `start_block` when it is at or below the tip (bwatch_interface.c:330-340, bwatch.c:404-434) and report every match with all owners (bwatch_interface.c:134-137). None of these methods is dev_only, none has a doc/schemas entry, and the rune evaluator (checkrune) bounds only method names and params: commando forwards any method a peer names (commando.c:414-425) and clnrest likewise.

So a rune bearer whose rune permits any of these undocumented plumbing methods authors wallet-ownership claims: `addscriptpubkeywatch owner=wallet/spk/7/p2wpkh scriptpubkey=<any p2wpkh script> start_block=<old height>` makes bwatch rescan and lightningd record every output ever paid to that foreign script as a wallet UTXO at keyindex 7 (status AVAILABLE, deposit coin movement, spend watch armed); `addoutpointwatch owner=wallet/utxo/<our real utxo> outpoint=<any outpoint about to be spent>` marks a real wallet UTXO spent and emits a withdrawal movement when the unrelated outpoint is spent; `delscriptpubkeywatch`/`deloutpointwatch` with owners read from `listwatch` silently remove the wallet's own watches so future deposits and spends are never recorded; a forged `wallet/utxo/` owner on a reorged block clears spendheight of an already-spent UTXO. A bearer permitted `watch_found`/`watch_revert` directly achieves the same with an arbitrary hex tx and no block at all.

Consequences: fake UTXOs enter coin selection (withdraw/fundchannel/splice/CPFP build transactions with inputs hsmd cannot validly sign, so wallet spends fail or produce invalid txs); real UTXOs are hidden as spent or resurrected as unspent; bookkeeper receives fabricated deposit/withdrawal movements; `listfunds` misreports balances. All persist in the DB. The project's own rune design treats method side effects that escalate beyond the grant as something to block (runes.c:1046-1053 refuses restricted runes `createrune`/`showrunes` effects); here a monitoring-shaped method carries wallet-write authority through an unverified label. Holds only when `--experimental-bwatch` is enabled.

## Evidence
1. [wallet/wallet.c:8396–8437](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L8396-L8437)
   wallet_watch_spk takes keyindex from the owner suffix and the script from the matched tx output, checks only that the script is some p2wpkh/p2tr/p2sh-p2wpkh form (addrtype_from_script), and records the output as wallet-owned under that keyindex (wallet_transaction_add, bwatch_got_utxo -> wallet_add_our_output, deposit coin movement, wallet/utxo outpoint watch). It never verifies the script is derived from HD key `keyindex`, despite the comment at 8366-8370 saying the round-tripped strings must not be trusted blindly.
2. [wallet/wallet.c:8546–8584](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L8546-L8584)
   wallet_utxo_spent_watch_found marks the outpoint named in the owner suffix as spent at `blockheight` (our_outputs and legacy outputs) and records a withdrawal movement for it, without checking that `tx` actually spends that outpoint (innum is explicitly UNUSED). wallet_utxo_spent_watch_revert (8589-8611) likewise clears spendheight for any suffix outpoint.
3. [lightningd/watchman.c:481–524](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/watchman.c#L481-L524)
   dispatch_watch_found selects the wallet handler purely by string prefix (wallet/utxo/, wallet/spk/) of an owner string supplied in the RPC; owners are opaque strings bwatch stores and echoes back, with no binding to lightningd as their author.
4. [lightningd/watchman.c:587–633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/watchman.c#L587-L633)
   json_watch_found is an ordinary json_command (not dev_only); its only gate is `cmd->ld->watchman` being non-NULL (616). A caller permitted watch_found injects an arbitrary hex tx plus owner strings directly; json_watch_revert (643-666) is the same for reverts.
5. [plugins/bwatch/bwatch\_interface.c:427–449](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bwatch/bwatch_interface.c#L427-L449)
   addoutpointwatch (and addscriptpubkeywatch, 343-368) accept any `owner` and any outpoint/scriptpubkey from the RPC caller; bwatch_add_watch (bwatch_store.c:503-560) appends the owner with no prefix check, persists it, and add_watch_and_maybe_rescan (330-340) replays historical blocks from start_block. Every later match reports all owners (bwatch_send_watch_found, 134-137).
6. [plugins/bwatch/bwatch\_interface.c:454–470](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bwatch/bwatch_interface.c#L454-L470)
   deloutpointwatch/delscriptpubkeywatch (372-389) remove an owner from a watch given only the owner string, which listwatch (632-698, json_out_watch_common emits owners) discloses, so the wallet's own wallet/spk and wallet/utxo watches can be removed by any caller permitted these methods.
7. [wallet/wallet.c:526–540](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L526-L540)
   wallet_get_unspent_utxos reads coin-selection candidates from our_outputs WHERE spendheight IS NULL (and wallet.c:283 states the wallet reads only our_outputs), so rows written or marked by the forged notifications directly drive withdraw/fundchannel/splice input selection and listfunds.

## Impact
Integrity: the wallet's authoritative UTXO table (our_outputs, read by coin selection), our_txs and the coin-movement ledger are populated with attacker-chosen ownership/spent state that persists in the DB and is mirrored into the legacy outputs table. Availability: coin selection picks inputs hsmd cannot validly sign, or real UTXOs are hidden as spent, so wallet spends (withdraw, fundchannel, splice, anchor/CPFP fee bumps) fail until the operator repairs the DB; no on-chain funds move. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker is a rune bearer reaching the node over commando (Lightning transport from any peer, every request goes to checkrune) or clnrest, holding a rune whose method restriction permits addscriptpubkeywatch/addoutpointwatch/del*watch or watch_found/watch_revert — none is dev_only and checkrune bounds only method names and params. One RPC with a crafted owner string suffices; bwatch persists it and reports matches on the immediate historical rescan or the next block. Attack requirements: the node must run with --experimental-bwatch (non-default) and the rune must permit these undocumented plumbing methods (e.g. a negative-restriction rune). No user interaction; deterministic.

## Recommended fix
1. wallet_watch_spk and wallet_utxo_spent_watch_found act on the keyindex/outpoint encoded in the owner string without verifying it against the transaction they were given, so an owner string is an unauthenticated capability. Fix criteria: Before recording an output as owned, the wallet must confirm the matched script equals the script it derives for that keyindex and form (e.g. via the our_addresses table), and before marking an outpoint spent it must confirm some input of tx references that outpoint. Verify that a watch_found with a wallet/spk owner for a foreign script, or a wallet/utxo owner for an outpoint tx does not spend, is logged and ignored.
2. bwatch's add*/del*watch RPCs let any RPC principal register or remove watches under lightningd-reserved owner prefixes, and watch_found/watch_revert accept notifications from any principal. Fix criteria: Owners with lightningd-reserved prefixes (wallet/, channel/, gossip/, ...) can only be created, removed or reported by lightningd/bwatch themselves (plugin-connection check or shared token), or the notification path authenticates the source. Verify a rune-authenticated caller cannot add or delete a wallet/ owner nor invoke watch_found successfully.

# Temporary channel failure on a zero-amount hop aborts pay plugin

## Details
handle_intermediate_failure (plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1442-1459) treats WIRE_TEMPORARY_CHANNEL_FAILURE as a capacity signal: estimated = errchan->amount, and if amount_msat_deduct(&estimated, 1 msat) fails it calls abort(). amount_msat_deduct is checked subtraction (common/amount.c:285-303), so it fails exactly when the blamed hop carries 0 msat. errchan is p->route[erring_index] (assign_blame, 1507-1536), the outgoing hop of the node that reported the error. Every hop's amount is our_amount plus the fees of all later hops, so the hop into the destination always carries exactly our_amount; a zero-amount payment therefore produces a 0 msat hop.

The legacy pay plugin accepts zero-amount payments: common/bolt11.c:843-871 decodes an explicit '0' hrp amount, and json_pay (plugins/pay.c:1036-1065) copies the invoice amount (or amount_msat for an amountless invoice, or partial_msat) into final_amount/our_amount with no non-zero check. CLN's own invoice command refuses such amounts (lightningd/invoice.c:1037-1053) and BOLT11 writers MUST encode a positive amount (bolt11.c:1298), so the invoice is attacker-crafted and non-conformant, but the reader is lenient. The hsmd preapproveinvoice stub approves (hsmd/libhsmd.c:953-968), route_can_carry (common/route.c:13-20) treats 0 msat as a probe and finds routes, exemptfee leaves a 5000 msat fee budget, and lightningd's sendonion/check_progress has no zero check (lightningd/pay.c:1057-1063 explicitly tolerates zero total_msat).

Attack: the payee publishes a zero-amount bolt11 invoice from a node id S absent from gossip with a one-hop routehint [P, scid], where P is a public node it runs (threat-model adversary 3). filter_routehints keeps the hint (P known and reachable); routehint_check_reachable finds S unreachable so the hint is used first; routehint_pre_getroute (2944-2960) routes to P for our_amount + hint fee; routehint_step_cb (3100-3139) appends the stitched hop (scid, amount = our_amount = 0). A non-zero fee_base_msat in the hint (e.g. 1000 msat) makes the first HTLC non-zero so the payer's channeld does not reject it as amount_below_minimum (channeld/channeld.c:6652-6657); the fee does not alter the stitched hop's amount. P receives the HTLC with an onion instructing it to forward 0 msat and answers temporary_channel_failure. lightningd's remote_routing_failure (lightningd/pay.c:463-529) reports erring_index = origin_index + 1 = 1 with no node/channel (sendonion route unknown); payment_result_infer fills them in; assign_blame yields errchan = &p->route[1] with amount 0; amount_msat_deduct(0, 1) fails and abort() fires. pay is an important builtin plugin (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2590), so lightningd exits. No routehint is strictly required: for any zero-amount payment the penultimate hop returning temporary_channel_failure reaches the same line; the routehint merely lets the payee be that hop.

Reachability of legacy pay: plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3570 sets take_over_pay = true (doc/lightningd-config.5.md:563 still documents false), but the rpc_command hook (xpay.c:3446-3514) hands `pay` to the legacy plugin when the params array has other than 1 or 2 elements, when calc_maxfee returns false (maxfee combined with maxfeepercent/exemptfee), or when xpay-handle-pay=false. `pay` is deprecated in v26.06 but allow-deprecated-apis defaults to true outside --developer. keysend shares the library and a zero-amount keysend failing at the penultimate hop would hit the same abort, but the payee cannot steer it via routehints. This resolves the first half of ledger lead l-e6-07: the estimate is zero only when our_amount is zero (or a zero-fee hint forwards a zero amount), so the abort is reachable but requires the victim to pay a zero-amount invoice.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1442–1458](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L1442-L1458)
   handle_intermediate_failure, case WIRE_TEMPORARY_CHANNEL_FAILURE: estimated = errchan->amount, then abort() if amount_msat_deduct(&estimated, 1 msat) fails. amount_msat_deduct is checked subtraction (common/amount.c:285-303), so it fails exactly when the blamed hop's amount is 0 msat. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1507–1535](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L1507-L1535)
   assign_blame: errchan = &p->route[erring_index] (the outgoing hop of the node that reported the error), errnode = route[index-1]. With route [victim->P, P->S] and P (erring_index 1) failing, errchan is the stitched routehint hop P->S.
3. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:3100–3138](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L3100-L3138)
   routehint_step_cb at PAYMENT_STEP_GOT_ROUTE appends the hint hops with hop.amount = route_msatoshi(p->our_amount, remaining hint hops). For the last hint hop there are no remaining hops, so its amount is exactly our_amount regardless of the hint's fees; with our_amount = 0 the hop carries 0 msat.
4. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2944–2959](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2944-L2959)
   routehint_pre_getroute sets getroute->amount = our_amount + the hint's fees and getroute->destination = the hint entry node P. A non-zero fee_base_msat in the payee's hint makes the first HTLC non-zero (so the payer's channeld does not reject it as amount_below_minimum, channeld/channeld.c:6652-6657) without changing the stitched hop's 0 msat amount.
5. [plugins/pay.c:1036–1064](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L1036-L1064)
   json_pay copies the invoice amount (or amount_msat for an amountless invoice, or partial_msat) into final_amount/our_amount with no non-zero check; the only amount checks are 'unnecessary'/'required' and partial <= total.
6. [common/bolt11.c:843–870](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L843-L870)
   bolt11 hrp amount parsing accepts an explicit '0' (strtoull returns 0 with no ERANGE, *end == 0, 0*m10 % 10 == 0) and sets *b11->msat = 0. CLN's own invoice command refuses zero (lightningd/invoice.c:1037-1053, param_positive_msat_or_any) and BOLT11 writers MUST encode a positive amount (bolt11.c:1298), so this is an attacker-crafted, non-conformant invoice the reader is lenient about.
7. [lightningd/pay.c:463–528](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L463-L528)
   remote_routing_failure: for a sendonion payment route_nodes is NULL, erring_node/erring_channel are left NULL and erring_index = origin_index + 1, so the routehint entry P (first hop) failing gives erring_index 1, which payment_result_infer and assign_blame map to p->route[1]. check_progress (1057-1063) explicitly tolerates a zero total_msat and send_payment_core has no zero check on msat.
8. [common/route.c:13–19](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/route.c#L13-L19)
   route_can_carry_even_disabled treats amount 0 as an 'ignore min' probe, so dijkstra/getroute find routes for a zero-amount payment instead of failing it.
9. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3446–3513](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L3446-L3513)
   xpay's rpc_command hook redirects `pay` to xpay by default (take_over_pay = true at xpay.c:3570; doc/lightningd-config.5.md:563 still documents false) but declines, leaving the legacy pay plugin to run, when the params array has other than 1 or 2 elements, when calc_maxfee returns false (maxfee combined with maxfeepercent/exemptfee), or when xpay-handle-pay=false. These are the routes to the vulnerable code.

## Impact
abort() in the important pay plugin makes lightningd exit (lightningd/plugin.c:297-302), taking every channel daemon offline until the operator restarts; repeated invoices repeat the crash. No confidentiality or integrity impact; funds and keys are not touched.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote payee (threat-model adversary 3) running a public node P. It crafts a non-conformant zero-amount bolt11 invoice from an unknown node id with a one-hop routehint through P carrying a small non-zero fee, and has P answer the resulting HTLC with temporary_channel_failure; the abort is deterministic and nothing in the path defends against it. The victim must deliberately pay a zero-amount invoice (or pass amount_msat=0 / partial_msat=0) through the legacy pay plugin, which default configurations reach with 3+ positional params or maxfee combined with maxfeepercent/exemptfee, and always with xpay-handle-pay=false. That is a strong precondition (AT:P) and a conscious action on the attacker's payload (UI:A); no privileges, network reachable, no race.

## Recommended fix
1. handle_intermediate_failure asserts via abort() that the amount of a hop on a payee-influenced route is at least 1 msat before storing it as a capacity estimate. Fix criteria: A zero hop amount yields an estimate of 0 msat (or skips the hint update) and the attempt fails cleanly with a retry or payment failure; no onion-error handling path in libplugin-pay aborts on route or amount values. Verify with a temporary_channel_failure reported for a 0 msat hop.
2. pay and libplugin-pay accept a zero our_amount (zero-amount invoice, amount_msat=0 on an amountless invoice, partial_msat=0), producing 0 msat hops that the protocol forbids. Fix criteria: json_pay rejects a zero final or partial amount with JSONRPC2_INVALID_PARAMS, matching the positive-amount rule CLN's invoice command already enforces, so no zero-amount route is ever built.

# Persisted layer records with direction >1 index out of bounds in localmods and biases

## Details
askrene persists layer records in the lightningd datastore under key ["askrene","layers",<name>] and re-parses them only at startup in populate_layer (plugins/askrene/layer.c:900-936, called from load_layers at init). The hand-written decoder fromwire_short_channel_id_dir (plugins/askrene/datastore_wire.c:20-25) copies `dir` from a raw u8 without constraining it to 0/1, whereas every RPC entry point enforces 0/1 via json_to_short_channel_id_dir -> json_to_zero_or_one (common/json_parse.c:591). Downstream code uses dir as an array index:

- layer_add_localmods (layer.c:1365-1375) passes each stored local_update scidd to gossmap_local_updatechan, which computes `lc = &mod->changes[scidd->dir]` on the two-element `changes[2]` of `struct localmod` (common/gossmap.c:986-1005, 1172). For dir >= 2 this points into orig[]/orig_cupdate_off[] (uninitialised for a freshly added mod), the next mod, or past the tal array for large dir; it then tal_free()s whatever pointer-sized value is there and writes a fresh tal pointer back (gossmap.c:1173-1197) — an out-of-bounds read, invalid free and out-of-bounds pointer write in the parent askrene process, on every getroutes that includes the layer.
- layer_apply_biases (layer.c:1128) does `biases[(idx<<1) | dir] += bias` on the per-request s8 array of exactly 2*gossmap_max_chan_idx elements (askrene.c:624); with dir up to 255 and a high channel index this writes up to 255 bytes past the end.
- Constraints/impressions/reservations only compare dir and are not affected.

Who can author such a record: askrene itself only writes validated data, so the triggering record must come from another `datastore` RPC caller. The operator and installed plugins are trusted by design; the in-scope author is a rune bearer whose rune admits the generic `datastore` method (via commando over a peer connection or clnrest). The project concedes such a bearer key/value storage ("allows plugins to store data ... for later retrieval", doc/schemas/datastore.json) and already treats the datastore as sensitive (readonly runes exclude listdatastore, lightningd/runes.c:462-469); it does not concede memory corruption of an important plugin. The bearer issues `datastore key=["askrene","layers","xpay"] mode=create-or-append hex=<DSTORE_CHANNEL_UPDATE record with dir=0xff>` (per-change saves by askrene use append_layer_datastore, so the record survives until a wholesale rewrite); at the next lightningd restart populate_layer loads it into the persistent `xpay` layer (created by plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3272-3278), and the next xpay payment — which always lists `xpay` in its getroutes layers (xpay.c:1949) — performs the corrupting write in cln-askrene. cln-askrene is an important plugin, so its crash stops lightningd. This finding holds only for a caller granted `datastore` write by rune; the operator-only variant is out of the threat model.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/askrene/datastore\_wire.c:20–25](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/datastore_wire.c#L20-L25)
   fromwire_short_channel_id_dir reads dir as a raw u8 with no 0/1 check; every fromwire_dstore_* record decoder (channel_update, channel_bias, channel_bias_v2, constraint, impression) uses it, so a persisted record can carry dir in 2..255.
2. [common/gossmap.c:1160–1198](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/gossmap.c#L1160-L1198)
   gossmap_local_updatechan does lc = &mod->changes[scidd->dir] where changes has two elements (struct localmod, lines 986-1005); dir 2..255 indexes past the struct, then tal_free()s the garbage pointer found there and writes a new tal pointer back.
3. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:1365–1375](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L1365-L1375)
   layer_add_localmods forwards each persisted local_update scidd (with the unchecked dir) to gossmap_local_updatechan on every getroutes that includes the layer.
4. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:1120–1130](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L1120-L1130)
   layer_apply_biases writes biases[(gossmap_chan_idx<<1) | bias->scidd.dir] += bias; with a persisted dir >1 this is an out-of-bounds read-modify-write of the per-request s8 array sized gossmap_max_chan_idx*2 (askrene.c:624).
5. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:900–936](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L900-L936)
   populate_layer loads every record from the datastore blob at init without validating scidd.dir; load_channel_update -> add_update_channel and load_channel_bias_v2 -> set_bias store the scidd verbatim.
6. [common/json\_parse.c:580–595](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse.c#L580-L595)
   The RPC path (json_to_short_channel_id_dir -> json_to_zero_or_one) enforces dir in {0,1}; only the datastore reload path lacks this check, so the invariant the consumers rely on is not re-established on reload.

## Impact
Out-of-bounds pointer read, invalid tal_free and out-of-bounds pointer write inside struct localmod (and up to 255 bytes past the biases array) in the askrene parent process. Realistic outcome is a crash of the important cln-askrene plugin — which stops lightningd — on every routing attempt until the record is removed, i.e. a persistent node DoS with on-chain exposure; limited integrity impact from corrupting adjacent localmod state. No confidentiality impact identified.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker must hold a rune that admits the generic `datastore` method, reachable remotely via commando (over a peer connection) or clnrest; such a rune is an operator-delegated privilege over all plugins' persistent state (the project itself flags the datastore as sensitive), hence PR:H rather than an ordinary app rune. They append a crafted DSTORE_CHANNEL_UPDATE or DSTORE_CHANNEL_BIAS_V2 record with dir>1 under the [askrene,layers,xpay] key; the record is only parsed at startup, so a lightningd restart must occur before askrene rewrites the layer wholesale (AT:P). The next xpay payment then performs the out-of-bounds write. Crafting the record is trivial (fixed wire layout).

## Recommended fix
1. fromwire_short_channel_id_dir accepts any u8 for dir although consumers use it as a 0/1 array index. Fix criteria: Records whose dir is not 0 or 1 must be rejected at decode time (fromwire_fail) so they never enter a layer; a persisted record with dir=0xff must not reach gossmap_local_updatechan or layer_apply_biases.
2. populate_layer trusts datastore content wholesale and continues loading after a malformed record only by accident of fromwire_fail. Fix criteria: Loading a layer must validate every field with the same constraints as the RPC parameters (dir, bias range) and log/skip invalid records without crashing or corrupting memory.

# setconfig multi-option: transient value bypasses pre-check, stale configvar triggers fatal()

## Details
`setconfig` on an OPT_MULTI dynamic plugin option (configs.c:674-739) performs a non-fatal consistency check of the config lines it will rewrite (grab_and_check → command_fail) only for non-transient calls and only over configvars returned by configvar_first/configvar_next, which skip `overridden` entries. After the asynchronous plugin round-trip, setconfig_success() → configvar_save_multi() (configs.c:536-560) rewrites every file-backed configvar for that option regardless of `overridden`, and configfile_replace_var() calls fatal() if the line on disk no longer equals cv->configline (configs.c:433-437).

Two states make a file-backed configvar permanently mismatch its line:
1. configvar_save_multi() comments the line out but only removes CONFIGVAR_NETWORK_CONF configvars (configs.c:553). An option set in `~/.lightning/config` (BASE_CONF, the primary documented config location) or in a `--conf` file (EXPLICIT_CONF) leaves a stale configvar whose configline is the original text while the file now reads `# setconfig commented out ...`.
2. configvar_parse() trims trailing whitespace in place (configvar.c:94-95); optarg aliases configline, so `opt=val  ` is stored as `opt=val` and never matches the file.

A second non-transient setconfig catches these via the pre-check and fails cleanly. But a rune bearer can bypass the pre-check: `setconfig opt [x]` (non-transient; comments out the base-config line, leaving the stale configvar) → `setconfig opt [t] transient=true` (no pre-check; configvar_finalize_overrides marks the stale configvar overridden) → `setconfig opt [z]` (pre-check now sees only the transient entry, file==NULL, nothing checked) → plugin accepts → configvar_save_multi iterates the stale configvar → grab_and_check mismatch → fatal(). In the trailing-whitespace case only the transient→permanent pair is needed. The same fatal is reachable without transient by two concurrent setconfig requests on the option (both pass the pre-check before either plugin reply).

Preconditions: a plugin registering an option with both `multi` and `dynamic` (supported by pyln-client `add_option(multi=True, dynamic=True)` and cln-plugin; none of the shipped plugins currently does — xpay-user-layer is multi but not dynamic), that option present in the base/explicit config (or with trailing whitespace), and a rune admitting `setconfig` on it. Result: lightningd fatal() — full node outage — from a caller only authorised to adjust one plugin option. tests/test_misc.py::test_setconfig_dynamic_multi_option (issue #8295) exercises the transient/permanent sequence only with the option absent from config files, which is why the stale-configvar path is untested.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/configs.c:536–560](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L536-L560)
   configvar_save_multi() comments out EVERY file-backed configvar for the option (ignoring `overridden`) via configfile_replace_var(), then removes only CONFIGVAR_NETWORK_CONF entries — BASE_CONF/EXPLICIT_CONF configvars survive with a configline that no longer matches the (now commented-out) file line.
2. [lightningd/configs.c:412–437](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L412-L437)
   configfile_replace_var() calls fatal() when grab_and_check() reports the on-disk line differs from cv->configline.
3. [lightningd/configs.c:383–409](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L383-L409)
   grab_and_check() compares the stored configline byte-for-byte with the current file line.
4. [lightningd/configs.c:704–738](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L704-L738)
   The non-fatal pre-check runs only when !transient and iterates configvar_first/next, which skip `overridden` configvars — so stale/overridden entries that configvar_save_multi will later touch are never checked.
5. [common/configvar.c:101–131](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/configvar.c#L101-L131)
   configvar_finalize_overrides(): a transient value for a multi option marks all earlier non-transient configvars (including file-backed stale ones) overridden, hiding them from the pre-check.
6. [common/configvar.c:134–167](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/configvar.c#L134-L167)
   configvar_remove() for the transient source un-overrides only the last matching configvar; the loop in configvar_save_multi does not consult `overridden` anyway.
7. [common/configvar.c:222–253](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/configvar.c#L222-L253)
   configvar_iter() returns only non-overridden entries — the basis of the pre-check's blind spot.
8. [common/configvar.c:91–96](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/configvar.c#L91-L96)
   trim_whitespace(cv->optarg) writes NUL into cv->configline (optarg aliases the line via opt_find_long), so any config line with trailing whitespace permanently mismatches grab_and_check — a second, operator-independent-of-setconfig source of the fatal mismatch.
9. [lightningd/configs.c:576–591](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/configs.c#L576-L591)
   setconfig_success() multi path: removes transient values then calls configvar_save_multi() after the plugin round-trip, with no re-check.

## Impact
fatal() aborts lightningd: all channels, HTLCs and RPC go offline until the operator restarts. No data disclosure; integrity limited to config lines the rune already permitted.

## Reproduction steps
1. Rune bearer (commando over a Lightning peer connection, or clnrest HTTP) allowed to setconfig a multi+dynamic plugin option that the operator placed in ~/.lightning/config (BASE_CONF) or a --conf file (EXPLICIT_CONF). Verified in code: plugin.c:1083-1092 registers OPT_MULTI|OPT_DYNAMIC from the manifest (pyln-client add_option(multi=True, dynamic=True); cln-plugin options.rs:652-674); configdir.c:85 stores the raw file line and lightningd.c:1271/1285 runs plugins_init before handle_opts->parse_configvars_final so the base-config line is bound to the plugin option; configvar_save_multi (configs.c:545-553) comments out every file-backed configvar but removes only CONFIGVAR_NETWORK_CONF, leaving a BASE_CONF/EXPLICIT_CONF configvar whose configline no longer matches disk; the pre-check (configs.c:704-739) runs only when !transient and only over non-overridden configvars, while configvar_updated->configvar_finalize_overrides (configvar.c:117-124) marks them overridden after a transient set. Three ordinary RPC calls (permanent, transient, permanent) deterministically reach fatal() at configs.c:436; with a trailing-whitespace config line (trim_whitespace at configvar.c:94-95 mutates configline through the optarg alias set by ccan opt_find_long_extra) only transient then permanent is needed. Requires a third-party plugin exposing such an option and that config placement, hence attack_requirements PRESENT; no dependency behaviour is assumed beyond vendored ccan/opt.

## Recommended fix
1. configfile_replace_var() escalates a mismatch between the in-memory configline and the file to fatal(), and configvar_save_multi() reaches it for configvars the pre-check never examined (overridden/stale ones, after the async plugin round-trip). Fix criteria: A config-file mismatch discovered while persisting a setconfig must fail the RPC command, never terminate lightningd; the set of configvars rewritten must be exactly the set checked immediately beforehand (re-check after the plugin reply). Verify the permanent→transient→permanent sequence on a base-config multi option returns an error or succeeds without aborting.
2. configvar_save_multi() comments out BASE_CONF/EXPLICIT_CONF lines but leaves their configvars in ld->configvars with a now-false configline; trim_whitespace() mutates configline so it never matches the file. Fix criteria: After commenting out a line, the corresponding configvar is removed or updated to the new file contents for every source type; the stored configline is the exact on-disk line (trimming must not alias it). Verify listconfigs sources and a second setconfig behave correctly for options from ~/.lightning/config and for lines with trailing whitespace.

# disableinvoicerequest during pending payment: payee's fulfil makes lightningd fatal() in crash loop

## Details
lightningd publishes BOLT12 invoice_requests (RPC `invoicerequest`) for a remote party to send us an invoice, which the offers plugin automatically pays (plugins/offers_inv_hook.c:190-202 -> xpay -> injectpaymentonion with `localinvreqid`). The resulting `payments` row stores `local_invreq_id` (pay.c:1836-1856). When the outgoing HTLC is fulfilled, fulfill_our_htlc_out() -> payment_succeeded() (pay.c:362-379) calls wallet_invoice_request_mark_used() (wallet/wallet.c:6431-6461), which does `fatal()` if the stored status is not active.

The only guard that the invoice_request is active runs at send time (check_invoice_request_usage, pay.c:798-849). Between send and fulfil, the operator may run `disableinvoicerequest` (offer.c:554-594 -> wallet_invoice_request_disable, wallet.c:6413-6423), which clears OFFER_STATUS_ACTIVE_F without checking for pending payments. The payee (a remote, unauthenticated Lightning counterparty) controls when the HTLC is fulfilled and can hold it for the full CLTV window (hours to days), making a stuck payment the natural reason an operator would disable the request. When the payee then releases the preimage, lightningd hits `fatal("%s: invreq_id %s not active")`.

Because payment_succeeded() runs inside the DB transaction wrapping the channeld message (subd.c), the abort discards wallet_htlc_update/wallet_payment_set_status. On restart the HTLC is still unresolved, the direct peer re-sends the fulfil/commitment_signed on reestablish (protocol-mandated), and lightningd fatal()s again: a crash loop that persists until the operator edits the database by hand (there is no `enableinvoicerequest` RPC, and `disableinvoicerequest` refuses already-disabled requests). Even a single occurrence is a DoS with on-chain consequences (pending HTLCs across all channels, missed timeouts).

Root cause: a status transition that the data layer treats as an invariant violation worth aborting the process over is reachable through an ordinary operator action plus a remote party's timing. The same pattern exists in wallet_offer_mark_used() (wallet.c:6264-6297), but there offer_status_update() expires UNPAID invoices on disable and invoices_resolve() rechecks UNPAID, so that sibling is guarded; the invoice_request side has no equivalent.

## Evidence
1. [wallet/wallet.c:6431–6464](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L6431-L6464)
   wallet_invoice_request_mark_used() fatal()s (6451-6455) when the stored invoice_request status lacks OFFER_STATUS_ACTIVE_F. It is the only status check between the payee's fulfil and process death; nothing re-validates that the request is still active before calling it. This is where the fix belongs (treat inactive as log-and-skip, not corruption).
2. [lightningd/pay.c:359–379](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L359-L379)
   payment_succeeded() unconditionally calls wallet_invoice_request_mark_used() whenever the payment row carries local_invreq_id (374-376); local_invreq_id is persisted on the payments row (wallet.c:4081-4082) and reloaded (wallet.c:4243), so the call recurs after restart.
3. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1661–1723](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1661-L1723)
   peer_got_commitsig -> peer_fulfilled_our_htlc -> fulfill_our_htlc_out: the peer's update_fulfill_htlc (channeld_got_commitsig) drives payment_succeeded for an HTLC we originated (am_origin, 1687-1688). The same function is reached from onchain_fulfilled_htlc (1783) when the preimage is discovered on-chain, so a force-close does not escape the loop.
4. [lightningd/subd.c:493–590](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L493-L590)
   Every subdaemon message is handled inside db_begin_transaction (493) / db_commit_transaction (590). fatal() aborts (log.c:1143) before commit, so wallet_htlc_update and wallet_payment_set_status are rolled back: the HTLC stays unresolved and the payment PENDING, and the peer must retransmit the fulfil on reestablish (we never sent revoke_and_ack), repeating the crash.
5. [wallet/wallet.c:6401–6429](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L6401-L6429)
   wallet_invoice_request_disable()/invoice_request_status_update() clear the active flag with no check for payments whose local_invreq_id references the request and are still PENDING. Unlike offer_status_update for offers, nothing expires or re-checks dependent state.
6. [lightningd/offer.c:554–593](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L554-L593)
   json_disableinvoicerequest only requires the request to currently be active; it does not refuse while a payment for it is in flight. There is no enableinvoicerequest RPC to undo it, and delpay refuses PENDING rows (pay.c:2357 param_payment_status_nopending), so recovery needs manual DB editing.
7. [lightningd/pay.c:798–848](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L798-L848)
   check_invoice_request_usage() validates the request is active only at sendpay/injectpaymentonion time (called at 1112 and 1928); the status is never rechecked when the HTLC later resolves.
8. [plugins/offers\_inv\_hook.c:190–201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_inv_hook.c#L190-L201)
   The offers plugin auto-pays any valid invoice received over onion message for one of our published invoice_requests, passing localinvreqid to xpay (198-200), which forwards it to injectpaymentonion (plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1539-1540). The remote payee thus controls creation and timing of the pending payment.

## Impact
Process abort of lightningd that recurs on every restart while the peer (or onchaind, after a force-close) re-reports the preimage; node is unavailable (all channels, all HTLCs, missed timeouts with on-chain consequences) until the operator manually edits the database. No confidentiality or integrity impact beyond the unrecorded payment state.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: the remote payee of one of our published BOLT12 invoice_requests (an unauthenticated Lightning counterparty; no privileges on our node). They send a valid invoice over onion message; the offers plugin auto-pays via xpay -> injectpaymentonion with localinvreqid, and the payments row stores local_invreq_id. The attacker withholds the preimage (permitted until CLTV expiry, hours to days). The operator, seeing a stuck payment or wishing to cancel a recurring request, runs the documented `disableinvoicerequest` (UI:ACTIVE); its docs concede payments may still reference the request and nothing re-validates. The attacker then fulfils (update_fulfill_htlc, or on-chain claim): payment_succeeded -> wallet_invoice_request_mark_used -> fatal(). The subd.c transaction is rolled back, so the HTLC stays unresolved, the peer retransmits on reestablish, and lightningd aborts on every restart until the operator hand-edits the invoicerequests table (no enableinvoicerequest RPC; delpay refuses PENDING). AT:P because the attacker must be the payee the victim chose to pay via an invoice_request, and the disable must land in the pending window the attacker controls.

## Recommended fix
1. wallet_invoice_request_mark_used() treats an inactive invoice_request as fatal corruption even though disableinvoicerequest can legitimately make it inactive while a payment referencing it is pending. Fix criteria: A fulfilled payment whose local_invreq_id is disabled (or missing) must complete normally (log and skip, or mark used regardless) and never abort the process. Verify: disable an invoice_request while its payment is pending, then fulfil; lightningd stays up and the payment is reported complete.
2. disableinvoicerequest does not consider payments in flight for the request, so the state machine has a transition with no consumer-side handling. Fix criteria: Either refuse to disable an invoice_request while a PENDING payment references it, or document/handle the pending case explicitly so that no later code path can observe an unexpected status. Verify via the same test as above.

# recover RPC re-execs lightningd with the wallet seed on its command line

## Details
The `recover` JSON-RPC command (lightningd/jsonrpc.c:318-326) takes the node's hsm seed — a BIP39 mnemonic, codex32 secret or 32-byte hex — as a parameter over the 0600 Unix socket, stores it in ld->recover_secret and requests a re-exec. In main()'s shutdown path (lightningd/lightningd.c:1583-1592) lightningd appends `--recover=<secret>` to its saved argv and execv()s itself (lightningd.c:1618). The successor parses the option in opt_set_hsm_secret() (options.c:1360-1441), writes hsm_secret with mode 0400 inside the 0700 lightning-dir, and continues running in offline mode "for manual recovery" (doc/lightningd-config.5.md:343) until the operator restarts it (tests/test_misc.py:5008 needs an explicit l1.restart() to clear the option).

For that whole window the complete wallet seed sits in the recovered daemon's argument vector. On Linux /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable unless procfs is mounted with hidepid (not the default on mainstream distributions, nor in the shipped Docker image); the systemd unit in contrib/init/lightningd.service runs as User=bitcoin on a shared host. Any other unprivileged local user, or any agent that inventories process command lines (ps/top/htop, systemctl status, auditd execve records, monitoring and crash collectors), obtains the seed and can derive every node key and sweep all on-chain funds.

The project explicitly protects this secret from other local principals: hsm_secret is 0400, lightning-dir 0700, the RPC socket 0600, and --recover is OPT_CONCEAL so listconfigs redacts it (options.c:1493). The project has also already treated command-line secret exposure as a defect once (CHANGELOG #4303: hsmtool passwords moved from argv to stdin). The recover RPC undoes those controls: a secret received over a private, operator-only channel is handed to the successor process through the one IPC mechanism that is readable by every local user. The operator never chose argv exposure — the documented alternative `recover=mnemonic` in the config file keeps the secret inside the 0700 directory — and doc/schemas/recover.json does not warn that the seed will appear on the daemon's command line. The hsm_secret file the option itself writes (0400) would suffice as the hand-off: the successor could simply start in offline mode without carrying the secret at all.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1583–1592](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1583-L1592)
   In main()'s shutdown path, when try_reexec is set and ld->recover_secret is non-NULL (set only by the recover RPC), the full hsm seed is formatted as "--recover=<secret>" and inserted into the saved orig_argv for the successor process.
2. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1612–1619](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1612-L1619)
   execv(orig_argv[0], orig_argv) starts the replacement lightningd with the seed in its argument vector; on Linux /proc/<pid>/cmdline is readable by every local user (default procfs hidepid=0), so ps/top/systemctl status/auditd and any process-inventory agent see it for the whole lifetime of the recovered node.
3. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:318–325](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L318-L325)
   json_recover() receives hsmsecret as a JSON-RPC parameter over the 0600 Unix socket (private to the operator), stores it as ld->recover_secret and sets try_reexec, so the seed arrives through a private channel and is then re-emitted through a public one.
4. [lightningd/options.c:1360–1441](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1360-L1441)
   opt_set_hsm_secret() consumes --recover and writes the seed to hsm_secret opened O_CREAT|O_EXCL with mode 0400 (line 1367) — the project's shipped control keeping the seed from other local users — then keeps a copy in ld->recover and enters offline mode; nothing scrubs the argv string, so the 0400 protection is undermined by the world-readable copy in the process arguments.
5. [lightningd/options.c:1493–1497](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1493-L1497)
   --recover is registered OPT_CONCEAL so listconfigs redacts it: the maintainers classify the value as a secret, yet the recover flow places it where any local process can read it.

## Impact
The hsm seed is the root of every node and wallet key; its disclosure is total loss of key confidentiality and lets the holder sweep on-chain funds and impersonate the node. The code path itself does not modify node state or affect availability, so integrity and availability are rated from the disclosure alone.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker is an unprivileged local user (or any process-inventory agent) on the host where the operator ran `lightning-cli recover`; reading /proc/<pid>/cmdline of the recovered lightningd yields the plaintext seed with no defence to defeat. The attack depends on runtime state the attacker does not control — the operator must have invoked the recover RPC and the node must not yet have been restarted — so attack_requirements is PRESENT. Not reachable by remote peers or rune holders; the finding's reach is bounded to co-located local principals.

## Recommended fix
1. The recover re-exec passes the seed to the successor lightningd via argv (lightningd.c:1587-1589), which every local user can read through /proc/<pid>/cmdline, defeating the 0400/0700 file protections the same flow sets up. Fix criteria: The seed never appears in the arguments or environment of any lightningd process spawned by the recover flow: the successor derives its state from the 0400 hsm_secret already written (e.g. a secret-free flag such as --offline/--recover-restart), or receives the secret over a private inherited descriptor that is closed after use. Verify by invoking `recover` and confirming /proc/<pid>/cmdline and /proc/<pid>/environ of the restarted daemon contain no seed material.
2. When --recover is parsed (options.c:1360-1441) the argv storage holding the secret is never overwritten, so an explicitly supplied secret stays visible for the process lifetime. Fix criteria: After opt_set_hsm_secret() consumes the value, the argv bytes holding it are scrubbed (and the documentation for --recover and the recover RPC warns against passing the seed on the command line, recommending the config-file form); verify the secret is absent from /proc/<pid>/cmdline shortly after startup.
