# channel_hint_update aborts when hint capacity times idle seconds overflows u64

## Details
channel_hint_update (plugins/channel_hint.c:68-111) relaxes a hint linearly: refill = capacity * (now - timestamp) / PAY_REFILL_TIME, where capacity is the channel's total msat and the elapsed time is whatever has passed since the hint was last touched. Both arithmetic steps abort() on overflow (lines 83-89; amount_msat_mul/amount_msat_add return false on u64 overflow, common/amount.c:268-277, 600-605). channel_hint_set_update (209-218) walks every hint at the start of each root payment (libplugin-pay.c:2650, in the local_channel_hints modifier used by both pay.c:643 and keysend.c:153) and discards the 'remove me' return value. The hint set is process-global (pay.c:242, keysend.c:140, bound to p->hints at libplugin-pay.c:154), there is no timer or expiry, so a remote hint's timestamp is only refreshed when a payment runs.

Hints for remote channels are created whenever an intermediate node returns a channel failure (libplugin-pay.c:1432-1459) with capacity = errchan->capacity: the gossip channel amount for ordinary hops (common/route.c:107-108, which gossipd stores only after bitcoind confirmed the funding output, gossmap_manage.c:855-856), or 2 x final_amount for routehint hops (libplugin-pay.c:3108, 3128). The stored capacity only ever grows (channel_hint.c:158-159). Local channel hints are re-added with a fresh timestamp immediately before the update loop (2600-2650) so they never accumulate idle time; remote hints do.

The product overflows u64 when capacity_msat * idle_seconds >= 2^64 (~1.8e19): a 1000 BTC channel after ~2.1 days, 100 BTC after ~21 days, 10 BTC after ~213 days, 5 BTC after ~14 months. The next root payment through that plugin then abort()s in channel_hint_set_update before any routing happens; pay and keysend are important plugins (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2590), so lightningd exits. Restarting clears the in-memory hints, so one planted hint yields one crash per idle period.

Attacker position: the endpoint of a large public channel on the victim's route (e.g. an attacker who funds a big channel between two of its own nodes and issues the victim an invoice reachable only across it, then returns temporary_channel_failure) plants the hint; the victim's idle time does the rest. Capacity cannot be inflated beyond the real on-chain funding amount, so the cost of the attack scales with capital, and the same overflow also occurs with no attacker when an ordinary payment fails at a large channel and the node then stays idle. Reachability in default configuration: xpay takes over `pay` by default (xpay.c:3570, CHANGELOG #9110), but keysend always runs libplugin-pay with its own global hint set, and `pay` invocations xpay declines to redirect (array params with more than two arguments, xpay.c:3449-3456, or xpay-handle-pay=false) still run the pay plugin's path. This resolves ledger lead l-e6-07 for channel_hint.c:83-89.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/channel\_hint.c:79–89](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/channel_hint.c#L79-L89)
   Refill math: seconds = now - hint->timestamp (unbounded wall-clock idle time); amount_msat_mul(&refill, capacity, seconds) returns false on u64 overflow -> abort(); amount_msat_add(estimated, refill) -> abort() on overflow. This is where the fix (saturate/clamp or cap elapsed time) belongs.
2. [plugins/channel\_hint.c:209–217](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/channel_hint.c#L209-L217)
   channel_hint_set_update calls channel_hint_update on every hint in the set and ignores the 'may be removed' return value, so stale hints and their timestamps persist and are recomputed on every root payment.
3. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2645–2650](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2645-L2650)
   channel_hint_set_update(root->hints, clock_time()) runs at the start of every root payment in the local_channel_hints modifier (used by pay.c:643 and keysend.c:153); the first payment after an idle period performs the multiplication with the full idle duration.
4. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1432–1458](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L1432-L1458)
   Hints for remote channels are created from intermediate-node channel failures (peer-authored failure onions) with capacity = errchan->capacity, the gossip channel amount for ordinary hops.
5. [plugins/pay.c:242](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L242)
   global_hints is created once at plugin init and lives for the plugin's lifetime (keysend.c:140 does the same); libplugin-pay.c:154 binds every payment to it, so remote hints survive across payments with no expiry or timer.
6. [common/route.c:107–108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/route.c#L107-L108)
   Route hop capacity is gossmap_chan_get_capacity, the funding amount gossipd recorded after bitcoind verified the UTXO; the attacker cannot inflate it beyond a real channel, so attack cost scales with the capital in the channel.
7. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:3102–3128](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L3102-L3128)
   Routehint hops get hop.capacity = 2 * final_amount, so a failed routehint hop creates a hint whose capacity is twice the invoice amount (a smaller, payee-influenced contribution).
8. [plugins/channel\_hint.c:154–159](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/channel_hint.c#L154-L159)
   On update the stored capacity only ever grows (max of observations), so a large capacity is never reduced.

## Impact
abort() in pay or keysend, both important plugins, makes lightningd exit; hints are in-memory so the crash is one-shot per planted hint and idle period, recurring only after another failure at a large channel and another idle window. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A hop on the victim's route (endpoint of a large public channel, which an attacker can fund between its own nodes and make the only path to an invoice it issues) returns a channel failure, planting a hint with the channel's real funding amount as capacity. The victim then issues no payment through that plugin for 2^64/capacity_msat seconds (hours to months depending on channel size) and its next pay/keysend aborts. Remote, no privileges, no security control to defeat (AC:L), but it depends on channel size and the victim's idle window (AT:P) and on the victim initiating payments (UI:P). Default-config reachable via keysend, and via pay when xpay does not redirect.

## Recommended fix
1. The refill computation multiplies msat capacity by unbounded elapsed seconds and treats overflow as a fatal invariant violation. Fix criteria: Refill must saturate (treat overflow as 'fully refilled' and clamp to capacity) or divide before multiplying / cap elapsed seconds at PAY_REFILL_TIME; no input-derived path may abort. Verify with a hint whose capacity*elapsed exceeds 2^64: the hint becomes fully relaxed and the plugin continues.
2. channel_hint_set_update ignores channel_hint_update's return value so useless hints accumulate forever and keep being recomputed. Fix criteria: Remove hints that report themselves useless (or expire them after PAY_REFILL_TIME), so the set is bounded and stale timestamps do not persist across long idle periods.

# Routehint hint-direction mismatch causes unbounded synchronous RETRY_GETROUTE loop in pay

## Details
The routehints modifier and the channel-hint store disagree about the direction key of a routehint channel. routehint_excluded (plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2834-2840) looks up the hint for routehint hop i under (scid, node_id_idx(r->pubkey, pay_destination)), while the hop appended to p->route (3130-3137) and therefore the hint recorded when that hop fails (1442-1459, errchan->direction) use node_id_cmp(prev_hop, next_hop) > 0. For a two-hop routehint [P:S1, X:S2] the two keys differ whenever (P > X) != (P > D); the payee chooses X freely (filter_routehints validates only the entry node P).

Flow: the victim runs legacy `pay` on the attacker's invoice (destination D unannounced). The routehint is selected, a route to P computed, the routehint stitched on and the onion sent. P (the attacker's public node) replies temporary_channel_failure; lightningd reports erring_index = origin_index+1 (lightningd/pay.c:527), assign_blame picks the stitched S1 hop (amount A+f2, dir(P,X)) and a hint (S1, dir(P,X)) with estimated_capacity = A+f2-1 is stored. The retry child keeps the same routehint offset (parent->route is non-NULL, 3155-3160) and next_routehint re-selects it: payment_get_excluded_channels (614-637) only compares our_amount A with the estimate (A+f2-1 >= A when f2 >= 1 msat, so the payee sets f2 = 1 msat base fee), and routehint_excluded's capacity check looks up (S1, dir(P,D)) and finds nothing. getroute to P succeeds, routehint_step_cb re-appends the hops, and payment_chanhints_apply_route rejects the route because A+f2 > A+f2-1 (first round fails; no state changes). payment_compute_onion_payloads (1886-1894) then sets RETRY_GETROUTE and calls payment_continue: no modifier handles that step, payment_getlocalmods sees p->mods (inherited from the parent, payment_new:140) and calls payment_getroute directly, which runs route()/dijkstra again and re-enters payment_continue. No RPC, no counter, no change of routehint: a synchronous loop nested on the stack (default COPTFLAGS=-Og, configure:46-51, so no sibling-call elimination), each iteration running a full dijkstra whose tal_arr(tmpctx, struct dijkstra, gossmap_max_node_idx) (common/dijkstra.c:156) is only freed when control returns to the plugin event loop (clean_tmpctx, plugins/libplugin.c:2484).

Bound: the only exits are payment_getroute's fee and CLTV budget checks (900-923), which deduct the route fee (f1+f2 plus public-path fees) and route[0].delay each iteration. The payee controls both: f1 = 0, f2 = 1 msat (the minimum that defeats the scid-only exclusion; with f2 = 0 the stored estimate A-1 < A would exclude S1), cltv_expiry_delta = 0 on both hops, bolt11 c = 0 (decode_c accepts any value, common/bolt11.c:306). With P a direct peer of the victim the local channel carries zero fee and zero delta in the localmods (common/gossmods_listpeerchannels.c:160-163), and with D unannounced the shadowroute modifier's listchannels(source=D) returns nothing, so it adds no CLTV. Hence route[0].delay = 0 and fee = 1 msat per iteration: the loop runs fee_budget iterations - at least 5000 (exemptfee floor, plugins/pay.c:1114) and 0.5% of the amount for larger invoices (500,000 for a 100k-sat invoice; the invoice amount is the attacker's). Each iteration costs a network-wide dijkstra (tens of ms of CPU and roughly 0.5-1 MB of retained tmpctx on mainnet) and about forty stack frames. Outcome: the pay plugin exhausts its stack (SIGSEGV), is OOM-killed as tmpctx grows by gigabytes, or is wedged for minutes to hours of CPU; `pay` is an important plugin, so lightningd exits when it dies.

With a non-zero CLTV (c >= 1 or honest deltas) the loop still runs up to maxdelay (2016) iterations per attempt before 'CLTV delay exceeds our CLTV budget', i.e. about a gigabyte of tmpctx and seconds to minutes of blocking, which is also what honest two-hop routehints with a mismatching direction cost today.

Reachability: in the default configuration (xpay-handle-pay=true) `pay` still goes to the legacy plugin whenever xpay's rpc_command hook declines (plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3446-3514: more than two positional params, `invstring` instead of `bolt11`, maxfee combinations calc_maxfee rejects), and always with xpay-handle-pay=false.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1886–1894](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L1886-L1894)
   payment_compute_onion_payloads: when payment_chanhints_apply_route rejects the route the step is set to PAYMENT_STEP_RETRY_GETROUTE and payment_continue is invoked synchronously. No iteration counter, no state change to the routehint or hints, so the identical route is rebuilt and rejected again, nesting on the stack.
2. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2834–2840](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2834-L2840)
   routehint_excluded's capacity check looks up the hint for routehint hop i under direction node_id_idx(&r->pubkey, p->pay_destination), i.e. relative to the final destination rather than the hop's actual next node, so the hint stored on failure is not found.
3. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:3130–3137](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L3130-L3137)
   The stitched route_hop uses direction node_id_cmp(prev_hop, next-hop pubkey) > 0. For a multi-hop routehint this differs from the lookup key whenever (P > X) != (P > destination), which the payee arranges by choosing X.
4. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1442–1459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L1442-L1459)
   A temporary_channel_failure blamed on the stitched hop stores a hint under errchan->direction (the stitched direction) with estimated_capacity = hop amount - 1, so apply_route can never accept the same hop again.
5. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:614–637](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L614-L637)
   payment_get_excluded_channels compares only our_amount against the estimate (and routehint_excluded matches it by scid only): with a 1 msat routehint fee the estimate A+f2-1 >= A, so this check does not exclude the routehint either.
6. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2365–2368](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2365-L2368)
   payment_continue dispatches RETRY_GETROUTE to payment_getlocalmods, which calls payment_getroute directly because p->mods is inherited from the parent (payment_new), so the whole cycle is one synchronous recursion with no RPC round-trip.
7. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:900–923](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L900-L923)
   The only loop exits: fee and route[0].delay are checked against and deducted from p->constraints each iteration. With payee-chosen f1=0, f2=1 msat, zero cltv deltas, c=0, a direct zero-rate peer as entry and an unannounced destination (no shadow CLTV), delay is 0 and fee 1 msat, so the loop runs fee_budget iterations (>= 5000; 0.5% of the invoice amount in msat).
8. [common/dijkstra.c:156](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/dijkstra.c#L156)
   Each iteration's dijkstra allocates a struct per gossmap node on tmpctx, which is only cleaned when the plugin returns to its event loop, so memory grows by roughly the gossmap node count times sizeof(struct dijkstra) per iteration.
9. [common/bolt11.c:306](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L306)
   decode_c accepts c = 0 without a minimum, letting the payee zero the final CLTV so the per-iteration CLTV deduction vanishes.

## Impact
Unbounded synchronous recursion and per-iteration dijkstra allocation inside the pay plugin: stack exhaustion or OOM kills the plugin, which is important, so lightningd exits; short of that the plugin is wedged for minutes to hours with the node unable to pay. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote payee running one public node P that is a peer of (or routable from) the victim publishes a bolt11 invoice to an unannounced destination with routehint [P:S1 (fee 0, delta 0), X:S2 (base fee 1 msat, delta 0)], X chosen so dir(P,X) != dir(P,D), and c=0. When the victim pays it through the legacy pay plugin, P answers temporary_channel_failure and the retry enters the synchronous getroute loop deterministically for fee_budget iterations. Requires the victim operator to deliberately pay the attacker's invoice (UI:A) and the legacy pay path (xpay-handle-pay=false, or a pay invocation xpay's hook declines to redirect in default configuration) (AT:P). No credentials needed.

## Recommended fix
1. routehint_excluded derives the hint direction from the final destination while the stitched hop (and the hint recorded on failure) derive it from the next hop, so a hint that makes the route unusable is not seen as excluding the routehint. Fix criteria: Both sites must compute the (scid, direction) key identically (direction relative to the actual next hop). Verify: after a temporary failure on a two-hop routehint hop, the retry no longer selects that routehint for the same amount.
2. PAYMENT_STEP_RETRY_GETROUTE re-runs the same route computation synchronously with no bound and no state change, so any persistent apply failure recurses forever. Fix criteria: Bound the RETRY_GETROUTE path (e.g. a per-payment counter that fails the attempt after N rejections, or exclude the offending hop/routehint before retrying) and avoid unbounded recursion through payment_continue. Verify that a route rejected by payment_chanhints_apply_route cannot loop more than a small fixed number of times.

# Unknown onion failure code leaves failcodename NULL; paystatus and duplicate-pay reply crash

## Details
Any node on a payment route (an intermediate hop or the payee) authors the failure onion returned to the payer, including its 16-bit failure type (an attacker running CLN can do this with the htlc_accepted hook's `failure_message`, lightningd/peer_htlcs.c:1183-1216). lightningd decrypts it (unwrap_onionreply), takes the type with fromwire_peektype (lightningd/pay.c:626-636, 449) and reports it to waitsendpay callers via json_add_routefail_info (lightningd/pay.c:214-221); for a type not in the BOLT4 enum onion_wire_name() yields 'UNKNOWN <n>' and `failcodename` is deliberately omitted while `failcode` is still emitted. In the pay plugin, tal_sendpay_result_from_json (plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1138-1142) accordingly stores failcodename = NULL; handle_final_failure / handle_intermediate_failure log a 'strange error' and payment_fail() leaves the attempt at PAYMENT_STEP_FAILED with p->result retained. The root payment is tal_steal'd onto the plugin and stays in the global `payments` list for the life of the process (start_payment, pay.c:678-683; nothing frees finished roots).

Two paths in plugins/pay.c then dereference the NULL string via json_add_string -> strlen(NULL) (common/json_stream.c:207-212):
1. `paystatus` (json_paystatus -> paystatus_add_payment -> json_add_sendpay_result, pay.c:99-111) walks every attempt of every stored payment and emits failcodename unconditionally for each failed result. Any later paystatus call by the operator (or a rune bearer permitted paystatus; the command is deprecated from v26.06 but available while allow-deprecated-apis is true, the non-developer default) crashes the plugin.
2. on_payment_failure (pay.c:389-400): when a second `pay` for the same payment_hash was suspended because the first was pending (payment_listsendpays_previous, pay.c:615-621), and the active payment's highest-failcode failure (payment_collect_result, libplugin-pay.c:268-274) has failcode >= NODE (0x2000) - e.g. the attacker-chosen unknown code 0x2fff - the failure is replayed to the suspended command with json_add_string(ret, "failcodename", NULL) and crashes.

The equivalent code in libplugin-pay.c payment_finished (2258-2261) guards the field, so the NULL case is known; pay.c's two copies lack the guard. `pay` is an `important` plugin, so the crash terminates lightningd.

Condition: the payment must have been run by the legacy pay plugin rather than xpay. xpay takes over `pay` by default (plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3570, CHANGELOG:219; doc/lightningd-config.5.md:563 still says default false) but only for invocations it recognises (xpay.c:3432-3514): legacy pay still handles `pay` when xpay-handle-pay=false, when positional params number other than 1 or 2 (e.g. `lightning-cli pay <bolt11> <amount_msat> <label>`), when object params use `invstring` instead of `bolt11` (pay.c:903-905 accepts it; xpay does not), or when calc_maxfee rejects the maxfee/maxfeepercent/exemptfee combination or an amountless invoice.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/pay.c:99–110](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L99-L110)
   json_add_sendpay_result, used by `paystatus` for every stored attempt, calls json_add_string(s, "failcodename", r->failcodename) unconditionally for each failed result; r->failcodename is NULL for an unrecognised failure type.
2. [plugins/pay.c:389–399](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L389-L399)
   on_payment_failure replays the active payment's failure (failcode >= NODE) to suspended duplicate `pay` calls and passes failure->failcodename to json_add_string without a NULL check.
3. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:1138–1141](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L1138-L1141)
   tal_sendpay_result_from_json treats failcodename as optional and stores NULL when waitsendpay's error data lacks it; the result is kept on the attempt (p->result) after payment_fail().
4. [lightningd/pay.c:214–220](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L214-L220)
   json_add_routefail_info emits `failcode` but omits `failcodename` whenever onion_wire_name() returns 'UNKNOWN <n>', i.e. for any failure type not in the BOLT4 enum.
5. [lightningd/pay.c:626–636](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L626-L636)
   payment_failed derives failcode with fromwire_peektype from the decrypted failure message authored by the erring remote node; no validation of the type value precedes remote_routing_failure.
6. [common/json\_stream.c:207–211](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_stream.c#L207-L211)
   json_add_string calls strlen(str) before json_add_stringn; a NULL str is a segfault.
7. [plugins/pay.c:675–683](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L675-L683)
   start_payment adds the root payment to the global `payments` list and tal_steals it onto the plugin, so the attempt tree with the NULL failcodename persists for the plugin's lifetime and is walked by every later paystatus.
8. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2258–2260](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2258-L2260)
   payment_finished guards the same field with `if (failure->failcodename)`, showing the NULL case is known; pay.c's two copies lack the guard.
9. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3432–3447](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L3432-L3447)
   xpay's rpc_command hook (take_over_pay defaults true at xpay.c:3570) redirects only `pay` calls with 1-2 positional args or an object containing `bolt11`; other invocations (3+ positional args, `invstring`, weird maxfee params) or xpay-handle-pay=false fall through to the legacy pay plugin - the condition under which this finding holds.

## Impact
Segfault in the important pay plugin shuts down lightningd. No data disclosure or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote node on the route (or the payee) returns a failure onion whose type is not in the BOLT4 enum; nothing in lightningd's BOLT4 processing rejects it and the attacker needs no privileges beyond being a hop or payee on a route the victim uses. The pay plugin stores failcodename=NULL on a persistent attempt record. The crash completes when the victim's operator or tooling runs the routine `paystatus` command, or when a duplicate `pay` for the same hash was suspended (passive interaction). Attack requirements are present: the payment must have been handled by the legacy pay plugin rather than xpay (xpay-handle-pay=false, or a pay invocation xpay does not redirect such as 3+ positional args or `invstring`), and paystatus must not be disabled via allow-deprecated-apis=false.

## Recommended fix
pay.c serialises failcodename without checking for NULL although the parser and lightningd both treat it as optional. Fix criteria: Both json_add_sendpay_result and on_payment_failure must tolerate a NULL failcodename (omit the field or emit a placeholder). Verify by injecting a waitsendpay failure with an unknown failcode and calling paystatus / a duplicate pay: the plugin must stay alive.

# Payee routehint reusing payer's own channel scid aborts pay plugin in channel-hint apply

## Details
The legacy `pay` plugin applies a route to its channel hints in payment_chanhints_apply_route (plugins/libplugin-pay.c:506-582), called from payment_compute_onion_payloads (line 1886) before createonion. Round one checks each hop individually against its hint (estimated_capacity >= hop amount, htlc_budget > 0); round two deducts each hop's amount from the hint with amount_msat_deduct (a checked subtraction, common/amount.c:285) and calls abort() at line 577 if it fails, with the comment 'Given our preemptive test above, this should never happen'. The pre-check never sums amounts per hint, so it is insufficient when two hops of p->route resolve to the same (scid, direction) key.

A payee controls the bolt11 'r' field; common/bolt11.c decode_r only checks pubkey validity and pay.c:960 stores the hints as p->routes. routehint_step_cb (3100-3139) appends hint hops verbatim at PAYMENT_STEP_GOT_ROUTE: hop.scid = routehint[i].short_channel_id, hop.amount = our_amount plus later-hop fees, hop.direction = node_id_cmp(prev_hop.node_id, next.pubkey) > 0. No check rejects an scid already used by the getroute part of the route. The payer's own channels always carry a hint (local_channel_hints, 2625-2642) keyed (scid, listpeerchannels.direction) where direction = node_id_idx(our_id, peer_id) (lightningd/peer_control.c:1064), with estimated_capacity = spendable_msat.

Attack: victim V has a public channel S with peer P. The payee publishes an invoice from node id D with a one-hop routehint [P, S] and chooses D so that node_id_idx(P, D) equals node_id_idx(V, P) (50% of fresh keys; a multi-hop hint with an arbitrary intermediate pubkey gives the same control). Fees/delta may be 0. filter_routehints keeps it (P is in gossip and reachable); routehint_check_reachable finds D unreachable so the hint is used first; routehint_excluded (2786-2842) does not exclude it because the last hint hop skips the capacity check and the local hint's estimate (spendable) is >= A. getroute from V to P picks the direct channel S (hop direction node_id_idx(V,P), amount A), the stitch appends (S, same direction, A), so p->route = [(S,d,A),(S,d,A)]. Round one passes twice when spendable >= A; round two deducts A twice and abort()s whenever spendable < 2A. Any amount A with spendable/2 < A <= spendable kills the pay plugin deterministically; omitting basic_mpp from the invoice features prevents splitting (adaptive_splitter_cb gates on payment_supports_mpp). If the attacker is P it knows spendable; otherwise balance probing or repeated invoices suffice.

`pay` is a builtin plugin registered important (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2590), so lightningd exits (plugin.c:297-302). Reachability of the legacy path: plugins/xpay/xpay.c sets take_over_pay = true by default (doc/lightningd-config.5.md:561 still documents the default as false), but the rpc_command hook (xpay.c:3446-3514) hands `pay` to the legacy plugin whenever the params array has other than 1 or 2 elements (e.g. `pay <bolt11> <amount_msat> <label>` positionally), whenever calc_maxfee returns false (maxfee combined with maxfeepercent/exemptfee, or an amountless invoice with maxfeepercent/exemptfee and no amount_msat), or when the operator sets xpay-handle-pay=false. keysend shares the library but has no routehints.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:506–581](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L506-L581)
   payment_chanhints_apply_route: the first loop validates every hop independently against its channel hint (estimated_capacity >= hop amount, htlc_budget > 0); the second loop deducts each hop's amount cumulatively from the same hint via amount_msat_deduct (checked subtraction) and calls abort() at line 577 when it underflows. Two hops sharing one (scid, direction) key pass the first loop while the second underflows when spendable < 2A.
2. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:3100–3138](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L3100-L3138)
   routehint_step_cb at PAYMENT_STEP_GOT_ROUTE appends payee-authored routehint hops to p->route with hop.scid taken verbatim from the invoice and hop.direction = node_id_cmp(prev_hop.node_id, next.pubkey) > 0, which the payee controls through its own node id. Nothing checks that the stitched (scid, direction) duplicates a hop already in the getroute part of the route.
3. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2786–2841](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2786-L2841)
   routehint_excluded skips the capacity check for the last routehint hop (line 2818) and otherwise only excludes a hint whose channel is disabled or whose estimate is below our_amount, so a one-hop hint naming the payer's own channel with spendable >= amount is not excluded.
4. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2625–2641](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2625-L2641)
   local_channel_hints registers a hint keyed by (scid, listpeerchannels.direction = node_id_idx(our_id, peer_id)) for every local channel with estimated_capacity = spendable_msat; both duplicated hops resolve to this hint.
5. [plugins/pay.c:960–962](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L960-L962)
   p->routes is the payee's bolt11 'r' field as decoded by common/bolt11.c decode_r (pubkey validity only), unvalidated beyond length and entry-node reachability in filter_routehints.
6. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3446–3513](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L3446-L3513)
   xpay's rpc_command hook redirects `pay` to xpay by default (take_over_pay = true) but declines — leaving the legacy pay plugin to handle the call — when the params array has other than 1 or 2 elements, when calc_maxfee returns false, or when xpay-handle-pay is false; these are the default-configuration routes to the vulnerable code.

## Impact
abort() in the pay plugin; pay is a builtin plugin registered important, so lightningd shuts down (plugin.c:297-302), stopping all channel operation until restarted. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote payee (threat-model adversary 3), optionally also the victim's channel peer P. They craft a bolt11 invoice from a node id chosen so node_id_idx(P, D) matches the victim's direction on channel S, a one-hop routehint [P, S], no basic_mpp feature, and an amount in (spendable/2, spendable]. When the victim's node runs the legacy pay plugin on it (routine for withdrawal services; default-config paths exist via 3+ positional params or calc_maxfee declining, and always with xpay-handle-pay=false), the route is stitched as two hops on the same hint, the second deduction underflows and abort() fires; there is no defence to defeat. Requirements: the amount window and a legacy-pay invocation.

## Recommended fix
1. payment_chanhints_apply_route validates hops individually but deducts cumulatively, and aborts on the resulting underflow instead of treating it as an unusable route. Fix criteria: Applying a route must never abort on payee-influenced data: either aggregate amounts per (scid,dir) in the pre-check, or make the second pass fail soft (unapply what was deducted and retry/fail the attempt). Verify by paying an invoice whose routehint reuses the first-hop channel scid: the attempt fails cleanly and the plugin stays alive.
2. routehint_step_cb stitches payee-authored hops without checking that their scids do not duplicate channels already in the route. Fix criteria: Reject or skip routehints whose (scid, direction) already appears in the computed route (or equals one of the payer's own channels); verify such a routehint is reported as unusable rather than used.

# Hook num_users refcount leaks when a deserializer stops the chain; ordering frozen, abort() armed

## Details
lightningd/plugin_hook.c tracks concurrent users of each plugin hook in hook->num_users so that a re-ordering of hook->hooks (computed by plugin_hook_make_ordered() every time a plugin manifest is accepted) can be deferred while a chained invocation is iterating the array by index. hook_start() (line 222-225) increments the count in plugin_hook_call_() (line 377); hook_done() (lines 227-244) is the only decrement and, on reaching zero, swaps in the deferred hook->new_hooks array. hook_done() is reached only when the chain runs to completion (line 343) or when no plugin is registered (line 402).

plugin_hook_callback() has a second exit: when the hook's deserialize_cb returns false ("stop the chain, the event is resolved"), lines 288-293 free cb_arg and ph_req and return. hook_done() is never called, so the increment is never undone and num_users leaks by one for every chain stopped this way.

Stopping the chain is the documented outcome of common hook results, and remote peers author the events: an htlc_accepted plugin answering 'fail' or 'resolve' (peer_htlcs.c:1201/1217/1230), a peer_connected plugin answering 'disconnect' (peer_control.c:1660-1672), an openchannel plugin answering 'reject' (opening_control.c:794-804), an openchannel2/rbf_channel plugin answering 'reject' (dual_open_control.c:742-764, 580-597), an invoice_payment plugin answering 'reject' (invoice.c:315-321) or the paying HTLC set having been destroyed by free_htlcs() (channel forgotten / onchaind complete) while the hook was in flight (invoice.c:309-313), and the rpc_command 'already modified' path (jsonrpc.c:941-950).

Condition: the default-loaded shipped plugins (offers, keysend, chanbackup, commando, cln-lsps-client) answer only 'continue', so a stock node does not realistically leak. The leak is reachable when the node runs any hook plugin that returns a chain-stopping result: the shipped cln-lsps-service does so for rejected JIT HTLCs (plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs:85,242-247, under experimental-lsps2-service), funder rejects peer liquidity requests (plugins/funder.c:860-868, under experimental-dual-fund), and hold-invoice/LSP/policy plugins fail or resolve HTLCs by design.

Consequences once num_users is permanently non-zero for a hook:
1. Hook ordering is silently frozen for that hook. plugin_hook_make_ordered() (lines 682-695) stores the new order in hook->new_hooks and only logs 'Deferring registration of hook %s until it's not in use'; hook->hooks keeps raw append order (plugin_hook_register line 205). Every plugin started afterwards via `plugin start`/`startdir`/`rescan` runs in registration order regardless of its before/after constraints (doc/developers-guide/plugin-development/hooks.md: load order 'overridden only by before and after requirements'), so a runtime-started filter plugin meant to precede a plugin that resolves/fails HTLCs can run after it and never see the event.
2. hook->new_hooks becomes permanently non-NULL after the first successful dynamic plugin start following the leak (make_ordered runs for every hook with registered instances). From then on destroy_hook_instance() (lines 73-82) abort()s whenever a hook_instance that was appended to hook->hooks is freed before a successful re-ordering refreshed new_hooks: plugin_parse_getmanifest_response() registers hooks (plugin.c:1821) before plugin_add_params() (1823) can reject an unknown `plugin start` option (1601-1602), and plugin_manifest_cb() then plugin_kill()s (1842) — tal_free(plugin) at plugin.c:461 — without check_plugins_manifests(); the 'Not a dynamic plugin' kill (1855-1857) and a before/after cycle (check_plugins_manifests 139-145, make_ordered returning at 673-679 without touching new_hooks) have the same shape. lightningd aborts, parking in-flight HTLCs.

The maintainers anticipated a live-lock of the deferral ('If this ever live locks, we will see this in the log!', line 693) but the count is simply never released on the early-exit path, so a node whose hook plugin ever stops a chain stays in this state for the rest of its uptime.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:288–293](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L288-L293)
   plugin_hook_callback(): when hook->deserialize_cb returns false (the plugin answered fail/resolve/reject/disconnect, or the payload's HTLC/peer has gone), the code frees cb_arg and ph_req and returns. hook_done() is never called on this path, so hook->num_users, incremented by hook_start() for this invocation, is never decremented. The refcount is leaked permanently for that hook.
2. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:222–244](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L222-L244)
   hook_start()/hook_done() are the only places num_users is touched. hook_done() is the sole decrement and the only place a deferred hook->new_hooks ordering is applied (when the count reaches 0). It is reached only from plugin_hook_call_next() when the chain runs to completion (line 343) or when no plugin is registered (line 402).
3. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:682–695](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L682-L695)
   plugin_hook_make_ordered(): after computing the topological order it only installs it when num_users == 0; otherwise it stores it in hook->new_hooks and logs 'Deferring registration of hook %s until it's not in use'. With a leaked count this branch is taken forever, so the before/after order of every hook instance registered later is never applied (hook->hooks keeps the raw append order from plugin_hook_register line 205), while new_hooks stays non-NULL permanently.
4. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:60–82](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L60-L82)
   destroy_hook_instance()/remove_hook_instance(): when a hook instance is freed it must be found in hook->hooks AND, if hook->new_hooks is non-NULL, in new_hooks, else abort(). Once new_hooks is permanently non-NULL (previous evidence), any hook instance appended to hooks but killed before a successful re-ordering refreshes new_hooks takes the abort() path.
5. [lightningd/plugin.c:1813–1827](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1813-L1827)
   plugin_parse_getmanifest_response() registers hooks (plugin_hooks_add) before plugin_add_params(); if the operator's `plugin start` options are rejected ('unknown parameter'), plugin_manifest_cb kills the plugin without check_plugins_manifests() ever rebuilding new_hooks, so its freshly appended hook_instance is in hooks but not in new_hooks -> abort(). plugin_manifest_cb lines 1855-1857 ('Not a dynamic plugin') is the same shape.
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1178–1230](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1178-L1230)
   htlc_accepted_hook_deserialize returns false whenever a plugin answers result:'fail' or 'resolve' (lines 1201, 1217, 1230); the HTLC that triggers the hook is authored by a remote peer. The shipped cln-lsps-service returns 'fail' for rejected JIT HTLCs (plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs:85,242-247, under experimental-lsps2-service); funder answers 'reject' to openchannel2 (plugins/funder.c:860-868, under experimental-dual-fund; dual_open_control.c:742-764 returns false); peer_connected 'disconnect' (peer_control.c:1660-1672), openchannel 'reject' (opening_control.c:794-804) and invoice_payment 'reject' or HTLC-set-destroyed (invoice.c:309-321) are the other peer-driven false returns. Default-loaded plugins (offers, keysend, chanbackup, commando, lsps-client) answer only 'continue'. Each chain-stopping event leaks one count.

## Impact
Integrity: the documented before/after ordering of hook invocations is silently never applied to any plugin started after the leak, so a runtime-started filter/policy plugin can run after the plugin it was meant to precede and never see the peer's event — a modest, configuration-dependent bypass. Availability: hook re-ordering is frozen for the process lifetime and, after the next successful dynamic plugin start, destroy_hook_instance() abort() is armed and fires on routine operator plugin-management failures (unknown `plugin start` option, non-dynamic plugin, dependency cycle), crashing lightningd with in-flight HTLCs parked. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote peer triggers the leak by sending an event that a registered hook plugin answers with a chain-stopping result: an HTLC the LSPS2 service, a hold-invoice or an LSP/policy plugin fails or resolves, a dual-funding open funder rejects, a connection a peer_connected plugin disconnects. No credentials or interaction are needed. Attack requirement: the node must run a hook plugin that returns non-continue — the default-loaded plugins answer only 'continue', while the shipped cln-lsps-service/funder do so under experimental options and third-party hold-invoice/LSP/policy plugins do by design. The consequences then apply to every later dynamic plugin start by the operator.

## Recommended fix
1. plugin_hook_callback() returns early when deserialize_cb reports the chain is finished without releasing the hook's in-use reference taken by hook_start(), so num_users never returns to zero and deferred orderings are never applied. Fix criteria: Every plugin_hook_call_() invocation must release exactly one reference whether the chain completes, is stopped by a deserializer, or ends because plugins died; after any sequence of hook outcomes num_users returns to 0 when no invocation is in flight, and a plugin started afterwards with before/after constraints is invoked in the computed order (verifiable by starting a plugin after a hook 'fail' and checking that no 'Deferring registration' log is emitted and hook->new_hooks is NULL).
2. destroy_hook_instance() aborts when a hook instance exists in hook->hooks but not in a pending hook->new_hooks, which is reachable because instances are appended to hooks before the manifest is fully validated and before any re-ordering refreshes new_hooks. Fix criteria: Freeing a hook instance that is absent from a pending new_hooks array must not terminate lightningd; a `plugin start` that fails after hook registration (bad option, non-dynamic plugin, unsatisfiable before/after) while another plugin's ordering is deferred must leave the node running with consistent hooks/new_hooks arrays.

# listforwards limit cast to signed int crashes lightningd on PostgreSQL via negative LIMIT

## Details
`listforwards` accepts an optional `limit` parsed with `param_u32` (lightningd/forwards.c:207), so any value up to 4294967295 is accepted. `listforwardings_add_forwardings()` hands the pointer to `forwarding_first()` (wallet/wallet.c), which in both index branches binds it with `db_bind_int(stmt, *listlimit)` (wallet.c:5789 and 5827). `db_bind_int` takes a C `int`, so limits in 2147483648..4294967295 become negative and are bound to the query's `LIMIT ?`.

On sqlite3 a negative LIMIT means 'no limit' and nothing bad happens. On a PostgreSQL backend (`--wallet=postgres://...`) the binding is sent as a binary INT4 parameter (db_postgres.c:105-111); PostgreSQL rejects the statement at execution with `ERROR: LIMIT must not be negative`, `db_postgres_query()` returns false (db_postgres.c:143-149), and `db_query_prepared()` calls `db_fatal()` (db/utils.c:154-158), aborting the whole lightningd process. The node restarts cleanly (the read transaction is rolled back) but the caller can repeat the request at will.

Who can trigger it: any JSON-RPC caller able to invoke `listforwards`. The operator is trusted, but runes are the project's intended bound on lesser callers: a bearer of a `readonly` rune, or a rune restricted to `method=listforwards`, over commando (any connected Lightning peer presenting the rune) or clnrest (HTTP `Rune` header) can call `listforwards index=created limit=4294967295` and kill the node. A read-only rune is not supposed to grant the ability to take the node down, so this is a privilege escalation within the rune model as well as a DoS with on-chain consequences (missed HTLC timeouts/penalties while down and crash-looping if automated).

The same u32-to-int cast of a caller-supplied `limit` recurs at the sibling list iterators (wallet/wallet.c:4551 payments_first, 4701 payments_by_status, 6686 wallet_htlcs_first, 6992 wallet_list_addresses, 7401/7478/7532 network-event and coin-move iterators, and wallet/invoices.c:521), which are outside this unit's reading range and should be checked by their readers; each is reachable from the corresponding list* RPC.

Assumption: PostgreSQL (libpq, any supported version) raises an execution error for a negative LIMIT value supplied as a parameter; this is long-standing server behaviour.

## Evidence
1. [wallet/wallet.c:5788–5791](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L5788-L5791)
   forwarding_first(), WAIT_INDEX_UPDATED branch: the caller-supplied u32 *listlimit is bound with db_bind_int(), whose parameter is a C int. Values 2^31..2^32-1 are converted to negative ints and bound to the statement's 'LIMIT ?'. (The else branch binds INT_MAX, showing the intended bound.)
2. [wallet/wallet.c:5826–5829](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L5826-L5829)
   Same unsigned-to-signed conversion in the created-index branch: db_bind_int(stmt, *listlimit) with the u32 limit bound to 'LIMIT ?'.
3. [lightningd/forwards.c:200–226](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/forwards.c#L200-L226)
   json_listforwards parses limit with param_u32 (json_to_u32 in common/json_parse_simple.c:113-125 accepts the full 0..4294967295 range), requires index to be set, and passes the pointer unchanged to listforwardings_add_forwardings() -> forwarding_first().
4. [db/bindings.c:43–49](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/bindings.c#L43-L49)
   db_bind_int(struct db_stmt *, int val): the u32 argument is implicitly converted to a signed int here and stored as DB_BINDING_INT.
5. [db/db\_postgres.c:105–110](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_postgres.c#L105-L110)
   PostgreSQL driver sends DB_BINDING_INT as a binary INT4OID parameter (cpu_to_be32(b->v.i)), so the negative value reaches the server's LIMIT clause unchanged.
6. [db/db\_postgres.c:137–150](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/db_postgres.c#L137-L150)
   db_postgres_query() returns false whenever PQresultStatus is neither EMPTY_QUERY nor TUPLES_OK; PostgreSQL rejects a negative LIMIT at execution time with 'LIMIT must not be negative' (nodeLimit.c, long-standing server behaviour; stated as an assumption about the PostgreSQL server, any supported version).
7. [db/utils.c:154–158](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/db/utils.c#L154-L158)
   db_query_prepared() turns any query failure into db_fatal(); there is no can-fail path used by forwarding_first().
8. [wallet/db.c:91–101](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/db.c#L91-L101)
   lightningd's db errorfn (installed by db_setup) calls fatal_vfmt() when fatal is true, so db_fatal() terminates the lightningd process.

## Impact
db_fatal() aborts lightningd: all channels go offline, HTLC timeouts and penalty watches are not serviced until restart, and the request can be repeated indefinitely for a crash loop. No data is disclosed or modified (the read transaction is rolled back).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds any rune that permits listforwards (e.g. a readonly rune) and reaches the node over commando (as a connected Lightning peer) or clnrest HTTPS. One request `listforwards index=created limit=4294967295` is enough; no race, no defence to bypass. Requires the node to use the PostgreSQL wallet backend, a supported but non-default deployment choice, hence AT:PRESENT. The operator/Unix-socket caller is trusted, so PR is LOW (rune bearer), not NONE.

## Recommended fix
1. forwarding_first() binds a u32 limit through db_bind_int(), silently converting values >= 2^31 to negative integers that the database layer rejects fatally on PostgreSQL. Fix criteria: A limit of any u32 value must never produce a negative LIMIT: clamp/reject limits above INT_MAX (or bind as u64) in forwarding_first and in the sibling list iterators that share the pattern. Verify that `listforwards index=created limit=4294967295` on a PostgreSQL-backed node returns a normal (possibly full) result instead of aborting the daemon.
2. db_query_prepared() escalates any read-only query failure, including caller-induced parameter errors, to db_fatal(), so a bad RPC parameter becomes process death. Fix criteria: Read paths driven by RPC parameters should validate parameters before binding, or return an RPC error on query failure rather than aborting; a malformed list* request must not terminate lightningd on any backend.

# Newline in bcli RPC string params injects extra bitcoin-cli arguments via -stdin

## Details
bcli invokes bitcoin-cli with `-stdin` and feeds every method argument as one line on the child's stdin (plugins/bcli.c gather_argsv 103-113, execute_bitcoin_cli 171-184). Bitcoin Core's `-stdin` reads one argument per line until EOF with std::getline and appends each line to the positional parameter list; with `-stdinrpcpass` the first line is the RPC password. bcli never checks that an argument is free of newline bytes. The `tx` parameter of bcli's `sendrawtransaction` RPC and the `txid`/`vout` parameters of `getutxout` are taken with param_string (verbatim token bytes, common/json_param.c 456-463) and written straight to that pipe, so a caller who embeds a raw 0x0A in the JSON string injects additional positional arguments into the bitcoin-cli command.

Who controls them: these are ordinary plugin RPC methods registered with lightningd (bcli.c commands[] 833-854), callable by any RPC caller including rune bearers over commando (plugins/commando.c execute_command 282-304 forwards each param token with json_add_jsonstr, preserving raw bytes, after checkrune approved the request) and by local socket clients. CLN's JSON validator (json_parse_simple.c 353-357) only enforces UTF-8 on strings; a raw newline is valid UTF-8, and lightningd forwards the request bytes to the plugin unchanged (plugin.c json_stream_forward_change_id 1187-1212). The rune evaluator (lightningd/runes.c check_condition 851-916) tests each param token separately, so a restriction on `allowhighfees` sees the literal false while the extra lines ride inside the `tx` token. Assumption: the vendored jsmn (external/jsmn submodule, absent from this checkout) accepts unescaped control characters inside string tokens, as upstream zserge/jsmn does (its string scanner only inspects quotes and backslash escapes).

Concrete effect: a rune that permits `sendrawtransaction` but pins `allowhighfees` to false (or restricts `tx` by prefix) is meant to keep bitcoind's absurd-fee and burn-amount sanity checks in force (doc/developers-guide/plugin-development/bitcoin-backend.md: allowhighfees 'suppress any high-fees check implemented in the backend'). With tx = "<hex>\n0\n21000000" bitcoin-cli receives `sendrawtransaction <hex> 0 21000000`: maxfeerate 0 disables the fee check and maxburnamount is raised — the former is exactly what the pinned parameter forbade, and the latter is something no sanctioned bcli path ever sets. For getutxout (reachable by any `readonly` rune, since it matches `method^get`), vout = "0\nfalse" sets include_mempool=false so the backend reports mempool-spent outputs as unspent; this is a minor information difference only. Injecting too many lines makes bitcoin-cli fail with a parameter-count error, so the attacker cannot change the RPC method (it is on argv) or inject bitcoin-cli options (stdin lines are never option-parsed), which bounds the impact to the trailing optional parameters of these two RPCs. clnrest and cln-grpc re-serialise params (Python json / serde_json escape the newline), so those ingresses are not affected; commando and direct socket callers are. Assumptions: Bitcoin Core `-stdin`/`-stdinrpcpass` semantics as described (27.1 pinned in Dockerfile; bcli requires >= 23.0 at bcli.c:740; maxburnamount exists from 25.0, maxfeerate from 0.19).

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bcli.c:171–183](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L171-L183)
   execute_bitcoin_cli writes the rpcpassword line (when configured), then every stdin arg followed by a single '\n'. An arg that itself contains 0x0A is delivered to bitcoin-cli as two or more lines, i.e. two or more positional arguments. No check or escaping is performed; this is where the fix belongs.
2. [plugins/bcli.c:103–112](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L103-L112)
   gather_argsv puts '-stdin' on the command line and routes every method argument to the stdinargs array (run_bitcoin_cliv always supplies one), so all caller-controlled values travel as newline-delimited stdin lines; only the fixed method literal is on argv.
3. [plugins/bcli.c:640–652](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L640-L652)
   sendrawtransaction takes `tx` with param_string (raw token bytes, no unescaping or hex validation) and passes it as a stdin argument; `allowhighfees` only appends '0' as the second positional (maxfeerate) when true. A `tx` of '<hex>\n0\n<amount>' yields bitcoin-cli `sendrawtransaction <hex> 0 <amount>` regardless of allowhighfees.
4. [plugins/bcli.c:685–691](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L685-L691)
   getutxout passes `txid` and `vout` (param_string, unvalidated) the same way; '0\nfalse' as vout becomes `gettxout <txid> 0 false`, flipping include_mempool. getutxout matches the `method^get` alternative of the built-in `readonly` rune set (lightningd/runes.c readonly_restrictions), so every readonly rune bearer reaches it.
5. [plugins/commando.c:282–303](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L282-L303)
   execute_command forwards each param token to lightningd with json_add_jsonstr (memcpy of json_tok_full), after checkrune has approved the request; raw bytes from the peer's custom message survive unchanged. The incoming message was parsed with json_parse_simple (line 376), which validates UTF-8 only.
6. [lightningd/plugin.c:1187–1211](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1187-L1211)
   json_stream_forward_change_id copies the caller's request bytes to the plugin verbatim (only the id is rewritten), so the raw newline survives from the RPC caller to bcli.
7. [common/json\_param.c:456–462](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_param.c#L456-L462)
   param_string copies the token bytes verbatim (tal_strndup of the token span), so a raw newline byte inside the JSON string reaches bcli unchanged; a JSON-escaped \n would stay two literal characters and not split.
8. [common/json\_parse\_simple.c:353–356](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse_simple.c#L353-L356)
   CLN's post-jsmn validator only checks strings for valid UTF-8 (common/utils.c utf8_check); a raw 0x0A inside a string is valid UTF-8 and is accepted on every JSON-RPC ingress (lightningd socket, commando, libplugin).
9. [lightningd/runes.c:851–915](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L851-L915)
   check_condition evaluates pname/parr restrictions on the individual param tokens: a rune pinning `pnameallowhighfees=false` passes because that token is the literal false; the injected lines ride inside the separate `tx` token, which the rune cannot see as extra bitcoin-cli parameters.

## Impact
Integrity: the operator's rune policy on sendrawtransaction (allowhighfees pinned false) is bypassed and bitcoind's fee/burn sanity limits are disabled for the broadcast through the operator's node; getutxout answers can be skewed by toggling include_mempool. The attacker cannot change the RPC method, inject bitcoin-cli options or reach the password line, so the effect is limited to the trailing optional parameters of these two RPCs. No confidentiality or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a rune holder reaching lightningd over commando (any connected peer presenting a rune) or any other JSON-RPC ingress that preserves raw bytes, whose rune allows bcli's sendrawtransaction (with other parameters constrained) or getutxout (included in every `readonly` rune via method^get). They send a JSON string containing a literal newline; commando, lightningd and bcli accept it unchanged, and bcli writes it as multiple -stdin lines, so bitcoin-cli gets extra positional parameters. No defence to evade; works against default bcli configuration with the pinned Bitcoin Core.

## Recommended fix
Caller-controlled strings are placed into a newline-delimited argument channel (bitcoin-cli -stdin) without ensuring they contain no line terminators, letting one parameter become several and escaping the rune evaluator's per-parameter view. Fix criteria: Each bitcoin-cli argument must map to exactly one stdin line: reject (command_fail) any argument containing '\n' or '\r' before spawning bitcoin-cli, and validate `tx`/`txid` as hex and `vout` as a non-negative integer, formatting them from parsed values as getrawblockbyheight does with param_number. Verify that sendrawtransaction with a tx containing an embedded newline is rejected by bcli and never reaches bitcoin-cli with extra parameters.

# Splice broadcast callback reads freed inflight PSBT after peer-timed splice_locked

## Details
send_splice_tx() (lightningd/channel_control.c:618-647) stores a raw borrowed pointer to inflight->funding_psbt in a `struct send_splice_info` allocated off NULL and completed asynchronously by bcli callbacks (send_splice_tx_done -> optionally check_utxo_block -> handle_tx_broadcast). handle_tx_broadcast() (524-556) then calls json_add_psbt(response, "psbt", info->psbt) to answer the pending splice RPC. Nothing ties the PSBT's lifetime to the pending callback: handle_peer_splice_locked() (1212-1284) calls wallet_channel_clear_inflights() (wallet/wallet.c:1642-1658), which tal_free()s every inflight and with it funding_psbt (a tal child, lightningd/channel.c:217), as soon as channeld reports got_splice_locked. The result is a heap use-after-free read in the lightningd master process whose timing the remote channel peer controls.

Path (remote peer is the splice counterparty; our node initiated the splice via splice_init/splice_update/splice_signed, so a splice_command is pending for the channel and cc != NULL in handle_tx_broadcast):
1. Our channeld must send tx_signatures first. do_i_sign_first() (channeld/channeld.c:3116-3146) makes the side with the smaller sum of input amounts sign first; the shared funding input carries an initiator serial_id (channeld.c:4679, psbt_add_serials(psbt, TX_INITIATOR)), so the initiator's sum includes the channel capacity. The initiator therefore signs first when (a) the peer, as accepter, contributes tx_add_input(s) totalling at least the initiator's inputs plus the channel capacity (accepter inputs are accepted with odd serial_ids, up to 4096, common/interactivetx.c:524-562; the peer gets its coins back in its own tx_add_output), or (b) the operator passed sign_first=true to splice_signed (channel_control.c:2567). In resume_splice_negotiation() (channeld.c:4046-4090) we then send update_inflight and splice_sending_sigs to lightningd (which moves the channel to CHANNELD_AWAITING_SPLICE and starts watch_splice_inflight, channel_control.c:780-818), write tx_signatures to the peer, and block in peer_read() waiting for the peer's tx_signatures.
2. The peer now holds the complete splice tx. It broadcasts it, waits for minimum_depth confirmations, and only then sends tx_signatures immediately followed by splice_locked. Meanwhile lightningd has seen the tx on chain: funding_spent() (lightningd/peer_control.c:2773-2786) just KEEP_WATCHINGs for a known inflight, and splice_found()/splice_depth_cb() (channel_control.c:694-760) queue channeld_funding_depth messages on the pipe to the blocked channeld.
3. channeld completes resume_splice_negotiation and sends channeld_splice_confirmed_signed (channeld.c:4259-4261); lightningd's handle_splice_confirmed_signed() (650-691) hands inflight->funding_psbt to send_splice_tx(), which asks bcli to sendrawtransaction. bitcoind rejects the already-mined tx (RPC error -27); bcli compares WEXITSTATUS() (non-negative, bcli.c:204) against RPC_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_IN_CHAIN == -27 (bcli.c:17, 663-665), so it reports failure and lightningd issues a second asynchronous bcli call, getutxout (597-616).
4. While those two bitcoin-cli subprocess round-trips are in flight, channeld reads the queued funding_depth (handle_funding_depth, channeld.c:6420-6512: sets locked_ready[LOCAL], sends splice_locked) and the peer's splice_locked (locked_ready[REMOTE]); check_mutual_splice_locked() (449-536) sends channeld_got_splice_locked. lightningd's handle_peer_splice_locked() runs update_channel_from_inflight, change_scid and wallet_channel_clear_inflights(): the inflight and its funding_psbt are freed. Nothing in that path resolves the pending splice_signed command (only handle_tx_broadcast/check_utxo_block, or channel_control_errmsg on disconnect, do), so cc is still non-NULL.
5. The getutxout reply arrives (the new funding output exists and is unspent): check_utxo_block() -> handle_tx_broadcast() -> json_add_psbt(response, "psbt", info->psbt) -> fmt_wally_psbt -> wally_psbt_to_base64 (bitcoin/psbt.c:884-895) walks the freed `struct wally_psbt` and its freed input/output arrays: a segfault or assert(ret == WALLY_OK) abort of lightningd (every channel and in-flight HTLC goes down), or heap contents emitted in the RPC reply to the operator.

The race is one the attacker reliably wins: the freeing side is two already-queued local IPC messages, the using side is two bitcoin-cli fork/exec round-trips. The same dangling pointer exists on the success path (one round-trip window) but cannot be exploited there because the splice cannot lock before confirmation. When the peer initiated the splice there is no pending command and info->psbt is not read, so the dangerous case is exactly the one where the operator ran the splice RPCs against the attacker's channel.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:618–647](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L618-L647)
   send_splice_tx() allocates `info` off NULL (so it outlives the channel's inflights) and stores `info->psbt = psbt`, a raw borrowed pointer to inflight->funding_psbt (no clone, no tal_steal), then issues the asynchronous bitcoind_sendrawtx(). Nothing ties the PSBT's lifetime to the pending callback. This is where the fix belongs.
2. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:524–556](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L524-L556)
   handle_tx_broadcast(), run from the bcli reply callbacks, calls json_add_psbt(response, "psbt", info->psbt) whenever a splice RPC command is still pending for the channel; this serialises whatever memory the stale pointer now points at (fmt_wally_psbt -> wally_psbt_to_base64, bitcoin/psbt.c:884-895, which also asserts the wally return code).
3. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1212–1284](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1212-L1284)
   handle_peer_splice_locked(), triggered by channeld's got_splice_locked (which the remote peer's splice_locked completes), ends with wallet_channel_clear_inflights(), tal_free()ing every inflight and therefore inflight->funding_psbt, regardless of whether a send_splice_tx() callback for that inflight is still outstanding; it does not resolve the pending splice command.
4. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:650–691](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L650-L691)
   handle_splice_confirmed_signed() is where the borrowed pointer originates: when the channel is CHANNELD_AWAITING_SPLICE it looks up the pending splice command and hands inflight->funding_psbt to send_splice_tx(). It runs when channeld reports the peer's tx_signatures, which the peer may deliver only after the splice tx is already mined.
5. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:558–616](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L558-L616)
   send_splice_tx_done()/check_utxo_block(): when bitcoind rejects sendrawtransaction (as it does for an already-mined tx), a second asynchronous bcli call (getutxout) is made before handle_tx_broadcast() runs, so the window between taking the pointer and using it spans two bitcoin-cli round-trips; if the output is found, handle_tx_broadcast() reads info->psbt.
6. [wallet/wallet.c:1642–1658](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L1642-L1658)
   wallet_channel_clear_inflights() deletes the DB rows and tal_free()s every inflight in the channel's list; funding_psbt is a tal child of the inflight (lightningd/channel.c:217) and is freed with it.
7. [channeld/channeld.c:4046–4090](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4046-L4090)
   resume_splice_negotiation(): when do_i_sign_first() is true we send update_inflight and splice_sending_sigs to lightningd, write tx_signatures to the peer, and then block in peer_read() waiting for the peer's tx_signatures; the peer therefore holds the fully signed splice tx and controls how long before we learn its signatures. Master messages (funding_depth) queue on the pipe meanwhile.
8. [channeld/channeld.c:3116–3146](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3116-L3146)
   do_i_sign_first(): the side whose inputs sum to less signs first (tie -> initiator). Because the shared funding input is given an initiator serial_id (channeld.c:4679), the initiator's sum includes the channel capacity, so the victim-initiator signs first when the peer contributes inputs totalling at least that, or when the operator sets sign_first. This is the attacker's lever for forcing the ordering in step 1.
9. [common/interactivetx.c:524–562](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/interactivetx.c#L524-L562)
   The remote accepter may add its own inputs to the splice via tx_add_input (odd serial_ids, up to 4096 messages); their amounts are counted on the accepter's side by do_i_sign_first(), letting the peer make the initiator sign first.
10. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:694–731](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L694-L731)
   splice_depth_cb() forwards each confirmation of the inflight to channeld while the channel is CHANNELD_AWAITING_SPLICE (set when we sent our sigs, handle_splice_sending_sigs 780-818), so by the time channeld finishes the delayed tx_signatures exchange a funding_depth message is already queued for it and channeld can immediately lock the splice.
11. [channeld/channeld.c:6420–6512](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6420-L6512)
   handle_funding_depth() for a splicing inflight at depth >= minimum_depth sets locked_ready[LOCAL], sends splice_locked to the peer and calls check_mutual_splice_locked(); with the peer's splice_locked already received, check_mutual_splice_locked() (449-536) sends channeld_got_splice_locked to lightningd, all via local IPC.
12. [plugins/bcli.c:663–665](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bcli.c#L663-L665)
   bcli reports success only if exitstatus == 0 or == RPC_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_IN_CHAIN (-27, bcli.c:17); exitstatus is WEXITSTATUS() (bcli.c:204), i.e. non-negative, so an already-mined splice tx is reported as failure and lightningd takes the longer getutxout path.
13. [lightningd/channel.c:217](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L217)
   new_inflight() makes funding_psbt a tal child of the inflight (tal_steal), so freeing the inflight frees the PSBT that info->psbt still points to.

## Impact
Heap use-after-free read in the lightningd master process: wally_psbt_to_base64 walks the freed `struct wally_psbt` (whose first words glibc overwrites with tcache metadata) and its freed input/output arrays, so lightningd segfaults or trips fmt_wally_psbt's assert(ret == WALLY_OK), taking every channel and in-flight HTLC down with on-chain consequences; or it writes heap contents into the RPC response. The response goes only to the trusted RPC caller, so no attacker-visible confidentiality impact; no integrity impact beyond the crash.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer (the threat model's primary unauthenticated adversary) with whom the victim operator runs a splice via splice_init/splice_update/splice_signed (splicing is on by default). The attacker must make the victim sign first: do_i_sign_first() has the side with the smaller input sum sign first and the shared funding input counts for the initiator, so the peer contributes tx_add_input(s) totalling at least the channel capacity plus the victim's splice-in (its coins return to it in its own output; only capital, not loss) -- or the operator used sign_first=true. The peer then withholds its tx_signatures until the fully-signed splice tx it holds has confirmed, and sends tx_signatures and splice_locked back to back; lightningd's got_splice_locked handling frees the inflight while the splice broadcast is waiting on two bcli round-trips, a race the attacker wins reliably. No security mechanism is bypassed; the peer needs no privileges on the victim's node, and the preconditions (victim-initiated splice with this peer, the attacker's input contribution, staying connected and answering connectd pings) are attack requirements. Assumption: bitcoin-cli (external) exits with abs(rpc_error_code) on an RPC error, so -27 never matches; the dangling pointer is read on the success path too, only with a shorter window.

## Recommended fix
1. send_splice_tx() borrows inflight->funding_psbt by raw pointer into an object whose lifetime is bound to asynchronous bitcoind callbacks, while handle_peer_splice_locked() frees all inflights independently of those callbacks. Fix criteria: The data handed to the splice broadcast callbacks must be owned by (cloned into) the callback context, or the callbacks must re-look-up the inflight/PSBT and tolerate its absence, so that clearing inflights on splice_locked can never leave a dangling pointer. Verify with a test where the peer delays tx_signatures until the splice tx is confirmed and sends splice_locked immediately after: splice_signed must complete (or fail cleanly) with no ASan use-after-free report.
2. The broadcast completion path also assumes the channel's inflight list is unchanged between send_splice_tx() and handle_tx_broadcast(); the splice_command resolution should not depend on inflight memory. Fix criteria: handle_tx_broadcast() answers the pending splice command from data captured at send time (tx bytes, txid, outnum, a cloned PSBT) and never dereferences inflight-owned memory; a splice that locks before the broadcast reply arrives must still produce a well-formed response.
