# psbt_validator keeps raw channel pointer across async getutxout; freed by peer reconnect

## Details
The `struct psbt_validator` used to check that funding inputs are confirmed stores a raw `struct channel *` and drives one asynchronous bitcoind `getutxout` request per input (bcli -> bitcoin-cli, tens to hundreds of ms each). Nothing ties the validator to the channel's or dualopend's lifetime: in handle_validate_inputs it is `tal(NULL, ...)`; in json_openchannel_update it is owned by the RPC command, which is not attached to the channel (open_attempt->cmd) until validation succeeds, so channel_cleanup_commands never fails it. On every re-entry validate_input_unspent dereferences `pv->channel->owner->ld->topology->bitcoind`, and the completion callbacks read `pv->channel->owner` (psbt_request_valid/invalid) or write `pv->channel->open_attempt->cmd` (openchannel_update_valid_psbt).

A remote peer controls both when the validation starts and when the channel dies:

Variant A (dualopend-requested, default config, we open to the peer): we run `fundchannel`/`openchannel_init` to the peer (the spender plugin's multifundchannel drives this automatically). The peer answers open_channel2 with accept_channel2 carrying `require_confirmed_inputs`; dualopend (opener_start, openingd/dualopend.c:3393) sends WIRE_DUALOPEND_VALIDATE_INPUTS for our own inputs and blocks in wire_sync_read. lightningd issues getutxout for our first input. The peer now drops the TCP connection and immediately reconnects: connectd reports peer_connected, lightningd's peer_connected() calls peer_channels_cleanup() synchronously (peer_control.c:1924 -> 185-186): the channel is DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT so channel_unsaved_close_conn -> channel_set_owner(NULL) (kills the blocked dualopend) -> delete_channel -> tal_free(channel). When bcli replies, validate_input_unspent runs on the freed channel: with a second input it dereferences `pv->channel->owner->ld` (owner was NULLed before free -> NULL deref, or a reused chunk -> wild deref); with one input psbt_request_valid reads `pv->channel->owner` and, if non-NULL stale, calls subd_send_msg on it. The inbound mirror (accepter validating the peer's inputs) needs our `require-confirmed-inputs` option but then needs no operator action, and the peer can contribute many inputs to widen the window.

Variant B (RPC path): after openchannel_init returns `requires_confirmed_inputs: true` (peer-set, stored at line 3669), the operator/spender calls openchannel_update; validation starts; the peer simply disconnects. dualopend (in its poll loop) sees EOF and exits; destroy_subd -> dualopen_errmsg -> channel_state_uncommitted -> forget_channel_open -> delete_channel. The pending cmd keeps pv alive; the callback then dereferences the freed channel or, for a saved channel during RBF (owner cleared, open_attempt freed by channel_fail_transient), NULL-derefs `pv->channel->open_attempt->cmd`.

Impact: lightningd crash (every channel offline) and use-after-free reads/writes on freed heap. The disconnect/reconnect timing is attacker-controlled and cheap to retry; getutxout latency (an external bitcoin-cli process per input) gives a comfortable window, but it is still a race.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3055–3105](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3055-L3105)
   validate_input_unspent is the bitcoind getutxout callback. On each re-entry it dereferences pv->channel->owner->ld->topology->bitcoind with no liveness check, and on completion calls pv->success/pv->invalid_input which read pv->channel->owner. pv->channel is a raw pointer captured when validation started; nothing clears it when the channel is freed.
2. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3607–3633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3607-L3633)
   handle_validate_inputs allocates pv with tal(NULL, ...) (no lifetime tie to the channel or dualopend), stores pv->channel = dualopend->channel and starts the asynchronous getutxout chain; the getutxout_call and its jsonrpc_request are tal'd on pv (bitcoind.c:655-661), so freeing the channel does not cancel the pending reply.
3. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3559–3586](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3559-L3586)
   psbt_request_valid / psbt_request_invalid read pv->channel->owner from the (possibly freed) channel; a stale non-NULL value is passed to subd_send_msg.
4. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:3236–3257](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L3236-L3257)
   RPC variant: json_openchannel_update builds the same validator tal'd on the RPC cmd whenever channel->req_confirmed_ins[REMOTE] is set (peer-controlled via DUALOPEND_PSBT_CHANGED at 3669). The cmd is not attached to channel->open_attempt->cmd until openchannel_update_valid_psbt (3107-3115) succeeds, so channel_cleanup_commands cannot fail it when the channel is deleted; the success callback then writes pv->channel->open_attempt->cmd through the dangling pointer.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:3214–3216](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3214-L3216)
   opener_start sets state->require_confirmed_inputs[REMOTE] directly from the peer's accept_channel2 TLV: the remote peer decides whether our dualopend asks lightningd to validate our inputs.
6. [openingd/dualopend.c:3391–3398](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3391-L3398)
   When require_confirmed_inputs[REMOTE] is set, the opener's dualopend calls validate_inputs for OUR inputs (role TX_INITIATOR) before lightningd hears anything about accept_channel2; the channel is still DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT (unsaved).
7. [openingd/dualopend.c:646–673](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L646-L673)
   validate_inputs does wire_sync_write(WIRE_DUALOPEND_VALIDATE_INPUTS) then blocks in wire_sync_read: dualopend cannot observe peer EOF, so the window is closed only by lightningd's reply after bcli answers getutxout.
8. [connectd/connectd.c:319–324](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L319-L324)
   connectd's peer_connected removes any previous connection for the same node id immediately (destroy_peer_immediately(oldpeer)) and at 424 sends connectd_peer_reconnected to lightningd: the attacker can stage a second BOLT8 connection and complete it at a chosen moment.
9. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1919–1925](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1919-L1925)
   handle_peer_connected calls peer_channels_cleanup(peer) synchronously on the (re)connect message, before the peer_connected hook runs.
10. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:163–188](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L163-L188)
   peer_channels_cleanup calls channel_unsaved_close_conn for channels in channel_state_uncommitted state (DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT, channel.h:709-713) and channel_fail_transient (owner cleared, open_attempt freed) for saved ones.
11. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:58–71](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L58-L71)
   channel_unsaved_close_conn: channel_set_owner(channel, NULL) frees the subd (destroy_subd SIGKILLs the dualopend blocked in wire_sync_read; sd->channel is already NULL so no errcb) and then delete_channel frees the channel object while the getutxout reply is still outstanding.
12. [lightningd/channel.c:89–130](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L89-L130)
   delete_channel ends in tal_free(channel); pv->channel now dangles. tal does not poison freed memory in release builds, so the later reads see NULL (owner was cleared) or reused heap.
13. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:4319–4326](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L4319-L4326)
   RPC variant: a plain peer disconnect makes the non-blocked dualopend exit (STATUS_PEER_CONNECTION_LOST, subd.c:525); destroy_subd -> dualopen_errmsg -> channel_state_uncommitted -> forget_channel_open -> delete_channel frees the channel referenced by the pending validator owned by the openchannel_update cmd.

## Impact
NULL/wild dereference or use-after-free in lightningd's main process: crash takes every channel offline (availability HIGH). The RPC-variant success path writes through the dangling pointer (pv->channel->open_attempt->cmd) and may send on a stale subd, so limited heap-integrity impact (LOW). No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any remote Lightning peer we open a dual-funded channel to (or any inbound peer if we run require-confirmed-inputs). The peer sets require_confirmed_inputs in accept_channel2 (dualopend.c:3215), which makes our dualopend block on WIRE_DUALOPEND_VALIDATE_INPUTS while lightningd issues one bitcoind getutxout per input (bcli spawns bitcoin-cli: tens to hundreds of ms). The peer then completes a pre-staged second connection; connectd replaces the old one immediately and lightningd synchronously frees the DUALOPEND_OPEN_INIT channel. The timing is attacker-chosen and the window is wide relative to connectd->lightningd message latency, but it is still a race (AT:P), and it requires the node to run with --experimental-dual-fund (non-default, production code) and, in default config, the operator to have initiated the open to that peer (UI:A). No privileges or runes are needed.

## Recommended fix
psbt_validator holds an unowned channel pointer across asynchronous bitcoind callbacks, and both the channel (delete_channel) and its owner can disappear in between via peer-driven disconnect/reconnect. Fix criteria: A pending input validation must be cancelled or safely abandoned when its channel or dualopend goes away (e.g. make the validator a child of the channel/dualopend or register destructors that NULL pv->channel/owner and fail the RPC), and every callback must check liveness before dereferencing channel or owner. Verify by starting a v2 open whose peer sets require_confirmed_inputs and disconnecting/reconnecting while getutxout is outstanding: lightningd must not crash and the openchannel_update command must fail cleanly.

# handle_splice_abort dereferences absent inflight and restarts channeld after channel_internal_error

## Details
lightningd's containment for a misbehaving channeld is channel_internal_error(): log, fail the channel permanently, release the subdaemon, and return. handle_splice_abort() (channel_control.c:330-403) violates that contract in two ways.

1. If the channeld_splice_abort message carries an outpoint, the handler takes `list_tail(&channel->inflights)` and immediately dereferences `inflight->funding->outpoint` (lines 353-362). If lightningd holds no inflight for the channel (a channeld process that lies about having an inflight, or one whose inflight list diverged from lightningd's), this is a NULL pointer dereference that crashes the whole lightningd process rather than failing one channel.

2. If the outpoint does not match the tail inflight, channel_internal_error() is called (357-366) but the function continues: wallet_inflight_del()/tal_free() remove an inflight that was not the one named, then (383-402) a new socketpair is created and peer_start_channeld() is called. channel_internal_error has by then run channel_fail_permanent (channel.c:1281-1309 -> 1106-1167): the channel is in AWAITING_UNILATERAL with our commitment transaction handed to broadcast_tx. Restarting channeld on that channel hands the peer a live channel daemon (and asks connectd to route the peer's messages to it) for a channel we have already force-closed, and permanently removes the wrong inflight record from the DB.

An honest channeld cannot reach either branch: check_tx_abort()/splice_abort() (channeld.c:1948-2060) only send an outpoint for an inflight they hold, and channeld's inflight list is populated from lightningd (init) or via add_inflight which lightningd records before replying. The attacker position is therefore the threat model's compromised subdaemon (channeld after a peer-side exploit) writing on the master pipe. From that position a single message crashes lightningd (all channels), defeating the containment that channel_internal_error is meant to provide; the second branch additionally leaves inconsistent persisted state. This is the channel_control.c counterpart of the already-recorded compromised-channeld-htlc-reply-double-free (peer_htlcs.c), which documents the same continue-after-channel_internal_error pattern.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:352–402](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L352-L402)
   handle_splice_abort(): when the (optional, channeld-chosen) outpoint is present, `inflight = list_tail(&channel->inflights)` is dereferenced at `inflight->funding->outpoint` with no NULL check (lines 353-362); a channel with no inflight — the common case — makes lightningd SIGSEGV. On an outpoint mismatch channel_internal_error() is called (357-366) but execution continues: wallet_inflight_del()/tal_free() remove the tail inflight (367-368) and lines 383-402 create a socketpair and call peer_start_channeld() on a channel channel_internal_error has just moved to AWAITING_UNILATERAL and dropped to chain. Every other channel_internal_error() in this file is followed by `return`.
2. [lightningd/channel.c:1281–1308](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1281-L1308)
   channel_internal_error() -> channel_fail_permanent(): the channel is failed permanently (owner released, state AWAITING_UNILATERAL, drop_to_chain) and the caller is expected to stop; handle_splice_abort does not.
3. [lightningd/channel.c:1106–1166](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1106-L1166)
   channel_fail_perm() sets AWAITING_UNILATERAL and broadcasts our commitment. Restarting channeld afterwards gives the peer a live channeld (channel_set_owner) for a channel whose commitment we have already published.
4. [channeld/channeld.c:1948–2002](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L1948-L2002)
   check_tx_abort() only sends an outpoint for an inflight it holds (matched by txid), and splice_abort() (2007-2060) only for a non-NULL inflight; an honest channeld's inflight list mirrors lightningd's (init + synchronous add_inflight), so the NULL/mismatch branches are reachable only from a channeld that has been compromised.
5. [lightningd/subd.c:928–936](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L928-L936)
   subd_release_channel() tal_free()s the owning channeld during channel_set_owner(NULL); the design relies on handlers returning after channel_internal_error rather than continuing to act on the channel.

## Impact
lightningd segfaults, taking every channel, HTLC and plugin of the node down (on-chain timeout exposure), where the containment contract would have failed only the one channel the compromised daemon served. In the mismatch branch, peer_start_channeld (1796-1960) performs no state check, so a fresh channeld is attached and connectd routes the peer to it for a channel already in AWAITING_UNILATERAL with our commitment handed to broadcast_tx — a persisted-state inconsistency. Deleting the tail inflight itself is nothing channeld could not already do with a matching outpoint, so integrity impact is limited to the restart-after-force-close.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker already executes code inside a lightning_channeld process (compromised via a peer-message bug) and writes one channeld_splice_abort on the master pipe with the optional inflight_outpoint present (generate-wire.py:462; CSV channeld_wire.csv:302). channel_msg dispatches it to handle_splice_abort with no guard (channel_control.c:1707). If lightningd holds no inflight for that channel (any channel not mid-splice) the NULL dereference kills lightningd; if it holds one, a mismatching outpoint force-closes the channel and then restarts channeld on it. Local pipe only; no race, no user interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. handle_splice_abort trusts that a channeld-supplied outpoint corresponds to an existing tail inflight and dereferences list_tail() without a NULL check. Fix criteria: A splice_abort carrying an outpoint when no inflight exists, or naming an outpoint other than the current inflight, must be treated as a channeld protocol violation: channel_internal_error() and return, with no dereference, no DB deletion and no channeld restart. Verify by feeding such a message from a test channeld and observing a clean channel failure with lightningd still running.
2. After channel_internal_error() the handler keeps acting on the channel (frees an inflight, restarts channeld). Fix criteria: Every channel_internal_error() call in channel_control.c is followed by an immediate return; the channeld restart path is only reached when the abort was validated. Verify that no channeld is spawned for a channel in AWAITING_UNILATERAL.

# createinvoicerequest error message discloses alias payer key for attacker-chosen invreq_metadata

## Details
lightningd/offer.c json_createinvoicerequest (lines 400-414) checks that a non-node-id `invreq_payer_id` equals payer_key(invreq_metadata) = our_pubkey + SHA256(nodealias_base || metadata)*G, where nodealias_base is an hsm_secret-derived secret (hsm_control.c:221-227). On mismatch the JSON-RPC error string embeds fmt_pubkey(&expected), i.e. the correct alias key for the caller-supplied metadata. param_b12_invreq (offer.c:317-339) only requires that invreq_metadata and invreq_payer_id be present; invrequest_decode performs no signature check, so an unsigned lnr1 with arbitrary metadata and any wrong payer_id suffices. The check and the error precede command_check_only (offer.c:418), so `check createinvoicerequest ...` reaches it too, and rune evaluation does not special-case `check` (no handling in runes.c or commando.c).

This makes createinvoicerequest an oracle for the node's BOLT12 payer aliases. fetchinvoice derives every outgoing invoice_request's invreq_payer_id as payer_key(invreq_metadata) (plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1037-1056, 1184-1196) and obtains the signed invreq through this same RPC (fetchinvoice.c:1092-1100); the resulting invreq and the returned invoice carry (invreq_metadata, invreq_payer_id) to the payee. A rune bearer who has captured such artefacts (e.g. a merchant this node paid, who is also a commando peer or clnrest client) submits the observed metadata with a wrong payer_id, reads payer_key(metadata) from the error and compares it to the observed payer_id, confirming this node was the payer. The alias mechanism exists precisely to prevent that linkage.

The gain is real only for a rune that permits createinvoicerequest (or check) but not the methods that already concede the same or more: fetchinvoice with the documented `payer_metadata` parameter returns an invoice echoing payer_key(chosen metadata); makesecret yields nodealias_base itself; payersign signs under payer_key(tweak); listinvoicerequests/listsendpays/listpays reveal payments directly. Local RPC-socket callers and plugins are fully trusted and out of scope. Neither createinvoicerequest nor payersign has a doc/schemas entry, so an operator granting it explicitly is unlikely; the position is narrow and the severity correspondingly low. The fix is to omit the expected key from the error (or emit it only under dev APIs).

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/offer.c:400–414](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L400-L414)
   When invreq_payer_id is not our node id, lightningd derives expected = payer_key(invreq_metadata) and, on mismatch, returns `payer_id did not match invreq_metadata derivation <expected pubkey>` to the RPC caller, revealing the node-secret-derived alias key for caller-chosen metadata. This runs before command_check_only (line 418), so the `check` command reaches it as well.
2. [lightningd/offer.c:341–354](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L341-L354)
   payer_key computes our_pubkey + SHA256(nodealias_base || metadata)*G; nodealias_base is derived from hsm_secret via hsmd (makesecret NODE_ALIAS_BASE_STRING, hsm_control.c:221-227) and is what makes the alias unlinkable to the node id for third parties.
3. [lightningd/offer.c:317–338](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/offer.c#L317-L338)
   param_b12_invreq only requires invreq_metadata and invreq_payer_id to be present; invrequest_decode does not verify a signature, so an attacker-authored unsigned lnr1 with arbitrary metadata and a deliberately wrong payer_id is accepted up to the derivation check.
4. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1037–1056](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L1037-L1056)
   fetchinvoice sets invreq_metadata (random, or caller-supplied payer_metadata) and derives invreq_payer_id = payer_key(invreq_metadata) with the same nodealias_base; these two fields travel to the payee in the invoice_request and are echoed in the invoice, so an observer holding them can use the oracle to confirm this node as payer.
5. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1092–1099](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L1092-L1099)
   fetchinvoice obtains the signed invoice_request through this same createinvoicerequest RPC (savetodb=false), confirming the alias derivation the oracle reveals is the one used for every outgoing BOLT12 payment.

## Impact
Discloses node-secret-derived alias public keys for attacker-chosen metadata, letting a rune bearer who also holds captured invoice_requests or invoices confirm that this node made specific BOLT12 payments, defeating the payer-alias unlinkability. Does not reveal nodealias_base or any private key and allows no signing; no integrity or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a rune bearer reaching lightningd over the network via commando (as a connected peer) or clnrest, whose rune permits createinvoicerequest or check but not fetchinvoice/makesecret/payersign/list* (otherwise sanctioned paths already reveal the same or more). They encode an unsigned lnr1 with the observed invreq_metadata and any payer_id other than the derived one, call createinvoicerequest savetodb=false (or check createinvoicerequest), and parse the pubkey out of the error message, which commando (commando.c:523-549) and clnrest (structs.rs:38-53) relay verbatim. One call per metadata value; deterministic; no user interaction; no race or deployment condition beyond the rune itself.

## Recommended fix
The payer_id/metadata consistency error echoes the secret-derived expected alias key to the caller. Fix criteria: The error returned for a payer_id mismatch must not include the derived key (at most behind command_dev_apis). After the fix a caller supplying arbitrary invreq_metadata learns only that the payer_id did not match.

# connect_activate_subd dereferences NULL channel->scid when replaying a canned error for an unconfirmed (CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN) channel on peer reconnect

## Details
connect_activate_subd() (lightningd/peer_control.c:1437-1541) runs from peer_connected_hook_final() for every channel in a channel_state_wants_peercomms() state with no owner (1604-1617). If channel->error is set it jumps straight to send_error (1444-1447), which, to make LND unilaterally close, evaluates `is_stub_scid(*channel->scid)` (1511) with no NULL check. channel->scid is NULL for every channel whose funding has not been seen on-chain (channel.c:379, set only via channel_set_scid/lockin), so for a CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN channel this is a NULL-pointer dereference and lightningd dies with SIGSEGV. The sibling uses at 2834 and 2859 guard the same call with `channel->scid &&`.

Reaching the crashing configuration (CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, channel->error set, owner NULL):
1. The operator funds a channel with the attacker via fundchannel_start/fundchannel_complete (external-wallet flow); the channel is CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN with funding not yet broadcast (opener LOCAL). This is the normal, documented flow.
2. The attacker disconnects and reconnects. connect_activate_subd restarts channeld with reconnected=true (1495-1498); channeld sends its channel_reestablish and then blocks synchronously in peer_read() waiting for the peer's (channeld/channeld.c:6030-6043), never servicing master-fd messages. The attacker simply withholds channel_reestablish (connectd answers pings itself), so the channel appears connected but stuck for as long as the attacker likes.
3. The operator runs fundchannel_cancel — the documented way to abort a committed-but-unbroadcast open, and the natural reaction to a stuck open. json_fundchannel_cancel (opening_control.c:1197-1198) → cancel_channel_before_broadcast (channel_control.c:2257-2300: state CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, opener LOCAL, funding not in wallet txs) → forget_channel (1511-1520), which sets channel->error and, because channel->owner is set, sends channeld_send_error to channeld and relies on channeld's send_error_reply to delete the channel (handle_error_channel → forget). channeld is blocked in step 2 and never processes it.
4. The attacker disconnects. channeld's peer_read fails → peer_failed_connection_lost → lightningd subd.c:525-529 closes the subd → destroy_subd calls channel_errmsg with peer_fd NULL (subd.c:650-659) → channel_fail_transient (peer_control.c:641-647) → channel_err (channel.c:1326-1349) clears the owner but leaves state CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN and channel->error set. channel_cleanup_commands (channel.c:1250-1279) does not touch channel->forgets, so nothing deletes the channel.
5. The attacker reconnects (or lightningd auto-reconnects to a peer it has a channel with): peer_connected_hook_final iterates the channel (wants_peercomms(CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN) is true, channel.h:733-752), connect_activate_subd sees channel->error, and line 1511 dereferences the NULL scid. Deterministic SIGSEGV of lightningd.

Without step 2 the same outcome needs the peer's disconnect to land in the few-ms window between lightningd queuing channeld_send_error and channeld processing it; the reestablish stall turns that race into a window the peer controls. channel->error is not persisted (comment at 1458), so after restart the channel is back to plain CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN and the sequence can be repeated. The same dereference is also reached from the sockpair() failure branch (1468-1470, 1485-1487) for any unconfirmed channel when socketpair() fails (fd exhaustion), where the generated warning goes through the same send_error label.

Routes checked and excluded: AWAITING_UNILATERAL is not wants_peercomms (channel.h:745), so ordinary force-closes of unconfirmed channels never enter connect_activate_subd; withheld channels are deleted by drop_to_chain (peer_control.c:372-413); a DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED permanent failure moves to AWAITING_UNILATERAL (channel.c:1130-1136).

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1503–1531](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1503-L1531)
   send_error label: `is_stub_scid(*channel->scid)` at 1511 with no NULL check; channel->scid is NULL for any channel whose funding has not been seen on-chain. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1443–1447](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1443-L1447)
   The send_error path is entered whenever channel->error is already set, before the state switch, so a CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN channel with a canned error reaches it.
3. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1603–1617](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1603-L1617)
   peer_connected_hook_final calls connect_activate_subd on every (re)connect for each ownerless channel in a wants_peercomms state, which includes CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN (channel.h:733-752).
4. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1511–1520](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1511-L1520)
   forget_channel (fundchannel_cancel after fundchannel_complete) sets channel->error while the channel is CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN and, if channeld owns it, merely asks channeld to deliver the error, relying on channeld's reply to delete the channel.
5. [channeld/channeld.c:6030–6043](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L6030-L6043)
   On a reconnect channeld blocks synchronously in peer_read() until the peer sends channel_reestablish, without servicing master-fd messages; a peer that withholds channel_reestablish keeps channeld from ever processing channeld_send_error, so the operator's cancel leaves channel->error set with the channel still owned.
6. [lightningd/subd.c:650–658](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L650-L658)
   When channeld dies (peer connection lost), destroy_subd invokes the channel's errcb (channel_errmsg) with peer_fd NULL.
7. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:641–647](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L641-L647)
   channel_errmsg with NULL peer_fd only calls channel_fail_transient: state stays CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN, owner is cleared, channel->error remains set and channel->forgets is never resolved.
8. [lightningd/channel.c:1326–1349](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1326-L1349)
   channel_err clears the owner but leaves state and channel->error untouched, so the channel reaches the next reconnect in exactly the crashing configuration.
9. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2257–2300](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2257-L2300)
   cancel_channel_before_broadcast: the documented fundchannel_cancel path for a committed-but-unbroadcast CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN channel we opened; no condition prevents it while channeld is stalled waiting for the peer's channel_reestablish.
10. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2833–2835](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2833-L2835)
   Sibling code guards the same call with `!channel->scid ||` (also 2859), showing the missing check at 1511 is an oversight.

## Impact
lightningd segfaults, taking down every subdaemon and in-flight HTLC handling until restarted; channel->error is not persisted so each occurrence is a one-shot outage rather than a crash loop, but the sequence can be repeated after restart while the channel remains unbroadcast.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote peer the victim opens a channel to. Requires the operator to run the documented fundchannel_cancel on a committed-but-unbroadcast channel while the peer is connected (AT:P, UI:A); the peer makes that likely and removes the timing race by reconnecting and withholding channel_reestablish, which stalls channeld (channeld.c:6037-6043) so the cancel can never complete, then disconnecting and reconnecting. No authentication beyond the Noise handshake; the crashing configuration is then deterministic. A minor secondary path is socketpair() failure on reconnect for any unconfirmed channel.

## Recommended fix
1. connect_activate_subd's send_error label dereferences channel->scid without a NULL check, although channels in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN (and the dualopend pre-lockin states) can reach it with scid unset via channel->error or a sockpair() failure. Fix criteria: The stub-scid special case must only run when channel->scid is non-NULL (as at 2834/2859); for an unconfirmed channel with no scid the error is simply sent and the peer disconnected without crashing.
2. forget_channel relies on channeld delivering the error and replying; if channeld dies first, channel_fail_transient leaves a CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN channel with channel->error set, no owner and unresolved channel->forgets, so it is re-activated on reconnect instead of being forgotten. Fix criteria: A channel left ownerless in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN with a pending cancel (channel->forgets non-empty / channel->error set by forget_channel) must be forgotten (and its fundchannel_cancel commands answered) when channeld exits, rather than waiting for the next reconnect. Verify: fundchannel_complete, reconnect the peer and withhold channel_reestablish, run fundchannel_cancel, disconnect and reconnect the peer; lightningd must not crash and the channel must be gone.

# Simple close stores peer-built closee tx with any locktime/fee as last_tx, discarding commitment and locking funds

## Details
With option_simple_close negotiated (--experimental-simple-close), the closee side of the protocol (closingd/simpleclosed.c handle_closing_complete) rebuilds the closer's proposed closing transaction from the peer's closing_complete fields - closer_scriptpubkey, fee_satoshis and locktime - signs it, sends closing_sig, and reports it to lightningd with simpleclosed_closee_broadcast. lightningd (simple_close_control.c handle_simpleclosed_closee_broadcast) validates only close_tx_check (1 input spending our funding, outputs to known scripts, and a commitment-shape heuristic that cannot fire because the simple close sequence is 0xFFFFFFFD) and the peer's signature, then calls channel_set_last_tx() and persists it. channel->last_tx is the transaction lightningd broadcasts for every close, cooperative or forced (peer_control.c drop_to_chain -> sign_and_send_last), and the commitment transaction it previously held is freed.

Signing the peer's variant is harmless per the BOLT design, because each side is only supposed to rely on its own closer transaction. CLN, however, adopts the peer's transaction as its own last-resort transaction without checking it is minable: locktime is unbounded (0xFFFFFFFF is a timestamp in 2106; 0x1FFFFFFF is block 536M), fee_satoshis may be 0, and fee_satoshis == closer balance yields a zero-value non-OP_RETURN output that bitcoind rejects as dust.

Attack: a peer with a channel to the victim (either side may send shutdown) sends closing_complete with closer_scriptpubkey equal to its shutdown script, locktime = 0xFFFFFFFF (or fee 0). The victim signs, replies, and lightningd overwrites last_tx (and the DB row) with this never-minable transaction. Variant A: the peer never sends closing_sig for the victim's own closing_complete; the channel stays in CLOSINGD_SIGEXCHANGE and any force close (`close` unilateraltimeout -> channel_fail_permanent -> drop_to_chain(false), or any channel error) broadcasts the dud; bitcoind rejects it as non-final and commit_tx_send_finished retries forever. Variant B: the peer first sends a valid closing_sig (lightningd stores the victim's good closer tx), then the poisoned closing_complete (overwriting it); simpleclosed_complete moves the channel to CLOSINGD_COMPLETE and drop_to_chain broadcasts the dud. In CLOSINGD_COMPLETE/AWAITING_UNILATERAL no RPC can renegotiate or regenerate the commitment; restart (resend_closing_transactions) rebroadcasts the same tx. The peer still holds its own commitment transaction and can close whenever it likes; the victim cannot. The victim's channel funds are therefore locked indefinitely at the attacker's discretion (no theft: the eventual split is correct). The legacy closingd path is not affected because lightningd stores a tx built by its own closingd (locktime 0, fee bounded by closing_fee_is_acceptable).

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/simple\_close\_control.c:165–208](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/simple_close_control.c#L165-L208)
   handle_simpleclosed_closee_broadcast takes the tx that the peer's closing_complete described, runs only close_tx_check and a remote-signature check, then unconditionally channel_set_last_tx() + wallet_channel_save(). This replaces channel->last_tx and last_sig (the commitment transaction with the peer's signature, or the node's own fully-signed closer tx stored by handle_simpleclosed_got_sig) with a transaction whose locktime, fee and closer-output value were chosen by the remote peer.
2. [lightningd/simple\_close\_control.c:41–113](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/simple_close_control.c#L41-L113)
   close_tx_check is the only validation of the stored tx: input count/outpoint, output scripts, and a shape heuristic that rejects only when BOTH locktime>>24==0x20 AND sequence>>24==0x80. The simple close tx always has sequence 0xFFFFFFFD, so any locktime (including 0xFFFFFFFF, a year-2106 timestamp) passes. No finality, minimum-fee or dust check.
3. [closingd/simpleclosed.c:329–335](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/closingd/simpleclosed.c#L329-L335)
   handle_closing_complete parses locktime (u32) and fee_sat (u64) straight from the remote peer's closing_complete; locktime is never bounded anywhere in the daemon or in lightningd.
4. [closingd/simpleclosed.c:379–389](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/closingd/simpleclosed.c#L379-L389)
   fee_sat is only required to be <= the closer's balance. fee_sat == 0 (unrelayable) and fee_sat == remote_sat (zero-value non-OP_RETURN closer output, rejected as dust) are both accepted.
5. [closingd/simpleclosed.c:415–467](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/closingd/simpleclosed.c#L415-L467)
   The chosen variant is built via make_close_tx with the peer's locktime and amounts, signed by hsmd, closing_sig is sent, and then the tx plus the peer's signature are handed to lightningd via simpleclosed_closee_broadcast, where it becomes last_tx.
6. [closingd/simpleclosed.c:660–692](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/closingd/simpleclosed.c#L660-L692)
   The exchange loop exits only once both the peer's closing_complete and the closing_sig for our own closing_complete have arrived, and the peer chooses the order. Sending closing_sig first then closing_complete makes the poisoned closee tx the last one stored before simpleclosed_complete triggers drop_to_chain; withholding closing_sig leaves the channel in CLOSINGD_SIGEXCHANGE with the poisoned last_tx. The project's own test (tests/test_closing.py test_simple_close_closee_path) assumes closee_broadcast always precedes got_sig, an ordering only the peer controls.
7. [common/close\_tx.c:129–136](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/close_tx.c#L129-L136)
   create_simple_close_tx sets nLockTime to the caller-supplied value and nSequence to 0xFFFFFFFD, so nLockTime is consensus-enforced: a future height/time locktime cannot be mined until then and bitcoind rejects it as non-final.
8. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:496–513](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L496-L513)
   drop_to_chain, for both cooperative and force (cooperative=false) closes, signs and broadcasts channel->last_tx via sign_and_send_last. Once last_tx is the peer's unminable tx, every exit path (simpleclosed_complete, close-timeout -> channel_fail_permanent -> channel_fail_perm -> drop_to_chain(false) at channel.c:1164, channel_internal_error, resend_closing_transactions on restart) broadcasts the dud and the funding output is never spent by this node.
9. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:295–314](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L295-L314)
   commit_tx_send_finished returns false while the tx is unconfirmed, so chaintopology keeps it in outgoing_txs and rebroadcasts the same rejected tx on every block; there is no fallback to a different transaction.
10. [lightningd/channel.c:978–985](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L978-L985)
   channel_set_last_tx overwrites last_sig and frees the previous last_tx: the commitment transaction and the peer's signature on it (the node's only unilateral exit) are not retained anywhere else and are overwritten in the DB by wallet_channel_save (wallet.c binds last_tx/last_sig).
11. [lightningd/closing\_control.c:128–136](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/closing_control.c#L128-L136)
   The operator's recovery attempt, `close` with unilateraltimeout, ends in channel_fail_permanent, which drops the same poisoned last_tx to chain; in CLOSINGD_COMPLETE `close` is refused outright (channel_state_can_close), and reconnect only re-enters channeld/simpleclosed, which refresh last_tx solely on peer-authored commitment_signed or closing_sig.
12. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1869–1876](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1869-L1876)
   handle_sign_commitment_tx, used by sign_last_tx at broadcast time, checks only 1 input and >0 outputs, so hsmd signs the unminable tx without objection.
13. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1450–1463](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1450-L1463)
   simpleclosed is used whenever OPT_SIMPLE_CLOSE is negotiated; CLN only advertises it with --experimental-simple-close (options.c:1510, documented in doc/lightningd-config.5.md), so the path is reachable only on nodes that enabled that option (AT:P).

## Impact
The node's commitment transaction (and, in variant B, its own fully-signed mutual close) is discarded from memory and DB and replaced by an unminable transaction: persistent corruption of the channel record (I:L). Every close path then broadcasts a tx bitcoind rejects, and no RPC can recover, so the channel's funds are unavailable until the attacker chooses to spend the funding output (A:H). No secrets are exposed and the eventual balance split is unchanged (C:N).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer with an open channel to the victim (PR:L; it may open the channel itself). The victim must run with --experimental-simple-close and the peer advertises the feature too (AT:PRESENT - non-default option). The attacker sends shutdown, then one closing_complete with its own shutdown script, any fee <= its balance and locktime 0xFFFFFFFF (optionally after a valid closing_sig to reach CLOSINGD_COMPLETE). All messages are well-formed and signed by the attacker; nothing must be bypassed (AC:L). No user interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. lightningd adopts the peer-constructed closee transaction as channel->last_tx - the transaction it relies on for cooperative and forced closes - discarding its commitment transaction, even though the simple-close protocol only guarantees that the node's OWN closer transaction is one it should rely on. Fix criteria: The commitment transaction (or the node's own fully-signed closer tx) must remain available for drop_to_chain regardless of what closing_complete the peer sends; a peer's closee tx must never displace it. Verify: after receiving a closing_complete with locktime 0xFFFFFFFF or fee 0, a forced close still broadcasts a minable commitment (or own closer) transaction.
2. Neither simpleclosed (handle_closing_complete) nor lightningd (close_tx_check) validates that the peer's proposed closing transaction is final and standard: locktime is unbounded, fee may be zero, and the closer output may be below dust / zero-valued. Fix criteria: Before storing or broadcasting a peer-proposed closing tx, require locktime <= current block height (per BOLT 2 'current block height or a bit earlier'), a fee at or above the node's minimum feerate, and no non-OP_RETURN output below the dust limit; reject otherwise with a warning. Verify that a closing_complete with locktime 0xFFFFFFFF or a zero-value closer output is refused and not persisted.

# Subdaemon-supplied tx/PSBT in hsmd sign handlers reaches assert/abort, killing hsmd and lightningd

## Details
hsmd's threat model (hsmd.c header, hsmd_wire.csv line 1) is that a subdaemon holding a client fd may be faulty or hostile: a malformed request is reported to lightningd and the offending client connection is closed, while hsmd itself must keep running because lightningd treats hsmd's death as fatal (new_global_subd must_not_exit; hsm_sync_req fatal on EOF). The transaction-signing handlers break that contract.

Every sign_* handler parses a client-supplied `bitcoin_tx` via fromwire_bitcoin_tx(), which deserialises the raw tx and an accompanying PSBT independently and performs no consistency check. The handlers then call sign_tx_input() -> bitcoin_tx_hash_for_sig() -> psbt_input_get_amount(tx->psbt, in), which `assert(in < psbt->num_inputs)` and `abort()`s when the selected PSBT input has neither witness_utxo nor non_witness_utxo; bitcoin_tx_hash_for_sig also asserts the libwally sighash call succeeded. Three client-controlled ways reach those aborts:

1. handle_sign_splice_tx passes the message's u32 input_index to sign_tx_input with no bounds check at all (contrast do_sign_local_htlc_tx and handle_sign_to_us_tx, which check input_num < num_inputs). input_index = 0xffffffff trips the assert.
2. handle_sign_mutual_close_tx and handle_sign_remote_htlc_tx sign input 0 without checking the tx has any input; a PSBT with zero inputs (or whose input 0 lacks utxo data) aborts.
3. All handlers, including those that do check tx->wtx->num_inputs (sign_remote_commitment_tx, handle_sign_to_us_tx), accept a well-formed raw tx paired with a PSBT whose matching input simply omits witness_utxo/non_witness_utxo (valid PSBT encoding, accepted by psbt_from_bytes with flags 0). psbt_input_get_amount then abort()s.

The attacker is a compromised per-channel subdaemon (threat-model adversary 6: channeld after a peer exploit, or openingd/dualopend/closingd/onchaind), which lightningd grants SIGN_REMOTE_TX / SIGN_CLOSING_TX / SIGN_SPLICE_TX / SIGN_ONCHAIN_TX. Any of these capability bits suffices; no MASTER capability is needed. A single crafted request deterministically aborts hsmd (asserts are compiled in), after which lightningd exits (`errx(1, "lightning_hsmd failed")` or `fatal("EOF reading from HSM")`), taking every channel offline. This escalates a per-channel compromise, which lightningd otherwise contains (a dying channeld only affects its own channel), into a whole-node outage, with the usual on-chain consequences of a node that cannot respond to HTLC deadlines while down. The ledger item l-e3-07 identified the splice/mutual-close/remote-htlc index paths; this record adds the PSBT-content path that defeats the existing num_inputs checks in the other handlers.

## Evidence
1. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1447–1479](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1447-L1479)
   handle_sign_splice_tx (HSM_PERM_SIGN_SPLICE_TX, granted to channeld) takes the u32 input_index straight from the client message (hsmd_wire.csv:337) and passes it to sign_tx_input() with no comparison against tx->wtx->num_inputs or tx->psbt->num_inputs; contrast handle_sign_to_us_tx:655 and do_sign_local_htlc_tx which do bound input_num.
2. [bitcoin/psbt.c:597–615](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/psbt.c#L597-L615)
   psbt_input_get_amount() is the sink: assert(in < psbt->num_inputs) aborts on an out-of-range index, and when the selected PSBT input carries neither witness_utxo nor non_witness_utxo (utxo) it falls into abort(). Both the index and the PSBT bytes are client-supplied.
3. [bitcoin/signature.c:120–151](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/signature.c#L120-L151)
   bitcoin_tx_hash_for_sig() (called by sign_tx_input at 153-170) calls psbt_input_get_amount(tx->psbt, in) unconditionally before hashing, so every sign handler reaches the assert/abort for a bad index or a utxo-less PSBT input.
4. [bitcoin/tx.c:760–776](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/tx.c#L760-L776)
   fromwire_bitcoin_tx() parses the raw tx (pull_bitcoin_tx_only) and the PSBT (fromwire_wally_psbt -> psbt_from_bytes, wally flags 0, psbt.c:927-941/964-983) independently and never checks that psbt->num_inputs matches wtx->num_inputs or that inputs carry utxo data, so a client controls both halves separately.
5. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1412–1444](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1412-L1444)
   handle_sign_mutual_close_tx (HSM_PERM_SIGN_CLOSING_TX: closingd and channeld) signs input 0 with no check that the tx or its PSBT has any input and never inspects the PSBT utxo fields.
6. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1584–1633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1584-L1633)
   handle_sign_remote_htlc_tx (HSM_PERM_SIGN_REMOTE_TX: channeld/openingd/dualopend) signs input 0 with no input-count or PSBT check.
7. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1643–1691](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1643-L1691)
   handle_sign_remote_commitment_tx checks tx->wtx->num_inputs == 1 but the PSBT parsed alongside is unchecked: a PSBT with zero inputs or whose input 0 lacks witness_utxo/non_witness_utxo still reaches abort() in psbt_input_get_amount.
8. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:645–671](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L645-L671)
   handle_sign_to_us_tx (HSM_PERM_SIGN_ONCHAIN_TX: onchaind and channeld) bounds input_num against tx->wtx->num_inputs only; the PSBT side is not validated, so the same abort() is reachable with a utxo-less PSBT input.
9. [hsmd/hsmd\_wire.csv:1](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/hsmd_wire.csv#L1)
   The protocol file states the intended contract: a bad client request is reported via hsmstatus_client_bad_request and is 'not the HSM's decision to crash'. hsmd/test/run-bad-request-close.c tests that a rejected request closes only the offending client.
10. [hsmd/hsmd.c:837–840](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/hsmd.c#L837-L840)
   The sanctioned path for a hostile client: hsmd_handle_client_message returns NULL and handle_client io_close()s only that client's connection; hsmd keeps serving lightningd and the other channels.
11. [lightningd/hsm\_control.c:56–70](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/hsm_control.c#L56-L70)
   lightningd's reaction to a reported bad client request is log_broken() and return 0, so the sanctioned outcome of a hostile subdaemon request is one closed client fd and a BROKEN log line; the assert/abort path instead kills hsmd.
12. [lightningd/subd.c:663–668](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L663-L668)
   hsmd is created with new_global_subd (must_not_exit = true, subd.c:811); destroy_subd therefore errx(1)s lightningd when hsmd dies. hsm_sync_req (hsm_control.c:308-317) additionally fatal()s on EOF from hsmd. A channeld death, by contrast, reaches channel_errmsg with peer_fd NULL -> channel_fail_transient (peer_control.c:641-646), i.e. one channel offline.
13. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1817–1825](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1817-L1825)
   channeld is granted SIGN_REMOTE_TX, SIGN_ONCHAIN_TX, SIGN_CLOSING_TX and SIGN_SPLICE_TX, so every affected handler is reachable from a compromised channeld; closing_control.c:474-476, onchain_control.c:1833-1836, opening_control.c:982-984 and dual_open_control.c:4475-4479 grant the corresponding subsets to closingd, onchaind, openingd and dualopend.

## Impact
Availability HIGH: hsmd aborts and lightningd exits, so the whole node (all channels, RPC, plugins) is down until manually restarted, and the compromised daemon can re-trigger it on every restart while it is re-spawned, with the usual on-chain consequences of a node unable to meet HTLC deadlines. No key material is disclosed and no signature over attacker content is produced on this path, so confidentiality and integrity are unaffected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker position: code execution inside any per-channel subdaemon that holds an hsmd client fd with a signing capability (channeld, openingd, dualopend, closingd, onchaind) - threat-model adversary 6, e.g. channeld after a remote peer exploit. Delivery: one hsmd_sign_splice_tx whose u32 input_index >= the PSBT's input count (no bounds check at libhsmd.c:1472), or any hsmd_sign_* message whose raw tx is well-formed but whose PSBT input lacks witness_utxo/non_witness_utxo. hsmd parses it (fromwire_bitcoin_tx, no cross-check), reaches psbt_input_get_amount and hits assert()/abort() deterministically; asserts are compiled in (no NDEBUG). Assumption: libwally-core at the external/libwally-core submodule pin accepts, with wally_psbt_from_bytes flags 0, a PSBT input carrying neither UTXO field, as BIP174 makes both optional; the splice index path does not depend on this assumption. What the position gains: the sanctioned outcome of a hostile client request is hsmd closing that one client fd (hsmd.c:840) and lightningd logging BROKEN (hsm_control.c:67-70), after which only that channel fails transiently; this path instead kills hsmd, which new_global_subd marks must_not_exit, so lightningd errx()s (subd.c:663-669). No race, no non-default configuration, no user action.

## Recommended fix
1. hsmd sign handlers forward a client-supplied input index and PSBT to bitcoin_tx_hash_for_sig/psbt_input_get_amount, whose failure mode is assert/abort, so a hostile client crashes the signer instead of being rejected. Fix criteria: Before signing, every handler that reaches sign_tx_input must verify input_index < tx->wtx->num_inputs, tx->psbt->num_inputs == tx->wtx->num_inputs, and that the selected PSBT input carries witness_utxo or non_witness_utxo (or derive the amount from a trusted source), returning hsmd_status_bad_request on failure. Verify by sending hsmd_sign_splice_tx with input_index 0xffffffff and hsmd_sign_remote_commitment_tx with a utxo-less PSBT input from a client fd: hsmd must log a bad request and close that client, and lightningd must stay up.
2. fromwire_bitcoin_tx accepts a raw tx and PSBT that disagree, and psbt_input_get_amount aborts rather than failing, so untrusted wire input can reach process-terminating paths in shared library code. Fix criteria: fromwire_bitcoin_tx (or a hsmd-side check) rejects transactions whose PSBT input count differs from the raw tx or whose inputs lack utxo data when the caller is untrusted; psbt_input_get_amount should be given a failing variant for untrusted callers so no client-reachable path ends in abort().

# Recurrence period index aliasing via u32 truncation lets payer bypass period-window checks

## Details
BOLT12 recurrence handling in the `offers` plugin's invoice_request hook must 'reject the invoice request for a period which has already passed' or 'whose immediate predecessor has not yet begun'. check_period() (plugins/offers_invreq_hook.c:465-594) implements this with offer_period_paywindow(), which calls offer_period_start(basetime, n, recurrence) (common/bolt12.c:475-492). For day- and month-based recurrences that function computes `recur->period * n` (u32 * size_t = u64) and passes it to `time_change(u64, u32 number, ...)` (line 449): the product is narrowed to 32 bits, and add_days()/add_months() then do `tm_mday += number` / `tm_mon += number` (int += u32), so the effective offset is (int)(uint32_t)(period * n) days or months rather than period * n.

The payer controls n: period_idx = invreq_recurrence_counter + invreq_recurrence_start (both tu32, lines 486/502). When our offer carries `offer_recurrence_base` (the configuration that makes `invreq_recurrence_start` mandatory), start is an arbitrary u32, and the only bound is `offer_recurrence_limit`, which is optional. The offer_* fields in the invreq are bound to our stored offer by the offer_id hash lookup (listoffers_done), so period/time_unit/basetime are ours, but the index is the payer's. Since period_idx reaches 2^33-2, the payer can pick an index with period*idx ≡ period*k (mod 2^32) for any small k, or ≡ a small negative multiple of period, so offer_period_start(idx-1), (idx), (idx+1) land on a window around now and the 'too early'/'too late' checks pass for an index the real timeline would reject (e.g. 2-monthly offer, start = 2^31: idx*2 = 2^32 → 0 months).

Two consequences. (1) Integrity of subscription records: lightningd signs and stores an invoice whose invreq_recurrence_start/counter denote a period index 2^31..2^33 (hundreds of millions of years out), which the spec-mandated window validation should have rejected; the paid chain can then continue from that bogus index. (2) Price bypass when `offer_recurrence_base.basetime` is in the future (the documented 'when the first period begins' use) and `proportional_amount` is set: legitimate payers can only request period 0 at full price (now < start, so no scaling), but an aliased index with effective offset -period gives start = B-period < now < end = B, so lines 559-587 scale the amount by (B-now)/period — down to the 1 msat floor just before B. With basetime at or before now, aliasing reproduces the legitimate current/next window and price, so only the recorded index is wrong. No memory-safety consequence: the int wrap is implementation-defined narrowing, mktime() normalises the resulting small tm offsets, and basetime on this path is always ours.

## Evidence
1. [common/bolt12.c:475–491](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L475-L491)
   offer_period_start() computes `recur->period * n` as size_t and passes it to time_change(), whose parameter is `u32 number`: the product is silently truncated modulo 2^32 for time_unit 1 (days) and 2 (months).
2. [common/bolt12.c:439–449](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L439-L449)
   time_change() takes `u32 number` (line 449), so the u64 product from offer_period_start() is truncated modulo 2^32 at the call; add_days()/add_months() then do `tm_mday += number` / `tm_mon += number` (int += u32), so truncated values above INT_MAX become negative offsets. The effective offset is (int)(u32)(period*n) units, and mktime() normalises the small resulting tm field changes normally.
3. [plugins/offers\_invreq\_hook.c:486–546](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_invreq_hook.c#L486-L546)
   period_idx is the payer's invreq_recurrence_counter plus (when our offer has offer_recurrence_base) the payer's arbitrary u32 invreq_recurrence_start; it is bounded only by offer_recurrence_limit if the operator set one, then used for the paywindow 'too early'/'too late' checks that are supposed to reject periods not currently payable.
4. [plugins/offers\_invreq\_hook.c:559–586](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers_invreq_hook.c#L559-L586)
   With proportional_amount, the invoice amount is scaled by the aliased window, so the payer also controls the fraction paid for the bogus period.
5. [common/bolt12.c:523–541](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L523-L541)
   offer_period_paywindow() derives start/end from offer_period_start(period_idx-1) and offer_period_start(period_idx+1); with aliasing these collapse onto the current window for a far-future period_idx.

## Impact
The merchant node issues and persists paid recurring invoices for period indices the protocol check should have rejected, and, when basetime is in the future with proportional_amount, at a proportionally reduced price (down to 1 msat) that no legitimate index can obtain. This corrupts subscription state and undercuts the offer's price for one pseudo-period, but exposes no data and crashes nothing: limited, bounded integrity loss.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote payer able to deliver an onion-message invoice_request to a node that published a recurring offer with recurrence_base, day/week/month units and no tight recurrence_limit (operator's product configuration, hence AT:PRESENT). They sign an invreq with their own payer key choosing invreq_recurrence_start/counter so that period*idx wraps modulo 2^32 onto the present (or, with a future basetime, a pre-basetime) window; the hook passes check_period() and lightningd signs and stores the invoice. No victim interaction, no privileges.

## Recommended fix
1. offer_period_start()/time_change() narrow period*n to u32 and then to int, so large period indices alias onto small or negative offsets instead of being treated as out of range. Fix criteria: Period arithmetic must be performed in 64-bit without truncation and must fail (return an explicit error) when the offset cannot be represented; for any period_idx whose true start is beyond representable time, check_period() must reject the request. A test with invreq_recurrence_start near 2^31/2^32 on day/month offers must be rejected as 'too early'.
2. check_period() accepts an unbounded payer-supplied invreq_recurrence_start when no offer_recurrence_limit is configured. Fix criteria: The hook must bound period_idx to a sane maximum (or require the computed period start to lie within a bounded distance of now) independently of offer_recurrence_limit, so a far-future index can never pass the paywindow check.

# IP discovery accepts a two-vote Sybil majority from channel-less peers per address type

## Details
The BOLT1 init `remote_addr` TLV lets a peer tell us which IP it sees us as. lightningd's IP discovery (`announce-addr-discovered`, default AUTO) turns the claims into an address in our signed node_announcement. best_remote_addr() (lightningd/peer_control.c:1721-1807) is meant to be Sybil-resistant: a peer with a committed channel ('preferred', channel_state_relationship) gets a vote worth preferred_bonus = total voters, so no number of channel-less peers can outvote it. Three gaps let an unauthenticated attacker forge the result:

1. Fallback threshold (peer_control.c:1797-1803). When no preferred peer voted for the address family, any address at least two non-preferred peers agree on is adopted, provided the agreement is not unanimous (best_score > 1 && best_score < preferred_bonus). Three inbound connections under fresh node_ids, two claiming A and one claiming B, give preferred_bonus=3, A=2 -> A is adopted.

2. Per-family tallying (peer_control.c:1738). Votes are counted only among peers whose remote_addr has the requested type. Channel peers that reported IPv4 contribute nothing to the IPv6 tally (and vice versa), so a well-connected IPv4 node has no preferred IPv6 vote and the fallback applies; a node whose channel peers never send remote_addr (CLN itself only sends it as connection receiver, peer_exchange_initmsg.c:243-262) has no preferred vote for either family.

3. No direction check on receipt (connectd/peer_exchange_initmsg.c:115-138). connectd forwards any routable IPv4/IPv6 remote_addr regardless of peer->incoming, although the spec and CLN's sender only emit it as the *receiver* of a connection. The attacker therefore needs only inbound connections to the victim's listening port.

handle_peer_connected (peer_control.c:1966-1979) stores the claim, calls update_remote_addr() whenever the claim differs from the current discovered address, and on a new winner calls channel_gossip_node_announce(), which signs (via hsmd) and broadcasts a new node_announcement. gather_addresses (gossip_generation.c:393-405) appends discovered_ip_v4 and discovered_ip_v6 when ip-discovery is TRUE, or AUTO with no configured announceable address (the NAT'd-node case the feature exists for). Channel-less peers are freed on disconnect (maybe_delete_peer, peer_control.c:144-162), so the attacker keeps the three sockets open until adoption; afterwards a re-tally that yields no winner clears discovered_ip_* but returns NULL and does not re-announce, so the poisoned node_announcement persists until some other event regenerates it.

Result: for three TCP connections, a remote attacker inserts an arbitrary public IP:port into the victim's signed node_announcement, either alongside the real discovered IPv4 or as the only address. connectd (connectd.c:228-235) tries gossip IPv6 addresses before IPv4, so every CLN node connecting via gossip tries the attacker's host first, spending a full handshake timeout there if the attacker accepts and stalls. The attacker learns the IPs and timing of nodes that want to reach the victim, degrades or blocks their reachability, or points the network's connection attempts at a third party.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1797–1803](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1797-L1803)
   Fallback branch: when no preferred (channel) peer voted for this address family, any address reported by at least two non-preferred peers that is not unanimous (best_score > 1 && best_score < preferred_bonus) becomes our discovered address. Two Sybil votes plus one dissenting Sybil vote satisfy it.
2. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1721–1774](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1721-L1774)
   best_remote_addr tallies only peers whose remote_addr has the requested type (line 1738); preferred = peer has a channel in a committed state; preferred_bonus = number of voters of that type. Channel peers that reported IPv4 give no protection to the IPv6 tally, and vice versa.
3. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1966–1979](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1966-L1979)
   handle_peer_connected stores the peer-supplied remote_addr, re-evaluates via update_remote_addr on every connection whose claim differs from the current discovered address, and on a new winner immediately signs and broadcasts a fresh node_announcement via channel_gossip_node_announce.
4. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1811–1844](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1811-L1844)
   update_remote_addr: a re-tally that returns NULL frees discovered_ip_* and returns NULL, so no re-announcement is sent; the poisoned address stays in the last signed node_announcement until an unrelated event regenerates it.
5. [lightningd/gossip\_generation.c:388–406](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/gossip_generation.c#L388-L406)
   gather_addresses appends discovered_ip_v4 and discovered_ip_v6 to the announced address list whenever ip-discovery is TRUE, or AUTO (default) with no configured announceable address.
6. [connectd/peer\_exchange\_initmsg.c:115–138](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/peer_exchange_initmsg.c#L115-L138)
   connectd accepts any routable IPv4/IPv6 remote_addr from the peer's init TLV with no check of connection direction, although CLN itself (lines 243-262) only sends remote_addr when it is the receiver of the connection. Inbound attacker connections can therefore vote.
7. [connectd/connectd.c:228–235](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L228-L235)
   When connecting via gossip, connectd tries IPv6 addresses from the node_announcement before IPv4, so an injected IPv6 is attempted before the victim's legitimate IPv4 by every CLN node.

## Impact
Integrity: the victim's hsmd-signed node_announcement carries an attacker-chosen address, propagated network-wide. Availability: CLN connecters try gossip IPv6 before IPv4, so connection attempts go to the attacker's host first and burn the handshake timeout; when the attacker's address is the only one announced, gossip-based reachability is lost. Confidentiality: the IPs and timing of nodes attempting to connect to the victim are observable by the attacker (node_ids are not, since Noise act1 requires the victim's key). All partial: operators with configured announce addresses in AUTO mode or ip-discovery=false are unaffected, and the legitimate discovered IPv4 may remain alongside.

## Reproduction steps
1. Unauthenticated remote attacker: three inbound Noise connections to the victim's listening port under three throwaway node_ids, each sending an init with a chosen routable remote_addr (two identical, one different); connectd forwards them without a direction check and lightningd adopts the majority. Requirements on the victim's state: ip-discovery active (default AUTO with no configured announce/public bind address, i.e. the NAT'd nodes the feature targets, or explicitly TRUE), at least one announced channel so node_announcements are emitted, and no committed-channel peer having reported a remote_addr of the targeted family; per-family tallying makes the last condition the norm for IPv6 against IPv4-reached nodes, and both families are open when channel peers do not send remote_addr. No shipped control has to be disabled.

## Recommended fix
1. best_remote_addr() adopts an address on the agreement of two unauthenticated, channel-less peers whenever no committed-channel peer has voted for that address family, and tallies each family independently so channel peers' IPv4 votes do not protect the IPv6 slot (and vice versa). Fix criteria: An address must not be announced on the strength of channel-less peers alone (require at least one preferred vote, or a configurable minimum of channel peers), and the absence of a preferred vote for one family must not lower the bar for that family below the other's. Verify: three fresh node_ids reporting the same remote_addr to a node with IPv4 channel peers must not change its node_announcement.
2. connectd accepts the init remote_addr TLV from the initiator of a connection it accepted, although the spec and CLN's own sender only emit it when the sender is the connection's receiver. Fix criteria: remote_addr received on an inbound (accepted) connection is ignored for IP discovery, so only peers the node itself connected out to can vote. Verify: an inbound peer's remote_addr does not appear in listpeers/affect best_remote_addr.

# handle_peer_spoke admits channel opens before the peer_connected hook has accepted the peer

## Details
The peer_connected hook is the documented mechanism for plugins to refuse a peer (doc/schemas/hook/peer_connected.json: result 'disconnect' = do not allow the connection to proceed). lightningd marks the peer PEER_CONNECTING (peer_control.c:1953-1955), dispatches the hook chain asynchronously (plugin_hook.c: plugin_hook_call_next sends a JSON-RPC request and returns), and only on 'continue' sets PEER_CONNECTED and activates channel subdaemons; on 'disconnect' it sends the plugin's warning and tells connectd to drop the connection (1568-1572, 1622-1633). connectd does not wait for that verdict: as soon as the peer's first message for an unknown channel_id arrives it allocates a subd and sends connectd_peer_spoke (connectd/multiplex.c:1593-1613), and lightningd keeps servicing connectd while the hook is outstanding.

handle_peer_spoke (peer_control.c:2137-2382) never checks peer->connected. For open_channel it creates peer->uncommitted_channel and spawns openingd (2261-2275); for open_channel2 it creates an unsaved channel and spawns dualopend (2277-2315). openingd then negotiates with the peer in parallel with the pending hook: the openchannel hook is consulted, accept_channel is sent, and when funding_created arrives opening_fundee_finished (opening_control.c:543-600) commits the channel to the DB in CHANNELD_AWAITING_LOCKIN and starts channeld, again without checking peer->connected. If the hook later answers 'disconnect', peer_connected_hook_final only disconnects; a committed channel persists, and on every reconnect the hook refuses the peer again without ever removing it (handle_peer_spoke's reestablish path returns without activating channeld for it). The maintainers' FIXME at 1603 ('It can race by opening a channel before this!') acknowledges the ordering.

In the default install the only subscriber is chanbackup (plugins/chanbackup.c:1188), so the window is one plugin round trip (plus a sendcustommsg RPC when the peer offers option_provide_storage): long enough for a refused peer to get openingd/dualopend spawned and the open negotiation started, but a persisted fundee channel needs the open to finish before the hook returns, which is realistic only when the deciding plugin does real work in the hook (ban-list lookup, external RPC/HTTP). The gain for the refused peer is a bypass of the operator's admission policy: it runs channel-open negotiation and can leave an unwanted (fundee-side, unfunded by us) channel row on a node whose plugin rejected it; the openingd resource itself is bounded and torn down by the disconnect.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2158–2163](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2158-L2163)
   handle_peer_spoke only checks that the peer exists and the connectd counter matches; it never checks peer->connected == PEER_CONNECTED, so it acts while the peer is still PEER_CONNECTING (hook pending).
2. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:2254–2315](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L2254-L2315)
   For an unknown channel_id with open_channel/open_channel2 it creates an uncommitted/unsaved channel and spawns openingd/dualopend, attaching it to the peer via connectd regardless of hook state.
3. [connectd/multiplex.c:1593–1613](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1593-L1613)
   connectd allocates a subd and sends connectd_peer_spoke for the first message on an unknown channel_id immediately; nothing gates this on lightningd having accepted the peer.
4. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1953–1955](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1953-L1955)
   handle_peer_connected sets PEER_CONNECTING and defers acceptance to the asynchronous peer_connected plugin hook; lightningd keeps processing connectd messages meanwhile.
5. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1556–1572](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1556-L1572)
   When the hook finally returns 'disconnect', peer_connected_hook_final only sends the warning and asks connectd to disconnect; it does not tear down channels committed in the meantime.
6. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1603–1606](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1603-L1606)
   Maintainer FIXME acknowledging that a channel can be opened before this point.
7. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:543–599](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L543-L599)
   openingd's fundee flow completes without consulting peer->connected: the channel is written to the DB and channeld started as soon as funding_created arrives.
8. [plugins/chanbackup.c:1187–1189](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/chanbackup.c#L1187-L1189)
   A default, important plugin subscribes to peer_connected, so the hook is asynchronous in every default deployment and the window always exists.

## Impact
Bypasses the operator-configured peer admission control: a refused peer runs channel-open negotiation and can leave a persisted fundee-side channel (unfunded by us) that the plugin's policy forbade and that the refusal never removes. No confidentiality impact. Availability is not materially affected: the openingd/dualopend spawn is bounded (one uncommitted v1 open per peer, MAX_INFLIGHT_OPENS for v2), torn down by the ensuing disconnect, and equally available to any non-refused peer.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote peer connects and follows init with open_channel (then funding_created once accept_channel arrives). The window exists in every default deployment because chanbackup subscribes to peer_connected and the hook is asynchronous; to go beyond spawning openingd and actually persist a channel the exchange must finish before the deciding plugin returns 'disconnect', which depends on that plugin's latency — hence attack_requirements PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
handle_peer_spoke acts on peer messages while the peer's admission decision (peer_connected hook) is still pending or has already been negative, because it does not check peer->connected. Fix criteria: Channel-creating (and other state-changing) handling of peer_spoke must only proceed for peers in PEER_CONNECTED; messages arriving earlier must be deferred until the hook completes or rejected with the disconnect. Verify: with a peer_connected hook that sleeps then returns 'disconnect', an open_channel sent right after init must not leave an openingd running or a channel in the database.
