# sendinvoice leaves sent->issuer_key uninitialized; payer's 'invoice' reply dereferences wild pointer

## Details
When the operator answers a remote payer's invoice_request with `sendinvoice`, plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1500 allocates `struct sent` with `tal()` (uninitialised memory) and populates only some members; `sent->issuer_key` is never assigned on this path (it is set only in json_fetchinvoice at line 892, try_establish at line 617 for offers without issuer_id, and json_dev_rawrequest at line 1639). createinvoice_done() then sends the signed invoice to the payer as an onion message with a reply path (want_reply=true), registers `sent` in sent_list and keeps it alive until payment or timeout (default 90s, operator-chosen).

Any onion message the payer sends back over that reply path is delivered by lightningd through the onion_message_recv_secret hook; offers.c:onion_message_recv() calls handle_invoice_onion_message(), which finds the `sent` by pathsecret and — because `sent->invreq` is non-NULL for a sendinvoice — treats the message as a fetchinvoice reply via handle_invreq_response() (lines 394-395). If the message carries an `invoice` TLV, the code parses it, checks that its request-range fields match `sent->invreq` (trivial: the attacker authored that invreq and can simply echo our own invoice back), checks the presence of amount/created_at/payment_hash/node_id, and then evaluates `pubkey_eq(inv->invoice_node_id, sent->issuer_key)` (line 248). `pubkey_eq` is a STRUCTEQ memcmp over 64 bytes read through the uninitialised `issuer_key` pointer.

Outcome depends on the stale heap contents at that slot: a non-canonical/garbage address or NULL produces SIGSEGV in the offers plugin, which is an `important` builtin plugin, so lightningd exits; a stale-but-mapped pointer produces a bogus comparison, which either fails the pending sendinvoice RPC with 'Incorrect invoice_node_id field' (while the invoice remains live in the DB) or, if the bytes happen to equal our node id, lets the attacker's echoed (correctly signed) invoice complete the sendinvoice command with a fetchinvoice-style success object that the operator's tooling will misinterpret. In --developer mode the `!sent->offer` branch at line 199 returns the attacker's invoice as success without any check.

The maintainers' sendinvoice tests (tests/test_pay.py:5187-5265) only ever receive payment or an invoice_error on the reply path, never an `invoice`, so this reply type was never exercised. Root cause is twofold: uninitialised allocation of `struct sent` plus reusing the invreq-response handler for a `sent` that represents an outgoing invoice.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1493–1592](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L1493-L1592)
   json_sendinvoice() allocates `struct sent` with tal() (not talz) and initialises offer, cmd, dev_*, their_paths, direct_dest, inv, wait_timeout, inv_preimage, inv_label and invreq, but never sets issuer_key (nor reply_secret until later). issuer_key is left as stale heap bytes.
2. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:364–397](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L364-L397)
   handle_invoice_onion_message() matches any onion message arriving on one of our reply paths to its `sent` by pathsecret, and when sent->invreq is non-NULL (true for sendinvoice, where invreq is the request we are answering) forwards it to handle_invreq_response(), which was written for fetchinvoice replies.
3. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:240–250](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L240-L250)
   handle_invreq_response() does pubkey_eq(inv->invoice_node_id, sent->issuer_key) — a 64-byte memcmp through the uninitialised pointer.
4. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:138–157](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L138-L157)
   invoice_matches_request() compares TLV ranges 0-159/1e9-2999999999 of the incoming invoice with sent->invreq. For a sendinvoice `sent`, invreq is the attacker's own request, so echoing back the very invoice we sent them satisfies this and all presence checks, reaching the pubkey_eq.
5. [plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1307–1351](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/fetchinvoice.c#L1307-L1351)
   createinvoice_done() sends our invoice with want_reply=true, creating the reply path (and pathsecret) that the attacker can use to deliver the crafted onion message.

## Impact
Likely outcome is a segfault of the important offers plugin and therefore lightningd shutdown (availability HIGH). Alternative outcomes let the remote party fail or spoof the result of the operator's pending sendinvoice command (integrity LOW).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the remote payer whose invoice_request the operator answered with sendinvoice. During the pending window they send one onion message along our reply path containing an `invoice` TLV (e.g. our own invoice echoed). No privileges; the operator's prior sendinvoice call is the only interaction. Whether the result is a crash or a spurious RPC failure depends on stale heap contents (runtime state), hence AT:PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
1. struct sent is allocated with tal() and json_sendinvoice() does not initialise issuer_key (or reply_secret), so later code reads an indeterminate pointer. Fix criteria: Every allocation of struct sent must be fully initialised (talz or explicit assignment of all members, issuer_key set to our own node id for sendinvoice); a reply containing an `invoice` during a pending sendinvoice must never read uninitialised memory.
2. handle_invoice_onion_message() dispatches any reply with sent->invreq set to handle_invreq_response(), although for sendinvoice the `sent` represents an invoice we issued and no invoice reply is expected. Fix criteria: Replies on a sendinvoice reply path must only accept invoice_error (or be ignored); an `invoice` TLV must not be processed as a fetchinvoice response, and the pending sendinvoice command must not complete successfully on it.

# THEIR_HTLC spend not matching current proposal is assumed to be peer's timeout; onchaind never completes

## Details
output_spent() in onchaind handles a spend of a THEIR_HTLC output (an HTLC the peer offered us) that does not match our *current* proposal by assuming it is the peer's HTLC-timeout spend, without validating the witness. Because handle_preimage() replaces earlier proposals (including ones lightningd has already broadcast), two unresolved/mis-resolved states are reachable from peer behaviour:

1. Live commitment (OUR_UNILATERAL or THEIR_UNILATERAL). resolve_their_htlc() installs an ignore proposal (welements == NULL) that tx_new_depth() resolves at cltv_expiry depth. When lightningd delivers the preimage, handle_preimage() frees that proposal and proposes a fulfill / HTLC-success tx whose welements are set by handle_spend_created(). If the peer then spends the output via its timeout path after cltv_expiry before our fulfill confirms (the standard fee race, which the peer can win by paying more), output_spent() falls into the non-revoked `case THEIR_HTLC`, which only annotates the txout ('we should resolve by ignoring once we reach depth'), while tx_new_depth() requires `!welements` to ignore. The output is never resolved: wait_for_resolved() loops forever, onchaind_all_irrevocably_resolved is never sent, the channel is never deleted, and onchaind is relaunched and replayed (re-fetching every block since the close) on every lightningd start.

2. Revoked commitment (THEIR_REVOKED_UNILATERAL). handle_their_cheat() proposes OUR_PENALTY_TX for the THEIR_HTLC output and lightningd broadcasts it immediately. init_reply() reads the htlcs message via queue_until_msg(), so the onchaind_known_preimage lightningd sends for a still-live fulfilled inbound HTLC (onchaind_tell_fulfill) is processed afterwards: handle_preimage() discards the penalty proposal and proposes THEIR_HTLC_FULFILL_TO_US, a conflicting spend whose deadline is the HTLC's cltv_expiry-1 (set by the peer when it offered the HTLC) rather than the penalty's close+to_self_delay, so with feerate_for_target() the replacement pays no more and bitcoind keeps the penalty (assumption: bitcoind BIP125 replacement rules). When the penalty confirms, resolved_by_proposal() fails (witness element 1 is the 33-byte revocation pubkey, not the expected 32-byte preimage) and control reaches `case THEIR_HTLC` with tx_type THEIR_REVOKED_UNILATERAL: the HTLC is recorded as timed out/stealable by the peer and steal_htlc_tx() is run on our own penalty tx. It tracks outputs[0] of that tx (our own wallet P2TR output) as DELAYED_CHEAT_OUTPUT_TO_THEM with the htlc_tx wscript and sends onchaind_spend_penalty; lightningd builds a tx spending our wallet UTXO, hsmd signs it without checking the UTXO script, bitcoind rejects it and lightningd re-signs and rebroadcasts it every block. The bogus tracked output stays unresolved until our wallet happens to spend that UTXO (when it is then misrecorded as STOLEN), so onchaind again never completes and the bookkeeper records our own penalty output as an external stealable/stolen deposit.

The peer controls both triggers: in case 1 by timing out on-chain an HTLC we hold the preimage for; in case 2 by broadcasting a revoked commitment that still contains an inbound HTLC we have fulfilled but whose removal they have not yet acknowledged (they keep that window open by stalling after revoke_and_ack). No funds are lost (case 1's HTLC loss is the protocol race the peer legitimately wins; case 2's penalty output pays our wallet). What the peer gains is a permanent, deterministic, restart-persistent failure of the channel's onchaind to complete, corrupted coin-movement accounting and, in case 2, a perpetually re-signed and rebroadcast invalid transaction.

## Evidence
1. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1239–1261](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1239-L1261)
   output_spent(): a spend of a THEIR_HTLC output that resolved_by_proposal() does not recognise is handled without inspecting the witness. On THEIR_REVOKED_UNILATERAL it unconditionally records the HTLC as timed out/stealable and calls steal_htlc_tx() on the spending tx; on a live commitment it only annotates the txout and leaves out->resolved NULL, relying on tx_new_depth() to ignore the output later.
2. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1430–1440](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1430-L1440)
   tx_new_depth() ignores an output at depth_required only when proposal->welements is NULL. After handle_preimage() has installed a fulfill/HTLC-success proposal (welements set by handle_spend_created), an output the peer spent via its timeout path can never be resolved: num_not_irrevocably_resolved() never reaches zero.
3. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1476–1561](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1476-L1561)
   handle_preimage() frees whatever proposal a matching THEIR_HTLC output has (the welements==NULL ignore proposal on a live commitment, or the already-broadcast OUR_PENALTY_TX proposal on a revoked one) and replaces it with THEIR_HTLC_FULFILL_TO_US / OUR_HTLC_SUCCESS_TX, so the witness elements later compared by resolved_by_proposal() no longer describe the transaction lightningd already broadcast.
4. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1132–1172](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1132-L1172)
   steal_htlc_tx() marks the HTLC output resolved by THEIR_HTLC_TIMEOUT_TO_THEM, tracks outputs[input_num] of the spending tx as DELAYED_CHEAT_OUTPUT_TO_THEM with the htlc_tx wscript and proposes onchaind_spend_penalty on it. When the spending tx is our own confirmed penalty tx, this tracks our own wallet output and asks lightningd/hsmd to sign a penalty spend of it with the wrong witness script.
5. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1746–1756](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1746-L1756)
   init_reply() reads WIRE_ONCHAIND_HTLCS via queue_until_msg(), so the onchaind_known_preimage messages lightningd sends right after the htlcs message are queued and processed in wait_for_resolved() only after handle_their_cheat()/handle_*_unilateral() have already proposed (and lightningd has broadcast) the penalty or ignore resolution.
6. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:47–86](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L47-L86)
   onchaind_tell_fulfill() (called from handle_onchain_init_reply) sends onchaind_known_preimage for every htlc_in of the channel that still carries a preimage, regardless of close type; a fulfilled incoming HTLC stays in ld->htlcs_in until SENT_REMOVE_ACK_REVOCATION (peer_htlcs.c update_in_htlc -> remove_htlc_in), a window the peer extends indefinitely by stalling after its revoke_and_ack.
7. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:1257–1267](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L1257-L1267)
   htlc_incoming_deadline() gives the replacement fulfill tx a deadline of hin->cltv_expiry-1, chosen by the peer when it offered the HTLC, whereas handle_onchaind_spend_penalty() gives the already-broadcast penalty tx the deadline close_blockheight + our_config.to_self_delay (lines 1408-1440); with feerate_for_target() (chaintopology.c:451-471, floor feerate beyond 100/200 blocks) a far-expiry HTLC makes the fulfill pay no more than the penalty, so bitcoind keeps the penalty and it is the penalty that confirms while onchaind expects the fulfill witness.
8. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1636–1700](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1636-L1700)
   wait_for_resolved() loops until num_not_irrevocably_resolved() is zero and only then sends onchaind_all_irrevocably_resolved; lightningd's handle_irrevocably_resolved() is the only path that deletes the channel. An output left without resolution keeps onchaind alive forever and onchaind_restart()/onchaind_replay() re-fetches every block since the close on each lightningd start to reach the same state.
9. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:644–671](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L644-L671)
   handle_sign_to_us_tx() (reached via do_sign_penalty_to_us) checks only the input count and signs with the derived revocation key; it never checks that the wscript matches the UTXO being spent (FIXME at 644), so the bogus penalty on our own wallet output is signed rather than rejected: no lightningd fatal(), but an invalid tx that bitcoind rejects and lightningd re-signs and rebroadcasts every block.

## Impact
No funds are lost by the victim. Impact is a permanent, deterministic failure of the channel's onchaind to resolve: the channel is never irrevocably resolved or deleted, onchaind runs forever and is relaunched and replays every block since the close on each restart, and in case 2 lightningd/hsmd sign and rebroadcast an invalid transaction every block while the bookkeeper misrecords our own penalty output as stolen. Availability of the channel-cleanup component and integrity of accounting are degraded, nothing more.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote channel peer, the threat model's primary unauthenticated adversary; opening a channel needs no credential from the victim. Case 1 needs the peer to win the on-chain HTLC timeout-vs-fulfill fee race after cltv_expiry while we hold the preimage; case 2 needs the peer to broadcast a revoked commitment containing an inbound HTLC we fulfilled but whose removal it has not yet acknowledged (it chooses the HTLC's cltv_expiry so our fulfill replacement cannot outbid our own penalty), burning its channel balance in the process. Both are specific channel/mempool states the peer steers into rather than defeats of any security control.

## Recommended fix
1. output_spent() classifies a non-proposal spend of a THEIR_HTLC output as the peer's HTLC-timeout spend without validating the witness, and on live commitments leaves the output unresolved whenever the current proposal carries witness elements. Fix criteria: A spend of THEIR_HTLC by a transaction other than the current proposal is positively identified from its witness (peer timeout path or HTLC-timeout 2-of-2, or one of our own superseded proposals) and the tracked output is marked resolved accordingly, so num_not_irrevocably_resolved() reaches zero and onchaind_all_irrevocably_resolved is sent. Verify: a peer timing out on-chain an HTLC we hold the preimage for leads to 'onchaind complete, forgetting peer' after 100 blocks on both our and their commitment.
2. handle_preimage() discards a proposal lightningd may already have broadcast (the penalty on a revoked commitment), so the remembered witness elements no longer match the transaction that confirms. Fix criteria: Superseding a proposal keeps onchaind able to recognise the superseded transaction if it confirms (retain previous witness elements, or do not replace an already-broadcast penalty with a fulfill on revoked commitments). Verify: on a revoked close with a known preimage for an inbound HTLC, whichever of penalty/fulfill confirms is logged as resolved by our proposal, no onchaind_spend_penalty is issued for our own wallet output, and the coin-movement ledger balances.

# HTLC reply/revoke handlers use freed hout and NULL owner after channel_internal_error

## Details
lightningd's response to a malformed or inconsistent message from a per-channel subdaemon is channel_internal_error(): it logs, fails the channel permanently and releases the owning channeld via channel_set_owner(channel, NULL) -> subd_release_channel -> tal_free(owner), synchronously, inside the message handler (subd.c's mark_freed pattern exists precisely because handlers may free the subd). Two HTLC handlers in lightningd/peer_htlcs.c keep using state that this call just invalidated.

1. rcvd_htlc_reply() (channeld_offer_htlc_reply callback). hout is allocated as a tal child of out->owner in send_htlc_out() (line 785) so it dies with the daemon. If the reply fails to parse (line 643), or carries an id that is HTLC_INVALID_ID or already present in ld->htlcs_out (line 709), the handler calls channel_internal_error() -- which frees the owner and therefore hout (running destroy_hout_subd_died) -- and then calls tal_free(hout) on the freed object. ccan/tal's tal_free reads the freed header: if the chunk has not been reused the destroying bit is still set and only freed memory is read; if it has been reused by a later same-size allocation (channel_fail_perm's logging, DB and drop_to_chain work allocate heavily) tal_free frees that live object, leaving a dangling pointer in whatever owns it. Behaviour is undefined memory corruption.

2. peer_got_revoke() -> peer_accepted_htlc(). If channeld reports a changed HTLC with newstate RCVD_ADD_ACK_REVOCATION for an id lightningd does not hold (or an htlc_in_update_state transition that state_update_ok rejects), peer_accepted_htlc calls channel_internal_error() (owner freed, channel->owner = NULL) and returns false; peer_got_revoke discards the return value (line 2734) and continues. Once revokenum matches revocations_received and the shachain insert succeeds (attacker-chosen; odd indices are accepted without derivation check), it reaches subd_send_msg(channel->owner, ...) at line 2792 with a NULL subd: subd_send_msg reads sd->msgname and lightningd segfaults deterministically. Line 2805 would additionally call local_fail_in_htlc(NULL, ...).

An honest channeld never sends these messages; the author is a compromised lightning_channeld (the threat model's adversary 6), whose reach lightningd's per-message checks are meant to confine to its own channel. These paths turn the designed outcome (one channel force-closed, log_broken) into a crash of lightningd itself, taking every channel and in-flight HTLC of the node down.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:643–650](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L643-L650)
   rcvd_htlc_reply (reply callback for channeld_offer_htlc): on a reply that fails fromwire it calls channel_internal_error(subd->channel, ...) and then tal_free(hout). hout is a tal child of the subd (see send_htlc_out) and channel_internal_error synchronously tal_frees that subd, so hout is already freed when tal_free(hout) reads its header: a double free / use-after-free.
2. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:709–716](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L709-L716)
   Same pattern when the reply carries an id already in ld->htlcs_out or HTLC_INVALID_ID: channel_internal_error() frees the owner (and hout), then tal_free(hout).
3. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2734–2736](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2734-L2736)
   peer_got_revoke ignores peer_accepted_htlc's false return. For a changed[] entry with newstate RCVD_ADD_ACK_REVOCATION and an id lightningd does not hold, peer_accepted_htlc has already called channel_internal_error (owner freed, channel->owner = NULL) but processing continues.
4. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2792](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2792)
   After the shachain checks pass (revokenum == revocations_received; attacker-chosen secret, accepted without derivation check for odd shachain indices) peer_got_revoke calls subd_send_msg(channel->owner, ...) with channel->owner == NULL: deterministic NULL dereference (subd_send_msg reads sd->msgname first). Line 2805 would then also pass a NULL hin to local_fail_in_htlc.
5. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1511–1516](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1511-L1516)
   peer_accepted_htlc: unknown id -> channel_internal_error(channel, ...) then goto fail; returns false with *failmsg set, leaving the caller to continue with a freed owner.
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:785–791](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L785-L791)
   send_htlc_out allocates hout off out->owner (the channeld subd) with destructor destroy_hout_subd_died so it is freed, and the HTLC failed, when the daemon is released. This is what makes the later explicit tal_free(hout) a second free.
7. [lightningd/channel.c:1281–1308](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1281-L1308)
   channel_internal_error -> channel_fail_permanent -> channel_fail_perm (channel.c:1128 channel_set_owner(channel, NULL)) -> subd_release_channel: the owning subd is tal_freed synchronously inside the message handler, together with every object allocated off it.
8. [lightningd/subd.c:928–935](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L928-L935)
   subd_release_channel clears owner->channel and tal_frees the subd immediately; sd_msg_read/sd_msg_reply only guard their own subsequent use of sd (mark_freed), not the handler's.
9. [lightningd/subd.c:845–852](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L845-L852)
   subd_send_msg dereferences sd (sd->msgname) unconditionally, so a NULL channel->owner crashes lightningd.

## Impact
lightningd segfaults (got_revoke path) or corrupts its heap (offer_htlc_reply path): every channel and in-flight HTLC of the node stops being serviced until restart, with possible forced closures and HTLC timeouts. The containment that channel_internal_error is designed to provide against a rogue channeld is lost. No controllable confidentiality or integrity effect shown; the double free's heap-corruption potential is not demonstrated to be steerable.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker runs code inside a lightning_channeld process (post peer-side exploit) and writes to its lightningd pipe. Deterministic path: send channeld_got_revoke with the current revocations_received as revokenum, any secret for an odd shachain index (or the peer's real one), and one changed[] entry {id: unknown, newstate: RCVD_ADD_ACK_REVOCATION}; lightningd frees the owner then dereferences NULL at peer_htlcs.c:2792. Alternative: answer a pending channeld_offer_htlc (arranged by routing a payment to the attacker's own peer node) with a malformed or duplicate-id reply, causing the double free. No race, no user interaction; the position is same-uid local code execution.

## Recommended fix
1. rcvd_htlc_reply explicitly frees hout after channel_internal_error has already released the subd that owns it. Fix criteria: After channel_internal_error() in the offer_htlc_reply callback no further access to hout (including tal_free) occurs, or hout is detached from the owner before the error path; a malformed or duplicate-id offer_htlc_reply from a test channeld yields a clean channel failure with no ASan/valgrind report.
2. peer_got_revoke ignores peer_accepted_htlc's failure and continues to use channel->owner and the HTLC after channel_internal_error has invalidated them. Fix criteria: Once channel_internal_error is invoked while handling got_revoke (unknown id or rejected state transition), the handler returns without sending to channel->owner or failing HTLCs by id; a got_revoke naming an unknown HTLC id produces only a channel failure, no crash.
3. channel_internal_error frees the owning subd synchronously, but callers are not uniformly written to stop after it. Fix criteria: Every caller of channel_internal_error in a subdaemon message handler returns immediately, or the owner release is deferred until the handler returns, so no handler can touch channel->owner or owner-owned objects after the call.

# Local opener never checks it can afford commitment fee for peer-offered HTLCs; funder output silently zeroed and channeld crashes on fee decrease

## Details
When Core Lightning is the channel opener (fee payer) and the remote non-opener offers HTLCs, add_htlc() in channeld/full_channel.c enforces the sender's reserve, max_accepted_htlcs, max_htlc_value_in_flight, htlc_minimum and dust exposure, but never checks that the local opener can still afford the commitment fee for the new untrimmed HTLC output: the only fee check (lines 818-834) is guarded by `channel->opener == sender`, and the comment at 549-573 records that rejecting the peer's HTLC was deliberately omitted. BOLT 2 only says the non-funder 'SHOULD NOT' offer such HTLCs; a malicious peer ignores that. (Assumption, not verified in this checkout: eclair's Commitments.receiveAdd fails the channel with CannotAffordFees and lnd's validateCommitmentSanity rejects with ErrBelowChanReserve in this situation.)

Consequences in CLN:
1. commit_tx() -> try_subtract_fee() finds the opener cannot cover base_fee (+660 sat with anchors), sets the opener's amount to 0 and returns false, which commit_tx() ignores (commit_tx.c:195). Both commitment transactions are built and signed with no output for the local opener: its entire remaining balance (including its channel reserve) becomes miner fee. The peer obtains a fully signed, unrevoked commitment in this shape as soon as we answer its commitment_signed, and can broadcast it at any time (or stall its revoke_and_ack after we fail the HTLCs and still hold it); our own last_tx has the same shape, so a later local force-close burns the same balance. The actual fee may be far below the nominal feerate.
2. If lightningd's desired feerate later drops below the committed one (increases are clamped by approx_max_feerate, decreases are not), want_fee_update() returns the lower target, channel_update_feerate() fails because can_opener_afford_feerate() is false, and channeld.c:1512 calls status_failed(). lightningd treats the exit as transient, connectd reconnects, channeld is restarted and dies again while the HTLCs remain committed.

The opener's loss is bounded by commit_tx_base_fee at the committed feerate for up to its own max_accepted_htlcs untrimmed HTLCs (mainnet default 30; 483 on testnet or if raised): roughly (724+172*N)*feerate/1000 (+660) sat, e.g. ~1.5k sat at 253 sat/kw and ~29k sat at 5000 sat/kw with N=30, or ~430k sat with N=483 at 5000 sat/kw. It is reached whenever the opener's balance has fallen into that range, which CLN's own headroom rule (fee for one more HTLC at 2x feerate above the peer-chosen reserve) permits after the opener has paid the peer most of the channel. The attacker needs only channel balance for N untrimmed HTLCs (which return to it on timeout) and pays nothing toward the commitment fee itself.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/full\_channel.c:785–881](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L785-L881)
   add_htlc()'s only fee-affordability check for an incoming HTLC (lines 818-834) is inside `if (channel->opener == sender)`. When the local node is the opener and the remote non-opener is the sender, the HTLC is admitted on the sender's reserve, max_accepted_htlcs, max_htlc_value_in_flight, htlc_minimum and dust-exposure grounds alone; nothing verifies the local opener can still pay commit_tx_base_fee (+660 sat anchors) for the extra untrimmed output. The sender==LOCAL branch (838-880) does check both sides' fees, so the asymmetry is specific to received HTLCs.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:716–732](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L716-L732)
   handle_peer_add_htlc() admits a peer's update_add_htlc solely via channel_add_htlc() (which calls add_htlc with enforce_aggregate_limits=true); any CHANNEL_ERR_* would peer_failed_warn, but no funder-affordability error exists for this direction. lightningd only learns of the HTLC after it is committed, and performs no fee check of its own.
3. [channeld/commit\_tx.c:190–195](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/commit_tx.c#L190-L195)
   commit_tx() discards try_subtract_fee()'s return value (line 195), so when the opener cannot cover base_fee the commitment is built with the opener's to_local/to_remote output removed and the opener's whole balance paid as fee. channel_txs() uses this for both the local commitment verified in handle_peer_commit_sig() and the remote commitment signed in send_commit_part(); the resulting tx is stored as channel->last_tx (lightningd/peer_htlcs.c:2238) and is what drop_to_chain() broadcasts. Contrast common/initial_commit_tx.c:148-160, which treats the same failure as an error for the initial commitment.
4. [common/initial\_commit\_tx.c:31–47](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/initial_commit_tx.c#L31-L47)
   try_subtract_fee() sets the opener's amount to zero and returns false when base_fee exceeds the opener's balance.
5. [channeld/full\_channel.c:549–573](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L549-L573)
   Design comment: the authors knew the non-opener could add HTLCs the opener cannot afford (lightning-rfc #728) and chose to self-regulate only when the local node sends (local_opener_has_fee_headroom), explicitly declining to reject the peer's HTLCs in this case.
6. [channeld/channeld.c:1484–1515](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L1484-L1515)
   send_commit(): if want_fee_update() yields a target, channel_update_feerate() must succeed or channeld calls status_failed(STATUS_FAIL_INTERNAL_ERROR). want_fee_update() (1184-1216) clamps increases to approx_max_feerate() but passes any decrease through unchanged, so once the peer's HTLC load leaves the opener below fee+reserve(+660), the next routine feerate decrease from lightningd kills channeld before the commitment is sent.
7. [channeld/full\_channel.c:1342–1429](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L1342-L1429)
   can_opener_afford_feerate() computes exactly the fee+reserve(+660) requirement that would have rejected the peer's HTLCs; it is consulted only for update_fee (and asserted when opener==REMOTE), never when the local opener receives an HTLC.
8. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:641–646](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L641-L646)
   A channeld exit reaches channel_errmsg() with peer_fd==NULL (subd.c:654-657) and is treated as a transient failure: the channel stays CHANNELD_NORMAL, connectd reconnects, and connect_activate_subd() (1613-1617) restarts channeld, which receives the same desired feerate and dies again while the peer's HTLCs remain committed.

## Impact
Integrity: the victim's remaining channel balance, bounded by base_fee for max_accepted_htlcs untrimmed HTLCs at the committed feerate (thousands to a few hundred thousand sat), is destroyed to miners if either commitment is broadcast; the peer holds a signed one. Availability: only that channel's channeld dies and crash-loops on reconnect while the HTLC load persists; lightningd and other channels keep running, and the operator can only escape by force-closing into the burned commitment. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote Lightning peer in a channel the victim opened to it (victim is the fee-paying opener) - the threat model's primary unauthenticated adversary, authoring update_add_htlc and commitment_signed. It needs channel balance sufficient for N untrimmed HTLCs (N <= victim's max_accepted_htlcs, 30 by default on mainnet) and the victim's balance must lie within the fee range those HTLCs induce, which is the normal state of a channel the victim has mostly paid out to the peer. The messages are ordinary protocol traffic; no defence stands in the path. The fund-burn commitment is obtained deterministically; the channeld crash additionally requires lightningd's desired feerate to fall below the committed one while the HTLCs are held, a routine event after any fee spike.

## Recommended fix
1. add_htlc() does not verify that the local opener can afford the commitment fee (plus anchors and reserve) when it is the recipient of a remote-offered HTLC. Fix criteria: An incoming HTLC that would leave the local opener unable to pay base_fee (+660 with anchors) while keeping its reserve must be rejected (or the channel failed) before it is stored; after the fix, a non-opener peer offering such HTLCs must not be able to produce a commitment where try_subtract_fee() fails.
2. commit_tx() ignores try_subtract_fee()'s failure, silently building and signing commitments that strip the opener's output and pay a sub-nominal fee. Fix criteria: Commitment construction must not proceed silently when the opener cannot pay the fee; the condition must surface as an error to the caller so channeld fails the channel instead of exchanging signatures over the degraded transaction.
3. send_commit() turns a failed can_opener_afford_feerate() on a feerate decrease into status_failed(), so peer-controlled HTLC load crashes channeld. Fix criteria: The fee-update path must handle an unaffordable target by skipping or clamping the update (or by failing the channel through the normal peer-error path), never by aborting channeld; a peer holding HTLCs must not be able to put channeld into a restart loop.

# tx_signatures during negotiation echoes uninitialised funding txid heap bytes to the peer

## Details
struct tx_state is created by new_tx_state() (openingd/dualopend.c:126) with tal(), which does not zero memory, and the `funding` outpoint member is left unset until the funding PSBT is complete: psbt_txid() assigns it only in opener_commits (2267), accepter_commits (2910) and rbf_wrap_up (3557), each of which runs after run_tx_interactive() has returned. handle_tx_sigs() (1364) can, however, be reached during run_tx_interactive(): opening_negotiate_msg() (1725) forwards any WIRE_TX_SIGNATURES the peer sends mid-negotiation to it. At that moment tx_state->psbt is non-NULL and neither channel_ready flag is set, so execution reaches

    if (!bitcoin_txid_eq(&tx_state->funding.txid, &txid))
        open_err_warn(state, "tx_signatures for %s received, working on funding_txid %s", ..., fmt_bitcoin_txid(tmpctx, &tx_state->funding.txid));

which hex-formats the 32 uninitialised bytes; open_err_warn -> peer_failed_warn -> peer_failed() (common/peer_failed.c:41) writes that text to the remote peer in a BOLT1 warning before exiting.

On the very first open state->tx_state is allocated in main() (4451) from a nearly fresh heap, so the bytes may well be zero. In rbf_remote_start() (3919) and rbf_local_start() (3737), however, a brand-new tx_state allocated from a heap already used by the completed first negotiation (PSBTs, wire messages, formatted strings, tal headers holding parent/child pointers) is promoted to state->tx_state immediately before rbf_wrap_up(); a tx_signatures sent during that RBF's interactive phase echoes 32 bytes of recycled heap to the peer. dualopend holds no private keys (hsmd does), so the exposure is heap pointers (ASLR information useful for exploiting a memory-corruption bug in the same process) and residual channel/wallet data rather than secrets, but it is a reliable, peer-triggered disclosure of uninitialised memory across the peer trust boundary.

Reachable only when the node runs with --experimental-dual-fund (lightningd/options.c:1504, off by default), which is what makes dualopend handle peer open_channel2 / tx_init_rbf at all.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/dualopend.c:126–146](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L126-L146)
   new_tx_state() allocates struct tx_state with tal() (ccan tal_alloc_ with clear=false: no memset) and initialises selected members but never `funding`; tx_state->funding.txid is whatever the malloc chunk held until psbt_txid() assigns it in opener_commits (2267), accepter_commits (2910) or rbf_wrap_up (3557).
2. [openingd/dualopend.c:1412–1419](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1412-L1419)
   handle_tx_sigs(): once tx_state->psbt is non-NULL (true for the whole of run_tx_interactive) and neither channel_ready flag is set, the peer-supplied txid is compared with the still-unassigned tx_state->funding.txid and, on the near-certain mismatch, open_err_warn() formats fmt_bitcoin_txid(&tx_state->funding.txid) — 32 uninitialised bytes as hex — into the warning text.
3. [openingd/dualopend.c:3520–3557](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3520-L3557)
   rbf_wrap_up(): run_tx_interactive() (3520) runs the whole interactive phase, during which the peer may send tx_signatures, before psbt_txid() first assigns tx_state->funding.txid (3557).
4. [openingd/dualopend.c:3919–3924](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3919-L3924)
   rbf_remote_start() (peer-initiated RBF): the previous tx_state is freed and the fresh, uninitialised one promoted to state->tx_state immediately before rbf_wrap_up(), so handle_tx_sigs() reads the new allocation, carved from a heap already used by the completed first negotiation.
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:3737–3747](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3737-L3747)
   rbf_local_start() (our RBF, peer as accepter): same promotion of the fresh tx_state before rbf_wrap_up(); the peer can send tx_signatures during the interactive phase that follows.
6. [openingd/dualopend.c:1725–1728](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1725-L1728)
   opening_negotiate_msg() dispatches WIRE_TX_SIGNATURES to handle_tx_sigs() at any point of the interactive negotiation (initial open via accepter_start 2849 / opener_start 3436, or RBF), so the peer chooses the moment.
7. [openingd/dualopend.c:2910](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L2910)
   accepter_commits(): first assignment of funding.txid on the initial accepter path, after run_tx_interactive (2849) has already returned; opener_commits (2267) likewise follows run_tx_interactive (3436). On the initial open state->tx_state comes from main() (4451), so its chunk is more likely fresh (zero) heap than on the RBF path.
8. [common/peer\_failed.c:27–50](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/peer_failed.c#L27-L50)
   peer_failed() (via peer_failed_warn <- open_err_warn) builds a BOLT1 warning from the formatted text and peer_write()s it to the remote peer before reporting to lightningd, so the 32 bytes reach the attacker.

## Impact
Discloses 32 bytes of dualopend heap per attempt — tal header pointers (heap layout/ASLR) and stale PSBT/wire/config data; no key material lives in this process (hsmd signs). The daemon's exit on the warning is its normal protocol-violation behaviour, so no additional availability or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote peer that can connect to a node running --experimental-dual-fund (non-default: AT:PRESENT) opens a v2 channel with open_channel2 and, during the interactive tx construction, sends a tx_signatures message with an arbitrary txid; for recycled-heap contents it first completes the negotiation (commitment_signed + tx_signatures, no broadcast needed), sends tx_init_rbf, and repeats the early tx_signatures during the RBF's interactive phase. The warning reply carries the uninitialised bytes. No authentication, no defence to defeat, deterministic.

## Recommended fix
tx_state->funding is read and formatted into a peer-visible warning before it has been assigned, because new_tx_state() does not initialise it and handle_tx_sigs() is reachable during the interactive negotiation. Fix criteria: tx_state must be fully initialised at creation (zeroed allocation or explicit initialisation of `funding`), and handle_tx_sigs must reject a tx_signatures received before the funding txid is known without echoing the local value. Verify that a tx_signatures sent during an initial or RBF interactive negotiation yields a warning whose text contains no local memory contents.

# checkrune pname restrictions evaluate raw first-duplicate keys; plugin methods decode differently

## Details
The rune evaluator in lightningd/runes.c is the sole authorisation decision for remote rune bearers reaching the node through commando. Its `pnameX` conditions are documented as applying to "the parameter named X" of the invoked method (doc/schemas/createrune.json:38). check_condition() implements this by indexing the caller's params object with the raw key bytes and strmap_add(), which silently fails on a second insertion of the same key. Consequences:

1. Duplicate members: for {"amount_msat": 1, "amount_msat": 100000000} the evaluator sees only the first value, so pnameamount_msat<1000 (or =, ^, /, ...) passes.
2. Escaped keys: for {"amount\u005fmsat": 100000000} the evaluator stores pnameamount\u005fmsat (plus a punctuation-stripped variant), so pnameamount_msat! (parameter must be absent) passes; combined with a plain satisfying member ({"amount_msat":1,"amount\u005fmsat":100000000}) it defeats value conditions too, because the consumer decodes both keys to amount_msat and keeps the last.
3. Alias members: the punctuation-stripped slot is also first-writer-wins, so {"amountmsat":1,"amount_msat":X} satisfies a rune written in the documented legacy spelling pnameamountmsat<N (createrune.json:287) while a serde consumer that ignores unknown fields reads amount_msat=X.

For built-in lightningd commands and C plugins the consumer is common/json_param.c param(), which compares raw bytes and rejects duplicates, so decision and execution agree. For methods implemented by plugins, however, commando.c try_command() hands the raw params token to checkrune (json_add_tok), then execute_command() re-emits every raw member (json_strdup does not unescape; duplicates are kept) into the lightningd request; the ccan json_out field-name escape assert is compiled only with DEBUGBUILD=1 (Makefile:65-69), so release builds write the escaped name raw as valid JSON. lightningd's parser accepts duplicate members and plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch() forwards the object byte-for-byte to the owning plugin. cln-plugin (plugins/src/codec.rs: serde_json::Value::from_str — escapes decoded, last duplicate wins before any typed decode) and pyln-client (json.loads — same semantics) therefore execute with parameters the rune never authorised.

Attack: a peer holding a rune such as ["method=lsps-lsps2-invoice","pnameamount_msat<100000"] (or any pname-restricted rune for a Python- or Rust-plugin method) sends a commando request whose params object repeats the restricted key, spells it with a \u escape, or pairs the legacy alias with the real name; checkrune passes, commando and lightningd forward the raw object, and the plugin runs the method with the attacker's second/decoded value. Shipped Rust plugins exposing parameterised methods: cln-lsps-client lsps-lsps2-getinfo/-buy/-approve/-invoice (only when experimental-lsps-client is set), cln-bip353 fetchbip353 and cln-currencyrate currencyconvert/currencyrate (default-loaded); operator-installed pyln-client plugins — the common case for third-party payment/rebalancing helpers — are affected generally. The finding holds only where the operator has issued a rune whose pname restriction guards a method implemented by such a plugin; the clnrest path is unaffected because it canonicalises the body through serde_json before both checkrune and the call.

Root cause: the authorisation evaluator keys parameters on first-occurrence raw bytes instead of rejecting ambiguous objects (duplicate, alias-colliding or escaped member names) or evaluating the same canonical form the executing method will see.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/runes.c:861–893](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L861-L893)
   check_condition() builds cached_params from the caller-supplied params object using the raw key bytes ("pname%.*s" of buf+t->start) and strmap_add(), whose false return on an existing key (ccan strmap.c:85, EEXIST) is ignored. For an object with duplicate member names only the FIRST occurrence is ever consulted, and a key spelled with a JSON escape (e.g. "amount\u005fmsat") is stored under its escaped spelling (and a punctuation-stripped variant) and never matches the rune's fieldname. The punctuation-stripped alias is also first-writer-wins, so {"amountmsat":1,"amount_msat":X} binds the legacy spelling pnameamountmsat to 1.
2. [lightningd/runes.c:895–917](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L895-L917)
   The pname/parr lookup and comparison: a missing key makes `!` (must-be-absent) pass (ccan rune.c RUNE_COND_IF_MISSING), and `=`,`<`,`>`,`^`,`/` are evaluated against the first duplicate's raw text.
3. [plugins/commando.c:420–427](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L420-L427)
   try_command() submits the peer's params token to checkrune with json_add_tok(), a verbatim byte copy (common/json_stream.c:393-404), so the evaluator sees exactly the peer's duplicate/escaped member names.
4. [plugins/commando.c:272–317](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L272-L317)
   After checkrune succeeds, execute_command() re-emits each params member with json_add_jsonstr(req->js, json_strdup(key), raw value): json_strdup does not unescape and no de-duplication occurs, so the lightningd request carries the duplicate members and escaped key spellings exactly as the peer wrote them.
5. [ccan/ccan/json\_out/json\_out.c:136–141](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/json_out/json_out.c#L136-L141)
   check_fieldname()'s assert that a field name needs no escaping is compiled only under CCAN_JSON_OUT_DEBUG, which Makefile:65-69 sets only when DEBUGBUILD=1; json_out_member_direct() then memcpy()s the name raw between quotes. In release builds commando therefore writes "amount\u005fmsat":... — valid JSON whose consumer decodes the key to amount_msat (in a DEBUGBUILD the same input aborts commando instead).
6. [lightningd/plugin.c:1310–1351](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1310-L1351)
   plugin_rpcmethod_dispatch() is reached straight from command_exec() (jsonrpc.c:763-771) with no param() parsing for plugin-owned methods, and forwards the whole request object byte-for-byte via json_stream_forward_change_id() (plugin.c:1187-1212, only the id is replaced); lightningd's own parser (common/json_parse_simple.c validate_jsmn_keyvalue) does not reject duplicate member names.
7. [plugins/src/codec.rs:95](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/src/codec.rs#L95)
   cln-plugin (crate published from this tree) parses every incoming line with serde_json::Value::from_str (serde_json 1.0.151 per Cargo.lock): string escapes are decoded and, in Value's map, a later duplicate key overwrites the earlier one. lib.rs dispatch_one (~970-980) hands request["params"] from that already-canonicalised Value to the rpcmethod callback, so a subsequent typed serde_json::from_value never sees a duplicate.
8. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs:307–318](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/client.rs#L307-L318)
   Shipped Rust example: lsps-lsps2-invoice (loaded when experimental-lsps-client is set) deserialises amount_msat, description, label from the canonicalised Value with a struct that does not deny unknown fields; lsps-lsps2-buy/-approve/-getinfo (lines 139-280) and the default-loaded cln-bip353 fetchbip353 / cln-currencyrate methods decode the same way.
9. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:829](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L829)
   pyln-client (PyPI) parses requests with json.loads(), where duplicate object keys resolve to the LAST value and \uXXXX escapes are decoded; every operator-installed Python plugin method therefore executes with a parameter set that can differ from the one checkrune authorised.
10. [common/json\_param.c:158–189](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_param.c#L158-L189)
   Contrast: lightningd's and the C plugins' param() rejects duplicate names ("duplicate json names") and compares raw bytes, so built-in/C-plugin commands stay consistent with the evaluator. The divergence is specific to methods executed by plugins whose JSON library canonicalises.

## Impact
The bearer escapes the parameter bounds the operator placed on a method they were allowed to call: amount caps or 'must be absent' conditions on LSP/JIT-channel or third-party payment and rebalancing plugin methods, so funds-moving or state-changing operations run with attacker-chosen arguments (integrity high). Where the restricted parameter selected what is returned, data beyond the intended scope can be read (confidentiality low). Availability impact is limited to whatever the over-privileged call can do (low).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning peer holding an operator-issued rune (PR:L) that permits a plugin-implemented method but caps or forbids a parameter with pnameX conditions; commando is always on, so the request arrives over the peer connection (AV:N). They send the request with the restricted key duplicated (first value satisfying the rune, second the real one), spelled with a JSON \u escape, or paired with its punctuation-stripped alias; checkrune evaluates the first/raw key and passes, commando and lightningd forward the raw object, and the plugin's JSON library (serde_json Value / Python json.loads) decodes it the other way and executes with the unauthorised value. No race or guesswork is involved (AC:L). It requires the deployment to have issued a pname-restricted rune for a method implemented by a cln-plugin (Rust) or pyln-client (Python) plugin rather than a C/built-in command (AT:P).

## Recommended fix
1. check_condition() silently tolerates duplicate member names (strmap_add failure ignored), including collisions after punctuation stripping, so the evaluated parameter set can differ from the one the executing method decodes. Fix criteria: A params object containing duplicate member names (exact, or colliding after the punctuation-stripping normalisation) must fail checkrune rather than be evaluated on the first occurrence. Verify: checkrune with {"x":1,"x":2} against a pnamex=1 rune, and with {"a_b":1,"ab":2} against pnameab=1, returns RUNE_NOT_PERMITTED/INVALID_PARAMS.
2. Parameter names (and values) are matched on raw escaped JSON bytes, whereas plugin JSON decoders apply escapes, so a key spelled with \u escapes is invisible to the evaluator but present to the method. Fix criteria: Either reject params objects whose member names contain JSON escape sequences, or unescape names (and string values) before building the pname map so the evaluator sees the canonical form the method will see. Verify: {"ke\u0079":1} against a pnamekey! rune is rejected, and against pnamekey=1 is evaluated as key=1.
3. commando re-emits the peer's raw member names and values after authorisation instead of forwarding the canonical object checkrune evaluated, so the two consumers can disagree. Fix criteria: The params object commando forwards for execution must be byte-identical in meaning to what checkrune evaluated: either reject objects with duplicate or escaped member names before calling checkrune, or canonicalise once and submit that canonical form to both. Verify: a commando request with duplicate or escaped keys is refused with COMMANDO_ERROR_REMOTE before any method runs.

# channel_reestablish next_revocation_number >= 2^48 crashes dualopend via rejected hsmd request

## Details
On reconnection to a dual-funded channel still owned by dualopend (states DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED / DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN; lightningd/peer_control.c:1464-1475 and 2230-2234 restart dualopend and it runs do_reconnect_dance(), dualopend.c:4624-4627), do_reconnect_dance() parses the peer's channel_reestablish and, if next_revocation_number != 0, calls check_future_dataloss_fields(), which sends hsmd_check_future_secret(next_revocation_number - 1, secret) to hsmd with no range check. The index is an attacker-chosen u64. hsmd's per_commit_secret() (common/derive_basepoints.c:97) refuses indices >= 2^48 (SHACHAIN_BITS=48, Makefile:293) and libhsmd's handle_check_future_secret returns hsmd_status_bad_request_fmt; hsmd.c report_bad_req() logs BROKEN in hsmd and sends hsmstatus_client_bad_request to lightningd (logged BROKEN at hsm_control.c:68), and handle_client() io_close()s the dualopend client connection (hsmd.c:839-840). Back in dualopend, wire_sync_read() returns NULL on EOF, fromwire_hsmd_check_future_secret_reply() fails and status_failed(STATUS_FAIL_HSM_IO, ...) aborts the subdaemon.

channeld's equivalent code path (channeld.c:5665-5669) has an explicit `if (next_revocation_number - 1 >= (1ULL << SHACHAIN_BITS)) peer_failed_err(...)` guard precisely to avoid handing hsmd an invalid index; dualopend omits it.

This holds only when the victim node runs with --experimental-dual-fund (opt-in, lightningd/options.c:1504) and the peer holds an in-progress v2 channel with it, which any peer can create by opening one (the funding tx need never confirm). Such a peer can, on every reconnect, deterministically crash lightning_dualopend, make hsmd drop that client and emit BROKEN logs in hsmd and lightningd, and keep the channel from re-establishing while they repeat it (lightningd treats the subdaemon death as a transient failure, dual_open_control.c:4312-4348). lightningd and hsmd stay up, and the peer could stall the channel by simply not reconnecting or fail it with an error message, so the impact is a reliable peer-triggered subdaemon crash plus BROKEN-level alert noise rather than fund loss.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/dualopend.c:3996–4020](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3996-L4020)
   check_future_dataloss_fields() forwards the peer's next_revocation_number - 1 to hsmd_check_future_secret with no upper bound (4004-4006); when hsmd rejects the request and closes the client fd, wire_sync_read returns NULL, fromwire_hsmd_check_future_secret_reply fails and status_failed(STATUS_FAIL_HSM_IO) terminates dualopend (4009-4013). This is the code the fix must change: a < 2^48 check before the hsmd call, as channeld has.
2. [openingd/dualopend.c:4106–4126](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L4106-L4126)
   do_reconnect_dance() parses channel_reestablish from peer_read() (4106-4114) and calls check_future_dataloss_fields() for any non-zero next_revocation_number (4122-4126); it runs on every reconnect while the channel is still owned by dualopend (dualopend.c:4624-4627, peer_control.c:1464-1475, 2230-2234).
3. [channeld/channeld.c:5665–5669](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L5665-L5669)
   The channeld sibling explicitly rejects next_revocation_number - 1 >= (1ULL << SHACHAIN_BITS) with a peer error before contacting hsmd; dualopend lacks this guard.
4. [common/derive\_basepoints.c:92–104](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/derive_basepoints.c#L92-L104)
   per_commit_secret() returns false for indices >= 2^48 (SHACHAIN_BITS=48, Makefile:293), so any peer value >= 2^48 + 1 is guaranteed to be refused by hsmd.
5. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1113–1138](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1113-L1138)
   handle_check_future_secret() turns the per_commit_secret failure into hsmd_status_bad_request_fmt("bad commit secret #n"), which calls report_bad_req (hsmd.c:116-137: status_broken plus hsmstatus_client_bad_request to lightningd, logged BROKEN at lightningd/hsm_control.c:68) and returns NULL.
6. [hsmd/hsmd.c:837–841](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/hsmd.c#L837-L841)
   handle_client() io_close()s the dualopend client connection when libhsmd returns NULL, so dualopend's synchronous wire_sync_read on HSM_FD sees EOF.
7. [lightningd/subd.c:650–659](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L650-L659)
   Context: the dualopend death is reported to dualopen_errmsg (dual_open_control.c:4312) with peer_fd=NULL, disconnect=false, warning=false, producing channel_fail_transient; the channel survives but the peer can repeat this on every reconnect.

## Impact
Deterministic crash of the per-channel dualopend subdaemon and forced closure of its hsmd client connection on each attempt, with BROKEN logs in hsmd and lightningd, blocking re-establishment of that channel while the peer persists; lightningd and hsmd keep running, no other channel is affected and no funds are exposed, so availability impact is LOW.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote peer reconnects to a dual-funded channel still owned by dualopend and sends channel_reestablish with next_revocation_number >= 2^48 + 1 and any your_last_per_commitment_secret; no defence exists on this path and the hsmd rejection is deterministic (per_commit_secret bound). Attack requirements are PRESENT: the victim must run with --experimental-dual-fund (opt-in) and the attacker must first have a v2 channel in DUALOPEND_OPEN_COMMITTED / AWAITING_LOCKIN state, which they can create themselves by opening one.

## Recommended fix
dualopend trusts the peer's next_revocation_number range before handing it to hsmd, unlike channeld. Fix criteria: Reject channel_reestablish whose next_revocation_number - 1 >= 2^48 with a peer error before any hsmd call (mirroring channeld). Verify that such a message yields a protocol error to the peer and no hsmd bad-request / STATUS_FAIL_HSM_IO.

# Late preimage on already-ignored HTLC output leaves HTLC-success second-stage output untracked

## Details
onchaind resolves an inbound HTLC output (THEIR_HTLC) on our own commitment (OUR_UNILATERAL) by proposing to ignore it once its cltv_expiry is reached (resolve_their_htlc -> propose_ignore). If the commitment transaction confirms at or after the HTLC's cltv_expiry, propose_ignore() clamps the required block and immediately calls ignore_output(), setting out->resolved with tx_type SELF and txid = commitment txid; the same happens later via tx_new_depth() when the expiry depth is reached.

When the preimage subsequently arrives (lightningd sends onchaind_known_preimage for every fulfilled inbound HTLC immediately after onchaind_htlcs, and again from fulfill_htlc() when a preimage is learned downstream while onchaind owns the channel), handle_preimage() explicitly tolerates resolved->tx_type == SELF and goes on to free the old proposal and propose OUR_HTLC_SUCCESS_TX, but it never clears out->resolved. lightningd's handle_onchaind_spend_htlc_success() builds, signs (hsmd) and broadcasts the HTLC-success transaction without checking the output's state.

When that HTLC-success tx confirms, output_spent() hits `if (out->resolved) continue;` before resolved_by_proposal(), so the OUR_HTLC_SUCCESS_TX branch that calls resolve_htlc_tx() never runs. resolve_htlc_tx() is the only code that tracks the HTLC-success tx's output (P2WSH to the htlc_tx wscript, CSV-locked to our delayed key) and asks lightningd to sweep it with onchaind_spend_to_us after to_self_delay. Nothing else in lightningd knows about or can spend that output (the wallet only recognises its own BIP32/BIP86 addresses; lightningd merely watches the HTLC-success tx for spends). The commitment txid's depth drives the SELF resolution to depth 100, onchaind reports all_irrevocably_resolved, and the channel is forgotten: the HTLC amount (minus fee) is permanently stranded in an output only recoverable with external tooling, and bookkeeper coin movements for the HTLC are never recorded. On THEIR_UNILATERAL the same state bug only skips coin-movement accounting, because the fulfill spend goes directly to a wallet address.

Trigger from the peer side: the channel peer sends us an HTLC (paying our invoice or routing), we fulfill it, the peer stops signing so the HTLC stays in the commitment; lightningd force-closes at cltv_expiry - (cltv_expiry_delta+1)/2 (default 17 blocks before expiry). If the commitment takes longer than that margin to confirm (low pre-anchor commitment feerate, fee spike, pinning, no wallet UTXOs for anchor CPFP), the HTLC is already expired when onchaind starts and the bug fires deterministically whenever our HTLC-success tx wins the race against the peer's timeout claim, including when the peer is simply offline. Alternatively a downstream payee can withhold the preimage until after the inbound HTLC's expiry depth. The counterparty does not gain the funds, so this is a griefing/funds-stranding defect, but it also fires in honest offline-peer scenarios.

## Evidence
1. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1488–1506](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1488-L1506)
   handle_preimage() accepts a THEIR_HTLC output whose resolved->tx_type is SELF (already 'ignored') and proceeds: it frees the old proposal and proposes OUR_HTLC_SUCCESS_TX via propose_immediate_resolution(), but never clears out->resolved. The only assignments to ->resolved in the file are new_tracked_output (NULL), ignore_output, resolved_by_proposal, resolved_by_other and unknown_spend; none runs here. The output therefore stays marked resolved while lightningd signs and broadcasts the HTLC-success tx.
2. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1212–1225](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1212-L1225)
   output_spent() does 'if (out->resolved) continue;' before resolved_by_proposal(). When our HTLC-success tx confirms and spends the SELF-resolved commitment output, the OUR_HTLC_SUCCESS_TX branch that calls resolve_htlc_tx() and record_coin_movements() is never reached; the function still returns interesting=true, so lightningd merely keeps watching the tx.
3. [onchaind/onchaind.c:690–711](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L690-L711)
   propose_ignore() clamps block_required to tx_blockheight and immediately calls ignore_output() (resolved->tx_type = SELF, resolved->txid = commitment txid) when the HTLC's cltv_expiry <= the block the commitment confirmed in. resolve_their_htlc() (lines 1989-2023) calls it for every OUR_UNILATERAL/THEIR_HTLC output during handle_our_unilateral(), before wait_for_resolved() dequeues the known_preimage messages queued by queue_until_msg().
4. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1430–1439](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1430-L1439)
   tx_new_depth() also calls ignore_output() on a THEIR_HTLC output once the commitment reaches the HTLC's expiry depth and the proposal has no welements; a preimage learned after that point (peer_htlcs.c fulfill path) hits the same bug.
5. [onchaind/onchaind.c:1076–1119](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L1076-L1119)
   resolve_htlc_tx() is the only code that creates the DELAYED_OUTPUT_TO_US tracked output for our HTLC-success tx and sends onchaind_spend_to_us so lightningd sweeps it after to_self_delay (OUR_DELAYED_RETURN_TO_WALLET). If it is not called, nothing in lightningd/ or wallet/ references the htlc_tx wscript or can spend that P2WSH output; wallet_can_spend() (wallet/wallet.c:998-1026) only matches the wallet's own BIP32/BIP86 addresses.
6. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:1480–1559](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L1480-L1559)
   handle_onchaind_spend_htlc_success() builds the HTLC-success tx (locktime 0, valid regardless of the HTLC's expiry), has hsmd sign it, broadcasts it with RBF handling and replies onchaind_spend_created. There is no check that the output is still unresolved or that the HTLC deadline has passed, so the tx is broadcast even for a SELF-resolved output.
7. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:47–85](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L47-L85)
   onchaind_tell_fulfill() sends onchaind_known_preimage for every inbound HTLC with a preimage right after onchaind_htlcs (handle_onchain_init_reply, line 165); onchaind queues these during output matching and processes them only in wait_for_resolved(), after resolve_their_htlc() may already have SELF-resolved the output.
8. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:457–459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L457-L459)
   fulfill_htlc() forwards a preimage learned later (e.g. from the downstream hop) to onchaind as onchaind_known_preimage when the channel is already owned by onchaind, which is the second route to handle_preimage() after tx_new_depth() has SELF-resolved the output.
9. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2966–2969](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2966-L2969)
   htlc_in_deadline() = cltv_expiry - (cltv_expiry_delta+1)/2: lightningd force-closes a channel holding a fulfilled inbound HTLC only this many blocks before expiry (default 17), so a commitment that takes longer than that to confirm lands at or after cltv_expiry and triggers the immediate ignore_output() path.

## Impact
The node permanently loses access (via lightningd) to the full value of the affected HTLC(s): the HTLC-success output is never tracked or swept and the channel is forgotten after 100 blocks. No confidentiality impact. Funds loss is rated as integrity impact on the node's balance; availability impact is limited to the stranded funds and incorrect accounting.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a channel peer (or the downstream payee controlling preimage timing). Peer sends an HTLC we fulfill, then goes silent so the HTLC remains committed; lightningd force-closes near expiry. If the commitment confirms at/after cltv_expiry (slow confirmation, which the peer influences via the commitment feerate if opener, or via pinning) or the preimage reaches lightningd after the expiry depth, onchaind SELF-resolves the output, then re-proposes an HTLC-success tx without clearing resolved; its second-stage output is never swept. Requires specific chain-timing conditions outside the attacker's full control.

## Recommended fix
1. handle_preimage() re-proposes a spend for an output whose resolved->tx_type is SELF but leaves out->resolved set, so the eventual confirmation of our own HTLC-success/fulfill tx is ignored by output_spent() and the second-stage output is never tracked. Fix criteria: When a SELF (ignored) resolution is superseded by a preimage-based proposal, the output must return to the unresolved state so that output_spent() recognises our HTLC-success transaction via resolved_by_proposal() and resolve_htlc_tx() tracks and later sweeps its delayed output. Verify: with an inbound HTLC whose cltv_expiry <= commitment block height and a known preimage, the logs show OUR_HTLC_SUCCESS_TX resolved by our proposal followed by OUR_DELAYED_RETURN_TO_WALLET for OUR_HTLC_SUCCESS_TX/DELAYED_OUTPUT_TO_US, and the funds appear in listfunds.
2. output_spent() treats any already-resolved output as finished even when a newer proposal with witness elements exists for it, so a spend by our own later proposal is silently dropped. Fix criteria: A spend of a tracked output that matches a live proposal's witness elements must be processed (including resolve_htlc_tx for HTLC txs and coin-movement recording) regardless of a prior SELF resolution; no code path may broadcast a transaction whose outputs onchaind will not subsequently track.
