# Any peer can set the remote channel_update of a public channel gossipd has not yet mapped

## Details
gossipd's heuristic at gossmap_manage.c:1103-1112 exists so that a peer's channel_update for its own *private* channel with us (which is never in the gossmap) still reaches lightningd. It forwards any channel_update whose scid is unknown to the gossmap and whose signature verifies against the sending peer's node_id, passing the sender as `source_peer` through tell_lightningd_peer_update (gossipd.c:320-344). On the lightningd side, channel_gossip_set_remote_update (channel_gossip.c:1343-1390) resolves the scid to one of our channels and only checks that `source` equals the channel counterparty when the channel is private (line 1374). For a channel flagged public (CHANNEL_FLAGS_ANNOUNCE_CHANNEL) it accepts the update from any source, on the stated assumption that gossipd already verified it against the channel's node — which holds for the process_channel_update path (sigcheck against gossmap_nth_node, lines 923-929) but not for the self-signed path.

The window is built into the channel_gossip state machine: while a public channel is in CGOSSIP_WAITING_FOR_MATCHING_PEER_SIGS or CGOSSIP_WAITING_FOR_ANNOUNCE_DEPTH (scid known, channel usable), our own channel_update is sent only to the peer (channel_gossip.c:530) and the channel_announcement is broadcast to gossipd only on CGOSSIP_ANNOUNCED (line 783), i.e. after ANNOUNCE_MIN_DEPTH=6 confirmations and the announcement_signatures exchange. Until then gossmap_find_chan fails for our scid, so the counterparty's genuine update *and* any third party's self-signed update for that scid both arrive at lightningd through the identical message, and the last one wins (no timestamp check on this path). The window also recurs whenever the peer is offline and cannot exchange announcement_signatures, or gossipd's store is rebuilt before the announcement is re-added.

Consequence: any connected peer P' (connectd forwards every WIRE_CHANNEL_UPDATE to gossipd tagged with the sender, connectd/multiplex.c:321,923) can craft a channel_update for that channel's scid, sign it with its own key, and have lightningd persist P'-chosen fee_base, fee_ppm, cltv_expiry_delta, htlc_minimum/maximum as the channel's remote update (cg->peer_update, written to the DB by wallet_channel_save). These values are exposed as listpeerchannels updates.remote (peer_control.c:1011-1024) and, through topology's listincoming and gossmods_from_listpeerchannels, become the invoice route hint for that channel (routehint.c:73-158; is_public is from channel_flags, so the unannounced public channel is hinted). The attacker can thus make our invoices advertise bogus inbound fees/cltv (payments fail at the real peer with fee_insufficient/incorrect_cltv_expiry, or payers overpay the real peer) or an htlc_maximum of 0 that turns the channel into a 'deadend' and removes the hint entirely — exactly when the hint is the only way payers can reach us over that channel. The real peer's next update restores the values, but the attacker can keep resending to win.

The attacker does not need the scid in advance: scids are block:txindex:output, so the attacker can watch the chain for funding-shaped outputs or spray self-signed updates for every output in recent blocks (gossipd does one ECDSA verify per message and forwards every hit; lightningd responds with nothing observable). Only a 10000-message backpressure drop in tell_lightningd_peer_update applies; there is no authorization check.

Root cause is split across the boundary: gossipd forwards self-signed updates for arbitrary scids without indicating that the signer is only the sender, and lightningd trusts `source` for public channels without requiring it to be the counterparty. The correct property is that a remote update for channel C is applied only when it was verified against C's counterparty key.

## Evidence
1. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1103–1112](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1103-L1112)
   For any scid absent from the gossmap, a channel_update whose signature verifies against the *sending* peer's node_id is forwarded to lightningd via tell_lightningd_peer_update with that sender as source_peer. Nothing ties the scid to a channel the sender is party to: the sender signs a channel_update for an arbitrary scid with its own key. The verified path (process_channel_update, lines 923-929) checks the signature against the channel's real node instead; lightningd receives the same message type from both.
2. [lightningd/channel\_gossip.c:1371–1389](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_gossip.c#L1371-L1389)
   channel_gossip_set_remote_update resolves the scid with any_channel_by_scid and enforces source == channel->peer->id only when is_private(channel) (no CHANNEL_FLAGS_ANNOUNCE_CHANNEL). For a public channel it accepts any source — the comment assumes gossipd verified the signature against the channel's node, which is false for the self-signed path — then overwrites cg->peer_update and persists it with wallet_channel_save (remote_feerate_base/remote_cltv_expiry_delta columns, wallet.c:2724-2726).
3. [lightningd/channel\_gossip.c:530](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_gossip.c#L530)
   Establishes the window: for a public channel that is not yet CGOSSIP_ANNOUNCED (states WAITING_FOR_MATCHING_PEER_SIGS / WAITING_FOR_ANNOUNCE_DEPTH, scid already known), our own channel_update goes only to the peer (msg_to_peer), and the channel_announcement is broadcast to gossipd only on reaching CGOSSIP_ANNOUNCED (line 783, after ANNOUNCE_MIN_DEPTH=6 and announcement_signatures). Until then gossmap_find_chan fails for our scid and every channel_update for it takes the self-signed path.
4. [gossipd/gossipd.c:320–343](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossipd.c#L320-L343)
   tell_lightningd_peer_update builds gossipd_remote_channel_update with the forwarding peer as source_node and the update's fee/cltv/htlc fields; it carries no indication of whether the signature was checked against the channel's node or merely the sender, so lightningd cannot apply the correct authorization rule. The only limit is a 10000-message backpressure drop.
5. [lightningd/routehint.c:73–157](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/routehint.c#L73-L157)
   Invoice route hints are built from listincoming (topology plugin), whose fee_base_msat, fee_proportional_millionths, cltv_expiry_delta and htlc_max_msat for the peer->us direction come from listpeerchannels updates.remote via gossmods_from_listpeerchannels (common/gossmods_listpeerchannels.c:181-190). is_public is taken from channel_flags (line 142), so the not-yet-announced public channel is included as a public hint carrying the attacker's values; htlc_max caps candidate.capacity, so htlc_max=0 makes it a 'deadend' and drops the hint.

## Impact
Integrity: attacker-controlled fee/cltv/htlc limits are persisted as the counterparty's channel parameters and surface in listpeerchannels and invoice route hints — limited scope, self-correcting on the next genuine update. Availability: invoices for that channel may become unpayable or payers may be steered to overpay during the window. No confidentiality impact (lightningd sends nothing back to the attacker).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any connected Lightning peer (no privileges). They sign channel_updates with their own node key for candidate scids (or spray all outputs of recent blocks), send them as ordinary gossip; gossipd forwards those for scids absent from its gossmap; lightningd overwrites the remote update for any matching public channel and saves it. Requires the target channel to be in the pre-announcement (or re-sync/pruned) state, a runtime condition outside the attacker's control, hence AT:PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
1. gossipd forwards a channel_update for an unknown scid when it is merely signed by the sending peer, without conveying to lightningd that the signer is the sender rather than the channel's verified node, so lightningd cannot apply the correct authorization rule. Fix criteria: The gossipd->lightningd remote-update message distinguishes 'signature verified against the channel's node in the gossmap' from 'signature verified against the sender only', and lightningd applies an update of the second kind only when the sender is the channel's counterparty (source == channel->peer->id) regardless of the channel's public/private flag.
2. channel_gossip_set_remote_update skips the source == counterparty check for public channels even when the channel has not reached CGOSSIP_ANNOUNCED, a state in which gossipd cannot possibly have verified the update against the channel's node. Fix criteria: For any channel that is private or not yet in CGOSSIP_ANNOUNCED, lightningd rejects a remote update whose source is not the channel counterparty. Verify by having a third peer send a self-signed channel_update for a not-yet-announced public channel and confirming listpeerchannels updates.remote and the invoice route hints are unchanged.

# Watchtower penalty tx built with wrong to_self_delay (and lease CSV), yielding unspendable penalty

## Details
channeld/watchtower.c:penalty_tx_create() builds the pre-signed penalty transaction that lightningd hands to watchtower plugins through the `commitment_revocation` hook (`penalty_tx`, documented as 'the penalty transaction that can spend the revoked commitment'). It must spend the peer's `to_local` output of the just-revoked remote commitment. That output is P2WSH of to_self_wscript(to_self_delay, csv, keyset) as produced by commit_tx() for side == REMOTE, where channel_txs() passes channel->config[!REMOTE] = config[LOCAL].to_self_delay (our_config.to_self_delay = our watchtime-blocks, the delay WE impose on the peer per BOLT2) and csv = lease_expiry - blockheight when the peer is lessor.

penalty_tx_create() instead uses channel->config[REMOTE].to_self_delay (watchtower.c:36) - the peer's own to_self_delay, which governs OUR to_local output - and a fixed lease csv of 1 (line 69, 'FIXME: csv_lock'). bitcoin_wscript_to_local pushes max(csv, delay), so whenever the two sides' to_self_delay values differ, or the channel is leased by the peer with lease remaining > to_self_delay, the witness script differs from the one hashed into the output. The PSBT input carries no scriptPubKey and hsmd's do_sign_penalty_to_us signs over whatever wscript it is given, so nothing detects the mismatch: the hook delivers a signed transaction whose P2WSH hash check fails on-chain, i.e. an unbroadcastable penalty. lightningd's own onchaind path is unaffected (onchain_control.c:1897 deliberately reverses the sides; onchaind.c:2522 uses to_self_delay[REMOTE] = our_config and grinds the lease csv), so the bug is exposed exactly when the watchtower is the only protection.

The mismatch precondition is attacker-controlled: check_config_bounds (openingd/common.c:36) accepts any peer to_self_delay up to max-locktime-blocks (default 2016), so a peer simply chooses a value different from the victim's watchtime-blocks; it also arises by default across implementations (CLN 144, eclair 720, lnd 144-2016) and with any tuned --watchtime-blocks. CLN's only test (tests/test_plugin.py::test_watchtower) uses pyln-testing's symmetric watchtime-blocks=5 for both nodes, so it never exercises the asymmetric case. Attack: the peer waits until the victim node is offline, broadcasts a revoked commitment with a balance favourable to itself, the watchtower's penalty_tx is rejected by the network, and after our to_self_delay blocks the peer sweeps its to_local - stealing up to the victim's whole channel balance in that old state. The shipped chanbackup plugin registers this hook but ignores penalty_tx (it only triggers staticbackup), so the affected consumers are the third-party watchtower plugins the project documentation directs users to.

## Evidence
1. [channeld/watchtower.c:36](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/watchtower.c#L36)
   remote_to_self_delay is read from channel->config[REMOTE].to_self_delay. config[REMOTE] is the peer's channel_config (their open/accept_channel), and per BOLT2 (common/channel_config.h:66) a node's to_self_delay is the delay imposed on the OTHER node's to_local output - so this is the delay on OUR output, not on the peer's output the penalty must spend.
2. [channeld/watchtower.c:68–75](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/watchtower.c#L68-L75)
   The peer's to_local witness script is built with that wrong delay and a hard-coded lease_remaining of 1 ('FIXME: csv_lock'); it becomes the P2WSH witness script of the penalty input (bitcoin_tx_add_input, scriptPubKey passed as NULL so nothing cross-checks it) and the script hsmd signs over (line 119-121); hsmd's do_sign_penalty_to_us (hsmd/libhsmd.c:1696) signs whatever wscript it is given.
3. [channeld/full\_channel.c:387–402](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/full_channel.c#L387-L402)
   channel_txs() builds the peer's commitment (side == REMOTE) with to_self_delay = channel->config[!side].to_self_delay = config[LOCAL].to_self_delay and csv from lease_expiry / channel_blockheight(); this is the script actually hashed into the revoked commitment's to_local output.
4. [channeld/commit\_tx.c:278–291](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/commit_tx.c#L278-L291)
   The to_local output is P2WSH of to_self_wscript(to_self_delay, side == lessor ? csv_lock : 0, keyset); spending a P2WSH requires the byte-identical script, so any difference in delay or csv makes the penalty input's witness invalid.
5. [channeld/commit\_tx.c:139–149](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/commit_tx.c#L139-L149)
   lessor = !opener and csv_lock = lease_expiry - blockheight while the lease runs; so when we opened a leased channel (peer is lessor) the peer's to_local CSV is max(to_self_delay, lease remaining), which the penalty's fixed csv=1 never matches while lease remaining > to_self_delay.
6. [bitcoin/script.c:620–635](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/script.c#L620-L635)
   bitcoin_wscript_to_local pushes max(lease_remaining, to_self_delay) into the script, so the script bytes (and the P2WSH hash) depend on the delay value.
7. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1986–1987](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1986-L1987)
   channeld_init passes channel->our_config as config[LOCAL] and channel_info.their_config as config[REMOTE] (consumed in channeld.c:7060 and new_full_channel at 7179).
8. [lightningd/opening\_common.c:160–165](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_common.c#L160-L165)
   our_config.to_self_delay = ld->config.locktime_blocks (watchtime-blocks, default 144 on mainnet) - the delay WE impose on the peer's to_local output, i.e. the value the penalty script must use.
9. [lightningd/onchain\_control.c:1893–1900](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/onchain_control.c#L1893-L1900)
   Contrast: for onchaind lightningd explicitly reverses the sides ('they specify ours, we specify theirs'), so onchaind's to_self_delay[REMOTE] = our_config.to_self_delay.
10. [onchaind/onchaind.c:2522–2524](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/onchaind/onchaind.c#L2522-L2524)
   Contrast: onchaind's steal_to_them_output spends the very same output with to_self_delay[REMOTE] (= our_config) and the ground lease csv - the correct script. The node's own online penalty path is therefore unaffected; only the pre-signed watchtower penalty_tx is wrong.
11. [openingd/common.c:36–42](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/common.c#L36-L42)
   check_config_bounds accepts any peer to_self_delay up to max_to_self_delay (max-locktime-blocks, default 2016); the peer therefore chooses its own to_self_delay and can trivially make it differ from ours, so the mismatch precondition is attacker-controlled, not a deployment setting.
12. [channeld/channeld.c:1314–1315](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L1314-L1315)
   penalty_base_new records the to_local output (direct_outputs[LOCAL]) of the REMOTE commitment built by channel_txs(..., REMOTE) - the CSV-delayed output the penalty must spend.
13. [channeld/channeld.c:2662–2677](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L2662-L2677)
   On the peer's revoke_and_ack, penalty_tx_create() is run for that commitment and the result is sent to lightningd in channeld_got_revoke.
14. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2821–2831](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2821-L2831)
   lightningd forwards the penalty_tx unchanged to plugins via the commitment_revocation hook; doc/schemas/hook/commitment_revocation.json documents it as 'The penalty transaction that can spend the revoked commitment. Can be sent to a watchtower for enforcement.' (doc/beginners-guide/watchtowers.md points users to the rust-teos watchtower-plugin, which consumes this hook).

## Impact
The watchtower safety mechanism is silently defeated: the delivered penalty_tx is invalid, so a revoked-state broadcast succeeds and the peer takes up to the victim's entire channel balance from the chosen old state (integrity of funds HIGH). No confidentiality impact. Availability impact limited to loss of the channel.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the remote channel peer (threat-model adversary 1), acting over the network with no user interaction. The script mismatch is under the attacker's control: it chooses its own to_self_delay at open/accept (any value <= max-locktime-blocks is accepted, openingd/common.c:36) so that it differs from the victim's watchtime-blocks, or it leases the channel; mixed-implementation defaults already differ. Attack requirement (AT:P): the victim must be offline for longer than its own to_self_delay and be relying on a watchtower fed by the commitment_revocation hook - the exact scenario the hook exists to defend - because an online lightningd's onchaind path builds the penalty correctly. Privileges: a channel with the victim (PR:L). No special skill: hold an old commitment and broadcast it while the victim is down.

## Recommended fix
1. penalty_tx_create() derives the peer's to_local witness script from the wrong side's to_self_delay (channel->config[REMOTE] instead of config[LOCAL]), so the script hash does not match the revoked commitment's output. Fix criteria: The witness script used for the penalty input must be byte-identical to the one commit_tx() put in the peer's commitment for that output (same to_self_delay source as channel_txs(side == REMOTE)). Verify with a channel whose two to_self_delay values differ (e.g. different watchtime-blocks per node): the hook's penalty_tx must be accepted by bitcoind and spend the revoked to_local output.
2. The lease CSV is hard-coded to 1, so for option_will_fund channels where the peer is lessor the script also mismatches while lease remaining > to_self_delay. Fix criteria: The penalty script must use the same csv_lock (lease_expiry vs the blockheight used for that commitment) that commit_tx() used; verify with a leased channel that the hook's penalty_tx is valid before lease expiry.

# Peer-chosen CompactSize witness item count in splice tx_signatures is passed unbounded to wally_tx_witness_stack_init_alloc, aborting channeld

## Details
When finalizing the peer's inputs after receiving splice `tx_signatures`, channeld hands each peer-supplied `witness_data` blob (u16 length, max 65535 bytes) to psbt_finalize_input() -> psbt_input_set_final_witness_stack() (common/psbt_internal.c:59-88). That function decodes the leading CompactSize element count from the attacker's bytes (varint_get accepts 0xff-prefixed 64-bit values) and uses it, with no bound against the remaining blob length and no cap, as the pre-allocation count for wally_tx_witness_stack_init_alloc(size, ...). The return value is ignored and the subsequent wally_tx_witness_stack_add() is assert()ed.

Established from this repository: libwally's allocations go through CLN's tal-backed allocator (common/setup.c:11-26), and tal aborts the process when malloc fails (ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c:89, 257-261; no daemon installs another errorfn). A count such as 2^50 makes libwally request count * sizeof(struct wally_tx_witness_item) bytes, malloc fails, and lightning_channeld aborts. Had the allocation returned NULL instead, in->final_witness would be NULL and the assert(ok) at line 82 would abort on the first element. Either way the crash is deterministic and repeatable on every reconnect while the splice inflight exists.

Assumption (external/libwally-core is a submodule not present in the checkout; CHANGELOG pins v1.5.6): wally_tx_witness_stack_init_alloc computes allocation_len * sizeof(*items) without overflow checking. If so, a count of 2^60 wraps the byte size to 0; tal returns a valid zero-length allocation, items_allocation_len records 2^60, and each attacker-supplied element (pointer + attacker-chosen length) is written out of bounds of the zero-length heap block by wally_tx_witness_stack_add. That variant could not be verified here and is therefore not reflected in the impact metrics; it should be checked when fixing.

Reachability: splicing is enabled by default (lightningd/options.c:1515-1519, OPT_SPLICE at lightningd.c:940). The remote peer initiates a splice, contributes at least one input via tx_add_input (so there is a remote-serial input to finalize), completes commitment exchange and sends tx_signatures carrying shared_input_signature and one witness blob whose leading CompactSize is huge. Nothing validates the blob's structure before the allocation (channeld.c:4186-4213); lightningd treats the subdaemon death as a transient channel failure.

## Evidence
1. [common/psbt\_internal.c:59–87](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/psbt_internal.c#L59-L87)
   psbt_input_set_final_witness_stack() decodes the leading CompactSize `size` from the peer's witness_data (next_size, line 71) and passes it straight to wally_tx_witness_stack_init_alloc(size, &in->final_witness) at line 77 with no check against the remaining blob length or any cap; the return value is ignored and the following wally_tx_witness_stack_add() result is assert()ed (line 82). This is the code the fix must change.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:4186–4212](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4186-L4212)
   Once both funding-input signatures are present (ours is set at 4019 when send_signature, theirs stored unverified at 4135), resume_splice_negotiation() calls psbt_finalize_input(current_psbt, in, inws[j]) for every remote-serial, non-funding input with the witness blob taken verbatim from the peer's tx_signatures (fromwire_tx_signatures at 4098, inws). Reached for the splice accepter via line 4553 and for the initiator via lines 4885/5085.
3. [ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c:257–261](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/ccan/ccan/tal/tal.c#L257-L261)
   libwally's allocation is routed to tal (common/setup.c:11-26 cln_wally_tal); tal's allocate() calls call_error("allocation failed") when malloc returns NULL, and the default errorfn (line 89) is abort(). No CLN daemon overrides it (tal_set_backend is called only in cli/lightning-cli.c), so a huge request aborts lightning_channeld deterministically.
4. [bitcoin/varint.c:45–69](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/bitcoin/varint.c#L45-L69)
   varint_get accepts the 0xff prefix and returns a full 64-bit value, so the item count is attacker-chosen up to 2^64-1 even though witness_data itself is bounded to 65535 bytes by its u16 `len` field (wire/peer_wire.csv:79-81).
5. [openingd/dualopend.c:1445](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L1445)
   Second call site of the same sink in dual-funding tx_signatures handling (filed separately as dualopend-tx-signatures-witness-count-unbounded-alloc); the fix in psbt_internal.c covers both.

## Impact
Established impact: lightning_channeld for that channel aborts (tal allocation failure -> abort, or assert(ok)), interrupting the channel and the splice; the peer can repeat it on each reconnect while the inflight exists (A:LOW, one channel's daemon, not the node). No confidentiality impact. Integrity is rated NONE because the out-of-bounds heap write variant depends on libwally v1.5.6's unchecked size multiplication, which is not verifiable in this checkout; if confirmed, integrity (and possibly confidentiality) would rise substantially.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any remote Lightning peer with a channel to the victim (AT:PRESENT: a channel must exist, which the attacker can open itself; splicing is default-on) initiates a splice, adds one input, and sends tx_signatures whose witness_data begins with a 0xff CompactSize of e.g. 2^50. No authentication beyond the BOLT8 peer connection (PR:NONE), no user interaction, no defence to bypass (AC:LOW); the abort is deterministic.

## Recommended fix
1. psbt_input_set_final_witness_stack() trusts the peer-encoded CompactSize element count and forwards it as an allocation size, and treats allocation/add failure as an assertion instead of a peer error. Fix criteria: Before any allocation, the item count must be bounded by what the remaining blob can contain (count <= remaining bytes) and by a hard cap on witness elements; allocation or parse failure must be reported to the caller. After the fix, a witness blob with count 2^50 or 2^60 is rejected without allocating or aborting.
2. channeld (and dualopend) pass raw peer witness blobs into finalization without first validating their structure, and psbt_finalize_input has no failure return ('FIXME: return an error??'). Fix criteria: psbt_finalize_input must return failure on malformed witness data, and both callers must turn that failure into a peer protocol failure (peer_failed_warn / open_err_warn) rather than continuing or crashing.

# LSPS2 service never enforces min_payment_size_msat: HTLC floor check compares against min_fee_msat

## Details
In the LSPS2 (bLIP-52) JIT-channel service, the opening_fee_params menu the operator's policy plugin returns carries two distinct lower bounds: min_fee_msat (the minimum opening fee) and min_payment_size_msat (the smallest payment for which the LSP will open a channel). Both are covered by the HMAC promise (proto/lsps2.rs:186-193) and are therefore operator-fixed. For a no-MPP buy (payment_size_msat absent, so lsps2.buy's validate() performs no amount check at all, core/lsps2/service.rs:101-106), the only amount check on the incoming HTLC is HtlcAcceptedHookHandler::handle step C (core/lsps2/htlc.rs:134), which rejects the HTLC when amount < min_fee_msat. min_payment_size_msat is never read anywhere on the service path (the only comparison against it in the tree is on the client side, client.rs:214). The upper bound at htlc.rs:142 correctly uses max_payment_size_msat.

Consequence: after the fee gate at htlc.rs:156 (fee + 1000 msat < amount, where fee = max(amount*ppm/1e6, min_fee_msat)), any HTLC of min_fee_msat + 1001 msat or more passes, and the service asks the policy for a capacity and calls fund_jit_channel -> fundchannel (zero-conf, LSP wallet funds, cln_adapters/rpc.rs:52-77) for the full policy capacity. Whenever the operator's policy sets min_payment_size_msat above min_fee_msat (+1000 msat) -- the only configuration in which the floor has independent meaning, e.g. min_fee 1 sat, proportional 1%, min_payment_size 100,000 sat intending a 1,000 sat minimum fee -- a peer can lsps2.buy from any connected node and route an HTLC of a few sats to the JIT scid; the LSP funds the channel, pays the on-chain fee and locks the policy capacity while collecting only min_fee_msat. RejectReason::AmountBelowMinimum also reports min_fee_msat as the minimum. When min_payment_size_msat <= min_fee_msat the fee gate subsumes the floor and the defect has no effect.

The triggering inputs are the lsps2.buy request (any peer, no authentication) and the HTLC amount (authored by the payer, who may be the same peer). The code runs only when the operator enables `experimental-lsps2-service` with a promise secret and a policy plugin, i.e. whenever the LSP service is in use (doc/lightningd-config.5.md:902-912).

## Evidence
1. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs:134–140](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs#L134-L140)
   Step C's lower bound compares the HTLC amount against opening_fee_params.min_fee_msat and reports it as the minimum; opening_fee_params.min_payment_size_msat is never read. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs:150–169](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs#L150-L169)
   The only remaining gate: compute_opening_fee (max(amount*ppm, min_fee)) + htlc_minimum_msat (hard-coded 1000) must be < amount, so an HTLC of min_fee_msat + 1001 msat is accepted regardless of min_payment_size_msat.
3. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs:171–202](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs#L171-L202)
   After the gates the handler queries the policy for a channel capacity and calls fund_jit_channel for that full capacity; the policy request carries init_payment_size but the shipped policy examples do not re-check the floor.
4. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln\_adapters/rpc.rs:52–77](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln_adapters/rpc.rs#L52-L77)
   fund_jit_channel is a fundchannel RPC from the LSP's own wallet (mindepth 0, unannounced) for the policy capacity: the sink that spends on-chain fees and locks LSP capital.
5. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/proto/lsps2.rs:166–193](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/proto/lsps2.rs#L166-L193)
   OpeningFeeParams carries min_payment_size_msat as a field distinct from min_fee_msat, and the promise HMAC covers it, so it is an operator-fixed bound the service is expected to enforce.
6. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/service.rs:96–127](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/service.rs#L96-L127)
   handle_buy accepts a buy from any peer_id; with payment_size_msat absent (no-MPP mode) validate() performs no amount check, so nothing upstream of the HTLC handler enforces min_payment_size_msat.
7. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs:154–200](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs#L154-L200)
   The htlc_accepted hook hands the incoming HTLC's amount_msat (set by the payer) and onion scid straight to HtlcAcceptedHookHandler::handle; the plugin is active whenever experimental-lsps2-service is set (lines 22-25, 92).

## Impact
The LSP's configured payment floor is bypassed: the node performs a fundchannel it configured itself to refuse (integrity of policy enforcement, low), spending on-chain fees and locking policy-sized capital per cheap HTLC while collecting only min_fee_msat (availability of LSP wallet liquidity, low). No funds are stolen and no secrets are exposed.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any node that can connect to the LSP sends lsps2.get_info and lsps2.buy (custommsg, no authentication) without payment_size_msat, obtains a JIT scid, and routes an HTLC of min_fee_msat + 1001 msat to it from any node (possibly itself). No privileges or user interaction. The impact exists only under the operator's policy configuration in which min_payment_size_msat exceeds min_fee_msat + 1000 msat; otherwise the fee gate subsumes the floor.

## Recommended fix
1. The HTLC lower-bound check in HtlcAcceptedHookHandler::handle reads opening_fee_params.min_fee_msat where the promised opening_fee_params.min_payment_size_msat is the bound the LSP committed to. Fix criteria: An incoming HTLC whose amount is below opening_fee_params.min_payment_size_msat is failed before any policy capacity query or fundchannel call, and the rejection reports that value; the existing fee-coverage check is retained. A unit test with min_payment_size_msat > min_fee_msat and an HTLC between the two asserts rejection with no fund_jit_channel call.
2. lsps2.buy with payment_size_msat present validates only fee coverage, not the [min_payment_size_msat, max_payment_size_msat] range, so the floor is unenforced on that path too once MPP flows fund channels. Fix criteria: A buy whose payment_size_msat lies outside [min_payment_size_msat, max_payment_size_msat] is refused with the bLIP-52 payment_size_too_small / payment_size_too_large error.

# Unterminated Unix-socket peer address from getpeername() makes lightningd fatal() on peer_connected

## Details
When connectd is configured to listen on a Unix domain socket (--bind-addr=/path, doc/lightningd-config.5.md 'bind-addr'; setup_listeners() case ADDR_INTERNAL_SOCKNAME, connectd/connectd.c:1490-1506), connection_in() calls get_remote_address() (connectd/connectd.c:489-517) which, for AF_UNIX, does memcpy(addr->u.sockname, sun->sun_path, sizeof(sun->sun_path)) with no check that the copied 108 bytes contain a NUL terminator. On Linux a client may bind() its own socket to a pathname of exactly sizeof(sun_path) (108) bytes with no terminating NUL (bind accepts addrlen == sizeof(struct sockaddr_un)), and getpeername() returns that sun_path verbatim, so the sockname is unterminated.

The address is struct-copied unchanged through the handshake (connectd/handshake.c h->addr = *addr) and init exchange (connectd/peer_exchange_initmsg.c peer->addr = *addr). After a successful Noise handshake and init, peer_connected() (connectd/connectd.c:424-440) serialises it into connectd_peer_connected / connectd_peer_reconnected with towire_wireaddr_internal(), which writes all 108 raw bytes. On the lightningd side fromwire_wireaddr_internal() (common/wireaddr.c:147-153) requires a NUL inside sockname and fails otherwise, so fromwire_connectd_peer_connected() returns false, fromwire_connectd_peer_reconnected() also fails, and handle_peer_connected() calls fatal("Connectd gave bad CONNECT_PEER_(RE)CONNECTED message") (lightningd/peer_control.c:1873-1891): the whole node aborts, repeatably on every restart while the attacker reconnects.

Attacker position: any local process that can connect() to the peer Unix socket (write permission on the socket inode) and knows the victim's public node_id to complete the Noise handshake; no rune, RPC-socket or lightning-dir access is required. connectd never chmods the socket (make_listen_fd), so its mode is 0777 & ~umask of the operator's shell/service (lightningd's umask(0) in complete_daemonize runs after connectd has already bound). With a 022 umask only same-uid processes (the operator) can connect; a different-uid local user reaches it where the umask is 002/000 or the operator has relaxed the socket's mode so another service account can peer over it. Remote peers arriving through a proxy that forwards to the Unix socket (e.g. Tor HiddenServicePort to a unix: target) cannot exploit it, because the proxy's client socket is unnamed and the attacker does not author sun_path. The same unterminated buffer is also formatted with "%s" in fmt_wireaddr_internal() (common/wireaddr.c:252) for connectd log lines, an over-read bounded in practice by the enclosing struct. Reachable only when a Unix-socket bind address is configured (non-default).

## Evidence
1. [connectd/connectd.c:512–516](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L512-L516)
   get_remote_address() AF_UNIX branch: memcpy(addr->u.sockname, sun->sun_path, sizeof(sun->sun_path)) copies all 108 bytes of the getpeername() result into the 108-byte sockname with no check that a NUL is present. A client that bind()s to a 108-byte pathname (Linux accepts addrlen == sizeof(struct sockaddr_un)) yields an unterminated sockname. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [common/wireaddr.c:147–152](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/wireaddr.c#L147-L152)
   fromwire_wireaddr_internal() for ADDR_INTERNAL_SOCKNAME reads the 108 raw bytes written by towire_wireaddr_internal() (lines 111-113) and calls fromwire_fail() when memchr() finds no NUL, so lightningd's parse of the connectd message fails.
3. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:1873–1891](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L1873-L1891)
   handle_peer_connected(): when fromwire_connectd_peer_connected() fails it tries fromwire_connectd_peer_reconnected(), and when that also fails calls fatal("Connectd gave bad CONNECT_PEER_(RE)CONNECTED message"), terminating lightningd.
4. [connectd/connectd.c:1490–1506](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L1490-L1506)
   setup_listeners() case ADDR_INTERNAL_SOCKNAME binds and listens on a Unix-domain socket for --bind-addr=/path (documented in doc/lightningd-config.5.md 'bind-addr'); make_listen_fd() applies no chmod, so the socket's mode is 0777 & ~umask and connectd inherits the operator's umask (connectd_init at lightningd.c:1338 runs before complete_daemonize's umask(0) at :1504).
5. [connectd/connectd.c:424–439](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/connectd.c#L424-L439)
   peer_connected() serialises the unmodified per-connection addr (struct-copied through handshake.c h->addr and peer_exchange_initmsg.c peer->addr) into connectd_peer_connected / connectd_peer_reconnected via towire_wireaddr_internal() and sends it to lightningd after the Noise handshake and init exchange succeed.

## Impact
Deterministic termination of lightningd via fatal() and therefore the whole node, repeatable on every restart while the attacker is present: a node-down DoS with on-chain consequences (missed HTLC timeouts, inability to respond to channel closes). No confidentiality or integrity effect; the fmt_wireaddr_internal over-read only reaches connectd's own log output.

## Reproduction steps
1. Local attacker (a process with write permission on the node's Unix peer socket, running as a uid other than the operator's) binds its client socket to a 108-byte unterminated pathname, connects, completes the public Noise handshake (needs only the victim's node_id) and sends a valid init. connectd forwards the unterminated address and lightningd fatal()s deterministically. Attack requirements: the non-default --bind-addr=/path Unix listener must be configured and the socket must be connectable by the attacker's uid (umask 002/000 or operator chmod; connectd itself does not restrict the mode). Assumes Linux AF_UNIX semantics (kernel accepts bind() with addrlen == sizeof(struct sockaddr_un) and a 108-byte non-NUL-terminated sun_path, and getpeername() returns the stored address bytes verbatim); this behaviour is not verifiable from the checkout.

## Recommended fix
connectd trusts the kernel-supplied peer sun_path to be NUL-terminated and copies all sizeof(sun_path) bytes into the equally-sized sockname buffer, then forwards it unchecked; lightningd treats the resulting unparsable address as a connectd bug and calls fatal(). Fix criteria: connectd must guarantee the sockname it stores is NUL-terminated (bounded copy that always leaves a terminator, or reject/replace unterminated peer paths with an unnamed-socket placeholder), and lightningd should not fatal() on a malformed per-peer address from connectd. Verify: a client bound to a 108-byte unterminated path connecting through the Unix listener completes the connection or is dropped without lightningd exiting.

# lsps2.buy lets any peer create unlimited, never-reclaimed datastore rows in the wallet DB

## Details
The LSPS2 service plugin (cln-lsps-service, shipped and loaded by default, active only when the operator sets `experimental-lsps2-service` and `experimental-lsps2-promise-secret` and installs an LSP-Policy plugin as doc/lightningd-config.5.md:902-912 requires) answers `lsps2.buy` from any connected peer by writing a new record into lightningd's datastore, i.e. a row in the wallet database (service.rs:117-127, rpc.rs:106-147, lightningd/datastore.c:196-200 → wallet.c:6481).

Root cause: allocation of a persistent resource on behalf of an unauthenticated peer with no limit and no reclamation. `OpeningFeeParams::validate` (proto/lsps2.rs:178-204) only recomputes the HMAC promise and checks `valid_until`; it does not record promise use, so a single `lsps2.get_info` menu entry (valid for whatever window the operator's policy chooses — one hour in the project's test policy) authorises unlimited `lsps2.buy` calls. `handle_buy` keeps no count of outstanding buys per peer or globally (its own FIXME at service.rs:115-116 notes the datastore is never consulted). The only deletion is in the htlc_accepted handler (htlc.rs:123-131), which removes a record only when an HTLC for that exact scid arrives after `valid_until`; records for scids never paid to, and records whose JIT channel was successfully opened, are never removed, and there is no periodic or block-driven sweep. lightningd's `datastore` command enforces no row or size cap.

Bound: `generate_jit` (proto/lsps2.rs:68-78) picks one of 50,000 scids at block height+12 and MUST_CREATE rejects duplicates, so a peer can add at most ~50,000 rows (~400 bytes each, ~20 MB) per block height; the key space renews every block, so the total is unbounded over time and survives restarts. Each call also costs the LSP a `getinfo` and a `datastore` RPC round trip. Because the rows persist indefinitely in the node's wallet DB (sqlite3/PostgreSQL) rather than being transient load, this is an attacker-driven resource leak, not volumetric traffic. Reachable by any peer connected over BOLT8 (no channel required) whose token the operator's policy does not reject.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/service.rs:96–137](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/service.rs#L96-L137)
   handle_buy: for every lsps2.buy whose opening_fee_params carries a valid promise it generates a fresh random JIT scid and calls store_buy_request, with no per-peer or global cap on outstanding buy records and no check that the promise was already used. The FIXME at 115-116 acknowledges the datastore is never consulted.
2. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln\_adapters/rpc.rs:106–147](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln_adapters/rpc.rs#L106-L147)
   store_buy_request persists the JSON record (peer id, full fee params, payment size) via lightningd `datastore` MUST_CREATE under [lsps, lsps2, <scid>]; lightningd/datastore.c imposes no row or size cap and wallet.c:6481 INSERTs it into the wallet DB, so each request becomes a durable DB row.
3. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs:122–131](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs#L122-L131)
   The only deletion path in the plugin: del_buy_request runs solely when an HTLC later arrives for that exact scid after valid_until. There is no sweep of expired records and no deletion after a successful JIT open, so records for scids never paid to live forever.
4. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/proto/lsps2.rs:178–203](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/proto/lsps2.rs#L178-L203)
   validate() checks only the HMAC over the fee parameters and that valid_until is in the future; nothing records a promise as consumed, so one lsps2.get_info response authorises an unbounded number of lsps2.buy calls until the policy's valid_until.
5. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/proto/lsps2.rs:68–77](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/proto/lsps2.rs#L68-L77)
   generate_jit draws tx_idx in 0..5000 and output_idx in 0..10 at block height+12, so MUST_CREATE collisions cap growth at 50,000 rows per block height; the cap resets every block, so growth over time is unbounded and (as a side effect) a peer that fills the space makes legitimate buys at that height fail with internal error.
6. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln\_adapters/hooks.rs:31–54](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln_adapters/hooks.rs#L31-L54)
   service_custommsg_hook dispatches every LSPS0-framed custom message from any connected peer (forwarded by connectd/multiplex.c:999-1028 regardless of channel state) to the router and thus to handle_buy with that peer's id.

## Impact
Unbounded, persistent growth of the LSP node's wallet database (up to ~20 MB per block height, sustained indefinitely) plus two lightningd RPC calls per request; the rows are never reclaimed and require manual cleanup, and filling a height's scid space also makes legitimate buys at that height fail. Degradation and eventual disk pressure rather than an immediate outage: availability LOW. No data disclosure; the rows live in the plugin's own datastore namespace, so no integrity impact on other state.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker connects to the LSP as an ordinary Lightning peer (no channel), sends one `lsps2.get_info` to obtain a promised fee menu, then replays `lsps2.buy` with that menu over the LSPS0 custom-message channel as fast as the LSP answers; each accepted call inserts a durable wallet-DB row. No defence stands in the way; the only condition is the LSP having enabled the experimental LSPS2 service with a policy plugin that offers the peer a menu (non-default configuration).

## Recommended fix
1. handle_buy allocates a persistent datastore record for every valid lsps2.buy with no bound on outstanding records per peer or in total, and promises are accepted an unlimited number of times. Fix criteria: The number of unconsumed buy records a single peer, and the service overall, can hold outstanding is capped (or buys are throttled) so that repeated lsps2.buy from one peer stops creating rows once the cap is reached. Verify by spamming lsps2.buy from a test peer and confirming the datastore row count under [lsps, lsps2] stops growing at the cap.
2. Buy records are released only when an HTLC arrives for the scid after valid_until; expired and consumed records are otherwise never removed, so the wallet DB grows permanently. Fix criteria: Expired records (past valid_until) and records whose JIT channel has been opened are removed on a schedule or on block/notification events independent of HTLC arrival. Verify that rows created by lsps2.buy disappear after valid_until without any HTLC, and that a successful JIT open removes its record.

# Upstream peer's HTLC extra_tlvs misparsed by LSPS2 service, re-encoded invalid, crashes lightningd

## Details
The cln-lsps-service plugin's htlc_accepted hook deserialises the upstream peer's update_add_htlc TLV extension (`htlc.extra_tlvs`) into a TlvStream via `TlvStream::from_bytes_auto` (core/tlv.rs:116-124). That function guesses whether the bytes carry a BigSize length prefix: if the first BigSize equals the remaining length it treats the rest as the stream. lightningd serialises `extra_tlvs` as raw records with no length prefix (peer_htlcs.c:1633-1635), so a peer that controls the first TLV type can make the guess succeed and the plugin parse a completely different record set. `from_bytes` does not apply the BOLT1 unknown-even rule, so the misparsed set may contain an unknown even type.

On the JIT success path (htlc.rs:225-232) the plugin re-encodes that misparsed set, adds type 65537, and returns it as `extra_tlvs` in the hook response. lightningd re-parses with `fromwire_tlv_update_add_htlc_tlvs`, which only knows type 0, fails on any unknown even type (wire/tlvstream.c:206-218), and calls `fatal()` (peer_htlcs.c:1115-1121), aborting lightningd.

Concrete input: upstream sends update_add_htlc with TLV type 3, length 2, value 01 AA (bytes `03 02 01 AA`). channeld accepts it (odd unknown type is kept in `tlvs->fields`, channeld.c:682-722). The plugin's auto-detect reads BigSize 3 == remaining 3 bytes, then parses `02 01 AA` as type 2, length 1 — an unknown even type. It re-encodes `02 01 AA fe 00 01 00 01 08 <fee>` and lightningd dies.

Attacker: a remote peer with a channel to the LSP (so it is the direct upstream and authors the update_add_htlc TLVs) who has also obtained a JIT scid via lsps2.get_info/lsps2.buy from any node it controls, and whose client node accepts the zero-conf channel so the handler reaches step G. The attacker pays no opening fee: the crash happens before the forward. After restart, htlcs_resubmit replays the hook; the buy record is still in the datastore so the plugin funds a second channel to the attacker (on-chain fee and locked liquidity) and then forwards normally. The attacker can repeat with a new HTLC for as long as the promise is valid.

The threat model lists lightningd crashing on peer input as a DoS with on-chain consequences. This plugin ships in PLUGINS (plugins/Makefile:156) and is enabled via `experimental-lsps2-service`.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs:116–124](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs#L116-L124)
   TlvStream::from_bytes_auto first tries from_bytes_with_length_prefix: if the leading BigSize equals the remaining byte count it parses the remainder as the stream. The upstream peer chooses the first TLV type, so for `03 02 01 AA` the guess succeeds and the plugin sees record {type 2, value AA} where lightningd saw {type 3, value 01 AA}.
2. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs:213–227](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/tlv.rs#L213-L227)
   The serde Deserialize impl (used for Htlc.extra_tlvs) routes every hex field through from_bytes_auto; from_bytes applies no unknown-even rule, so the misparsed even type is accepted.
3. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln\_adapters/types.rs:29–39](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/cln_adapters/types.rs#L29-L39)
   Htlc.extra_tlvs: Option<TlvStream> is the hook field populated from the upstream peer's update_add_htlc TLVs.
4. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs:220–232](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/core/lsps2/htlc.rs#L220-L232)
   Step G clones the misparsed extra_tlvs, adds type 65537 (opening fee) and returns HtlcDecision::Forward.
5. [plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs:203–239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/lsps-plugin/src/service.rs#L203-L239)
   decision_to_response/json_continue_forward serialise extra_tlvs.to_bytes() into the hook response's "extra_tlvs" field with no validation against update_add_htlc_tlvs rules.
6. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1095–1136](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1095-L1136)
   htlc_accepted_hook_deserialize re-parses the plugin's extra_tlvs with fromwire_tlv_update_add_htlc_tlvs (extra_types NULL, only type 0 known) and calls fatal() when the parse fails; an unknown even type such as 2 fails it.
7. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:1628–1633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L1628-L1633)
   The hook payload's extra_tlvs_raw is towire_tlvstream_raw(hin->extra_tlvs): the upstream peer's records with no length prefix (serialised as hex at line 1298-1299). This is the framing the plugin's auto-detect gets wrong.
8. [channeld/channeld.c:682–721](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L682-L721)
   handle_peer_add_htlc parses update_add_htlc; fromwire_tlv keeps unknown odd types in tlvs->fields (only unknown even fail), and channel_add_htlc stores tlvs->fields as the HTLC's extra_tlvs, which reach lightningd via added_htlc (common/htlc_wire.c:197-215, FROMWIRE_TLV_ANY_TYPE).
9. [wire/tlvstream.c:206–217](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/tlvstream.c#L206-L217)
   fromwire_tlv fails the whole stream on an unknown even type when extra_types is NULL, which is what makes the re-encoded stream rejected and the fatal() reachable.
10. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:3238–3261](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L3238-L3261)
   After the crash lightningd restarts and htlcs_resubmit replays peer_accepted_htlc for the unresolved HTLC; extra_tlvs are not persisted (wallet/wallet.c:3611-3617) so the replay does not re-crash, but the buy record is still present and the handler funds a second channel before forwarding.

## Impact
lightningd fatal() aborts the whole node: all channels offline, pending HTLCs at risk of on-chain timeout, repeatable each time the node restarts and the attacker sends another such HTLC. On each restart the replayed hook funds an additional channel to the attacker from the LSP wallet (integrity of funds allocation, low).

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote peer with a channel to the LSP (direct upstream; the normal position of an LSP's routing peer) buys a JIT scid from a node it controls, then sends an HTLC to that scid with update_add_htlc TLV bytes `03 02 01 AA`. Its client accepts the zero-conf channel so the handler reaches the forward step; the plugin's re-encoded extra_tlvs fail lightningd's parse and lightningd aborts. Requires the operator to have enabled the experimental LSPS2 service and policy plugin. No defences to bypass; deterministic.

## Recommended fix
1. TlvStream::from_bytes_auto guesses the framing of attacker-influenced bytes; extra_tlvs from the htlc_accepted hook are always unprefixed raw records, while onion.payload is always length-prefixed. Fix criteria: Each hook field is parsed with the framing lightningd actually uses (payload: length-prefixed; extra_tlvs: raw), with no heuristic. A unit test feeding `03 02 01 AA` as extra_tlvs must yield exactly one record of type 3.
2. The plugin returns a re-encoded extra_tlvs stream to lightningd without validating it against update_add_htlc_tlvs rules, and lightningd treats a bad stream as a fatal plugin bug. Fix criteria: Before returning extra_tlvs the plugin rejects or drops any record that would fail lightningd's update_add_htlc_tlvs parse (unknown even types, malformed type 0); on any parse/encode doubt it fails the HTLC instead of forwarding. Verify that no upstream-chosen TLV bytes can produce a response that aborts lightningd.

# Concurrent renepay payments share the fake-destination chan_extra, making the second payment fail

## Details
renepay routes every payment to a constant fake node (routing_destination = 02000...0001, main.c:373-377) and links the real destination (or each blinded-path introduction node) to it with a fake local channel: scid 0 for BOLT11 (selfpay_cb, mods.c:261-278), scid i for blinded path i (blindedhints_cb, 619-646). add_hintchan (mods.c:478-541) creates that channel's chan_extra in the *plugin-global* pay_plugin->uncertainty, makes it a tal child of the *payment's* local_gossmods, and adds the channel to the payment's local_gossmods only when the chan_extra did not already exist (FIXME at 527-530 acknowledges the race).

Two renepay payments to different invoices that overlap in time (A pending, B started) therefore interact as follows:
1. B's selfpay_cb (slot 6) finds A's scid-0 chan_extra (getmychannels at slot 4 never runs uncertainty_update), takes the else branch and never adds dest_B -> routing_destination to B's local_gossmods.
2. B's compute_routes applies only B's mods (mods.c:700); gossmap_find_node(routing_destination) is NULL (routebuilder.c:204-210) and B fails at once with PAY_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND 'Destination is unknown in the network gossip' although the invoice is payable (mods.c:738-755: nothing in flight, so payment_fail). For BOLT12 B loses exactly the blinded paths whose index collides with A's.
3. B's routehints_done (582-592) or refreshgossmap_cb (427-450, if the store changed) runs uncertainty_update with only B's mods applied; uncertainty.c:86-94 tal_frees A's scid-0 chan_extra and A's private route-hint chan_extras. When A later retries, those channels have no chan_extra and are disabled (routebuilder.c:185-195), or, if the store changed, A's refreshgossmap re-creates the scid-0 chan_extra via new_chan_extra, which has no destructor (chan_extra.c:88-116) and lives on in the global map after A ends; each later payment that finds it skips its own fake channel and fails until some payment's uncertainty_update deletes it, so payments fail alternately.

No attacker is needed for the failure (any two overlapping renepay invocations to different invoices trigger it; tests/test_renepay.py::test_concurrency pays the *same* invoice five times, which merges into one payment, so it does not cover this). A payment counterparty or any routing node on a renepay path controls how long A stays pending: it may withhold the HTLC resolution until CLTV expiry (hours) and A's sleep/collect_results loop (mods.c:1328-1331) has no timeout. For that whole window every renepay the operator issues to any other invoice fails immediately, and A itself is sabotaged on retry — a cross-payment denial beyond the single stuck HTLC the protocol already permits. The operator can fall back to pay/xpay; no funds are at risk.

Reachability: cln-renepay is built (plugins/Makefile:136) and loaded by default (lightningd/plugin.c:2585, the one non-important builtin); the renepay command is deprecated in v26.06 (removal v27.03) but remains callable because allow-deprecated-apis defaults true outside --developer. No memory-safety consequence: chan_extra users look objects up by scid per call and return RENEPAY_CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND when absent; the destructor's second chan_extra_map_del is a harmless failed htable_del.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:478–540](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L478-L540)
   Primary location (the fix must change this). add_hintchan looks the scid up in the plugin-global pay_plugin->uncertainty. If a chan_extra already exists (here: created by another payment still in flight, keyed by the same fake scid) it takes the else branch and does NOT add the channel to this payment's local_gossmods. Otherwise it creates the chan_extra, tal_steals it into this payment's local_gossmods and attaches a destructor removing it from the global map (525-533); the FIXME at 527-530 acknowledges the concurrent-payment race.
2. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:261–277](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L261-L277)
   selfpay_cb runs for every non-BOLT12 payment and calls add_hintchan(destination -> routing_destination, scid 0). routing_destination is the same constant for every payment (main.c:373-377), so every BOLT11 payment collides on scid 0 and needs its own local channel with that scid to reach the routing target at all.
3. [plugins/renepay/routebuilder.c:179–209](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routebuilder.c#L179-L209)
   get_routes disables every gossmap channel without a chan_extra (185-195) and fails with PAY_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND 'Destination is unknown in the network gossip' when gossmap_find_node(routing_destination) is NULL (204-210). compute_routes_cb applies only the current payment's local_gossmods (mods.c:700), so for the second payment the fake node does not exist and, with nothing in flight, mods.c:738-755 calls payment_fail.
4. [plugins/renepay/main.c:367–376](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/main.c#L367-L376)
   payment->routing_destination is the fixed node id 02000...0001 for every payment, so two concurrent payments always collide on scid 0 (BOLT11) or scid i (BOLT12 blinded path i, mods.c:633).
5. [plugins/renepay/uncertainty.c:74–121](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/uncertainty.c#L74-L121)
   uncertainty_update tal_frees every chan_extra whose scid is not in the gossmap as currently modified (86-94) and re-creates missing ones via new_chan_extra, owned by the map with no destructor (98-117). It is called with only the *current* payment's local mods applied (mods.c:436-441, 583-586), so payment B's call frees payment A's fake-channel and hint chan_extras, and A's later refresh re-creates its scid-0 chan_extra as a permanent global object.
6. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:582–591](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L582-L591)
   routehints_done applies this payment's local mods and calls uncertainty_update: for payment B this is where payment A's scid-0 and hint chan_extras are freed. refreshgossmap_cb (427-450) does the same whenever the gossip store changed. getmychannels (300-420) never calls uncertainty_update, so nothing clears A's stale scid-0 chan_extra before B's selfpay runs.
7. [plugins/renepay/chan\_extra.c:88–115](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/chan_extra.c#L88-L115)
   new_chan_extra attaches no destructor, so a scid-0 chan_extra re-created by uncertainty_update outlives every payment; later payments then see 'ce exists', skip their own fake channel and fail until some other payment's uncertainty_update (run without scid 0 in its view) deletes it again.
8. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:1311–1334](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L1311-L1334)
   Program order: selfpay (slot 6) runs before refreshgossmap (8) and routehints (10), so a payment never removes a stale global scid-0 chan_extra before deciding whether to add its own fake channel; and the sleep/collect_results loop (26-30) has no timeout, so a payment whose HTLC is withheld stays pending, keeping its chan_extra alive, until the hop resolves it.

## Impact
Concurrent renepay payments fail spuriously (PAY_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND / no feasible flow) for as long as the attacker holds the first payment's HTLC, and the shared uncertainty-network knowledge for hint and fake channels is destroyed or left as a stale global object, so later payments can alternately fail. lightningd, channels and the pay/xpay engines are unaffected and the operator can retry or fall back, so availability impact is partial (A:L). Routing knowledge is perturbed but no payment is mis-sent and no funds are at risk, so integrity and confidentiality are unaffected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker position: the payee of a renepay payment or any routing node on its path (threat-model adversaries 1 and 3), who authors the HTLC resolution timing. It accepts the HTLC and withholds the resolution (BOLT 2 permits this until CLTV expiry), keeping payment A in renepay's sleep/collect_results loop (mods.c:1328-1331), which has no timeout. Every renepay payment B the victim starts in that window hits add_hintchan's existing-chan_extra branch (mods.c:534-541) and fails at get_routes (routebuilder.c:204-210); B's uncertainty_update (uncertainty.c:86-94) also destroys A's fake/hint chan_extras so A fails on retry. Remote over the Lightning network (AV:N), no defence to bypass (AC:L); the attacker must be on a renepay path and the victim must issue another renepay payment during the hold (AT:P); the victim consciously chose to pay to/through the attacker with renepay and then issues further payments (UI:A); no privileges on the victim node (PR:N). The defect also fires with no attacker whenever the operator runs two renepay payments concurrently.

## Recommended fix
Per-payment fake and hint channels get their chan_extra in the plugin-global uncertainty network keyed only by scid, with lifetime tied to one payment's local_gossmods; another payment misreads the presence of that object as 'public channel already known' and its uncertainty_update frees objects it does not own. Fix criteria: Two renepay payments started while one another is pending (same or different destinations, BOLT11 or BOLT12) both compute routes and complete independently; one payment's refresh/hint processing never frees or hides another payment's fake-destination or hint chan_extras (e.g. per-payment scoping of hint knowledge, or scids/objects unique per payment); the selfpay/blinded fake channel is always present in the payment's own gossmap view.

# Disabled node removed from gossmap before retry crashes renepay in tal_disabledmap_get_bitmap

## Details
renepay keeps a per-payment list of node ids to avoid (payment->disabledmap->disabled_nodes). Entries come from (a) onion failure handling in routefail.c, where the erring node or its successor on the route is disabled for several failure codes chosen by the remote erring node (temporary/permanent_node_failure, required_node_feature_missing, invalid_onion_payload, incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details, mpp_timeout from an intermediate: hops[erring_index-1]; invalid_onion_blinding and, by fall-through, invalid_onion_version/hmac/key: hops[erring_index]), and (b) the RPC `exclude` parameter. On every route computation get_routes() -> tal_disabledmap_get_bitmap() (disabledmap.c:113-124) resolves each id with gossmap_find_node() and dereferences the result (node->num_chans, gossmap_nth_chan) without a NULL check.

The node ids were valid when the route was built, but the gossmap used for the next attempt is refreshed first (refreshgossmap_cb, mods.c:427-450; program slot 20 precedes compute_routes at slot 22). common/gossmap.c removes a node when its last channel is deleted (remove_chan_from_node -> remove_node, 398-430), and gossipd writes the delete record at spend-height+72 blocks (gossmap_manage_new_block, gossmap_manage.c:1424-1440; deadline set at 1464) or by the prune timer (prune_network, 409-470, deletes when either side's channel_update is older than two weeks). Only nodes from this payment's local_gossmods (listpeerchannels peers, hint nodes, the fake blinded destination) are immune because the mods are re-applied in compute_routes_cb (mods.c:700-733); any public node that was an intermediate hop is not. renepay never consults gossmap_chan_is_dying(), so a node whose channels are already spent remains routable throughout the 72-block dying window.

Remote path: the attacker is both payee and a public routing node W whose only public channel(s) it controls (e.g. W-Y with Y another attacker node that stays connected). The invoice's route hint names W as the hop to the payee, so the payer must route via W. The attacker closes W's channel(s) on-chain at block N; between N and N+71 W is still in the victim's gossmap and routable. When block N+72 is mined the attacker presents/accepts the invoice; renepay routes through W; W holds the HTLC (permitted by BOLT 2) until the victim's gossipd processes block N+72 and writes the delete records, then fails with e.g. temporary_node_failure (routefail.c:393-401 disables W). collect_results sets retry; pendingsendpays and checktimeout (mods.c:968-974, stop_time = start + retry_for, default 60 s, main.c:201-202) pass if the hold stayed inside the window; refreshgossmap_cb applies the deletion and W vanishes; get_routes dereferences NULL and the plugin segfaults. Against an automated payer (withdrawal/payout service) the attacker chooses the payment start time and the window is the victim's block-polling latency, making the race reliable; against a manual payer it is roughly 10% per attempt at the default retry_for and repeatable with fresh channels. The cost is one on-chain channel open/close per attempt.

Deterministic local reproduction: `renepay invstring exclude=[<node id not in gossmap>]` (payment.c:143-149) crashes the plugin on the first compute_routes; this is operator/rune-bearer input and therefore informational, but it also means a legitimate exclusion of a node that has since left the network kills the plugin.

Impact: SIGSEGV of cln-renepay. It is not an important plugin (lightningd/plugin.c:2585), so lightningd continues, but the `renepay` command disappears, every in-progress renepay payment loses its driver (RPC callers get a plugin-died error; HTLCs already handed to lightningd continue there) and the uncertainty-network knowledge is lost until the operator restarts the plugin. No funds are at risk.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/disabledmap.c:113–123](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/disabledmap.c#L113-L123)
   tal_disabledmap_get_bitmap() calls gossmap_find_node() for every entry of p->disabled_nodes and immediately reads node->num_chans and calls gossmap_nth_chan(node, ...) with no NULL check. gossmap_find_node() (common/gossmap.c:261-268) returns NULL for a node id not (or no longer) in the gossmap, so this is a NULL pointer dereference (SIGSEGV) of the plugin. The equivalent loop in askrene (plugins/askrene/layer.c:1336-1338) checks for NULL and skips, showing unknown disabled nodes are an expected condition.
2. [plugins/renepay/routefail.c:313–323](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routefail.c#L313-L323)
   On an INVALID_ONION_BLINDING (and, via fall-through, INVALID_ONION_VERSION/HMAC/KEY) failure from an intermediate hop, the node *after* the erring hop (route->hops[erring_index].node_id) is added to disabled_nodes. The erring node is remote and chooses the failure code.
3. [plugins/renepay/routefail.c:345–352](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routefail.c#L345-L352)
   On INCORRECT_OR_UNKNOWN_PAYMENT_DETAILS from an intermediate hop the erring node itself (hops[erring_index-1].node_id) is disabled; lines 393-401 (PERMANENT/TEMPORARY_NODE_FAILURE, REQUIRED_NODE_FEATURE_MISSING, INVALID_ONION_PAYLOAD) and 464-471 (MPP_TIMEOUT) do the same. Any routing node can therefore put its own node id into disabled_nodes with a single failure message.
4. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:427–449](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L427-L449)
   refreshgossmap_cb runs before every compute_routes (program slots 20/22, lines 1322-1326) and calls gossmap_refresh(), which applies channel deletions written by gossipd since the previous attempt.
5. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:700–732](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L700-L732)
   compute_routes_cb applies only this payment's local_gossmods (local channels from the one listpeerchannels call and payee hints) and then calls get_routes(); a public node whose channels were all deleted is absent from the map at this point.
6. [plugins/renepay/routebuilder.c:165–171](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routebuilder.c#L165-L171)
   get_routes() calls tal_disabledmap_get_bitmap(this_ctx, disabledmap, gossmap) first thing on every route computation, so a stale disabled node is dereferenced on the very next retry.
7. [common/gossmap.c:398–429](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/gossmap.c#L398-L429)
   remove_chan_from_node() calls remove_node() when a node's last channel is removed; gossmap_remove_chan() is reached from remove_channel_by_deletemsg() during gossmap_refresh()/map_catchup. A node therefore disappears from the gossmap (gossmap_find_node -> NULL) as soon as gossipd deletes its last channel.
8. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1424–1439](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1424-L1439)
   gossmap_manage_new_block() deletes a channel from gossip_store exactly when the block height reaches spend-height+72 (deadline set at 1443-1476). An attacker who closes their channels on-chain knows the deletion block in advance and can time an invoice/HTLC-hold around it.
9. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:409–469](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L409-L469)
   prune_network() (every GOSSIP_PRUNE_INTERVAL/4) also deletes channels with a stale channel_update on either side; the comment notes nodes may be left channel-less and gossmap removes them on next refresh. Second deletion trigger.
10. [plugins/renepay/payment.c:140–148](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/payment.c#L140-L148)
   payment_set_constraints() adds every node id from the RPC `exclude` parameter to disabled_nodes without checking that it exists in the gossmap: a node that is unknown (typo, or a legitimately excluded node that has since closed all channels) crashes the plugin deterministically on the first compute_routes. This path is operator/rune-holder controlled and is noted as the deterministic reproduction, not the rated attack path.
11. [lightningd/plugin.c:2576–2589](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2576-L2589)
   cln-renepay is loaded as not important, so the segfault kills only the renepay plugin (not restarted) and not lightningd.

## Impact
A NULL dereference terminates the cln-renepay process. It is registered as not important (lightningd/plugin.c:2584), so lightningd, channels and the pay/xpay engines keep running, but the renepay command and all in-progress renepay payments' state are lost until the operator restarts the plugin. Partial availability loss; no confidentiality or integrity impact; no funds at risk.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote Lightning node that is both the payee (so its route hint forces the path through its routing node W) and W itself. It pre-closes W's channels on-chain, times the invoice around the spend+72 deletion block, holds the HTLC until the victim's gossipd deletes W's channels, then returns a node-disabling failure code (routefail.c:313-324, 345-353, 393-401, 464-471). The victim's next retry refreshes the gossmap (mods.c:427-450), W is gone, and tal_disabledmap_get_bitmap dereferences NULL. No security mechanism is bypassed (AC:L) but the deletion must land inside the payment's retry_for window (AT:PRESENT; ~10% per attempt at the 60 s default, repeatable). The victim must choose to pay the attacker's invoice with renepay (UI:ACTIVE). The `exclude`-parameter trigger is deterministic but operator/rune-bearer controlled.

## Recommended fix
tal_disabledmap_get_bitmap() assumes every id in disabled_nodes resolves in the current gossmap, although the list outlives the gossmap snapshot it was built from and the `exclude` parameter is never validated against the map. Fix criteria: A disabled node id that gossmap_find_node() cannot resolve is skipped (optionally logged) and route computation proceeds; a payment whose previously disabled intermediate node has been pruned/deleted from gossip between attempts, and a renepay call whose `exclude` list names an unknown node, both complete without crashing the plugin.
