# recoverchannel SCB parser trusts len_tlv: generated modern_scb_chan reads past the input buffer

## Details
tools/gen/impl_template emits, for a subtype field that is a length-prefixed TLV stream, `fromwire_tlv_X(ctx, cursor, &(size_t){len})` with no check that `len` fits in the remaining `*plen` and without reducing `*plen` afterwards. The only such field in the tree is modern_scb_chan.tlvs with its u32 len_tlv (common/scb_wire.csv:46-47). In the generated fromwire_modern_scb_chan the TLV engine (wire/tlvstream.c) is therefore bounded by the attacker's len_tlv rather than by the real buffer: after the fixed fields it reads bigsize type/length pairs from past the end of the exact-size tal buffer, and for an unknown odd type copies `length` bytes (bounded only by len_tlv, up to 4 GiB) from that out-of-bounds memory with tal_dup_arr before skipping over it. Garbage usually terminates the stream parse within a few records (type ordering/even-type checks), but each attempt reads tens to hundreds of bytes of lightningd heap, and a 0xfe/0xff-prefixed length in that garbage makes the copy cross the heap mapping and SIGSEGV lightningd.

Because the template also returns the struct unconditionally for varsize subtypes (impl_template:181-188), fromwire_modern_scb_chan never returns NULL, so json_recoverchannel's `scb_chan == NULL` check (opening_control.c:1727) is dead and a malformed blob proceeds to stub_chan/wallet_channel_insert with zeroed fields.

Reachable path: the `recoverchannel` JSON-RPC method (lightningd/opening_control.c:1696-1790) hex-decodes caller-supplied `scb` strings straight into fromwire_modern_scb_chan. A caller who may invoke recoverchannel but is not the operator — a rune bearer over commando (always on) or clnrest whose rune permits the method — supplies the bytes. Such a rune concedes channel-recovery writes, not reading lightningd heap or crashing the node; this is the same semi-trusted-author relationship as the recorded htlc-wire-tlvstream-max-not-decremented (compromised channeld) and checkmessage (rune bearer) findings. If no rune ever grants recoverchannel, the remaining authors are the operator (emergency.recover file, RPC) and the node itself (staticbackup output; peer_storage blobs are secretstream-authenticated with the node's secret and a peer can only replay them), and the defect is latent.

An honest writer always emits len_tlv = tal_bytelen(towire_tlv_scb_tlvs(...)), so a correctly generated backup never triggers it; the problem is purely the reader's trust in the declared length.

## Evidence
1. [tools/gen/impl\_template:121–122](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/gen/impl_template#L121-L122)
   For a subtype field that is a TLV stream with a length prefix, the generator emits `field = fromwire_tlv_X(ctx, cursor, &(size_t){len});`: the declared length becomes the TLV parser's bound, it is never compared with the caller's remaining *plen, and *plen is not decremented by what the sub-parser consumed. This is the root defect; it is the generated-code sibling of the hand-written bug recorded as htlc-wire-tlvstream-max-not-decremented.
2. [common/scb\_wire.csv:46–47](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/scb_wire.csv#L46-L47)
   modern_scb_chan declares `len_tlv` as a u32 followed by `tlvs,scb_tlvs,len_tlv`, so the generated fromwire_modern_scb_chan takes this template path; this is the only length-prefixed TLV subtype field in any CSV in the tree (checked by scanning all csv files).
3. [lightningd/opening\_control.c:1711–1730](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/opening_control.c#L1711-L1730)
   json_recoverchannel hex-decodes each caller-supplied `scb` string into an exact-size tal buffer (scblen = tal_count) and hands it to fromwire_modern_scb_chan with no other validation; the command is an ordinary JSON-RPC method (opening_control.c:1819) with no dev/operator gate beyond the rune check, so a commando peer or clnrest client whose rune permits `recoverchannel` controls len_tlv and every byte around it. The `scb_chan == NULL` check never fires (template 181-188).
4. [wire/tlvstream.c:155–289](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/tlvstream.c#L155-L289)
   fromwire_tlv loops `while (*max > 0)` with *max = the attacker's len_tlv, reads type/length bigsizes from *cursor (now beyond the buffer), and for an unknown odd type does tal_dup_arr(record, u8, *cursor, field.length, 0) and `*cursor += field.length`, copying up to field.length bytes of lightningd heap from past the input; the only guard is `field.length > *max` against the fake bound.
5. [tools/gen/impl\_template:181–187](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/gen/impl_template#L181-L187)
   Varsize subtypes return the allocated struct unconditionally (`return modern_scb_chan;`) rather than NULL when *cursor was set to NULL, so a malformed blob yields zeroed fields plus whatever the TLV sub-parser produced; recoverchannel's NULL check is dead and parsing errors are not surfaced.
6. [plugins/chanbackup.c:326–351](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/chanbackup.c#L326-L351)
   read_static_chan_backup parses whole backups (a `num`-element array of modern_scb_chan sharing one cursor/plen) from the emergency.recover file and from peer_storage_retrieval; both are secretstream-authenticated with the node's own secret (926-945), and json_to_scb_chan (111-135) parses lightningd's staticbackup output, so these callers are not attacker paths today but inherit the same desynchronisation if the blob is ever corrupt.

## Impact
Bytes read past the buffer are only copied into tlv_field records or parsed as scb_tlvs types; nothing out-of-bounds is returned to the caller (the response carries only the caller's own cid) and heap garbage will not decode as a valid shachain/basepoints, so confidentiality is not affected. Availability: the over-read is bounded by the attacker's len_tlv (up to 4 GiB) rather than the buffer, so a garbage 0xfe/0xff-prefixed length yields a huge tal_dup_arr memcpy (or an abort from tal on allocation failure, ccan/tal/tal.c:89) and a buffer ending at a mapping edge faults on the first bigsize read — a lightningd crash that takes every subdaemon down, but one that depends on heap layout per attempt (LOW). Integrity is not newly affected: the rune already allows inserting channel stubs.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a non-operator RPC caller holding a rune that permits `recoverchannel` — a commando peer (custom message, always on; commando.c:414-425 forwards any method checkrune accepts) or a clnrest client. One `recoverchannel ["<hex>"]` whose modern_scb_chan carries valid fixed fields and a len_tlv far larger than the bytes that follow makes fromwire_tlv read type/length bigsizes and copy up to `length` bytes from past the tal buffer (opening_control.c:1725, tlvstream.c:155-290). Retries are free and the attacker shapes the heap with earlier array elements and request sizes. Requires a rune granting recoverchannel to a non-operator, a non-default configuration (AT:PRESENT).

## Recommended fix
1. The generated subtype parser lets a declared TLV length exceed the remaining input and does not reconcile the outer bound with the bytes the TLV sub-parser consumed, breaking the fromwire invariant that *cursor + *plen bounds the buffer. Fix criteria: The generated code must fail the parse when the declared TLV length exceeds *plen, bound the TLV sub-parser by min(len, *plen), and decrement *plen by exactly the bytes consumed (failing if the sub-parser did not consume exactly len). A recoverchannel blob with len_tlv larger than its trailing bytes must produce an RPC error with no read past the buffer (verify under ASan).
2. Varsize subtype parsers return the struct even when *cursor is NULL, so callers' NULL checks (opening_control.c:1727) cannot detect malformed input. Fix criteria: fromwire_<varsize subtype> must return NULL (freeing the struct) when parsing failed, so json_recoverchannel rejects malformed SCB entries instead of inserting zeroed channel stubs.

# check listpeerchannels executes the command and returns channel data to check-only rune bearers

## Details
The `check` RPC (lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1605-1647) is documented as a safe dry-run: it validates a command's parameters "up to the point where something in the system would need to be altered" and its response schema permits only {"command_to_check": name}. Implementation-wise, json_check() switches the command into CMD_CHECK mode, marks the DB read-only, and dispatches the real handler, trusting each handler to stop at `if (command_check_only(cmd)) return command_check_done(cmd);`. Handlers that use plain param() get this for free (common/json_param.c:372-389); handlers that use param_check() must add the guard themselves.

json_listpeerchannels() (lightningd/peer_control.c:3051-3092) uses param_check() and never checks command_check_only(). Under `check listpeerchannels` it therefore executes normally: it opens a success response, iterates every peer and channel (json_add_peerchannels/json_add_channel, which only read in-memory state and so never trip the read-only DB assert), and returns the complete listpeerchannels result -- peer ids, channel ids, short_channel_ids, funding outpoints, local/remote balances, in-flight HTLC lists (payment hashes, amounts), fee settings, aliases, private-channel flags -- instead of the check acknowledgement. A sweep of every param_check() caller in lightningd/ and wallet/ shows only this handler and json_dev_finalizepsbt (wallet/walletrpc.c:1036-1069, which under check finalizes and returns the caller's own PSBT) lack the guard.

Why this crosses a trust boundary: the rune evaluator (lightningd/runes.c:847-852) authorises the *outer* method only. commando passes the peer's `method` and `params` tokens to checkrune unchanged (plugins/commando.c:420-428) and, on `valid`, forwards the same request to lightningd and relays the reply (commando.c:272-316); clnrest builds the checkrune call from the URL suffix and body (plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:309-329) and forwards after verification. For {"method":"check","params":{"command_to_check":"listpeerchannels"}} checkrune sees method=check and pnamecommand_to_check=listpeerchannels; any restriction a rune places on `listpeerchannels` itself (not being in the allowed method set, method/listpeerchannels, a pnameid=<peer> scope) is never applied. The `readonly` shorthand does not include `check` (runes.c:439), so the affected runes are those explicitly permitting `check` -- a grant operators give precisely because check is advertised as harmless validation (e.g. for a form-validating client). Any commando peer or clnrest client holding such a rune obtains the node's full channel inventory.

The DB is read-only during the call and json_add_channel performs only reads, so there is no crash or write; the impact is disclosure beyond the rune's grant and breach of the documented check contract.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/peer\_control.c:3051–3091](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_control.c#L3051-L3091)
   json_listpeerchannels() parses with param_check() (which, unlike param(), does not auto-complete in CMD_CHECK mode) and never calls command_check_only(). Under `check listpeerchannels` it therefore builds the full `channels` array via json_add_peerchannels()/json_add_channel() (in-memory reads only; no DB write, so the read-only DB flag does not trip) and returns it with command_success(). A sweep of every param_check() user in lightningd/ and wallet/ finds only this handler and json_dev_finalizepsbt without the guard.
2. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:1605–1646](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L1605-L1646)
   json_check() resolves command_to_check via param_command() (find_cmd on the raw name, no dev-only gate), sets cmd->mode = CMD_CHECK, marks the DB read-only, and calls the target's dispatch() with the remaining params. Nothing here prevents the target from running its body or emitting a normal result: the 'check never executes' guarantee is delegated entirely to each handler honouring command_check_only().
3. [common/json\_param.c:362–390](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_param.c#L362-L390)
   param() returns false after command_check_done() when command_check_only(cmd), so plain-param() commands cannot run under check. param_check() deliberately omits that step and relies on the caller to add the guard; listpeerchannels is the built-in that lacks it.
4. [lightningd/runes.c:847–851](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L847-L851)
   check_condition evaluates a rune's `method` alternatives against cinfo->method only — the outer method name ("check") — and pname/parr conditions against check's own params (command_to_check plus pass-through params). A rune that omits or restricts listpeerchannels is never consulted about the inner command. The `readonly` shorthand (readonly_restrictions, runes.c:439) does not include `check`, so the affected runes are those explicitly permitting `check`.
5. [plugins/commando.c:420–428](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L420-L428)
   commando's try_command sends checkrune the peer-supplied `method` token and `params` verbatim; for {"method":"check","params":{"command_to_check":"listpeerchannels"}} the rune is evaluated for method=check. On `valid`, execute_command (lines 272-316) forwards the same method and params to lightningd, whose reply (the channel list) is relayed to the peer. No method is special-cased.
6. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:309–328](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs#L309-L328)
   clnrest's fill_rune_restrictions sets the checkrune method to rest_map.rpc_method — the path suffix after v1/ ("check" for POST /v1/check) — and params to the request body; verify_rune then call_rpc("check", body) returns lightningd's result to the HTTP client. The rune is never evaluated for listpeerchannels.
7. [doc/schemas/check.json:9–11](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/schemas/check.json#L9-L11)
   The published contract: check "is guaranteed to be safe, and will do all checks up to the point where something in the system would need to be altered", and its response schema has additionalProperties:false with only command_to_check. Operators and client libraries treat `check` as a side-effect-free, data-free validation call, which is why granting it in a rune is reasonable.
8. [wallet/walletrpc.c:1036–1068](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/walletrpc.c#L1036-L1068)
   Sibling instance of the same omission: json_dev_finalizepsbt() uses param_check() with no command_check_only() guard, so `check dev-finalizepsbt psbt=...` runs psbt_finalize()/psbt_final_tx() on the caller's PSBT and returns the finalized transaction (reachable on non-developer nodes because param_command() does not apply the dev_only gate). Included so the fix covers both; the disclosure impact is in listpeerchannels.

## Impact
Disclosure of the node's complete channel inventory (peer ids, channel/funding identifiers, local/remote balances, in-flight HTLC hashes and amounts, fee policy, private-channel flags) to a bearer whose rune did not grant listpeerchannels -- the data the rune system exists to gate, but no keys or funds, and limited to this one dataset. No integrity or availability impact: DB is read-only during the call and json_add_channel only reads in-memory state.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a remote Lightning peer (commando, always on) or clnrest client holding an operator-issued rune whose restrictions permit `check` but not listpeerchannels (e.g. ["method=check"] handed to a form-validating client, or a rune granting check alongside a pnameid-scoped listpeerchannels). They send check with command_to_check=listpeerchannels. checkrune passes on method=check (runes.c:847-852; commando.c:420-428; handlers.rs:309-329); commando/clnrest forward the request; json_check dispatches json_listpeerchannels in CMD_CHECK mode; the handler lacks the command_check_only guard and returns the full channel listing in the reply. No race, no user interaction; the only requirement is that such a rune has been issued (AT:P). The rune itself is the low privilege (PR:L).

## Recommended fix
1. json_listpeerchannels (and json_dev_finalizepsbt) use param_check() without the command_check_only()/command_check_done() guard, so in CMD_CHECK mode the command body executes and its result is returned, violating the contract that `check` only validates. Fix criteria: `check listpeerchannels` (with any valid parameters) must return only {"command_to_check":"listpeerchannels"} and never channel data; likewise `check dev-finalizepsbt` must not return a transaction. Verify with a rune restricted to method=check over commando/clnrest: the reply contains no `channels` member.
2. The check framework relies on every param_check() user remembering the guard; a single omission silently turns check into execution with no central enforcement in json_check(). Fix criteria: json_check() (or command_success/json_stream_success in CMD_CHECK mode) should refuse to emit a normal result for a command still in check mode -- e.g. assert/convert any success response other than command_check_done into the check acknowledgement -- so a missing guard cannot leak data. Verify by auditing that every built-in reached via check with valid params yields exactly the command_to_check response.

# Peer accept_channel2 minimum_depth above ours trips dualopend assert at our lock-in depth

## Details
When we are the opener of a dual-funded (v2) channel, dualopend stores the peer's accept_channel2.minimum_depth into state->minimum_depth (openingd/dualopend.c:3179) with no bound and never forwards it to lightningd: dualopend_wire.csv carries minimum_depth only in dualopend_init and dualopend_reinit (master->dualopend), and dualopend_commit_rcvd carries only the commitment tx, signature and penalty base. lightningd therefore keeps channel->minimum_depth = config.funding_confirms (1 on mainnet, 3 on testnet/regtest; lightningd/dual_open_control.c:4524, options.c:984/1052) and its confirmation watch (opening_depth_cb -> dualopend_tell_depth, dual_open_control.c:981-998, 1025) sends WIRE_DUALOPEND_DEPTH_REACHED as soon as *our* threshold is met. dualopend's handle_funding_depth (dualopend.c:3976) then runs assert(state->minimum_depth <= depth) against the *peer's* value, so any peer that answers our open_channel2 with minimum_depth > our funding_confirms (e.g. 2 against the mainnet default 1) deterministically aborts lightning_dualopend the moment the funding tx reaches our depth. The v1 path does not have this mismatch: openingd reports their_mindepth to lightningd in openingd_funder_reply (openingd_wire.csv:73) so both sides use the same number.

Consequence: lightningd's subd death handler (subd.c:653-658) calls dualopen_errmsg with peer_fd NULL, disconnect=false, warning=false, which takes the channel_fail_transient branch (dual_open_control.c:4340-4351) -> channel_err (channel.c:1326-1349): the channel loses its owner and stays in DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN with no daemon, with BROKEN-level 'Owning subdaemon lightning_dualopend died' logging and a core dump. connectd keeps the TCP session (destroy_connected_subd only removes the subd entry, connectd/multiplex.c:1447-1467); a new dualopend is started only when the peer's next message for this channel_id makes connectd emit peer_spoke (multiplex.c:1593-1613) and lightningd runs peer_restart_dualopend (peer_control.c:2230-2237), or on reconnect. The reinit passes channel->minimum_depth (ours) and local_channel_ready = (channel->scid != NULL), which is already true because channel_apply_scid ran at our depth in opening_depth_cb before the DEPTH_REACHED was sent, so the restarted daemon retransmits channel_ready in do_reconnect_dance (dualopend.c:4199-4203) and the open completes once the peer sends its channel_ready. The fault thus self-heals after a restart, but the attacker gains a reliable remote SIGABRT of a channel-handling subdaemon on a channel we funded; the practical effect on the channel is a stall of lock-in which the same peer could also produce by withholding channel_ready, so the gain over the protocol-sanctioned stall is modest. The same mismatch means lightningd treats the channel as locked at our depth while the peer waits for theirs (lead l-e3-09); that is bounded by the peer's ability to never send channel_ready and funds remain recoverable by closing.

No test covers the failing direction: the v1+v2 tests test_shutdown_awaiting_lockin and test_lockin_between_restart (tests/test_connection.py:1003-1005, 2296-2298) give the accepter funding-confirms 3, which equals the regtest default (chainparams.c:83 .testnet=true -> testnet_config, options.c:1052), so CI's dual-fund matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yaml:586-591) never has an accepter minimum_depth above the opener's. This is also an interoperability bug: any honest peer whose default minimum_depth exceeds our funding_confirms triggers it on every v2 open we initiate.

## Evidence
1. [openingd/dualopend.c:3964–3983](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3964-L3983)
   handle_funding_depth (dualopend.c:3964-3983) receives WIRE_DUALOPEND_DEPTH_REACHED from lightningd and runs assert(state->minimum_depth <= depth) at 3976 ('We check this before we arrive here, but for sanity'). When we are the opener, state->minimum_depth is the peer's accept_channel2 value, which lightningd never learned, so the assert aborts dualopend (SIGABRT; asserts are compiled in) whenever the peer chose a minimum_depth larger than our config.funding_confirms.
2. [openingd/dualopend.c:3174–3194](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/openingd/dualopend.c#L3174-L3194)
   opener_start parses the peer's accept_channel2 directly into state->minimum_depth with no bound and no comparison against our own minimum_depth; nothing later reports this value to lightningd (dualopend_wire.csv only carries minimum_depth master->dualopend in dualopend_init/reinit).
3. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:4524](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L4524)
   When we open, lightningd sets channel->minimum_depth = config.funding_confirms (default 1) and never updates it from the peer's accept_channel2.
4. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:981–997](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L981-L997)
   dualopen_tell_depth compares the confirmation depth to channel->minimum_depth (ours) and sends dualopend_depth_reached as soon as our own threshold is met, which is the value dualopend's assert disagrees with.
5. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:1025–1026](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L1025-L1026)
   opening_depth_cb gates the DEPTH_REACHED send on depth >= channel->minimum_depth (ours), so the message is sent at depth 1 by default regardless of the peer's minimum_depth.
6. [lightningd/subd.c:654–657](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L654-L657)
   When the subdaemon dies from the assert, lightningd invokes the channel errcb with peer_fd NULL, disconnect=false, warning=false.
7. [lightningd/dual\_open\_control.c:4340–4350](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/dual_open_control.c#L4340-L4350)
   dualopen_errmsg with no peer_fd and disconnect=false calls channel_fail_transient: the channel is left ownerless (channel_err sets owner NULL, lightningd/channel.c:1342) and only gets a new dualopend after a reconnection, which re-inits it with our minimum_depth so the assert cannot fire again.

## Impact
A channel subdaemon is killed by SIGABRT on peer input; the affected channel is left without an owner in DUALOPEND_AWAITING_LOCKIN until a reconnection, delaying lock-in and producing BROKEN logs. No funds, keys or other channels are affected; lightningd itself keeps running and the open completes after reconnect. Availability impact is limited to this one channel and is transient.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the remote peer to whom our node initiates a dual-funded open (requires --experimental-dual-fund on our side and the operator choosing to fund a channel to the attacker). Attacker replies to open_channel2 with accept_channel2.minimum_depth = any value > our funding_confirms (default 1). After the funding tx confirms once, lightningd sends DEPTH_REACHED, dualopend asserts and aborts. Deterministic, no race, no special network position.

## Recommended fix
dualopend treats a peer-chosen minimum_depth as an invariant lightningd has already enforced, while lightningd only knows and enforces our own configured minimum_depth; the sanity assert turns the mismatch into a process abort. Fix criteria: A peer minimum_depth differing from ours must not be able to abort dualopend: either lightningd learns the negotiated minimum_depth (e.g. dualopend reports it after accept_channel2, and the depth watch uses it) or handle_funding_depth handles depth < state->minimum_depth gracefully (wait, or fail the open with a protocol message). Verify by opening a v2 channel to a peer that replies with minimum_depth greater than funding_confirms and confirming dualopend survives the first DEPTH_REACHED and the channel locks in normally.

# invoice_payment hook completion re-resolves by label, marking a replaced invoice paid

## Details
When an inbound HTLC set completes, htlc_set_add_() (lightningd/htlc_set.c:253-257) frees the set's timeout and calls invoice_try_pay() (lightningd/invoice.c:447-464), which has already validated the payment against invoice I1 via invoice_check_payment (payment_hash, secret, amount >= expected). The hook payload it builds carries only I1's label, preimage and the paid msat — not the dbid or payment_hash that was validated — and the `invoice_payment` hook is dispatched asynchronously (lightningd/plugin_hook.c:338-410) because the default-loaded important offers plugin registers it (plugins/offers.c:472-486; plugins/fetchinvoice.c:1264-1305 replies after a list scan). I1's row stays UNPAID until the reply arrives, and the event loop services other RPC requests meanwhile.

invoice_payment_hooks_done() (invoice.c:273-298) then re-resolves the target *by label*: invoices_find_by_label(payload->label) returns whatever row currently carries that label, and invoices_resolve(dbid, payload->msat, ...) (wallet/invoices.c:592-637) marks it PAID with msatoshi_received = payload->msat and a fresh pay_index, checking only that the row's state is UNPAID — not that the preimage hashes to that row's payment_hash or that the amount satisfies that row's msatoshi. The HTLC set is then fulfilled with the *old* preimage (correct for I1's hash) and notify_invoice_payment pairs the label with that preimage.

Because json_delinvoice (invoice.c:1437-1482) accepts `delinvoice L unpaid` while I1 is still UNPAID, and `invoice` only rejects a label that currently exists, a caller can delete I1 and create I2 under the same label L (any amount, a payment_hash never paid) inside the hook round trip. hooks_done then records I2 as PAID with amount_received far below its amount, assigns it a pay_index (so waitinvoice/waitanyinvoice fire), and emits an invoice_payment notification whose preimage does not hash to I2's payment_hash.

Root cause: a check-then-act split across the asynchronous hook where the 'act' re-identifies its target by a reusable, caller-chosen key (label) instead of the validated identity (dbid/payment_hash), and invoices_resolve() performs no consistency check of its own.

This finding holds where a party other than the rune bearer consumes the PAID state or label→preimage pairing of the bearer's invoices (e.g. an operator's accounting or plugin that credits rune-scoped tenants on paid status); where the bearer is the sole consumer of its own invoices the forged state deceives only itself.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/invoice.c:273–297](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L273-L297)
   invoice_payment_hooks_done(): after the asynchronous plugin hook returns, the invoice to resolve is looked up again by payload->label (invoices_find_by_label) and invoices_resolve() is applied to whatever row currently carries that label, with the msat and preimage captured from the original (validated) invoice; the HTLC set is fulfilled with the old preimage and notify_invoice_payment pairs the label with it.
2. [lightningd/invoice.c:447–463](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L447-L463)
   invoice_try_pay(): the hook payload stores only label, preimage and msat of the invoice that passed invoice_check_payment; the dbid/payment_hash that was actually validated is not kept, so the identity check is lost across the hook round trip.
3. [lightningd/htlc\_set.c:253–257](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/htlc_set.c#L253-L257)
   When the set completes, its timeout is freed ('in case invoice_hook is slow!') before invoice_try_pay is called, so the set stays alive for the whole hook round trip and is fulfilled by hooks_done regardless of what happened to the invoice row in between.
4. [lightningd/invoice.c:1437–1481](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/invoice.c#L1437-L1481)
   json_delinvoice(): deletes an invoice whose status still reads 'unpaid' (state changes only in hooks_done) and never consults pending HTLC sets, so the validated invoice can be removed — and its label freed for re-use by `invoice` — while its HTLC set awaits the hook reply.
5. [wallet/invoices.c:592–636](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/invoices.c#L592-L636)
   invoices_resolve(): checks only state == UNPAID, then sets state=PAID, pay_index and msatoshi_received for the given dbid without comparing the received amount against that invoice's own msatoshi or the fulfilled preimage against its payment_hash.
6. [plugins/offers.c:472–485](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/offers.c#L472-L485)
   The default-loaded important offers plugin registers the invoice_payment hook, so every inbound invoice payment on a stock node takes the asynchronous hook round trip that opens the window.
7. [lightningd/plugin\_hook.c:338–409](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin_hook.c#L338-L409)
   plugin_hook_call_next()/plugin_hook_call_(): with a registered plugin the hook request is sent and the function returns; the final callback runs only when the plugin's reply is read, so other RPC requests (delinvoice, invoice) are serviced by the event loop in between.

## Impact
Integrity of the node's invoice ledger: an invoice whose payment_hash was never paid and whose amount was never received is persisted as PAID with a pay_index (so waitinvoice/waitanyinvoice consumers and the invoice_payment notification report label L paid), and the notification pairs the label with a preimage foreign to that invoice. No funds leave the node and nothing is disclosed, so integrity LOW; a downstream system crediting on paid status would be the subsequent victim but cannot be assumed from the code.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a network client holding a rune that permits `invoice` and `delinvoice` (over commando on the peer connection, or clnrest), who also pays its own tiny invoice from any Lightning node — all within the rune's method bounds. It creates I1 (label L, 1 sat), pays it, and immediately issues `delinvoice L unpaid` then `invoice <large> L` so both land inside the offers-plugin hook round trip after the HTLC set completes; hooks_done then marks I2 PAID. The window is a few milliseconds but attacker-timed on both sides, and a miss costs nothing (delinvoice first: HTLC fails as unknown, retry; too late: I1 is simply paid), so this is a race that must be won (AT:P), not a defence to defeat. No user interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. invoice_payment_hooks_done() identifies the invoice to resolve by label, a reusable key, instead of the dbid/payment_hash that invoice_check_payment validated before the hook. Fix criteria: The invoice resolved after the hook must be the same row that was validated: carry the dbid (or payment_hash) in the payload and resolve by it, failing the HTLC set if that row no longer exists. Verify that deleting and re-creating an invoice under the same label during the hook leaves the new invoice UNPAID and fails or correctly fulfils the HTLC without touching the new invoice.
2. invoices_resolve() marks an invoice PAID without checking that the received amount satisfies that invoice's own amount or that the fulfilled preimage matches its payment_hash. Fix criteria: Resolution refuses (returns false) when the preimage does not hash to the target invoice's payment_hash or the amount is below the invoice's amount, so no code path can record a never-paid invoice as paid. Verify with the replacement scenario that invoices_resolve rejects the mismatched invoice.

# Pending splice RPC never fails when channeld dies from peer disconnect; channel stays splice-busy

## Details
lightningd tracks in-progress splice RPCs (splice_init, splice_update, splice_signed, stfu_channels) as struct splice_command entries in ld->splice_commands; each is tal'd off the JSON command and removed only when that command completes. Completion comes from channeld replies (splice_confirmed_*, splice_abort, confirmed_stfu, *_error) or from channel_control_errmsg(), which fails the pending command with SPLICE_CHANNEL_ERROR (363, documented in doc/schemas/splice_init.json as 'The channel was disconnected during the splice command') only `if (cc && disconnect)`.

When the peer drops the TCP/Noise connection (or the operator runs `disconnect`), channeld's peer_read() fails and peer_failed_connection_lost() sends only WIRE_STATUS_PEER_CONNECTION_LOST (common/peer_failed.c:108-111); no status_peer_error carrying disconnect=true is produced. subd.c handles that status by closing the subd (525-528); destroy_subd() then calls errcb(channel, NULL, 'Owning subdaemon channeld died', NULL, false, false) (650-657). channel_control_errmsg therefore leaves the splice_command in place and channel_errmsg only runs channel_fail_transient(disconnect=false), which clears channel->owner. On reconnect peer_channels_cleanup -> channel_cleanup_commands (channel.c:1250-1279) completes only open_attempt/openchannel_signed_cmd, and channel_err returns early because the owner is already NULL; peer_start_channeld passes no knowledge of the pending command to the new channeld. The command is allocated off ld->jsonrpc and survives the RPC connection closing (jsonrpc.c:138-146, 1047-1063).

Result: the RPC call never returns, and since splice_command_for_chan() keeps returning the stale entry, every later splice_init/splice_update/splice_signed/stfu_channels on that channel fails with SPLICE_BUSY_ERROR (355). The stale entry is cleared only by lightningd restart, by a later channeld_splice_abort/splice_*_error/tx-broadcast event for that channel (e.g. the operator's `abort_channels`, which depends on the new channeld's blocking wait for the peer's tx_abort echo, or a peer-initiated splice, whose outcome is then delivered as the response to the stale command), none of which a hostile peer need cooperate with.

A channel peer triggers it deliberately: when it sees our stfu (or splice_init / tx_add_* / commitment_signed for the splice) it drops the connection and reconnects. The same happens on any ordinary connection loss during a splice, and when the operator uses `disconnect` to unstick a channeld a peer has parked in a synchronous read. This contradicts the documented contract (error 363) and the intent stated in the comment above channel_control_errmsg.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1778–1794](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1778-L1794)
   channel_control_errmsg() fails the channel's pending splice_command (SPLICE_CHANNEL_ERROR 363) only when `disconnect` is true; the subdaemon-died path arrives with disconnect=false and the command is left pending. This is the fix location.
2. [lightningd/subd.c:650–657](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L650-L657)
   destroy_subd() invokes errcb(channel, NULL, 'Owning subdaemon ... died', NULL, false, false): disconnect=false and no peer_fd, so the splice command is not failed when channeld exits after losing the peer connection.
3. [lightningd/subd.c:525–528](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/subd.c#L525-L528)
   WIRE_STATUS_PEER_CONNECTION_LOST just closes the subd (goto close) and reaches destroy_subd without any status_peer_error carrying a disconnect flag.
4. [common/peer\_failed.c:108–111](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/peer_failed.c#L108-L111)
   peer_failed_connection_lost() (called from peer_read on EOF, common/peer_io.c:18-22) sends only towire_status_peer_connection_lost, unlike peer_failed_warn/err which send status_peer_error with disconnect=true and do reach the `cc && disconnect` branch.
5. [lightningd/channel.c:1250–1279](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel.c#L1250-L1279)
   channel_cleanup_commands(), run from peer_channels_cleanup on reconnect (peer_control.c:183) and from channel_errmsg, completes open_attempt and openchannel_signed_cmd only; splice commands are not in its scope, and channel_err (1326-1330) returns early because the owner was already cleared when channeld died.
6. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2385–2459](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2385-L2459)
   json_splice_init(): the splice_command is tal'd off the command and removed only by destroy_splice_command when the command completes; a stale entry makes every new splice_init fail with SPLICE_BUSY_ERROR (2411-2415). json_splice_update, json_splice_signed and json_stfu_channels (2462-2686) apply the same busy check.
7. [lightningd/jsonrpc.c:138–146](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/jsonrpc.c#L138-L146)
   destroy_jcon() only detaches pending commands (c->jcon = NULL); commands are allocated off ld->jsonrpc (1047-1063), so the stale splice_command persists after the RPC client disconnects, for the life of lightningd.
8. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:2686–2720](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L2686-L2720)
   json_abort_channels is the only operator path that can produce the channeld_splice_abort which handle_splice_abort (334-375) uses to fail the stale command; it depends on the restarted channeld's splice_abort() receiving the peer's tx_abort echo (channeld.c:2009-2058), so a non-cooperating peer leaves restart as the sole remedy.

## Impact
One RPC call (and any plugin command built on it, e.g. spender splicein/spliceout) never returns and splicing/stfu on that one channel is refused with SPLICE_BUSY_ERROR after reconnect until lightningd restarts or a later channeld splice event for the channel happens to complete the stale command (whose response then describes an unrelated splice). HTLC forwarding, payments and channel close are unaffected; funds are not locked. Availability impact limited to the splice feature of one channel; no confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote channel counterparty (BOLT8 peer with a CHANNELD_NORMAL channel). It needs the operator to have a splice/stfu RPC in flight on that channel, a condition it observes directly (our stfu, splice_init, tx_add_*, commitment_signed arrive), then simply drops the connection: channeld exits with STATUS_PEER_CONNECTION_LOST, destroy_subd reports disconnect=false and the command is orphaned. No defences to defeat; the only requirements are the operator's splice action (UI:P) and its timing (AT:P).

## Recommended fix
1. Pending splice commands are failed only on the disconnect=true error path; a channeld exit caused by peer connection loss is reported by destroy_subd with disconnect=false and no peer_fd, so the command and its ld->splice_commands entry stay alive indefinitely and block all later splice RPCs on the channel. Fix criteria: Whenever the channel's owning subdaemon goes away for any reason (connection lost, crash, forced disconnect), every pending splice command for that channel is completed with an error (SPLICE_CHANNEL_ERROR as documented) or re-attached to the restarted daemon. Verify: start splice_init or stfu_channels, drop the peer connection, and confirm the RPC returns error 363 promptly and a new splice_init on the same channel is accepted after reconnect without restarting lightningd.
2. The splice_command registry has no local operator path to clear an entry whose channeld no longer exists; abort_channels depends on a new channeld negotiating tx_abort with the peer. Fix criteria: Provide a way to clear or fail a stale splice command locally (e.g. fail pending splice commands when channeld is restarted for the channel, or have abort_channels fail them without waiting on the peer), so a non-cooperating peer cannot leave the channel splice-busy until restart.

# pyln plugin error replies carry full Python tracebacks to remote rune bearers

## Details
pyln-client's Request.set_exception() (contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:146-172) always attaches traceback.format_exc() as a 'traceback' member of the JSON-RPC error object it writes when a method handler fails; Plugin._dispatch_request() (plugin.py:720-734) routes every exception from a non-hook method there, including framework TypeErrors raised by inspect.Signature.bind in _bind_kwargs for an unexpected or missing argument. lightningd's plugin_rpcmethod_cb() (lightningd/plugin.c:1214-1225) forwards the plugin's response object unchanged except for the id, and commando's cmd_done() (plugins/commando.c:155-191) copies the whole lightningd reply, error object included, into the custom-message reply sent to the remote peer that issued the request. Any remote peer holding a rune that permits a method implemented with pyln-client can therefore obtain a full Python traceback on demand by calling the method with a wrong argument or any other exception-triggering input.

The traceback discloses absolute filesystem paths of the plugin and of pyln-client (home directory/username, virtualenv and site-packages layout, Python version), the source line of each frame including the operator's private plugin code, internal method names and the exception text, which plugins commonly build from internal state. None of this is granted by a rune, whose documented purpose (doc/schemas/createrune.json) is to bound which methods and parameters a bearer may invoke.

Scope notes established from the code: (1) the clnrest path does NOT relay the field — clnrest calls lightningd through cln-rpc, whose RpcError struct (cln-rpc/src/primitives.rs:1260-1264, deserialised at cln-rpc/src/lib.rs:260) carries only code/message/data and drops unknown members under serde defaults; the verbatim relay is commando's alone. (2) _dispatch_request() also logs the same traceback at level 'info' (plugin.py:733, Plugin.log default level), which getlog (default level info) exposes to any rune that permits getlog, e.g. the 'readonly' shorthand; the gain is therefore over bearers whose rune permits the pyln method but not getlog. (3) No pyln-client plugin ships with CLN; the finding holds for any operator-installed plugin built on the published pyln-client library, which offers no switch to suppress the field. Impact is disclosure aiding reconnaissance; no integrity or availability effect.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:146–172](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L146-L172)
   Request.set_exception() unconditionally places traceback.format_exc() into the JSON-RPC error object as a 'traceback' member alongside 'Error while processing <method>: <str(exc)>'. format_exc() includes absolute source file paths, line numbers, the source text of each frame and the exception message. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py:720–733](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-client/pyln/client/plugin.py#L720-L733)
   _dispatch_request() routes every exception raised by a non-hook method handler (including framework TypeErrors from inspect.Signature.bind on an unexpected/missing argument) to set_exception(), so any malformed call elicits the traceback. Line 733 also logs the same traceback at level 'info' (visible via getlog to runes that permit it).
3. [lightningd/plugin.c:1214–1225](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L1214-L1225)
   plugin_rpcmethod_cb() is the response callback for both result and error replies (plugin_response_handle at plugin.c:692 invokes it regardless); it forwards the plugin's entire response object to the original command with only the id replaced (json_stream_forward_change_id), so the 'traceback' member reaches the caller unchanged.
4. [plugins/commando.c:155–190](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L155-L190)
   cmd_done() is registered for both success and failure (execute_command at commando.c:275-279: 'We handle success and failure the same') and copies the whole lightningd reply object verbatim apart from the id into the custom-message reply that send_response() ships to the remote peer, so the traceback leaves the node.

## Impact
Discloses the node host's filesystem layout (home directory/username, virtualenv and site-packages paths), Python version, the operator's private plugin source lines at each frame, internal method names and exception text to a partially trusted remote caller whose rune permits only the method. Reconnaissance value only; no secrets such as hsm_secret or runes are in the traceback by construction, and there is no integrity or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote Lightning peer holding a rune for a pyln-client-implemented method (PR:L; AT:P because such a plugin must be installed and the rune must permit its method — no pyln plugin ships with CLN) sends a commando request (AV:N) for that method with an unexpected keyword or otherwise invalid argument. commando's checkrune passes, execute_command forwards the params verbatim, the pyln framework raises, set_exception() formats the traceback into the error object, and lightningd and commando relay it byte-for-byte. Deterministic, no user interaction, no control to defeat. clnrest does not relay the field (cln-rpc RpcError drops unknown error members), so the HTTP path is not an avenue.

## Recommended fix
Request.set_exception() in pyln-client includes traceback.format_exc() in the JSON-RPC error object returned to the RPC caller, and lightningd and commando relay that object unchanged to remote rune bearers. Fix criteria: Tracebacks must go only to the plugin's log (as _dispatch_request already does at plugin.py:733), not into the JSON-RPC error returned to callers, unless the plugin author explicitly opts in. Verify that a failing pyln plugin method call via commando returns an error object containing no file paths or source lines.

# Route hint naming the payer as source makes sendonion fail silently and renepay loop forever

## Details
renepay's sendonion/injectpaymentonion error callback sendonion_fail() (plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:400-408) ignores the RPC error: it logs at debug level and frees the aux command. Because route_sendpay_request() calls route_pending_register() before send_outreq() (routetracker.c:502-504), a route that lightningd rejects outright stays in pending_routes with its HTLC committed in the uncertainty network and its amount counted in total_delivering, although lightningd never created a sendpay row for it and will never emit a sendpay_failure for that partid.

A payee can force exactly this rejection. add_hintchan() (mods.c:467-533) converts bolt11 route hints into local gossmap channels without validating the endpoints; routehints_done() (mods.c:562-580) passes the hint pubkey as src and the destination as dst. A hint whose pubkey is the payer's own (public) node id and whose scid is unused becomes a direct payer->payee channel with MAX_CAPACITY, zero fee and liquidity [0, MAX_CAPACITY]; linearize_channel() gives it near-zero probability cost, so the MCF solver routes the payment over it. renepay then calls sendonion with first_hop = {id: payee, channel: fake scid}; lightningd's find_channel_for_htlc_add() finds no such peer/channel and send_payment_core() fails the command with 'No connection to first peer found' before wallet_add_payment (lightningd/pay.c:1116-1130). The 'First peer not ready' branch (sendpay_fail with a NULL payment, pay.c:1153) is equally silent.

The state machine then spins: collect_results_cb() (mods.c:872-931) sees no finalized routes, have_results stays false, and the program jumps back to sleep_pay_mod every COLLECTOR_TIME_WINDOW_MSEC forever (mods.c:1311-1335). checktimeout_pay_mod is only in the outer loop, so retry_for is never honoured; the renepay RPC never returns, the payment stays PAYMENT_PENDING in payment_map, and any later renepay for the same invoice attaches to it and hangs too (main.c:436-442). Recovery requires restarting the plugin.

If the solver splits the payment and another part of the same group fails while one is still pending, pendingsendpays_done() recomputes next_partid from listsendpays (mods.c:1134-1146), which does not know the phantom part; it can reissue that partid and route_pending_register() then plugin_err()s on the duplicate key (routetracker.c:186-190), killing the plugin.

The pay plugin treats sendpay RPC errors as part failures; renepay does not. renepay is not an important plugin, so lightningd is unaffected; the impact is a permanently hung renepay payment/command and leaked state until restart, or a plugin crash in the duplicate-partid variant.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:400–407](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L400-L407)
   sendonion_fail() is the error callback for the sendonion/injectpaymentonion RPC; it only logs at LOG_DBG and frees the aux command. The rejected route is neither finalized nor removed, so the payment never learns the part was not sent.
2. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:502–503](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L502-L503)
   route_pending_register() runs before send_outreq(): the route is put in pending_routes, its HTLC committed in the uncertainty network and total_delivering/total_sent incremented, all before lightningd has accepted it. An RPC rejection therefore leaves a phantom pending part that no sendpay_failure notification will ever resolve.
3. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:467–532](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L467-L532)
   add_hintchan() adds any payee-supplied hint as a local gossmap channel (gossmap_local_addchan + uncertainty_add_channel with MAX_CAPACITY, fee/cltv from the hint, liquidity [0, MAX_CAPACITY]) without checking that src is not our own node id; the MCF solver (linearize_channel) assigns it near-zero probability cost and zero fee, so it carries the payment.
4. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:562–579](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L562-L579)
   routehints_done() walks each bolt11 hint backwards and passes r[j].pubkey as src and the destination (or next hint hop) as dst; a single-hop hint whose pubkey is the payer's node id yields src == pay_plugin->my_id.
5. [lightningd/pay.c:1116–1129](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L1116-L1129)
   send_payment_core(): find_channel_for_htlc_add() returns NULL when peer_by_id(first_hop.id) finds no peer or no channel matches the scid; the command fails with a plain RPC error 'No connection to first peer found' (json_stream_fail/command_failed) before wallet_add_payment, so no sendpay row exists and notify_sendpay_failure is never emitted for that partid. The 'First peer not ready' branch at 1153 (sendpay_fail with payment NULL) behaves the same.
6. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:872–930](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L872-L930)
   collect_results_cb(): routetracker_have_results() is tal_count(finalized_routes) > 0; with the phantom route never finalized have_results stays false and nothing here checks stop_time.
7. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:1311–1334](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L1311-L1334)
   The virtual program loops sleep -> collect_results while nothaveresults (positions 26-30); checktimeout_pay_mod sits only in the outer loop (18), which is never reached again, so the payment and its RPC command never terminate.
8. [plugins/renepay/main.c:436–441](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/main.c#L436-L441)
   A later renepay for the same invoice finds the payment PAYMENT_PENDING and merely registers its command on it, so it hangs as well; the payment cannot be retried through renepay until the plugin restarts.
9. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:176–211](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L176-L211)
   Aggravating variant: the phantom route keeps its (groupid, partid) in pending_routes but has no DB row; when another part of the same group fails and one is still pending, pendingsendpays_done() (mods.c:1134-1146) recomputes next_partid from listsendpays and can reissue the phantom's partid, upon which route_pending_register() plugin_err()s on the duplicate key, killing the plugin.

## Impact
The renepay RPC for that invoice never returns and the payment can never be retried through renepay; a 50 ms timer, the command and the phantom route leak until plugin restart. In the duplicate-partid variant the non-important plugin dies and all renepay use stops. Other invoices and the pay/xpay plugins are unaffected, and no HTLC or funds are committed, so availability impact is partial. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the payee (threat-model adversary 3: controls invoices and route hints). They hand the victim a bolt11 invoice whose route hint names the victim's own node id (public) as the hop pubkey with an unused scid and zero fee. When the victim pays with renepay the solver uses the fake direct channel, lightningd rejects sendonion with a non-notifying RPC error, and renepay loops forever. Deterministic given the code: no race, no configuration, no dependency assumption; the victim must choose to pay the invoice with renepay (shipped and loaded by default).

## Recommended fix
1. sendonion/injectpaymentonion RPC failures are ignored by sendonion_fail(), leaving a route marked pending that lightningd never created and will never report on. Fix criteria: An RPC error from sendonion/injectpaymentonion finalizes the route as failed (releasing its committed HTLC and amounts, or registering it only after lightningd accepts it) so collect_results sees a result; a payment whose only part is rejected by lightningd fails or retries and returns to the caller.
2. The result-collection loop has no deadline, so a payment with an in-flight part that never resolves spins past retry_for. Fix criteria: The sleep/collect loop observes stop_time and ends the payment (PAY_STOPPED_RETRYING) when exceeded even with no results.
3. add_hintchan() accepts hint channels whose source is our own node although we have no such channel. Fix criteria: Hints with src == our node id (or otherwise contradicting listpeerchannels) are ignored.

# BitcoinD/ElementsD default data dir /tmp/bitcoind-test allows symlink-following file truncation

## Details
pyln-testing is published to PyPI (.github/workflows/pypi-publish.yml:22) and is documented for third-party plugin test suites. Its public `BitcoinD` and `ElementsD` constructors default `bitcoin_dir` to the fixed, predictable path `/tmp/bitcoind-test` (contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py:590, 813). The in-tree `bitcoind` fixture always overrides this (`chaind(bitcoin_dir=directory)`, fixtures.py:157, a per-test directory under the session base dir), so the insecure default is reachable only for a consumer who writes `BitcoinD()` / `ElementsD()` without `bitcoin_dir` — a condition on the caller, not on the attacker.

With the default, nothing verifies the directory: `TailableProc.__init__` skips `os.makedirs` when `outputDir` already exists (utils.py:360-362) and immediately opens `<dir>/log` and `<dir>/errlog` with mode `"wt"` — O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, which follows symlinks (utils.py:365-366); `BitcoinD.__init__` only checks `os.path.exists(<dir>/regtest)` (utils.py:600-602); `start()` -> `set_port()` -> `write_config()` opens `<dir>/bitcoin.conf` (or `elements.conf`) with `'w'` (utils.py:111, 626, 828). None of these opens use O_NOFOLLOW/O_EXCL or check ownership. `/tmp` is sticky, so whoever creates `/tmp/bitcoind-test` first owns it permanently; the harness adopts it as-is.

Attack: a co-tenant pre-creates `/tmp/bitcoind-test/regtest/` (mode 0755 or 0777) and plants symlinks `/tmp/bitcoind-test/log`, `errlog` and `bitcoin.conf` pointing at files writable by the victim (e.g. `~victim/.bashrc`, `~victim/.ssh/authorized_keys`, files in the victim's checkout). The next time the victim constructs `BitcoinD()`/`ElementsD()` with the default, those targets are truncated with the victim's privileges; `bitcoin.conf` is additionally overwritten with the fixed config text (`regtest=1`, `rpcuser=rpcuser`, `rpcpassword=rpcpass`, ...), and bitcoind's log output is then streamed into the `log` target. Linux `fs.protected_symlinks` does not intervene: it only restricts symlinks whose parent directory is sticky and world-writable, and `/tmp/bitcoind-test` is the attacker's own non-sticky directory (assumption about the kernel's may_follow_link rule). The attacker chooses the destination but not the content, so the impact is destructive truncation/overwrite of victim-writable files and derailment of the test run, not arbitrary content injection.

This is a classic insecure-temporary-file defect (CWE-377, exploited via link following, CWE-59) in shipped library code. It holds only where the consumer relies on the default argument; no in-repository code does.

## Evidence
1. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py:590–602](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py#L590-L602)
   BitcoinD.__init__ defaults bitcoin_dir to the fixed, world-shared path /tmp/bitcoind-test and only creates <dir>/regtest if it does not already exist, so a pre-created attacker-owned directory is accepted as-is.
2. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py:360–368](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py#L360-L368)
   TailableProc.__init__ then opens <dir>/log and <dir>/errlog with mode 'wt' (O_TRUNC, follows symlinks), truncating whatever an attacker-planted symlink points at.
3. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py:110–117](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py#L110-L117)
   write_config() opens <dir>/bitcoin.conf (or elements.conf) with 'w' and writes fixed config lines plus the port; via a planted symlink this truncates and overwrites an attacker-chosen victim-writable file.
4. [contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py:812–828](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/contrib/pyln-testing/pyln/testing/utils.py#L812-L828)
   ElementsD inherits the same default directory and conf-file handling.

## Impact
Integrity LOW: the attacker chooses which victim-writable files are truncated and gets only fixed config text / bitcoind log output written into them — destructive, but content is not attacker-controlled. Confidentiality NONE: the regtest datadir the attacker then owns holds only throwaway regtest state, and the test bitcoind is in any case reachable by every local user through the fixed rpcuser/rpcpass credentials in BITCOIND_CONFIG (utils.py:39-44), so owning the directory adds nothing. Availability LOW: the victim's test run fails and tooling whose files were truncated breaks.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any other unprivileged local account on a host shared with the victim. They pre-create /tmp/bitcoind-test/regtest and symlinks named log, errlog and bitcoin.conf (or elements.conf) in the directory they own; no race is needed since the directory persists. Victim: a pyln-testing consumer whose code constructs BitcoinD()/ElementsD() without bitcoin_dir (the in-tree fixture always passes one, hence attack_requirements PRESENT). When the victim next runs that test code — an ordinary action, not a subversion of any protection, hence user_interaction PASSIVE — TailableProc.__init__ and write_config truncate/overwrite the symlink targets with the victim's privileges. No ownership, O_NOFOLLOW or O_EXCL check stands in the way, and fs.protected_symlinks does not apply to a symlink in a non-sticky attacker-owned directory.

## Recommended fix
A shipped constructor defaults to a fixed, predictable path in the world-shared temp directory and then writes files there without ownership or symlink checks, so another local user can pre-own the directory and redirect the writes. Fix criteria: The default data directory must be private and unpredictable (e.g. created with tempfile.mkdtemp under the session base dir) or the parameter made mandatory; files under it must be created with O_NOFOLLOW/O_EXCL or only after verifying the directory is owned by the current user and not world-writable. Verify that with a pre-created attacker-owned /tmp/bitcoind-test containing symlinks, BitcoinD()/ElementsD() either refuse to start or never write through the symlinks.

# Payee-controlled oversized onion payload (long hint chain or big blinded path) crashes renepay

## Details
renepay builds every onion in create_onion() (plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:329-381) and never bounds the assembled payload. create_onionpacket() (common/sphinx.c:545-549) returns NULL when the summed hop payloads plus 32-byte HMACs exceed ROUTING_INFO_SIZE (1300 bytes); create_onion() passes that NULL straight to serialize_onionpacket() (sphinx.c:179-183), whose first statement reads m->routinginfo, so cln-renepay dies with SIGSEGV. Every other caller in the tree checks for NULL first (plugins/xpay/xpay.c:1487, lightningd/pay.c:1265 and 2461, plugins/offers.c:178), confirming that an over-long payload is an expected error path renepay alone mishandles. For a bolt12 blinded hop whose encrypted_recipient_data pushes the TLV stream to 65536 bytes or more (enclen is u16), onion_blinded_hop() -> make_tlv_hop() (common/onion_encode.c:15-32) abort()s even earlier.

Both triggering inputs are payee-authored and reach the sink unbounded:
- BOLT11: decode_r() (common/bolt11.c:504-537) accepts any number of 51-byte hint hops. routehints_done() (plugins/renepay/mods.c:552-580) adds every hop as a MAX_CAPACITY local channel with the hint's fees/delta; gossmap add_channel() (common/gossmap.c:494-506) creates nodes for unknown pubkeys, so a chain of fresh keys ending at a private destination is the only path to it. No hop bound exists in renepay (payment_info.h:47-49 keeps max_num_hops as a TODO; no ROUTING_MAX_HOPS use). minflow() (mcf.c:1795-1860) returns the best flowset even when its probability is below min_probability (is_better() only prefers, never discards; compute_routes_cb comments 'We let this return an unlikely path'), and get_routes() (routebuilder.c:328-410) rejects routes only on fee budget, CLTV delay (maxdelay, default 2016) and htlc_min/max. Each non-final hop costs 51-59 bytes and the final hop ~91, so a hint chain of roughly 22-25 zero-fee, zero-delta hops yields a route whose onion cannot fit in 1300 bytes.
- BOLT12: invoice_decode() (common/bolt12.c:598-618) rejects only zero-hop paths; blindedhints_cb() (mods.c:621-645) routes to the introduction node and sphinx_append_blinded_path() (routetracker.c:280-306) appends every hop's full encrypted_recipient_data. Two hops carrying ~700 bytes each suffice for the NULL path; >= 64 KiB in one hop reaches the make_tlv_hop abort.

The crash occurs in route_sendpay_request() (routetracker.c:409-440), called from waitblockheight_done (mods.c:806), before anything is sent to the network, as soon as the victim pays the attacker's invoice with renepay. renepay is the one builtin plugin not marked important (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2590), so lightningd, pay and xpay continue; the renepay RPC and all in-memory retry/MPP state are lost until the operator restarts the plugin (lightningd does not auto-restart it). The xpay sibling for the >= 64 KiB abort is xpay-oversized-hop-payload-abort (primary location common/onion_encode.c); this record covers renepay's distinct entry points and the lower-threshold NULL-dereference for payloads between 1300 bytes and 64 KiB.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:374–379](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L374-L379)
   create_onion() calls create_onionpacket() and passes its result straight to serialize_onionpacket() without a NULL check.
2. [common/sphinx.c:545–548](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L545-L548)
   create_onionpacket() returns NULL when the summed hop payloads (each payload + 32-byte HMAC) exceed fixed_size = ROUTING_INFO_SIZE (1300 bytes).
3. [common/sphinx.c:179–182](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/sphinx.c#L179-L182)
   serialize_onionpacket() dereferences m->routinginfo unconditionally, so a NULL packet is a NULL-pointer dereference (SIGSEGV).
4. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:290–305](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L290-L305)
   sphinx_append_blinded_path() adds one hop per payee-authored blinded_path hop with the full encrypted_recipient_data; no size accounting. For >= 64 KiB of encrypted_recipient_data in a hop, onion_blinded_hop() -> make_tlv_hop() (common/onion_encode.c:15-32) abort()s before create_onionpacket is even reached.
5. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:567–579](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L567-L579)
   Every hop of every bolt11 route hint becomes a gossmap channel; a hint chain of arbitrary length (decode_r loops while data remains, common/bolt11.c:522-531) thus yields a route of arbitrary hop count.
6. [plugins/renepay/routebuilder.c:328–349](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routebuilder.c#L328-L349)
   get_routes() bounds routes only by fee budget and cumulative CLTV delay (maxdelay, default 2016); with zero-fee, zero-delta hint hops a 25-hop route passes. No ROUTING_MAX_HOPS check exists anywhere in plugins/renepay.
7. [common/bolt12.c:598–617](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt12.c#L598-L617)
   invoice_decode() rejects only zero-hop blinded paths; neither hop count nor encrypted_recipient_data length is bounded, and renepay (main.c:346-349) steals the paths unchecked.

## Impact
SIGSEGV/abort terminates the cln-renepay process. It is the one builtin plugin not marked important, so lightningd, channels, and the pay/xpay engines keep running and in-flight HTLCs stay tracked by lightningd; the renepay RPC and its in-memory payment/retry state are unavailable until the operator manually restarts the plugin. Partial loss of node availability; no confidentiality or integrity impact and no fund loss.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the payee: they issue a bolt11 invoice whose only route hint is a chain of ~22-25 hops of fresh pubkeys from a public introduction node to a private destination, or a bolt12 invoice whose blinded path carries more than ~1.2 KB of encrypted_recipient_data across its hops. The victim pays it with renepay; the MCF solver must use the hinted/blinded path, create_onion() builds a payload exceeding 1300 bytes, create_onionpacket() returns NULL and serialize_onionpacket() dereferences it (or make_tlv_hop aborts for >= 64 KiB). The invoice is delivered over any channel (network); no peer cooperation, configuration or race is needed; the victim must choose to pay the invoice.

## Recommended fix
1. create_onion() assumes create_onionpacket() succeeds and never bounds the payload it assembles from payee-controlled hint chains and blinded paths. Fix criteria: A NULL from create_onionpacket() (or an over-long payload detected beforehand) fails that route/payment with an RPC error instead of crashing; invoices with hint chains or blinded paths that cannot fit a 1300-byte onion are rejected at decode/route time; blinded hops with encrypted_recipient_data too large for a TLV hop are rejected before onion_blinded_hop().
2. The route builder has no maximum hop count, so routes longer than the onion can carry are produced. Fix criteria: Routes exceeding the hop limit the onion supports (ROUTING_MAX_HOPS) are discarded by the solver/route builder.

# Payee route hint whose pubkey equals the destination aborts renepay in gossmap_local_addchan

## Details
renepay turns every bolt11 route hint into a local gossmap channel. In routehints_done() (plugins/renepay/mods.c:567-580) each hint hop r[j] is added with add_hintchan(payment, &r[j].pubkey, end, ...), where `end` is the invoice destination for the last hop. add_hintchan() (467-533) performs no sanity check on the endpoints: if the hint's scid is not already known it calls gossmap_local_addchan(payment->local_gossmods, src, dst, ...). common/gossmap.c:1059 opens that function with assert(!node_id_eq(n1, n2)).

A payee therefore crashes the payer's renepay plugin with a valid, signed bolt11 invoice containing a single route hint whose pubkey is the payee's own node id (the invoice's receiver_id) and any unused short_channel_id. bolt11 decode_r() (common/bolt11.c:504-537) accepts it (only node_id_valid is checked), json_renepay steals b11->routes into payment_info.routehints (main.c:335), the pipeline reaches routehints_done after waitblockheight, and the assert fires. Two consecutive hint hops with the same pubkey trigger it identically. The BOLT12 sibling blindedhints_cb() (619-644) has the same shape: src is the unsigned, payee-chosen first_node_id and dst is the constant fake node 020000..0001, which is a valid curve point, so an invoice path whose first_node_id is that point aborts too.

The pay plugin's analogous hint handling has its own abort (pay-routehint-duplicate-local-channel-abort); renepay does not share that one (gossmap_local_addchan returns false for a duplicate scid and add_hintchan only logs), but it has this self-loop variant instead. renepay is not an important plugin (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2590), so the result is the loss of the renepay payment engine (and all in-progress renepay payments' state) until the operator restarts it; lightningd itself keeps running.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:562–579](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L562-L579)
   routehints_done() walks every bolt11 route hint backwards and calls add_hintchan(payment, &r[j].pubkey, end, ...) where `end` is the invoice destination for the last hop and the previous hint's pubkey otherwise. Nothing checks that r[j].pubkey differs from `end`, so a hint whose node is the payee itself (or two consecutive hops with the same pubkey) produces src == dst.
2. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:478–523](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L478-L523)
   add_hintchan() only looks up the scid in the uncertainty network; for a payee-chosen unknown scid it falls into the add branch and calls gossmap_local_addchan(payment->local_gossmods, src, dst, scid, ...) with the two identical node ids.
3. [common/gossmap.c:1047–1062](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/gossmap.c#L1047-L1062)
   gossmap_local_addchan() begins with assert(!node_id_eq(n1, n2)); asserts are compiled in release builds, so the process aborts.
4. [common/bolt11.c:504–536](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/bolt11.c#L504-L536)
   decode_r() only checks that each hint pubkey is a valid point; it does not compare it with receiver_id or with neighbouring hops, so the invoice decodes and the hints are stolen into payment_info.routehints (main.c:335).
5. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:619–643](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L619-L643)
   Same sink for BOLT12: blindedhints_cb() passes first_node_id (payee-chosen, unsigned) as src and the fixed fake routing_destination 02000..0001 as dst to add_hintchan(); a path whose first_node_id is that (valid, x=1) point also hits the assert.
6. [lightningd/plugin.c:2576–2589](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2576-L2589)
   cln-renepay is the only builtin plugin loaded as not important, so the abort kills only the renepay plugin (it is not restarted) rather than lightningd.

## Impact
abort() terminates the cln-renepay plugin process. It is registered as not important (lightningd/plugin.c:2584) so destroy_plugin() (plugin.c:297-303) does not exit lightningd, and lightningd does not restart it: the `renepay` command and every renepay payment in progress (their RPC callers get a plugin-died error; HTLCs already handed to sendpay continue under lightningd) are lost until the operator runs `plugin start` or restarts the node. lightningd, channels and the pay/xpay engines keep working, so the node's availability is partially, not totally, lost. No confidentiality or integrity impact; no funds at risk.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker is any payee: they hand the victim a bolt11 invoice signed with their own key containing one route hint whose pubkey is their own node id (the invoice receiver_id) and any scid absent from the gossmap. decode_r() (common/bolt11.c:504-537) only requires node_id_valid(); json_renepay steals b11->routes unchanged (main.c:335). The renepay pipeline (mods.c:1312-1318) runs the routehints modifier before compute_routes/send_routes, so routehints_done() calls add_hintchan(&r[j].pubkey, destination) with identical ids, uncertainty_find_channel() misses the unknown scid, uncertainty_add_channel() succeeds, and gossmap_local_addchan() hits assert(!node_id_eq(n1, n2)) (common/gossmap.c:1059; asserts are compiled in release builds) before any HTLC is sent. No configuration or race is needed; the victim must choose to pay the invoice with `renepay` (UI:Active). Two consecutive hint hops with the same pubkey, or a BOLT12 blinded path whose first_node_id is the valid point 02..01 used as routing_destination (main.c:373-377), reach the same assert.

## Recommended fix
add_hintchan()/routehints_done()/blindedhints_cb() pass payee-controlled endpoint pairs into gossmap_local_addchan(), whose precondition (distinct node ids) is enforced only by an assert. Fix criteria: Hints whose source equals their destination (including hint pubkey == invoice destination, consecutive duplicate hops, and a blinded first_node_id equal to the fake routing destination) are rejected or skipped with a logged note before any gossmap_localmods call; paying such an invoice with renepay returns an RPC error or ignores the hint and the plugin stays alive.
