# Unparseable-onion failure for a route renepay no longer tracks kills the plugin via plugin_err

## Details
renepay keeps in-flight routes in pay_plugin->pending_routes and resolves sendpay_failure notifications against them. When a payment finishes — payment_fail from checktimeout_cb after retry_for (default 60 s, main.c:201) or from a final error found by collect_results_cb, or payment_success — payment_finish() -> payment_cleanup() -> routetracker_cleanup() (routetracker.c:43-70) frees every pending route of that payment hash even though their HTLCs are still outstanding at lightningd (the comment there acknowledges this). The payment object stays in payment_map (main.c:398; nothing ever removes it).

When the notification for such a still-outstanding part later arrives, notification_sendpay_failure() (routetracker.c:535-554) finds the payment but not the route, builds a dummy route with tal_route_from_json() (hops = NULL, shared_secrets = NULL; the data object always has amount_msat/amount_sent_msat for a renepay sendonion) and calls tal_sendpay_result_from_json(). If lightningd could not unwrap the failure onion it emits code PAY_UNPARSEABLE_ONION whose data carries only `onionreply` (lightningd/pay.c:234-253, 609-623). get_data_details() fails (no erring_index/failcode) and get_data_details_onionreply() returns false because shared_secrets is NULL (json.c:88-90), so the parser returns NULL and renepay calls plugin_err("Unable to parse sendpay_failure") (routetracker.c:551-554), which is plugin_exit(1) (libplugin.c:1975-1986). The same path is taken for sendpays of that payment_hash created by another plugin (e.g. the operator also ran `pay` on the invoice), whose keys are never in pending_routes.

Attack: a payee, or any intermediate node on one part of a multi-part renepay payment, holds its HTLC while the payment finishes, then fails the held HTLC with a garbage `reason` blob (update_fail_htlc -> peer_htlcs.c -> payment_failed(): HMAC check in unwrap_onionreply fails -> PAY_UNPARSEABLE_ONION). renepay's inner loop (mods.c:1311-1335) only reaches checktimeout/collect_results once some part has a result, so the attacker needs one part to fail (or succeed) while another is held: a malicious payee simply fails one part (mpp_timeout, or a final incorrect_or_unknown_payment_details which ends the payment immediately) and holds the other; an intermediate attacker relies on the honest payee's standard mpp_timeout on the other parts and renepay's 60 s retry_for expiry. Payees can push renepay to split (invoice amount above any single channel, BOLT12 payinfo htlc_maximum_msat), and renepay splits larger payments by default.

cln-renepay is loaded by default but is the one builtin plugin not marked important (lightningd/plugin.c:2576-2590), so lightningd survives; renepay, all its in-memory payment/uncertainty state and every in-flight renepay command are lost until the operator restarts the plugin.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:535–554](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L535-L554)
   notification_sendpay_failure(): when (payment_hash, groupid, partid) is not in pending_routes it builds a dummy route via tal_route_from_json() (shared_secrets = NULL) and then calls plugin_err() when tal_sendpay_result_from_json() returns NULL — the fatal sink; the fix must make an unparseable/untracked notification non-fatal here.
2. [plugins/renepay/json.c:240–249](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/json.c#L240-L249)
   tal_sendpay_result_from_json(): with code != 0 it requires erring_index+failcode (get_data_details) or an onionreply plus non-NULL shared_secrets (get_data_details_onionreply, lines 88-90 return false when shared_secrets is NULL); otherwise it returns NULL.
3. [lightningd/pay.c:234–252](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L234-L252)
   json_sendpay_fail_fields(): for PAY_UNPARSEABLE_ONION the notification data carries only `onionreply` and no erring_index/failcode, so the dummy-route path has nothing it can parse.
4. [lightningd/pay.c:609–624](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L609-L624)
   payment_failed() produces PAY_UNPARSEABLE_ONION whenever unwrap_onionreply() fails on the peer-supplied failure blob (any invalid HMAC), i.e. whenever the failing node returns garbage in update_fail_htlc; renepay's sendonion passes shared_secrets (pay.c:1353,1389) so lightningd itself performs this unwrap.
5. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:43–69](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L43-L69)
   routetracker_cleanup() (called from payment_cleanup on every payment_fail/payment_success) frees all pending routes of the payment while their HTLCs may still be in flight, so a later sendpay_failure for such a part is reported against an untracked key.
6. [plugins/renepay/payment.c:304–318](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/payment.c#L304-L318)
   payment_finish() -> payment_cleanup() runs on timeout (checktimeout_cb), on a final error from any part (collect_results_cb) or on success, regardless of other parts still pending.
7. [plugins/renepay/mods.c:1311–1335](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/mods.c#L1311-L1335)
   Payment program: the sleep/collect_results loop only exits once some part has a result, after which pendingsendpays -> checktimeout fails the payment with 'Timed out' once retry_for (default 60 s) has elapsed even though other parts are still pending — the attacker-orchestrable condition that leaves a held HTLC untracked.

## Impact
plugin_err() -> plugin_exit(1) terminates cln-renepay; its in-memory payment map, uncertainty network and every in-flight renepay command are lost and the renepay RPC is unavailable until the operator restarts the plugin. cln-renepay is deliberately not important (plugin.c:2576-2590), so lightningd, channels, HTLC resolution and the pay/xpay plugins keep running: a partial loss of availability of the node. No confidentiality or integrity impact; funds in flight are resolved by lightningd regardless.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the payee or any intermediate node on one part of a multi-part renepay payment (threat-model adversaries 1 and 3). They hold their HTLC until the payment has finished (final error or mpp_timeout on another part, success of another part, or the 60 s retry_for expiry), then fail it with an invalid failure onion. lightningd emits a PAY_UNPARSEABLE_ONION sendpay_failure for a key renepay no longer tracks and the plugin plugin_err()s. Requires the payment to have been split into at least two concurrent parts with one resolving while the other is held — runtime state a malicious payee controls directly and an intermediate can rely on the honest payee's standard mpp_timeout for; the victim only performs a routine payment.

## Recommended fix
notification_sendpay_failure() treats a sendpay_failure it cannot fully parse as a fatal internal error, although notifications for untracked sendpays (routes freed by routetracker_cleanup at payment end, or sendpays created by other plugins) legitimately lack the data renepay expects (no erring_index/failcode and no shared_secrets to unwrap the onionreply). Fix criteria: An unparseable or untracked sendpay_failure/sendpay_success is logged and acknowledged (notification_handled) without plugin_err; a PAY_UNPARSEABLE_ONION notification arriving for a part whose route renepay no longer tracks leaves the plugin running, and the same holds for sendpays of the same payment_hash created outside renepay.

# Final-node error carrying a malformed channel_update aborts renepay in update_gossip_failure

## Details
When a sendpay fails, renepay's routefail_start() -> update_gossip() (plugins/renepay/routefail.c:153-173) extracts any channel_update embedded in the failure message (temporary_channel_failure, amount_below_minimum, fee_insufficient, incorrect_cltv_expiry, expiry_too_soon) and submits it to lightningd's addgossip. If addgossip rejects it, update_gossip_failure() (routefail.c:120-151) tries to disable the erring channel: it uses result->erring_channel if present, otherwise executes `assert(index < tal_count(r->route->hops))` and indexes route->hops[index] with index = erring_index.

For every route with at least one hop renepay pays via `sendonion` with shared_secrets (routetracker.c:445-470). lightningd therefore stores the payment with route_nodes == NULL (pay.c:1385-1389) and, when the failure onion comes back, unwraps it itself and reports erring_channel = NULL, erring_index = origin_index + 1 (pay.c:466-473, 527-541). renepay builds exactly tal_count(route->hops) sphinx hops for a BOLT11 route (routetracker.c:348-372), so the payee is sphinx hop N-1, unwrap_onionreply yields origin_index N-1 (common/sphinx.c:888-893) and the notification carries erring_index == N == tal_count(route->hops). renepay copies erring_index and raw_message verbatim from the sendpay_failure notification (json.c:126-160) onto the pending route, whose hops array is non-NULL (routetracker.c:535-571).

A malicious payee triggers the assert deterministically: on receiving the HTLC it fails it with temporary_channel_failure (or any of the other channel_update-bearing codes) whose `len > 0` channel_update field holds garbage. channel_update_from_onion_error() accepts any bytes and patch_channel_update() prefixes the WIRE_CHANNEL_UPDATE type if absent (routefail.c:66-109); gossipd's inject_gossip dispatches to gossmap_manage_channel_update, whose fromwire_channel_update fails and returns 'channel_update: malformed ...' (gossmap_manage.c:1036-1045); lightningd turns the non-empty error into an RPC failure (gossip_control.c:436-437); update_gossip_failure() then evaluates assert(N < N) and abort()s. (A well-formed update with a bad signature for a known channel also yields an error string, gossmap_manage.c:928-930.) The BOLT4 rule that a final node MUST NOT return these codes is only enforced later, in handle_failure()'s FINAL_NODE branches (routefail.c:486-499, 529-546), which the assert pre-empts.

cln-renepay is loaded by default but is the one builtin plugin not marked important (lightningd/plugin.c:2578-2585), so lightningd keeps running; the renepay plugin and all its in-memory payment state are gone until the operator restarts it, and every renepay RPC in flight fails.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/renepay/routefail.c:120–150](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routefail.c#L120-L150)
   update_gossip_failure(): when addgossip fails and result->erring_channel is NULL it falls to the route->hops branch and executes assert(index < tal_count(r->route->hops)) with index = erring_index; for an error authored by the final node erring_index == tal_count(hops), so the assert fails and abort()s before handle_failure()'s final-node handling (486-499, 529-546) runs.
2. [plugins/renepay/routefail.c:66–108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routefail.c#L66-L108)
   channel_update_from_onion_error() extracts the channel_update bytes embedded in temporary_channel_failure, amount_below_minimum, fee_insufficient, incorrect_cltv_expiry and expiry_too_soon; any non-empty bytes are accepted, patch_channel_update() prefixes the WIRE_CHANNEL_UPDATE type if missing, and update_gossip() (153-173) submits the blob to addgossip.
3. [lightningd/pay.c:466–541](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L466-L541)
   remote_routing_failure(): for sendonion payments (route_nodes == NULL, set by json_sendonion at 1385-1389) lightningd sets erring_channel = NULL and erring_index = origin_index + 1; for an error from the final node that equals the number of route hops. json_add_routefail_info (206-232) then emits erring_index, failcode and raw_message without erring_channel.
4. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:348–375](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L348-L375)
   create_onion() adds one sphinx hop per route hop (non-final payloads for hops[1..N-1] addressed to hops[0..N-2], then the final hop for hops[N-1].node_id), so the onion has tal_count(route->hops) hops and the payee is hop N-1; common/sphinx.c:888-893 reports that hop's 0-based index as origin_index.
5. [plugins/renepay/routetracker.c:535–570](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/routetracker.c#L535-L570)
   notification_sendpay_failure() looks the route up in pending_routes (so route->hops is the N-entry array from flow_to_route), parses the notification into route->result and calls routefail_start() with no bound check on erring_index.
6. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1036–1044](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1036-L1044)
   gossmap_manage_channel_update() returns 'channel_update: malformed ...' when fromwire_channel_update fails on the payee's garbage; gossipd's inject_gossip (gossipd.c:483-498) forwards the string and lightningd's json_addgossip_reply (gossip_control.c:436-437) turns any non-empty error into an RPC failure, which invokes update_gossip_failure.
7. [plugins/renepay/json.c:126–159](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/renepay/json.c#L126-L159)
   get_data_details() stores lightningd's erring_index and raw_message as-is; erring_channel stays NULL because the sendonion failure notification lacks it.

## Impact
abort() terminates cln-renepay and all its in-memory payment state; every renepay RPC in flight fails. cln-renepay is the one builtin plugin not marked important (plugin.c:2578-2585), so lightningd, its channels, HTLC tracking and the other payment plugins (pay, xpay) keep running; the HTLCs already sent via sendonion resolve normally in lightningd. The loss is confined to the renepay service until the operator restarts the plugin, so availability impact is partial. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the payee of a BOLT11 invoice the victim pays with renepay (the last node renepay addresses). On receipt of the HTLC they fail it with temporary_channel_failure (or another channel_update-bearing code) whose channel_update field is non-empty garbage. lightningd reports erring_index == hop count with no erring_channel, addgossip rejects the blob, and renepay's assert fires. Deterministic; no configuration, race or special network position beyond being paid; the victim merely pays the attacker's invoice through renepay.

## Recommended fix
update_gossip_failure() assumes an erring node that returned a channel_update is never the final node, and enforces that assumption with an assert on an index the remote node controls. Fix criteria: erring_index >= tal_count(route->hops) (final node or beyond) skips channel disabling or disables the last hop without indexing out of range; a final node returning a channel_update-bearing failcode with garbage channel_update results in a normal failed route and the plugin stays alive.

# Rebalance detection pairs by counterparty-chosen payment hash and amount, hiding real payments from income

## Details
Bookkeeper classifies an outgoing payment as a rebalance (a payment to ourselves) when it finds another channel movement with the same payment hash whose credit equals our debit minus fees (plugins/bkpr/recorder.c:556-578). The query matches any row in `channelmoves` -- it does not require the credit to be an `invoice` credit on one of our channels, a different account, or any evidence that the payment terminated at this node. The payment hash is chosen by the remote counterparty: for a payment we make it is the hash in their invoice, and for a forward it is the hash of the HTLC they sent. Rebalance pairs are then consumed by the income statement: maybe_channel_income (incomestmt.c:234-237) returns NULL for any invoice event that is paired, so it is excluded from `bkpr-listincome`, `bkpr-dumpincomecsv` and `bkpr-report`, and the routing fee is relabelled `rebalance_fee` (incomestmt.c:384-388).

A counterparty can therefore make a genuine expense vanish from the operator's books:

1. The attacker controls two nodes A and B and knows a preimage P with hash H. A routes a payment of X msat through the victim to B with hash H. The victim records an inbound `routed` credit of X under hash H (lightningd/coin_mvts.c new_channel_mvt_routed_hin) and an outbound routed debit; the fee is correctly booked as routing income.
2. The attacker (as a merchant/payee) issues the victim an invoice for X msat with payment hash H (they hold P) and the victim pays it. Bookkeeper ingests the outgoing `invoice` debit of X+fees, computes credit = X, finds the earlier `routed` credit of X with hash H, and records the two as a rebalance pair.
3. The victim's income statement now omits the X msat the victim actually paid to the attacker and shows its routing fee as a `rebalance_fee`; bkpr-listaccountevents marks both as is_rebalance.

A variant needs no routing position: the attacker pays one of the victim's invoices (hash H, amount X), learns P on settlement, then has the victim pay an attacker invoice with the same hash H for X (e.g. a refund); both the inbound and outbound invoice events are then suppressed. lightningd has no check that a bolt11 being paid does not reuse the hash of a prior movement.

The root cause is that a heuristic driven entirely by counterparty-controlled values (payment hash, amount) is used as proof that money moved between two of our own channels. The recorder.c comment acknowledges that any repeat of hash+amount is treated as a rebalance; the consequence is that a payee or routing peer can control how the operator's accounting classifies payments. Impact is limited to the integrity of bookkeeper's reports (tax/accounting output); funds and node state are unaffected. Primary sink: recorder.c (ingestion); consuming sites in incomestmt.c are in this unit.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/recorder.c:536–580](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/recorder.c#L536-L580)
   maybe_record_rebalance selects ANY channelmoves row with the same payment_hash and credit_msat == debit - fees (lines 556-562), with no restriction on primary_tag (a 'routed' inbound HTLC credit qualifies), account, or whether the payment resolved to one of our own invoices, and records the first unpaired match as a rebalance pair (lines 574-578). The comment at 541-544 acknowledges that any repeat of hash+amount is treated as a rebalance.
2. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1655–1662](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1655-L1662)
   The check runs for every outgoing invoice-tagged channel move as it is ingested from listchannelmoves; the matching credit row only has to have an equal or lower created_index.
3. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:234–252](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L234-L252)
   maybe_channel_income returns NULL for every invoice-tagged event that find_rebalance() reports as paired, so the real outgoing payment (and, if the paired row is an invoice credit, the incoming one) disappears from bkpr-listincome, bkpr-dumpincomecsv and bkpr-report.
4. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:380–388](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L380-L388)
   The routing fee paid on the hidden payment is re-labelled 'rebalance_fee' instead of 'invoice_fee', misclassifying a payment to a third party as a self-payment cost.
5. [lightningd/coin\_mvts.c:10–63](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/coin_mvts.c#L10-L63)
   Both forwarded HTLCs (new_channel_mvt_routed_hin: COIN_CREDIT of hin->msat under hin->payment_hash) and our own payments (new_channel_mvt_invoice_hout: COIN_DEBIT of hout->msat with hout->fees) carry the HTLC payment hash chosen by the remote party; nothing distinguishes a forward credit from an invoice credit in the hash/amount the recorder matches on.
6. [lightningd/htlc\_end.c:311–316](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/htlc_end.c#L311-L316)
   For our own payments hout->fees = first-hop msat - final_msat, so the recorder's credit = debit - fees equals exactly the invoice amount the payee chose; the attacker can therefore make the inbound forward amount (which they also set) equal it.
7. [plugins/bkpr/channel\_event.c:57–58](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/channel_event.c#L57-L58)
   bkpr-listaccountevents reports both paired rows as is_rebalance=true, so every bookkeeper view is affected.

## Impact
The operator's income statement, CSV export and report omit a real outgoing payment (and, in the refund variant, a real inbound one), its fee is relabelled rebalance_fee, and bkpr-listaccountevents flags both rows and a forwarded HTLC as rebalances; the bogus pair is persisted to the datastore and reloaded on restart. Accounting/tax records are falsified at the counterparty's choice. Funds, channel state, balances and availability are unaffected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote counterparty, no privileges on the node. Step 1: from a node it controls, route an HTLC through the victim (or pay a victim invoice) with hash H and inbound amount Y, so a credit row under H with credit_msat=Y is recorded. Step 2: issue the victim a bolt11 for Y msat with payment hash H and have it paid (a routine commercial action, or an automated withdrawal); lightningd/pay only reject hashes already in our own payments table (pay.c:1033-1047), not forwarded or received hashes. Bookkeeper then pairs the outgoing debit with the earlier credit. Requires the attacker to have a route through, or a prior payment to, the victim.

## Recommended fix
maybe_record_rebalance treats any channelmove sharing the counterparty-chosen payment_hash and amount as the other half of a self-payment, without requiring it to be an inbound invoice settlement on one of our own channel accounts (primary_tag 'invoice', credit side, different account) or using lightningd's knowledge that the payment resolved to our own invoice. Fix criteria: A pair must only be recorded when the credit side is an invoice-tagged settlement of an invoice owned by this node on a different channel account (e.g. filter on primary_tag/account, or use lightningd's own invoice/payment records). Verify that a forwarded HTLC and a later outgoing payment sharing hash and amount are no longer paired and the payment appears in bkpr-listincome.

# Bookkeeper CSV exports do not neutralise formula/delimiter content in attacker-authored descriptions

## Details
`bkpr-dumpincomecsv` writes income statements for import into accounting software (koinly, harmony and quickbooks formats emit a per-row description; cointracker does not), and `bkpr-report escape=csv` is documented (doc/schemas/bkpr-report.json) as a way to 'directly produce valid CSV files'. The description on invoice-type rows is authored by a remote party:

* for a debit (payment the node made), bookkeeper calls listsendpays (bookkeeper.c:1214-1240) and decodes the paid invoice string itself (fetch_out_desc_invstr, bookkeeper.c:1072-1110): the bolt11 `d` field or bolt12 `offer_description`, both chosen by the payee and validated only as UTF-8 (common/bolt11.c:200-220);
* for a credit, bookkeeper calls listinvoices (bookkeeper.c:1145-1162). For a keysend, keysend.c:489-493 picks the longest unknown UTF-8 TLV field of the sender's onion payload and stores it as the invoice description `keysend: <text>` (keysend.c:556-565), so an unauthenticated remote sender authors everything after the fixed prefix.

The only sanitiser is csv_safe_str (incomestmt.c:95-108): `"` -> `'`, JSON-escape of control characters, wrap in `"..."`. It does not neutralise spreadsheet formula triggers (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, and the `|`, `!`, `&`, `'` and parentheses a DDE or HYPERLINK payload needs), and bkpr-report's escape_value (report.c:390-427) quotes correctly but likewise leaves them intact. Two injections follow:

1. Formula injection (CWE-1236). A payee description beginning with `=`/`+`/`-`/`@` is emitted as the quoted Description (koinly, incomestmt.c:609-610) or Note (harmony, 751) cell and as a `{description}` tag in bkpr-report csv output. Excel and LibreOffice evaluate a quoted CSV cell whose content starts with `=` on import, so `=cmd|' /C calc'!A0` (DDE, after the application's prompt) or `=HYPERLINK(CHAR(104)&...&A1,...)` (exfiltration of neighbouring cells) runs when the operator opens the export. The keysend path cannot start a cell with `=` in these formats because of the `keysend: ` prefix.

2. Delimiter injection. quickbooks_entry (incomestmt.c:782-784) prints `<tag> (<account>) <asset>: "<desc>"` as an UNQUOTED field with the quoted description in the middle; RFC 4180 quoting applies only to a field that begins with a quote, so a comma inside the description splits the row. A keysend or payee description such as `x,99.0,` places attacker text in the Credit and Debit columns of the operator's QuickBooks import (the counterparty rewrites the amounts shown for its row), and a segment after a comma beginning with `=` becomes an unquoted formula cell -- this is also the route by which a keysend sender plants a formula despite the prefix.

The attacker is a payment counterparty (threat-model adversary 3) and, for keysend, anyone who can route an HTLC to the node (adversary 1); the victim is the operator who exports and opens/imports the CSV. Impact is integrity of the operator's accounting import and, through the spreadsheet application and subject to its own warnings, code execution or data exfiltration on the operator's workstation.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:95–108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L95-L108)
   csv_safe_str is the only sanitiser applied to descriptions: it replaces double quotes with single quotes, JSON-escapes control characters and wraps the value in quotes. It does nothing about leading '=', '+', '-', '@' (spreadsheet formula triggers) and relies on the caller emitting the result as a whole quoted field.
2. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:781–784](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L781-L784)
   quickbooks_entry embeds the quoted description inside an unquoted field: "%s (%s) %s: %s". A comma in the description therefore splits the row, shifting attacker text into the Credit/Debit columns; a following '=...' segment becomes an unquoted formula cell. Reachable from keysend despite the 'keysend: ' prefix.
3. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:608–610](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L608-L610)
   koinly_entry writes the description as a quoted Description cell; a payee-authored description beginning with '=' (bolt11 'd' / bolt12 offer_description) is evaluated as a formula by Excel/LibreOffice CSV import.
4. [plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c:750–751](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/incomestmt.c#L750-L751)
   harmony_entry: same quoted-but-unneutralised description in the Note column.
5. [plugins/bkpr/report.c:390–427](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/report.c#L390-L427)
   Sibling sink: bkpr-report escape=csv quotes fields containing , " \n \r correctly but leaves formula prefixes intact; doc/schemas/bkpr-report.json advertises this mode to 'directly produce valid CSV files'.
6. [plugins/keysend.c:489–493](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/keysend.c#L489-L493)
   Source 1 (unauthenticated remote sender): the longest unknown TLV field of the onion payload is accepted as the description with only a utf8_check.
7. [plugins/keysend.c:556–564](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/keysend.c#L556-L564)
   The sender's text is stored verbatim as the invoice description 'keysend: <text>' via the invoice RPC; bookkeeper reads it back through listinvoices.
8. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1072–1109](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1072-L1109)
   Source 2 (payee of any payment the node makes): fetch_out_desc_invstr decodes the paid bolt11 (description, utf8-checked only in common/bolt11.c:200-220) or bolt12 (offer_description) and returns the payee's text as the description.
9. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1145–1161](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1145-L1161)
   listinvoices_done takes the stored invoice description (the keysend sender's text for keysends), json-unescapes it and records it against the payment hash with add_payment_hash_description.
10. [plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c:1214–1239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/bkpr/bookkeeper.c#L1214-L1239)
   lookup_invoice_desc issues listinvoices for credit events and listsendpays for debit events, so both remote-authored sources reach the description table joined into income events (descriptions.c:333-343, incomestmt.c:42/65).

## Impact
The node's own exported accounting data is corrupted: in the quickbooks format the counterparty shifts columns and writes arbitrary Credit/Debit values for its row; in all formats it plants formula cells. No effect on node confidentiality or availability. Subsequent-system impact: Assumes the documented behaviour of spreadsheet CSV importers (Excel, LibreOffice Calc) that a cell beginning with '=' is evaluated even when quoted: HYPERLINK/WEBSERVICE-style formulas can exfiltrate neighbouring cells (other payments, balances, the node's accounting) to an attacker URL on click/recalculation, and DDE payloads can run commands on the operator's workstation after a security prompt. Bounded by the application's protections and the operator accepting its warnings, hence LOW rather than HIGH.

## Reproduction steps
1. Remote and unauthenticated for the keysend path: send the node a keysend whose text TLV contains a comma-split payload (e.g. 'x,99.0,=cmd|...'); keysend is a default-loaded plugin and the description is stored unmodified. For direct formula cells in the quoted koinly/harmony/bkpr-report output the attacker is the payee of a payment the node makes (a merchant handing the node an invoice whose 'd' field starts with '='). The payload fires when the operator later runs bkpr-dumpincomecsv or bkpr-report escape=csv and opens or imports the file in a spreadsheet/accounting application -- a deliberate but routine action (UI:ACTIVE); DDE payloads additionally require the operator to accept the application's prompt.

## Recommended fix
1. csv_safe_str (and bkpr-report's escape_value) treat CSV safety as quoting only; values beginning with formula trigger characters (=, +, -, @, and tab/CR variants) are emitted unchanged, so spreadsheet importers evaluate attacker-authored descriptions. Fix criteria: Any CSV cell derived from untrusted text must be rendered inert for spreadsheet importers (e.g. prefixing a quote/apostrophe or stripping leading = + - @ and control characters) in every emitter and in escape_value. Verify that a keysend/bolt11 description beginning with '=' appears in all four formats and in bkpr-report escape=csv as a literal string that Excel/LibreOffice do not evaluate.
2. quickbooks_entry embeds the quoted description in the middle of an unquoted field, so RFC 4180 quoting does not apply and commas in the description change the row's column structure. Fix criteria: The whole Description field in the quickbooks format must be a single properly quoted CSV field (quotes doubled, field enclosed). Verify that a description containing commas and quotes yields exactly four columns per row when parsed by a standard CSV reader.

# Unvalidated bias description with control characters silently truncates persistent askrene layer on reload

## Details
askrene-bias-channel and askrene-bias-node (plugins/askrene/askrene.c:1276-1289, 1312-1326) accept a free-form `description` via param_string, which copies the raw JSON token bytes without any character-class check. For a persistent layer, layer_set_bias/layer_set_node_bias (layer.c:1042-1087) serialise the description with towire_wirestring (datastore_wire.c:104-108) and append the record to the datastore; the write cannot fail on content. On the next start, load_layers/populate_layer decode the same bytes with fromwire_wirestring (wire/fromwire.c:265-279), which rejects any byte below 0x20 and calls fromwire_fail (cursor NULL, remaining length 0). populate_layer (layer.c:900-937) treats length 0 as end-of-data, so every record after the poisoned bias is silently dropped with only a LOG_BROKEN line. Record order fixes what is lost: between complete saves, every constraint, impression, local channel, update or disabled node appended after the bias; after a complete save (save_complete_layer, layer.c:820-886, which xpay triggers via askrene-age on each payment), the remaining channel biases and all node biases.

The triggering input needs a raw (unescaped) control byte inside the JSON string. CLN's JSON input path accepts that: json_parse_input validates structure and UTF-8 only (common/json_parse_simple.c:354-356; C0 bytes are valid UTF-8), and jsmn's string tokenizer does not check for control characters (external/jsmn, submodule absent from this checkout — stated as an assumption). commando forwards a rune-bearing peer's params byte-for-byte after checkrune (commando.c:286-305) and lightningd forwards the request raw to askrene (plugin.c:1346), so a peer holding a rune that permits askrene-bias-channel or askrene-bias-node on a persistent layer (e.g. the shared `xpay` layer) can poison it. clnrest and cln-grpc re-serialise through serde_json and are not vectors; the Unix socket and plugins are trusted principals.

Gain beyond the rune's grant: the rune lets the bearer set or zero biases; it does not let them delete the layer's node biases or the constraints, impressions and route-hint channels xpay has learned, which this path destroys at the next restart without any error visible to the writer or operator. Impact is limited to persisted routing-quality data (integrity, low) and is relearned over time; no crash, disclosure or funds exposure.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/askrene/datastore\_wire.c:72–108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/datastore_wire.c#L72-L108)
   fromwire_opt_wirestring (72-78) decodes the persisted description with fromwire_wirestring, which rejects any byte below 0x20; towire_opt_wirestring (104-108) writes the caller's string with towire_wirestring unvalidated. Encoder and decoder disagree on the accepted alphabet, so a record that was written successfully cannot be read back.
2. [plugins/askrene/askrene.c:1276–1289](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/askrene.c#L1276-L1289)
   askrene-bias-channel takes `description` via param_string, which copies the raw JSON token bytes (common/json_param.c:456-463) with no character-class check, and hands it to layer_set_bias which persists it. askrene-bias-node (1312-1326) is identical for node biases.
3. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:1042–1063](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L1042-L1063)
   layer_set_bias stores the description and calls save_channel_bias, which for a persistent layer appends the record to the datastore in create-or-append mode (680-690, 509-520); the datastore call cannot fail on content, so the writer receives success.
4. [wire/fromwire.c:265–279](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/fromwire.c#L265-L279)
   fromwire_wirestring breaks out of its scan on the first byte < ' ' and returns fromwire_fail, which sets *cursor = NULL and *max = 0 (16-21). The comment states it is only meant for subdaemon data.
5. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:900–937](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L900-L937)
   populate_layer loops while len != 0; after fromwire_fail len is 0, so the loop exits and every record after the poisoned bias is discarded. The only signal is a LOG_BROKEN line (933-936); no error is returned and the layer is kept in its truncated state.
6. [plugins/askrene/layer.c:820–886](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/askrene/layer.c#L820-L886)
   save_complete_layer (called from new_layer and from askrene-age, which xpay invokes per payment) serialises disabled nodes, channels, updates, constraints/impressions, then channel biases, then node biases. After a complete save the poisoned bias therefore drops later biases and every node bias; between complete saves it drops every constraint, impression, channel or update appended after it.
7. [plugins/commando.c:286–305](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/commando.c#L286-L305)
   After checkrune succeeds, execute_command re-emits each param with json_add_jsonstr, a byte-for-byte copy of the peer's JSON token (common/json_stream.c:223-235). lightningd then forwards the request raw to the askrene plugin (lightningd/plugin.c:1346), so a raw control byte inside the description string travels from a rune-bearing peer to the datastore unchanged.

## Impact
Silent loss of persisted askrene layer records the rune does not grant control over: node biases, and the constraints/impressions/channels appended after the poisoned record (all of them until the next complete save). Routing quality for the affected layer degrades until relearned; no crash, no disclosure, no effect on funds or availability.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker is a remote peer holding a rune that permits askrene-bias-channel or askrene-bias-node on a persistent layer (PR:L — a limited credential the operator issued). Over commando (AV:N) they send the method with a description containing a raw byte < 0x20; checkrune passes, commando and lightningd forward the bytes unchanged, askrene persists them and reports success (AC:L, UI:N). The loss materialises only at the next lightningd restart, and which records are lost depends on whether a complete save has run since the write (AT:P). Depends on jsmn (external/jsmn, pinned submodule not present in checkout) accepting raw control bytes inside string tokens, consistent with CLN's own validator adding only UTF-8 checks.

## Recommended fix
1. The description string is accepted by the RPC and persisted with an encoder (towire_wirestring) whose accepted alphabet is wider than the decoder's (fromwire_wirestring rejects bytes below 0x20), so a successfully stored record cannot be read back. Fix criteria: Every description accepted by askrene-bias-channel/-node on a persistent layer must round-trip through the datastore: either reject descriptions containing bytes below 0x20 at parameter validation time, or persist descriptions with a length-prefixed encoding whose decoder accepts every byte the encoder writes.
2. populate_layer treats a decode failure in one record as end-of-data and silently discards every subsequent record. Fix criteria: A record that fails to decode must not cause the remaining records of the layer to be dropped silently: records must be framed so a bad one can be skipped, or the failure must be surfaced as an error rather than a log line, and reload of a layer containing one undecodable bias must retain all other records.

# --daemon leaves umask(0) permanently; later-created files become world-writable

## Details
When started with --daemon, lightningd finishes daemonising in complete_daemonize() (lightningd/lightningd.c:691-718) after all startup initialisation, and there calls umask(0) (line 713) following the ccan/daemonize textbook recipe. Unlike a textbook daemon, lightningd keeps creating files and spawning processes for the rest of its life and never restores a mask: ld->initial_umask is saved (lightningd.c:333, 713) with a comment promising to re-apply it for `plugin start`, but no code in the tree reads it (rg: only lightningd.c/lightningd.h mention it). doc/CHANGELOG.md:3918 records that v0.8.1 (PR 3375) did restore the initial umask before spawning a `plugin start`ed plugin; that behaviour has regressed — plugin_exec() (plugin.c:2000, pipecmdarr) and the plugin_control.c start paths contain no umask handling.

What the ordering in main() settles:
- Startup artefacts are unaffected: hsm_secret (0400, O_EXCL), pidfile (0640), the sqlite DB (sqlite's 0644 default under the operator's umask; journals/WAL copy the DB mode), the RPC socket (its own umask dance in jsonrpc_listen, jsonrpc.c:1461-1466), gossip_store (0600) are all created before complete_daemonize() runs at lightningd.c:1505.
- Log rotation: --daemon requires --log-file (options.c:1132). The documented rotation procedure — move the file, send SIGHUP (doc/lightningd.8.md:43; exactly what tests/test_misc.py:2062-2065 does) — makes rotate_log() (log.c:926-940) fopen(path, "a") a new file with no explicit mode. Under umask 0 the kernel applies 0666: world-readable and world-writable.
- `plugin start` / `plugin startdir` / `plugin rescan` after daemonisation spawn plugins that inherit umask 0; any file they create with a default mode (Python open('w'), Rust fs::write, C fopen) is 0666 (0777 for directories/executables). Shipped plugins that write secrets set explicit modes (chanbackup 0400, clnrest/grpc key files 0600 via set_mode); shipped bookkeeper's bkpr-dumpincomecsv fopen("w") and clnrest/grpc public .pem files are umask-dependent, as is any third-party plugin.
- The re-exec path (lightningd.c:1612-1618; taken automatically when a subdaemon reports a different version after an in-place upgrade, subd.c:466-469, or after `recover`, jsonrpc.c:324) execv()s lightningd with umask 0 inherited. The new instance and every subdaemon and plugin it launches run under umask 0 for their lifetime; its own fopen("a") of the log file (log.c:999) yields 0666 if the file is absent.

Condition under which it is exploitable: another local account must be able to traverse to the created file. Relative --log-file paths resolve in the netdir (chdir at options.c:1875), which is 0700 only when lightningd created it (mkdir 0700, EEXIST tolerated, options.c:1879-1883); absolute paths such as /var/log/... or the documentation's own example /tmp/024b9a1fa8.debug.log (doc/lightningd-config.5.md:229) are outside it. Under the common operator umask 022 the increment is write access (0644 → 0666: any local user can append to or truncate the node log); under a restrictive umask (027/077) the rotated log additionally becomes world-readable, disclosing peer ids, IPs, channel/payment activity and anything else logged at INFO (e.g. malformed rune tokens, see common/json_command.c:19). The shipped systemd unit (contrib/init/lightningd.service, Type=simple) and the Docker entrypoint do not use --daemon; the man page quick start (doc/lightningd.8.md:81) and contrib/config-example do.

Root cause: umask(0) is applied as a one-way global side effect in a long-lived, file-creating, process-spawning daemon, and file creations that rely on the ambient umask (fopen without explicit mode, child processes) assume the operator's mask is still in force.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/lightningd.c:712–713](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L712-L713)
   complete_daemonize() sets umask(0) ('Discard our parent's old-fashioned umask prejudices') and stores the previous mask in ld->initial_umask; the process mask is never restored afterwards (rg over the tree finds no other umask() call except jsonrpc_listen's socket-local save/restore).
2. [lightningd/lightningd.c:331–334](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L331-L334)
   new_lightningd() initialises initial_umask with the stated intent to re-apply it later for `plugin start`; nothing in lightningd/ or common/ reads ld->initial_umask.
3. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1504–1505](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1504-L1505)
   complete_daemonize() runs after all startup file creation (hsm_secret, DB, pidfile, RPC socket, gossip_store), so only files created and processes spawned later — rotated logs, `plugin start`ed plugins, per-channel subdaemons, the re-exec'd self — run under umask 0.
4. [lightningd/log.c:926–940](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/log.c#L926-L940)
   rotate_log() (SIGHUP) recreates each --log-file with fopen(path, "a") and no explicit mode; with the process umask 0 a missing file is created 0666 (world-readable and world-writable).
5. [lightningd/options.c:1132–1133](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1132-L1133)
   check_config() requires --log-file whenever --daemon is used, so every daemonised node has a file log subject to SIGHUP rotation.
6. [lightningd/plugin.c:2000](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/plugin.c#L2000)
   plugin_exec() spawns plugins with pipecmdarr(); for plugins started at runtime (plugin start/startdir/rescan, plugin_control.c:66-158,243-251) the child inherits lightningd's umask 0 with no restoration — the behaviour CHANGELOG 0.8.1 says PR 3375 added has regressed.
7. [lightningd/lightningd.c:1612–1619](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/lightningd.c#L1612-L1619)
   On subdaemon version mismatch (subd.c:466-469) or `recover` (jsonrpc.c:324), lightningd execv()s itself; execv preserves the umask, so the new process and every subdaemon and plugin it spawns run under umask 0, and its own fopen("a") of a missing log file (log.c:999) yields 0666.
8. [lightningd/options.c:1875–1889](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/options.c#L1875-L1889)
   lightningd chdir()s into the netdir, so relative --log-file paths land there; the basedir/netdir are created 0700 only when lightningd creates them (EEXIST tolerated), and absolute log paths (e.g. /var/log, the docs' /tmp example) lie outside that fence — the condition under which the 0666 file is reachable by other local users.
9. [doc/lightningd.8.md:41–44](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/lightningd.8.md#L41-L44)
   Documentation tells operators to rotate logs by sending SIGHUP (so lightningd, not logrotate, creates the new file) and (line 81) to start lightningd with --daemon — the combination that produces the 0666 log file; tests/test_misc.py:2062-2065 performs exactly mv + SIGHUP.
10. [doc/CHANGELOG.md:3918](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/doc/CHANGELOG.md#L3918)
   v0.8.1: "'plugin start' now restores initial umask before spawning the plugin process (PR 3375)" — the project previously recognised and fixed the inherited-umask-0 problem; the fix is no longer present in the code.

## Impact
Integrity LOW: any local user can append to or truncate the node log (and other default-mode files created by runtime-started plugins). Confidentiality LOW: for operators with a restrictive umask (027/077) the rotated log becomes world-readable (peer ids, IPs, channel/payment activity, malformed rune tokens logged at INFO); under umask 022 the log was already 0644 so the confidentiality increment is limited to plugin-created files. Availability NONE. No key or fund exposure: hsm_secret, DB, gossip_store, RPC socket, chanbackup and TLS key files use explicit modes or are created before daemonising.

## Reproduction steps
1. Operator runs lightningd --daemon (the man-page quick start; not the shipped systemd unit or Docker image). After a routine mv+SIGHUP log rotation, a runtime `plugin start`, or the automatic re-exec on in-place upgrade/recover, newly created umask-dependent files are 0666. An unprivileged local account on the host that can traverse to the file's directory (log outside the 0700 lightning-dir, or a pre-existing non-0700 dir) then reads and/or writes it with ordinary filesystem calls. Attack requirements PRESENT: --daemon, a post-daemonise creation event, and a traversable directory. Privileges LOW: any local account.

## Recommended fix
1. complete_daemonize() sets umask(0) globally for a process that keeps creating files and spawning children, and the saved initial_umask is never re-applied (the v0.8.1 restoration before `plugin start` has regressed). Fix criteria: After daemonising, lightningd's effective umask for all later file creation and for every spawned subdaemon/plugin (including the re-exec'd self) equals the operator's original mask or a safe default (022 or stricter). Verify: with --daemon, a SIGHUP-rotated log file, a file created by a `plugin start`ed plugin, and files created by a version-mismatch re-exec are not group/world-writable.
2. Log files are (re)created with fopen("a") relying on the ambient umask instead of an explicit restrictive mode. Fix criteria: Log files are created (at startup and on SIGHUP rotation) with an explicit mode no more permissive than 0640 regardless of umask; verify the rotated and initial log files have that mode when the process umask is 0.

# Legacy pay replays a completed MPP/retried payment with an uninitialized payment_preimage when the group's first-listed part has none

## Details
payment_listsendpays_previous (plugins/pay.c:513-634) is the legacy `pay` plugin's idempotency check: before paying it calls listsendpays for the payment_hash and, if a prior group completed, replays that result as a no-op. For each new groupid it json_scans only the first-listed row for destination/created_at/amount_msat/amount_sent_msat/payment_preimage (570-580) and ignores the error json_scan returns. json_scan (common/json_parse.c:347-359) fills fields in guide order and stops at the first missing non-optional member, and listsendpays (lightningd/pay.c:173-176) emits payment_preimage only for completed rows. Rows are ordered by id (wallet/wallet.c:4587), and the retry modifier (plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2559-2564) gives each retry a new partid in the same group without deleting the failed row. Hence any payment whose first attempt failed (a hop or the payee returned e.g. temporary_channel_failure) and whose retry succeeded leaves a group of [failed row, complete row]; `completed` is OR-ed across rows (595) and the stack variable `preimage`, never written, is returned as `payment_preimage` with status 'complete' (604-613).

Any remote node on the route, or the payee, can make the first part fail while a later one completes, and this also happens under ordinary network conditions. When the payer later re-invokes `pay` for the same invoice through the legacy path — an idempotent retry after a client timeout/crash, or a second operator call — it receives a bogus payment_preimage as proof of payment (and 32 bytes of pay-plugin stack). The real preimage remains in the DB and in listsendpays/listpays, so the damage is a wrong proof in one response, not loss of funds.

Reachability in the default build: plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3570 sets take_over_pay=true (the manpage's 'default false' is stale), but handle_rpc_command does not redirect `pay` with array params of other than 1 or 2 elements (3448-3453; lightning-cli's default positional form `pay <bolt11> <amount> <label>`), with no bolt11, or when calc_maxfee fails; operators may also set xpay-handle-pay=false. A variant where the first row also lacks destination/amount_msat (rows created by raw sendonion without them) leaves msat/sent uninitialized and the per-part amount_msat_accumulate can plugin_err the important plugin, but that requires operator-created rows and is not attacker-driven.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/pay.c:564–580](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L564-L580)
   On each new groupid the first-listed sendpay row is json_scan'ed into stack variables destination/created_at/msat/sent/preimage (declared uninitialized at 535-538) with a non-optional 'payment_preimage:%' member, and the returned error string is discarded. A failed or pending row has no payment_preimage, so `preimage` is never written.
2. [plugins/pay.c:595–613](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/pay.c#L595-L613)
   `completed` is OR-ed over every row of the group (595). When any later row is 'complete', the function returns status 'complete' with json_add_preimage(&preimage) at 605 — the never-initialized stack value — to the RPC caller.
3. [common/json\_parse.c:347–358](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/json_parse.c#L347-L358)
   parse_field returns 'object does not have member' as soon as a non-optional member (no '?' suffix) is absent; earlier guide fields were already filled by handle_percent, later ones are left untouched.
4. [lightningd/pay.c:173–175](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/pay.c#L173-L175)
   json_add_payment_fields emits payment_preimage only when the row has one, i.e. only for completed parts; failed/pending parts of the same group lack it.
5. [wallet/wallet.c:4586–4587](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wallet/wallet.c#L4586-L4587)
   payments_by_hash (used by listsendpays with payment_hash) orders rows by id, so within a group the earliest-created part is listed first — the one that failed before a retry.
6. [plugins/libplugin-pay.c:2559–2563](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/libplugin-pay.c#L2559-L2563)
   On a non-final failure the retry modifier creates a child payment with a fresh partid in the same groupid (payment_new at 121: partid = root->next_partid++); the failed row is never deleted (lightningd/pay.c:642/1533 only set PAYMENT_FAILED), so the group is [failed part, ..., complete part].
7. [plugins/xpay/xpay.c:3448–3452](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L3448-L3452)
   Although take_over_pay defaults to true (3570), xpay does not redirect `pay` calls with array params of other than 1 or 2 elements (e.g. lightning-cli's default positional `pay <bolt11> <amount> <label>`), nor when bolt11 is missing or calc_maxfee fails; those reach the legacy pay plugin and payment_listsendpays_previous. xpay-handle-pay=false routes every pay there.

## Impact
The RPC response reports status 'complete' with a payment_preimage that is uninitialized stack memory, so the caller's stored proof of payment for that call is wrong (integrity, low: the correct preimage is still in the DB and listsendpays). The 32 leaked stack bytes go to the RPC caller, who is the trusted operator or an already pay-authorised rune bearer, so no confidentiality gain accrues to the attacker. No availability impact on the attacker-reachable path.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote hop or the payee (unauthenticated, over the Lightning network) fails the first HTLC part of a legacy-pay payment; the retry succeeds in the same group. The precondition is also met by ordinary routing failures. The victim must later re-invoke `pay` for the same invoice on a path xpay does not redirect (positional >2 args, missing bolt11, maxfee conversion failure, or xpay-handle-pay=false), which is a specific operator/client action.

## Recommended fix
Group summary fields are read only from the first-listed row of each group and the json_scan error is discarded, so a group can be reported complete using a payment_preimage (and potentially other fields) that was never parsed. Fix criteria: Take payment_preimage (and the other summary fields) from the row whose status is 'complete', or make payment_preimage optional in the scan and only report completion when a preimage was actually parsed; treat any json_scan error as a failure of the replay. Verify with a payment whose first part failed and a later part succeeded: a repeated legacy `pay` must return the stored preimage (sha256(preimage) == payment_hash), never an unparsed value.

# channeld granted unused SIGN_GOSSIP capability lets compromised channeld forge node_announcement and channel_update

## Details
hsmd's permission model is the mechanism that is supposed to bound a compromised per-channel subdaemon (threat model adversary 6). lightningd/channel_control.c grants every channeld HSM_PERM_SIGN_GOSSIP, but in this version channeld never sends any of the three requests that capability unlocks: channel_announcement, channel_update and node_announcement signing all happen in lightningd/channel_gossip.c over the MASTER connection. The grant is dead weight for an honest channeld and live capability for a compromised one.

Two of the gated handlers sign with the node identity key over caller-chosen content: handle_sign_node_announcement only checks the type byte and signs everything after the signature field, and handle_channel_update_sig signs any parseable channel_update regardless of short_channel_id. Unlike the per-channel signers, nothing ties these to the client's (node_id, dbid). A channeld compromised by its peer can therefore (a) produce a node_announcement for this node advertising attacker-chosen addresses, features, alias and timestamp, and (b) produce channel_updates for every channel this node has, e.g. setting disable or absurd fee/HTLC parameters, or a timestamp in the near future that out-ranks the node's own later updates. connectd forwards subdaemon output to the peer unfiltered (multiplex.c read_from_subd_done), and the peer, or any node that receives the messages, relays them because the signatures verify.

Impact: forged node_announcement redirects inbound connection attempts to attacker addresses (BOLT8 prevents impersonation, but inbound connectivity is lost and the attacker learns who tries to connect); forged channel_updates disable or misprice all of the node's channels network-wide, which is a routing/revenue denial of service against the whole node, not just the compromised channel. A compromised channeld without this grant could only affect its own channel's gossip via the messages lightningd signs for it.

The root cause is on the lightningd side (unnecessary grant) and is made exploitable by hsmd's coarse SIGN_GOSSIP bit covering node-wide signatures. If channeld's ECDH grant is likewise unused at runtime (channeld links libcommon wholesale, so static inspection does not settle it), the same forged node_announcement combined with an ECDH oracle on the node key would allow completing BOLT8 handshakes as this node; that is noted as a lead rather than claimed here.

## Evidence
1. [lightningd/channel\_control.c:1817–1826](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_control.c#L1817-L1826)
   peer_start_channeld requests channeld's hsmd client fd with HSM_PERM_SIGN_GOSSIP (plus ECDH, COMMITMENT_POINT, SIGN_REMOTE_TX, SIGN_ONCHAIN_TX, SIGN_CLOSING_TX, SIGN_SPLICE_TX, LOCK_OUTPOINT). channeld is the only non-master client ever given SIGN_GOSSIP (grep of HSM_PERM_ across lightningd/: openingd, dualopend, closingd, onchaind, connectd never receive it). This is the line the fix must change.
2. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:105–108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L105-L108)
   hsmd_check_client_capabilities gates WIRE_HSMD_CANNOUNCEMENT_SIG_REQ, WIRE_HSMD_CUPDATE_SIG_REQ and WIRE_HSMD_NODE_ANNOUNCEMENT_SIG_REQ on HSM_PERM_SIGN_GOSSIP alone; the latter two are node-identity signatures whose content is not bound to the client's (node_id, dbid).
3. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1266–1303](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1266-L1303)
   handle_sign_node_announcement checks only tal_count(ann) >= 66 and the WIRE_NODE_ANNOUNCEMENT type, then signs sha256d(ann+66) with node_key(): addresses, features, alias, colour and timestamp are entirely caller-chosen.
4. [hsmd/libhsmd.c:1306–1353](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/libhsmd.c#L1306-L1353)
   handle_channel_update_sig signs any channel_update that fromwire_channel_update parses, with the node key; short_channel_id, channel_flags (disable), fees, htlc limits and timestamp are caller-chosen, so a client for channel X can sign updates for every channel this node has.
5. [hsmd/hsmd.c:768–772](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/hsmd/hsmd.c#L768-L772)
   handle_client applies hsmd_check_client_capabilities before dispatch for every request on every client fd — this is the shipped control that bounds a compromised subdaemon, and it passes these three requests for any client holding SIGN_GOSSIP (hsmd.c:1-8 states the per-client capability-map design).
6. [channeld/channeld.c](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c) (whole file)
   channeld (and channeld/watchtower.c) issues no hsmd_cannouncement_sig_req, hsmd_cupdate_sig_req or hsmd_node_announcement_sig_req; its towire_hsmd_* calls are limited to sign_remote_commitment_tx, sign_remote_htlc_tx, get_per_commitment_point, revoke_commitment_tx, validate_commitment_tx, validate_revocation, sign_splice_tx, check_outpoint, lock_outpoint, setup_channel, check_future_secret and sign_penalty_to_us. The SIGN_GOSSIP capability is never used legitimately.
7. [lightningd/channel\_gossip.c:482](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/channel_gossip.c#L482)
   All channel_update signing is done by lightningd over its MASTER fd via hsm_sync_req (also sign_any_cannouncement at 720/768 and node_announcement_sig_req at 1446), confirming gossip signing moved out of channeld while the grant remained.
8. [connectd/multiplex.c:1390–1400](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/connectd/multiplex.c#L1390-L1400)
   read_from_subd_done passes whatever channeld writes to msg_to_peer_outq without type filtering (maybe_update_channelid only inspects open/accept/funding_created), so a compromised channeld can inject the forged node_announcement/channel_update into the gossip network via its own peer, which relays it as validly signed.
9. [gossipd/gossmap\_manage.c:1001–1010](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/gossipd/gossmap_manage.c#L1001-L1010)
   timestamp_reasonable accepts gossip timestamps up to 24 hours in the future, so a forged channel_update/node_announcement stamped ahead out-ranks the node's own genuine updates on every receiving node for up to a day.

## Impact
Integrity LOW: the node's public gossip records (node_announcement, channel_update for all channels) can be replaced with attacker-signed versions; keys and channel state are not affected. Availability LOW: inbound connectivity and routing through all the node's channels can be disrupted network-wide, but the node itself keeps running and funds are not at risk. Confidentiality unaffected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker position: code execution inside channeld (e.g. after a remote peer exploits channeld), holding the hsmd client fd lightningd created for it. Steps: send hsmd_node_announcement_sig_req / hsmd_cupdate_sig_req with crafted content, receive node-key signatures, write the signed gossip to the peer via connectd. No configuration precondition, no race, no user action.

## Recommended fix
1. lightningd grants channeld HSM_PERM_SIGN_GOSSIP although channeld no longer performs any gossip signing, violating least privilege for the daemon the hsmd permission model is meant to contain. Fix criteria: channeld's hsmd fd is requested without HSM_PERM_SIGN_GOSSIP (and any other bit its request set does not use). Verify by sending hsmd_node_announcement_sig_req and hsmd_cupdate_sig_req over a channeld client fd: hsmd must reject them as 'client does not have capability' and existing channel/gossip functionality must be unchanged.
2. hsmd's SIGN_GOSSIP bit bundles node-wide node_announcement/channel_update signing with the per-channel channel_announcement signing, so any holder can sign gossip for channels and identity records it does not own. Fix criteria: Node-identity gossip signatures (node_announcement, channel_update for arbitrary scids) are reachable only from the MASTER client, or are gated by a separate capability never handed to per-channel daemons; per-channel clients can obtain at most a channel_announcement signature bound to their own (node_id, dbid).

# fromwire_len_and_tlvstream never deducts the TLV stream from *max: a compromised channeld makes lightningd read past the channeld_got_commitsig buffer

## Details
common/htlc_wire.c:fromwire_len_and_tlvstream() (lines 197-217) parses the length-prefixed TLV stream embedded in struct added_htlc (and existing_htlc). It validates `len <= *max`, then calls fromwire_tlv(cursor, &len, ...). fromwire_tlv advances *cursor by the whole stream but decrements only the local `len` (tlvstream.c:286-289); the caller's *max is never reduced. From that point the (cursor, max) pair used by fromwire_added_htlc's trailing fromwire_bool, by the remaining `added` elements and by every later field of the generated fromwire_channeld_got_commitsig (fulfilled/failed/changed arrays, tx, inflight commitsigs) overstates the remaining bytes by up to 65535. The generated parser returns `cursor != NULL` without requiring plen == 0 (tools/gen/impl_template:410), so nothing detects the desynchronisation.

For a well-formed message the reads still land inside the buffer and only the trailing-bytes accounting is wrong (silent). For a crafted message the bound is defeated: the sender declares a TLV length that consumes the real remainder of the buffer (a valid stream, e.g. one odd-typed record), after which fromwire() (wire/fromwire.c:27-40) memcpy()s the following fields from heap memory past the end of the tal buffer that wire_io.c sized exactly to the message. Choosing num_added = 2 makes the second added_htlc (u64 id, amount, sha256, u32, 1366-byte onion, bools) be read entirely from out-of-bounds memory; its OOB-derived counts then size further reads, all capped by the stale max (<= 65535 bytes past the buffer) or by the first fromwire failure on garbage.

Who can send it: added_htlc arrays travel channeld -> lightningd in channeld_got_commitsig (channeld_wire.csv:172). An honest channeld's towire_len_and_tlvstream (htlc_wire.c:81-91) always writes the exact serialized length, so a remote peer cannot trigger this through an honest channeld; the triggering author is a compromised channeld (threat model adversary 6: 'a compromised subdaemon ... attacking lightningd; lightningd's checks are meant to bound it'). lightningd does treat channeld input as checked rather than trusted: malformed subdaemon messages are log_broken + close (subd.c:585-588), a failed channeld_got_commitsig parse is channel_internal_error (peer_htlcs.c:2507), and peer_htlcs.c:2379 validates HTLC ids because 'don't trust it blindly'. The intended consequence of a misbehaving channeld is therefore a single-channel force-close. This bug gives that position more: an up-to-64KB heap over-read inside the master daemon, whose contents become HTLC fields that are persisted to the channel_htlcs table and logged (operator-visible; an OOB-derived HTLC id is echoed back to channeld if lightningd later fails that HTLC), and a SIGSEGV of lightningd — taking down every channel — if the over-read crosses the end of the heap mapping. The mirror direction (existing_htlc in channeld_init, lightningd -> channeld) is authored by the trusted master and is not an attack path.

## Evidence
1. [common/htlc\_wire.c:197–217](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/htlc_wire.c#L197-L217)
   Primary defect. Reads u16 len, checks len <= *max, then calls fromwire_tlv(cursor, &len, ...). fromwire_tlv advances *cursor by the whole stream but decrements only the local `len`; the caller's *max is never reduced, so on return (*cursor, *max) overstate the remaining buffer by the stream length (up to 65535). The fix belongs here.
2. [common/htlc\_wire.c:229–239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/common/htlc_wire.c#L229-L239)
   fromwire_added_htlc continues with fromwire_bool(cursor, max) for fail_immediate using the stale *max, and returns into the generated channeld_got_commitsig parser which keeps using the same desynchronised pair for the next array element and every later field.
3. [wire/tlvstream.c:284–289](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/tlvstream.c#L284-L289)
   fromwire_tlv advances *cursor (directly, or via the type's fromwire) and decrements only the *max it was handed — here the local `len` — so it cannot repair the caller's bound.
4. [wire/fromwire.c:23–41](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/fromwire.c#L23-L41)
   fromwire() bounds every read by *max and then memcpy()s n bytes from *cursor; with *cursor at the end of the tal buffer and *max stale, these memcpy()s read heap memory past the message buffer.
5. [tools/gen/impl\_template:351–410](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/tools/gen/impl_template#L351-L410)
   The generated fromwire_channeld_got_commitsig parses the `added` array in a loop sharing one (cursor, plen) pair and returns `cursor != NULL` without requiring plen == 0, so the desynchronisation is neither detected nor contained by the enclosing parser.
6. [channeld/channeld\_wire.csv:171–172](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld_wire.csv#L171-L172)
   channeld_got_commitsig carries `added` (array of added_htlc, u16 count chosen by the sender) from channeld to lightningd: the attacker-side direction. The mirror existing_htlc field travels lightningd -> channeld (line 57) and is authored by the trusted master, so it is not an attack path.
7. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2493–2511](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2493-L2511)
   lightningd parses the message here with msg as the exact-size tal buffer read from the subdaemon pipe. A parse failure is bounded to channel_internal_error (force-close of that one channel) — the project's intended consequence of a misbehaving channeld — whereas this bug yields an over-read inside lightningd instead of a clean failure.
8. [lightningd/peer\_htlcs.c:2379–2387](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/peer_htlcs.c#L2379-L2387)
   Shows lightningd deliberately validates channeld-reported HTLC data rather than trusting it ("don't trust it blindly"): channeld -> lightningd is a boundary lightningd maintains, matching the threat model's adversary 6 (compromised subdaemon bounded by lightningd's checks).
9. [wire/wire\_io.c:37–45](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/wire/wire_io.c#L37-L45)
   The subdaemon message buffer is tal_resize()d to exactly the declared length before the body is read, so the over-read begins immediately past the message and reaches adjacent heap chunks.

## Impact
Up to 65535 bytes of lightningd heap past the message buffer are copied into HTLC fields, persisted to the DB and logged, with only a thin read-back channel (an OOB-derived HTLC id returned in channeld_fail_htlc): limited confidentiality loss. Integrity is not newly affected — a compromised channeld can already author arbitrary HTLC fields. Availability: the usual outcome is a garbage-induced parse failure and channel_internal_error (already conceded), but a read crossing the heap mapping end crashes the master daemon and all channels; glibc keeps top padding, so this is possible but not reliable.

## Reproduction steps
1. The attacker must already control a channeld process (threat model adversary 6, e.g. after a peer-reachable exploit of channeld) and write one crafted channeld_got_commitsig to the local pipe; the over-read itself is deterministic and no check in the generated parser or in peer_htlcs.c catches it. Whether it ends in a crash rather than a parse failure depends on lightningd's heap layout past the message buffer, which the attacker does not control (AT:P). channeld holds no keys and only its own peer's channel, so the position is low-privilege.

## Recommended fix
1. fromwire_len_and_tlvstream() parses a sub-stream with a private length copy and never reconciles the caller's *max with the bytes consumed, breaking the fromwire invariant that *cursor + *max bounds the buffer. Fix criteria: After fromwire_tlv returns, *max must be reduced by exactly the bytes the sub-stream consumed (the declared len), and parsing must fail if the sub-parser did not consume exactly len. A channeld_got_commitsig whose declared TLV length swallows the remaining buffer must then fail to parse (channel_internal_error) rather than read past the buffer; verify with a crafted added_htlc under ASan.
2. Generated message parsers (tools/gen/impl_template) accept a message as long as cursor is non-NULL, ignoring unconsumed or over-accounted bytes, so a bounds desynchronisation in any hand-written subtype parser goes undetected. Fix criteria: Generated fromwire_* for subdaemon messages should reject messages whose remaining length is not exactly zero after all fields are parsed, or otherwise assert the (cursor, plen) invariant, so a hand-written subtype parser cannot leave the pair inconsistent without the message being rejected.
