# NULL dereference in splice initiator when peer answers commitment with tx_signatures

## Details
When the local node initiates a splice and the operator finishes the PSBT (`splice_update` with no further changes, channeld.c:4949-4952), channeld runs splice_initiator_user_finalized(). After saving the new inflight via WIRE_CHANNELD_ADD_INFLIGHT (persisted by lightningd with last_tx NULL) it calls `interactive_send_commitments(peer, psbt, TX_INITIATOR, idx, true, true, NULL, 0)` and then unconditionally does `new_inflight->last_tx = tal_steal(new_inflight, their_commit->tx); new_inflight->last_sig = their_commit->commit_signature;` (channeld.c:4845-4846) and passes `their_commit->tx` to towire_channeld_update_inflight.

interactive_send_commitments() reads the next peer message with peer_expect_msg_four(COMMITMENT_SIGNED, TX_SIGNATURES, TX_ABORT, 0) (channeld.c:3254). check_tx_abort() returns immediately for any type other than TX_ABORT (channeld.c:1955). `result` is only assigned when the type is WIRE_COMMITMENT_SIGNED (channeld.c:3280-3290); for a TX_SIGNATURES message the function returns NULL, as its own comment states ('If the first message received is tx_abort or tx_signatures, NULL is returned'). The caller passes msg_received=NULL and never checks the return, so lightning_channeld dereferences NULL and dies with SIGSEGV. Whether we commit first (we send commitment_signed, then read) or second (we read first), the attacker's reply at that point is the same message.

A malicious accepter therefore only needs to answer, where commitment_signed is expected, with a well-formed tx_signatures. lightningd sees the owning subdaemon die (subd.c:595-660 destroy_subd -> channel_errmsg with peer_fd NULL -> channel_fail_transient, peer_control.c:641-646): the channel goes offline until reconnect and the splice RPC fails. The half-negotiated inflight (last_tx NULL) remains in the database: maybe_cleanup_last_inflight() (channel.c:133-150) is only invoked from dual_open_control.c, so peer_start_channeld hands the stale inflight to the next channeld (channel_control.c:1960), which on reconnect advertises next_funding and enters resume_splice_negotiation(); that path handles the NULL return with peer_failed_err (channeld.c:3985-3989), so the crash itself is triggerable once per operator-initiated splice, after which the peer can tx_abort or let the stale inflight be errored out under CLN's normal error policy. Splicing is enabled by default in this release (options.c:1270: '--experimental-splicing is now enabled by default').

## Evidence
1. [channeld/channeld.c:4845–4851](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L4845-L4851)
   splice_initiator_user_finalized() dereferences their_commit->tx and their_commit->commit_signature without checking for NULL.
2. [channeld/channeld.c:3263–3289](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3263-L3289)
   interactive_send_commitments() accepts WIRE_TX_SIGNATURES from peer_expect_msg_four(), only populates result when the message is WIRE_COMMITMENT_SIGNED, and returns NULL otherwise (documented: 'If the first message received is tx_abort or tx_signatures, NULL is returned').
3. [channeld/channeld.c:3968–3979](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/channeld/channeld.c#L3968-L3979)
   The sibling path resume_splice_negotiation() does handle the NULL return ('if (their_commit) ... if (!inflight->last_tx) peer_failed_err'), showing the maintainers know the return can be NULL; the initiator path simply forgot.

## Impact
Deterministic SIGSEGV of the per-channel daemon; lightningd treats it as a transient channel failure (reconnect), the splice command fails and a half-negotiated inflight with no commitment is left in the database and handed to the next channeld. One crash per operator-initiated splice with this peer; no funds or secrets are affected and the dereference is a NULL read, not a write.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the remote channel peer (PR:L: they must hold a channel with the victim) acting as splice accepter. The victim operator must have started a splice with this peer and finalized the PSBT (AT:PRESENT, a runtime condition outside the attacker's control). The attacker then sends a well-formed tx_signatures where commitment_signed is expected; peer_expect_msg_four admits that type and nothing else guards the dereference (AC:L); no user interaction beyond the operator's own splice command (UI:N). Splicing is on by default in v26.06.

## Recommended fix
splice_initiator_user_finalized() assumes interactive_send_commitments() always returns a commitment, although the callee returns NULL when the peer sends tx_signatures (or any accepted non-commitment message) instead. Fix criteria: A peer message other than commitment_signed at this point must be handled explicitly (peer_failed_warn/err or proper deferral) so that channeld never dereferences a NULL commitsig; sending tx_signatures in place of commitment_signed must produce a protocol error, not a crash.

# clnrest WebSocket notification stream never re-validates the rune after connect

## Details
When clnrest is enabled (`clnrest-port` set), its Socket.IO endpoint streams every lightningd notification (invoice_creation, invoice_payment incl. preimage, sendpay_success/failure incl. payment_preimage, forward_event, channel_opened/channel_state_changed, connect/disconnect, coin_movement, balance_snapshot, block_added, custommsg raw peer payloads, ...) to connected clients. Authorisation is a single `checkrune` call for the pseudo-method `listclnrest-notifications`, performed by `auth_socket_io_middleware` when the client joins the '/' namespace (handlers.rs:575-591, wired at main.rs:131). Thereafter `notification_background_task` (main.rs:266-274) emits to all connected sockets for the lifetime of the connection; the rune is not stored on the socket and is never re-evaluated. The HTTP path, by contrast, re-runs verify_rune on every request (handlers.rs:276).

Consequences:
- `blacklistrune` / `destroyrune` — documented as the way to "effectively revoke the rune you have created" (doc/schemas/blacklistrune.json) — do not cut off an already-connected client. Blacklist enforcement lives only inside checkrune (runes.c:1010), which nothing re-invokes for an open socket, so the bearer's existing stream keeps delivering the node's real-time payment, forwarding, channel and peer activity until the connection drops or the clnrest plugin is restarted.
- Rune `time<`, `rate=` and `per=` restrictions are evaluated once at connect and never again, so a deliberately short-lived rune grants an unbounded subscription.
- There is no RPC to enumerate or disconnect notification subscribers, so the operator cannot detect or terminate such a session short of restarting the plugin.

Assumed dependency behaviour (socketioxide 0.16, pinned in plugins/rest-plugin/Cargo.toml; not verifiable in this checkout): `.with()` attaches a connect-time middleware only, `SocketIo::emit` broadcasts to all sockets of the root namespace, and engine.io ping/pong keeps an idle client connected indefinitely. The clients shown in doc/developers-guide/app-development/rest.md are long-running by design, so the window is indefinite. Impact is confidentiality of ongoing node activity after authorisation was withdrawn; no RPC execution is gained.

## Evidence
1. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs:575–591](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/handlers.rs#L575-L591)
   auth_socket_io_middleware is the only authorisation on the notification socket: it reads the `rune` header once at Socket.IO namespace connect and calls verify_rune for pseudo-method listclnrest-notifications. The rune is not retained on the socket and is never re-checked; by contrast the HTTP path re-runs verify_rune on every request (handlers.rs:276).
2. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/main.rs:266–274](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/main.rs#L266-L274)
   notification_background_task forwards every lightningd notification (plugin subscribes to '*', main.rs:84) via io.emit to all sockets currently connected to the '/' namespace, for as long as each TCP/engine.io connection stays alive, with no per-socket authorisation state or expiry.
3. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/main.rs:131–133](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/main.rs#L131-L133)
   The middleware is wired only as a connect-time handler on ns('/'); no periodic re-validation task, no reaction to blacklistrune/destroyrune, and no RPC to enumerate or disconnect subscribers exists anywhere in the plugin.
4. [plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs:11–71](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/plugins/rest-plugin/src/shared.rs#L11-L71)
   verify_rune is a one-shot checkrune/showrunes call; the rune's time<, rate=/per= restrictions and the blacklist are evaluated only at this instant.
5. [lightningd/runes.c:1010–1011](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/runes.c#L1010-L1011)
   Blacklisting (blacklistrune / its alias destroyrune) and all other restrictions are enforced solely when checkrune is invoked; a consumer that never calls checkrune again never observes revocation or expiry.
6. [lightningd/connect\_control.c:417](https://github.com/Halbarevi/core-lightning/blob/6f25f6969ea7d76c1aa4652b4c3d8316b4a0bee8/lightningd/connect_control.c#L417)
   Every raw inbound peer custom message is emitted as a `custommsg` notification before the hook runs, so the retained stream carries commando request payloads in addition to invoice_payment/sendpay preimages, forwarding, channel and peer events.

## Impact
Continued disclosure of the node's live notification stream — invoice and sendpay events including preimages, forwarding amounts/fees, channel state, peer connects, raw peer custommsg payloads — to a party whose authorisation the operator has withdrawn. The attacker does not control which information arrives and gains no RPC execution, keys or stored state, so confidentiality is LOW. No integrity or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a network client who at some point held a rune valid for listclnrest-notifications (any readonly rune suffices) and connected to the clnrest Socket.IO endpoint while it was valid. Later the operator blacklists/destroys the rune, or its time< restriction lapses; the attacker simply keeps the existing connection open (answering engine.io pings, which socket.io clients do automatically) and continues to receive all notifications. No control is defeated; the precondition is runtime state — a connection that predates revocation/expiry — which is a present attack requirement. Requires clnrest to be enabled by the operator (off by default), which is the surface the threat model names for rune holders. Depends on socketioxide 0.16 connect-middleware and keepalive semantics as stated in the description.

## Recommended fix
1. Authorisation for the long-lived notification subscription is evaluated once at connect; revocation, expiry and rate restrictions of the rune are never re-applied to the open socket. Fix criteria: A socket whose rune would no longer pass checkrune (blacklisted, destroyed, time-expired, rate-exceeded) stops receiving notifications within a bounded, documented interval and is disconnected. Verify: connect with a rune, blacklist it, trigger an invoice; the client must receive no further notifications. Same for a rune with a short `time<` restriction after it elapses.
2. Operators have no visibility into or control over connected notification subscribers. Fix criteria: Operators can enumerate current subscribers (rune unique_id, remote address, connect time) and disconnect them; connects/disconnects are logged with the rune unique_id.
